articles.title: 'You cannot change or build the marketing organization of the future with the creative organization of the past': Adobe CEO lays out how work and collaboration are fundamentally changing
articles.text:
'You cannot change or build the marketing organization of the future with the creative organization of the past': Adobe CEO lays out how work and collaboration are fundamentally changing
Organizational structures and the definition of work are being challenged
Marketing is more fast-paced than ever, with creatives now required to cater to more languages and geographies than ever as well as much faster refresh cycles.
"Marketing professionals face unprecedented pressure to create compelling content across channels, optimize campaigns, and deliver," Adobe CEO Shantanu Narayen declared in an open letter to shareholders.
But Adobe believes marketing teams will need to rethink far more than which tools their employees use to keep up with the shift.
Speaking with the media at its annual Adobe Max conference, Creative VP Resh Sidhu warned that entire organizational structures could no longer be suited to the future of marketing.
Sidhu argued the importance for businesses to reconsider workflows, employee skills and their entire approach to creative production, hinting at the ongoing AI-driven evolution.
"You cannot change... or build the marketing organization of the future with the creative organization of the past," she said.
Teams are under intense pressure to change how they work
The comments came in response to a question about whether AI could create a division between teams based on willingness and ability to use AI.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Discussions quickly turned to AI literacy – Product Marketing VP Deepa Subramaniam and Sidhu agreed that AI is already changing how their own teams operate, and rather than simply treating AI as another tool or piece of software, agents are increasingly being seen as digital colleagues.
But while the company is looking to incorporate AI fluency into its employee upskilling and support schemes, they argued that simply tracking how frequently employees interact with AI is virtually meaningless.
"We're not counting tokens over here," Sidhu said, referring to her team's 'customer zero' status as the earliest adopter of new Adobe tools.
AI isn't a tool – it's changing the definition of work
But leveraging AI crucially helps their teams – and broader marketing teams – to spend more time developing other concepts, testing alternatives and refining their campaigns beyond what's been possible thus far. The execs also agreed that marketing can now start much earlier than at the marketing team, thanks to more people being able to experiment with their ideas through AI – something they perceive as improving quality of output by being able to access more perspectives.
But this adds its own complexities, because if AI is now enabling employees to work across other areas of the business, companies will need to reconsider how responsibilities are shared and how the future of inter-team collaboration looks.
While the two agreed that creators on an individual level must retain the choice about when, why and whether to use AI, the reality for business leaders is far more challenging.
As AI becomes more embedded into daily workflows, the focus is increasingly shifting to redefining entire work structures now that many processes have become more democratized.
The message was clear, though. The businesses that benefit most – and risk being left behind the least – will be those who fundamentally challenge what work looks like to redesign and adapt in readiness for the future.

articles.title: Cómo evitar que un desconocido te llene el calendario del celular con falsas alertas de cobro
articles.text:
Los estafadores envían falsas alertas de cobro o de seguridad como invitaciones de calendario, y en Google Calendar el ajuste de fábrica las agrega solo a la agenda del usuario, sin que abra ningún correo. Google, Apple y la empresa de seguridad Malwarebytes publicaron pasos para frenarlas.
La técnica consiste en crear un evento con un mensaje urgente: una renovación de suscripción, una transferencia o una factura vencida. Según el sitio Techlicious, que citó un aviso de Google de junio de 2026, los eventos incluyen montos altos, números de transacción inventados y un teléfono para “disputar” el cargo.
Malwarebytes documentó en marzo de 2026 una campaña en la que los delincuentes se hacían pasar por la propia empresa y enviaban falsos recibos de renovación. Quien llama termina entregando datos de la tarjeta, de su cuenta bancaria o acceso remoto a su computadora, explicó la firma en su blog.
Google describe en su ayuda oficial que, con la opción “De todos”, todas las invitaciones se agregan automáticamente al calendario. Por eso el evento aparece aunque el correo original haya ido a la carpeta de spam.
Cómo bloquear las invitaciones en Android y Gmail
En la aplicación Calendar de Android, según la página de ayuda de Google sobre spam: tocar Menú, luego Configuración, General, “Agregar invitaciones” y “Agregar invitaciones a mi calendario”, y elegir “Solo si el remitente es conocido”. Se considera conocido a quien está en los contactos, en la misma organización o con quien hubo interacción previa.
Con esa opción, las invitaciones de desconocidos llegan solo por correo y no se suman a la agenda. Google aclara que los cambios afectan únicamente a las invitaciones nuevas, y que las ya agregadas deben eliminarse a mano.
Otra alternativa es “Cuando responda a la invitación en el correo”, que añade el evento solo después de contestar. En la versión web se llega desde el engranaje, en Configuración y “Configuración de eventos”. Google advierte que la opción de remitentes conocidos puede revelar a quien envía que no está en los contactos del usuario.
Si siguen apareciendo eventos no deseados en el teléfono, Google recomienda revisar qué aplicaciones tienen permiso para modificar el calendario, desde Configuración, Privacidad y el administrador de permisos. También se puede ocultar un calendario ajeno desde el menú de la aplicación, desmarcándolo.
Qué hacer con un evento sospechoso ya agregado
Lo primero es no tocar ningún enlace ni llamar al número del evento. Malwarebytes y Techlicious coinciden en que conviene denunciarlo antes de borrarlo: se abre el evento, se toca el menú de tres puntos y se elige “Denunciar como spam”. Google precisa que solo se pueden denunciar eventos enviados desde Google Calendar y que el evento desaparece, junto con toda la serie si se repite.
En el iPhone, Apple indica en su soporte (para iOS 26 o posterior) que, si el evento viene de un contacto desconocido, se debe tocar “Reportar como basura” y luego “Eliminar y reportar como basura”. Para cualquier otro evento basta con “Eliminar evento” y confirmar.
Cuando entran muchos eventos de golpe, puede tratarse de un calendario suscrito. Apple explica el procedimiento: en Calendario, tocar “Calendarios”, pulsar el botón de información junto al que no se reconoce y elegir “Cancelar suscripción” o “Eliminar calendario”. Si el calendario no se puede quitar, se puede ocultar quitando la marca.
Malwarebytes agrega que los eventos a veces reaparecen por la sincronización entre dispositivos. En ese caso hay que eliminar el calendario o el evento en todos los lugares donde exista, incluidos Outlook y la aplicación del teléfono.
Si ya se hizo clic o se llamó al teléfono
Ni Google ni Apple ofrecen en esas páginas un procedimiento único para quien ya entró en el enlace. Las recomendaciones de Malwarebytes apuntan a verificar cualquier supuesto problema de facturación directamente en el sitio oficial o el soporte de la empresa, no en los datos del evento, y a activar la verificación en dos pasos en las cuentas.
Si se ingresó una contraseña o un código en una página enlazada desde el evento, corresponde cambiar esa clave de inmediato y, si se compartieron datos de una tarjeta, avisar al banco. Estas dos medidas son una indicación general de prudencia y no provienen de las páginas de ayuda citadas.
Los pasos se comprobaron en noviembre de 2026 en las páginas de ayuda de Google y de Apple. Los nombres de los menús pueden variar según el modelo del teléfono y la versión del sistema, y Apple documenta el botón “Reportar como basura” a partir de iOS 26.

articles.title: Lançamento: Galaxy Tab S12 Plus (512 GB) já recebe desconto pré-Black Friday • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Lançamento: Galaxy Tab S12 Plus (512 GB) já recebe desconto pré-Black Friday
Galaxy Tab S12 Plus (512 GB) tem RAM de 12 GB, tela grande e muita bateria; tablet da Samsung recebe desconto de R$ 2 mil com cupom no Magalu
O Galaxy Tab S12 Plus Wi-Fi de 512 GB está saindo por apenas R$ 8.449,10 no Pix com o cupom TABLET1000 no Magazine Luiza, como parte da campanha de esquenta para a “Black das Blacks” da varejista. A oferta representa uma redução de R$ 2.000 frente ao preço original de R$ 10.499.
O novo tablet da Samsung oferece grandes ganhos em relação ao seu antecessor e oferece uma bateria de longa duração.
Equipado com o processador Dimensity 9500 de 3 nm e 12 GB de RAM, o Galaxy Tab S12 Plus jogos pesados e multitarefas sem engasgos. Segundo a Samsung, o chip está 48% mais potente em termos de CPU e apresenta ganho de 67% na GPU frente ao Galaxy Tab S10 Plus, seu antecessor direto.
Para trabalho, leituras e reprodução de conteúdos, a tela Dynamic AMOLED conta com um espaço amplo de 12,6 polegadas, e excelente fluidez graças à taxa de atualização de 120 Hz. Em relação ao brilho, o tablet chega até 1.600 nits, oferecendo uma excelente visibilidade. O conjunto acompanha caneta S Pen, que entrega precisão nos desenhos.
A bateria de 10.600 mAh garante até 21 horas de reprodução de vídeos, de acordo com a fabricante, e suporta recarda rápida de até 45 W. Já em termos de longevidade, o sistema operacional promete ser atualizado até o Android 26, e o tablet recebe certificação IP68, garantindo resistência contra água e poeira em eventuais acidentes.
Por fim, o Galaxy Tab S12 Plus suporta modo Samsung DeX sem fio, permitindo o uso da interface como de um desktop para uso profissional, apesar de não vir com teclado na caixa. Lembrando que na oferta com o cupom TABLET1000 no Magazine Luiza, seu preço cai para R$ 8.449,10 no Pix.

articles.title: Kioxia and Dell Build a 157 PB Rack With 640 SSDs
articles.text:
Thursday, November 12th 2026
Kioxia and Dell Build a 157 PB Rack With 640 SSDs
Kioxia and Dell have managed to fit a massive 157 PB of raw flash storage into a single 42U server rack. The configuration runs Dell's software-defined ObjectScale object storage platform on 16 PowerEdge R7725xd servers, which together carry 640 of Kioxia's 245.76 TB LC9 Series SSDs. Kioxia calls it the industry's first 157 PB single-rack object store, a claim it bases on its own market survey. Each 2U server holds 40 of the E3.L drives, the same setup the two companies showed off in May at 9.8 PB per server, so the 16 servers take up 32U and leave 10U of the rack free.
The LC9 drives are PCIe 5.0 NVMe SSDs built on Kioxia's eighth-generation BiCS FLASH QLC with a 32-die stack. The full 245.76 TB capacity is limited to the E3.L form factor, though, since the 2.5-inch and E3.S versions top out at 122.88 TB, which would roughly halve the rack to about 78.6 PB. Dell's George Papadopoulos says customers can "consolidate more data into fewer systems and racks" while cutting down on cabling, power, and cooling.Both companies pitch the rack as more efficient than HDDs or lower-capacity SSDs at the same capacity, but the announcement doesn't include any power or footprint figures to back that up. There's no word on pricing or availability either. Kioxia also isn't alone at this capacity, as Micron started shipping its own 245 TB 6600 ION earlier this year and quotes up to 176.9 PB per rack in E3.L configurations.
Source:
				Kioxia (via Business Wire)

articles.title: Une faute de frappe en cherchant ChatGPT ou Gemini peut vous mener sur un site piégé
articles.text:
Une seule lettre sépare chatlgpt.com de chatgpt.com. La société de cybersécurité Island a recensé 186 adresses de ce genre, et sur certaines d’entre elles, des pirates vous poussent à installer vous-même un logiciel malveillant sur votre ordinateur.
Vous voulez ouvrir ChatGPT, Claude ou Gemini, et vos doigts glissent sur le clavier. C'est le syndrome du Knacki, diront certaines mauvaises langues. Et les pirates comptent sur cette erreur. Ils enregistrent les adresses mal orthographiées des assistants d’IA, ce que les spécialistes appellent du typosquatting, et Island a relevé des imitations de 27 marques d’IA. Avec 25 imitations, ChatGPT est la marque la plus copiée, devant Claude et DeepSeek. Gemini a ses imitations, dont geimini.com, et la française Mistral AI a la sienne, mistrial.ai. En suivant les redirections de ces adresses, les chercheurs d’Island sont tombés sur des malwares et sur des extensions qui détournent vos recherches.
Les pirates vous font exécuter une commande PowerShell
Sur cloude.ai, fausse adresse de Claude, le propriétaire n’a mis en ligne qu’une page d’attente, dite page parking, et il peut revendre le trafic de ses visiteurs. Vous êtes ensuite transféré vers un système de distribution de trafic, chargé de choisir votre destination en fonction de votre pays, de votre système d’exploitation et de votre navigateur. Les pirates profilent alors votre navigateur et relèvent votre adresse IP. Seule une partie des visiteurs voit le piège.
Il s’agit d’une fausse page de vérification humaine aux couleurs de Cloudflare, traduite en six langues, dont le français. Sur Windows, une commande est copiée dans votre presse-papiers, puis les pirates vous demandent de la coller dans la fenêtre Exécuter. Avec cette technique, le ClickFix, c’est vous qui lancez leur programme. Les pirates téléchargent alors un script PowerShell dans un dossier temporaire et l’exécutent dans une fenêtre cachée, sans tenir compte des restrictions d’exécution de Windows. Sur Mac, les pirates affichent plutôt une fausse mise à jour de sécurité et vous demandent de coller une commande dans le Terminal.
Island a retrouvé le script de profilage sur 211 adresses d’entrée, dont de fausses adresses de banques nord-américaines, de l’opérateur Verizon ou de Microsoft Azure. Comme l’explique Oleg Zaytsev, chercheur principal en sécurité chez Island, ces sites sont des « sosies d’applications d’IA qui transforment la tentative d’ouvrir un outil familier en une invitation à vérifier, installer ou exécuter autre chose ». Aucune vraie vérification Cloudflare ne vous demande d’ouvrir la fenêtre Exécuter ou le Terminal pour coller du texte.
Les pirates détournent votre moteur de recherche
Si vous tapez ckaude.ai, deepceek.com ou copiot.com, vous risquez d’atterrir sur une fausse page de contrôle de sécurité. Les pirates vous proposent d’installer Net Guard, qu’ils font passer pour un outil d’analyse de votre Wi-Fi. Le fichier est signé par le Microsoft Store et correspond exactement à l’application publiée sur la boutique de Microsoft. Une fois Net Guard installé, les pirates peuvent changer votre moteur de recherche par défaut pendant que vous n’utilisez pas votre PC et installer des extensions dans Chrome.
Sur preplexity.ai, fausse adresse de Perplexity, les pirates vous invitent à ajouter à Chrome une extension de recherche Bing. En réalité, vos recherches transitent par le serveur d’une société tierce, sans qu’aucune autorisation vous soit demandée à l’installation. Au bureau, ce tiers peut ainsi récupérer les noms de serveurs internes, de clients ou de projets que vous tapez dans la barre d’adresse, prévient Island.
Google prépare pour Chrome une protection contre les extensions qui détournent votre moteur de recherche, mais seulement contre celles imposées à votre insu par des clés de politique locale, un réglage normalement réservé aux administrateurs. Ici, c’est vous qui installez l’extension. Island a recensé 30 extensions issues du même kit, que vous ne trouverez pas en cherchant dans le Chrome Web Store. Treize ont été retirées, et les autres comptaient 972 000 utilisateurs déclarés début novembre.
Pour ouvrir ChatGPT ou Gemini, passez plutôt par un favori ou par l’application officielle. Et si votre moteur de recherche a changé sans raison, ouvrez Paramètres puis Moteur de recherche dans Chrome, avant de passer en revue vos extensions.

articles.title: Citrix Patches 12 NetScaler and Secure Access Client Flaws, Including Authentication Bypass
articles.text:
Citrix has released patches for multiple critical security flaws impacting NetScaler ADC, Citrix NetScaler Gateway, and NetScaler Console that could lead to denial-of-service (DoS) or an authentication bypass.
The critical vulnerabilities that impact NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway are listed below -
- CVE-2026-120868 (CVSS score: 9.3) - A memory overflow vulnerability in Packet Processing can lead to unpredictable or erroneous behavior or DoS. (All NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway deployments)
- CVE-2026-107407 (CVSS score: 9.3) - A memory overflow vulnerability in SMPP traffic can lead to unpredictable or erroneous behavior or DoS. (NetScaler ADC configured with a Load Balancing or Content Switching virtual server of type SMPP)
- CVE-2026-107408 (CVSS score: 9.3) - A memory corruption vulnerability in DNS / DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) can lead to unpredictable or erroneous behavior or DoS. (NetScaler ADC configured for DNS load balancing and recursive DNS resolution)
- CVE-2026-107409 (CVSS score: 9.3) - A memory corruption vulnerability in DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) can lead to unpredictable or erroneous behavior or DoS. (NetScaler configured with DNS Load Balancing over HTTPS)
- CVE-2026-107410 (CVSS score: 9.3) - A memory overflow in NetScaler Push can lead to unpredictable or erroneous behavior or DoS. (NetScaler configured as Load Balancing virtual server of type PUSH)
- CVE-2026-107412 (CVSS score: 9.5) - Multiple memory overflow vulnerabilities can lead to unpredictable or erroneous behavior and DoS. (NetScaler configured as a Gateway or an AAA virtual server)
- CVE-2026-107415 (CVSS score: 9.3) - A memory overflow vulnerability in Email OTP authentication can lead to unpredictable or erroneous behavior or DoS. (NetScaler ADC or NetScaler Gateway configured with an Email Action)
- CVE-2026-111344 (CVSS score: 9.3) - A memory overflow vulnerability in Endpoint Analysis (EPA/EPAS) can lead to unpredictable or erroneous behavior or DoS. (NetScaler configured as a VPN virtual server or an authentication (AAA) virtual server with Endpoint Analysis)
- CVE-2026-120864 (CVSS score: 9.3) - A memory overflow vulnerability in ICA proxy can lead to unpredictable or erroneous behavior or DoS. (NetScaler configured as a Gateway VPN virtual server, an AAA virtual server, or a CR virtual server of type HDX)
All the issues have been patched in the following versions -
- Citrix NetScaler ADC and Citrix NetScaler Gateway 14.1-73.57 and later releases
- Citrix NetScaler ADC and Citrix NetScaler Gateway 13.1-64.39 and later releases of 13.1
- Citrix NetScaler ADC 14.1-FIPS 14.1-73.58 FIPS and later releases of 14.1-FIPS
- Citrix NetScaler ADC 13.1-FIPS and 13.1-NDcPP 13.1-37.293 and later releases of 13.1-FIPS and 13.1-NDcPP
Also addressed by Citrix are a number of flaws in NetScaler Console and Secure Access Client for Windows and Linux -
- CVE-2026-120869 (CVSS score: 9.4) - An improper authentication vulnerability in NetScaler Console can allow an unauthenticated attacker to bypass authentication controls to access restricted resources on the appliance. (Fixed in NetScaler Console 14.1-74.34 and later)
- CVE-2026-118268 (CVSS score: 8.5) - An improper privilege management vulnerability in Secure Access Client for Windows can allow a low-privileged user to escalate privileges to SYSTEM. (Fixed in Secure Access Client for Windows 26.11.1.6 and later)
- CVE-2026-118269 (CVSS score: 8.5) - An improper privilege management vulnerability in Secure Access Client for Linux can allow a low-privileged user to gain root privileges. (Fixed in Secure Access Client for Linux 26.10.4 and later)
The security updates, Citrix said, follow a deeper review of its codebase by integrating artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted code analysis to detect and resolve vulnerabilities with an aim to harden the products before potential threats could materialize.
The company said it's not aware of any exploits for any of the announced vulnerabilities, but urged customers to apply the updates as they are designed to "enhance the security posture of NetScaler."

articles.title: I wasn't expecting these Ninja Black Friday deals so early — Amazon's already slashed prices by up to 57%
articles.text:
I wasn't expecting these Ninja Black Friday deals so early — Amazon's already slashed prices by up to 57%
Save on everything from air fryers and blenders to espresso machines and frozen drinks makers
The Amazon Black Friday sale may as well officially launch now. It's not due to kick off until Tuesday, November 17, but after spotting some excellent discounts on Apple AirPods yesterday, followed by a whole host of Ninja kitchen appliance deals today, I'm not entirely sure what it's waiting for.
Yes, to my surprise, I've spotted discounts of up to 57% on Ninja air fryers, blenders and viral products like the Slushi frozen drinks maker and Swirl ice cream machine — perfectly timed for the approaching Australian summer.
• Browse all the latest Amazon deals
Elsewhere, there are savings to be found on multicookers, the Luxe Café espresso machine and the recently released BlendBoss blender. With Black Friday just around the corner, there's always a chance these discounts could improve, but that's far from guaranteed. So, if you spot something you've had your eye on at a price you're happy with, there's no reason to wait.
• Browse the Ninja storefront at Amazon
The Ninja Slushi lets you skip the ice and still enjoy perfectly smooth icy drinks with very little effort. Whether you're craving a frappe, smoothie, or even a cheeky spiked slushi, its multiple drink modes have you covered. Check out our Ninja Slushi review for the full rundown.
This compact air fryer packs 1700W of power into a portable design, with two borosilicate glassware containers that serve as both frying baskets and serving dishes. The borosilicate means they can also withstand extreme temperatures, making it easy to take your favourite foods from frozen to crispy, and it's safer to use than any non-stick basket.
The larger, 5.7L Crispi Pro is also available with a 20% discount, now AU$318 (was AU$399.99).
Not only will you be able to make single-serve smoothies with this blender, it will also let you prepare larger batches, thanks two two jars. Its headline act, however, is the alert that you'll get if it needs a little extra liquid for the smoothest results.
Now, this popular, space-saving air fryer did drop to an incredibly low AU$179 during the Prime Big Deal Days sale in October, so there's a possibility that could happen again during Black Friday proper. Still, for a talented machine such as this, this is still a price I can recommend. Our reviewer called it ‘the air fryer of my dreams’, thanks to the two drawers stacked on top of each other instead of side by side. Each drawer is relatively small at 4.75L, but it should easily feed 2-3 people, and the performance is exemplary.
Sometimes the standard drawer capacities of air fryers just isn't enough, which is why it's lovely to have one that offers flexibility. This 10L air fryer can be used a single or dual basket appliance, and you can use the divider to change the capacity of the two as needed. It will take up some counter space though as it's a big machine. Also available in white for AU$287.
It's got a cult-like following and two members of our own staff are massive fans. If you love your chilled desserts – ice creams, gelatos, smoothies – but want to control your calorie intake, you really should consider getting the Ninja Creami. This Deluxe edition gets you three containers, which is great value at this price, although it was over AU$50 cheaper in July.
This is another Ninja appliance that dropped slightly lower in price during the most recent Prime Day sale, but a 40% discount is still one to take notice of. Read our review for more info, but you can think of it as the Creami’s upgraded sibling. It handles everything the original model does, then goes further with a built-in soft-serve unit featuring six dedicated programs.
We gave the Ninja BlendBoss 4.5 stars out of 5 in our review, praising it as "a small but mighty blender that makes it easy to blend your favorite smoothies and iced beverages". We liked its powerful operation, small footprint, and the fact that it blends right into a tumbler you can take away. This is its first real discount, because it's a pretty new product. The best price is on the Watermelon Bubblegum colour, but others also get discounts.
If you're keen to get outside and cook this summer, chances are that this deal is for you. This Ninja outdoor pizza oven offers 8 functions, including pizza, max roast, specialty roast and smoker, amongst others, so it’s by no means limited to just pizza.
This 3-in-1 coffee machine brews quality espresso, drip coffee and even fast cold brew using its Barista Assist technology, an integrated grinder and weight-based dosing. There's a lot it can do, and it does it very well. I do, however, reckon this one will drop lower in price during Black Friday proper, as I've seen it drop around AU$200 further during previous sales.
Also available in Cyberspace and Oat Milk for AU$739.

Max is a senior staff writer for TechRadar who covers home entertainment and audio first, NBN second and virtually anything else that falls under the consumer electronics umbrella third. He's also a bit of an ecommerce fiend, particularly when it comes to finding the latest coupon codes for a variety of publications. He has written for TechRadar's sister publication What Hi-Fi? as well as Pocket-lint, and he's also the editor of Australian Hi-Fi and Audio Esoterica magazines. Max also dabbled in the men's lifestyle publication space, but is now firmly rooted in his first passion of technology.

articles.title: Melhor TV de 55 polegadas: 8 modelos para comprar em 2026 • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Melhor TV de 55 polegadas: 8 modelos para comprar em 2026
Encontre a TV de 55" ideal de marcas como LG, TCL e Samsung; lista reúne modelos 4K com recursos avançados de imagem e áudio
TVs de 55 polegadas são ideais para salas médias e quartos grandes. Como é um investimento de longo prazo, a escolha deve alinhar as prioridades de uso ao orçamento disponível.
Quem busca por máxima qualidade de imagem, com cores vivas e preto profundo, encontra as melhores opções em TVs OLED. Já televisores com painel QLED (especialmente as variantes MiniLED) tendem a oferecer melhor custo-benefício e imagem superior a TVs de LED tradicionais.
A seguir, o Tecnoblog apresenta oito modelos de smart TVs de 55 polegadas para comprar em 2026. Confira abaixo televisões da LG, Samsung, Hisense e TCL, e entenda os pontos positivos e negativos de cada uma.
A TCL C6K é um dos destaques da marca e uma ótima pedida para uma TV de 55 polegadas. Esse modelo conta com painel Mini LED com até 512 zonas de iluminação para controle de luz mais preciso, gerando melhor contrastes e pretos mais profundos na comparação com painéis mais simples.
Com sistema operacional Google TV, essa TV tem design ultrafino e tem áudio Onkyo 2.1 Hi-Fi com subwoofer integrado, garantindo maior experiência com graves. A TCL C6K também é compatível com Dolby Atmos, que promete melhor sensação espacial com áudio tridimensional.
Outro destaque da TCL C6K é o suporte à taxa de atualização de até 144 Hz VRR em resolução 4K, o que ajuda em jogos de alto desempenho. O modelo conta com quatro entradas HDMI (sendo duas 2.1), duas portas USB, entrada de rede Ethernet e saída de áudio óptica, bem como suporte a Wi-Fi 5 e Bluetooth 2.1.
A LG OLED C6 é um dos melhores modelos da marca e também uma das melhores escolhas de TV para o ano de 2026. Esse produto se destaca pelo painel de OLED, que entrega cores vibrantes, pretos absolutos e contraste infinito, com qualidade muito superior na comparação com TVs de LED, QLED e Mini LED.
Essa é uma TV ideal para gamers, graças à taxa de atualização nativa de 120 Hz (chegando até 165 Hz em VRR) e suporte ao AMD FreeSync e Nvidia G-Sync. Mas se você não joga, não se preocupe: a LG C6 tem suporte a Dolby Vision, HDR10+ e HLG, tendo a melhor qualidade de imagem para séries e filmes.
Falando do áudio, essa TV tem sistema de som de 2.2 canais e potência total de 40W. São dois alto-falantes convencionais e outros dois subwoofers, que reforçam os graves e dão maior sensação de imersão. A TV é compatível com o padrão Dolby Atmos.
O sistema operacional dessa TV é o webOS, com cinco anos de atualizações garantidas pelo programa LG Re:new. Essa TV tem quatro entradas HDMI, três portas USB, saída de áudio óptica e entrada de rede Ethernet, bem como Wi-Fi 6 e Bluetooth 5.3.
Eu tenho essa TV em casa, e mesmo com o investimento alto não me arrependo nem um segundo pela compra. A qualidade da imagem e som é excelente, muito acima da média de TVs básicas e intermediárias.
A Samsung M75H é uma excelente opção para quem quer uma TV de 55 polegadas com qualidade acima da média das TVs mais básicas sem pagar muito mais caro. Seu principal diferencial é a tecnologia Mini LED, que utiliza emissores menores para iluminação do painel 40 vezes mais precisa, trazendo um melhor contraste e pretos mais profundos.
Essa TV conta com suporte a HDR10+, que melhora o brilho e contraste durante as cenas. A Samsung também destaca a Tecnologia de Cores Puras, que reduz a sensação de desbotamento graças ao aprimoramento de precisão dos pixels. No áudio, essa TV tem dois falantes simples de 10 W + 10 W, sem subwoofer integrado.
O sistema operacional da Samsung M75H é o One UI Tizen, com sete anos de atualizações garantidas e acesso aos principais apps de streaming, jogos em nuvem e integração com dispositivos de casa conectada. Essa TV tem três entradas HDMI, uma porta USB e entrada de rede Ethernet, além de Wi-Fi 5 e Bluetooth 5.3.
A Samsung QN70F é uma smart TV de 55 polegadas que combina a tecnologia QLED com iluminação Mini LED. Na prática, isso permite um controle de iluminação da tela mais preciso, resultando em contraste mais refinado, nível de brilho elevado e melhor reprodução de detalhes em cenas claras e escuras.
Essa TV é equipada com o processador NQ4 AI Gen 2, que utiliza 20 redes neurais para analisar e aprimorar brilho, cores e textura em tempo real e fazer upscaling de imagens em resolução inferior para próximo do 4K. Também há o Modo AI, que ajusta imagem e som de forma automática conforme o tipo de conteúdo exibido.
Com painel nativo de 120 Hz, essa TV também suporta até 144 Hz com a tecnologia VRR e a torna ideal para gamers. O sistema operacional é o One UI Tizen, com sete anos de atualizações garantidas, e a TV tem quatro entradas HDMI, duas USB, saída de áudio óptica e porta Ethernet, além de Wi-Fi 5 e Bluetooth 5.3.
A LG QNED70 foi lançada em 2026 e é uma excelente opção de compra para quem busca uma TV de 55 polegadas da LG que não seja tão básica. Esse modelo se destaca pelo painel QNED com iluminação Mini LED, que utiliza pontos quânticos e LEDs minúsculos que geram cores vibrantes, pretos mais profundos, imagens mais realistas e bom nível de contraste para séries, filmes e esportes.
Equipada com processador AI Alpha 7 Gen9, a LG QNED70 utiliza inteligência artificial para fazer upscaling de imagens com resolução inferior ao 4K. A TV também conta com outros modos de IA, como o Picture Wizard e Sound Wizard, com algoritmo que aprende as preferências de imagem e som. O áudio é básico, com dois falantes de 10 W cada, mas o recurso AI Sound Pro simula o ambiente em 9.1.2.
Outro destaque é o sistema operacional webOS, com cinco anos de atualizações garantidas e compatibilidade com Apple AirPlay e Google Cast. O controle remoto AI Magic permite interagir com a interface como se fosse um mouse. A LG QNED70 tem três entradas HDMI, uma USB e porta de rede Ethernet, bem como Bluetooth 5.3 e Wi-Fi 5.
A Samsung Q7F é uma opção ideal para quem busca uma smart TV para uso cotidiano e não quer chegar aos preços das linhas Neo QLED e OLED da marca. O modelo conta com painel QLED, com pontos quânticos que garantem 100% do volume de cor e certificação Pantone para maior fidelidade cromática.
Equipada com processador AI Q4, a Samsung Q7F faz upscaling de conteúdos com resoluções inferiores com auxílio de inteligência artificial. A fabricante também disponibilizou o recurso Vision AI, que ajusta imagens automaticamente, e o Color Booster Pro que melhora as cores.
O sistema operacional é o One UI Tizen, que conta com sete anos de atualizações garantidas além de integração com Samsung SmartThings, Amazon Alexa e Apple AirPlay. O controle remoto SolarCell não utiliza pilhas e pode ser recarregado via USB-C ou luz ambiente. Falando de portas, essa TV conta com três entradas HDMI, uma USB e entrada Ethernet, além de Wi-Fi 5 e Bluetooth 5.3.
A TCL P7K é uma opção de TV de 55 polegadas com bom custo-benefício. O destaque é o painel QLED, que utiliza pontos quânticos para trazer cores mais vibrantes e realistas em comparação com TVs mais simples. Ela conta com sistema operacional Google TV, com milhares de apps disponíveis para download na Play Store.
Essa TV tem processador AiPQ Engine, que utiliza inteligência artificial para fazer upscaling de imagens de resoluções menores para algo mais próximo do 4K. Essa TV também tem suporte a Dolby Atmos e Dolby Vision, garantindo HDR de qualidade e experiência de áudio mais imersiva.
O painel tem apenas 60 Hz, mas o modo Game Accelerator emula taxa de atualização para até 120 Hz durante as sessões de games. A TCL P7K conta com três entradas HDMI, uma porta USB, entrada Ethernet e saída de áudio óptico, além de suporte a Wi-Fi 5 e Bluetooth 5.4.
A Hisense Q6QV é um modelo acima do básico da marca e é uma interessante opção de TV de 55 polegadas com excelente custo-benefício. Ela conta com painel QLED, que utiliza pontos que entregam cores mais realistas e vibrantes na comparação com TVs mais simples, com painel de LED convencional.
Com processador AiPQ, essa TV utiliza inteligência artificial para melhorar a definição de conteúdos com resoluções inferiores. O chip também habilita outros modos, como o AI Sports Mode, que otimiza imagem e som em transmissões esportivas, bem como o AI Smooth Motion, que reduz borrões em games, esportes e cenas de alta velocidade.
A Hisense também equipou a Q6QV com certificação Dolby Atmos e Dolby Vision, com experiência de brilho e som mais imersivas. Falando sobre áudio, essa TV traz speakers básicos de apenas 10 W + 10 W, sendo indicada a utilização de soundbar ou home theater para uma melhor experiência sonora. O sistema operacional é o Vidaa U9, que tem Google Assistente e Alexa. Essa TV tem três portas HDMI, duas USB, saída de áudio óptica, saída de áudio P2, além de Wi-Fi e Bluetooth.
A TV com melhor custo-benefício dessa lista é a Hisense Q6QV. O modelo é comumente encontrado por menos de R$ 2,5 mil, conta com painel QLED e tem suporte a Dolby Atmos e Dolby Vision, algo que não está presente mesmo em modelos um pouco mais caros.
Dessa lista, a melhor TV pra jogos é a LG OLED C6. Esse modelo tem taxa de atualização nativa de 120 Hz e chega a até 165 Hz no modo VRR, tem tempo de resposta de pixel de apenas 0,1 ms, suporta controles Bluetooth de baixa latência e é compatível com AMD FreeSync e Nvidia G-Sync.
A Hisense Q6QV e Samsung M75H são os modelos com menor gasto energético dessa lista, com consumo máximo de 130 W e classificação A no selo do Inmetro.
Sim, é possível instalar uma TV de 55 polegadas na parede. Observe no manual do fabricante qual o tamanho da furação VESA. É necessário utilizar um suporte de TV para parede, vendido separadamente.
De acordo com a LG, a distância recomendada do sofá para uma TV de 55 polegadas é de 2,3 metros, contados a partir do encosto. Ter uma distância menor pode causar fadiga ocular e exigir movimentação do pescoço para atingir todos os pontos da tela.

articles.title: FBI alerta que hackers de Corea del Norte usaron falsas videollamadas de Zoom para robar USD 400 millones
articles.text:
El FBI informó que hackers del Gobierno de Corea del Norte robaron más de USD 400 millones en criptomonedas en los últimos 18 meses con falsas videollamadas de Zoom, Microsoft Teams y Google Meet, en las que reproducen videos grabados en secreto de conocidos de la víctima.
La oficina federal llama a la maniobra “FaceStealer” (ladrón de rostros). El Departamento de Justicia anunció el mismo día la incautación de la infraestructura en la nube que usaban los atacantes, y el FBI publicó una alerta técnica con el detalle del método. La oficina ya identificó y retuvo más de 900 videos de webcam de víctimas que los hackers habían grabado para usarlos contra otras personas.
Cómo funciona la trampa
Todo empieza con una víctima previa. Los hackers toman su cuenta de Telegram u otra app de mensajes cifrados, leen sus chats y su lista de contactos, y graban su imagen mientras espera que empiece una videollamada. Después escriben a sus contactos, con su nombre, para proponer una reunión.
Los pretextos habituales son “ponerse al día”, “hablar de una colaboración” o “conversar sobre oportunidades de inversión”. Como leen el historial de mensajes, adaptan el texto a las conversaciones anteriores de cada persona, según el FBI.
Poco antes de la cita, el atacante envía un enlace que parece de Zoom o Teams pero lleva a una copia controlada por los hackers, con una dirección web de escritura casi idéntica a la oficial. Al entrar, la víctima ve el video grabado del conocido y, a veces, de otros supuestos participantes.
Luego, quien se hace pasar por el conocido escribe que hay un problema de audio. Le pide hacer clic en una actualización, ejecutar un comando o pegar un código. Ese paso instala el programa malicioso que roba contraseñas, captura la pantalla y abre una puerta de acceso al equipo.
El robo no siempre es inmediato. En varios casos, los hackers esperaron entre meses y más de un año para vaciar las carteras de criptomonedas, a la espera de que el saldo creciera, según la alerta.
Deepfakes y ataques a programadores
El FBI advirtió que los atacantes empezaron a usar inteligencia artificial para fabricar deepfakes (videos falsos hechos con IA) de personas conocidas del mundo cripto, aunque la alerta aclara que el esquema sigue basándose sobre todo en videos reales robados.
Los ataques apuntan también a quienes mantienen programas de código abierto. Según el FBI, en lo que va del año los hackers estuvieron cerca de infectar una biblioteca de JavaScript con decenas de millones de descargas semanales. Una detección rápida frenó el intento.
“Si no puede imaginar un escenario en el que caería en esto, no está pensando con suficiente creatividad”, dijo Patrick Grandy, director a cargo de la oficina del FBI en Los Ángeles.
Qué recomienda el FBI
La alerta pide entrar a las reuniones desde la aplicación oficial con un código de invitación, no desde enlaces, y no encender la cámara hasta ver y oír a quien invitó. También aconseja confirmar la cita por otro canal, no ejecutar comandos para “actualizar” y activar la verificación en dos pasos en Telegram, WhatsApp y Slack.
Quien sospeche que fue víctima debe pasar sus criptomonedas a una billetera nueva, creada en otro dispositivo, y avisar a sus contactos y a su empleador. El FBI pide denunciar el caso en IC3.gov con la palabra clave “FaceStealer”.
El comunicado del Departamento de Justicia informa además que se obtuvo autorización judicial para incautar o inmovilizar más de USD 1.200 millones de lo robado a la plataforma Binance. Según ese texto, militares norcoreanos se llevaron activos por más de USD 6.000 millones alrededor del 29 de octubre, y el Gobierno estadounidense y empresas privadas congelaron más de USD 2.700 millones. El rastreo continúa porque los atacantes siguen lavando fondos.

articles.title: Applied Materials Announces Fourth Quarter and Fiscal Year 2026 Results
articles.text:
Thursday, November 12th 2026
Applied Materials Announces Fourth Quarter and Fiscal Year 2026 Results
Applied Materials, Inc. (NASDAQ: AMAT) today reported results for its fourth quarter and fiscal year ended Oct. 25, 2026.
Fourth Quarter Results
Applied generated record revenue of $10.41 billion. On a GAAP basis, the company reported gross margin of 50.4 percent, record operating income of $3.66 billion or 35.1 percent of revenue, and earnings per share (EPS) of $3.40. On a non-GAAP basis, the company reported gross margin of 50.6 percent, record operating income of $3.68 billion or 35.3 percent of revenue, and record EPS of $4.16. The company generated record cash from operations of $3.30 billion and distributed $2.42 billion to shareholders through $2.00 billion in share repurchases and $421 million in dividends.Fiscal Year Results
Applied generated record revenue of $34.45 billion. On a GAAP basis, the company reported gross margin of 50.0 percent, record operating income of $11.09 billion or 32.2 percent of revenue, and record EPS of $12.62. On a non-GAAP basis, the company reported gross margin of 50.1 percent, record operating income of $11.42 billion or 33.1 percent of revenue, and record EPS of $12.89. The company generated record cash from operations of $8.87 billion and distributed $4.75 billion to shareholders through $3.18 billion in share repurchases and $1.57 billion in dividends.
Gary Dickerson, President and CEO"Applied Materials delivered record results in fiscal 2026, and we are on track to grow our Semiconductor Systems business more than 40 percent in our calendar 2026. AI continues to fuel strong incremental demand for semiconductors and Applied has built the most-enabling portfolio to advance the AI-computing roadmap, putting us in a great position for multi-year revenue and profit growth."
Brice Hill, Senior Vice President and CFO"With technology leadership in the most critical areas of the wafer fab equipment market, Applied Materials increased fiscal fourth quarter revenue by 53 percent year over year and non-GAAP earnings per share by 92 percent. We generated record quarterly free cash flow of $2.6 billion and distributed over $2.4 billion to shareholders, including the largest quarterly share buyback in more than eight years."
Recent Highlights
EPIC Center
- Unveiled the EPIC Center in Silicon Valley, the world's largest facility dedicated to collaborative semiconductor process technology and manufacturing equipment R&D. By bringing chipmakers, equipment partners and university researchers into the same building as Applied's scientists and engineers, EPIC enables parallel rather than sequential development of materials, equipment and process technology, resulting in shorter learning cycles and faster commercialization of the innovations that will power the AI era.
- Announced four new EPIC Center partnerships, bringing the total to 15 announced to date.
  - Intel will join EPIC as a founding partner to accelerate development of chipmaking innovations for next-generation transistors, interconnects and advanced packaging technologies. The collaboration will bring together cutting-edge capabilities from Applied's EPIC Center and Intel's R&D campus in Hillsboro, Oregon to shorten time-to-market of advanced semiconductor technologies essential to AI computing.
  - KIOXIA Corporation will join the EPIC Center as an innovation partner to advance next-generation memory technologies. Applied and KIOXIA will work together at the EPIC Center on advanced memory-cell and structure creation, multi-chip stacking architectures, and new materials engineering approaches designed to increase memory density and performance for the AI era.
  - BE Semiconductor Industries N.V. (Besi) will join the EPIC Center as an innovation partner. This is an expansion of Applied's longstanding strategic partnership with Besi and extends the companies' co-innovation beyond hybrid bonding into new interconnect architectures and applications supporting the semiconductor industry's AI-driven scaling roadmap.
  - The UCLA Samueli School of Engineering will join the EPIC Center as a research partner. Together with Applied's scientists and engineers, UCLA researchers will work to solve semiconductor materials and integration challenges with a focus on shortening the time it takes to bring breakthrough research to commercialization.
New Products and Technologies
- Introduced the VeritySEM 20 metrology system, a next-generation critical dimension scanning electron microscope (CD-SEM). The VeritySEM 20 system is engineered to address the patterning control challenges of high-NA EUV by using advanced eBeam metrology innovations and AI-driven process efficiencies to accurately measure thinner photoresists, support tighter process windows and enable faster recipe creation.
Corporate Initiatives
- Entered into an accelerated share purchase agreement to increase Applied's investment in Besi to approximately 20 percent of Besi's outstanding shares. The share purchase would add to Applied's current investment in Besi, which was initially made in April 2025.
- Hosted an Investor Breakfast Presentation during SEMICON West, where Applied executives presented the company's longer-term growth expectations and outlined how our leadership in materials engineering positions the company to outperform the wafer fab equipment (WFE) market over the coming years.
Business Outlook
Applied's total revenue and non-GAAP diluted EPS for the first quarter of fiscal 2027 are expected to be as follows:Fourth Quarter and Fiscal Year Reportable Segment Information
Effective in the first quarter of fiscal 2026, management moved our 200-millimeter equipment business to Semiconductor Systems. The business was previously included in Applied Global Services. Additionally, effective in the first quarter of fiscal 2026, management began fully allocating corporate support costs to our operating segments. Prior-period numbers have been recast to conform to the current-year presentation. Display operating segment financial results are included in the Other category balances below.

articles.title: La Malaisie cherche à savoir si des puces NVIDIA ont été réexportées illégalement
articles.text:
En Malaisie, Speedmatrix n’avait besoin d’aucun permis pour faire entrer des puces d’IA de NVIDIA dans les centres de données qu’elle loue. Pour les faire sortir du pays, cette filiale de Megaspeed devait en revanche obtenir l’accord du gouvernement, qui vérifie avec les douanes si elle a réexporté une partie de ces puces.
Le feuilleton continue. On vous a raconté comment les services de renseignement américains soupçonnaient Alice Huang d’espionner le patron de NVIDIA pour le compte de Pékin. Cette ancienne dirigeante de Megaspeed, une société singapourienne de centres de données cliente de NVIDIA, a entretenu une liaison avec Jensen Huang, qui a quitté la direction du géant des puces après 33 ans. Le gouvernement américain enquête aussi sur Megaspeed, soupçonnée d’avoir fait passer des puces en Chine malgré les restrictions à l’exportation. Et la Malaisie, où sa filiale Speedmatrix fait tourner ses serveurs, cherche à son tour à savoir si ces puces ont été détournées vers d’autres pays, nous révèle Le Parisien.
La Malaisie exige un permis pour réexporter les puces de NVIDIA
L'affaire remonterait à l'an dernier. Selon le New York Times, Megaspeed a créé une filiale en Malaisie pour acheter près de 2 milliards de dollars de puces NVIDIA. Speedmatrix loue de la place dans des centres de données malaisiens, où elle installe ses serveurs et ses puces d’IA. D’après le quotidien américain, des clients installés en Chine utiliseraient à distance les centres de données de Megaspeed en Malaisie et en Indonésie. Louer ainsi de la puissance de calcul n’est pas forcément illégal, mais Washington veut savoir si l’entreprise a aussi expédié des puces vers la Chine.
Pour faire entrer ces puces sur son sol, la Malaisie ne demande aucun permis, a rappelé le ministère de l’Investissement, du Commerce et de l’Industrie dans un communiqué consacré à Megaspeed et à Speedmatrix. Depuis juillet 2025, en revanche, toute entreprise doit obtenir l’autorisation du ministère pour réexporter ou faire transiter par le pays des puces d’IA américaines haut de gamme. Et si elle donne de fausses informations aux douanes sur ces marchandises, elle commet une « grave infraction », prévient le ministère. Avec les douanes, il cherche donc à savoir si Speedmatrix a ensuite expédié une partie de ses puces vers d’autres pays, et si elle avait l’autorisation de le faire.
Le gouvernement malaisien dément avoir blanchi Speedmatrix
Megaspeed assure que plusieurs inspections, menées par les autorités américaines et malaisiennes et par NVIDIA, n’ont relevé aucune irrégularité dans ses activités. Le ministère malaisien conteste cette version. Ses agents se sont bien rendus dans les centres de données où travaille Speedmatrix, dans le cadre de la surveillance habituelle d’un secteur en pleine expansion, mais le ministère n’a jamais blanchi l’entreprise. « Toute affirmation contraire est inexacte », souligne-t-il.
En début de semaine, Johari Abdul Ghani, ministre de l’Investissement, du Commerce et de l’Industrie, affirmait n’avoir reçu aucune preuve d’une infraction de Speedmatrix à la loi malaisienne, et son ministère n’avait ouvert aucune enquête. Comme l’explique le ministre, « la Malaisie ne se laissera pas utiliser pour contourner les contrôles à l’exportation ». Kuala Lumpur mènera ses vérifications selon sa loi et travaille avec Singapour, où Megaspeed fait l’objet d’une enquête, et avec les États-Unis.
Avant sa démission, Jensen Huang affirmait que NVIDIA avait compté une à une les puces déployées par Megaspeed, sans trouver trace d’un envoi illégal vers la Chine. Mais d’après The Information, dont nous avons relayé l’enquête, le réseau d’Alice Huang aurait permis de faire entrer en Chine environ 240 000 puces NVIDIA, pour 7,5 milliards de dollars.

articles.title: 186 Fake AI Domains Redirect Users to ClickFix Lures, Browser Malware, and Search Hijackers
articles.text:
Cybersecurity researchers have found that lookalike domains masquerading as artificial intelligence (AI) tools are being used to serve ClickFix-style lures, browser-hijacking malware, and a set of extensions that hijack user searches.
This delivery pattern has been codenamed TypoPrompting by Island.
"AI-app lookalikes that turn an attempt to reach a familiar tool into a prompt to verify, install or run something else," the cybersecurity company said in a report shared with The Hacker News.
In all, the campaign spans 186 bogus domains spanning 27 AI brands, including Anthropic Claude, OpenAI ChatGPT, Google Gemini and Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM), Microsoft Copilot, SpaceXAI Grok, DeepSeek, Mistral, Perplexity, Midjourney, ElevenLabs, Lovable, and Cursor.
While one category leads to a ClickFix lure that serves a PowerShell command via a fake Cloudflare verification page, the second route takes unsuspecting users to "Security Check" pages that deliver a browser-hijacking malware called Net Guard. The third pathway sends users to a search-hijack extension family with 16 live Chrome Web Store listings and 972,000 declared users.
Some of the AI lookalike domains are listed below -
- cloude[.]ai
- cluade[.]ai
- clsude[.]ai
- chatlgpt[.]com
- geimini[.]com
- notebookklm[.]com
- griok[.]com
- preplexity[.]ai
- deepceek[.]com
- elevenlebs[.]io
- copiot[.]com
- midj0urney[.]org
An analysis of registration records shows that some of these domains, like cloude[.]ai and cluade[.]ai, were registered as early as July 13, 2023.
The use of parked domains for malware delivery is not new. In December 2025, Infoblox highlighted how domains without a current web page can be monetized to redirect visitors to sites that serve scams and malware after profiling the host and the device they are visiting from.
"When a domain owner opts into direct search, traffic to the domain is sold to advertisers who bid on keywords and traffic characteristics," the DNS threat intelligence firm noted at the time. "In practice, the site visitor is usually funneled through a series of traffic distribution systems (TDSs) operated by third-party advertising platforms, creating a complex web where a legitimate business model is weaponized for abuse."
In the case of the ClickFix route, the parked page initiates a redirect chain that fingerprints the web browser and collects the public IP address before displaying the fake Cloudflare verification page.
Island said the fingerprint gate script spans a broader set of 211 entry domains, including lookalikes of banks, insurers, and enterprise software, such as Scotiabank, Charles Schwab, Blue Cross Blue Shield, Verizon, ServiceNow, and Microsoft Azure.
These domains serve three types of lures -
- Fake verification pages on Windows that are designed to run a clipboard command
- Terminal or security updates on macOS that are designed to run a shell command
- Archive download pages that instruct users to extract and run an executable
Separately, eight typosquat domains for Claude, DeepSeek, Copilot, ElevenLabs, and Voice AI lead to fake "Security Check" pages that ultimately deliver Net Guard.
While the app purports to be a Wi-Fi and DNS safety scanner and matches the MSIX hash for a legitimate app of the same name, it contains capabilities to run attacker-controlled JavaScript, change the default search engine while the user is idle, edit browser profiles, and install arbitrary Chrome extensions.
"The download from the 'Security Check' pages is the Microsoft Store app itself, unmodified," Oleg Zaytsev, Lead Security Researcher at Island, told The Hacker News. "It is byte-for-byte identical to Net Guard as Microsoft distributes it, and it carries Microsoft’s own Store signature."
"The hidden browser control comes with every copy, whether installed from the Store or from a typo site, and it switches itself on without asking. It waits until the user stops using the computer, then takes over Chrome's search settings and can run scripts inside the browser, following instructions from the operator's server."
The third route revolves around a lookalike domain for Perplexity ("preplexity[.]ai"), which redirects the browser to a browser extension called Quick Search that's available on the Chrome Web Store.
"The analyzed extension needs no executable JavaScript or declared permissions to perform its main action," Island said. "Its manifest overrides the default search provider with find.flashysearches[.]com . Searches made through that provider are sent to a third party. In a workplace, those queries can include internal hostnames, customer names and project details."
Quick Search is part of a larger set of 16 extensions, including GPT for Chrome, which has 80,000 users. In all, the extensions collectively have 972,000 users as of November 3, 2026.
"An address one letter away from an AI tool can lead to a very different request," Island said. "As these services become part of everyday work, reaching the right one should be a managed path, not a test of typing accuracy."
(The story was updated after publication to include a response from Island.)

articles.title: Steam ofrece 4 juegos gratis hasta el 16 de noviembre de 2026: cómo acceder a ellos
articles.text:
Steam habilitó cuatro juegos gratuitos por tiempo limitado: Cities: Skylines II, Company of Heroes 3, Deep Rock Galactic: Rogue Core e IL-2 Sturmovik: Battle of Stalingrad.
La promoción permite jugar sin costo a estos títulos hasta el 16 de noviembre de 2026. La oferta es temporal y las páginas de Steam mantienen opciones de compra para quienes quieran conservarlos una vez finalizado el período gratuito.
La selección reúne propuestas de simulación urbana, estrategia militar, acción cooperativa y combate aéreo ambientado en la Segunda Guerra Mundial.
De qué tratan los juegos gratis de Steam
Cities: Skylines II propone construir una ciudad desde cero y administrarla como una metrópolis. El juego incorpora una simulación económica, gestión de recursos, transporte y planificación urbana.
En Company of Heroes 3, los jugadores controlan fuerzas terrestres, aéreas y navales en combates estratégicos. El título incluye campañas ambientadas en el norte de África e Italia, además de modos multijugador y cooperativo.
Deep Rock Galactic: Rogue Core es un juego de acción cooperativa para entre uno y cuatro participantes. Los jugadores exploran minas generadas de forma procedimental, enfrentan criaturas alienígenas y obtienen mejoras durante cada partida.
Por su parte, IL-2 Sturmovik: Battle of Stalingrad es un simulador de vuelo centrado en batallas aéreas de la Segunda Guerra Mundial. Incluye modos para un jugador, combates en línea, cooperación y compatibilidad con realidad virtual.
Cómo acceder a estos nuevos juegos
Para iniciar la descarga, hay que ingresar a Steam y abrir la página de cada título. Allí aparece la opción “Play Game” o “Install”, que permite comenzar la instalación mientras la promoción siga vigente.
Los usuarios deben verificar que la oferta continúe activa antes de descargar los juegos. En el caso de Company of Heroes 3, Steam solicita una verificación de edad debido a que el contenido incluye violencia y sangre.
La promoción finalizará el 16 de noviembre de 2026, por lo que los cuatro títulos deberán instalarse y ejecutarse dentro de ese plazo para aprovechar el acceso gratuito.
Valve Steam Machine, uno de los mejores inventos del 2026
La Valve Steam Machine fue incluida por la revista TIME entre los Mejores Inventos de 2026. El dispositivo, desarrollado por Valve, propone llevar la experiencia de los videojuegos de computadora al televisor o al escritorio con un equipo de tamaño reducido.
La distinción no corresponde a un único ganador general: la publicación seleccionó a la Steam Machine como una de las 300 innovaciones de su lista anual. TIME destacó el equilibrio entre potencia, formato compacto y funcionamiento silencioso de la computadora orientada al entretenimiento.
La Steam Machine tiene forma de cubo y mide seis pulgadas de lado. Valve diseñó el equipo para ejecutar motores gráficos complejos y cargar mundos abiertos, dos exigencias habituales de los videojuegos actuales, sin requerir una computadora de gran tamaño.
El diseño del dispositivo apunta a que pueda ubicarse junto a un televisor, en una sala de estar, o sobre un escritorio. Según TIME, la elección de un formato cúbico permitió incorporar un ventilador de 120 milímetros, encargado de refrigerar el equipo.
La ventilación fue uno de los aspectos resaltados por la revista. El sistema busca mantener fríos el procesador y la tarjeta gráfica de AMD a velocidades inferiores a las habituales en una laptop. De ese modo, la Steam Machine puede reducir el ruido durante las partidas.
La propuesta de Valve se diferencia de una consola tradicional porque se presenta como una computadora preparada para videojuegos. Su objetivo es ofrecer un equipo compacto capaz de procesar títulos exigentes sin perder las prestaciones necesarias para ejecutar gráficos detallados.
La selección de TIME reconoce productos e ideas que, de acuerdo con sus criterios editoriales, aportan soluciones novedosas o mejoran experiencias cotidianas. En el caso de la Steam Machine, la revista puso el foco en la combinación de hardware potente y diseño reducido.

articles.title: The RTX PRO 5500 runs the exact same GB202 configuration as the RTX 5090 that launched at $1,999 — the added 52GB of VRAM costs professionals an eyewatering $16,000 markup
articles.text:
The RTX PRO 5500 runs the exact same GB202 configuration as the RTX 5090 that launched at $1,999 — the added 52GB of VRAM costs professionals an eyewatering $16,000 markup
One launched at $1,999; the other is listed at $17,999
- The RTX PRO 5500 uses the same GB202 configuration as the RTX 5090: 170 SMs and 21,760 CUDA cores
- It is not a complete rebadge, however; it comes with a different board, 84GB of ECC memory, a narrower bus, and pro features
- Leaks and a board partner suggest GB202 is shifting from the 5090 to RTX PRO cards, though Nvidia denies discontinuation
Nvidia insists the GeForce RTX 5090 has not been discontinued, but its GPU keeps turning up elsewhere, with the latest emerging as the RTX PRO 5500, a workstation card that US reseller SHI Government Solutions listed recently at $17,999.
That overlap has fueled claims that Nvidia is simply rebadging its gaming flagship as a pro card to maximize profits while abandoning gamers.
The reality, however, might be more nuanced, and arguably more consequential for anyone still hoping to buy a 5090.
The same chip in a different card with a very different price tag?
On paper, the RTX 5090 and RTX 5500 Pro have almost everything that matters for compute. Both use the GB202 die with 170 of its 192 streaming multiprocessors enabled, giving each 21,760 CUDA cores, 680 Tensor cores, and 96 MB of L2 cache.
It would therefore not be a far cry to suggest that Nvidia essentially took the RTX 5090, slapped on higher-capacity memory, and launched it as the RTX 5500 Pro. There are, however, some differences in the boards around that silicon.
As we reported when the card appeared in September 2026, the RTX PRO 5500 packs 84GB of ECC GDDR7 memory using 28 3GB modules split across both sides of the board, compared to 32GB on the 5090. It runs that memory over a narrower, slower interface, so bandwidth falls to 1,398GB/s from the 5090's 1,792GB/s, a 22% cut.
The GPU is rated for 600W rather than 575W, can be split into two isolated 42GB instances, ships with professional drivers, and is built for rack-mounted workstations with blower or liquid cooling. So one could argue that no 5090 is being pulled off a shelf and relabeled. What the two products share here is the silicon, and it's the scarce part at a time when one can't find an RTX 5090 anywhere close to MSRP on shelves.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Here is the detail that makes the 5500 more than just another workstation card. Of the GB202 products in Tom's Hardware's comparison, only the RTX 5090 and the RTX PRO 5500 use the 170-SM configuration. The RTX PRO 6000 uses a higher bin at 188 SMs, the 6000D uses 156, and the RTX PRO 5000 uses 110. By that measure, the 5500 is the first pro card built to draw on exactly the dies that previously had one main home: the 5090.
The economics of where those dies go are stark: The RTX 5090 launched at $1,999. In October 2026, Reuters reported that ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent had ordered more than three million RTX PRO 5500s at about $11,400 each, while the SHI listing puts its MSRP at $17,999.
The same GPU configuration is worth roughly 5.7 times its gaming launch price in a Chinese bulk order, and about nine times at that US list price. An extra 52GB of GDDR7 memory is not cheap in the current memory market, but it does not come anywhere close to explaining a gap of that size. Nvidia therefore earns substantially more profit per die in a 5500 than in a 5090, making it a no-brainer to supply the former rather than the latter.
Demand also sharpens the trade-off: Reuters' sources said total Chinese orders for the export-compliant card had passed six million, while Nvidia could make no more than three million of them in 2027. If those figures are close, Nvidia has more buyers for the 5500 than it can supply, which leaves little commercial reason to send a 170-SM die anywhere else, resulting in the RTX 5090 shortage we see worldwide.
Not discontinued, just not available?
The idea that GB202 is being reassigned did not start with the 5500's price tag. On October 10 2-26, leaker MEGAsizeGPU claimed that "all future GB202 supplies are RTX Pro exclusive," while a second account, hongxing2020, shared what it described as a factory notice saying Nvidia would stop making every RTX 5090 model, including China's D variants, as TweakTown reported.
Two days later, Darren Allan at TechRadar predicted that any end would not be announced. Instead, Nvidia would allocate so few chips that "stock will effectively dwindle to next to nothing."
Nvidia's response, when it came, was carefully worded. Speaking in Taipei on October 16, SVP Jeff Fisher said that "although the RTX 5090 has other variants, it has definitely not been discontinued." He acknowledged that supply was constrained, but neither he nor Nvidia has said how GB202 output is divided between the 5090 and the other products built on the same chip.
A denial of discontinuation is not a denial of reallocation, however, but the proof continued to pile on: Ten days later, German overclocker der8auer reported that an unnamed Nvidia board partner, while never told the 5090 was end-of-life, could no longer order the GB202 and 32GB memory kit it needs to build one, nor place backorders as it had during earlier shortages, according to Wccftech.
A cooler supplier also told him that two partners had cut RTX 5090 cooler orders for the first quarter of 2027 and placed none for the second. Those accounts are anonymous and secondhand, but they fit a pattern in which the 5090 is never formally discontinued, just starved.
Anyone looking for a literal rebadge should look at China's gray market. In late October, Hong Kong outlet HKEPC shared a video, covered by Wccftech, that appears to show hundreds of retail RTX 5090s in a Chinese facility, where technicians strip the GPU and memory from each card and move them onto custom boards with dual-slot blower coolers for AI servers. HKEPC was also the source of September's photos of 5090s stacked on pallets, which TechRadar Pro reported may have been AI-generated, so the footage deserves some caution.
In September, Chinese manufacturer Suqiao also listed a modified 96GB RTX 5090 on Alibaba for $3,888, according to Tom's Hardware, though the listing's own memory specifications did not fully add up. Third parties, in other words, are already turning gaming cards into high-memory AI cards for a fraction of what Nvidia charges for its official equivalent.
Nvidia does not need to rebadge the RTX 5090. The RTX PRO 5500 lets it sell the same GPU configuration at several times the price into a market with more demand than supply, without ever announcing that its gaming flagship is gone. Interestingly, its product page still lists the 5500 as coming soon, with no official price.
Until Nvidia says how it is dividing GB202 between gamers and workstation buyers, "not discontinued" and "not available" can both be true at once. For gamers, that distinction is unlikely to matter much.

Rahim Amir is a UAE-based tech writer who enjoys building PCs as much as he enjoys writing about them. He has been professionally writing about PC hardware since 2023, focusing on buyer’s guides, hardware reviews, and sponsored content and features related to tech.
Having built hundreds of gaming PCs and being an avid gamer in his spare time, Rahim tends to have stronger opinions about hardware than most. This is particularly on display when he gets his way with powerful, but minimalistic RGB builds even as Small Form Factor (SFF) PCs come a close second.
