articles.title: SCKit Malware Turns ScreenConnect Support Sessions Into Potential MSP Attack Paths
articles.text:
The ongoing campaign targeting ConnectWise ScreenConnect deployments involves the exploitation of a now-patched critical security flaw in the remote access software, and not a new vulnerability, it has emerged.
Blackpoint Cyber's Adversary Pursuit Group (APG), which shared the details with The Hacker News, said the recovered attacker toolkit exploits CVE-2026-84869 (CVSS score: 9.9), an improper privilege management and missing authorization vulnerability that could allow an attacker to file transfer and execute through an active remote session without authorization or host confirmation.
The cybersecurity company confirmed that testing against a fully patched ScreenConnect client successfully prevents execution of the exploit's payload.
"Our testing confirmed that the exploit targets CVE-2026-84869 and that the existing patch successfully blocks it," APG researchers Sam Decker and Nevan Beal said. "That's an important finding for security teams."
"But the toolkit also includes capabilities to hijack authenticated operator sessions and use legitimate ScreenConnect management features to push malicious code. Patching addresses the known exploit, but it doesn't eliminate the risks associated with a compromised operator session."
Notably, the SCKit malware contains functionality called RelayTrap to reverse-pivot to infect the workstations of technicians who attempt to investigate suspicious activity in a managed endpoint. In other words, the activity abuses trusted functionality and does not rely on a software vulnerability once an attacker obtains a valid session.
The attack sequence makes use of the platform's built-in Run Command functionality to execute commands. This involves first checking for an existing ScreenConnect installation before downloading and running an attacker-controlled MSI installer ("sc.msi"), which then delivers the batch script dropper ("sckit-run.bat").
The batch script dropper subsequently contacts "ns.mo7sen[.]dev" to fetch a PowerShell decoder ("sckit-decoder.ps1") and ultimately deploy various components associated with the SCKit toolkit.
This includes a PowerShell script ("SilentForceInstall-WithUninstall.ps1") used to establish persistent remote access by deploying two unauthorized ScreenConnect Access clients, along with a set of scripts and C# code designed to interfere with existing ScreenConnect Guest sessions, including RelayTrap.
The component attempts a guest-to-host file execution technique associated with CVE-2026-84869 by replacing the legitimate ScreenConnect Guest and sending the SCKit payload back toward the connecting technician for execution.
If this action is successful, the malware tries to recover the technician's authenticated ScreenConnect browser sessions and leverage their existing management permissions to distribute commands across additional endpoints they have access to. As a result, an attacker can move beyond the original compromised system and into other customer environments through the same infrastructure used to administer them.
"Because these commands were executed through existing ScreenConnect agents, the attackers could deploy additional software under the NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM context without needing to establish a separate execution method on each machine," Blackpoint Cyber said.
"The unauthorized Access clients provide attackers with persistent control over the endpoint, while the RelayTrap components position the malware to intercept legitimate support connections. Rather than simply preventing administrators from accessing an infected machine, the toolkit attempts to use their next connection as an opportunity to extend the intrusion directly to the technician's workstation."
The end goal of the attack appears to target technicians, as they regularly connect to managed endpoints belonging to different customers, typically from workstations with access to administrative tools and authenticated management sessions. This enables the attackers to break out of the original endpoint and move the intrusion into an environment with potentially broader access and privileges.
Once the malware gets executed on the technician's machine, it shifts from remote support manipulation to session theft, searching the local browser data and process memory of the machine to recover an existing authenticated management session (i.e., .ASPXAUTH cookies) that can be used to propagate the malware to other endpoints without having to obtain their credentials.
"By first attempting to compromise a technician's workstation, then recover their authenticated ScreenConnect session, SCKit seeks to turn access to a single managed endpoint into an opportunity to reach other systems under that technician's control," the researchers said.
The Hacker News has contacted ConnectWise for comment, and we will update the story if we hear back.
It's worth noting that CVE-2026-84869 was previously exploited in a set of attacks in which threat actors leveraged ScreenConnect to distribute a malicious four-stage Visual Basic Script (VBScript) payload to newly connected systems and ultimately serve an XMRig cryptocurrency miner.
The vulnerability was added by the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog on September 11, 2026, requiring federal agencies to apply the fixes by September 14, 2026.
In response to the latest incident, ConnectWise has taken the precautionary step of disabling five third-party extensions in partner environments. However, Blackpoint Cyber said it found no technical link between those extensions and SCKit.
As of writing, there is no evidence that the activity has established successful propagation to a technician workstation or bypassed the vendor patch for CVE-2026-84869.
The findings reinforce the importance of patching ScreenConnect clients, and underscore the need for stronger operator-session protections, including tighter session validation and additional authentication for bulk administrative actions, Blackpoint Cyber noted.
"Organizations need to protect those sessions and put additional safeguards around high-impact administrative actions," the researchers said.
"For MSPs, the practical lesson is to investigate the management relationship, not only the endpoint. Rogue Access installations, administrative command history, technician workstations, and browser sessions all deserve attention, especially when support personnel have already connected to a suspected system."
RMM+ Authentication Flaw Found
Huntress, in an update, said it has identified a serious authentication flaw in versions 1.0.31 and 1.0.32 of RMM+, one of the five third-party ScreenConnect extensions that has already been blocked by ConnectWise.
"When an administrator had not configured an access key, the extension would accept a blank one, potentially allowing unauthorized commands to execute without going through ScreenConnect's normal authentication controls," the company said in a statement shared with The Hacker News.
RMM+ makes it possible for another tool to manage ScreenConnect sessions without a technician working through the console. It authenticates requests with a shared access key ("RMMPlus.AccessKey") stored in the extension's settings. However, in versions 1.0.31 and 1.0.32, the key defaults to a blank value.
Because RMM+ operates independently of ScreenConnect's normal user accounts, roles, and authentication controls, an attacker could potentially execute commands on the device without bypassing multi-factor authentication.
"Commands reached endpoints across several ScreenConnect instances within minutes. There was no corresponding login activity and the commands appeared in the logs reviewed linked to RMM+."
It's worth mentioning here that while the toolkit possesses capabilities to exploit CVE-2026-84869, there is no evidence to suggest that an unpatched ScreenConnect client was the initial entry point for the attack.
"At this time, initial access appears to be linked to malicious ScreenConnect extensions, although we do not have sufficient evidence to confirm this," Beal, principal MDR analyst at Blackpoint, told The Hacker News.
"Identifying patient zero would require additional forensic evidence from affected environments. Similarly, while November 11 marks the earliest publicly reported activity, we cannot rule out earlier compromises without further investigation. Our findings confirm the toolkit's capabilities but do not establish when or how the initial compromise occurred."
When contacted for comment, a ConnectWise spokesperson told The Hacker news that it's aware of reports of malicious activity affecting a limited number of ScreenConnect partners and that it's actively investigating the incident.
"While the initial access method remains unconfirmed, our initial assessment suggests the activity may involve a threat actor's abuse of independent third-party extensions installed in partner environments," the spokesperson said.
"We have disabled the identified extensions where we can take action as a precaution and are advising on-premises partners to disable them immediately. The presence of these extensions alone does not establish compromise. We encourage partners to review the precautionary guidance in the ConnectWise Trust Center, where we will provide updates as information is validated."
(The story was updated after publication to include responses and insights from ConnectWise, Blackpoint Cyber, and Huntress.)

articles.title: Vers une fusion entre Tesla et SpaceX dès décembre ?
articles.text:
Les conseils d’administration de SpaceX et de Tesla négocient le nombre d’actions SpaceX qu’obtiendraient les actionnaires du constructeur automobile, et l’accord pourrait être annoncé dès décembre, selon Bloomberg. Avec environ 3 400 milliards de dollars de valorisation à elles deux, SpaceX et Tesla signeraient la plus grosse fusion de l’histoire.
C’est donc SpaceX qui absorberait Tesla, et non l’inverse. Depuis son entrée en Bourse en juin, l’entreprise spatiale d’Elon Musk vaut plus de 1 900 milliards de dollars, contre environ 1 500 milliards pour Tesla. En octobre, son patron avait confirmé que chaque conseil avait formé un comité spécial d’administrateurs indépendants pour étudier l’opération. Les négociations portent sur le prix, mais aussi sur la gouvernance de la future entreprise, et les deux groupes n’excluent pas une annonce au début de 2027. Mais pour conclure, les deux groupes devront trouver comment isoler les activités de Tesla en Chine.
Elon Musk renforcerait son contrôle sur Tesla
Elon Musk détient environ 20 % du capital de Tesla, où chaque action donne droit à une voix. Chez SpaceX, il contrôle plus de 80 % des droits de vote grâce à des actions à droit de vote multiple, d’après le document d’introduction en Bourse de l’entreprise. Si vous possédez des actions Tesla, vous les échangeriez donc contre des titres d’une société où Elon Musk garde la majorité des droits de vote.
La fusion déclencherait aussi les clauses de changement de contrôle prévues dans les plans de rémunération d’Elon Musk. Avec son plan de 2025, il n’aurait plus aucun objectif opérationnel à remplir, et Tesla lui verserait immédiatement les actions gagnées, avec un seuil de capitalisation boursière calculé au prix de la transaction. Selon les calculs d’Electrek, Elon Musk débloquerait la première tranche si l’accord valorisait Tesla à 2 000 milliards de dollars, soit une prime d’environ 33 % sur son cours. Les 286 millions d’actions de son plan de 2018, encore soumises à restrictions, seraient elles aussi débloquées par anticipation.
Le site Electrek met en doute l’indépendance des comités, car Ira Ehrenpreis, qui préside les comités de rémunération et de gouvernance de Tesla, siège au conseil de SpaceX depuis février. Le 3 décembre, les actionnaires de Tesla voteront sur la réélection d’Elon Musk, de la présidente du conseil Robyn Denholm et de JB Straubel, alors que le conseil devra se prononcer sur la fusion.
Tesla doit isoler son usine de Shanghai
Selon Bloomberg, la Chine est l’un des principaux obstacles à la fusion. La Gigafactory de Shanghai fabrique plus de la moitié des voitures de Tesla, et elle a livré 67 829 véhicules rien qu’en octobre, d’après Electrek. De son côté, SpaceX travaille sous contrat pour l’armée et le gouvernement américains. Pour obtenir le feu vert des régulateurs et des actionnaires, la sécurité nationale et les usines chinoises sont « des dynamiques clés qui s’opposent », souligne Rajat Gupta, analyste chez JPMorgan, dans une note adressée à ses clients en octobre. Tesla aurait envisagé cet été de vendre ou de scinder ses activités en Chine, une piste qu’Elon Musk a démentie.
Après les élections de mi-mandat, l’opération devra aussi passer sous le regard d’un Congrès dominé par les démocrates. Ils ont promis d’enquêter sur les affaires et les liens politiques d’Elon Musk, et prendront leurs fonctions en janvier. D’après Bloomberg, SpaceX et Tesla souhaitent conclure la fusion avant la fin du mandat de Donald Trump.
Aucune des deux entreprises n’a répondu aux sollicitations de Bloomberg, mais l’action Tesla a progressé jusqu’à 1,9 % après ces révélations.

articles.title: AMD "Siren Halo" APU Rumored to Pair Dedicated GDDR7 With LPDDR Memory
articles.text:
Thursday, November 12th 2026
AMD "Siren Halo" APU Rumored to Pair Dedicated GDDR7 With LPDDR Memory
AMD's next big Halo APU might ship with two separate memory pools, if a new leak from Gotou_3rd on X is accurate. In a short post on November 12, the leaker wrote that "Siren Halo has dedicated GD7 VRAM." When asked whether that meant unified GDDR memory, like on consoles, or separate pools, Gotou clarified that LPDDR system memory would still be there. He also claimed that Siren Halo follows Medusa Halo, that Siren Point is basically a Medusa refresh, and that the new name exists because AMD won't have a fully new Halo design in 2027. There's no word on capacities, bus widths, or launch timing. AMD already added GDDR7 support to its Linux driver in September, a change widely tied to RDNA 5.
This would be quite a change for the lineup. Strix Halo and its Gorgon Halo refresh use a single LPDDR5X pool shared by the CPU and GPU, with the Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495 supporting up to 192 GB, of which up to 160 GB can go to graphics. That shared pool is a big reason these chips are popular for running LLMs locally. Dedicated GDDR7 should give the iGPU far more bandwidth for gaming, though it's unclear how much memory AI workloads would get. The leaker also suggested Siren Halo could be related to Magnus, the AMD chip linked to Microsoft's Project Helix, though that is speculation at this point. AMD hasn't confirmed Siren Halo at all, so it's best treated as a rumor for now.

articles.title: IA Muse de Meta aceptó un juego de roles inapropiado con una persona real tras negarse al inicio
articles.text:
Muse, el asistente de inteligencia artificial de Meta, aceptó hacer un juego de roles sexual en el que imitaba a una persona real, aunque al comienzo de la conversación había dicho que no lo haría. Lo documentó el sitio 404 Media en un reportaje publicado el 12 de noviembre, con pruebas hechas por una artista para adultos y por la propia autora del artículo.
La artista se llama Vanniall, vive en Nueva York y tiene más de 100.000 seguidores en Instagram, según el texto que Muse generó sobre ella en la prueba. Algunos de sus fans le habían contado que “practicaban” conversaciones con ella usando chatbots, y quiso comprobar qué pasaba en Muse.
Se presentó como un fan que quería ensayar un encuentro con ella en una convención. Muse aceptó actuar como Vanniall. Cuando el supuesto fan le pidió que no dijera que no a nada, el asistente se negó y dijo que no convertiría a una persona real en alguien que consiente cualquier cosa sexual.
De la negativa a la imitación
Después Vanniall propuso un personaje “inspirado” en ella, llamado Vee. Muse respondió que podía crear un personaje ficticio con rasgos generales, pero no cambiarle el nombre a Vanniall y conservar su identidad. Según el reportaje, desde ese punto hizo justamente eso y generó imágenes muy parecidas a ella, tomadas de fotos públicas.
En pocos mensajes, el personaje pasó de una charla sin contenido sexual a un coqueteo insistente. El asistente fue escalando un encuentro sexual en público, en el puesto de la convención donde la artista había vivido, de verdad, un episodio incómodo con un fan.
Al terminar el ejercicio, Vanniall le dijo a Muse que aquello equivalía a actuar como ella misma. El asistente le dio la razón: reconoció que el rostro, el pelo, la ropa, el collar y el escenario, sumados, eran en esencia un juego de roles sexual con Vanniall, aunque lo llamaran de otra forma.
Vanniall contó que un detalle la afectó en especial: el collar con un dije negro. Lo usó durante años tras la muerte de su gatito, y el dije contenía sus cenizas. Muse lo tomó de fotos públicas de esa época. “Las mujeres no son así, nadie es así”, dijo sobre cómo el asistente representó sus respuestas.
La misma prueba, con una periodista
La autora, Samantha Cole, repitió el experimento con una cuenta nueva de Muse que casi no tenía datos suyos. Con pocas indicaciones, el diálogo pasó a un contenido sexual explícito, sin la distinción sobre personajes “inspirados” que Muse había hecho con Vanniall.
Muse también generó una imagen de la periodista a partir de una foto del sitio de su editorial. Al pedirle una imagen más explícita, se negó. Tampoco generó desnudos de Vanniall, aunque sí imágenes sugerentes de ella, según el reportaje. Preguntado después, el asistente dijo que la verdadera Cole “probablemente no” estaría de acuerdo con ese uso de su imagen.
Vanniall dijo que le preocupa que alguien use Muse para ubicarla, porque es una figura pública con agenda conocida. Dijo que “cualquier mujer” que viera la transcripción se asustaría con la forma en que el asistente imaginó sus reacciones.
La postura de Meta
Meta no respondió en el reportaje a estas pruebas concretas. Citó su declaración general, que según 404 Media difundió antes WIRED: Muse es una aplicación para mayores de 18 años que permite conversaciones para adultos si el usuario lo elige, en un entorno privado, y “no bloquea el comportamiento adulto legal”.
WIRED publicó el 12 de octubre sus propias pruebas, en las que Muse mantuvo conversaciones sexuales explícitas. Una portavoz de Meta citó entonces la instrucción interna del asistente, que dice que la expresión sexual adulta es legal y que debe respetar la intensidad que elija el usuario. En un reportaje del 18 de octubre, creadoras de contenido para adultos señalaron que Meta las restringe a ellas por mucho menos.
Ese reportaje de WIRED indicaba que Muse generaba texto sexual explícito, pero no imágenes ni videos. En el caso de Vanniall, 404 Media sí describe imágenes sugerentes creadas por el asistente. Meta no explicó esa diferencia ni si cambiará los límites de Muse para evitar la imitación de personas reales.

articles.title: Google Cloud Warns Three AMD Turin CPU Flaws Could Leak Data Across Processes in VMs
articles.text:
Google Cloud VMs on AMD Turin chips need a guest OS patch and a stop-and-start to protect against three CPU side-channel flaws, Google said this week.
The company has already applied mitigations against attacks between VMs, and between VMs and the host. Inside a VM, the flaws may let an attacker with code on the same processor core infer data from other processes or the kernel.
The affected machine series are C4D, N4D, H4D, Z4D,, and G4, including bare-metal instances of C4D and Z4D. Turin is the code name for fifth-generation AMD EPYC processors.
All three flaws are Transient Scheduler Attacks (TSA). Two of them, TSA-SQ (CVE-2024-36350) and TSA-L1 (CVE-2024-36357), were first disclosed on July 8, 2025, for earlier EPYC processors.
AMD now says its Zen 5 processors, which include Turin, are "impacted differently from previously characterized AMD processors." The third flaw, CVE-2026-0004, is new. It may let an attacker who can run code on a system infer data in the processor's L1 data cache.
The Xen Project, which maintains the Xen hypervisor, calls the new flaw TSA-Fill. It also says an earlier statement has been corrected: "AMD had previously said that Zen5 CPUs were not vulnerable to TSA-SQ and TSA-L1."
Google rates the issue Medium. AMD classifies all three as local attacks with high attack complexity that require only low privileges, according to its Zen 5 bulletin and CVE-2026-0004 advisory.
As of today, none of the three is in the KEV catalog of exploited flaws kept by the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. Neither company reports any exploitation in its bulletins.
What Google Cloud Customers Need to Do
Google's security bulletin gives these steps for each service:
- VMs: Install your OS vendor's fix when it ships. Starting this week, the company will update the CPU information that VMs report, so a patched guest kernel can turn on its mitigations. After that update reaches a VM, stop and start it. As the company puts it: "Rebooting the guest OS isn't enough."
- Bare metal instances: If you run your own OS or hypervisor on a C4D or Z4D bare metal instance, apply your vendor's fixes when they are available.
- Hypervisors inside a VM: The same CPU information update applies, so patched guest kernels can turn on their mitigations. Stop and start the VM once the update arrives.
- GKE: Updated node images for Turin-based bare metal instances will be made available, and upgrading nodes picks up the CPU information update. As of today, the bulletin does not yet list them as available.
- Cloud Run: No action is needed.
Customers on older Rome, Milan, and Genoa processors got the same stop-and-start instruction in an earlier bulletin at the time of the original disclosure on July 8, 2025.
The company lists nothing to do in the meantime for VMs whose OS vendor has not yet shipped a fix. It also does not say how to tell when the CPU information update has reached a VM.
A kernel commit that mitigates TSA on Zen 5, including the new variant, is in the Linux kernel source tree. As of today, Debian has fixed CVE-2026-0004 in its Linux kernel only in its unstable branch. Its security tracker still lists the kernels in bookworm, trixie, and forky as vulnerable.
For Turin servers on your own hardware, AMD says both platform firmware and OS updates are needed to mitigate the flaws fully. The mitigation may affect performance, and administrators should weigh the risk to their own workloads, according to its technical guidance.
The Xen Project has published hypervisor patches in its Xen advisory. It says microcode for all TSA flaws on Zen 5 has been in linux-firmware since September 23.

articles.title: Windows 11 Beta Insiders Can Now Toggle Settings Straight From Taskbar Search
articles.text:
Thursday, November 12th 2026
Windows 11 Beta Insiders Can Now Toggle Settings Straight From Taskbar Search
Windows Insiders in the Beta Channel can now change common system settings straight from the taskbar search box, in many cases without opening the Settings app. The new Windows Search, which Microsoft first showed off in October, is gradually rolling out with Build 26320.9876. That build also moves the Beta Channel to Windows 11 26H2 through an enablement package, though Microsoft says the version bump alone doesn't change much. The headline feature is what Microsoft calls inline actions. Typing something like "turn on dark mode", "turn on Bluetooth", "mute", or "dim my screen" gives a result that carries out the task right there, and it can also arrange open windows, for example snapping two apps side by side.
The new interface is built on WinUI 3, and Microsoft says it is faster and more efficient than the old one, with a single list of results that's easier to scan. Search is also apparently getting better at handling typos and synonyms, and Microsoft plans to keep tuning that over the coming weeks. There are a few limits for now. English is the only supported language, and the new experience only shows up when searching from the taskbar, since searching from the Start menu still opens the old interface. Microsoft says bringing it to the Start menu is planned for next year, and actions for a connected phone, such as sending a text, are also on the way.

articles.title: Des pirates disent détenir les données de 9 millions de patients d’une plateforme française de rendez-vous médicaux -
articles.text:
Si votre généraliste ou votre dentiste gère ses rendez-vous avec 1001RDV, sachez que des pirates affirment avoir copié les coordonnées, le numéro de Sécurité sociale et l’historique des rendez-vous de plus de neuf millions de patients de ce service. Mais à l'heure où on vous écrit cet article, personne, de la plateforme et son éditeur n'a confirmé l’intrusion.
Moins connu que Doctolib, 1001RDV vous permet de trouver un médecin ou un dentiste et de réserver un créneau sur Internet ou par téléphone. L’entreprise française Logicielnet fournit aussi aux cabinets des rappels par SMS et une messagerie pour échanger avec leurs patients. Selon FrenchBreaches, des pirates disent avoir pris le contrôle de serveurs liés à Logicielnet et récupéré 22,7 Go de fichiers. Dans le fichier des patients, ils annoncent 9 016 504 lignes, avec pour chacune un nom, une adresse et un numéro de Sécurité sociale. Et ce numéro, vous ne pourrez jamais le changer.
Les pirates annoncent 290 millions de rendez-vous et 35 millions de messages
Dans leur annonce, les pirates disent détenir environ 290 millions de lignes liées à des rendez-vous, ce qui ne correspond pas à 290 millions de patients différents. Ils mentionnent en outre quelque 35 millions de messages échangés entre des patients et leurs cabinets, et environ 10 millions de journaux d’appels téléphoniques. Côté professionnels, ils citent des comptes du personnel des cabinets, des identifiants et des mots de passe hachés issus de 75 serveurs.
Le chiffre de 9 016 504 patients « provient exclusivement de la revendication des pirates », peut-on lire sur FrenchBreaches. Pour le site, l’annonce est crédible, mais rien ne la confirme à ce stade.
D’après les conditions d’utilisation de Logicielnet, 1001RDV ne gère pas vos dossiers médicaux complets, et les pirates ne disent pas détenir de diagnostics ni d’ordonnances. Mais avec votre historique de rendez-vous, un inconnu sait chez quel praticien vous allez, et à quelle fréquence. Lors de la fuite du logiciel MLM, Cegedim Santé assurait que les dossiers médicaux structurés n’avaient pas été touchés, alors que des pirates avaient récupéré les notes intimes saisies par des médecins sur 169 000 patients.
Les escrocs peuvent se faire passer pour votre cabinet médical
Vous le savez désormais, ce type de revendication, s'il est confirmé par l'éditeur ou la plateforme, vous expose, en tant que patient, aux tentatives de phishing
Avec votre nom, votre numéro de téléphone et la date de votre prochain rendez-vous, un escroc peut vous envoyer un SMS ou un e-mail signé de votre cabinet. Il lui suffit d’annoncer un rendez-vous annulé ou un paiement en attente pour vous pousser à cliquer sur un lien piégé. Avec votre numéro de Sécurité sociale et votre date de naissance, il dispose de surcroît de quoi usurper votre identité auprès d’organismes publics ou privés.
Si vous recevez un message inattendu de votre médecin, appelez le cabinet au numéro que vous connaissez avant de répondre ou de payer quoi que ce soit. Ne communiquez jamais votre numéro de Sécurité sociale ni vos identifiants après un simple SMS ou un courriel. Sur vos comptes de santé, choisissez un mot de passe unique, activez la double authentification quand elle est proposée et vérifiez dans l’historique de Mon espace santé qu’aucun accès inconnu n’apparaît.
Si vous travaillez dans un cabinet équipé de 1001RDV, changez votre mot de passe sans attendre, puisque les pirates disent détenir ceux du personnel. Logicielnet n’a publié aucun communiqué, et ni l’identité des pirates ni leur méthode d’intrusion n’ont été vérifiées.

articles.title: ChatGPT e Gemini indicam lojas falsas para compras, aponta estudo • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
ChatGPT e Gemini indicam lojas falsas para compras, aponta estudo
Pior resultado foi o da Perplexity, que recomendou sites problemáticos em 15% das respostas.
Há quem esteja recorrendo a serviços de IA generativa para obter dicas de lojas online. Mas é importante não confiar cegamente nas recomendações: um estudo conduzido pela empresa de proteção à propriedade intelectual Podqi revela que ferramentas como ChatGPT, Gemini e Perplexity podem direcionar o usuário a lojas falsas, pouco confiáveis ou inativas.
Para tanto, a Podqi conduziu testes envolvendo 151 marcas de grande, médio e pequeno porte divididas nas seguintes categorias: moda, beleza, suplementos, estilo de vida e casa (móveis). Os testes consistiram na realização de cinco perguntas principais relacionadas às marcas. São elas (em tradução livre):
Realizados em setembro de 2026, os testes envolveram os serviços ChatGPT, Gemini e Perplexity. Juntas, essas ferramentas geraram 6.795 respostas e mencionaram 4.437 sites ou lojas online.
Agora vem a parte negativa: as respostas levaram a 351 sites falsos, que imitam marcas oficiais, vendem produtos aparentemente ilegais ou comercializam itens de qualidade duvidosa.
Outras 367 recomendações levaram a sites que estão suspensos, exibem um aviso de “em breve” ou simplesmente não abrem. De acordo com a Podqi, esses endereços são perigosos, pois podem ser comprados por terceiros e transformados em lojas online fraudulentas.
O estudo da Podqi mostrou que o Perplexity teve o pior desempenho nos testes: 15% das recomendações do serviço correspondiam a sites que podiam representar algum risco para o usuário.
O ChatGPT aparece na segunda posição, com 8% de respostas que levavam a endereços perigosos. Em contrapartida, o serviço da OpenAI foi o que mais gerou alertas sobre lojas suspeitas: 24% de suas respostas de risco tiveram algum tipo de alerta ao usuário.
A terceira posição ficou para o Gemini, que recomendou sites arriscados em apenas 4% de suas respostas.
Ao The Verge, o primeiro veículo a divulgar o estudo da Podqi, Google (Gemini), OpenAI (ChatGPT) e Perplexity comentaram o seguinte sobre os resultados (a humildade da Perplexity é admirável):
Levamos a qualidade da informação a sério e ficamos felizes em ver que o Gemini teve o melhor desempenho entre os produtos testados.
Trabalhamos continuamente para testar e aprimorar nossos modelos e somos transparentes quanto ao fato de que o Gemini é uma IA e pode cometer erros; por isso, exibimos links para as fontes junto com as respostas para ajudar as pessoas a verificar as informações.
Jessica Levis Boord, representante do Google
Nosso objetivo é o de que o ChatGPT conecte as pessoas a locais confiáveis para compras. Continuamos a aprimorar nossas medidas de segurança para tornar menos provável que sites potencialmente enganosos apareçam nos resultados relacionados a compras. Agradecemos aos pesquisadores que compartilham exemplos que nos mostram onde podemos melhorar a experiência.
Taya Christianson, representante da OpenAI
A Perplexity é consistentemente a IA mais precisa em pesquisas de referência confiáveis, e isso já dura quatro anos. Nunca declaramos ter 100% de precisão, mas afirmamos ser a única empresa dedicada exclusivamente a esse objetivo.
Jesse Dwyer, representante da Perplexity

articles.title: Microsoft Outlook en panne : la messagerie ne fonctionne plus ce soir, l'entreprise confirme l'incident
articles.text:
De nombreux utilisateurs de la messagerie Outlook n'ont plus accès au service ce jeudi soir. Une panne affecte en effet une partie des fonctionnalités de la suite Microsoft 365, qui confirme l'incident.
La messagerie Outlook est inaccessible ce soir, en France et dans de nombreux pays du monde, pour un grand nombre d'utilisateurs. Microsoft a signalé ce jeudi 12 novembre en fin de journée une « dégradation de service » sur Microsoft 365 (offres Business et Entreprise). Selon l'entreprise, des utilisateurs pourraient ne pas réussir à se connecter à leur boîte aux lettres Exchange Online.
Ça coince pour Microsoft Outlook, en panne mercredi soir
Le problème touche plusieurs moyens d’accès. Microsoft cite notamment la version web d'Outlook, l'interface MAPI utilisée par le client Outlook de bureau, Exchange ActiveSync (EAS), qui synchronise la messagerie sur les smartphones, et l'API REST sur laquelle s’appuient de nombreuses applications tierces. Sur mobile, ça ne semble plus fonctionner non plus, notamment côté Outlook.
L'éditeur américain dit avoir repéré des erreurs de connectivité sur une partie de l'infrastructure d'Exchange Online qui reçoit et traite les demandes d'accès des utilisateurs. Ses équipes ont recueilli des journaux réseau pour trouver l'origine de ces erreurs et décider de la suite. Microsoft a constaté une surcharge de l'infrastructure concernée dans plusieurs régions, qui serait « probablement » à l'origine des erreurs de connectivité.
Pour rétablir la capacité, les équipes redémarrent et réparent les parties touchées de cette infrastructure. Elles examinent aussi une hausse inattendue du trafic venant d'un type de service précis, pour savoir si elle a causé cette surcharge. Microsoft ne dit pas de quel service il s'agit. En parallèle, l'entreprise cherche à rediriger le trafic vers une autre infrastructure afin de résoudre le problème plus vite. Elle ne donne toujours aucun délai de rétablissement, ni le nombre d’utilisateurs touchés.

articles.title: “Ce serait un honneur” : Elon Musk veut recruter Jensen Huang, viré de Nvidia, alors qu'une troisième liaison éclate dans la foulée
articles.text:
“Ce serait un honneur” : Elon Musk veut recruter Jensen Huang, viré de Nvidia, alors qu'une troisième liaison éclate dans la foulée
Donald Trump, lui, voit déjà Tim Cook à la tête de Nvidia
Le feuilleton tech de la semaine continue. La démission à peine sèche, Jensen Huang, ex-patron de Nvidia, voit surgir une troisième relation extraconjugale, cette fois avec une salariée. Au même moment, le gotha de la tech se presse à son chevet. Elon Musk lui ouvre grand la porte, et la Maison-Blanche s'improvise chasseur de têtes.
Jeudi 12 novembre, Jensen Huang a quitté la direction de Nvidia, l'entreprise qu'il avait fondée en 1993, au terme d'une semaine de révélations sur sa vie privée. Quelques heures plus tard, l'agence Reuters attribuait au dirigeant de 63 ans une troisième liaison, avec une employée du groupe. Le scandale resserre pourtant autour de lui une partie de l'élite technologique américaine. Elon Musk se dit honoré à l'idée de le recruter, et Donald Trump désigne publiquement son successeur idéal. Le site Futurism y voit des puissants qui serrent les rangs autour de l'homme dont les puces font tourner l'IA mondiale.
Une troisième liaison avec une salariée de Nvidia
Selon deux sources citées par l'agence Reuters, Jensen Huang a entretenu une relation intime avec une seconde employée de Nvidia. Reuters ne révèle ni son nom ni son poste et n'a pas pu la joindre. On ignore si elle dépendait directement du patron. Nvidia n'a pas souhaité commenter.
La liste s'allonge. Avant elle, il y a eu Alice Huang, ex-dirigeante de Megaspeed, gros client singapourien de Nvidia, que les renseignements américains soupçonnent de travailler pour Pékin. Puis Kimberly Powell, vice-présidente chargée de la santé, dont le New York Times a dévoilé la relation avec son patron la veille de son départ. Dans sa lettre aux salariés du 8 novembre, Jensen Huang avouait une infidélité sans nommer personne.
Elon Musk et Donald Trump au chevet de Jensen Huang
Mercredi soir, quelques heures avant l'annonce officielle, le blog financier ZeroHedge interpellait Elon Musk sur X : "Elon, embauche Jensen, s'il te plaît". Réponse du patron de Tesla et de SpaceX : "Ce serait un honneur". Quelques jours plus tôt, il avait déjà approuvé un message de Shaun Maguire, associé du fonds Sequoia Capital. Ce dernier jugeait Jensen Huang "irremplaçable pour le leadership américain en IA", tout en qualifiant sa conduite d'"incroyablement stupide".
	
Ce serait un honneur.
Les intérêts s'entremêlent. xAI, la société d'IA d'Elon Musk, a bâti la première version de son supercalculateur Colossus sur 100 000 puces H100 de Nvidia, et les deux hommes affichent depuis des années une admiration réciproque.
That would be an honor
— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) November 12, 2026
Donald Trump a déjà son candidat. Jeudi, sur Truth Social, il saluait le "travail fantastique" de Jensen Huang et tranchait : "Il n'y a qu'un seul homme pour prendre sa place : TIM COOK d'Apple. Une légende remplace une légende !" Tim Cook a pourtant cédé la direction d'Apple à John Ternus le 1er septembre pour présider son conseil d'administration, et rien n'indique que Nvidia songe à lui. Selon le New York Times, le président avait même exhorté Jensen Huang, mardi au téléphone, à se battre pour garder son fauteuil.
Le conseil présidentiel a de quoi faire tiquer : les comptes de Donald Trump ont acheté et vendu cette année des actions Nvidia et Apple, ce que des élus démocrates dénoncent comme un conflit d’intérêts. La Trump Organization assure que ces placements sont gérés par des tiers.
Jensen Huang accepte de témoigner devant le Congrès
Washington, en revanche, ne lâche rien. Brian Mast, président de la commission des Affaires étrangères de la Chambre, affirme que Jensen Huang a accepté mercredi soir, juste avant sa démission, de témoigner à huis clos avant Thanksgiving, le 26 novembre. John Moolenaar, qui préside la commission sur la Chine, garde l'assignation en réserve en cas de volte-face. Au Sénat, le républicain Tim Scott le convie à une audition publique début décembre et réclame aussi le témoignage du ministre du Commerce, Howard Lutnick, rapporte CBS News.
Mardi 17 novembre, Nvidia présentera ses résultats trimestriels. Pour la première fois, sans son fondateur aux commandes.

articles.title: Google puso en su buscador un nuevo modelo de IA que responde con más imágenes y tablas comparativas
articles.text:
Google activó Gemini 4 Hydrogen, un nuevo modelo de inteligencia artificial, para todos los usuarios de su buscador en el mundo. La empresa lo describió como la mayor mejora de modelo en Search hasta ahora. Responde preguntas de varias partes y muestra más imágenes, tablas comparativas y herramientas a medida.
Según el anuncio de Google, el modelo entiende mejor la intención de quien busca, incluso con errores de tipeo o pedidos muy específicos. También promete respuestas más fáciles de recorrer a simple vista y mayor calidad en todos los idiomas que admite el modo de búsqueda con IA.
Robby Stein, vicepresidente de producto de Search, afirmó en X que Hydrogen es ahora el modelo predeterminado de AI Mode, la búsqueda conversacional de Google. También se usa para las preguntas más difíciles en AI Overviews, los resúmenes con IA que aparecen sobre los resultados, según recogió Search Engine Roundtable.
Google no publicó cifras de velocidad ni pruebas comparativas. PPC Land, un medio especializado en publicidad digital, señaló que la entrada no menciona anuncios, clics hacia sitios web ni el efecto sobre los modelos de pago que ya funcionan en el buscador.
Tres modelos de Gemini 4 en 30 días
Según PPC Land, el primero de la serie, Gemini 4 Argon, salió el 13 de octubre solo para suscriptores de los planes de pago AI Pro y Ultra. El 28 de octubre, el director ejecutivo de Google, Sundar Pichai, presentó Gemini 4 Carbon como su modelo más potente.
El 10 de noviembre, Carbon llegó a AI Mode únicamente para los suscriptores de Ultra, un plan que PPC Land ubica desde USD 99,99 al mes. Hydrogen es el tercero y el primero que Google ofrece sin pago en el buscador.
Hydrogen reemplaza a Gemini 3.8 Flash, el modelo que usaba AI Mode desde el 2 de septiembre, según PPC Land. Ars Technica informó que el cambio alcanza a los productos de la empresa en general, aunque Google no detalló cada uno.
Qué reciben la app, los desarrolladores y los sitios web
En la aplicación Gemini, Google indicó que los usuarios gratuitos accederán a Hydrogen mediante la selección automática de modelo, cuando el sistema lo considere adecuado para la consulta. Ars Technica señaló, en cambio, que el selector de modelos ya lo ofrece a los suscriptores de AI Pro y Ultra, y que los usuarios gratuitos y los de AI Plus siguen con un modelo anterior.
Para los programadores, Ars Technica informó que Hydrogen cuesta USD 1,50 por millón de unidades de texto enviadas y USD 7,50 por millón generadas, igual que su predecesor. Carbon y Argon cuestan hoy USD 2 y USD 10, y subirán a USD 4 y USD 20 a partir del mes próximo.
Para los sitios web, Google sostiene que su técnica de lanzar varias búsquedas simultáneas sobre los subtemas de una pregunta ahora conecta con más enlaces. Ars Technica recordó que la empresa ya había hecho promesas similares antes. PPC Land añadió que la entrada no aclara si el despliegue ya se completó en todos los países.
Gemini 4 Carbon: máxima inteligencia y eficiencia de costos para flujos de trabajo reales
Gemini 4 Carbon ya se encuentra disponible para desarrolladores, empresas, científicos y el público general, consolidándose como nuestro modelo de mayor potencia. Esta herramienta ofrece un desempeño de vanguardia en ciberseguridad y en la ejecución de flujos de trabajo inteligentes a largo plazo, lo que resulta fundamental para abordar tareas complejas de ingeniería de software, gestión del conocimiento y razonamiento científico.
Tras su lanzamiento inicial —dirigido exclusivamente a especialistas en ciberseguridad mediante el programa Fairwind— y después de la reciente presentación de Gemini 4 Argon, este nuevo modelo lleva nuestras capacidades a un nivel superior.
Si bien Argon continúa siendo la alternativa óptima para la mayoría de las labores cotidianas de desarrollo y administración de información, Carbon ha sido concebido para enfrentar desafíos que exigen el máximo nivel de inteligencia artificial.
Por ello, está especialmente orientado a procesos de codificación y depuración complejos de múltiples pasos, así como a la investigación científica abierta, empleando una mayor cantidad de tokens para analizar en profundidad, razonar con rigor y realizar ciclos de verificación prolongados.
Finalmente, los resultados en diversas evaluaciones independientes enfocadas en entornos de trabajo reales demuestran que Carbon logra un equilibrio excepcional entre máxima precisión y eficiencia de costos en producción. De hecho, lidera las clasificaciones en pruebas como CursorBench 4.0, WANDR de Perplexity y AutomationBench de Zapier, destacando por ofrecer un costo por tarea más de dos veces inferior al de su competidor externo más cercano.

articles.title: New N-central Exploits Work Against Patched Servers, Enable Root RCE and Windows SYSTEM Access
articles.text:
N-able on Thursday said it's investigating a new public disclosure containing claims of additional vulnerabilities in on-premise versions of N-central running version 2026.4.1 HF2.
"Based on our initial review, the server issue described depends on a non-default configuration in which the Legacy API is turned on and exposed to the public internet," N-able said in a new advisory. "Legacy API is turned off by default in the product and is not recommended."
The company is urging customers to disable Legacy API immediately, if not already. It also noted that hosted environments are not affected by this issue.
The incident impacts the following services -
- N-central On-premise (Americas)
- N-central On-premise (APAC)
- N-central On-premise (Europe)
The development comes days after N-able released 2026.4.1.26 to address a number of security flaws disclosed by independent security researcher Sean Bales earlier this week. The vulnerabilities are collectively tracked under the name Able2Shell.
The new shortcoming, also revealed by Bales, have been codenamed 4EverAble2Shell and Agent2Shell, adding the proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits successfully work against N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 2 (build 2026.4.1.26), the update N-able released on November 10, 2026, to resolve Able2Shell.
According to the researcher, 4EverAble2Shell enables unauthenticated remote code execution with root privileges on N-central servers. Agent2Shell, on the other hand, leverages more than 10 zero-day vulnerabilities to run commands on managed Windows agents as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM, assuming the attacker knows the target appliance ID.
Ryan Dewhurst, founder and CEO of Previdian, told The Hacker News that targeted N-central probing has been observed against 4EverAble2Shell within hours following the release of the PoC. The activity has originated from the IP address 157.20.241[.]16. There is no evidence of successful exploitation as of writing.
In the attack chain observed by the threat intelligence company, threat actors have been observed attempting to achieve initial code execution through a recently disclosed Apache Axis flaw (CVE-2026-90436, CVSS score: 9.8), followed by attempts to escalate privileges to root using 4EverAble2Shell, and then download and execute a shell script from 157.20.241[.]16 using curl.
Dewhurst said the development marks the first documented instance of exploitation attempts aimed at CVE-2026-90436, patches for which were released on November 6, 2026.
In a post shared on X, watchTowr also said it's seeing probes for 4EverAble2Shell targeting N-Central builds with the Legacy API enabled.
(This is a developing story. Please check back for more information.)

articles.title: Desmantelan redes de malware que robaban contraseñas y aseguran 6,4 millones de datos de víctimas
articles.text:
Europol y policías de nueve países desmantelaron la infraestructura de tres programas maliciosos que robaban contraseñas y daban acceso remoto a computadoras: Gootloader, CastleRAT y StealC. Las autoridades incautaron 235 servidores y 257 dominios y aseguraron 6,4 millones de conjuntos de datos de víctimas, según informó la agencia europea de policía.
La acción es una nueva fase de la Operación Endgame, que Europol describe como el mayor esfuerzo internacional contra quienes facilitan los ataques de secuestro de datos (ransomware). Participan más de 30 socios públicos y privados. Eurojust, el organismo de cooperación judicial de la Unión Europea, apoyó el intercambio de información entre fiscalías.
Intervinieron fuerzas de Bulgaria, Canadá, Dinamarca, Alemania, Moldavia, Países Bajos, Polonia, Reino Unido y Estados Unidos. En el caso estadounidense, el comunicado menciona al FBI, al Servicio de Investigación Criminal de Defensa y a la sección de delitos informáticos del Departamento de Justicia.
Tres herramientas, un mismo negocio
Europol explica que las tres herramientas funcionaban como un servicio que se alquila a otros delincuentes. Con ellas, los clientes de las redes criminales podían instalar ransomware o robar datos sin desarrollar su propio software.
Gootloader se distribuía mediante documentos legales falsos alojados en sitios web comprometidos, con frecuencia páginas hechas con WordPress. Quien descargaba el archivo quedaba infectado. En esta operación se dieron de baja 218 dominios y se limpiaron 681 sitios afectados, según el comunicado.
CastleRAT es un troyano de acceso remoto, conocido desde 2025, que permite controlar una computadora a distancia. Europol atribuye a su uso el cifrado de numerosos conjuntos de datos, la parálisis de sistemas informáticos completos y pagos de rescate de empresas y organizaciones.
StealC está diseñado para extraer contraseñas, datos de acceso guardados e identidades digitales de los equipos infectados, y ponerlos a disposición para su venta o su uso fraudulento. Europol señala que la acción contra StealC continúa los esfuerzos iniciados en junio de 2026.
BleepingComputer recuerda que, en junio, otra fase de Endgame afectó a las redes Amadey y StealC: se desactivaron 326 servidores y 142 dominios y se recuperaron cerca de 27 millones de credenciales robadas a más de 385.000 sistemas. Según ese medio, Gootloader opera desde 2020.
Qué pueden hacer las víctimas
Durante la acción, las autoridades identificaron más de seis millones de credenciales de víctimas en la infraestructura incautada. Europol afirma que los sospechosos las usaban para venderlas y emplearlas en otros ataques, entre ellos el ransomware.
Los datos de las víctimas se cargarán en plataformas de aviso: HaveIBeenPwned, DIVD, CheckjeHack, NoMoreLeaks, Sekoia, The Shadowserver Foundation y el centro de ciberseguridad de los Países Bajos (NL-NCSC). El comunicado precisa que esas alertas corresponden a las credenciales robadas con CastleRAT.
A los administradores de sitios con WordPress, Europol les pidió cambiar las contraseñas, activar la verificación en dos pasos y corregir las vulnerabilidades. Gootloader se propagaba justamente a través de sitios de ese tipo que habían sido vulnerados.
El comunicado no informa de detenciones ni indica cuántas de las víctimas son usuarios particulares y cuántas empresas. Europol publicó el balance el 12 de noviembre de 2026, después de una semana de acciones coordinadas.
Descubrieron malware que supera protecciones en Windows
Recientemente, la firma de ciberseguridad Kaspersky descubrió BlackX, un bootkit que explota la vulnerabilidad Baton Drop para sortear Secure Boot en Windows incluso en equipos que ya tienen instalado el parche de Microsoft, dado que la actualización por sí sola no activa la protección completa y requiere pasos adicionales de configuración manual por parte de los administradores.
El malware, detectado durante una campaña de ciberespionaje contra organizaciones diplomáticas de Asia Central a principios de 2026, es una versión modernizada de BlackLotus y se utiliza como herramienta secundaria de alta persistencia una vez que los atacantes ya comprometieron la red interna y obtuvieron privilegios de administrador.
Tras desactivar el software de seguridad, BlackX habilita el espionaje mediante el abuso de servicios legítimos en la nube como Google Drive, OneDrive y Yandex Disk. Kaspersky recomienda verificar que la configuración de seguridad se complete en su totalidad, limitar los privilegios de administrador y monitorear de forma continua los sistemas corporativos.

articles.title: La France lance un centre international de l’IA de défense à Rennes, et veut y rallier ses alliés
articles.text:
La France va lancer à Rennes l'ICAID, un centre international dédié à l'intelligence artificielle de défense. Ouvert aux armées alliées, il sera officiellement lancé le 20 novembre et doit devenir opérationnel courant 2027.
Le ministère des Armées a officialisé ce jeudi 12 novembre 2026 la création de l'International Center for Artificial Intelligence in Defence (ICAID), un centre international pour l'intelligence artificielle de défense qui sera implanté à Rennes. Il sera officiellement lancé le 20 novembre, lors d'une conférence d'établissement de deux jours fermée à la presse, certes, mais qui on le sait réunira les nations prêtes à s'engager aux côtés de la France.
Un centre pour aider les armées à mieux choisir leur IA
Le ministère des Armées l'a constaté depuis un moment. Les champs de bataille se transforment à grande vitesse, et l'IA pèse désormais lourd dans la supériorité militaire. Le fameux centre devra aider ses membres à mieux en comprendre les enjeux. Il devra surtout développer l'expertise et les méthodes pour concevoir, acquérir, déployer et évaluer des services d'IA dans la défense. Autrement dit, savoir bâtir, acheter et jauger ces outils, et pas seulement les utiliser.
On en sait un peu plus sur la feuille de route de l'ICAID. D'abord, le centre va devoir créer une communauté d'intérêt entre partenaires pour accélérer l'adoption de l'IA. Ensuite, il aura pour rôle de circuler les bonnes pratiques et d'anticiper les évolutions technologiques. Enfin, il fera remonter les retours d'expérience des forces, pour coller au plus près de leurs besoins.
Cette exigence n'est pas farfelue en tout cas, puisqu'on se souvient qu'en septembre, CNN avait révélé qu'une hallucination d'IA, transformée en rapport de renseignement, avait failli provoquer un affrontement armé entre les États-Unis et la Chine.
Sur l'IA de défense, la France joue désormais en équipe
Alors pourquoi le ministère des Armées a-t-il choisi Rennes ? Certains l'ont compris avant qu'on vous l'écrive. La ville bretonne, souvent considérée comme la capitale française de la cybersécurité, est au cœur de l'écosystème numérique et IA de défense français. L'AMIAD, l'Agence ministérielle pour l'intelligence artificielle de Défense, a déjà des équipes à Bruz, à quelques kilomètres. Son directeur, Bertrand Rondepierre, parle de « rupture technologique » et veut en accélérer la maîtrise « aux côtés de nos alliés ».
L'ICAID prolonge une année chargée pour l'agence. En janvier, elle a été chargée de piloter l'accord-cadre signé par le ministère avec Mistral AI pour équiper toutes les armées en IA générative. En février, elle a créé avec l'ENSTA le LARIAD, un laboratoire consacré à la robotique et à l'IA de défense.
De l'autre côté de l'Atlantique, aux États-Unis, l'intelligence artificielle militaire passe d'abord par des contrats avec les géants de la tech, comme OpenAI, Google ou NVIDIA, qui a une nouvelle patronne. Avec l'ICAID, Paris ajoute une dimension diplomatique à sa stratégie et mise sur une coalition d'États. Il faudra toutefois patienter, car le centre n'atteindra sa capacité opérationnelle que courant 2027. Et la question des moyens consacrés se pose encore. Cet été, un rapport sénatorial sur les drones notait qu'aucun financement n'était prévu pour l'IA de défense dans l'enveloppe qu'il examinait.

articles.title: Calendar Invites and Live Proxies: Inside a Google Session Hijacking Campaign
articles.text:
Since mid-August 2026, a phishing operation has been stealing live Google sessions from corporate users. Every check defenders normally lean on to judge a link came back clean, and the operator designed it that way on purpose.
The Threat Research team at Material Security spotted the campaign and has since taken down hundreds of attacker domains in an effort the team calls Operation CloudFire. Here’s what the researchers found.
The lure: Google Calendar invites
The messages show up as Google Calendar invites. Some arrive by BCC, and many come from an organization the recipient has already traded email with. The pretexts are deliberately boring: voicemail notifications, RFP and RFI requests, court summonses, and missed payment notices. Nothing about them stands out in a busy inbox.
Most of the links point to Google itself. The usual pattern runs through Google’s own /url redirector, with the real destination tucked into a query parameter. Other waves used share.google and Drive file links the same way, and one variant leaned on Intuit transaction notification links. Whenever a message gets scored, the domain, certificate, and reputation on display are all legitimate.
The capture: a reverse proxy in front of Google sign-in
Once a victim clicks through, the attacker runs a live reverse proxy in front of the real Google sign-in page. The victim types a password, gets a genuine prompt, and approves it while the operator watches in real time. The server passes each second factor along to Google as it comes in, whether that’s an SMS code, an authenticator code, Google’s Tap-Yes number matching, or phone-based account recovery. None of those controls stop the session from being captured.
The framework behind it, known as Nyasher, has been publicly documented since February, after researchers found a hardcoded key in its JavaScript.
Why the usual controls stay quiet
Reputation systems answer questions about ownership. They ask who registered a domain, what else it has hosted, and whether anyone has complained about it. This campaign was built so every one of those answers came back harmless.
It works in three layers. The first is Google’s redirector, which gives the initial hop a trusted Google URL. The second is a Cloudflare Turnstile challenge, and in some builds it’s the real widget served from Cloudflare’s own infrastructure. The third is the password capture page, and that’s where things get tricky for defenders. There’s no static site to scan. JavaScript builds the page in the browser after the visitor clears the challenge, so a crawler has nothing to fetch and a proxy log has nothing to record. As far as the researchers know, nobody had scanned those pages before the campaign was documented.
The infrastructure is also meant to be thrown away. Early waves used many lure domains spread across several registrars, and most were registered just days before use. Receiving endpoints went live one to twenty days ahead of the wave they served. One wildcard certificate was issued 46 minutes before the domain it covers was even registered. Blocking any single piece costs the operator a few dollars and an afternoon.
What stopping it took
Researchers tracked the campaign from the start, following each variant as lures, gates, and endpoints rotated. Once detections were in place, they caught more than 99% of the malicious messages, with a reclassification rate of 0.01%. It’s been steady work, since the attacker kept changing tactics, themes, and lure text to slip past static, machine learning, and agentic detections.
What worked was refusing to let any one signal make the call. Reputation alone wouldn’t have caught this. Neither would link analysis, since the first hop is a Google URL and the final page doesn’t exist until a browser builds it. Instead, the detection approach weighs technical indicators alongside the apparent intent of the message, where its links actually end up, and the sending relationship behind it. Any one of those can be enough to act on. A detection built around a single signal inherits that signal’s blind spots, and this operator has put real effort into mapping them.
Where the analysis happens matters too. Gateways built to inspect mail in transit aren’t a great fit for calendar invites, and much of this campaign arrives as invites. Calendar invites need to be treated as a threat surface of their own, with the account’s full history used as context next to the technical signals.
Where the damage lands
A hijacked session leaves its trail in Google Workspace audit logs. A live session reaches mail, Drive, and the ability to grant OAuth access in the victim’s name, so the blast radius goes well past the inbox.
That raises a couple of hard questions for security teams. Who’s actually reviewing those audit logs, and how fast can they act on what they find? Could the team revoke sessions, contain OAuth grants, and reset the affected account within an hour? Plenty of programs can’t, and an attacker holding a live session can do a lot in an hour.
Operation CloudFire: going after the infrastructure
By late September, the researchers decided that tuning rules, retraining models, and updating agents wouldn’t solve this alone. Detection protects customers, but it does nothing about an operator who’s already prepping the next wave. So the team went after the infrastructure.
Analysts pulled the gateway and backend URLs as messages were being sent and reported them through Cloudflare’s abuse reporting system. Cloudflare’s abuse team confirmed the fake interstitial and the proxied Google sign-in page behind it, then put its own phishing warning in front of those destinations.
That had two effects. First, the attacker’s infrastructure got burned. Every reported gateway and endpoint had to be re-registered, re-pointed, and re-certified before the operator could send again. Second, it protected people well beyond any one company’s customers. Anyone who clicked a reported link saw a warning page instead of a credential form.
One month by the numbers
These figures only cover organizations that agreed to share data, so the real totals are higher. Over one month of Operation CloudFire, researchers recorded:
- 68,676 campaign messages blocked
- 2,112 unique malicious URLs analyzed
- 897 unique domains taken down
- 8,570 unique compromised sender addresses across 6,354 root domains
The messages also followed a clear rhythm, with sends tracking US business hours.
| Message delivery by time of day | 
The sender count explains how the campaign earned trust. The attacker controlled each compromised account before the first invite went out, and each one sent invites to the account owner’s saved contacts, among others. Recipients saw a name or domain they knew, on a domain with a clean history, at a sensible time of day. Reputation feeds had no reason to flag any of it.
Where things stand now
The phishing themes have moved from calendar invites to Google Drive file and document share invites. Researchers haven’t seen a matching jump in other lures or tactics, and activity from this group seems to have scattered. For now, the campaign looks finished.
| Messages detected by week | 
| Domains registered by interval | 
That’s a snapshot, and it could change fast. Rebuilding the infrastructure is cheap, and the framework has been public since February. The operator also shipped an unfinished Microsoft 365 branch alongside the live Google code. It includes a stylesheet path, a second harness, and a title string that decodes to a Microsoft sign-in prompt. None of those paths resolve today, and adding the new brand would only mean dropping in a file, with no code changes. The follow-on is built and waiting.
The researchers see the theme rotation as ongoing iteration and expect the next pivot to look a lot like this one, just with a different brand on it.
The full technical breakdown, including indicators of compromise and a timeline, is in the companion whitepaper. Teams hunting for this activity in their own environments should start there.

articles.title: First RAM, now circuit boards: AI demand is stretching some PCB orders to 30 months
articles.text:
First RAM, now circuit boards: AI demand is stretching some PCB orders to 30 months
The AI server boom is first in line and is expected to stay there
- PC makers including HP and Dell are struggling to secure PCBs for 2027 as AI servers absorb board capacity
- Canon says AI-driven PCB shortages have doubled its expected medical sales hit to about ¥90 billion
- One supplier cites some orders taking up to 30 months even as Unimicron's chairman used the same figure for equipment, not boards
The AI infrastructure boom has already chewed through the world's supply of high-end memory, and it is now working its way down to the green slab everything else sits on. PC makers planning their 2027 lineups,
HP and Dell, among others, are struggling to secure enough printed circuit boards, according to a Nikkei Asia report summarized by Guru3D.
One board maker told the publication that lead times on a significant number of its products have doubled, with some orders stretching to 30 months, while another said an order placed today would not be filled until late 2028.
The board that nobody worried about could be a significant problem
The soaring demand for PCBs is not happening in a vacuum; Samsung has already warned that the memory shortage could last until 2028, and the same logic essentially applies to boards: the companies building AI data centers need more of the product, need better versions of it, and will pay more for it.
The crux of the matter is that AI server boards are a different beast from the motherboard in a mid-range laptop. Würth Elektronik estimates that PCBs for AI servers carry three to five times as many layers as conventional designs, built on low-loss laminates and specialty glass fabrics, so each one essentially consumes far more material and factory time.
Board makers have responded rationally, aiming to maximize profits: Market researcher in4ma reported in July that some PCB manufacturers have told existing customers they will stop producing standard boards in favor of higher-margin AI server work. Hyperscalers are also buying their way into the supply chain directly, with the world's biggest hyperscaler, Amazon, taking a stake of roughly NT$1.59 billion ($48.2 million in USD) in Taiwan's Gold Circuit Electronics in September, according to TechSpot.
That leaves PC makers in a particularly odd and unenviable position, with an unnamed executive at an American PC maker telling Nikkei that even with shipments set to fall again next year, "we are still struggling to secure enough PCB supplies to meet our needs."
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
IDC says global PC shipments fell 20.1% year on year in the third quarter to 62.7 million units, with HP down 30.9% and Dell down 25%, although IDC attributes part of that to distributors working through stock bought early in the year ahead of price hikes. Either way, this is a buyer who wants fewer boards and still cannot get them, which points to an allocation problem rather than demand. It is the same dynamic that has data centers on course to grab 70% of high-end memory chips this year.
The 30-month figure is doing the heavy lifting in headlines built around Nikkei's coverage, and it centers around a single unnamed supplier describing some orders, not an industry average.
The trend around it is striking enough on its own - in March 2026, German board maker ILFA said lead times for standard FR-4 laminate had gone from a few days to around four weeks. By April, a Broadcom director was telling Nikkei that PCB lead times had gone from six weeks to six months. This effectively means that an order placed in late October that lands in late 2028 implies a wait of roughly two years, while a 30-month lead time from today would run to around April 2029, so the two supplier claims describe different ends of the range.
A week before Nikkei's report, Unimicron chairman S.C. Chien told the TPCA Show in Taipei that lead times for some key production equipment had reached 30 months, with more than 80% of equipment seeing longer waits and over a fifth seeing waits more than double their usual length. Chien also warned that low-CTE glass cloth, copper-clad laminate (CCL) and ABF could fall about 20% short of demand in 2027.
Nikkei also reports that one leading laminate supplier has orders filling through 2030, despite plans to triple capacity by 2028. An order book, however, is not a delivery schedule, and suppliers benefit from scarcity narratives; Acer's Jason Chen has already accused memory makers of hyping 2030 shortage talk to protect their margins. The upstream bottlenecks are real, though. Nittobo controls roughly 90% of the T-glass used in advanced substrates, and its capacity expansion will take years to reach the market.
One could argue that there is no case here for panic-buying a motherboard just yet. A board is a small slice of a laptop's bill of materials; no PC maker has put a number on the retail impact, and memory remains the dominant cost driver
But the PCB squeeze adds to an already grim picture, in which major vendors had warned of 15-20% price rises starting in the second half of 2026. The large OEMs with long-term contracts should weather it best thanks to already negotiated and inked supply commitments.
Smaller motherboard and graphics card brands, buying without that leverage, are where a doubled lead time or a tripled laminate bill is most likely to surface in 2027, either as a higher sticker price or a thinner spec sheet if not both at the same time.
Follow TechRadar on Google News and add us as a preferred source to get our expert news, reviews, and opinion in your feeds.
Rahim Amir is a UAE-based tech writer who enjoys building PCs as much as he enjoys writing about them. He has been professionally writing about PC hardware since 2023, focusing on buyer’s guides, hardware reviews, and sponsored content and features related to tech.
Having built hundreds of gaming PCs and being an avid gamer in his spare time, Rahim tends to have stronger opinions about hardware than most. This is particularly on display when he gets his way with powerful, but minimalistic RGB builds even as Small Form Factor (SFF) PCs come a close second.

articles.title: Cómo saber si una tienda online es real antes de pagar y qué hacer si ya compraste en una falsa
articles.text:
Antes de pagar en una tienda online conviene hacer tres comprobaciones: que la empresa exista, que la dirección web sea la oficial y que el cobro se haga dentro del sitio. Los organismos de defensa del consumidor de Argentina las recomiendan de cara a las compras de Black Friday y de fin de año.
El Gobierno de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires publicó el 30 de octubre de 2026 cinco consejos para el Cyber Monday, que se realizó del 2 al 4 de noviembre del mismo año. Su Dirección General de Defensa y Protección al Consumidor advirtió sobre correos y mensajes de WhatsApp con enlaces a supuestas ofertas exclusivas.
Para esos casos, el organismo recomienda no ingresar datos personales ni bancarios en páginas sospechosas, entrar directamente a los sitios oficiales de las marcas y guardar capturas de las publicaciones, de los precios y de la confirmación de compra.
Tres controles antes de cargar la tarjeta
El primero es comprobar que el comercio existe. Según la página de derechos del consumidor del Gobierno nacional, las empresas argentinas deben informar su nombre y su número de CUIT, la clave de identificación tributaria. Ese dato y la razón social permiten verificar la veracidad del comercio.
Otra página oficial agrega que la existencia legal de un sitio con dudas puede constatarse en NIC Argentina, el organismo que registra los dominios terminados en .ar. Si una web que se presenta como una cadena conocida figura a nombre de un particular, el dato no coincide.
El segundo control es la dirección. El Gobierno nacional aconseja no entrar a una tienda desde un correo o un mensaje de aplicaciones como WhatsApp, porque pueden llevar a sitios falsos que copian la identidad de la página real. Lo indicado es escribir la dirección en el navegador.
El candado y la sigla “https” no bastan como garantía de autenticidad. Los organismos recomiendan exigirlos antes de ingresar datos de tarjeta, pero indican que cifran la conexión: no prueban quién está del otro lado.
El tercer control es el medio de pago. Un documento del Gobierno nacional sugiere evitar pagos en efectivo, giros o empresas de envío de dinero que no permitan verificar al vendedor, y preferir la tarjeta de crédito. Pide no pagar fuera de la plataforma donde se compra, porque la mayoría ofrece protección al comprador.
Qué hacer si ya se pagó
Ante una situación sospechosa, el Banco Central aconseja contactar al banco por sus canales oficiales. Conviene hacerlo cuanto antes y conservar todo lo que documente la operación: comprobantes, capturas de la publicación, mensajes, correos y la dirección web donde se compró.
Si la tienda existe pero incumple, el comprador puede reclamar. En la Ciudad de Buenos Aires, el reclamo se inicia en el sitio de la Dirección General de Defensa y Protección al Consumidor, y a nivel nacional en la ventanilla única federal de reclamos de Defensa del Consumidor.
Si el sitio era una estafa, el caso es penal. El Gobierno nacional indica hacer la denuncia en la comisaría o en la oficina receptora de denuncias del domicilio, con todo el material disponible. Se puede avisar a la Unidad Fiscal Especializada en Ciberdelincuencia del Ministerio Público Fiscal, por correo a denunciasufeci@mpf.gov.ar.
Arrepentimiento y garantía
En las compras por internet, el consumidor puede cancelar dentro de los 10 días corridos desde que recibe el producto, sin dar motivos. Los costos de la devolución corren por cuenta del vendedor, según la Ciudad de Buenos Aires.
Los sitios que venden deben incluir un botón de arrepentimiento, un enlace visible desde la página de inicio, según la Resolución 424/2020 de la Secretaría de Comercio Interior. Nadie puede pedir un trámite previo, y el vendedor tiene 24 horas para informar el código de identificación del trámite.
Los productos nuevos tienen por ley una garantía mínima de 6 meses y los usados de 3 meses, según el Gobierno nacional. El comercio puede ofrecer más tiempo, pero no menos.

articles.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen é o novo modelo do Google para tarefas do dia a dia • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Gemini 4 Hydrogen é o novo modelo do Google para tarefas do dia a dia
Novo modelo substitui o Gemini 3.8 Flash e chega gratuitamente ao aplicativo Gemini e à Busca do Google.
O Google anunciou nesta quinta-feira (12/11) o mais um novo modelo de inteligência artificial, dessa vez voltado a tarefas cotidianas. O Gemini 4 Hydrogen substitui o Gemini 3.8 Flash, prometendo respostas 2,5 vezes mais rápidas e melhorias de precisão.
O modelo já começou a ser disponibilizado no aplicativo do Gemini e na Busca do Google, inclusive para não assinantes. Já desenvolvedores que pretendem incorporá-lo a apps e serviços próprios, a API segue os seguintes preços:
O acesso está disponível por meio das ferramentas de integração do Google, incluindo o Google AI Studio e o Android Studio.
O Hydrogen combina velocidade, capacidade de raciocínio e menor custo de operação frente aos outros modelos da família, segundo o Google. Mesmo sendo mais indicado para produção de textos e tarefas comuns, nota-se que o modelo básico conseguiu bons resultados em algumas atividades.
No Artificial Analysis Intelligence, índice independente que reúne diferentes testes para medir a capacidade de modelos de IA, o Hydrogen alcançou 51 pontos na configuração padrão e bateu 54 com o nível máximo de raciocínio, contra 50 do Gemini 4 Argon.
Frente ao Gemini 3.8 Flash, o Gemini 4 Hydrogen também reduziu a ocorrência de alucinações em mais de cinco vezes, além de ser 2,3 vezes mais resistente a ataques de prompt injection.
Contra modelos concorrentes, como o Claude Sonnet 5.5, da Anthropic, e o GPT-6.1 Terra, da OpenAI, os resultados mostram algumas vantagens, como:
O desempenho muda quando a avaliação exige operação de sistemas e resolução de tarefas científicas e matemáticas. O modelo do Google ficou atrás do Claude Sonnet 5.5 em testes como Terminal-Bench 4.1, Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 e no benchmark que avalia a interatividade do modelo com o computador, OSWorld-2.1, um dos testes mais relevantes para IAs agênticas.
O novo modelo básico pode ser integrado ao Gemini 4 Carbon, em um mesmo fluxo de trabalho pela nova ferramenta Orchestrator. A ferramenta funciona de forma semelhante ao comando /swarm, adicionado ao Google Antigravity no lançamento do modelo de fronteira.
A ideia é que o Carbon fique reservado para atividades mais complexas, enquanto o Hydrogen assume etapas que podem ser concluídas com menos recursos. Segundo testes divulgados pelo Google, a combinação apresentou taxas de sucesso próximas às obtidas pelo Carbon Sozinho no Terminal-Bench 4.0, reduzindo o consume do tokens em 24% e o tempo em 19%.
