articles.title: Attacker Used 4,837 Hijacked GitHub Accounts to Run a CI Secret Stealer in 1,806+ Repositories
articles.text:
Starting Tuesday, an attacker used stolen credentials for 4,837 GitHub accounts to plant a secret stealer in repositories those accounts could write to, according to Aikido Security, a security software company.
The stealer is built to take the secrets and cloud credentials that a repository's CI workflows can reach. It ran in at least 1,806 repositories, where the attacker has likely collected those credentials, the company says.
Each attack started with a pull request titled docs: dependency audit notes, opened from a branch named wfx-docs to test whether the account could write to the repository. These test pull requests were opened in 61,764 repositories, and the stealer followed in some of them.
In a separate analysis, researchers at SafeDep, which sells software supply chain security tools, counted 8,093 repositories that received malicious commits between 12:46 UTC on Tuesday and 04:36 UTC today. That count covers every repository that received malicious commits, not only those where the stealer ran. Their search covered only the default branches of public repositories, so the true total is higher, the researchers say.
In 7,309 of those repositories, the stealer was added to an existing workflow. In 771, it came as an npm postinstall hook, which also runs on a developer's machine during npm install.
After pushing the stealer, the attacker usually reverted the change within minutes. Where the stealer ran, its logs were deleted, usually along with the run itself. In those repositories, every secret and cloud role available to the workflows should be treated as compromised.
More pull requests with the same title were opened early today, after the company's own GitHub search ended on Wednesday, a check by The Hacker News found. Three that were checked, opened between 05:04 and 05:38 UTC, came from wfx-docs branches. It is not clear whether the stealer followed.
Any account that opened one of the attacker's test pull requests is compromised, even if the stealer never ran, Aikido said in its technical analysis. The analysis does not explain how the attacker obtained the credentials.
SafeDep's researchers advise owners of affected repositories to revoke the commit author's tokens, OAuth app grants, SSH keys, and sessions, and to turn on 2FA. Owners should also rotate every secret and variable the repository can read. Anyone who ran npm install on an affected commit should treat that machine as compromised and rotate its keys.
In most other repositories that received a test, nothing was pushed afterward, or the stealer did not run due to the repository's settings or the account's permissions. The figures cover only the public repositories the company could see.
The tests also reached repositories that the compromised accounts did not own. Of the test pull requests, 10,431 were submitted via collaborator or organization access, and 92% of those were still open when the company checked.
Signs a Repository Was Hit
Check for these signs, from Tuesday onward, in any repository you can write to:
- Branch: wfx-docs
- Branch: chore/[a-z0-9]{8}, short-lived
- Branch: ci-check-[0-9]{4}
- Pull request title: docs: dependency audit notes
- Commit message: ci: refresh build cache, which adds about 1,500 lines to an existing workflow
- Commit message: chore: add ci helper, which adds a .ci-xxxxxx.sh script and a postinstall hook in package.json that runs it on any npm install
- Commit message: chore: add dependency audit workflow, which adds .github/workflows/build-audit-xxxxxx.yml on a chore/ branch
- Commit message: chore: initial commit, pushed before a new workflow file in an empty repository
- Commit message: ci: restore
- Commit message: ci: cleanup
- SHA-256 (stealer script): 89695abb392d5cfd4972672961e644bb46baa98aa1ed7173c2a2816c762735cf
- IP: 194.150.166[.]244:8080/exfil
- IP: 18.143.168[.]96:8080/exfil
- IP: 153.75.82[.]159:8080
A repository can show no wfx-loot artifacts, wfx- cache entries, or WFX-BEGIN step summaries and still have lost data. A missing run number on the attacker's commit is the more reliable sign that the stealer ran.
The stealer sends data by HTTP POST to the addresses above or to a Telegram chat, the SafeDep researchers found. In a sample of 200 payload commits, about a fifth used Telegram only.
The stealer is built to collect credentials from every source on the runner, according to the company. They include GitHub Actions secrets and variables, the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN, OIDC and Actions runtime tokens, keys for AI services, and secrets in the memory of the runner's own processes. It reads credential files for AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, PyPI, SSH, and other tools from their usual locations.
It also copies the repository, its last 100 commits, and recent workflow artifacts. On self-hosted runners, it takes cloud credentials from instance metadata as well as Docker container state and systemd units.
The stealer also has settings for private repositories, and the company says that suggests it may be running in them.
The stealer is designed to use those credentials to reach deeper into cloud accounts. It exchanges GitHub OIDC tokens for AWS, GCP, and Azure sessions, and on AWS it can create long-lived access keys for IAM users.
Some of its steps are built to survive credential rotation. It can rewrite an AWS role's trust policy to open the role to any AWS account.
It can also add federated identity credentials with the prefix wfx-ci- to Azure AD applications. Workflows in the compromised repository can then sign in to Azure without a stored secret, even after all tokens are rotated.
To find these backdoors, the researchers suggest checking for:
- Entra ID: federated credentials named wfx-ci-* that you did not create
- AWS CloudTrail: AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity or AssumeRole sessions named wfx-*, followed by CreateAccessKey or UpdateAssumeRolePolicy
- GCP: GenerateAccessToken and SignJwt calls from your GitHub workload identity pool
- Vault: JWT logins from the GitHub OIDC issuer
The stealer reached at least one Packagist package and one Go module through automated publishing triggers. At least 50 of the compromised users appear to publish packages for npm, Go, Packagist, PyPI, or crates.
The attacker appears to be after CI secrets rather than trying to spread through packages, the company says.
Version 3.14.3 of the Packagist package digitalelvis/neuronai-studio is malicious, and the company advises treating any machine that installed or opened it as compromised. Its package listing shows the version was published on Wednesday. Early today, the version was still listed, under a notice that versions of the package had been flagged as malware.
A normal composer install does not run the stealer, but running npm install inside the package's vendor directory does, the researchers found. Users should block v3.14.3 and pin v3.14.2 or earlier.
Two versions of the Go module github.com/onuragtas/docker-env, v1.0.278 and v1.0.280, carry the stealer only in a GitHub Actions workflow file. The Go code and release binaries are unchanged, and Go builds never run workflow files, so users of the module may not have been affected. The company still recommends removing those versions.
The researchers also found the stealer in another Go module, github.com/vkuznet/gocurl, in pseudo-version v0.0.0-20261111095532-8d5aad0cb0da, inside a workflow that has never run. Users should block that pseudo-version.
The stealer also reached 28 WebdriverIO repositories through commits authored as the bot account wdio-bot. No package release was affected, but the bot's token should be treated as stolen.
The company found that the accounts used this week overlap with those hit in GhostAction's October wave, in which stolen GitHub accounts pushed secret-stealing workflows into repositories.
Accounts hit in October were about 1,000 times more likely than other active accounts to be used this week. In more than 100 repositories, the new stealer was added to October's workflow files, leaving the older step that sends data out in place.
Aikido said, "we don't attribute November to the same actor at this stage," because the infrastructure, tools, and methods differ, and stolen credentials often end up with several attackers.
Correction (November 12, 2026): An earlier version of this article said the stealer sent data only by HTTP POST to two addresses and that the attacker reverted each change within a minute. A second analysis found a third server, a Telegram channel, and changes left in place for longer.

articles.title: Investigador de Google dijo que 48 agentes de IA descubrieron un sitio maya, pero ya estaba mapeado
articles.text:
El investigador de Google Pietro Miotti dijo que 48 agentes de inteligencia artificial habían hallado en México un sitio maya que no figuraba en el registro oficial. Después se supo que arqueólogos ya lo habían mapeado en un estudio de 2025. El caso abrió una discusión sobre aficionados que usan IA en campos científicos.
Miotti aclaró no ser arqueólogo. Según The Verge, trabajó por su cuenta y sin recursos de la empresa. Su blog describe un proyecto de tres días, del 18 al 21 de octubre, que había empezado con una idea durante un viaje a Perú.
Como los datos públicos de Perú eran escasos, Miotti pasó a la región maya. Convirtió en imágenes unos 1.200 kilómetros cuadrados de lidar de la NASA, una tecnología que dispara pulsos láser a través de la vegetación para dibujar el relieve del suelo, y puso a los agentes a revisarlas una por una.
No usó un modelo especial: los agentes miraron las imágenes siguiendo una guía para distinguir pirámides, plataformas y plazas de colinas, sumideros y caminos. Entre los candidatos quedó un sitio en una colina, con una plaza nivelada, una pirámide ovalada y un patio elevado.
El 21 de octubre, el Instituto Nacional de Antropología e Historia (INAH) de México respondió que no tenía registrado ningún sitio arqueológico en esas coordenadas. Miotti contó que usó a los agentes para traducir su informe al español y escribió que era “por lejos el mejor momento de la historia para estar vivo”.
El sitio ya estaba en un estudio de 2025
La corrección llegó el 11 de noviembre. Miotti actualizó su entrada para reconocer que el lugar figura en un artículo de Francisco Estrada-Belli, Marcello Canuto, Ivan Šprajc y Juan Carlos Fernandez-Diaz, publicado en 2025 en la revista científica Journal of Archaeological Science: Reports. Los agentes y él pasaron por alto ese trabajo.
El sitio estaba ausente del registro del INAH, pero no era desconocido para los especialistas. Miotti escribió que los agentes lo redescubrieron en lugar de descubrirlo. Dijo a The Verge que, como no es arqueólogo, no sabía que un lugar sin registrar no equivale a un lugar sin mapear.
Según Miotti, comprobar si un sitio ya se conoce exige comparar imágenes con las figuras de los artículos, porque los arqueólogos no publican las coordenadas. Dijo que esa tarea es mucho más difícil para los agentes y que las herramientas deben mejorar en ella.
Los arqueólogos critican la palabra “descubrimiento”
La publicación original superó el millón de vistas en la red social X, según el sitio especializado Sysnote. Sarah Parcak, profesora de la Universidad de Alabama en Birmingham, escribió en Bluesky que “para esto existe la revisión por pares”, y recordó que la ausencia en una base oficial no prueba que algo sea desconocido.
Elizabeth Graham, profesora de arqueología mesoamericana en el University College de Londres, dijo a The Verge que los especialistas conocen “toneladas de sitios” sin explorar y que el problema es la falta de fondos para excavarlos. También objetó el verbo “descubrir”: las comunidades locales suelen conocer los lugares de su zona.
Šprajc, profesor del Centro de Investigación de la Academia Eslovena de Ciencias y Artes y coautor del estudio que documentaba el sitio, dijo que el trabajo de los agentes no le impresionó. Recordó que los arqueólogos usan lidar desde hace tiempo y que consultar al INAH no basta, porque el instituto no tiene toda la información.
Šprajc contó que acababa de recibir otro correo de un “descubridor” con IA y que teme una avalancha de mensajes. También advirtió de un riesgo: publicar la ubicación de sitios puede atraer a saqueadores, aunque dijo que no veía un problema mayor mientras no ocurra.
Miotti respondió que no esperaba tanta atención. Dijo que actualizó la entrada apenas le avisaron y que arqueólogos y estudiantes de doctorado le escribieron interesados en su método. Sostiene que los agentes pueden ayudar a ordenar grandes volúmenes de datos, siempre que un experto verifique lo que encuentran.
En su blog, Miotti informó que el sitio quedó en manos del INAH y de los arqueólogos que lo mapearon primero, y que publicará una actualización si surge algo.

articles.title: Black Friday : iPhone, Pixel, Redmi… les prix baissent déjà sur ces 7 smartphones chez Amazon
articles.text:
Amazon n’a pas attendu sa Black Friday Week, annoncée du 19 au 30 novembre : une partie de son rayon smartphones affiche déjà des remises, de l’entrée de gamme 5G jusqu’au très haut de gamme. Nous avons retenu 7 offres, toutes vendues par Amazon, en mesurant chaque remise au prix de lancement quand il est connu et à ce qu’en disent nos tests.
Les smartphones sortis cette année sont arrivés plus chers. Google a lancé ses Pixel 11 Pro 100 € au-dessus de leurs prédécesseurs, et l’iPhone 18 Pro a repris le prix qu’affichait l’iPhone 17 Pro Max l’an dernier. Les baisses appliquées avant le Black Friday du vendredi 27 novembre permettent de rattraper une partie de cette hausse, ou de se tourner vers un modèle de l’an dernier.
Les sept offres couvrent trois marques et toutes les gammes de prix, de 284 € à 1 589 €. En euros, les remises vont de 100 € sur l’iPhone 17 Pro à 340 € sur l’iPhone Air ; en proportion, c’est le milieu de gamme Xiaomi qui baisse le plus, jusqu’à -31 % sur le Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G. Les prix barrés sont les prix conseillés affichés par Amazon, et tous les prix ont été relevés le 12 novembre.
Apple, Google, Xiaomi : les 7 smartphones moins chers chez Amazon
- Apple iPhone 17 Pro 512 Go (Orange) à 1 479 € au lieu de 1579€
- Xiaomi 17T 12 + 512 Go (Bleu) à 603 € au lieu de 803 €
- Google Pixel 11 Pro 256 Go (Brume) à 988 € au lieu de 1 199 €
- Google Pixel 11 Pro XL 1 To (Noir) à 1 589 € au lieu de 1 789 €
- Xiaomi Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G 8 + 512 Go (Violet) à 379 € au lieu de 553 €
- Xiaomi Redmi Note 17 5G 6 + 256 Go (Violet) à 284 € au lieu de 403 €
- Apple iPhone Air 256 Go (Or clair) à 989 € au lieu de 1 329 €
VPN, logiciels, abonnements : les promos à saisir en ce moment
Pour qui chaque offre a du sens
Quatre de ces modèles ont fait l’objet d’un test complet chez nous, et c’est l’iPhone Air qui profite de la plus forte remise en euros. Dans notre test de l’iPhone Air, nous lui avions attribué 8/10 pour sa finesse, son écran très lumineux et ses performances, tout en pointant une autonomie d’une journée, et encore. Voici ce que chaque offre apporte et à qui elle s’adresse.
- Apple iPhone Air : à 989 €, c’est le seul iPhone de la sélection sous les 1 000 €, avec 340 € de moins que le prix conseillé. Épais de 5,6 mm et équipé de la puce A19 Pro, il vise ceux qui veulent un iPhone très léger et acceptent ses concessions : un seul capteur photo à l’arrière, un seul haut-parleur, l’eSIM uniquement et une recharge à prévoir chaque jour.
- Apple iPhone 17 Pro : parmi les modèles que nous avons testés, c’est le mieux noté de la sélection, avec 9/10, pour ses performances, sa chauffe mieux maîtrisée grâce à une chambre à vapeur et sa polyvalence en photo, téléobjectif 4x compris. La remise reste modeste, 100 €, et intéresse surtout ceux qui ont besoin des 512 Go de cette version.
- Google Pixel 11 Pro : à 988 €, il passe 211 € sous son prix de lancement. Nous lui avions donné 8/10 pour son design, son écran plus lumineux, ses fonctions exclusives comme la dictée Rambler et le téléprompteur, et ses qualités de photophone. Son processeur Tensor G6 reste en retrait dans les jeux 3D, et son autonomie ne dépasse pas une grosse journée. Le Pixel 11 Pro XL 1 To, à 1 589 €, apporte surtout un écran plus grand et beaucoup de stockage, sans gain d’autonomie notable selon notre test.
- Xiaomi 17T : c’est l’offre photo de la sélection à moins de 700 €. Son téléobjectif Leica 5x de 50 Mpx, stabilisé, monte jusqu’à un zoom 10x de qualité optique, et il s’accompagne d’un écran AMOLED 120 Hz annoncé à 3 500 nits, d’une batterie de 6 500 mAh et d’une charge à 67 W. Lancé à 749,99 € en 256 Go, il est proposé ici en 512 Go pour 603 €. Nous ne l’avons pas testé : ces caractéristiques sont celles annoncées par Xiaomi.
- Xiaomi Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G : il s’adresse à ceux qui veulent tenir deux jours sans recharger. Sa batterie de 8 340 mAh est annoncée jusqu’à 2,4 jours en usage modéré, son écran AMOLED de 6,83 pouces monte à 3 500 nits et il est certifié IP68 et IP69K. Ce n’est pas un smartphone pour les joueurs : son Snapdragon 6s Gen 4 vise les usages courants, il ne filme pas en 4K et le chargeur n’est pas fourni. À 379 €, il descend 20 € sous le prix que nous avions relayé le 31 octobre.
- Xiaomi Redmi Note 17 5G : le plus abordable des sept, à 284 € en 6 + 256 Go. Il mise sur un écran AMOLED de 6,99 pouces à 120 Hz, une batterie de 7 700 mAh, la certification IP65 et un verre Gorilla Glass 7i. Son Snapdragon 4 Gen 4 suffit aux usages courants, mais la photo repose sur le seul capteur principal de 50 Mpx et l’eSIM n’est pas prise en charge.
Dernier modèle ou modèle de l’an dernier : où se font les économies ?
L’iPhone 17 Pro garde un vrai argument face à son successeur. Lancé au prix de l’ancien iPhone 17 Pro Max, l’iPhone 18 Pro ne mérite pas forcément davantage votre attention, et nous estimons dans notre comparatif des meilleurs smartphones que les meilleures affaires se trouvent plutôt du côté de la génération précédente. Notre test des Pixel 11 Pro tire le même constat chez Google : leur principal adversaire reste le Pixel 10 Pro.
Ces prix peuvent encore bouger pendant la Black Friday Week d’Amazon, du 19 au 30 novembre, sans qu’aucune baisse supplémentaire soit garantie. Sur les deux Redmi, les remises atteignent déjà 30 % et 31 % du prix conseillé ; sur les iPhone et les Pixel, l’écart se mesure surtout en euros, de 100 € à 340 €. Si votre smartphone actuel tient encore quelques semaines, comparer le prix du jour à celui de la fin du mois reste un réflexe utile.
Smartphones en promo pour le Black Friday : vos questions
Quand a lieu la Black Friday Week d’Amazon en 2026 ?
Amazon l’annonce du 19 au 30 novembre sur sa page de promotions. Le Black Friday lui-même tombe le vendredi 27 novembre.
Le Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G est-il livré avec un chargeur ?
Non, aucun chargeur n’est fourni dans la boîte. Pour profiter de la charge HyperCharge 67 W, il faut un chargeur compatible, acheté à part.
L’iPhone Air accepte-t-il une carte SIM physique ?
Non, il fonctionne uniquement en eSIM. Votre opérateur doit donc proposer l’eSIM pour y transférer votre ligne.
Comment profiter des offres exclusives du Black Friday ?
Durant tout le mois de novembre, Clubic vous propose chaque jour des sélections thématiques regroupant les meilleures offres à saisir en direct.
Retrouvez tous les bons plans du Black Friday 2026 sur la page dédiée à l'événement.
Pour les aficionados de X, n'hésitez pas à suivre notre compte Clubic Bons Plans pour être au courant en direct des meilleures offres.

articles.title: Critical Apache HTTP/2 Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code Remotely
articles.text:
A critical flaw in Apache HTTP Server's HTTP/2 module, mod_http2, can let a remote attacker run code on the server. Tracked as CVE-2026-119618, it affects versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70 and is fixed in version 2.4.71, released yesterday.
Only servers with HTTP/2 enabled are affected, according to Red Hat, which ships the server as part of Red Hat Enterprise Linux.
An attacker who can reach the server needs no authentication to exploit the flaw and could take full control of the server process, the Linux vendor says. It rates the flaw 9.8 out of 10 on the CVSS scale.
The vendor's assessment, published yesterday, also says "public research has demonstrated a reliable exploit" against a server in its default configuration with mod_http2 enabled. It does not name or link that research. Security company Wiz said later that day that no exploit was available and that no exploitation in the wild had been reported.
HTTP/2 runs only where the Protocols directive turns it on, as the module documentation explains. The directive uses h2 for HTTP/2 over TLS and h2c for HTTP/2 over plain TCP. It can be set for the whole server or for a single virtual host, so admins should check the server-wide setting and every virtual host.
Standalone builds of the module, released on GitHub as mod_h2, are affected from version 2.0.8 through 2.0.42.
Admins who run the Apache HTTP Server project's own releases should move to version 2.4.71, the fixed release named in its security advisory. That release also fixes a crash in mod_md, rated important, and a one-byte overwrite of stack memory in mod_vhost_alias, rated low.
The distributions in the table below ship their own builds of the server, with their own package version numbers. On Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9, for example, the fix ships as mod_http2-2.0.26-7.el9_9.1.
Red Hat shipped fixes for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 and 10 yesterday and rates the flaw Important on those releases rather than Critical. Their mod_http2 packages give each HTTP/2 stream its own memory allocator, which makes an attack much harder, according to the vendor's severity assessment. Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 and earlier do not contain the vulnerable code.
| Platform | Status | Fixed package | 
|---|---|---|
| Apache HTTP Server project releases | Fixed | 2.4.71 | 
| Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 | Fixed (RHSA-2026:98981) | mod_http2-2.0.26-7.el9_9.1 | 
| Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10 | Fixed (RHSA-2026:98978) | mod_http2-2.0.29-5.el10_3.1 | 
| Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.4 Update Services for SAP Solutions, and 9.6, 9.8, 10.0 and 10.2 Extended Update Support | Fixed (RHSA-2026:98968, RHSA-2026:98954, RHSA-2026:98982, RHSA-2026:98953 and RHSA-2026:98979) | See each advisory | 
| Red Hat Enterprise Linux 6, 7 and 8 | Not affected | None needed | 
| Red Hat JBoss Core Services and Red Hat Hardened Images | Affected, no fix listed | None listed | 
| Debian unstable (sid) | Fixed | apache2 2.4.71-1 | 
| Debian bookworm, trixie and forky | Vulnerable | None listed | 
| Amazon Linux 2 (Core), Amazon Linux 2023 and Amazon Linux 2027 Preview | Pending fix | None listed | 
| Ubuntu | No status page | None listed | 
The Debian rows come from Debian's security tracker, and the Amazon row from the Amazon Linux tracker. Ubuntu's CVE tracker had no page for the flaw when The Hacker News checked it today.
The Apache HTTP Server advisory offers no workaround. In its vulnerability analysis, Wiz advises admins who cannot update yet to remove h2 and h2c from the Protocols directive, leaving Protocols http/1.1.
The standalone mod_h2 project has published no fixed release so far. Its release list on GitHub ends at 2.0.42, the last affected version, and its repository has been read-only since it was archived on June 9. The Protocols change above also applies to servers that use those builds.
The flaw was reported on October 26 by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, a free scanning service for open-source projects that uses the company's AI models. Anthony Weems and Simon Scannell of Google Cloud Vulnerability Research reported it last week.
An earlier HTTP/2 flaw, CVE-2026-23918, was fixed in version 2.4.67, released on May 4. Servers updated to that release, or to any later one up to 2.4.70, still run a version that the new flaw affects.

articles.title: Microsoft Outlook is down for many: Here's what we know
articles.text:
Microsoft Outlook is down for many: Here's what we know
Office, Outlook, and other Microsoft services appear to be having major issues
Microsoft Outlook might be down for many. Reports of outages from across the US started coming in around 12:30 PM ET. On DownDetector, there are over 120,000 concurrent reports.
Other connected services like Microsoft Teams. Microsoft 365, Copilot, and Ondreive are also gettign reports. More tellingly,. we could not open Microsoft's own services status ((https://status.cloud.microsoft/) page to check on the status of Microsoft services.
Microsoft's cloud services, Azure, also had reports of service issues, which may account for the wide-spread nature of these outages.
On social media, people have bene reporting their inability to reach the services like Outlook. On X (formerly Twitter) is where we saw evidence that the outage may extend globally.
Follow along as we track this continuing, and apparently widespread Outlook outage.
Our first indication that something was awry with Outlook was on Downdetector, which noted a sharp rise in reports of service outages for Outlook. Microsoft 365, Microsoft Store, Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Teams, OneDrive, and Microsoft Azure.
It's worth noting that users report these issues to Downdetector. Microsoft has yet to comment or confirm any of this.
We've contacted Microsoft for comment and will update this live blog when they reply.
Not everything is offline
There are some indications that the situation is worsening. While we were able to access OneDrive online 30 minutes ago, the site is no longer responding.
The pain is being felt by individuals and organizations, such as universities, where entire email systems are now inaccessible.
When one service catches a cold...
A look at DownDetector indicates that it's not just Outlook and Microsoft services that are struggling. However, these user-based reports can be misleading. Sometimes when people can't access one service connected to larger services, they assume it's their local one.
We checked, for instance, AWS's status page and found no widespread reports of outages.
Microsoft knows
A Microsoft 365 support account has acknowledged the issues across "the Americas" and wrote, "We're investigating reports of users experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas. More details can be found in the Microsoft 365 admin center under EX1550543."
So they're investigating, but there's no news of a fix, just that they're working to mitigate it.
What, we work?
Millions rely on Microsoft tools like Outlook and OneDrive to get work done. When they're offline, well, as you can see below, things kind of slow down.
We're still not here
By 2:25 PM ET, DownDetector was showing a small slowdown in outage reports across Microsoft services, but social media is still filled with posts about the ongoing Outlook outage that is across the US and the rest of the Americas.
Some perspective
Sure, millions can't access work and personal emails, but they still have social media where they can complain or at least take their minds off the fact that a huge chunk of Microsoft products are currently not functioning. As this X user notes, at least social media isn't out.
What is real
As we noted earlier, big outages like this can have a knock-on effect. That's likely why cloud provider Cloudflare has popped up here on DownDetector, along with Google and Gmail. To be clear, there's no other indication that these services are experiencing similar outages.
Microsoft's status page still isn't loading
We're still waiting for another update from Microsoft 365 Status on X (formerly Twitter), but if you're hoping to check the company's direct status page, you'll hit a roadblock. Why? Well, the actual status page appears to be down as well and will not load.
Let's take a look at Down Detector
Alright, it's clear that the main services seeing outages, and in turn being effectively down for users right now, are Outlook as well as Microsoft 365, but Down Detector is currently showing a slight dip towards recovery. Even so, many users are still reporting errors.
In fact, even with the dip, Microsoft Outlook still shows over 77,000 reports. That is down from the high, as of yet, of over 131,000 reports.
Microsoft is rolling out a fix or two
Some good news correlating with that slight dip on Down Detector: it appears that Microsoft's team is on the case and is now testing a fix, well, more specifically, two fixes concurrently. It seems that a main culprit was servers failing automated health checks and, as a result, becoming unavailable to users.
To address that, Microsoft is testing a configuration change and, at the same time, restarting each affected service to let them 'return to service.' That's a good sign all around.
While Microsoft's teams are working on a fix, impacted folks are still taking to social networks like X and Threads to comment and even offer a bit of joy in light of not being able to use Outlook or other 365 essentials.
Microsoft's 365 Status page is back online
This is likely a good sign — Microsoft's own 365 Status Page is back up and loading again, confirming the active issue: "Service degradation on Microsoft 365 (Business or Enterprise)."
The message reads in full:
User impact: Users may be unable to connect to multiple Microsoft 365 services. 
More info: Potentially impacted services include:
- Exchange Online
- Microsoft Teams
- SharePoint Online
- Microsoft Copilot 365
- Microsoft Defender XDR
Current status: We're aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact. As a precaution, we've paused all deployments and configuration changes while we review recent changes for any correlation to this event. We've determined that the elevated load isn't driven by an overall increase in traffic, but by a large number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable, which is shifting load onto the remaining infrastructure. We're investigating what's causing these servers to become unavailable while we work to safely return them to service. 
Scope of impact: This issue may affect users attempting to access the affected Microsoft 365 services. 
Next update by: Thursday, November 12, 2026, at 10:00 PM UTC
Microsoft has provided another update on the 365 Status account on X, writing, "We've not identified any recent change correlated with the start of impact; however, our investigation indicates the failed health checks may originate from a specific component that's responsible for processing server health."
It continues, "We've taken steps to prevent additional servers from being impacted while we work to return the affected servers to service." So it's clear there is some more work to do to get this resolved, and it is focused on mitigating further impact on the affected servers. We're waiting for a solution to resolve the issues. Let us know in the comments if you're still impacted.
You have to laugh, right?
When times get tough, humor carries the day. Posts across social media feature people venting their anger, frustration, and concern, but there are the jokers. This Threads post on the ongoing outage was one of our favorites.
A silver lining for one?
You know the one person who might be happy about this outage? Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. This is the one tech story big enough (the outage spans countries) to push aside the wild story of his ouster. Leaves us wondering if Nvidia is a Microsoft services house.
Also, shouldn't AI be able to figure out what's going on here?
We're almost back, baby
We may be turning a corner. Microsoft at 402PM ET reported on X that it had built and validated a new "alternative health check method" to replace the one that kept shutting services down. The fix is so good that "a subset of affected servers" have now "successfully returned to service."
Microsoft adds that an automated system is checking on unresponsive servers and restarting them.
Put another way, it looks like, while Microsoft may not have discovered the root cause, it has built and deployed a fix. Your Outlook might be back before you know it.
A full report on status
You can tell the situation is improving because we can finally access the Microsoft 365 Service Health Status page, and it has a lot of information about all the services affected by this Outlook (and more) outage.
If you want all the latest details on the service disruption, this might be a good page to bookmark.
Fixing slowly
We're not out of the woods yet. Your current blog author (Lance Ulanoff) just tried to access his OneDrive and... well, you can see the result. Clearly, Microsoft's fix is rolling out slowly, and it now seems unlikely this will all be resolved before the end of the workday (on the East Coast, at least).
What's your experience been like? Can you access any of Microsoft's online and cloud-connected services? Let us know in the comments.
Talk about not getting schooled
Is the Microsoft Outlook outage a good enough excuse for your teachers and college professors? I've noticed some students, like this one, complaining online that they have assignments to turn in. I guess many of them use Outlook and other Microsoft 365 services like OneDrive.
Wonder if searches for Google Drive and Google Workspace are on the rise.
Let's take a look at the current status of Microsoft's 365 and Outlook outage — as of now, it's still unresolved, and Down Detector is still showing over 40,000 reports of issues. That's down from a high of over 131,000, but it's still a mixed bag, with access not back for everyone or even most users.
Here's what the current, most recent update on the Microsoft 365 Status page shows:
Current status: We’re continuing to pursue all available pathways to restore service, as our actions taken thus far have not provided the anticipated relief. Our investigation has found that a core process on the affected servers is becoming overwhelmed, which causes the servers to stop responding and contributes to the capacity loss.
To validate a potential recovery approach, we're fully isolating a portion of our service infrastructure, restarting the affected components, and gradually reintroducing traffic to confirm our services remain stable before applying this approach more broadly. We're also analyzing traffic patterns across our entire service infrastructure and evaluating whether isolating traffic within each region may allow affected regions to recover independently.
Slow and steady recovery
Microsoft's work to restore Outlook services to millions of users across the Amnericas continues and it sounds like they may finally have a handle on things. In a new update from around 6:05PM ET, Microsoft reports returning servers to service (always a good sign) and that "they remain stable so far."
The other thing Microsoft notes that I think it'll be good for Microsoft customers to keep in mind as the recovery continues is that access to affected services like email may be gradual. You're inbox may not fill out in one fell-swoop. You may get chunks of emails or maybe none for a while as the servers are all stuffed with a backlog. We caution patience.
Maybe wait until tomorrow. By then, I bet it'll be all clear and you'll be back to emailing, Teaming, accessing files, and being buried by work.
Beware Outlook scams
As Outlook comes back online, you may also receive texts and emails telling you that you need to reset a password or click a link to restore your account.
Do not fall for it.
These phishing attempts will try to use social engineering to fool you into sharing your Outlook credentials. They might try now because they know you're anxious to get back into your email. Microsoft won't ask you to do these things. So be extra cautious as the whole system slowly comes back online.
You must confirm your public display name before commenting
Please logout and then login again, you will then be prompted to enter your display name.

articles.title: Google ahora te deja abrir tu casa con el celular: solo necesitas acercar tu Android a la puerta
articles.text:
Google incorporó llaves digitales para el hogar a Google Wallet, una función que permitirá a los usuarios de Android abrir cerraduras inteligentes compatibles al acercar el teléfono o, en algunos casos, de forma automática al aproximarse a la puerta.
La novedad está disponible en vista previa pública dentro de la aplicación Google Home y llegará al resto de los usuarios durante las próximas semanas.
Para usarla, se necesita una cerradura inteligente compatible con los estándares Matter y Aliro, un hub de Google habilitado para Matter y un teléfono Android compatible.
La llave digital queda vinculada a la vivienda configurada en Google Home, no a una única cerradura.
Así, una misma credencial puede utilizarse en todas las cerraduras Aliro compatibles de ese hogar y cada integrante de la casa puede añadir su propia llave a su cuenta personal de Google Wallet.
Cómo funciona Google Wallet para abrir una casa
La primera alternativa es Tap to Unlock. El usuario debe acercar la parte trasera de un teléfono Android con NFC al lector de la cerradura para abrir la puerta.
La llave puede funcionar incluso con la pantalla bloqueada, aunque es posible modificar los requisitos de verificación desde Google Wallet.
La segunda opción es Unlock on Approach, que permite desbloquear la puerta sin contacto al detectar que el usuario se acerca. Esta función debe activarse manualmente desde Google Wallet y exige que tanto el teléfono como la cerradura sean compatibles con Ultra-Wideband (UWB) y el estándar Aliro.
El sistema requiere un Google Hub compatible con Matter y Thread Border Router, como Nest Hub de segunda generación, Nest Hub Max, Nest Wifi Pro o Google TV Streamer.
Para abrir mediante NFC, se necesita un teléfono con Android 9 o posterior; la apertura automática solo está disponible en teléfonos Android compatibles con Aliro UWB, entre ellos los modelos de la serie Google Pixel 10 Pro y superiores. Los relojes con Wear OS no son compatibles en el lanzamiento.
Cómo agregar llaves digitales a Google Wallet
Antes de comenzar, el usuario debe instalar las versiones más recientes de Google Home y Google Wallet en su teléfono Android.
Al configurar una cerradura compatible con Matter y Aliro en Google Home, la aplicación ofrecerá la opción de añadir la llave digital directamente a Google Wallet.
Es posible agregarla más adelante desde Google Home, en la ruta Configuración de la casa > Llave de Google Wallet, o desde los ajustes de la cerradura.
Una vez incorporada, el usuario puede administrar la apertura al aproximarse, exigir el desbloqueo del dispositivo antes de abrir la puerta o eliminar la llave desde Google Wallet.
Entre las cerraduras compatibles en el lanzamiento figuran Aqara u400, Schlage Sense Pro —con NFC disponible inicialmente y UWB previsto para una actualización posterior— y Nuki Keypad 2 NFC.
Los miembros del hogar vinculados a la misma cuenta de Google Home pueden sumar su propia llave digital a Google Wallet, mientras que los visitantes temporales pueden recibir códigos de acceso desde la aplicación.
Google llevó Gemini Intelligence a los Pixel 10
Google lanzó una actualización para los Pixel que incorpora Gemini Intelligence a la serie Pixel 10, con herramientas de IA para ordenar dictados y automatizar tareas cotidianas.
Una de las novedades es Rambler, que transforma mensajes de voz en textos más claros al eliminar muletillas y dar formato al contenido.
Asimismo, llega Create My Widget, una función que permite crear widgets mediante descripciones escritas, como un control de gastos, información sobre un partido o una cuenta regresiva de viaje.
La herramienta puede usar datos de Gmail, Calendar y el buscador. Además, los Pixel 10 reciben sugerencias proactivas y resúmenes de conversaciones largas en nuevos idiomas, incluido español.
Google también amplió a Reino Unido, India y Japón una función de Gemini para realizar gestiones en aplicaciones, como pedir comida, solicitar transporte o buscar restaurantes. Por otra parte, los equipos desde Pixel 6a suman diez estilos de íconos personalizados generados por IA.

articles.title: Samsung amplia lista de celulares com One UI 9 no Brasil • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Samsung amplia lista de celulares com One UI 9 no Brasil
Galaxy A15 e A17 5G, além de A34 e A54, começaram a receber o Android 17 com One UI 9 na última semana.
Promessa é dívida, e a Samsung está pagando: os smartphones Galaxy A15 5G, Galaxy A17 5G, Galaxy A34 e Galaxy A54 vendidos no Brasil estão recebendo a versão mais recente do Android (17) com a One UI 9.
O Galaxy A15 5G e o Galaxy A54 receberam a atualização na quinta-feira passada (05/11), enquanto o Galaxy A17 5G passou a receber na segunda (09/11). Já o Galaxy A34 aparenta ter recebido a atualização ontem (11/11).
Embora o changelog do aparelho ainda não registre a novidade, podemos confirmar que a atualização já está disponível para o modelo.
Para os modelos A34 e A54, esta será a última atualização de versão do Android oferecida pela Samsung, cumprindo a promessa de 4 atualizações de versão para os modelos. De agora em diante, eles passam a receber apenas patches de segurança e talvez a One UI 9.5, ainda em desenvolvimento.
Entre os modelos vendidos no Brasil, a Samsung ainda precisa atualizar:
A descrição oficial da Samsung diz o seguinte: “A One UI 9 aproxima o Galaxy AI do seu dia a dia com experiências mais úteis e intuitivas. Aproveite novas formas de simplificar tarefas, criar e manter-se conectado com funções de IA que se adaptam à maneira como você usa o seu Galaxy.”
Esta nova versão da One UI é baseada no Android 17, o mais recente liberado pelo Google. Entre as novidades de software estão o Now Brief e o New Nudge mais inteligentes, a partir das informações que o sistema captura no próprio telefone da pessoa.
Outra função recente é o aplicativo My FanCam, capaz de analisar vídeos e produzir cortes focando em pessoas específicas. Ele foi originalmente apresentado junto com a safra 2026 de telefones dobráveis.
Por serem modelos intermediários e de entrada, os modelos atualizados pode não receber todos os novos recursos da One UI 9, ao contrário de modelos das linhas Z e S.

articles.title: AMD Patches Radeon SSD Write Bug in Adrenalin 26.11.1 Optional Driver
articles.text:
Thursday, November 12th 2026
AMD Patches Radeon SSD Write Bug in Adrenalin 26.11.1 Optional Driver
AMD's Adrenalin 26.11.1 optional driver is now available with the promised fix for the Radeon bug that kept system drives writing in the background. According to the release notes, the update addresses excessive writes to the system drive while the PC is idle on Radeon RX 7000 series cards and newer. It also fixes a related case where excessive writes could show up while moving or resizing application windows.
AMD confirmed the problem earlier this week, tracing it to the External Events Client Module (atieclxx.exe) in the 26.10.1 and 26.10.2 drivers. User reports put the write rate anywhere from 0.3 MB/s to 5 MB/s, which works out to roughly 26 GB to 432 GB a day on a machine that's doing nothing. Until now, affected users had to disable the External Events Utility, turn off Resizable BAR, or use a community-made open-source tool that blocks the writes. The release notes only mention RX 7000 and newer for the idle fix, so it isn't clear whether older Radeon cards were affected at all.
DOWNLOAD: AMD Software Adrenalin 26.11.1 OptionalThe driver does come with a fairly long list of known issues, including crashes or driver timeouts in Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced, War Thunder, and Cyberpunk 2077, plus visual corruption in Phantom Blade Zero and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare Remastered on RX 9000 cards. AMD also notes that Smart Access Memory may get disabled after installation on Windows 10, so anyone who switched off Resizable BAR as a workaround should make sure it's back on after updating. The full changelog is pasted below.
Fixed Issues
- Excessive writes to the system drive may be observed while the system is idle on Radeon RX 7000 series graphics products and above.
- Excessive writes to the system drive may be observed while moving or resizing application windows.
Known Issues
- Intermittent application crash or driver timeout may be observed while playing Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced on Radeon RX 7000 series graphics products.
- Intermittent driver timeout may be observed while playing War Thunder on Radeon RX 5000 series graphics products. Users experiencing this issue are recommended to use AMD Software: Adrenalin Edition 26.9.1.
- Intermittent application crash or driver timeout may be observed while playing Cyberpunk 2077 with AMD FSR Upscaling, AMD Radeon Anti-Lag and in-game frame generation enabled during video playback on a secondary display on some Radeon RX 9000 series graphics products. Users experiencing this issue are recommended to disable in-game frame generation.
- Call of Duty : Modern Warfare Remastered may become unresponsive while using Alt+Tab during gameplay on Ryzen AI Max PRO 400 Series processors.
- Black screen may be observed when launching Gears of War: Reloaded on AMD Ryzen AI 9 400 Series processors. Users experiencing this issue are recommended to switch the in-game display mode to Windowed and then back to Fullscreen.
- Failure to install may be observed while installing AI Bundle components in some regions with limited access to HuggingFace and GitHub.
- AMD Smart Access Memory may become disabled after driver installation on Windows 10 systems.
- Visual corruption may appear on character hair while playing Phantom Blade Zero on Radeon RX 9000 series graphics products. Users experiencing this issue are recommended to disable the High-Quality Hair setting in the game.
- Black corruption may be observed while playing Call of Duty : Modern Warfare Remastered on Radeon RX 9000 series graphics products.

articles.title: Disney+ casse ses prix avec cette nouvelle promo !
articles.text:
Dans quelques semaines, c'est le Black Friday. Et Disney+ prend les devants avec une offre qui va faire parler !
Parmi les plateformes de streaming, Disney+ est une des options les plus sexy, avec une offre qui ne cesse de s'enrichir - jusqu'à potentiellement bientôt s'ouvrir à la Ligue 1. Alors, pour ceux qui regardent les grands noms du secteur et qui peuvent chercher à ouvrir un nouvel abonnement, ce que propose aujourd'hui Disney+ comme promotion devrait attirer l'oeil.
Disney+ met le paquet pour le Black Friday !
À la fin du mois, c'est le Black Friday. Mais Disney+ prend de l'avance, avec cette nouvelle promotion, qui court du mercredi 11 novembre au mardi 24 novembre. Une promotion qui va réduire l'ensemble des offres proposées par Disney+.
Pour rappel, le groupe américain déploie trois types de souscriptions différentes (Standard avec publicité, Standard et Premium). Et la nouvelle offre promotionnelle qui vient d'être lancée par Disney+ permet de réduire le prix de l'abonnement pour les deux premiers mois.
De 2 à 5 € par mois d'économie grâce à cette promo
Pour ce qui est du rabais en lui-même, il faut noter que Disney+ va permettre d'économiser entre 2 et 5 euros par mois, selon le type d'abonnemement qui sera pris. Dans le détail, cela donne :
- Standard avec publicité : passe de 6,99 à 4,99 € par mois (2 € d'économies) ;
- Standard : passe de 10,99 à 7,99 € par mois (3 € d'économies) ;
- Premium : passe de 15,99 à 10,99 € par mois (5 € d'économies).
Évidemment, cette promotion ne s'applique pas aux abonnés actuels. Seuls les nouveaux clients, ainsi que les anciens n'ayant plus d'abonnement actif, peuvent bénéficier de ces prix pour deux mois. La promotion est sans engagement, ce qui signifie que vous pourrez résilier l'abonnement Disney+ à l'issue des deux mois à prix réduit.

articles.title: ScreenConnect Attacks Target at Least 288 Endpoints Across 48 Organizations With Rogue Clients
articles.text:
ConnectWise has taken the precautionary step of disabling five third-party extensions in partner environments following reports of unauthorized access.
In an advisory posted on its site, the company said there is no evidence that the incident involves a compromise of its infrastructure or a vulnerability in the ScreenConnect software.
"Our initial assessment suggests the activity may involve a threat actor's abuse of independent third-party extensions installed in partner environments," it said. "We are continuing to validate this assessment. The initial access method and full scope remain under investigation."
ConnectWise has identified about 400 partner environments with at least one of the third-party extensions installed. It also emphasized that the presence of the extensions alone does not indicate or establish compromise.
While these extensions provide an API capable of executing remote commands, access to that API is secured by a passphrase configured by the partner during setup, it added. The list of extensions identified for precautionary disabling is below -
- Labtech Plus
- RMM Plus
- RMM+
- RMM Plus Password Link
- RMM+ Password Link
ConnectWise also said it has urged on-premises partners to disable the extensions, and is recommending all partners to ensure security controls are running, preserve suspicious activity logs, and stay vigilant for -
- Unusual sign-ins, unfamiliar locations, repeated login failures, and unexpected multi-factor authentication (MFA) prompts
- New administrator accounts or changes to user permissions
- Unexpected extension installations, remote commands, and Toolbox activity
- Unapproved remote-access software on customer devices and technician workstations
- Unexpected support requests, password-reset messages, and software downloads through a trusted channel
The company has shared the following indicators of compromise (IoCs) -
- 
    IP addresses:
    
  - 185.99.255[.]28
  - 155.94.150[.]39
- 
    Domains and URLs: 
    
  - ns[.]mo7sen[.]dev
  - ns[.]mo7sen[.]dev/EadF.php?p=4
  - sc[.]payproofkit[.]com
  - cdn007-digitaldownloads[.]com
  - newnewnew[.]gotdns[.]org
  - Soxnewwork[.]homedns[.]org
- 
    Artifacts:
    
  - sckit-run.bat
  - sckit-decoder.ps1
  - TrapWatch.ps1
  - Panel-Lateral.ps1
  - Run-Lateral-Full.bat
  - runnew.cmd
  - ToolboxRelayUploader.exe
  - Sqlite3.exe
Cybersecurity company Huntress, which is also tracking the activity, said it has observed attackers using access to cloud-hosted ScreenConnect panels to push Run commands with an aim to install rogue ScreenConnect clients on at least 288 managed endpoints across 48 organizations. The activity was first detected on November 11, 2026, at around 5:47 p.m. UTC.
Huntress told The Hacker News that it has not seen evidence of a new vulnerability, but noted the exact method through which the attacker got panel access remains unclear. Current telemetry points to compromised credentials or hijacked operator sessions to gain initial access, it said.
The overall attack unfolds in a worm-like fashion using a two-step process -
- Initial access: Attackers use a compromised ScreenConnect panel's Run Command feature to deploy a rogue ScreenClient client across endpoints, creating a persistent backdoor that no longer depends on the original panel.
- Lateral movement: When a technician connects to an infected endpoint through ScreenConnect, the malware can spread back to their workstation, steal saved browser sessions and authentication tokens, and pivot to other ScreenConnect panels the technician has access to.
"The rogue clients deliver SCKit, a custom malicious toolkit that establishes persistent remote access and creates a relay trap for intercepting session cookies," Huntress researchers Ben Nahorney and Susannah Matt said.
"The infection path works in two stages: from an infected endpoint to a technician who connects to it, and from a technician's workstation to every endpoint their panel can connect to. However, not all functionality has been observed during observed incidents; some functionality has been discovered through analysing the payloads."
SCKit is delivered as an encrypted payload and via a Base64-encoded dropper ("sckit-run.bat"), which then contacts a remote server to fetch a PowerShell payload ("sckit-decoder.ps1") that's responsible for launching the toolkit.
Other components of the malware are designed to add Microsoft Defender exclusions, install a second attacker-controlled ScreenConnect client, create a scheduled task named "TrapWatch," and replace the legitimate ScreenConnect installation with an attacker-controlled copy.
There are signs that at least one of the scripts is generated by a large language model (LLM) based on the detailed source code references and comments that explain its functionality.
"Going beyond what we've observed, we've reconstructed an additional functionality intended to spread from a technician's workstation to the ScreenConnect panel," Huntress said. "This has been discovered from analysis of its scripts, configuration, and tools. To date we have not observed a successful jump from an infected endpoint to a technician workstation, or from that workstation to other endpoints."
This involves abusing the connection to fetch a dropper ("Run-Lateral-Full.bat"), which then connects to an external server ("ns.mo7sen[.]dev") to download a loader that gathers the workstation's unique ID, sends it back to the attacker, and returns a tailored encrypted kit for that specific workstation -
- "Panel-Lateral.ps1," which in conjunction with "LabConfig.ps1," steals the .aspxauth session cookie from the workstation and attempts to replay the cookie against the panel and get the tokens necessary to enumerate any other sessions the technician can access.
- "ToolboxRelayUploader.exe," which leverages access gained to any other sessions to upload a payload, "WithUninstall.ps1," to the panel's Shared Toolbox.
"A panel request tells every reachable session to run the toolbox item," Huntress said. "This payload is designed to run as SYSTEM on those endpoints, installing the trap and extending the cycle. Roughly 60 seconds after the broadcast, ToolboxRelayUploader.exe deletes the Shared Toolbox item."
To add to the concern, the threat actor has been observed tagging each compromised managed service provider (MSP) with a sequential number. Huntress said the tags it has observed start partway through the sequence, indicating other MSPs may have been compromised earlier. ScreenConnect users are advised to check their Run Command history even if they haven't received alerts.
In a separate alert, Sophos said it has also observed unauthorized ScreenConnect client deployments following the same modus operandi. The activity has originated from three ScreenConnect instance IDs -
- d905b2b1b165d0a9
- 4b8f4089ddaac6a9
- df1f7ef0cfacd0d8
It's suspected that these are compromised instances that are being used to execute commands and deploy additional malicious instances, whose IDs are below -
- 2588ef5c15954b10
- ed630cc2c873b091
"Curl.exe downloaded ScreenConnect.ClientSetup.msi from 185.99.255[.]28 to C:\Windows\TEMP\sc.msi," Sophos explained. "A ScreenConnect-generated command file then launched msiexec.exe to install the client silently. The researchers also observed ScreenConnect scripts staging batch files and using PowerShell with execution-policy bypass to retrieve a second-stage script from ns[.]mo7sen[.]dev/EadF.php?p=4."
(This is a developing story. Please check back for more details.)

articles.title: GPU Taskman, la nueva herramienta de Microsoft para conocer en qué se usa la memoria de video de la PC
articles.text:
Microsoft desarrolló una herramienta de código abierto que desglosa, proceso por proceso, el consumo de memoria de video de una computadora. Se llama GPU Taskman y nace como una respuesta a una limitación conocida del Administrador de tareas de Windows: este indica cuánta memoria gráfica se está utilizando, pero no aclara qué aplicaciones o modelos la están consumiendo.
El proyecto fue creado por Scott Hanselman, vicepresidente y miembro del personal técnico en Microsoft y GitHub. Se trata de una iniciativa personal del ingeniero, publicada en su propio repositorio de GitHub, y no de un producto oficial de la compañía. Hanselman invitó a la comunidad de desarrolladores a sumar mejoras mediante pull requests, lo que ubica al proyecto en una fase temprana de desarrollo: actualmente se encuentra en la versión 0,35 y requiere validaciones adicionales según el hardware utilizado.
Qué información muestra la herramienta
GPU Taskman combina en una sola interfaz datos que hasta ahora aparecían dispersos o directamente no estaban disponibles. La herramienta reúne el consumo de VRAM por proceso individual, la memoria del sistema accesible por la GPU y telemetría de hardware que incluye temperatura, consumo energético, frecuencias de reloj, actividad de memoria y estadísticas de PCIe.
A diferencia del Administrador de tareas, que ofrece una cifra global de memoria ocupada sin distinguir su origen, GPU Taskman identifica qué parte de la VRAM corresponde a un modelo de inteligencia artificial, a un navegador, al compositor del escritorio o a cualquier otro proceso en ejecución. Esta capacidad de distinguir entre tipos de carga de trabajo permite determinar con precisión qué aplicación está saturando la memoria gráfica.
Su aporte para los modelos de inteligencia artificial locales
Uno de los aspectos centrales de la herramienta es su capacidad para analizar cargas de trabajo de IA que se ejecutan de manera local en el equipo, en lugar de en la nube. GPU Taskman puede identificar los modelos compatibles y desglosar su consumo de memoria entre los pesos del modelo, la caché KV y los búferes de cálculo.
Por el momento, la utilidad reconoce entornos como llama.cpp, Ollama y LM Studio. Cada modelo de lenguaje cargado reserva una porción fija de VRAM, y el resto de las aplicaciones abiertas debe repartirse lo que queda disponible. Visualizar ese reparto con claridad permite anticipar problemas de rendimiento antes de que el sistema comience a funcionar con lentitud sin una causa aparente.
Utilidad para equipos de uso gráfico intensivo
La herramienta también resulta de interés para quienes utilizan computadoras orientadas a videojuegos o edición de video, tareas que compiten por el mismo recurso limitado que representa la VRAM. GPU Taskman permite detectar picos de consumo de memoria gráfica, un fenómeno que puede traducirse en problemas de stuttering o tirones durante el uso del equipo.
Según plantea su creador en el repositorio, el objetivo del proyecto es ofrecer una vía más transparente para entender el rendimiento del hardware, en un contexto en el que crecen las cargas de inteligencia artificial que se ejecutan directamente en el equipo.
Compatibilidad y forma de instalación
GPU Taskman es compatible tanto con tarjetas gráficas de NVIDIA como de AMD. Su creador no confirmó, hasta el momento, soporte para gráficas Intel. La herramienta puede instalarse en Windows 10 y 11, Linux, macOS, WSL y sistemas Apple Silicon.
Para utilizarla alcanza con descargar los archivos del proyecto desde GitHub, sin necesidad de registro ni licencia alguna. Al tratarse de un desarrollo de código abierto, cualquier usuario puede revisar, descargar o modificar el código sin costo.

United Airlines bane agentes de IA na compra de passagens
A United justifica a restrição pela proteção de dados sensíveis, pelo risco de erros operacionais e por exigências regulatórias.
Embora esta (ainda) não seja uma prática amplamente disseminada, já há pessoas por aí usando agentes de IA para automatizar diversos tipos de compras, entre elas, a de passagens aéreas. Mas, alegando preocupações sobre privacidade e segurança, a United Airlines decidiu restringir o uso desse tipo de tecnologia em seus aplicativos e sites.
Agentes de inteligência artificial consistem em mecanismos que podem realizar determinadas tarefas para o usuário, atuando quase como se fossem pessoas que executam um trabalho específico.
Entre esses trabalhos está justamente o de aquisição de passagens aéreas: o agente pode ser instruído a fechar a compra quando o preço de determinado trecho chega a um patamar predefinido ou fazer um upgrade de categoria se encontrar uma condição especial, por exemplo.
Mas, nesta semana, a United Airlines anunciou a decisão de impedir que agentes pessoais de IA não autorizados acessem as suas plataformas para executar tarefas como:
As restrições passam a valer não somente para o site e os aplicativos da companhia aérea, como também para acessos feitos por meio de plataformas de terceiros, a exemplo de sistemas operados por agências de viagem.
A decisão da United Airlines de restringir o acesso de agentes de IA a seus sistemas está baseada em três argumentos principais:
Ainda não há uma data exata para as restrições começarem, muito menos sabe-se quais agentes de IA serão afetados. É de presumir, porém, que a medida atingirá soluções de plataformas como Meta Muse, ChatGPT (Dots) e Instinct.

articles.title: CDPR Feels "Great Responsibility" After Witcher 4 Wins Most Wanted Game Award
articles.text:
Thursday, November 12th 2026
CDPR Feels "Great Responsibility" After Witcher 4 Wins Most Wanted Game Award
The Witcher 4 has been voted Most Wanted Game at the Golden Joystick Awards 2026, beating the likes of Fable and Resident Evil Veronica. CD Projekt Red production director Małgorzata Mitręga accepted the award near the end of the November 11 show, just before Resident Evil Requiem was crowned the night's big winner. It's a step up from last year, when The Witcher 4 came in a close second in the same category with 16.68% of the vote against GTA 6's 18.03%. GTA 6, which launches on November 19, wasn't on this year's ballot. Here's what Mitręga said on stage:
This is a huge, huge honor for us, but it's also a great responsibility. We all know it. We are working hard, giving heart and soul there, all the skills we have, passion we have, and moments like that are such a boost for us, for the stamina, to (keep) it going, to deliver (for) you when the time is right.
The Witcher 3 also had a good night, with its Remastered re-release from September winning Best Remake/Remaster. That brings the 2015 RPG to 12 Golden Joysticks, more than any other game in the show's history. That tally includes the Studio of the Year prizes CDPR won during its original run and a Best Performance award for Geralt actor Doug Cockle. With the Songs of the Past expansion due in 2027, that number may keep climbing. The Witcher 4, on the other hand, is still a while away. CDPR is targeting a 2028 release window for that one. Of course, "targeting" is not a promise, so 2028 is best treated as a goal for now.
Source:
				GamesRadar+

This is just monthly news to say 'Hey guys Witcher 4 still a thing don't forget us'
A 'Most Wanted' Award? Please tell us again you have nothing of substance without telling us there is no substance. I get strong 'oh great leader!' vibes from thisI think we have to conclude The Witcher franchise is now firmly in the Mainstream Cesspool segment of gaming. There are still occasionally worthwhile games in that segment but its like you say, a bit of a wasteland the last five to ten years, it starts to feel like the umpteenth Netflix Original you've already/never seen, or that 'epic football match' between two teams we've already watched a few dozen times. The typical you know what you'll get, slight plot twist included, now gimme my bag of crisps and don't think too hard about what you're actually doing, type of entertainment.
But the reality is, every Witcher fan that stayed for longer than part 3 knows the game has to offer more than that. Cyberpunk is being dragged on not because of its quality content, but because of graphics posterchild and silly cosmetic content. I hope that's not the writing on the wall here, and the loss of Geralt brings us a mind blowing narrative we just can't fault. Tall order, especially given the fact there is an actual Witcher universe now, with seasonal series, spinoffs etc.

articles.title: 'The next chapter is shaped by what education leaders are asking for': Microsoft is pulling free emails for schools, colleges, and universities — who now face big bills to keep student mailboxes
articles.text:
'The next chapter is shaped by what education leaders are asking for': Microsoft is pulling free emails for schools, colleges, and universities — who now face big bills to keep student mailboxes
Free as in not
- Free Microsoft Exchange email provision is being pulled from Microsoft 365 Education
- Microsoft has refreshed its 365 Education portfolio, swapping its feature-packed free tier with a stripped back option without email
- The Office 365 A1 plan will be retired on January 1, 2028, with an extension for any customers already enrolled to the end of the period
Microsoft has announced an "evolution" to its Microsoft 365 Education portfolio that will see the removal of free email for students as the popular free tier A1 (also known as MA1) is being retired on January 1, 2028.
The A1 tier offered free Microsoft Exchange access for students (the Student Use Benefit program) requiring emails with from their school, college, or university. Many institutions rely on the roll-call of email addresses to distribute work and integrate student accounts with other services.
While any customers with existing enrollments prior to January 1, 2028 will get a term-long extension, Microsoft’s announcement presents a big headache for administrators at educational facilities around the world. The decision also affects the free Exchange Online for Alumni provision, which is also set to be cancelled.
Squeezed education
The announcement, made on the Microsoft website, adds a new tier, Microsoft 365 Education A7, which includes Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Agent 365 among other additional features. But it is the removal of the A1 plan and loss of free email for students which will have the biggest impact.
The education sector is experiencing numerous funding issues at the moment, challenges that don’t only exist in the UK. But certainly for educators across British universities and colleges, where Microsoft 365 is preferred over Google Docs (more commonly found in schools), this news represents a huge budgetary challenge.
License flexibility and transition planning have been explained within the announcement, but the pricing structure is also changing for Microsoft 365 Education plans, effective from the same January 1, 2028 date.
The company states: “Office 365 A1 users and Student Use Benefit users who need continued service must move to an eligible Microsoft 365 Education student or faculty edition at renewal. Exchange Online for Alumni users who need continued email service can move to the new paid Exchange Online for Alumni offer.”

Existing pricing will be honoured until the end of the agreement.
It's all about AI
Perhaps inevitably, Microsoft’s decision to pull free email is cloaked in references to AI services and experiences. The surviving plans all feature enhanced AI provision, and the announcement states that institutions should base their upgrade on their “productivity, management, security, analytics, and AI needs.”
Additionally, a Microsoft representative told The Register that "Microsoft's broader goal is not technology adoption for its own sake. It is to support AI and digital experiences that strengthen learning, preserve educator judgment and give institutions the controls they need to manage data, privacy, and responsible use."

articles.title: Pré-Black Friday : Amazon baisse déjà les prix de sa maison connectée, jusqu’à -39% sur 5 offres
articles.text:
Amazon n’attend pas le 27 novembre pour lancer son Black Friday : ses propres marques de maison connectée affichent déjà des remises estampillées « Pré-Black Friday ». Nous avons retenu 5 offres, de la petite caméra d’intérieur au routeur Wi-Fi maillé, en comparant chaque prix au plus bas pratiqué ces 30 derniers jours.
Ring, Blink, eero et Echo ont un point commun : ce sont des marques d’Amazon, et leurs produits sont vendus et expédiés par Amazon lui-même. Les cinq appareils retenus ici portent déjà la mention « Offre Pré-Black Friday » sur leur fiche, à quinze jours du vendredi 27 novembre.
La sélection couvre la surveillance de l’intérieur et de l’extérieur, la porte d’entrée et le Wi-Fi du logement. Les prix barrés indiqués correspondent au prix le plus bas affiché par Amazon sur les 30 derniers jours, relevé le 12 novembre : la remise annoncée mesure donc une baisse récente.
Les 5 appareils Amazon déjà remisés avant le Black Friday
- Ring Caméra intérieure 2e génération à 17,99 € au lieu de 19,99 €
- Pack de 2 caméras Blink Outdoor 4 avec modules d’extension de piles à 65,99 € au lieu de 107,97 €
- Pack de 3 caméras Ring Caméra intérieure Plus 2K (nouvelle génération) à 59,99 € au lieu de 89,97 €
- Pack Echo Show 8 (nouvelle génération) et sonnette vidéo sans fil Ring à 159,99 € au lieu de 184,98 €
- Routeur Wi-Fi 6 maillé Amazon eero 6+ à 89,99 € au lieu de 94,99 €
VPN, logiciels, abonnements : les promos à saisir en ce moment
Ce que chaque appareil apporte, et ses limites
Ces cinq appareils appartiennent tous à Amazon, mais chacun répond à un besoin différent : surveiller une pièce, l’extérieur, la porte d’entrée, ou couvrir le logement en Wi-Fi. Voici l’usage qu’il sert et le point à vérifier avant de commander.
- Ring Caméra intérieure 2e génération : c’est le modèle que nous avons évalué dans notre test de la Ring Indoor Cam, avec une note de 7/10. Nous y avions apprécié sa détection de mouvement très réactive, son image 1080p suffisante de jour comme de nuit et son cache qui masque physiquement l’objectif. Son micro reste moyen et sa coque en plastique paraît fragile. À 17,99 €, c’est l’entrée la moins chère de cette sélection.
- Blink Outdoor 4 : pensée pour l’extérieur, elle fonctionne sur piles AA et supporte de -20 à 45 °C. Le module d’extension fourni avec chaque caméra double l’autonomie, jusqu’à quatre ans selon Blink, et le Sync Module Core inclus sert de passerelle. À son lancement, le pack d’une seule caméra avec module était annoncé à 99,99 € : ici, il y en a deux pour 65,99 €. Limite à connaître : son Wi-Fi reste cantonné à la bande des 2,4 GHz.
- Ring Caméra intérieure Plus : elle passe à une vidéo 2K avec un zoom jusqu’à 4x, et garde les couleurs dans la pénombre tant qu’une lumière ambiante éclaire la pièce, selon Ring. Le pack de trois revient à moins de 20 € par caméra, à peine plus que le modèle 1080p vendu seul : de quoi équiper trois pièces. Nous ne l’avons pas encore testée.
- Echo Show 8 et sonnette Ring : le pack associe l’écran connecté de 8,7 pouces d’Amazon à une sonnette vidéo sans fil en 2K. Quand quelqu’un sonne, l’image de l’entrée s’affiche sur l’Echo Show, sans avoir à sortir son téléphone. La sonnette s’installe sans câblage, mais sa batterie intégrée n’est pas amovible.
- eero 6+ : ce routeur Wi-Fi 6 accepte des débits jusqu’à 1 Gb/s et couvre jusqu’à 140 m² selon Amazon. Il intègre un hub Thread et Zigbee, utile pour connecter des objets domotiques compatibles sans boîtier supplémentaire. Sa baisse reste modeste par rapport aux dernières semaines : elle intéressera d’abord ceux qui comptaient déjà renouveler leur routeur.
Des remises inégales d’un appareil à l’autre
Par rapport au prix le plus bas pratiqué par Amazon sur les 30 derniers jours, les deux packs de caméras portent les plus fortes baisses : -39 % sur les Blink Outdoor 4 et -33 % sur les trois Ring Caméra intérieure Plus. Le pack Echo Show 8 recule de 14 %, la caméra Ring 2e génération de 10 % et le routeur eero 6+ de 5 %. Nous avons retenu cette référence plutôt que le prix conseillé, affiché sur certaines fiches, parce qu’elle reflète ce que vous auriez réellement payé ces dernières semaines.
Le prix d’achat n’est pas le seul budget à prévoir. Comme nous le rappelons dans notre comparatif des meilleures caméras de surveillance, Ring ne conserve aucun historique vidéo sans abonnement, quand d’autres marques fonctionnent sans. Chez Blink, l’enregistrement illimité des clips passe aussi par une offre payante, avec un essai gratuit de 30 jours. Si vous comptez sur les vidéos enregistrées, ajoutez ce coût mensuel avant de comparer.
Caméras Ring, Blink et routeur eero : vos questions
Les caméras Ring fonctionnent-elles sans abonnement ?
Le direct reste accessible, mais retrouver les vidéos enregistrées demande l’abonnement Ring. La Ring Caméra intérieure 2e génération n’a pas non plus de port microSD pour un enregistrement local, comme nous l’avions relevé dans notre test.
La Blink Outdoor 4 se connecte-t-elle au Wi-Fi 5 GHz ?
Non, elle reste limitée à la bande des 2,4 GHz, plus encombrée mais de meilleure portée. Vérifiez que votre box diffuse bien un réseau sur cette bande à l’endroit où vous comptez la fixer.
Un seul routeur eero 6+ suffit-il pour tout un logement ?
Amazon annonce une couverture jusqu’à 140 m² pour une unité. Au-delà, le réseau maillé s’étend en ajoutant d’autres appareils eero compatibles.
