articles.title: La precarga de GTA VI colapsa redes británicas con archivos de 212 GB
articles.text:
La descarga anticipada de Grand Theft Auto 6 colapsó parte de la infraestructura de internet en el Reino Unido, más de una semana antes de su estreno oficial, previsto para el 19 de noviembre de 2026.
El fenómeno comenzó el martes 10 de noviembre, cuando se habilitó la precarga del título para consolas Xbox y PlayStation 5. Miles de jugadores iniciaron desde temprano la descarga de un archivo de 212 gigabytes, lo que generó picos de tráfico sin precedentes en las redes británicas y dejó en evidencia los límites de algunos proveedores de internet frente a lanzamientos de esta magnitud.
Qué impacto tuvo la precarga de GTA 6 en el tráfico de internet
La precarga de un videojuego es el proceso que permite descargar por adelantado todos sus archivos para poder jugarlo de inmediato el día de su lanzamiento oficial, sin esperas adicionales.
En el caso de GTA 6, esa descarga de 212 GB se concentró en un lapso corto de tiempo y provocó una demanda de datos tan alta que terminó por convertirse en un récord histórico de tráfico para al menos un proveedor británico.
Según los datos publicados por Virgin Media O2, la demanda generada por el lanzamiento provocó tanto el mayor pico de tráfico en internet como el mayor volumen diario de datos registrados en la historia de su red.
El proveedor informó que el tráfico máximo superó en un 3,8% el récord anterior, establecido durante el partido entre el Arsenal y el Atlético de Madrid por la Liga de Campeones, disputado en abril.
El volumen total de datos descargados durante la jornada también marcó un nuevo techo. Esa cifra superó en un 4% la marca anterior, registrada apenas unos días antes, el 1 de noviembre, con el lanzamiento de la minitemporada del capítulo 7 de Fortnite.
La velocidad con la que creció la demanda resultó uno de los datos más llamativos del fenómeno. Apenas una hora después de habilitarse la precarga, Virgin Media O2 detectó un aumento del tráfico del 51,6% respecto de la semana anterior, y para las 9:00 de la mañana el volumen total de datos descargados a través de su red ya era un 73,3% superior al registrado en el mismo período de referencia.
Por qué algunos proveedores de internet tuvieron problemas de congestión
El fuerte incremento de tráfico no solo dejó estadísticas inéditas: también generó dificultades concretas para algunos proveedores de internet del Reino Unido. Jeremy Chelot, director ejecutivo de Netomnia y YouFibre, señaló que la demanda estaba generando problemas en sus redes y que algunos usuarios de Yorkshire experimentaban congestión en el servicio.
Para muchos jugadores que reservaron el título a través de las tiendas digitales oficiales, la precarga debería haberse activado de forma automática. Sin embargo, ese proceso requiere tener habilitadas las descargas automáticas y mantener la consola en modo de reposo, dos condiciones que no todos los usuarios cumplen de manera simultánea.
Por ese motivo, se anticipan nuevas oleadas de tráfico en los próximos días, a medida que más jugadores activen esas configuraciones o decidan iniciar manualmente la descarga antes del estreno del 19 de noviembre.
Cuánto espacio de almacenamiento ocupa GTA 6 en consolas
El tamaño del archivo representa otro obstáculo para los usuarios. Los 212 GB que ocupa GTA 6 equivalen a una porción considerable de la memoria disponible en consolas con capacidad limitada, en especial en el modelo básico de PlayStation 5.
Varios usuarios se quejaron de que el juego ocupa casi un tercio del almacenamiento total de esa versión de consola, lo que podría obligarlos a eliminar otros títulos o archivos para poder completar la instalación.
A este inconveniente se suma el de algunos compradores que reservaron el título en tiendas físicas y todavía no recibieron sus códigos de descarga. Rockstar decidió distribuir el videojuego exclusivamente en formato digital, sin versión en disco, aunque ciertos comercios ofrecen cajas que contienen códigos para descargarlo. Esas cajas no estarán disponibles hasta el 12 de noviembre.
Cómo se compara GTA 6 con otros videojuegos de gran tamaño
Con 212 GB, GTA 6 se ubica entre los videojuegos más pesados disponibles actualmente en las tiendas digitales de Xbox y PlayStation. Otros títulos, como los de la franquicia Call of Duty, han requerido incluso más espacio de almacenamiento.
La diferencia radica en la forma de distribución: en esos casos, los contenidos suelen entregarse por etapas, lo que evita que los jugadores deban descargar todos los archivos de una sola vez, algo que sí ocurrió con el lanzamiento de GTA 6 y que explica buena parte de la presión ejercida sobre las redes británicas en las últimas horas.

articles.title: Grok vaza dados confidenciais de mais de 35 mil aplicativos • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Grok vaza dados confidenciais de mais de 35 mil aplicativos
Links de projetos podiam ser rastreados pela internet e permitiam acesso a documentos de empresas, incluindo a própria SpaceX.
Mais de 35 mil aplicativos criados no Grok Build estavam acessíveis na internet, expondo informações que iam de exames médicos a propostas comerciais, além de 24 documentos da própria SpaceX. Entre os projetos encontrados havia sistemas usados por empresas da lista Fortune 500 e organizações ligadas aos setores de saúde, defesa e infraestrutura.
A exposição foi identificada pela empresa de cibersegurança Claroc e revelada pelo ArsTechnica. O problema resultava da estrutura dos links criados pelo agente de programação e a forma como o compartilhamento era configurado. Links podiam ser encontrados em bases públicas de DNS e, uma vez abertos, davam acesso aos aplicativos e, em alguns casos, aos bancos de dados deles.
Entre os aplicativos estavam um painel de saúde ocupacional, de uma construtora peruana, com mais de 3 mil exames médicos de trabalhadores. Outro, ligado à Tesla, mostrava o desempenho de 22 técnicos de um centro de serviços.
Havia inclusive dados pessoas. Em um deles, um sistema usado por uma empresa de cruzeiros de luxo mantinha um checklist de cozinha com os nomes completos e números de identificação de tripulantes. Em outro, uma construtora dos Estados Unidos mantinha uma planilha com cerca de 583 potenciais compradores de imóveis.
O Grok não é o primeiro serviço de inteligência artificial a expor informações de usuários na internet. No ano passado, a OpenAI precisou revisar a função de compartilhamento de conversas após links gerados pela plataforma serem indexados pelo Google.
O Grok Build permite criar aplicativos a partir de comandos em texto ou voz e publicá-los rapidamente para testes ou uso interno. Quando um projeto é compartilhado, a plataforma gera um endereço composto por palavras aleatórias.
A combinação parece funcionar como um código. Sem conhecer aquelas palavras, seria improvável chegar ao aplicativo por tentativa e erro. No entanto, segundo o ArsTechnica, os domínios apareciam em serviços de DNS passivo, bases que registram domínios observados na internet.
Foi pesquisando esses registros que Asaf Aprozper, cofundador e CTO da Claroc, conseguiu levantar dezenas de milhares de endereços do Grok Build. Segundo ele, os links sozinhos não deveria permitir a abertura dos projetos, mas, aparentemente, o agente da empresa de Elon Musk adotava como padrão a opção de que “qualquer pessoa com o link” possa abrir o documento.
Para restringir a visualização a usuários convidados ou apenas ao próprio criador, era necessário alterar manualmente a configuração.
A Claroc encontrou até mesmo 24 aplicativos da SpaceX disponíveis pela internet. Entre eles havia um plano confidencial de integração para um novo integrante da equipe de vendas e um mapa de territórios com informações sobre 594 contas.
Outros projetos revelavam endereços de sistemas internos e propostas de anúncios no X. Para a Claroc, os casos mostram como ferramentas de vibe coding podem levar aplicações internas para a internet sem passar por controles corporativos.
A empresa de segurança afirma ter comunicado a SpaceX sobre o problema no domingo (08/11), mas não recebeu resposta. De acordo com o Ars Technica, a empresa removeu o acesso aos projetos internos após procurarem a companhia para comentar a reportagem. Os projetos de terceiros, porém, continuaram acessíveis.

articles.title: Microsoft Admits Not Everyone Wants AI in Bing, Offers Options to Disable It
articles.text:
Thursday, November 12th 2026
Microsoft Admits Not Everyone Wants AI in Bing, Offers Options to Disable It
Bing users who would rather skip the AI answers now have two official ways to do it, according to a new post on Microsoft's Bing Search Blog. The first is the Microsoft Bing AI Search Choice extension for Chrome and Edge, which adds a single toggle for AI-generated answers that applies to every Bing search. The second needs no install: adding "-ai" to the end of a query removes the AI answer for that one search. Microsoft says its research shows users want "to choose whether or not AI is involved in every session," though it hasn't published that research.
Installing the extension also makes Bing the browser's default search engine, and there doesn't seem to be a way to get one without the other, so it looks like a play for Chrome users as well. It's also still labeled a preview, and it isn't new, since Microsoft's head of search, Jordi Ribas, first announced it back in June. Bing doesn't appear to have a matching switch in its own settings either, so anyone on another browser has to type the operator every time.Microsoft has been scaling back AI in other places too, having recently removed eight Copilot actions from File Explorer and dropped the Copilot+ branding from its newest Surface PCs. The Bing push hasn't slowed, though, with the Bing Wallpaper app recently caught redirecting desktop clicks to Bing.com. Google still gives users no way to switch off AI Overviews, so Bing is at least offering a choice, strings and all.
Sources:
				Microsoft Bing, 				via Windows Central

articles.title: A 2013 hack of a Russian cybercrime forum may have leaked the details of millions of users
articles.text:
A 2013 hack of a Russian cybercrime forum may have leaked the details of millions of users
Details from the YouHack breach have re-emerged on the internet
- Data from a 2013 breach of the YouHack cybercrime forum resurfaced online, exposing 7.2 million email addresses and password pairs
- The leak also included forum user details, usernames, IP addresses, and weakly protected MD5 password hashes
- Researchers warn recycled breach data and cracked passwords remain valuable for credential-stuffing and account takeover attacks
A large treasure trove of data stolen roughly 13 years ago has again surfaced on the clear web, with millions of email addresses, belonging to both innocent victims and notorious cybercriminals leaked online and found their way to Have I Been Pwned? (HIBP).
HIBP is a free online service that allows users to check whether their email address or phone number appeared in any known data breach.
HIBP recently added a new database containing roughly 7.2 million addresses. As it turns out, these addresses were stolen in May 2013, when an infamous Russian-language hacking forum YouHack suffered a breach at the hands of unnamed miscreants.
The leaked archive contains almost 7.2 million email addresses and password pairs belonging to various victims whose secrets were posted on the forum. It also contains 107,000 forum members’ email addresses, usernames, IP addresses, and MD5 password hashes - “most of which were unsalted” - HIBP said.
Unsalted MD5 passwords
Decade-old email addresses, usernames, and IP addresses of various hackers are probably not valuable information. Cybercriminals are known for using VPNs and proxy services to hide their locations, as well as disposable emails, so even if the data was recent, its usability would still be questionable, at best. Passwords, however, are a different story.
Just like the rest of us mortals, cybercriminals are known for failing to practice basic cyber-hygiene, often using the same passwords across a myriad of services. When those passwords are hashed with MD5 and unsalted, it becomes a problem.
As a cryptographic hashing algorithm, MD5 converts passwords into fixed-length strings. It is considered wildly outdated and insecure, because threat actors can crack them easily using off-the-shelf software and hardware. The problem is even worse when hashes are unsalted, which means the system hasn’t added a unique random value to each password before hashing it. This allows attackers to use precomputed lookup tables and identify identical passwords across different accounts much more easily. Once cracked, passwords can be used to access other accounts where victims have reused them.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Mother of all breaches
According toThe Register, this is not the first time this archive has made it to the clearweb. Back in 2024, the “Mother of All Breaches” saw 26 billion records, weighing 12 terabytes, were leaked. This was a bundle of numerous different security incidents, and among them were files grabbed from YouHack, as well.
The same publication reports that this is the second Russian data breach to be reported today. At the same time, a 2023 breach of Sberbank’s loyalty program (SberSpasibo) also leaked, exposing records belonging to 48 million users. Among the records are 3.3 million unique email addresses, people’s phone numbers, and dates of birth. A number of bank card numbers were also leaked, and since these were stored as unsalted SHA-1 hashes, they were also at risk of being fully exposed.
This attack happened sometime between April 2017 and February 2022, the report further states, and was claimed by a pro-Ukraine hacktivist organization calling itself NLB. The same group also claimed responsibility for the attack on Russia’s largest private bank, Alfa-Bank.
Although we cannot know for certain, it is possible the leaks are the result of the war between Russia and Ukraine spilling into cyberspace. The two sides have been trading blows over the internet since the full-scale invasion began, with Russia's February 2022 attack on Viasat's satellite communications network disrupting thousands of connections in Ukraine and across Europe.
Ukraine has also launched destructive cyber operations against Russian targets, including a December 2025 attack on logistics company Eltrans+, which reportedly wiped or encrypted 165TB of data and disabled more than 700 servers.

articles.title: Un grupo de organizaciones demandó a OpenAI y Anthropic para frenar el desarrollo de la IA más avanzada
articles.text:
Un grupo de organizaciones sin fines de lucro demandó a OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta y la división de inteligencia artificial de SpaceX para que un juez les prohíba seguir desarrollando los modelos de IA más avanzados. Los demandantes argumentan que las propias empresas admiten que esa tecnología puede ser catastrófica.
La demanda se presentó ante el Tribunal Superior de California en el condado de San Francisco. Los demandantes son Irreplaceable Education Fund, Public Citizen, Heat Initiative y The Alliance for Secure AI, según el comunicado de Public Citizen.
Los grupos invocan la ley de competencia desleal de California. Sostienen que las compañías incurren en prácticas que causan una molestia pública, es decir, un daño a la salud y la seguridad de la comunidad.
La agencia Reuters indicó que el reclamo apunta a productos como ChatGPT, Gemini y Claude.
Qué piden los demandantes y con qué argumentos
El texto, de 63 páginas según Courthouse News Service, enumera las prácticas que busca frenar: la mejora recursiva de sistemas de IA (que se perfeccionan a sí mismos), el desarrollo de inteligencia artificial general o superinteligencia, y los sistemas capaces de vulnerar redes ajenas o de escapar de su control.
Los autores citan advertencias de los propios directivos. Según Reuters, la demanda menciona declaraciones de Dario Amodei, director ejecutivo de Anthropic, y de Elon Musk, director ejecutivo de SpaceX, sobre el potencial de la IA para destruir la civilización. Courthouse News añade una cita de Musk que compara el desarrollo de la IA con “invocar al demonio”.
Asimismo, describen incidentes recientes. Según el reclamo, centenares de agentes de OpenAI (asistentes de IA que ejecutan tareas por su cuenta) escaparon este verano de un entorno cerrado y entraron en una plataforma de terceros.
Otros agentes intentaron vulnerar la biblioteca en línea de la Universidad de Nuevo México y accedieron a una base de datos sanitaria de Australia.
La demanda agrega que un agente presentó un informe falso ante la policía de Filadelfia y que otro eludió un muro de pago para acceder al recuento de votos de Georgia.
“Ninguna otra industria” puede autorregularse, dice la demanda
“Ninguna otra industria tiene permitido tratar el desarrollo de productos inseguros como algo inevitable”, afirma el texto, según la agencia, que agrega que tampoco se concede a ninguna el derecho de autorregularse en productos tan peligrosos.
El abogado que presentó el reclamo es Matthew Platkin, exfiscal general de Nueva Jersey. “Es patentemente ilegal que las empresas desarrollen y lancen productos que saben que son inseguros”, dijo en el comunicado.
Brendan Steinhauser, director ejecutivo de The Alliance for Secure AI, afirmó que se exige responsabilidad a toda industria cuya producción amenaza la seguridad pública.
El antecedente de Florida y la respuesta de las empresas
No es el primer intento judicial de limitar el desarrollo de modelos. Según Reuters, el fiscal general de Florida, James Uthmeier, demandó a OpenAI en junio por presentar de forma engañosa la seguridad de ChatGPT. En septiembre pidió al juez que le prohíba desarrollar nuevos modelos sin supervisión externa. Esa moción sigue pendiente, según los registros del tribunal.
Tras la presentación de Florida, el vocero de OpenAI, Drew Pusateri, dijo que la empresa había pausado el entrenamiento de sus modelos más capaces y que no lo retomaría hasta contar con más salvaguardas. Reuters no recibió en ese texto una respuesta de OpenAI a la nueva demanda. Meta declinó hacer comentarios, según el medio The Aigentic.
La demanda llega después de las elecciones legislativas de Estados Unidos, en las que los demócratas recuperaron el control del Congreso y subrayaron la necesidad de regular la tecnología, según AP, que informó primero del caso. Los demandantes piden al juez que bloquee el desarrollo y el despliegue de sistemas avanzados. El tribunal aún no fijó fecha para una audiencia.

articles.title: AMD Advances Built-in Protection from Physical Attacks for Security-Critical Systems
articles.text:
Thursday, November 12th 2026
AMD Advances Built-in Protection from Physical Attacks for Security-Critical Systems
What's the News? AMD today announced AMD Versal tamper-resistant ("TR") devices, designed to protect security-critical information against sophisticated physical attacks while delivering the high-performance heterogeneous processing capabilities of AMD Versal AI Edge Series Gen 2. Versal TR devices are the industry's first adaptive SoC or FPGA-based devices providing built-in protection against physical attacks on the silicon backside. A sensor-based protection die is bonded to the main compute die using 3D active-on-active technology, shielding the entire backside of the device, protecting sensitive information, detecting physical attacks and preventing boot if the protection die is tampered with or removed. Combined with embedded CPUs, AI Engines and programmable logic, Versal TR devices help customers strengthen the protection of security-critical information without compromising system performance, size, weight, power or time to market.
Why It Matters? Protecting sensitive information from sophisticated physical attacks is a priority across markets and embedded applications. From data center networking and fintech applications to defense systems and critical industrial infrastructure, customers seeking higher levels of device security today typically build custom solutions in-house using mechanical enclosures, ASICs and other components, adding development cost, specialist resources, verification effort and re-spin risk. Versal TR devices integrate heterogeneous processing with enhanced security features including backside physical attack protection in a single device. This reduces the need for separate compute, security and enclosure-based protection components. This approach can save board area and simplify board design versus custom solutions while giving customers access to AMD tools, technical support and a broad partner ecosystem.What's the Role for AMD?
Kirk Saban, corporate vice president, Product, Software and Solutions, AMD Embedded"Protecting critical information requires continued innovation in silicon security capabilities to stay ahead of emerging threats. With Versal tamper-resistant devices, AMD is bringing built-in protection against physical attacks together with high-performance heterogeneous compute in a commercial adaptive SoC, helping customers simplify the development of security-critical systems while maintaining the performance and flexibility their applications demand."
What Do AMD Versal TR Devices Deliver?
Versal TR devices combine multiple layers of physical and cryptographic protection with Versal AI Edge Series Gen 2 heterogeneous compute. In addition to backside protection, devices feature:
- Expanded hardware acceleration for post-quantum cryptography, including new support for Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm (ML-DSA) and Stateless Hash-Based Digital Signature Algorithm (SLH-DSA).
- Hybrid boot flow support that allows users to leverage multiple signature algorithms.
- Application security unit (ASU) key vault improvements and a new memory element aging sensor (MEAS) provide additional safeguards for cryptographic keys.
Versal TR devices also expand glitch detection by combining improvements to the Versal architecture glitch detector with a new orthogonal glitch detector, providing improved coverage that includes glitches occurring simultaneously across two voltage rails.
Based on Versal AI Edge Series Gen 2 adaptive SoCs, Versal TR devices integrate Arm CPUs, AI Engines, programmable logic, hard IP and connectivity, delivering up to 229,000 DMIPS of scalar compute, up to 369 INT8 TOPS and up to 543,000 LUTs.
The Versal TR portfolio includes three devices - 2VE3358TR, 2VE3558TR and 2VE3858TR - that provide a common platform across different performance and cost requirements. Each Versal TR device also has a footprint-compatible standard counterpart available today, allowing customers to develop on the standard Versal platform and transition to the Versal TR device with minimal effort without rerunning synthesis or place and route.
When Will AMD Versal TR Devices Be Available?
The first Versal TR devices are expected to sample in the second half of 2027 and move to production in the first half of 2028. Customers can evaluate and build designs on select footprint-equivalent standard Versal AI Edge Series Gen 2 devices today and later transition to the corresponding tamper-resistant device while keeping their high-performance design intact.
Source:
				AMD			
	
	
	
		
	
		
6 Comments on AMD Advances Built-in Protection from Physical Attacks for Security-Critical Systems
This protection just bumps it all up like 10 notches. Instead of using simple wire or other low-level protection, another chip is bonded on top of the FPGA and this chip contains several layers for detecting various attacks. Methods vary, but anything from directly drilling into it, blasting it with X-RAYs, lasers, microwaves etc. will be detected and it will instantly trip the protection, wiping the keys and rendering it useless. Also all interconnects are using inner layers so there is no way to disconnect this protection layer or poke at it's signals.
Obviously this is very specialized chip that will only be used on a few special devices where it really matters, like again for the banking sector or protecting confidentiality, holding keys for private computing etc. Something where possible attacks are expected to be from very motivated people with literally infinite budgets.
- The mechanical protection is fairy simple, any layers of functioning silicon can't be drilled or worked trough, mesh of tracks that is checked for target resistance or two layers forming a capacitor that is checked for target capacitance will do the job nicely.
- For detecting lasers and xrays, array of diode (PIN) detectors could be used, some photosensitive, some shaded for xrays, with some logic so it requires more than usual background radiation or light level to trip.
- For microwaves, small antenna elements at various wavelengths, with a diode and a detector. Since this is about GHz and THz frequencies that could affect the underlying silicon, all this is very small and can be built on a chip.
- Detecting glitches at sensitive rails and signals is done by sampling them with ADC and looking for any abnormalities. Clocks can be checked too, to have correct frequencies without any glitches or mixed in unwanted signals.
Often there are two "trip" levels, one that is "soft" and simply resets the chip (this can be set quite strictly and might also happen due to potentially normally occurring edge conditions, like undervoltage), this makes it impossible to continue glitch attacks or putting it into undefined state, but it's recoverable.
Then there is actual tamper that means someone is trying to mess with it and results in secure element memory wiping and invalidation of the whole chip and there is no way back from this.
All this is done on a special chip and that is stacked on top of the FPGA, just like RAM can be layered over CPU in mobile phone phone SoCs.

This Swiss-based service offers an impressive range of features at an attractive price, making it an excellent choice for sharing large files with friends and family or syncing them across all your devices."
Price context & historical value

articles.title: Nintendo vai encerrar login com Google e Apple; veja o que muda • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Nintendo vai encerrar login com Google e Apple; veja o que muda
Usuários precisarão utilizar senha ou chave de acesso para entrar na Conta Nintendo a partir de janeiro de 2027.
A Nintendo deixará de permitir o login com contas do Google e da Apple a partir de 26 de janeiro de 2027. A mudança afeta usuários que utilizam esses serviços para acessar a Conta Nintendo, responsável por recursos como compras digitais, assinaturas e funcionalidades online do Switch e Switch 2.
A fabricante recomenda que os jogadores configurem uma senha própria ou uma chave de acesso (passkey) antes do prazo. A decisão foi comunicada na terça-feira (10/11), mas a empresa não explicou os motivos para encerrar a integração.
Além de impedir o login com Google e Apple, a Nintendo deixará de permitir a criação de novas contas utilizando as credenciais dessas empresas. A opção de vincular contas também será removida. Outra função que será descontinuada é a missão do programa My Nintendo, que oferece pontos de platina para usuários que associam suas contas do Google. Esses pontos podem ser utilizados para resgatar recompensas.
A mudança não significa que os jogadores perderão suas contas. Quem já estiver conectado em um dispositivo poderá continuar utilizando o serviço. Entretanto, caso seja necessário entrar novamente, o acesso deverá ser feito com e-mail/ID de usuário e a senha da Conta Nintendo, ou com uma passkey previamente cadastrada.
O encerramento também não impede o uso de endereços do Gmail como e-mail cadastrado. A restrição vale para a autenticação realizada pelos serviços do Google e da Apple.
Para evitar problemas, a Nintendo orienta que os usuários verifiquem seus métodos de autenticação antes de janeiro. Quem ainda não possui uma senha própria pode configurá-la no site oficial da Conta Nintendo. O procedimento é relativamente simples.
A empresa também recomenda o uso de passkeys, tecnologia que permite entrar em serviços sem digitar uma senha tradicional. A autenticação pode ser realizada por impressão digital, reconhecimento facial ou desbloqueio do dispositivo.
Para cadastrar uma chave de acesso, é necessário entrar nas configurações de segurança da Conta Nintendo e selecionar a opção correspondente. É possível registrar até dez passkeys em dispositivos compatíveis.
Quem não lembra os dados de acesso pode seguir o guia de recuperação da Conta Nintendo. O aviso oficial informa que a mudança poderá sofrer atraso, dependendo do andamento das alterações no sistema.

articles.title: Un nouveau rival du DLSS promet une meilleure génération d'images sur presque toutes les cartes graphiques
articles.text:
Apex Compute dévoile Apex Neural Rendering, une suite de rendu par IA censée fonctionner sur les cartes NVIDIA, AMD et Intel, y compris anciennes. Seule la génération d’images est disponible, en bêta.
Le DLSS n’a jamais été disponible que sur GeForce RTX, et sa génération d’images reste réservée à des cartes récentes. Apex Neural Rendering (ANR) vise justement l’inverse : une technologie de génération d'images qui tourne partout, y compris sur le Steam Deck.
Une compatibilité large, des GTX 16 aux Arc
ANR regroupe trois briques : la génération d’images, l’upscaling (super-résolution) et la reconstruction de rayons. Seule la première est pour l’instant accessible en bêta, les deux autres devant suivre plus tard.
Le périmètre matériel est large : GeForce GTX 16 et RTX 20 ou plus récentes, Radeon RX 5000 ou plus récentes, Intel Arc séries A et B, plus le Steam Deck. Côté logiciel, la bêta fonctionne sous Windows 10 et 11, Linux et SteamOS via Proton. Autrement dit, des GPU que NVIDIA laisse de côté pour ses propres outils peuvent ici prétendre à la génération d’images.
Sur une GeForce RTX 5090 en 4K, Apex Compute annonce 1,01 ms pour générer une image en mode 2x, contre 1,26 ms pour la génération d’images du DLSS. En 4x, l’écart est de 0,61 ms contre 0,82 ms. L’empreinte mémoire serait de 214 Mo, contre 562 Mo pour le DLSS.
Ces chiffres touchent un point sensible de la technique : la latence ajoutée. Mais il s’agit de benchmarks publiés par l’éditeur lui-même, et un calcul d’image plus rapide ne garantit ni plus de fluidité globale ni une latence d’entrée plus basse. Apex Compute revendique aussi une meilleure qualité visuelle, avec des comparaisons côte à côte tirées notamment de The Last of Us Part II. Là encore, seuls des tests indépendants en conditions réelles pourront trancher.
Une installation qui passe par GitHub et OptiScaler
La bêta de ANR FG se récupère sur GitHub et s’appuie pour l’instant sur OptiScaler. L’installation impose de modifier le dossier de chaque jeu : on est loin d’un simple curseur dans les options graphiques. La compatibilité variera donc d'un titre à l’autre.
C’est la même logique que celle de ces technologies NVIDIA désormais exécutées sur GPU AMD : les briques d’upscaling deviennent de moins en moins captives d’un constructeur. Reste à voir si ANR convaincra au-delà des bidouilleurs, une fois l’upscaling et la reconstruction de rayons livrés.
Pour l’instant, la promesse tient surtout à un tableau de chiffres signé par son auteur. À vos dossiers de jeux, donc, si le bricolage ne vous effraie pas.

articles.title: Google y Adobe se integran para agilizar el uso de PDF en la nube: adiós a descargar y subir archivos
articles.text:
Google y Adobe anunciaron una ampliación de su colaboración durante Adobe MAX 2026 que integra Acrobat dentro de Gmail y Google Drive. La alianza permitirá editar archivos PDF sin necesidad de descargarlos ni subirlos de nuevo a la nube, ya que el editor de Adobe quedará disponible desde las vistas previas de los documentos.
El objetivo declarado es reducir los cambios de programa que debe hacer un usuario para completar tareas cotidianas con archivos PDF.
La noticia llega acompañada de otro anuncio relacionado: Adobe abrirá sus programas de edición creativa a agentes de inteligencia artificial externos a partir de 2027, mediante un protocolo que ya empieza a instalarse en la industria tecnológica.
Integración de Acrobat en Gmail y Drive: así funciona la edición sin descargas
Cuando un usuario recibe un documento PDF en Gmail y necesita modificarlo, podrá recurrir a Acrobat sin abrirlo por separado. Esto es posible gracias a la integración con Gmail y Google Drive, que habilita el acceso al editor de Adobe directamente desde las vistas previas de los archivos.
El mecanismo se activa a través de las aplicaciones sugeridas y de la opción “Editar con” de Google. No se trata de un cambio técnico complejo, pero resulta útil para quienes trabajan de forma habitual con archivos PDF dentro del ecosistema de Google.
La magnitud del uso de estos archivos explica el interés de ambas compañías en simplificar el proceso. Según datos de Adobe, cada año se abren más de 400.000 millones de documentos PDF con Acrobat, una cifra que da cuenta del volumen de archivos que podrían beneficiarse de esta integración directa entre plataformas.
La alianza entre Google y Adobe elimina un paso que hasta ahora resultaba habitual: descargar el PDF recibido por correo, editarlo en un programa aparte y volver a subirlo a la nube. Con la nueva integración, ese proceso se resuelve dentro del propio entorno de Gmail o Drive, sin salir de la vista previa del documento.
Gemini y la inteligencia artificial de Google llegan a las herramientas de Adobe
Google incorporará sus modelos de inteligencia artificial a Acrobat, lo que permitirá trabajar con los documentos mediante instrucciones escritas en lenguaje natural. Esto incluye consultar información contenida en el archivo, realizar modificaciones puntuales o generar nuevos materiales a partir de su contenido.
Las funciones de edición conversacional de PDF ya existían en Adobe antes de este acuerdo. La novedad es que ahora esas funciones también podrán apoyarse en tecnología desarrollada por Google, lo que amplía las opciones disponibles para el usuario final.
En sentido inverso, los conectores de Adobe para Gemini y Gemini Enterprise permitirán utilizar algunas de sus herramientas directamente desde el asistente de Google. La edición de imágenes y documentos desde Gemini podrá realizarse recurriendo a las aplicaciones de Adobe, sin necesidad de abrirlas por separado.
También está prevista la incorporación de estas capacidades al Modo IA de la Búsqueda de Google, aunque todavía no se detalló cómo funcionará ese apartado específico de la integración.
Este movimiento no surge de manera aislada. Adobe ya había anunciado previamente la llegada de su agente creativo a Gemini, además de planes de trabajo conjunto con ChatGPT, Claude y Copilot. La diferencia ahora es que las integraciones con los servicios de Google se concretaron tanto para usuarios particulares como para el entorno empresarial.
Photoshop, Illustrator y Premiere se abren a agentes externos
Adobe presentó en Adobe MAX un avance de sus integraciones MCP locales para Creative Cloud, que llegarán en beta privada a principios de 2027. A través de este desarrollo, agentes de inteligencia artificial de otras compañías, como Anthropic u OpenAI, podrán trabajar directamente con Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere y After Effects.
MCP es un protocolo que permite a un agente de inteligencia artificial conectarse con herramientas externas para completar una tarea. Se trata de un estándar que fue ganando terreno de forma progresiva dentro de la industria tecnológica.
En términos prácticos, el agente realizará cambios en los archivos nativos de los proyectos guardados en el ordenador del usuario. Las capas, los vectores o las secuencias de video seguirán siendo editables de forma manual en todo momento.
Si el sistema está conectado además a otras herramientas compatibles, como Google Drive o Slack, podrá recuperar un briefing redactado en Google Docs, trabajar sobre el proyecto correspondiente y compartir el resultado final con el equipo dentro de un mismo flujo de trabajo.
Adobe Creative Agent desembarca en Premiere, Illustrator e InDesign
El agente propio de Adobe, denominado Adobe Creative Agent, llega en versión beta a Premiere, Illustrator, InDesign, After Effects y Frame.io. Se trata de una herramienta interna de la compañía, distinta de las integraciones MCP que habilitarán el acceso de agentes externos.
En Premiere, por ejemplo, el agente puede aplicar efectos a todos los clips de una secuencia de manera simultánea o ajustar el color y la exposición del conjunto completo en una sola operación, sin necesidad de repetir el proceso clip por clip.

articles.title: Jensen Resigns Over Second Affair - EE Times
articles.text:
A lot can change in a week. Just days after admitting to an extramarital affair with a Chinese intelligence asset, Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia CEO after The New York Times exposed a second affair with a senior Nvidia staff member.
As late as Wednesday evening, it looked like Jensen was going to ride out the scandal over his affair with the executive revealed to be a Chinese spy. But the emergence of a second affair, this time with one of Huang’s direct reports within Nvidia, was another huge blow. It was the coincident timing of these two separate scandals that really made Huang’s position untenable; he might have survived either one had they presented separately (then-Intel CEO Brian Krzanich resigned in 2018 over a similar offense, but he didn’t have Jensen’s history with the company, nor his star power).
The personal and professional reputation of the industry’s most famous CEO is now indelibly stained.
Huang cofounded Nvidia in 1993 and has been the CEO since day 1. In those 33 years, Nvidia has become the biggest tech company in the world, today worth around $4 trillion, largely due to the AI revolution. Nvidia GPUs became the de facto standard for machine intelligence and have driven almost all significant breakthroughs in AI in the last 10 years. During that time, Jensen managed Nvidia with a famously small team of around 42,000 (Intel has double that) in a unique style. The company executed ruthlessly and relentlessly under his leadership to become one of the most important companies in the U.S. economy today.
For his tenure to end like this is ridiculous; too far-fetched even for an episode of the HBO series Silicon Valley.
Jensen’s personal brand—the rockstar tech guru and charismatic business genius at the helm of the world’s biggest semiconductor company—is so irrevocably linked with Nvidia’s brand that it is going to be incredibly hard to separate them. But that is what must be done, and then, a new CEO must be found. For a company that has only ever had one CEO and with no obvious internal successor, that is going to be an enormous task. Nvidia’s board said it is considering internal and external candidates.
Even in the last few years, Jensen personally has had a huge impact on the industry with his bombastic stage presence and outspoken support for causes such as open-source models. He’s also given us so many iconic moments, from unveiling the A100 from the oven in his kitchen to introducing “Jensen math” and “the more you buy, the more you save.”
His departure has certainly left a big leather jacket to fill.

articles.title: NVIDIA : qui est vraiment Colette Kress, ancienne de Microsoft qui succède à Jensen Huang
articles.text:
Après la démission de Jensen Huang, c'est Colette Kress qui prend les commandes de NVIDIA par intérim. Directrice financière du géant des puces depuis 2013 et son départ de Microsoft, elle a accompagné son ascension dans l'ombre de son cofondateur.
Colette Kress devient donc la nouvelle patronne de NVIDIA, au moins le temps que le conseil d'administration trouve un successeur durable au démissionnaire Jensen Huang, comme l'annonce l'entreprise ce jeudi 12 novembre 2026. La directrice financière, bien connue des investisseurs pour ses commentaires trimestriels, cumulera d'ailleurs les deux casquettes. Un choix de continuité pour une entreprise qui n'avait jamais eu d'autre dirigeant que son cofondateur, et dont le chiffre d'affaires a été multiplié par plus de cinquante depuis l'arrivée de cette financière passée par Texas Instruments, Microsoft et Cisco. Colette Kress annonce la couleur, ou essaie-t-elle de rassurer : l'intelligence artificielle sera son cheval de bataille.
Colette Kress, une carrière bâtie chez les géants de la tech, rompue à la finance
Diplômée en finance de l'université de l'Arizona, titulaire d'un MBA de la Southern Methodist University, au Texas, Colette Kress a fait ses premières armes chez Texas Instruments, où elle a passé huit ans. Elle rejoint ensuite le géant Microsoft en 1997 et y reste treize ans, dont quatre comme directrice financière de la division Serveurs et outils.
En 2010, elle part chez Cisco, où elle pilote pendant trois ans la stratégie financière, la planification et le développement de l'activité au sein de l'organisation Business Technology and Operations Finance. C'est là que NVIDIA vient la chercher, en septembre 2013, au terme d'une recherche de près de deux ans. Elle a alors 46 ans, et Jensen Huang salue son « expérience fantastique », et sa connaissance approfondie du secteur.
À son arrivée, NVIDIA est la plus petite entreprise pour laquelle elle ait jamais travaillé, confiera-t-elle un jour. Le groupe réalisait alors 4,13 milliards de dollars de chiffre d'affaires sur l'exercice, contre 215,9 milliards lors de l'exercice 2026. De grande entreprise à mastodonte planétaire de l'IA et des semi-conducteurs, donc. Entre-temps, Colette Kress est devenue la voix financière de NVIDIA, celle sur qui Jensen Huang comptait lors de chaque présentation trimestrielle des résultats.
L'IA, au cœur du discours d'une Colette Kress qui ne peut pas ambitionner aller au-delà de l'intérim
L'intelligence artificielle est au centre du discours de Colette Kress. À chaque publication de résultats, c'est elle qui détaille les ventes de puces pour centres de données et chiffre ainsi l'appétit du marché. Depuis 2025, elle table sur 3 000 à 4 000 milliards de dollars d'investissements mondiaux dans les infrastructures d'IA d'ici la fin de la décennie. Au mois de mai, elle expliquait que l'IA n'était plus un simple atout, mais une nécessité dans tous les secteurs. Selon elle, les laboratoires d'IA restent d'ailleurs limités par la puissance de calcul.
Elle est aussi en première ligne sur les grands contrats de l'IA. En décembre 2025, c'est elle qui a reconnu que l'accord d'investissement de 100 milliards de dollars annoncé avec OpenAI n'en était encore qu'au stade de la lettre d'intention. Fin août, elle promettait une croissance de 70 % pour l'exercice 2028, bien au-delà des attentes des analystes. Elle assure enfin que NVIDIA avait anticipé la pénurie de mémoire vive provoquée par la ruée vers l'IA.
Colette Kress est une femme riche, cela n'étonnera personne ici. En juillet 2025, l'indice des milliardaires de Bloomberg l'a fait entrer dans le club très fermé des directeurs financiers milliardaires. Forbes la classe d'ailleurs 32ème de son palmarès 2026 des Américaines les plus riches ayant fait fortune seules, et Fortune la place 49ème de sa liste des femmes les plus puissantes. Ses actions NVIDIA valaient environ 750 millions de dollars mercredi soir, contre plus d'un milliard au pic du titre le mois dernier.
Depuis la démission de Jensen Huang, Colette Kress cumule donc les postes de PDG par intérim et de directrice financière, le temps que le conseil trouve un successeur permanent, en interne ou à l'extérieur, ce qui pourrait prendre du temps. Harvey C. Jones, nommé premier président du conseil d'administration, a salué sa connaissance approfondie de l'activité, des clients et des finances du groupe. Son premier grand rendez-vous tombe dès le 17 novembre, avec des résultats trimestriels qui seront les premiers de NVIDIA sans Jensen Huang. Forcément un événement.
Alors pour assurer un intérim, Colette Kress est sans doute le choix le plus logique. Les résultats trimestriels tombent dans cinq jours et c'est elle qui les présente depuis des années. Les investisseurs la connaissent et lui font confiance, et rien de ce qui a été publié ne la relie à l'affaire Alice Huang, on imagine que les juristes de NVIDIA ont procédé aux vérifications nécessaires. Sa nomination envoie donc un message de stabilité aux marchés comme aux clients. Mais c'est une financière, pas la visionnaire produit qu'était Jensen Huang. Elle va cumuler deux postes en pleine crise, sans expérience avérée des dossiers politiques, notamment chinois, qui sont au cœur du scandale. Et si l'intérim venait à durer, l'incertitude sur l'avenir de NVIDIA pourrait grandir. C'est donc le bon profil pour tenir la barre quelques mois, mais probablement pas celui qui dirigera NVIDIA à long terme.

articles.title: Penguin Solutions Introduces CXL-Enabled DDR4 Module to Help Address Memory Shortages in AI Data Centers
articles.text:
Thursday, November 12th 2026
Penguin Solutions Introduces CXL-Enabled DDR4 Module to Help Address Memory Shortages in AI Data Centers
Penguin Solutions, Inc., the AI Factory Platform Company, today introduced the SMART CXL-8F2W-D4, an eight-DIMM DDR4 Compute Express Link (CXL) memory add-in card that enables organizations to adapt DDR4 memory for use in AI systems. Using DDR4 as an alternative to newer-generation DDR5 memory provides an innovative approach offering performance, sourcing, and economic benefits for the buildout of AI infrastructure.
According to TechInsights, Inc., AI data centers account for 34% of DRAM demand in 2026, a figure expected to climb to nearly 50% by 2029. This rapid growth is driving up memory costs and putting increasing pressure on infrastructure budgets. For organizations deploying new servers, whether as part of a technology refresh or a new data center buildout, the rising cost of memory presents a significant challenge, underscoring the need for more cost-effective ways to expand memory capacity.
Satya Iyer, Senior Vice President and General Manager, Integrated Memory at Penguin Solutions"As AI inference workloads accelerate, rising memory costs are creating new challenges for organizations building and scaling AI data centers," "Many organizations already have significant investments in DDR4 memory that can be leveraged to address growing memory demands. By combining CXL technology with our proven memory screening and validation expertise, we're helping customers maximize the value of existing memory investments, reduce infrastructure costs, and meet the performance and reliability requirements of production AI environments."
Penguin's SMART CXL-8F2W-D4 utilizes the Marvell StructeraX CXL controller and supports up to eight DDR4 RDIMMs, making that memory available to compatible servers as additional system capacity. This helps IT teams address memory limitations for AI inference, in-memory databases, and other memory-intensive workloads.
With DDR4 memory available from previous-generation servers and data centers, Penguin Solutions has launched a program to recover memory during technology refresh cycles or source it through resellers. The program enables organizations to repurpose existing DDR4 inventory to address immediate memory needs.
To help customers deploy reused memory with confidence, Penguin Solutions combines the SMART CXL-8F2W-D4 with its Zefr ultra-high reliability memory screening process. The process simulates strenuous real-world conditions to validate DDR4 for production environments. Customer-owned DDR4 memory undergoes inspection, testing, and qualification before installation, and each populated card is validated in a compatible host system prior to shipment.
By repurposing existing DDR4 memory, organizations can potentially reduce the cost of expanding system memory capacity, extend the useful life of existing components, and maximize previous investments while addressing evolving workload requirements and the reliability and compatibility considerations associated with reused components.
The SMART CXL-8F2W-D4 is available for qualified customer opportunities on compatible CXL 2.0 platforms.

articles.title: Distributed training and inference: Google's agent projects - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Google Cloud takes aim at the cost of keeping idle AI agents running on Kubernetes
Kubernetes has become the go-to platform for distributed training and inference, but what happens to the compute bill when it runs AI agents that spend most of their time waiting?
When an agent’s container or virtual machine stays provisioned, customers pay for the wait as well as the work. To help customers control those costs and make agent workloads more predictable, Google LLC has donated three projects to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation, according to Allan Naim (pictured, left), director of product management, AI infrastructure, at Google Cloud. For Kubernetes itself, the new challenge is freeing up compute between bursts of activity while letting each agent pick up where it left off.
“Act 2 is a few years back; Kubernetes became the de facto for inference and training,” Naim said. “What’s really interesting right now is we’re embarking on this Act 3 … where the typical patterns are very, very different from how Kubernetes was designed.”
Naim and Gari Singh (right), product manager at Google Cloud, spoke with theCUBE’s Rebecca Knight at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how Google Cloud is using open-source tools to cut compute costs when AI agents sit idle. (* Disclosure below.)
Open building blocks for distributed training and inference meet agentic AI
Cost presents a serious problem in agentic workloads, with agents sitting idle 90% to 95% of the time waiting on models, test runs or human approvals, Naim explained. Google developed Agent Substrate, an open-source runtime that hosts AI agents in isolated environments on Kubernetes. When an agent is suspended, the runtime saves a snapshot of its memory and local files and frees up its compute for other agents. When work resumes, it restores the agent from that snapshot in an available sandbox.
“It helps from an economic standpoint,” Naim said. “We’ve seen 10x reduction in cost in terms of running Agent Substrate on Kubernetes versus running these agents directly on dedicated virtual machines and containers.”
Security is another concern. In response, Google open-sourced gVisor in 2018, which sits on top of the host kernel to block or audit every system call an agent makes, according to Singh.
“Agents and agent harnesses are designed to solve a problem — and to try to solve a problem — until they can’t solve the problem,” Singh said. “They will find all kinds of clever workarounds. They know everything that’s around. You want to make sure that it didn’t go make some low-level change to [your] low-level security, didn’t make an outbound network call, didn’t try to open a file that it shouldn’t.”
Google is also working with Anyscale Inc. on KubeRay, which runs Anyscale’s Ray platform natively on Kubernetes so platform teams can offer distributed training and inference to many research groups, Singh noted. OpenRL brings that approach to reinforcement learning, which teaches post-trained models guardrails, Naim added.
“In the past, to do reinforcement learning, you needed to hire a dozen research scientists with PhDs,” Naim said. “Our goal was, ‘How can we bring reinforcement learning into the world of platform engineering so that you can run reinforcement learning on your Kubernetes environment and take advantage of it to actually do continuous improvement for your agentic workload?'”

articles.title: Los chatbots de IA recomendaron tiendas falsas en hasta 15% de las respuestas sobre compras
articles.text:
Según un estudio de Podqi, empresa dedicada a proteger la propiedad intelectual de las marcas, ChatGPT y Perplexity incluyeron sitios falsos o riesgosos de tiendas en hasta el 15% de sus respuestas a consultas sobre dónde adquirir una marca. El informe se publicó cuando faltaban pocas semanas para las compras de fin de año.
La firma hizo sus pruebas en dos tandas durante septiembre de 2026 y planteó preguntas sobre 151 marcas, entre ellas Lululemon, Birkenstock, Stüssy, Madhappy y Le Creuset. Las consultas eran del tipo “¿cuáles son los mejores sitios para comprar tal marca?” o “¿tiene sitios regionales?”. En total, la empresa analizó 6.795 respuestas.
La compañía consideró riesgosos los sitios que imitan a una tienda real o venden copias, los dominios antiguos de una marca que otra persona volvió a registrar y las páginas muertas que cualquiera podría comprar y reutilizar.
La definición incluye los casos en que el chatbot recomienda el sitio, lo muestra sin comentarios o advierte sobre él.
Perplexity fue el peor y Gemini el mejor
Perplexity mostró un sitio riesgoso en 15% de sus respuestas. ChatGPT lo hizo en 8% y Gemini, el de mejor resultado, en 4%. Según el estudio, publicado en exclusiva por The Verge, ChatGPT fue el que más advirtió sobre esos sitios: lo hizo en 24% de las veces que los mostró.
Las marcas pequeñas aparecieron más expuestas. Las consultas sobre empresas grandes tuvieron sitios riesgosos en las respuestas aproximadamente la mitad de las veces. Las preguntas sobre sitios regionales también fallaron más, y los chatbots llegaron a listar páginas locales de marcas que no las tienen.
En un caso citado por el medio, Perplexity señaló una página equivocada como el sitio oficial de Stüssy y la presentó como “el mejor punto de partida para artículos auténticos garantizados”.
El estudio usó preguntas redactadas por Podqi, no conversaciones reales de usuarios, y que se apoyó en una herramienta que sigue las respuestas de los chatbots.
Podqi tiene un interés comercial en el tema: protege marcas, y Madhappy, una de las firmas analizadas, es cliente suya.
Su director ejecutivo, Trevor West, dijo que los consumidores deben tener presente que, aunque un chatbot dé un resultado, conviene verificar la fuente antes de ingresar datos personales o de la tarjeta.
Las empresas tecnológicas reaccionaron ante los resultados
Una portavoz de Google, Jessica Levis Boord, dijo que la compañía se alegra de que Gemini haya tenido el mejor desempeño y recordó que muestra enlaces a las fuentes para que el usuario pueda comprobar las respuestas.
OpenAI afirmó que su objetivo es que ChatGPT conecte a las personas con lugares confiables para comprar y que sigue mejorando sus protecciones.
Perplexity, por boca de su portavoz Jesse Dwyer, respondió que es “consistentemente la IA más precisa” en pruebas de investigación y que nunca afirma ser exacta al 100%, pero sí ser la única empresa enfocada en la precisión. No explicó el caso de Stüssy que cita el estudio.
El problema no es nuevo. En julio, la firma Searchable publicó una prueba con más de 72.000 preguntas a ChatGPT, Gemini y Perplexity sobre comercios del Reino Unido: aproximadamente una de cada 15 respuestas con direcciones web señalaba un enlace caído, una copia o un negocio distinto. Allí Perplexity falló en 10% de los casos, ChatGPT en 4% y Gemini en 5%.
Otra investigación, de la firma británica Ask Silver, encontró en junio fr 2026 dos sitios clonados de la marca Russell & Bromley entre las fuentes de una respuesta de ChatGPT, según la web Memeburn. OpenAI dijo entonces que había retirado esos sitios de su índice de búsqueda.
El riesgo aumenta en la temporada de fiestas, cuando más gente busca productos agotados o mejores precios y es probable que más consumidores usen chatbots para comprar en tiendas que no conocen.
Los ejemplos del estudio muestran el patrón: las respuestas fallan sobre todo cuando se pregunta por una marca poco conocida o por una versión regional de su tienda.
En esos casos, la recomendación más segura sigue siendo escribir el nombre de la marca en un buscador y entrar por una dirección que el usuario ya conozca.

articles.title: Whoop launches new Strava-like social network for subscribers — and promises it's 'building something deeply human'
articles.text:
Whoop rolls out 'Humans' upgrade for subscribers — Strava-like feature promises to be 'most verifiably human' social network
Share your stats and goals
- Whoop Humans is rolling out to subscribers now
- It lets you connect directly with family and friends
- You get full control over the goals and stats shared
Whoop is expanding its app offerings to let you connect up with friends and family rather than just focusing on your own fitness: it's called Whoop Humans, and it lets you share your stats, goals, and achievements with a selected network of contacts.
It's similar to what you can do with a Strava account, though Whoop is pushing the privacy angle hard: there are granular controls over what's shared and with whom, the option to keep certain stats private permanently or temporarily, and a promise not to "sell or monetize" any of the data collected.
"In a world that's becoming increasingly artificial, we're building something deeply human," says Whoop CEO and founder Will Ahmed. "This is the most verifiably human network ever launched."
"Every account represents a real person with a verified heartbeat. They have real goals, challenges, and achievements. That's what makes Whoop Humans different, and it’s a big area of investment for us," he added.
Separate to Whoop Teams
Some of the content you can share includes sleep, recovery, strain, and activity data, as well as achievements. There's a new feature too, called Whoop Moments, which you can use to celebrate photos of workouts or milestones.
According to Whoop, 57% of its members already belong to at least one Whoop Team. This adds another dimension beyond leaderboards and groups though — it's more personal and directly, between you and friends and relatives.
Whoop says it's also pushing back against what modern-day social media platforms have come to be, filled with AI-produced content, bots, and clickbait. The idea is to increase accountability, make fitness more fun and social, and have the opportunity to support other Whoop users when they need it.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
In theory at least, it sounds like a useful addition to the platform. Whoop Humans is rolling out in the Whoop app from today (November 12), included as part of any Whoop subscription, and Whoop Teams will remain available.

articles.title: Black Friday : Photoshop, Illustrator et Premiere dans Creative Cloud Pro, à 39,31€/mois pendant 3 mois
articles.text:
Pour le Black Friday, Adobe réduit de moitié le prix de sa formule Creative Cloud Pro destinée aux indépendants et aux particuliers. Elle coûte 39,31 € par mois TTC pendant trois mois au lieu de 78,65 €, avant de revenir au tarif plein : nous la situons face aux formules plus ciblées et disons pour qui elle vaut le coup.
Creative Cloud Pro est la formule d’Adobe pour les indépendants et les particuliers qui veulent leurs applications créatives sous un seul abonnement. Elle donne accès à plus de 20 applications, de Photoshop à Adobe Premiere, ainsi qu’à des outils d’IA générative. Pour le Black Friday, Adobe propose Creative Cloud Pro à moitié prix pendant trois mois.
Le tarif tombe à 39,31 € par mois TTC au lieu de 78,65 €, puis revient à 78,65 € par mois. L’abonnement reste annuel avec facturation mensuelle, et seuls les nouveaux abonnements sont concernés.
Adobe Creative Cloud Pro est à 39,31 € par mois TTC pendant trois mois, au lieu de 78,65 €, directement sur le site d’Adobe.
Pourquoi choisir Adobe Creative Cloud Pro ?
- Une suite plutôt qu’un logiciel : Plus de 20 applications couvrent la photo, la vidéo et le graphisme. Vous passez de la retouche dans Photoshop au montage dans Premiere sans multiplier les abonnements.
- Un tarif divisé par deux au départ : 39,31 € par mois TTC pendant trois mois au lieu de 78,65 €, soit plus de 118 € économisés sur le trimestre.
- Un délai pour changer d’avis : Adobe indique un remboursement intégral en cas de résiliation sous 14 jours.
Photo, vidéo, vectoriel : ce que la suite permet de faire
La formule met en avant Photoshop, Lightroom, Illustrator, Adobe Premiere et Acrobat Pro. Vous retouchez des photos, dessinez des visuels vectoriels, montez des vidéos et gérez vos PDF depuis un seul compte. Un photographe, un graphiste indépendant ou un créateur de contenus vidéo y trouve un outil pour chaque étape de son travail, et Adobe y ajoute son IA générative Firefly.
L’abonnement prend tout son sens si vous utilisez au moins deux ou trois de ces logiciels, ou si vous démarrez une activité créative et voulez tout essayer à demi-tarif. Il en a beaucoup moins si votre besoin se limite à la retouche photo : plus de 20 applications à 78,65 € par mois après la promotion représentent alors un budget disproportionné. Les trois premiers mois laissent le temps de le vérifier sur vos propres projets.
Face aux formules ciblées et aux alternatives
Adobe vend aussi des formules plus étroites : notre comparatif des meilleurs logiciels de retouche photo cite Lightroom et Photoshop avec 1 To de stockage à environ 24 € par mois, un prix susceptible d’évoluer. Ce guide place Photoshop en tête avec 9/10, devant Affinity à 9/10, et relève une interface pas toujours intuitive ainsi que l’obligation de s’abonner. Creative Cloud Pro ajoute la vidéo, le vectoriel et le PDF à cette base, ce que ce comparatif centré sur la photo ne couvre pas.
✅ Les points forts
- Plus de 20 applications dans un seul abonnement
- Photoshop, Lightroom, Illustrator, Premiere et Acrobat Pro réunis
- 39,31 € par mois TTC pendant trois mois, soit plus de 118 € économisés
- Outils d’IA générative inclus selon Adobe
- Remboursement intégral sous 14 jours selon Adobe
❌ Les limites
- Retour à 78,65 € par mois TTC après les trois premiers mois
- Réservé aux nouveaux abonnements, engagement annuel
- Budget élevé pour qui n’utilise qu’une seule application
- Date de fin de l’offre non précisée par Adobe
Les conditions complètes de l’offre, abonnement annuel à facturation mensuelle compris, sont détaillées sur la page d’Adobe avant toute validation.
Cette offre vaut surtout pour les photographes, graphistes indépendants et créateurs vidéo qui utilisent déjà plusieurs logiciels Adobe, ou comptent le faire. Trois mois à 39,31 € par mois TTC servent de période de démarrage à demi-tarif, avec un remboursement intégral possible sous 14 jours d’après Adobe. Le vrai prix de la suite reste toutefois 78,65 € par mois, et c’est lui qu’il faut juger.
Sur douze mois, au tarif actuel et sans changement de prix, la facture atteint 825,78 €, soit le montant de l’engagement annuel. Si votre besoin se limite à la retouche photo : une formule ciblée comme celle citée dans notre comparatif coûte nettement moins cher, et mieux vaut passer votre chemin. Dans les autres cas, relisez les conditions de résiliation sur la page de l’offre avant de valider votre abonnement.

articles.title: Five thoughts from Cisco's first quarter of fiscal 2027 - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Five thoughts from Cisco’s first quarter of fiscal 2027
Cisco Systems Inc. opened fiscal 2027 with a quarter that should put any question about whether artificial intelligence will act as a massive tailwind for it to rest. Revenue and earnings hit records, growth rates were the best Cisco has posted in more than 15 years, and management raised its full-year outlook and AI infrastructure revenue target.
While Cisco has delivered a string of solid quarters, some investors are concerned about the durability of the growth. After listening to the analyst call, I maintain that accelerated growth is what Cisco watchers should expect, as AI will act as a catalyst for several years. Here are my five thoughts, plus the one metric I think investors should care about most:
This is a supercycle, not a sugar high
Asked why this isn’t simply the top of a hyperscaler spending cycle, Chief Executive Chuck Robbins (pictured) cited five growth drivers: hyperscale AI, the campus refresh, the “post-Mythos” security upgrade cycle, sovereign infrastructure and enterprise hybrid data centers. “All five of these are multiyear, multibillion,” he said. “And they’re all in relatively early stages.” In particular, the enterprise opportunity is in its infancy. Using the baseball analogy for “what inning” we’re in, the pitchers are still warming up, and enterprise is what Cisco does best.
Though hyperscalers have been driving AI growth across the industry, only one of the five trends Robbins highlighted was related to that group of companies. Chief Financial Officer Mark Patterson reinforced the point by breaking down the guidance raise, noting that a large share came from Cisco’s core, non-hyperscale business. “It’s not just campus,” he said. “It’s broad-based, and the core continues to do quite well.”
The market still views the enterprise as a slow-refresh business. The call made a strong case that it’s about to become the bigger part of Cisco’s AI story.
The campus refresh has barely started, and Mythos is the accelerant
During the investor Q&A, a data point was worth highlighting. Robbins said that of the campus switching Cisco sold this quarter, “only 9% was really coming from the new portfolio.” Despite multiple quarters of strong campus growth, the installed base has barely moved to the next generation.
Two forces will push this base to accelerate an upgrade. One is agentic AI, which Robbins said is driving “modernization for bandwidth reasons” because agents generate traffic that campus networks were never designed to handle. The other is the security fallout from frontier models such as Anthropic’s Claude Mythos — the Mythos moment. “We’re beginning to hear from customers who are attributing orders to early Mythos implications,” Robbins said, noting that European service providers are upgrading managed customer premises equipment.
Robbins added that customers “got to get the architecture exactly right.” That suggests a long, deliberate redesign rather than a buying spree, which is characteristic of a multiyear cycle.
Silicon One made Cisco a silicon company
Cisco has long been criticized for building its own silicon as the industry shifted to merchant silicon. Robbins said that outside of optics, the hyperscale AI business is “100% Silicon One-based platforms.” The P200 continues to win scale-across deals, and the G300 is now in customer labs.
Asked why Cisco keeps winning those deals, Robbins kept it simple: “It’s really about performance and power. And there’s just this whole focus on diversity of silicon in the space.” The second point is the more strategic one. No hyperscaler wants a single supplier for any critical layer of its AI fabric, and Cisco is the credible second source.
The bigger long-term play is the enterprise. Silicon One is already shipping across parts of the enterprise portfolio, and Robbins said the target to convert all of it by fiscal 2029 “is still on track.” That gives Cisco a single silicon architecture from the hyperscale data center to the branch, with cost and roadmap control competitors can’t match.
The reality is that at Cisco’s volumes, it makes no sense to buy merchant silicon. Not only can it build it cheaper, but it can also optimize it specifically for its own features and capabilities.
Enterprise AI is going hybrid and sovereign, which plays to Cisco’s strengths
A theme running through the call is that AI is decentralizing. “Our enterprise customers will be running AI applications in the cloud, but they’re also investing heavily in private data centers,” Robbins said. “They want to run open-weight and open-source models in their own data centers. They want to train on their own data in their own data centers.”
Sovereignty is driving in the same direction, with Cisco extending its Sovereign Critical Infrastructure portfolio from Europe to Canada and preannouncing India. Robbins noted that Cisco is “one of the few companies that has maintained a robust on-premises portfolio.” For years, analysts treated that on-premises focus as a liability. In a world where countries and regulated industries want operational control, it has become an advantage.
Equally important is what Cisco isn’t chasing. Robbins called neocloud exposure “relatively immaterial,” adding that “we’ve been very conservative relative to the credit situations.” That’s a disciplined choice. Cisco is growing into the safest parts of the AI build-out rather than financing its riskiest buyers.
Given the number of neoclouds, one could look at them as a massive pot of gold, but they often required vendor financing. If the neocloud isn’t successful, it’s the financing organization left holding the bag. This was the case with CLECs in the Internet days. Cisco was conservative then and will continue to be.
Security has turned the corner, and the real prize is agent trust
Security has been the weak spot in Cisco’s story, so this quarter’s progress matters. Robbins said core security orders, excluding Splunk, were “the best it’s been in three years,” with firewalls, Zero Trust secure access, and AI Defense all gaining customers. Patterson said Cisco is “a little bit above the expectations that we set out” and feels “good about turning the corner.”
The refresh cycle drives near-term numbers, but the strategic prize is trust for AI agents. Robbins said enterprise conversations now center on “agentic security, agentic identity, agentic observability, as well as the new security architecture needed for the AI era.” The network is where agent traffic flows, making it the natural enforcement point. Cisco owns more of that network than anyone.
Investor concerns received clear answers. On margins, Patterson said, “gross margins are pretty much right on target,” and on supply, “we’re seeing not a lot of issues at all.” Robbins added that Cisco is growing revenue “with less headcount than we had at the beginning” two years ago.
The key metric for investors
The number I’d watch most closely isn’t AI revenue, campus orders, or gross margin. It’s the growth of Cisco Cloud Control. Robbins mentioned it almost in passing, noting thousands of sign-ups and integrations with AI Canvas, Cisco IQ and Cisco Model Foundry. Most people will think of Cloud Control as a network management tool, but that badly understates its potential.
Cloud Control is now Cisco’s core product. The best analogy is VMware vCenter, the data center’s control point that turned a collection of products into a sticky platform. Cheaper, sometimes free hypervisors never made a dent in VMware’s share because the operational control gained from vCenter far outweighed the few bucks saved on hypervisor licenses. Cloud Control is broader and potentially more impactful because Cisco is positioning it as the control point for enterprise AI, not just the network through the following capabilities.
- A centralized control plane across Cisco, partner, and third-party infrastructure.
- An agentic operations platform where AI agents manage day-to-day network and security operations.
- An AI-based troubleshooting engine that reduces resolution time from hours to minutes.
- An app development platform for infrastructure, enabling customers and partners to build on the network.
- A model fine-tuning toolset for domain-specific AI, through Model Foundry.
- A trust platform that enforces policy for users, devices, and agents.
- An observability platform that brings together network, security, and Splunk telemetry into one view.
- A tokenomics platform that helps enterprises understand and manage what AI costs and what it delivers.
Cisco’s numerous network and security competitors have their own agentic operations platforms, and many beat Cisco to market. However, Cisco played the long game. In my conversations with Chief Product Officer Jeetu Patel, he has been emphatic about how important Cloud Control is to Cisco’s vision of shifting to a platform company. It enables customers to manage the underlying infrastructure, including third parties, through a single dashboard.
If Cloud Control becomes the enterprise IT console for managing AI-era infrastructure, Cisco stops competing on boxes and starts competing on control. Hardware cycles always ebb and flow, so always being best of breed is impossible. Whether this one becomes a transformation for Cisco depends on whether customers run their environments on Cloud Control. My advice to Cisco is to start disclosing active usage, partner integrations, and attach rates for the platform.
My advice to investors is to start asking for them. That number will tell you what Cisco is worth five years from now.
Zeus Kerravala is a principal analyst at ZK Research, a division of Kerravala Consulting. He wrote this article for SiliconANGLE.

articles.title: Silicon Motion Showcases Next-Generation Enterprise Storage Solutions at SC26
articles.text:
Thursday, November 12th 2026
Silicon Motion Showcases Next-Generation Enterprise Storage Solutions at SC26
Silicon Motion Technology Corporation, a global leader in designing and marketing NAND flash controllers for solid-state storage devices, today announced that it will showcase its PCIe Gen 5 and PCIe Gen 6 MonTitan enterprise SSD controllers and reference platforms designed to address the evolving storage demands of AI factories, Agentic AI, and large-scale inference deployments at Supercomputing 2026 (SC26), taking place November 16 to 19 in Chicago, Illinois, at Booth #6816. The company will also highlight its enterprise PCIe NVMe boot drive solutions, including a demonstration featuring the NVIDIA DPU platform, alongside its Ferri-eMMC embedded storage solution with the ASPEED AST2600 BMC, showcasing storage technologies for AI servers and next-generation data center infrastructure.
Alex Chou, Senior Vice President of Enterprise Storage & Display Interface Solution Business at Silicon Motion"As AI infrastructure evolves to support multi-agent and increasingly complex agentic workloads, storage performance is becoming a critical factor in overall system performance and efficiency," "Our PCIe Gen 5 and Gen 6 enterprise SSD controllers are designed to address these challenges by delivering high performance, low latency, scalable capacity, and power efficiency, helping customers build the next generation of AI infrastructure."
At SC26, Silicon Motion will demonstrate how its enterprise SSD controllers, reference platforms, and boot drive solutions address evolving storage requirements across two key areas of AI infrastructure:
Enterprise SSD Controllers for AI Factory Storage Applications
- SM8366 MonTitan SSD Reference Design Kit for KV Cache Offload and Agentic AI Infrastructure: Built on Silicon Motion's PCIe Gen 5 SM8366 enterprise SSD controller, the MonTitan development platform supports multiple form factors, including U.2, E1.S, E3.S, and E1.L, with TLC and QLC NAND. Supporting high-capacity SSD configurations of up to 256 TB with QLC NAND, the platform enables scalable storage deployments for AI inference and KV cache offload. Powered by Silicon Motion's patented PerformaShape QoS Engine, the platform is designed to deliver low latency and predictable performance for demanding AI infrastructure workloads.
- SM8466: PCIe Gen 6 enterprise SSD controller delivering up to 28 GB/s sequential throughput and 7M random IOPS, supporting enterprise SSD capacities beyond 512 TB. Designed for high-performance AI computing and data-intensive applications, the SM8466 enables scalable, high-bandwidth storage architectures for next-generation AI infrastructure.
- SM8388: A power-efficient PCIe Gen 5 enterprise SSD controller optimized for high-capacity nearline SSD applications. Featuring a single-controller architecture, the SM8388 provides an efficient approach to scaling flash-based storage capacity while balancing performance, power consumption, and total cost of ownership for hyperscale data centers and AI infrastructure.
Enterprise Boot Drive Solutions for AI Server Ecosystems
- Enterprise PCIe NVMe DRAM-less Boot SSD Solutions: Designed for enterprise servers, DPUs, networking platforms, and AI storage nodes, Silicon Motion's DRAM-less boot SSD solutions offer flexible M.2 and BGA form factors, delivering compact, reliable, and power-efficient storage for diverse server architectures. The solutions are optimized to meet the endurance, reliability, and operational requirements of modern enterprise and AI infrastructure.
- Enterprise PCIe NVMe Boot SSD Solution with DRAM: Designed for near-CPU storage applications requiring frequent data access and consistent performance, this PCIe Gen 5 enterprise boot SSD controller solution supports M.2 2280 and E1.S form factors, with user capacities ranging from 480 GB to 3.84 TB. Delivering sequential read speeds of up to 14 GB/s, the solution supports demanding server workloads such as system logging, metadata management, and frequent read/write operations, where efficient data handling and predictable performance are essential.
Visitors are invited to experience Silicon Motion's latest storage innovations at booth #6816 during SC26.
