articles.title: Panne Outlook : la messagerie de Microsoft toujours inaccessible ce vendredi, ce que l’on sait
articles.text:
[ Mise à jour du 13 novembre à 8h48 : la situation s’améliore en partie, sans être réglée. Microsoft observe une reprise partielle dans certaines régions, mais reconnaît qu’elle n’est « pas durable ». En France, Outlook restait inaccessible ce vendredi matin. En Australie, le ministre de l’Intérieur Tony Burke affirme que Microsoft estimerait avoir affaire à « une mise à jour qui a mal tourné », comme lors de la panne CrowdStrike de 2024, ce que l’éditeur n’a pas confirmé publiquement, précise Reuters. ]
Les premiers signalements sont arrivés jeudi 12 novembre, peu avant 19 heures, heure de Paris. « Nous enquêtons sur des signalements d’utilisateurs qui rencontrent des problèmes pour accéder à leurs boîtes Exchange Online par plusieurs méthodes de connexion sur le continent américain », écrivait alors le compte Microsoft 365 Status sur X, en référence au service qui fait tourner Outlook. L’alerte s’est vite étendue à toutes les régions du monde, et la liste des services touchés s’est allongée au fil de la soirée : Teams, SharePoint, l’assistant Copilot ou encore des outils de cybersécurité réservés aux entreprises. En France, Outlook restait inaccessible ce vendredi matin, sur ordinateur comme sur smartphone, comme nous avons pu le constater à la rédaction.
 We’re investigating reports of users experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas. More details can be found in the Microsoft 365 admin center under EX1550543.
— Microsoft 365 Status (@MSFT365Status) November 12, 2026
L’ampleur de la panne est rare pour Microsoft. Downdetector a reçu environ 200 000 signalements d’utilisateurs, venus de plus de 70 pays, selon Bloomberg, qui la classe parmi les plus importantes de l’histoire de l’éditeur, dont les précédentes interruptions duraient rarement plus de quelques heures. Les conséquences se font sentir bien au-delà des bureaux. Au Japon, le ministère des Finances a indiqué ne pas avoir pu recevoir d’e-mails pendant presque toute la journée, et des ministères ont dû afficher leurs agendas sur papier. En Nouvelle-Zélande, les services d’immigration ont suspendu le traitement des demandes de visa. Aux États-Unis, des districts scolaires, des universités et des hôpitaux ont prévenu que leurs communications pourraient être limitées.
 Microsoft’s outage reports on November 12 reached 74 countries and territories in about an hour on Downdetector.
Microsoft says its Exchange Online incident began at 16:17 UTC. Reports to Downdetector about Outlook began climbing at about 17:25 UTC, 12:25 in New York. By 18:25, reports about five Microsoft services combined reached 19,650 a minute, against <15 a minute on an average Thursday.
Outlook reports alone peaked at more than 2,000 times their normal level.
Reports did not stay in the Americas. They jumped tenfold in the UK at 17:43, in India at 23:21 local time and in New Zealand at 06:55 local time. Between 17:00 and 18:55 UTC, nearly 3 in 10 reports came from outside the US. We count a country here once its reports reach ten times normal and at least 20 in five minutes.
Reports about Microsoft 365, Copilot, Teams and OneDrive each rose more than a hundredfold, and Azure about a hundredfold. Xbox, GitHub and LinkedIn, also Microsoft’s, rose far less.
Microsoft said a portion of its infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions. At 19:38 UTC, reports were still running at more than 11,000 a minute.
— Downdetector (@downdetector) November 12, 2026
Des serveurs qui retombent dès qu’ils sont relancés
Microsoft a d’abord parlé d’une partie de son infrastructure qui « subit une charge élevée dans plusieurs régions », avant de corriger le tir dans la soirée. « La charge élevée n’est pas due à une hausse du trafic, mais à un certain nombre de serveurs devenus indisponibles de manière inattendue, ce qui met sous tension le reste de l’infrastructure », a précisé l’éditeur. Ses ingénieurs ont ensuite découvert qu’« un processus central sur les serveurs touchés se retrouve débordé », ce qui les empêche de répondre et aggrave la perte de capacité. Microsoft assure n’avoir « connaissance d’aucune activité malveillante » à l’origine de l’incident, rapporte Bloomberg.
Pour tenter de reprendre la main pendant la nuit, Microsoft a suspendu tous ses déploiements, redémarré les serveurs touchés et redirigé une partie du trafic, sans résultat durable. « Les serveurs que nous avons remis en service peuvent redevenir inactifs dès qu’ils reçoivent du trafic », reconnaissait l’éditeur au milieu de la nuit, avant de commencer à reconstruire une partie de ses machines avec une configuration antérieure. Vendredi matin, le constat restait le même : « Nous observons une reprise partielle dans les régions où nous avons appliqué ces ajustements, mais ces actions ne permettent pas un rétablissement durable. » Microsoft ne donne toujours aucun délai de retour à la normale.
 We’re continuing our efforts to improve server stability to improve traffic flow. This includes adjusting traffic protocols, redistributing traffic, and applying strategic traffic blocking measures. We’re observing partial recovery across regions in which we’ve applied these adjustments; however, these actions aren’t resulting in sustained recovery, so we’re reviewing what additional actions we can take to improve overall infrastructure stability. More info under EX1550543 and MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin center, as well as https://t.co/pYdahqxDv3 if the admin center is not available to you.
— Microsoft 365 Status (@MSFT365Status) November 13, 2026
La panne gêne aussi les assistants d’intelligence artificielle qui se connectent aux comptes Microsoft pour lire les e-mails ou consulter l’agenda. Outre Copilot, Anthropic et OpenAI ont signalé que Claude et ChatGPT ne parvenaient plus à accéder aux services de Microsoft 365.
Que faire en attendant ?
Le problème vient des serveurs de Microsoft. Il est donc inutile de réinstaller Outlook, de réinitialiser son mot de passe ou de modifier ses paramètres. Le plus simple est de suivre l’évolution de la situation sur la page d’état des services de Microsoft ou sur le compte X Microsoft 365 Status, et de passer par un autre moyen de communication pour les échanges urgents. Microsoft prévient que le retour du service pourrait être progressif, à mesure que les applications se reconnectent.
Cette panne n’a pas de lien avec un autre incident survenu cette semaine sur la messagerie grand public de Microsoft, où des filtres anti-spam défaillants ont bloqué des e-mails légitimes pendant quatre jours.

articles.title: “Pas de rétablissement durable” : Microsoft n’arrive plus à relancer Microsoft 365, Outlook et Teams toujours en panne
articles.text:
Panne Microsoft 365 : Outlook et Teams toujours perturbés, Microsoft peine à relancer ses serveurs
Vendredi 13 : Outlook a pris sa journée
Des boîtes mail figées, des agendas Teams muets, un Copilot qui ne répond plus. Depuis jeudi soir, une partie du monde professionnel tourne au ralenti dans 74 pays. Microsoft relance ses serveurs un par un, mais ils retombent en panne dès que le trafic revient. Et l'éditeur ne sait toujours pas expliquer pourquoi.
Une panne mondiale paralyse Microsoft 365 depuis le jeudi 12 novembre, peu avant 19 heures (heure de Paris). Outlook, Teams, SharePoint et Copilot sont perturbés dans 74 pays selon Downdetector, dont la France. Vendredi matin, Microsoft admettait que ses correctifs ne donnaient pas les résultats attendus et n'annonçait aucune date de retour à la normale.
Panne Outlook et Teams : quels services Microsoft 365 sont touchés ?
Le problème part d'Exchange Online, le service qui héberge les boîtes mail des comptes professionnels et scolaires. Outlook sur le web, le logiciel de bureau et les applications mobiles n'arrivent plus à se connecter, et l'envoi des messages peut prendre des heures. Exchange Online avait déjà connu des ratés : en octobre 2025, un bug de connexion empêchait d'ouvrir Outlook classique, sur un périmètre bien plus restreint.
We're investigating reports of users experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas. More details can be found in the Microsoft 365 admin center under EX1550543.
— Microsoft 365 Status (@MSFT365Status) November 12, 2026
Tout ce qui dépend de la messagerie est touché par ricochet. Dans Teams, le calendrier, les invitations et la planification de réunions sont en panne. Les appels, les visioconférences et les conversations, eux, fonctionnent pour l'essentiel. Copilot Chat peut ne plus charger ou ne plus répondre. Planner, To Do, Intune et les outils de sécurité Defender figurent aussi dans la liste de Microsoft.
La panne touche même les assistants concurrents : OpenAI et Anthropic ont signalé des dysfonctionnements sur leurs connecteurs Microsoft 365, qui permettent à ChatGPT et Claude de lire les mails et l'agenda. Aux États-Unis, Downdetector a compté près de 130 000 signalements sur Outlook au plus fort de la panne.
Pourquoi la panne Microsoft 365 dure aussi longtemps
Microsoft écarte un afflux de trafic. D'après l'éditeur, cité par BleepingComputer, des serveurs sont devenus "indisponibles de manière inattendue", et leur charge s'est reportée sur le reste de l'infrastructure. Ces machines ont d'abord échoué aux contrôles de santé automatiques. Ensuite, le processus qui établit les connexions sécurisées a saturé. Les connexions sécurisées avaient déjà fait tomber Microsoft : en février 2020, Teams était resté hors service trois heures à cause d'un certificat de sécurité expiré.
Microsoft a gelé tous ses déploiements, redirigé le trafic et redémarré les serveurs touchés, sans grand succès. Dans la nuit, l'entreprise a reconnu que certains serveurs relancés cessaient de répondre dès qu'ils recevaient de nouveau du trafic.
The servers we returned to service can become unresponsive again once they receive traffic; we're analyzing diagnostic data to determine what's triggering the behavior. In parallel, we're temporarily limiting which types of traffic can reach the affected infrastructure in some…
— Microsoft 365 Status (@MSFT365Status) November 13, 2026
La meilleure piste à ce stade : Microsoft dit avoir "commencé à annuler une modification récente de la configuration réseau, qui coïncide avec le début de l'incident". La cause reste à confirmer. Charles Lamanna, vice-président exécutif de Microsoft, a écarté toute cyberattaque.
Au petit matin, le bilan restait maigre. Microsoft constate "un rétablissement partiel dans les régions où nous avons appliqué ces ajustements", mais reconnaît que ces mesures "ne permettent pas un rétablissement durable".
We’re continuing our efforts to improve server stability to improve traffic flow. This includes adjusting traffic protocols, redistributing traffic, and applying strategic traffic blocking measures. We're observing partial recovery across regions in which we've applied these…
— Microsoft 365 Status (@MSFT365Status) November 13, 2026
Cette panne rappelle forcément celle de juillet 2024, mais les deux ne se ressemblent pas. À l'époque, une mise à jour défectueuse de CrowdStrike, un éditeur de cybersécurité, avait bloqué 8,5 millions de PC sous Windows, des aéroports jusqu'aux hôpitaux. Cette fois, le problème vient du cloud de Microsoft lui-même.
Outlook ne fonctionne plus : que faire en attendant le retour à la normale ?
Ne réinstallez pas Outlook et ne changez pas votre mot de passe : la panne vient des serveurs de Microsoft. Pour suivre le rétablissement, consultez la page d'état officielle de Microsoft 365 ou Downdetector pour les signalements en France.
D'ici là, les messages instantanés de Teams restent le moyen le plus fiable de joindre vos collègues. Vous pouvez en général ouvrir vos fichiers SharePoint et OneDrive, mais la recherche peut échouer. Les administrateurs informatiques trouveront le détail de l'incident dans le centre d'administration Microsoft 365, sous les références EX1550543 et MO1550821.

articles.title: Without Jensen Huang, is it game over for GeForce?
articles.text:
THE AFTERMATH: Jensen Huang's resignation this morning ends Nvidia's 33-year founder era, but it doesn't end the story. There's a search for a successor with no obvious candidate, an espionage case now touching four governments, a congressional hearing, and a growing roster of people offering their own picks for who should run the world's most important AI chipmaker.
Nvidia moved quickly to project continuity. In an internal memo, longtime director Harvey Jones told employees he would serve as the company's first-ever board chair. Jones, a former Synopsys CEO, has sat on Nvidia's board since its founding in 1993. The fact that Nvidia never had a separate chair until today says a lot about how much authority sat with one person.
CFO Colette Kress, at Nvidia since 2013, will run the company on an interim basis while keeping her finance role. CNBC reports she is gathering the executive team at the Santa Clara HQ to talk leadership and continuity. Her first real test: Nvidia is set to report quarterly results in just a few days, on November 17.
Meanwhile, investors are not waiting and the immediate reaction has been that Nvidia shares opened down more than 13%, briefly dropping the company below a $4 trillion market cap, before partially recovering by midday. Nvidia is still on track for six straight weekly losses, its longest losing streak since 2012. Apple has reclaimed the title of world's most valuable company. Wall Street and everyone else is split on what comes next.
No succession plan
Bloomberg reports that Nvidia has hired an outside firm to find candidates, but replacing Huang won't be easy. For three decades, Huang combined deep technical knowledge with tight operational control, running the company with a famously flat structure and dozens of direct reports.
Kress has become the obvious continuity pick, with the expectation that she will hold the seat for about a year before an outsider takes over. Among insiders, the name that comes up most is Ian Buck, who runs Nvidia's hyperscale and HPC business and is closely tied to CUDA's origins.
Ben Bajarin called him the most logical choice, though Bloomberg notes he lacks the operating experience typically expected of a CEO. Analysts have also floated chief scientist Bill Dally, CTO Michael Kagan, and 32-year veteran Jeff Fisher. Huang's children, Madison and Spencer, both hold management roles at the company, but even observers who mention them question whether either is ready.
The outside list is a who's who of chip leadership: Arm CEO and former Nvidia executive Rene Haas, Intel's Lip-Bu Tan, Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji, and AMD's Lisa Su, who happens to be Huang's first cousin once removed and runs Nvidia's most credible rival. Some analysts have even suggested a co-CEO setup, pairing a technical leader with an operator.
President Trump has also got a favorite. He declared that only Tim Cook could fill Huang's shoes, adding: "A Legend replaces a Legend!"
Elon Musk, meanwhile, is recruiting. Hours before the resignation, while reports of a possible ouster were circulating, a user on X asked Musk to hire Huang. Musk replied: "That would be an honor." He also endorsed a post arguing Nvidia's board should wait for its investigation to conclude before acting.
Is it also game over for GeForce?
That list should worry anyone who buys graphics cards. Look closely and you'll notice most of those names built their careers in data centers, finance, mobile chips, or CPUs. None of them co-founded a company in 1993 to make 3D graphics for PC games.
Huang did, and for all of Nvidia's pivot to AI, he never fully let go of that. Even after rebranding Nvidia as an AI infrastructure company, he kept reminding audiences that GeForce is what brought CUDA into the world, and that the AI boom wouldn't exist without it. At GTC in March, he called the modern Nvidia "the house that GeForce made."
Nvidia's gaming business hit a record $16 billion in the company's last fiscal year, but it was still a rounding error next to the data center. Then this year, Nvidia stopped reporting gaming separately and folded it into a new "Edge Computing" bucket alongside workstations, consoles, robotics, cars, and telecom gear. In the most recent quarter, that entire group brought in $7.2 billion, versus $89 billion from the data center. That's a mere 7.5% of revenue for everything Nvidia sells outside a data center and the earnings release didn't mention GeForce or gaming once.
Under Huang, GeForce arguably survived in part on sentiment, the founder's attachment to the business that built the company.
Gamers have been feeling the shift for a couple of years now. As AI swallowed the world's memory supply, Nvidia reportedly cut GeForce production by as much as 40% in the first half of the year. Kress herself (now interim CEO) warned investors that supply constraints would weigh on gaming going forward. It was widely known that no new gaming GPUs would come out this year, which would be the first such gap in roughly three decades.
Under Huang, GeForce arguably survived in part on sentiment, the founder's attachment to the business that built the company. A successor without that history will look at the same spreadsheet and see a comparatively unattractive consumer business competing with data center chips for the same scarce memory and TSMC wafers. From there, the options range from benign neglect to a spin-off or outright sale.
Then again, GeForce is still the entry point to CUDA for many developers and students. Consumer and data center GPUs share architectures, so much of the R&D carries over.
Nvidia also supplies the chip inside Nintendo's Switch 2. Untangling all of that would be messy. A more realistic risk isn't a sale but a slow fade: fewer launches, longer gaps between generations, and graphics card pricing dictated by how much memory is left after the data center business has taken its share. (If the AI bubble goes bust, that's an entirely different conversation.)
Whoever takes the job, how much attention Nvidia gives GeForce over the next couple of years will be telling.
The spy story keeps getting stranger
The Wall Street Journal is reporting a most surreal detail about the whole spy saga (yet): Huang was introduced to Alice Huang by Kang Wei, a Chinese businessman and former star fund manager he'd known for about a decade. Kang was also Alice Huang's husband, according to people who know the couple.
Huang and Kang reportedly first crossed paths in the 2010s, when Kang's firm Shanghai Hexi was investing in video game companies and Nvidia was mostly a gaming chip business. For roughly two years, Kang appeared to accept his wife's relationship with the Nvidia CEO, at times joking to associates that she worked as Huang's assistant.
The Journal describes the couple as serial dealmakers who moved from games to pharmaceuticals to cloud computing. In 2023, they renamed a Singapore company Megaspeed International, with Alice Huang as a director. Using Alibaba as a promised anchor customer, Megaspeed secured access to chips as an Nvidia partner.
According to the WSJ's sources, Alice Huang and Kang Wei pitched investors on new data center projects, promising to triple their money in three years and expressing confidence they could get Nvidia chips into China.
People familiar with the matter say most of the servers went to Malaysian data centers serving Alibaba, but some were shipped into China. Megaspeed says it followed all export control rules, but the WSJ has sources who say the couple pitched investors on new data center projects, promising to triple their money in three years and expressing confidence they could get Nvidia chips into China.
The New York Times is also reporting today that Singapore's government has just disclosed it held Alice Huang's passport from June 2025 to February over potential false declarations tied to Megaspeed. She was eventually released for lack of evidence, given a stern warning, and banned from re-entering the country.
What happens now with the "central bank of AI"
Beyond Nvidia's own stock, the GPU maker became more than a chip supplier under Jensen: it is an investor, financier, and loan guarantor to a huge slice of the AI industry, with obligations CNBC estimates at around $400 billion.
To name a few such data points: shares of Nvidia-backed neoclouds dropped today, with CoreWeave down about 8%. Big commitments include the $12.9 billion Hugging Face acquisition, which is under review, and a $10 billion share purchase tied to Anthropic's IPO next week.
But none of this changes Nvidia's product roadmap. Vera Rubin is shipping, demand remains strong, and while AMD stock has climbed ~30% in the last few days, there's no way AMD could magically absorb Nvidia's customers even if they all switched tomorrow.
AMD isn't the only alternative, either. Google is now selling its TPUs to outside customers like Anthropic and Meta instead of only renting them through its cloud, and Amazon has signed up Anthropic and OpenAI for gigawatts of Trainium chips. Intel remains the question mark. Nvidia even owns a stake in it after a $5 billion investment last year, and its CEO is on some analysts' list to run Nvidia.
For 33 years, Nvidia's succession plan was essentially Jensen Huang. It now needs a real one.

articles.title: ByteDance estaria trabalhando em IA rival do Muse • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
ByteDance estaria trabalhando em IA rival do Muse
Agente pessoal pode chegar “nas próximas semanas” com proposta bastante semelhante à nova inteligência artificial da empresa estadunidense.
A empresa chinesa ByteDance, criadora do TikTok, estaria trabalhando no lançamento de um novo agente pessoal de IA nos moldes do Muse, da Meta. A ideia seria alcançar as principais companhias estadunidenses do setor em termos de tecnologia. A expectativa é pelo lançamento “nas próximas semanas”, mas ainda não há informações sobre seu funcionamento.
Em uma reunião fechada, o co-fundador da empresa, Zhang Yiming conversou com o time responsável sobre prioridades no desenvolvimento da nova inteligência artificial. Segundo ele, a dona do TikTok teria potencial de competir diretamente com nomes como Anthropic, OpenAI e a própria Meta por volta de 2029 ou 2030. As informações foram divulgadas pela Bloomberg.
A ideia da empresa seria bater de frente com os principais nomes do mercado nos próximos três anos, sobretudo as companhias estadunidenses. Ainda não há informações sobre a aplicação da IA em si. A expectativa é por um modelo bem parecido com o Muse, agente pessoal da Meta anunciado por Mark Zuckerberg no início de setembro.
Isso significa acesso a serviços de e-mail, agendas e até contas de bancos. Agentes como o Muse podem responder mensagens, fazer pedidos online, realizar transações, entre outras atividades automatizadas. Outro uso está relacionado a hardware como os Meta Glasses e até o “tamagochi” Charm. Ainda não está claro se a ideia da ByteDance também passa por oferecer os serviços em dispositivos.
Vale lembrar que o Muse está disponível apenas nos Estados Unidos e já apareceu envolvido em diferentes polêmicas. Nas primeiras semanas de funcionamento, a Meta contou com atendentes humanos terceirizados para realizar as tarefas de chamadas telefônicas, o que levou à suspensão dos testes da recurso.
Já em outubro, uma pesquisa da empresa de segurança Claroc identificou cerca de 7 mil conversas do agente expostas para qualquer um ler online. Segundo o site Engadget, a entrada da ByteDance no mercado de agentes pessoais de IA levantaria dúvidas relacionadas à privacidade.
O governo dos Estados Unidos, por exemplo, tem combatido a entrada de tecnologias chinesas no país para evitar o acesso a dados de cidadãos. As políticas vão desde a proibição de chips até o bloqueio de chamadas telefônicas a partir de telefonias chinesas.

These are the same magnetic, infinity-mirror fans available individually, with 5 reverse-blade intake fans and 2 standard-blade exhaust fans already installed. Builders get a coordinated case-fan setup, less installation work, and more of their budget available for other components.

LINK FAN uses magnetic alignment and reinforced connections to simplify assembly. A single 7-pin cable connects up to 7 linked fans to LUMI HUB. Through LUMI, each fan's speed and lighting remain individually adjustable through LUMI software within the same chain. One hub supports up to 14 LINK FANs, while LUMI offers 20 lighting effects.Pricing and Availability
KING 95 3D and LINK FAN launch on November 11, 2026. Both product families are offered in Black and White, with Standard and Reverse Blade options for LINK FAN.For more information, visit the product page.

articles.text:
Hbada's new flagship E3 Ultra (Gen 5) ergonomic chair arrives with a 150-degree recline, 8D armrests, and it's $360 off for Black Friday
Three-zone lumbar support adapts as you change position
The Hbada E3 Ultra (Gen 5) ergonomic chair has arrived with an unusual combination of adjustable support, built-in massage, and heating. Designed for people who spend long hours at their desks, it offers a 150-degree recline, adaptive lumbar support, and numerous adjustments to help support different sitting positions.
Best For: Remote workers, creatives, and anyone wanting a highly adjustable office chair with integrated massage and heating.
The Deal: The Hbada E3 Ultra (Gen 5) has launched priced at $639 in the US and £639 in the UK, down from its eventual $999/£999 retail price. That's a $360/£360 saving, or 36% off.
Hbada's new ergonomic office chair features full-body posture tracking, three-zone dynamic lumbar support, heated 4D massage, 150-degree recline, 8D armrests, 4D headrest, adjustable seat depth, breathable mesh, and wired controls.
Also available in the UK, Hbada's new ergonomic office chair offers the same mix of great features and comes heavily discounted.
Why we recommend it
The Hbada E3 Ultra (Gen 5) takes a more fancy approach to ergonomic seating than a conventional office chair. Its Full-Body Active Tracking System combines a 12-rail linkage, eight-axis synchronized movement, and spring damping to help the chair follow posture changes.
Its three-zone lumbar system features adjustable wings that rotate approximately 80 degrees, along with 60mm of height adjustment and 32mm of tracking movement. This will maintain lower-back contact whether you're working upright or leaning back.
The most unusual feature is without doubt the heated 4D massage system which offers kneading, tapping, and vibration functions. There are three massage intensity settings and three heating levels, with separate controls for each. Heating sessions last five minutes.
The chair also includes 8D armrests, a 4D headrest, adjustable seat depth, and breathable mesh upholstery. The backrest reclines to 150 degrees and locks into four positions.
For more of our favorites, see our guide to the best office chairs we've tested.
Price context & historical value
The $639/£639 introductory price represents a 36% reduction against Hbada's eventual $999/£999 retail price. As the chair has only just launched, it hasn't previously been available at a lower price.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the E3 Ultra (Gen 5) if...
If you want extensive ergonomic adjustments, a deep recline, and integrated heating and massage, the E3 Ultra (Gen 5) is the chair for you, especially at the introductory price.
❌ Skip the E3 Ultra (Gen 5) if...
If you prefer a simpler chair, don't need powered comfort features, or would rather wait for independent reviews to establish its long-term durability before spending this much money.

articles.title: Beyond data breaches, NordVPN's new tool promises to help you shrink your full digital footprint
articles.text:
Beyond data breaches, NordVPN's new tool promises to help you shrink your full digital footprint
A breach alert only tells you half the story — NordVPN's new Digital footprint scanner tracks the passive digital shadow you leave behind every day
- NordVPN's new tool scans open-source data to show where your details are visible online
- Digital footprint tracks forgotten accounts, leaked location data, and more
- Users get personalized tips to reduce exposure, though it won't completely erase your web presence
NordVPN is rolling out a new tool called Digital footprint to show users exactly what information about them sits in plain sight online. Rather than just alerting you when a database gets hacked, the scanner pieces together old accounts, web browsing trails, and exposed location records.
Most people assume that changing a leaked password keeps them safe. Yet data brokers still buy and assemble personal profiles based on ordinary internet use, which banks and employers can then use to evaluate you.
The release arrives as the best VPN brand continues to turn its core tunnel into an all-in-one security app. By combining the new tool with its built-in dark web monitoring, the provider wants to help users spot their exposed records before scammers can exploit them.
NordVPN – the best VPN overall 
NordVPN came out on top in our 2026 round of VPN tests. We think it's the best VPN for most people. We’re confident that virtually anyone can sign up for NordVPN and get what they need from it. It’s easy to use, very secure, fast enough for gaming, and offers flawless streaming service unblocking.
Subscriptions start from $3.49 per month, and you can try it out risk-free with a 30-day money-back guarantee.
What NordVPN's Digital footprint checks
Data leaks grab headlines, particularly after global data breaches jumped 13 percent. But forgotten message boards, unmanaged apps, and location breadcrumbs leak just as much personal information.
"People know about data breaches, but that’s only part of the picture. Your data is also out there because of accounts you forgot about, profiles that were built about you, and everyday browsing. Digital footprint shows you the full extent of your exposure and tells you what to do about it,” said Domininkas Virbickas, product director at NordVPN.
To find that material, the system scans open-source intelligence across the web. It flags lingering profiles you abandoned years ago, highlights exposed geographic data, and maps out what a curious stranger could dig up on you in minutes.
NEW: Leave No Trace — A weekly newsletter on digital privacy and online surveillance.
Leave No Trace investigates the companies and governments putting our digital freedom at risk — and the people fighting back.
📩 Subscribe now to get every edition delivered to your inbox every Friday, launching this September.
Does it actually remove my data?
In short, no, it doesn't remove data.
NordVPN is clear that you cannot scrub your past from the internet with a single click. The scanner does not act as an automated takedown service. Instead, it grades your overall exposure, guides you through manual steps to minimize your profile, and monitors whether your trail shrinks or grows over time.
Trimming those public scraps still matters. Fewer public records mean data brokers have less to trade, which cuts your risk of identity theft. It also stops automated scoring systems from misjudging your credit score based on scattered online footprints.
Because the tool focuses on guidance rather than automated removal, the legwork ultimately falls on you. You still need to manually shut down abandoned accounts, adjust privacy settings, and ask data brokers to delete your files. Think of the feature as an audit: it shows you where the leaks are, but you have to do the manual cleanup yourself.
The addition also highlights how standalone VPNs are shifting their priorities. Basic connection encryption is no longer enough to win over subscribers on its own. For existing NordVPN users, the Digital footprint checker adds a helpful diagnostic layer, provided you are willing to spend the time following through on its recommendations.

articles.title: Hyperspectral Imaging Lets Machines See Sick Plants First - EE Times
articles.text:
Twelve days after planting soybean seeds in a greenhouse at North Dakota State University, researchers could distinguish plants affected by sudden-death syndrome from healthy plants using hyperspectral imaging. To the human eye, the plants still looked alike.
For Xin “Rex” Sun, director of the Peltier Institute for Advancement in Agricultural Technology at North Dakota State University, the experiment illustrates the promise of detecting crop disease before visible symptoms appear. His team said it identified spectral differences several days to approximately a week before they became visible.
The research has not yet been validated under field conditions. But it points toward a potentially valuable agricultural tool: a sensor that could identify problems early enough for farmers to intervene before damage becomes widespread.
The obstacle is economics. Hyperspectral cameras can cost tens or hundreds of thousands of dollars, require specialized expertise, and generate enormous quantities of data. Few farmers can justify that investment without a clear financial return.
Sun believes the solution may be to use hyperspectral imaging to discover which wavelengths reveal a particular disease, then build cheaper cameras that capture only those wavelengths.
Finding the wavelengths that matter
Conventional cameras capture reflected light in three broad bands: red, green, and blue. Hyperspectral imaging divides light into many narrower wavelength bands, revealing changes in a plant’s physiological or chemical condition that may not yet affect its appearance.
Sun’s laboratory recently acquired a short-wave infrared (SWIR) camera covering approximately 1,000 to 2,500 nm, with more than 200 spectral bands. Such equipment is valuable for research because scientists do not necessarily know which wavelengths will reveal the differences they are looking for. A farmer diagnosing one particular disease may need only a fraction of that information.
“That’s the beauty of using hyperspectral imaging technology,” Sun said. “It’s all about selecting the bands.”
He described a hypothetical case in which researchers discover that two or three wavelengths reliably distinguish soybeans affected by sudden-death syndrome from healthy plants. A multispectral camera capturing those wavelengths could then replace the much more expensive research instrument.
Sun’s laboratory already works with multispectral cameras containing four to 10 bands. Such devices can cost hundreds or thousands of dollars rather than the six-figure prices associated with some research-grade hyperspectral systems.
Reducing the number of bands also reduces the computing burden. Extensive hyperspectral measurements can generate hundreds of gigabytes or more of data, requiring substantial processing resources.
“If we can find three or four bands out of the hyperspectral imaging, those small processors can process them,” Sun said. “Then it can be fast enough in the field to give you a good result.”
But identifying useful wavelengths is only part of the challenge. Sun cautioned that disease and other stresses can produce similar spectral changes, particularly before symptoms become visible. Changing sunlight, soil conditions, and other environmental factors also affect measurements.
His team has been collecting agricultural imagery under different conditions to develop models that work outside controlled experiments. It has not yet established a sufficiently validated set of wavelengths for field diagnosis of soybean sudden-death syndrome.
Making spectral cameras like semiconductor chips
At Belgian semiconductor research organization imec, researchers are developing technologies that could make application-specific spectral sensors commercially practical. Carolina Blanch, a senior researcher working on hyperspectral imaging applications, agreed that many applications do not require the full spectrum.
“We typically start with high-resolution spectral cameras that capture around 100 bands, then identify which ones are most relevant,” she said. “For most applications, 10 or fewer bands are sufficient.”
However, designing a different sensor for every crop disease is not necessarily economical. Blanch said imec also develops standardized sensors with nine, 16, or 25 spectral bands, potentially serving multiple applications and spreading manufacturing costs across larger markets.
Klaas Tack, technical lead of hyperspectral imaging at imec, explained how semiconductor manufacturing could reduce costs further.
Traditional hyperspectral cameras often rely on separate optical components to divide incoming light into different wavelengths. Imec instead integrates spectral filters directly with image detectors during semiconductor fabrication.
“We developed a process in our fab where we integrate the filters with the detector,” Tack said. “Because we’re doing this at wafer level, we’re manufacturing many detectors at the same time.”
The approach reduces components, size, weight, and alignment requirements. It also enables compact snapshot sensors that capture spatial and spectral information in a single exposure, avoiding some motion artifacts associated with scanning cameras. That matters when sensors operate on moving tractors or drones, or when wind moves leaves during image acquisition.
Manufacturing volume is the remaining economic hurdle. Semiconductor fabrication involves substantial upfront costs, but producing large numbers of sensors could reduce their unit price dramatically.
Tack points to imec spinoff Spectricity, which targets smartphone applications with low-cost snapshot multispectral sensors. Those devices are not designed for agricultural disease detection, but they illustrate the potential economics of high-volume production.
“When the volume is high enough, you can dramatically reduce the cost,” Tack said.
From research instrument to farm equipment
Not every agricultural application will benefit equally from cheaper, silicon-based sensors. Some diseases and stress can be detected using visible and near-infrared wavelengths. Others benefit from SWIR measurements, which can reveal additional information about plant chemistry and water-related stress.
SWIR detectors remain more expensive than conventional CMOS sensors, and Tack said integrating spectral filters with them is more complicated. Further manufacturing advances may be needed to achieve comparable cost reductions.
For Sun, another challenge is converting spectral measurements into reliable decisions. His team is developing a field-based platform that could carry sensors through crops, diagnose problems, and eventually support interventions. The goal is to replace expensive laboratory analysis with affordable sensing and processing on agricultural machinery.
Tack believes the underlying visible and near-infrared sensor technology is already available for application developers, although he cannot predict when agricultural products will reach widespread deployment. “I think today we can provide them with the technology that is required,” he said.
Sun said he expects significant progress over the next five or six years but emphasizes that field validation remains essential. “If you’re a farmer, you need to think twice,” he said of investing in an expensive hyperspectral system. “If I spend that much money, I want to know how soon I get my money back.”
The potential benefit is not simply higher yields. Earlier and more accurate information could help farmers target interventions, avoid unnecessary treatments, and maintain production at a lower cost.
Hyperspectral imaging has already demonstrated that it can reveal differences invisible to the human eye. Making that capability useful on farms may depend less on capturing hundreds of wavelengths than on identifying the few that matter—and manufacturing sensors that farmers can afford.

articles.title: Outlook, Hotmail, Live, MSN : des mails ont été bloqué pendant 4 jours, Microsoft annonce une mauvaise nouvelle
articles.text:
Autour du 5 novembre, les serveurs d’Outlook, Hotmail, Live et MSN ont commencé à renvoyer à leurs expéditeurs, particuliers comme entreprises, des e-mails qui n’avaient rien de suspect. Les messages refusés revenaient avec une erreur 550 5.7.1 et le code AS9031519, qui reprochent à tort un défaut d’authentification du courrier. Microsoft a rétabli le flux le 9 novembre à 12 h 02, heure de Paris.
Microsoft reconnaît une erreur dans ses propres filtres
Le diagnostic est tombé avec l’incident EX1545193 : une mise à jour des règles anti-spam maison a classé parmi les indésirables des domaines parfaitement en règle. Les expéditeurs concernés respectaient les trois standards d’authentification exigés, SPF, DKIM et DMARC, qui servent à vérifier qu’un e-mail provient bien du domaine qu’il annonce. Ils n’avaient donc rien à corriger de leur côté.
Lire aussi : Microsoft publie une mise à jour surprise pour Outlook classique
Microsoft durcit l’authentification depuis le 5 mai 2025 : les domaines qui expédient plus de 5 000 e-mails par jour vers ses messageries doivent présenter SPF, DKIM et DMARC. Le groupe revendique cette arme contre l’usurpation d’adresse et l’hameçonnage. La panne de novembre a frappé bien au-delà de ce périmètre. Des expéditeurs très en dessous du seuil ont vu leurs messages refusés, avec un code AS9031519 qui ne figure dans aucune documentation de l’éditeur.
L’éditeur ne s’est rendu compte de rien par lui-même. Ce sont les signalements des utilisateurs, multipliés sur les forums d’entraide, qui ont déclenché l’alerte, plusieurs jours après les premiers refus. Seule la déclinaison grand public d’Outlook semble touchée ; les comptes professionnels Microsoft 365 auraient été épargnés.
Les e-mails rejetés sont définitivement perdus
C’est la mauvaise nouvelle que Microsoft vient de confirmer : les messages refusés entre le 5 et le 9 novembre n’ont jamais atteint leur destinataire et ne peuvent pas être restaurés. Ils ne dorment pas dans le dossier des courriers indésirables, et aucune manipulation ne les fera réapparaître. Côté destinataire, le message n’a tout simplement jamais existé ; seul l’expéditeur a été prévenu du rejet, par un avis de non-remise. La seule issue consiste à renvoyer chaque message, un par un, et Microsoft précise que les expéditeurs n’ont aucun réglage à modifier avant de s’y mettre. Les rejets étaient d’ailleurs intermittents : en plein incident, un message refusé pouvait passer au second envoi, un quart d’heure plus tard.
Fin février, les serveurs de Microsoft avaient déjà rejeté des e-mails légitimes pendant une semaine entière. L’éditeur promet cette fois de revoir ses processus de mise à jour et ses procédures de test, pour qu’une règle défaillante ne soit plus déployée sans garde-fou.

articles.title: Ibiza tiene un problema para dar alojamiento a 30.000 trabajadores de temporada. Ahora tiene también un plan para solucionarlo
articles.text:
Ibiza no es la única región de España que lidia con la crisis de la vivienda, pero es cierto que allí tiene una dimensión especial: la isla tiene una considerable población flotante alimentada por el sector turístico, lo que hace que los alquileres vacacionales resulten más atractivos para los caseros y los precios se hayan disparado hasta alcanzar niveles prohibitivos, con municipios en los que el m2 se cotiza ya a más de 7.000 euros. Eso es un problema para los residentes, pero también para los trabajadores de temporada, muchos de ellos (ironía) dedicados al sector turístico.
Ahora en la isla está tomando forma un plan para atenderlos.
¿Qué ha pasado? Que Ibiza está buscando una solución para uno de sus grandes retos en materia habitacional: qué hacer con los miles de trabajadores que cada año llegan a la isla para cubrir empleos temporales, a menudo ligados a la hostelería y el sector turístico.
El Consell de Ibiza calcula que son alrededor de 30.000 personas, gente que habitualmente necesita buscar un techo para los meses de temporada alta y se encuentra, verano tras verano, con el mismo problema: un mercado residencial tensionado con precios intocables.
¿Tan grave es? Llega con echar un vistazo a Idealista para comprobarlo. Ahora mismo la opción de alquiler más barata es un piso de 55 m2 en un tercero sin ascensor que cuesta 840 euros al mes. Y ese, aclara el anuncio, es el precio de “temporada de invierno”, hasta finales de abril.
Ante semejante panorama hay trabajadores que optan por alojarse en caravanas, aunque esa tampoco es una solución ideal. Y no solo por la falta de espacio. En los últimos años algunos de esos trabajadores se han enfrentado a desalojos de asentamientos, en ocasiones justo antes de temporada alta.
Además, cada año llegan a Ibiza cerca de 30.000 trabajadores de temporada. Debemos dar respuesta a sus necesidades de alojamiento sin restar vivienda a los residentes ni aumentar todavía más la presión sobre el mercado residencial. https://t.co/mBMYL9w8uV
— Mariano Juan Colomar (@MJC_Ibz) September 29, 2026
¿Cuál es la solución? Hace unas semanas, durante una intervención en el Tourism Innovation Summit (TIS 2026), el vicepresidente primero del Consell Insular, Mariano Juan Colomar, deslizó una idea: reforzar las opciones de alojamiento temporal pensado específicamente para trabajadores de temporada.
La idea es muy sencilla: ofrecerles opciones residenciales adaptadas a sus necesidades, cerca de sus puestos de trabajo, y evitar de esa forma que su demanda tense todavía más el mercado.
“Se trata de diferenciar distintas necesidades. Los trabajadores de temporada necesitan un alojamiento digno durante unos meses, mientras que los residentes necesitan viviendas disponibles durante todo el año. La planificación territorial tiene que poder dar respuesta específica a cada una de estas realidades”, admitió el dirigente insular.
Pero… ¿Cómo hacerlo? Durante su discurso, Juan Colomar centró el foco en el Plan de Intervención en Ámbitos Turísticos (PIAT), un instrumento de planificación que, entre otros objetivos, busca mejorar la gestión turística.
El objetivo del Consell es tenerlo aprobado antes de que finalice esta legislatura y que, en la práctica, facilite la construcción de alojamiento para los trabajadores de temporada. La prensa balear habla de centrarse sobre todo en las zonas turísticas, cerca de los centros de trabajo, de tal modo que las plantillas temporales eviten viajes innecesarios.
La idea no es solo ofrecer una solución a los camareros, recepcionistas, cocineros, monitores… que ahora se encuentran sin opciones de alojamiento asequible. Al cubrir su demanda el Gobierno insular quiere destensar también el mercado. “Debemos dar respuesta a sus necesidades de alojamiento sin restar vivienda a los residentes ni aumentar todavía más la presión sobre el mercado residencial”, aboga Juan. De cara a las empresas, la idea es facilitar también la estabilidad de las plantillas y mejorar su capacidad para captar profesionales con los que cubrir sus vacantes.
¿Cómo serán esos alojamientos? Esa es una de las grandes preguntas. En marzo La Voz de Ibiza se hacía eco de una propuesta de la patronal de la pequeña y mediana empresa de Ibiza (Pimeef): apostar por módulos prefabricados que podrían instalarse de forma temporal en terrenos de los propios empresarios.
“Son soluciones que ya existen y actividades que ya se hacen en otros sitios en el extranjero”, recordaba su presidente, Alfonso Rojo. En el pasado Pimeef reclamó también zonas reguladas de caravanas precisamente para acoger a los trabajadores temporales.
Durante su intervención en el TIS 2026, Juan no entró en detalles sobre cómo y dónde podría crearse alojamiento para esos 30.000 empleados temporales, pero elDiario ha avanzado algunas ideas clave de la propuesta. Para empezar, otorga un papel fundamental al sector privado, del que deberá partir la iniciativa. Según el medio, de hecho, el proyecto se desarrollará en terrenos y con financiación privados.
¿Sabemos algo más? Sí. Que los ayuntamientos también jugarán un papel importante. El PIAT facilitará la oferta de alojamiento, “permitiendo el uso residencial”, pero su campo de actuación está limitado. “El plan no se mete en la tipología constructiva”, aclaran desde el Consell insular a elDiario. Dicho de otro modo, el tipo de alojamiento por el que se opte en cada caso dependerá en gran medida de lo que contemplen las ordenanzas locales de cada municipio.
“El ejemplo más claro que se nos ponía es ese hotel que a su alrededor tiene una amplia disponibilidad de espacio, en el que no se puede construir, donde se podrían habilitar ese tipo de residencias”, explica Rojo antes de recordar que “con la normativa actual no se permite, pero se puede modificar al ser medidas excepcionales”.
En general, en la clase empresarial pitiusa hay dudas sobre el alcance real que podría tener el plan, si servirá para atender a 30.000 personas o la disponibilidad de terrenos. La propuesta también genera recelo entre los sindicatos, sobre todo en función del tipo de construcción que se elija o la situación en la que deje al empleado frente a la empresa.
¿Por qué es importante? Por lo que se juega Ibiza. Lo explicaba claramente hace unos meses Vicent Marí, presidente del Consell, en una entrevista con La Voz de Ibiza: “No pensemos solo en el sector turístico en sí, alojamiento y restauración. Pensemos en distribución, servicios, agricultura, construcción. Hay toda una serie de servicios que vienen a ser prestados por gente de la península y luego se vuelven. Pero necesitan un espacio donde residir”.
De ahí que el Gobierno insular defienda crear equipamiento específico, con residencias o incluso modelos co-living. “En vez de ser viviendas individuales, pueden ser espacios con zonas comunes, como una especie de vivienda compartida”.

articles.title: AI agent tooling provider LangChain secures $300M investment - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
AI agent tooling provider LangChain secures $300M investment
LangChain Inc., a startup with a set of popular open-source tools for building artificial intelligence agents, has raised $300 million in funding.
The Wall Street Journal reported today that Alphabet Inc.’s CapitalG fund led the round. It was joined by IVP, Sapphire Ventures, GIC and DFJ Growth. LangChain is now worth $3 billion.
San Francisco-based LangChain is best known for the eponymous open-source framework it released in 2022. The software reduces the amount of work involved in building AI agents. LangChain makes it relatively simple to connect an AI agent to a large language model, integrate it with tools and add a system prompt. The framework also enables developers to customize details such as the format of prompt responses.
LangChain’s second open-source tool, LangGraph, is designed for situations where a task is too complicated to be automated by a single agent. LangGraph can link together multiple LangChain-powered agents into a single automation workflow. It can also add in other elements such as a mechanism that requires humans to approve sensitive actions.
The third component of LangChain’s open-source portfolio is Deep Agents. It extends LangChain and LangGraph with features that make it easier for agents to perform complex work. There’s a virtual file system in which agents can keep data, a work planning tool and a subagent generation feature.
LangChain generates revenue with a suite of paid products called LangSmith. Developers can use it to not only build agents but also to maintain them once they’re in production.
An AI agent usually goes through multiple iterations before it’s released to users. LangSmith enables software teams to save those iterations in a centralized repository. If an update introduces a bug into an agent’s code base, developers can use LangSmith to quickly restore an earlier, bug-free version. Furthermore, they can compare the output quality of different agent versions to identify the one that should be deployed to production.
LangSmith also includes a set of observability features. It generates traces, logs that describe every single step of the workflow through an agent processed a prompt. LangSmith analyzes those traces to find technical issues. From there, it prioritizes them based on their severity and generates code fixes.
After its previous funding round last year, LangChain disclosed that its open-source tools were being downloaded about 90 million times per month. Its LangSmith suite, in turn, is used by Autodesk Inc., Cisco Systems Inc. and a long list of other tech firms.
LangChain reportedly plans to nearly double its headcount to 850 employees by the end of 2027. The company will hire infrastructure experts, AI engineers, salespeople and marketers.

articles.title: Phishing, cloud, IA : les cybercriminels multiplient les offensives en Europe
articles.text:
Dans son dernier rapport sur les cybermenaces européennes, Proofpoint alerte sur une forte hausse du phishing et des attaques de plus en plus ciblées. Les comptes cloud et les infrastructures d'intelligence artificielle sont particulièrement concernés.
Le phishing se porte très bien en Europe, et les cybercriminels semblent avoir trouvé de quoi prolonger leurs activités dans le cloud et les infrastructures d’intelligence artificielle. Dans son dernier rapport sur les cybermenaces européennes, Proofpoint fait état d’une multiplication par 4,5 des détections de phishing en un an, contre 1,5 à l’échelle mondiale. Derrière cette flambée, les chercheurs décrivent des attaques de plus en plus ciblées, exploitant aussi bien les (mauvaises) habitudes des internautes que les nouveaux usages numériques des entreprises.
Protégez votre entreprise gratuitement pendant 30 jours
Découvrez Bitdefender Ultimate Small Business Security et protégez votre activité contre les cybermenaces. Aucune coordonnée bancaire requise.
Le phishing explose, les attaques se diversifient
Et le moins que l’on puisse dire, c’est que les leurres font mouche, puisque Proofpoint comptabilise 8,3 clics pour 100 messages malveillants distribués en Europe, contre 2 en moyenne dans le monde. Les escrocs misent notamment sur la confiance que leurs victimes accordent aux services dont ils usurpent l'identité. En septembre dernier, une campagne se faisant passer pour l'Assurance maladie française redirigeait ainsi les internautes vers une copie du portail Ameli, dont le faux formulaire de connexion était précédé de plusieurs étapes de vérification, parmi lesquelles un CAPTCHA. L'opération reposait sur des centaines de domaines malveillants et un kit de phishing jusqu'alors inconnu des chercheurs.
Sans grande surprise, les comptes professionnels sont également dans le viseur, d’autant que leur compromission peut ouvrir l’accès aux messageries et aux services cloud des entreprises. Pour parvenir à leurs fins, les cybercriminels misent aussi bien sur le vol d’identifiants que sur le détournement de sessions déjà authentifiées, afin d’exploiter les droits accordés aux utilisateurs. Un ciblage qui s’avère payant, puisque Proofpoint a constaté des effets chez 64 % des organisations européennes visées par ces attaques dites de précision, contre 33 % pour celles confrontées à des attaques par force brute, fondées sur la multiplication des tentatives de connexion.
Les entreprises accordent également des droits d’accès à leurs applications et agents d’intelligence artificielle, qu’elles autorisent à consulter des documents, interroger des services internes ou automatiser des tâches. Les cybercriminels s’intéressent donc aussi aux permissions de ces outils, qu’ils cherchent à détourner, ainsi qu’aux logiciels nécessaires à leur fonctionnement. D'une période de 90 jours à la suivante, la proportion de capteurs européens ayant détecté des attaques contre ces infrastructures a été multipliée par 4,6.
Des comptes aux applications d'IA, comment limiter les risques ?
Un message qui vous presse de vérifier vos informations personnelles, de régulariser un paiement ou de communiquer un code de connexion doit immédiatement éveiller vos soupçons, même s'il reprend à la perfection l'identité d'un service connu. Pour vérifier une demande, ouvrez directement le site officiel ou l'application du service concerné, sans suivre le lien reçu. Privilégiez aussi les passkeys lorsqu'elles sont proposées : liées au domaine du service légitime, elles ne peuvent pas être utilisées pour vous authentifier sur une copie frauduleuse.
Dans les entreprises, l'authentification multifacteur résistante au phishing permet de réduire les risques de vol de comptes, mais attention aux sessions déjà ouvertes. Un pirate qui récupère un cookie de session peut parfois accéder à un service sans avoir à saisir de mot de passe ni de code de vérification. Si vous soupçonnez une compromission, changer le mot de passe ne suffit donc pas toujours. Il faut également fermer les sessions actives et révoquer les jetons d'accès concernés pour couper les connexions frauduleuses.
Enfin, avant de connecter un assistant IA à votre messagerie ou à vos documents professionnels, prenez le temps de vérifier les autorisations qu'il réclame. Un outil chargé de résumer quelques fichiers n'a pas nécessairement besoin d'accéder à l'ensemble de votre espace de stockage. Les entreprises doivent aussi contrôler les permissions accordées via OAuth, supprimer les accès devenus inutiles et tenir leurs infrastructures d'IA à jour. Car une application abandonnée depuis des mois peut encore disposer des droits nécessaires pour consulter des données sensibles.

articles.title: Pendant le Black Friday 2026, ce casque Sony noté 5/5 chute à 329,99 €
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 – Le casque Bluetooth Sony WH-1000XM6 "5 étoiles" à 329,99 €
Le casque Bluetooth Sony WH-1000XM6 passe sous les 350 € chez Boulanger.com. C'est actuellement le meilleur produit de notre comparatif.
Les points essentiels pour améliorer la formule du casque audio WH-1000XM5 paraissaient évidents. Pourtant, Sony a choisi d'aller au-delà de ces attentes, visant à propulser le WH-1000XM6 au sommet de la chaîne.

Points forts
- Restitution précise des médiums.
- Aigus naturels, superbe dynamique.
- Réduction du bruit la plus polyvalente du marché.
- Parfait compromis entre confort et maintien.
- Conception pliable.
- Utilisation intuitive et fonctionnalités nombreuses.
Points faibles
- Basses un peu trop généreuses.
- Finition légère pour du haut de gamme.
- Absence d'audio via USB-C.
- Microphones perfectibles.
Il aura donc fallu attendre le WH-1000XM6 pour que Sony affine véritablement la formule éprouvée du casque audio WH-1000XM4, la cinquième mouture ayant servi de laboratoire pour des expériences en design et sonorité, avec des résultats parfois mitigés. Malgré une finition un peu légère pour un casque premium, une autonomie dans la moyenne et des micros encore perfectibles, le WH-1000XM6 frôle la perfection sur deux points essentiels. Il peut se targuer de proposer la réduction du bruit la plus polyvalente du marché et une précision sonore rarement rencontrée sur le marché des casques Bluetooth. Une montée en gamme qui justifie pleinement l’écart de prix avec son prédécesseur.

Le Sony WH-1000XM4C est quasiment le même casque qu’en 2020. Si le XM4C laisse derrière lui le NFC et quelques heures d’écoute, ces régressions sont largement excusées par son réglage sonore encore mieux maîtrisé qu’auparavant, qui gagne en naturel dans le médium et l’aigu.

En somme, malgré son approche old school, le XM4C est un casque diablement efficace, qui a encore toute sa place sur le marché.

articles.title: Carro voador chinês deve entrar em operação nos próximos meses • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Carro voador chinês deve entrar em operação nos próximos meses
Montadora XPeng já fez demonstrações com protótipo e promete disponibilizar veículo em 2027.
A XPeng já tem uma previsão de quando seu “carro voador” chegará ao mercado. Com aprovação da aviação civil chinesa, o modelo poderá realizar voos recreativos em áreas rurais e voos de emergência já no verão de 2027 – nosso inverno aqui no Brasil, entre junho e agosto.
O veículo ainda não tem nome, mas seu protótipo já vem sendo demonstrado pelos últimos anos. Trata-se de um conjunto com duas partes: uma espécie de SUV que funciona como base e o próprio módulo de voo, que sai de dentro do carro principal e se “transforma” para levantar voo.
Segundo o The Guardian, o modelo custará US$ 300 mil, aproximadamente R$ 1,67 mi na cotação atual. No cockpit de voo, há espaço para duas pessoas, e o veículo funciona de forma autônoma. Também é possível pilotar o módulo de maneira simples.
O produto da XPeng é divido em um carro padrão, uma van de seis rodas, e um módulo de voo em si, menor e que “abre” as hélices para tomar sua forma definitiva. Segundo o CEO Deli Zhao, o modelo sai da SUV “exatamente como um Transformer”.
Em termos de design, o veículo não é muito diferente de outros carros voadores (ou eVTOLs, sigla em inglês para aeronaves elétricas de decolagem e pouso vertical, em inglês). A Embraer tem um protótipo com essa proposta, da mesma forma que a Uber divulgou seus primeiros conceitos de eVTOL quando ainda planejava lançar seu UberAir.
A diferença aqui fica por conta da SUV que “guarda” o módulo, permitindo aos usuários viajarem tanto por terra quanto em voo. Vale reforçar que o veículo tem permissão para altitudes baixas, além de operação limitada a áreas rurais em um primeiro momento.
Em uma conferência em Lisboa, Portugal, a XPeng demonstrou o veículo para o público. Segundo Zhao, as viagens correram bem, e “ninguém se machucou”. O modelo consegue voar por distâncias de até 30 quilômetros, o que deve aumentar com a evolução da bateria utilizada, prevista para chegar a 400 kW por quilo.
A aprovação dos voos passa pela chamada “economia de altitude baixa”, projeto econômico desenvolvido em Pequim para movimentar os céus da cidade com o transporte de cargas e pessoas. Zhao afirma que existem outros acordos encaminhados para levar a tecnologia para mais países asiáticos.
Ele foi questionado ainda sobre outra demonstração de “carro voador”: o da Tesla. Na ocasião, a empresa de Elon Musk exibiu um automóvel padrão com jatos de água que podem sustentar quedas e até virar o veículo no ar. De acordo com o executivo chinês, o protótipo da Tesla estava, na verdade, “pulando, e não voando”.

articles.title: Microsoft confirma caída de su correo electrónico Outlook que afecta a millones de usuarios en todo el mundo
articles.text:
Microsoft Outlook registra una caída que impide a usuarios acceder a sus bandejas de entrada. La empresa informó que el incidente afecta la conectividad de Exchange Online y puede extenderse a usuarios de Microsoft 365 en distintas regiones.
La compañía indicó que investiga reportes de problemas para acceder a los buzones de Exchange Online mediante varios métodos de conexión en América. Más tarde, confirmó que la falla podría afectar la conectividad de los servicios de Microsoft 365 para usuarios de cualquier región.
El sitio de monitoreo Downdetector registró un aumento abrupto de los reportes de fallas de Microsoft Outlook en Estados Unidos. Según los reportes de usuarios, el 36% de los inconvenientes está vinculado con la aplicación, el 24% con el sitio web y el 23% con la recepción de mensajes.
Qué ha dicho Microsoft sobre la caída de Outlook
Microsoft atribuyó los errores de conectividad a una carga elevada en parte de su infraestructura, presente en múltiples regiones. La empresa señaló que ese problema probablemente contribuye a las dificultades de acceso.
La compañía comenzó a redistribuir el tráfico de conexiones dentro de su infraestructura mundial para equilibrar la carga. También remitió a los incidentes EX1550543 y MO1550821 en el centro de administración de Microsoft 365.
En su actualización más reciente, Microsoft aseguró que trabaja para reducir el impacto: pausó todos los despliegues, trasladó tráfico adicional fuera de la infraestructura afectada y reinició los servidores comprometidos para devolverlos al servicio.
“Hemos determinado que la carga elevada no se debe a un aumento del tráfico, sino a que varios servidores no están disponibles de forma inesperada, lo que sobrecarga la infraestructura restante. Estamos trabajando para que vuelvan a estar operativos de forma segura”, compartió la empresa en X a través de la cuenta MSFT365Status.
Qué está fallando en Outlook
La caída afecta el acceso a los buzones de correo de Exchange Online, el servicio empresarial de correo electrónico de Microsoft. TechCrunch indicó que algunos usuarios no pueden ingresar a sus bandejas de entrada.
Downdetector refleja problemas tanto en la aplicación como en la versión web de Outlook. Los reportes también incluyen dificultades para recibir mensajes.
Microsoft a empresa indicó que continuará publicando información en el centro de administración de Microsoft 365 y en su página de estado para quienes no puedan acceder a esa plataforma.
Qué dicen los usuarios sobre la caída de Outlook
Los usuarios de Microsoft Outlook reaccionaron con humor y frustración a la caída del servicio, que les impidió acceder al correo electrónico laboral y alteró sus actividades durante la jornada.
En X, varios usuarios señalaron que no podían ingresar a sus cuentas de trabajo y aprovecharon la interrupción para compartir memes.
The Dude escribió: “Microsoft Outlook está caído en todo el país y no puedo acceder a mi correo electrónico laboral. Será mejor que haga otros planes para mi día”.
Otros mensajes convirtieron la falla en una excusa para una pausa inesperada. Chubby comentó que no era la única persona con inconvenientes y propuso adelantar el descanso para almorzar. Por su parte, Vult se despidió del servicio con una referencia a Valhalla: “Descansa, hermano, tenemos la guardia. Te veré en Valhalla”.
Las publicaciones también reflejaron la incertidumbre de quienes dependen de Outlook para trabajar. Una usuaria en portugués afirmó que la caída de Outlook y Microsoft hacía que “el mundo” se viniera abajo y compartió una imagen con la frase “¡Por mí!”.
Los memes se multiplicaron con imágenes de personas descansando o reaccionando con sorpresa ante la interrupción.
Entre ellas, Bruccehurlz publicó una animación de una actriz bebiendo un cóctel junto al mensaje: “Los usuarios de Outlook durante la caída de Microsoft”.

articles.title: Noctua Introduces NT-CP1 Carbice Carbon Nanotube Thermal Pad for AM5
articles.text:
Thursday, November 12th 2026
Noctua Introduces NT-CP1 Carbice Carbon Nanotube Thermal Pad for AM5
Noctua today introduced the new NT-CP1 AM5/4 carbon nanotube thermal pad for AMD AM5 and AM4 processors. Leveraging Carbice's novel, space-grade carbon nanotube technology, the NT-CP1 is a premium-quality, easy-to-apply thermal pad that offers superior long-term stability for peace of mind. While thermal pastes and most other thermal pads gradually lose performance over time due to pump-out, delamination, cracking and other degradation effects, Carbice pads keep improving their performance over the first few hundred to a few thousand thermal cycles. This is possible thanks to the pad's robust mechanics, phase-change polymer coating and carbon nanotubes that incrementally conform to surface microstructures, enhancing the heat transfer rate with time and thermal cycling. Once this initial activation phase is completed, the NT-CP1 maintains stable, maintenance-free performance for years and years. As such, it is ideal for everyone who seeks to rule out thermal issues due to degradation and never wants to bother with reapply paste again.
Unlike other carbon or graphite-based thermal pads that can be brittle, slippery and highly electrically conductive, Carbice pads are sturdy, safe and easy to install using a straightforward "peel, press, peel" process. The NT-CP1's aluminium backbone makes it surprisingly robust and easy to remove. The slightly tacky polymer coating helps to keep the pad in place once pressed onto the CPU and ensures that the contact surfaces are electrically non-conductive before usage unless the polymer layer is penetrated.Whereas graphite and graphene-based pads tend to have a high carbon footprint due to energy-intensive mining or high-temperature growth processing, the NT-CP1 is manufactured by Carbice Corporation in the United States out of recycled aluminium and waste carbon gas that's used to grow carbon nanotube forests in an energy-efficient, low-temperature process. The NT-CP1 pad can be recycled through standard aluminium recycling and offers a complete path to waste circularity.
"Carbice pads offer a unique combination of ultimate performance stability and convenient installation. This makes the NT-CP1 the perfect choice for everyone who's looking for a thermal pad that's super easy to apply and never needs to be replaced," said Roland Mossig, CEO of Noctua. "Carbice's carbon nanotube thermal pads were first built for spacecraft. Now, with Noctua, every PC builder can put that same technology in their system. Noctua has spent two decades earning the trust of builders who care about every detail, and they share our belief that great engineering should last. The NT-CP1 is better for your hardware and better for people and our planet, and we couldn't ask for a better partner to deliver it," said Baratunde Cola, CEO and founder of Carbice.
The AM5/4 version has been carefully fine-tuned and validated for optimal performance on AMD Ryzen CPUs and APUs. With its ultra-thin 90µm profile and precut 33x33mm size, it fits both AM5 and AM4 socket processors.
Overall, the NT-CP1 Carbice pad is an innovative premium choice for users looking for a clean, convenient and environmentally friendly thermal interface material solution with reliable long-term performance, space-grade dependability and zero maintenance.
Suggested retail price
The manufacturer's suggested retail price is EUR 24.95 / USD 24.95.

My pick of the best wired buds, cheap over-ears, players, speakers and more
Looking for a touch of inspiration ahead of this gift-giving season — specifically for the music-lover in your life? I love that. I want to help you find them a gift they'll love, whether they're embracing the retro wired trend, vinyl/CD/cassette collecting or streaming to a wireless hi-fi setup.

articles.title: Russia’s Google says nearly 3% of its data was lost after crippling Ukraine drone strikes, opens secret availability zones — Yandex Cloud blames lack of user backups for lost data, now forcibly applies backup rules by default
articles.text:
Russia’s Google says nearly 3% of its data was lost after crippling Ukraine drone strikes, opens secret availability zones — Yandex Cloud blames lack of user backups for lost data, now forcibly applies backup rules by default
Those who had made use of the Yandex Cloud backup tools ‘did not lose any data,’ it says.
Yandex, sometimes called Russia’s Google, has updated its customers in the wake of extensive damage to its data centers in drone strikes. In a blog post this week, the firm’s cloud business boasted that it had “restored access to more than 97% of customer data” [machine translation]. That might sound like a great success, but in the small print, as highlighted by The Register, there’s the admission “the remaining 2.84% cannot be restored due to critical damage to equipment.”
Data centers operated by Yandex have been under attack from Ukrainian drones for several weeks now. We covered reports about withering online troll activity and online payment system disruption last month. We know of at least three Yandex locations that have been damaged by Ukrainian drone assaults to date.
The recent Yandex blog post also appears to blame the small proportion of users who suffered unrecoverable data loss for not making backups. When talking about the 2.84% of data that cannot be restored, it says that was partly due to “the lack of customer backups on the platform.” In contrast, those who made use of the Yandex Cloud backup tools “did not lose any data,” says the firm.
Yandex has now changed the backup policy, so that “currently, all virtual machines created in Yandex Cloud work with the backup function enabled by default.” Even if Putin decides to end his war on Ukraine, it might be beneficial to stick with a backup-by-default policy. Users are advised to have their own data backup systems in addition to the cloud. Following the 3-2-1 backup strategy, for example.
Yandex is also opening a new ru-central1-f availability zone at a new location. This is designed to improve the cloud’s fault tolerance and disaster resilience. Servers at ru-central1-f will be more limited in the range of services they can offer, for now. Yandex didn’t share any geographic details of the newly opened datacenter site.
