articles.title: Amazon highlights EGP 29 billion GDP contribution as it expands Egyptian operations
articles.text:
Amazon highlights EGP 29 billion GDP contribution as it expands Egyptian operations
- US e-commerce and technology company Amazon announced that its investments contributed more than EGP 29 billion to Egypt's GDP over the past decade, according to an economic impact assessment conducted by consultancy Keystone Strategy.
- The company said its investments supported more than 60,000 direct, indirect, induced and seasonal jobs across Egypt during the period, spanning logistics, technology, operations and professional services.
- According to Keystone Strategy, the estimated GDP contribution reflects Amazon's cumulative investments in infrastructure, technology, logistics and employee compensation. Amazon expanded its presence in Egypt following its acquisition of Souq.com in 2017 and the launch of Amazon.eg in 2021.
- The findings were announced at the Global Entrepreneurship Festival in Cairo. Amazon said it would continue investing in local infrastructure, technology and small businesses.
Press release:
Amazon today announced that its investments have contributed more than EGP 29 billion to Egypt’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) over the past decade and supported more than 60,000 direct, indirect, induced and seasonal jobs across the country. According to analysis by the economic consultancy Keystone Strategy, the GDP contribution reflects Amazon’s cumulative investment in infrastructure, technology, logistics and employee compensation. The findings were unveiled at the Global Entrepreneurship Festival, the largest entrepreneurship event in Africa, held in Cairo under the auspices of the Prime Minister of Egypt, H.E. Dr. Mostafa Madbouly.
“Amazon’s presence in Egypt reflects our long-term confidence in this country and its people. Over the past decade, we have invested consistently in infrastructure, in technology, in logistics and in the tens of thousands of Egyptian businesses that grow and create jobs through Amazon. We have done so through periods of economic uncertainty because we believe in what Egypt can achieve. The figures we are sharing today are not just a measure of our investment. They reflect the ambition of Egyptian entrepreneurs, the resilience of local businesses and the talent of a workforce that continues to deliver. We are proud of what we have built here, and we intend to keep building,” said Omar Elsahy, General Manager, Amazon Egypt.
A decade of investment: Building a lasting economic footprint in Egypt
Since acquiring Souq.com in 2017 and launching Amazon.eg in 2021, Amazon has steadily deepened its presence in Egypt. According to estimates by Keystone Strategy, Amazon’s cumulative investment over the past decade has contributed more than EGP 29 billion to Egypt’s GDP spanning infrastructure, technology, logistics, and employee compensation.
Amazon’s presence has built a foundation of economic activity that reaches well beyond the company’s own operations. Investment at this level, maintained year after year, including through currency volatility and wider regional uncertainty, supports local supply chains, stimulates demand and creates the conditions for growth and employment across sectors such as logistics, technology and professional services.
More than 60,000 jobs supported across Egypt
Amazon’s impact extends well beyond its direct workforce. The more than 60,000 jobs supported over the past decade span direct, indirect, induced and seasonal roles across sectors including logistics, operations, technology and professional services from the teams in Amazon's fulfillment and logistics operations and its regional customer service center, to the suppliers, delivery partners and service providers that its presence sustains.
Beyond Amazon’s own operations, thousands of small and medium-sized Egyptian businesses sell and grow through Amazon, creating their own jobs, hiring their own teams and building livelihoods in communities across the country. Today, tens of thousands of Egyptian selling partners reach customers nationwide and around the world, and the jobs and economic activity they generate are a critical part of Amazon’s wider impact on the Egyptian economy.
Expanding services, deepening local investment
The company has also continued to expand its services for customers, including Amazon Now, which delivers groceries, fresh produce sourced from local farmers and everyday household essentials within minutes through micro-fulfillment centers across the country. This sustained investment in infrastructure, technology and local businesses reinforces Amazon’s role as a long-term partner in Egypt’s growth and job-creation agenda.
What is next for Amazon in Egypt
Amazon remains committed to empowering entrepreneurs, supporting small and medium-sized businesses, and investing in the people, technology and infrastructure that help the Egyptian economy grow. As Egypt continues to prioritize private-sector investment, entrepreneurship and job creation, Amazon will keep building for the long term.

articles.title: Cloud-native developers top 21 million and lead in AI adoption - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
CNCF data shows cloud native is the on-ramp to AI, and maintainers are paying the price
The global population of cloud-native developers has topped 21 million, but the headcount tells only part of the story. Artificial intelligence is changing what those developers build and how open-source projects absorb their work.
Fresh research is putting numbers on that shift. The latest State of Cloud Native Development report from the Cloud Native Computing Foundation and SlashData Ltd. counts more than 21 million practitioners, or 41% of developers worldwide. Yet that figure likely misses many people who rely on cloud-native infrastructure without knowing it, according to Bob Killen (pictured, right), director of technical program management at CNCF.
“The big thing is it actually might be undercounting a significant amount of them,” Killen said. “Because there’s a very large amount of people that are essentially consuming cloud-native applications without even realizing it.”
Killen and Liam Bollmann-Dodd (left), principal market research consultant at SlashData, spoke with theCUBE’s Rebecca Knight at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed the latest State of Cloud Native Development findings, AI adoption, the strain on open-source maintainers and the shift toward cost discipline. (* Disclosure below.)
AI adoption separates cloud-native developers from the pack
The report’s most striking finding concerns AI. About 75% of cloud-native developers use AI in some form, compared with only about 55% of other developers, Bollmann-Dodd noted. The gap mirrors a broader trend of agentic AI pushing Kubernetes into a second act.
“It’s a massive difference,” Bollmann-Dodd said. “So somehow being cloud native enables you and your organization and your personal stack to do AI in all its forms.”
Maintainers face a flood of AI-made code
The same AI wave is straining the people who keep the ecosystem running. Sustainability dominated the Maintainer Summit ahead of KubeCon, as maintainers face a flood of pull requests frequently generated by agents, Killen explained.
“How do we as maintainers keep up with the flooding of PRs and issues and things like that?” Killen said. “Especially when many of them are frankly just slop. And the real frustrating part is they’ll be just good enough.”
Cost discipline is the next shift. Just as financial operations practices followed rising cloud bills, cloud-native developers will soon manage model and token spending closely, according to Bollmann-Dodd.
“I think token maxing is dead and it’s going to stay dead forever,” Bollmann-Dodd said. “And I think it’s going to become much more focused on how you spend your money and how you spend your tokens.”

articles.title: 100 000 billets de train vendus en 30 minutes, la SNCF crie au record pour son ouverture des ventes
articles.text:
La SNCF a ouvert ce jeudi la vente des billets de train TGV INOUI pour des trajets jusqu’au 2 juillet 2027. Sur SNCF Connect, plus de 100 000 billets sont partis en 30 minutes, un record selon la plateforme.
L'ouverture des ventes des billets de train SNCF, très attendue par les voyageurs, a eu lieu ce jeudi 12 novembre, avec un calendrier élargi jusqu'au 2 juillet 2027 pour les TGV INOUI. SNCF Connect fait état auprès de Clubic d'une affluence record dès les premières heures, et attendait à midi l'équivalent de deux journées de ventes habituelles. Ces chiffres, qui portent sur la seule plateforme, méritent toutefois d'être replacés dans leur contexte.
Record historique de ventes de billets TGV sur SNCF Connect
En temps normal, un billet SNCF s'achète au plus tôt quatre mois avant le départ. Cette fois, les trajets directs en TGV INOUI sont réservables du 7 janvier au 2 juillet 2027, en France comme vers Bruxelles, Luxembourg et Fribourg-en-Brisgau, selon les jours et les trains. Les Intercités s'arrêtent au 31 mars. L'Italie et l'Espagne, ainsi que la Suisse avec TGV Lyria, prennent le train en marche le 1er avril. L'Allemagne garde son propre rythme, puisque les billets ouvrent progressivement, six mois avant le départ.
Il faut rappeler que l'an dernier, et historiquement d'ailleurs, l'ouverture du 12 novembre s'arrêtait pour l'essentiel fin mars. Seuls l'axe Sud-Est, à titre de test, et quelques lignes internationales allaient jusqu'en juillet. Les autres voyageurs devaient remettre le réveil le 28 janvier pour réserver leur printemps. Les habitués des trains OUIGO ont déjà pris de l'avance, puisque leurs trains jusqu'au 2 juillet sont en vente depuis le 30 septembre.
On peut dire que la matinée du 12 novembre a été mouvementée. On apprend ainsi que plus de 100 000 billets se sont envolés sur SNCF Connect en à peine une demi-heure, un « record historique » selon la plateforme. Elle tablait sur près d'un million de ventes à midi, l'équivalent de presque deux journées ordinaires. L'entreprise n'en démord pas, et affirme que réserver trois à quatre mois avant le départ, plutôt que dans les sept derniers jours, ferait économiser jusqu'à 45 % en moyenne, tous transporteurs confondus.
Un record SNCF Connect à lire entre les lignes
Ce record mérite son astérisque. Avec près de six mois de trajets mis en vente d'un coup, il y a mécaniquement plus de dates, donc plus de billets, à vendre. Il faut savoir que lors de l'ouverture des ventes de Noël 2025, SNCF Connect annonçait déjà plus de 900 000 billets écoulés à la mi-journée. Et ces chiffres ne portent que sur la plateforme, sans les guichets par exemple.
Le cap du million à midi, lui, était annoncé au conditionnel dans le point d'étape envoyé à la presse. Il faudra attendre le bilan définitif pour le confirmer. Quant à la promesse d'économies, elle se lit avec prudence. « Jusqu'à 45 % en moyenne » mélange un plafond, le meilleur cas possible, et une moyenne, le cas typique : difficile de savoir ce que le voyageur peut vraiment espérer. Surtout, la SNCF compare des billets pris trois à quatre mois avant le départ avec ceux achetés dans les sept derniers jours, quand les prix sont au plus haut.
Ceux qui ont déjà réservé gardent une marge de manœuvre. Les billets TGV INOUI et Intercités s'échangent et se remboursent sans frais jusqu'à sept jours avant le départ. Ensuite, il faut compter 19 euros en TGV INOUI, et 40 % du prix, dans la limite de 15 euros, sur les Intercités à réservation obligatoire. Les retardataires peuvent s'appuyer sur les alertes « petits prix » et « train complet » de SNCF Connect. La seconde, valable sur un trajet simple, seul ou jusqu'à neuf voyageurs, aurait prévenu un client sur deux d'une place libérée… en 2024.

articles.title: Ohne Airpods: Wie es ist, nach Jahren wieder kabelgebundene Kopfhörer zu tragen
articles.text:
Ohne Airpods: Wie es ist, nach Jahren wieder kabelgebundene Kopfhörer zu tragen
Meine Airpods gehören zu meinen liebsten Gadgets. Das kompakte Case ist immer in der Hosentasche dabei, sie koppeln sich schnell und einfach mit iPhone, iPad oder Mac, bieten für unterwegs eine gute Geräuschunterdrückung – und verheddern kann sich auch nichts. Und doch werden sie unweigerlich kaputtgehen. Irgendwann macht selbst der beste Akku nicht mehr mit. Austauschen lässt sich die Batterie dann nicht. Es ist das größte Problem bei den allermeisten kabellosen Buds.
Nicht nur deswegen sah man in den vergangenen Monaten immer Promis und Nutzer:innen mit kabelgebundenen Kopfhörern. Wie der iPod scheinen sie aktuell ein Comeback zu feiern – und zwar auch als modisches Accessoire. Lässig baumeln sie aus den Jacken, als hätte es nie kabellose In-Ears gegeben. Außerdem ist die Bedienung einfach. Kabel rein, los hören. Kein aufladen, kein koppeln. Doch ein wichtiges Feature oft: die Geräuschunterdrückung. Selbst bei günstigen Buds ist sie mittlerweile standardmäßig an Bord. Bose löst das Problem nun mit den „Kabelgebundenen Noise-Cancelling-Earbuds“, wie das Modell etwas sperrig heißt.
Kabel-In-Ears mit USB-C und ANC
Im Karton findet ihr das, was draufsteht. Die In-Ears, Gummistöpsel in drei und Stabilitätsaufsätze in zwei Größen und ein Transportetui. Nach dem Auspacken seid ihr direkt bereit zum Loshören – zumindest am Smartphone. Schon 2016 marschierte Apple bei der Vorstellung des iPhone 7 schließlich voran und strich die Kopfhörerbuchse am iPhone 7. Den Schritt bezeichnete der damalige Marketing-Chef Phil Schiller noch mit Mut. Längst sind aber so gut wie alle Hersteller nachgeschoben. Damit ihr keinen Adapter braucht, kommen die Bose-Buds mit USB-C-Stecker. Der passt allerdings nicht in ältere iPhones oder gar in iPods.
Die Bedienung ist leicht erklärt: Am Kabel drei Tasten. Zwei regeln die Lautstärke. Der dritte funktioniert universal als Start- und Stop-Taste. Haltet ihr den Knopf gedrückt, switcht ihr zudem durch die integrierten Modi: Neben Noise-Cancelling gibt es einen Aware-Modus, der die Mikrofone quasi auf Durchzug schaltet, damit man mehr von der Umgebung mitbekommt. Als dritte Option lässt sich jede Unterstützung abschalten. Darüber hinaus nehmt ihr über den Button anrufe an oder springt (durch mehrfaches Drücken) durch die Playlist.
Eine App gibt es nicht. Es gibt also keine Möglichkeit, mit einem Equalizer herumzuspielen, wie es bei manchen Bluetooth-Modellen der Fall ist. Das ist allerdings kein Nachteil, denn ich brauche nicht für jedes Gadget eine eigene App, für die ich dann am „besten“ noch einen Account anlegen muss.
Wir suchen Bass
Beim Klang müsst ihr dann folglich nehmen, was ihr bekommt. Die In-Ears bieten klare Höhen, lassen allerdings etwas an Tiefe vermissen. Bässe deuten die Buds nur an. Für Hiphop-Fans ist das eher nichts. Wer unterwegs nur Podcast hören will, bekommt aber klare stimmen geliefert. Der Noise-Cancelling-Modus tut Seins dazu, dass man den Episoden oder eben der Musik in Ruhe folgen kann. Zwar ist die Geräuschunterdrückung nicht perfekt, um relativ ungestört in der Bahn unterwegs zu sein reicht es aber.
Natürlich kann man mit den Bose-In-Ears auch telefonieren oder an Videokonferenzen teilnehmen, ein entsprechendes Mikrofon ist in die Fernbedienung am Kabel eingebaut. Ich habe meine Kolleg:innen gebeten, den Klang zu bewerten. Die Rückmeldung: Mit dem Kabelheadset war ich im Meeting gut zu verstehen.
Das Leben mit dem Kabel
Und wie lebt es sich nun wieder zurück an der Strippe? Sicherlich ist es praktisch, nicht mehr auf den Ladestand der In-Ears achten zu müssen. Einen einzelnen Ohrhörer kann man ebenfalls nicht mehr verlieren. Aber es zeigt sich auch, dass früher eben doch nicht alles besser. Gerade bei kaltem Wetter unter der dicken Jacke artet es schnell in Fummelei aus, wenn man etwa das Ticket auf dem Smartphone im ÖPNV vorzeigen will oder aber an der Fernbedienung die Wiedergabe pausieren will.
Und natürlich funktioniert der Plug-and-Play-Gedanke hervorragend am iPhone und Macbook, nicht aber an der Apple Watch. Die hat bekanntlich gar keinen Anschluss. Beim Sport Musik hören? Zumindest für mich nicht möglich, obwohl die In-Ears dank IPX4-Zertifizierung (Spritzwasserschutz) durchaus dafür geeignet sind. Ein zweites Problem habe ich im Büro festgestellt. Der Bildschirm ist an die eine USB-C-Buchse angestöpselt, die Bose-Kopfhörer an die zweite. Will ich jetzt aber mein Smartphone am Laptop laden, sieht es finster aus. Mein Macbook Air hat nur zwei USB-C-Plätze (und einen Klinkenanschluss).
Fazit
Bose verbindet Retro-Charme mit der praktischen ANC-Funktion moderner Bluetooth-In-Ears. Eine Mischung, die durchaus gelungen ist. Wer zu gewissen Abstrichen bereit ist und vorsichtig mit dem Kabel umgeht, kann von den kabelgebundenen In-Ears durchaus länger etwas haben als von akkubetriebenen Alternativen. Für einen Preis von rund 100 Euro kein schlechter Deal.

articles.title: Más allá del debate sobre su éxito, el 11N deja una pregunta: para qué sirve realmente una huelga general en 2026
articles.text:
El 11N ha sido una huelga especial por varias razones. Además de ser la primera gran convocatoria nacional en 14 años y llegar en plena campaña preelectoral, su detonante fue la crisis de la vivienda, un problema grave que sin embargo no está directamente relacionado con los derechos laborales. Dejando claro todo eso, el 11N también ofreció algunas imágenes previsibles que habíamos visto en huelgas anteriores: piquetes, manifestaciones, negocios cerrados y un encontronazo entre la patronal y los sindicatos a la hora de estimar el éxito de la convocatoria.
Más allá de todo eso, de las peculiaridades y el guion esperable del 11N, hay algunas preguntas que quedan botando: ¿Para qué sirven las huelgas en 2026? ¿Tienen el mismo impacto que en los años 90 u 80 o han perdido capacidad de presión? Y sobre todo, ¿cómo diablos medimos su alcance?
¿Cómo fue el 11N? La respuesta más rápida es ‘depende’. Depende de a quién le preguntes. Aunque en un principio hablaron de un seguimiento “dispar”, con un nivel de respaldo que oscilaba entre el 41 y 75% en función de la región, los sindicatos acabaron celebrando la jornada como “un éxito rotundo”.
La cosa cambia si consultamos a la CEOE. Para la patronal española fue un “fracaso” sin paliativos, una movilización que alcanzó un “mínimo histórico” con un apoyo de apenas el 5%. Por si no fuera suficiente, a ese baile de cifras se suman las que han ido desgranando las instituciones de uno y otro color.
En realidad, nada de eso resulta sorprendente. Los desacuerdos en torno a los niveles de seguimiento son la tónica habitual en estos casos (lo noticioso sería que no lo hubiera), igual que lo son otras imágenes que dejó el 11N: piquetes, carreteras cortadas, retrasos en el transporte, manifestaciones multitudinarias y disturbios con decenas de detenidos, como vimos en Barcelona o Madrid.
¿Cómo medir el alcance real? Esa es la pregunta que se han hecho no pocos analistas en las últimas horas. El 11N dejó una demostración de fuerza innegable en las calles, pero… ¿Y a nivel laboral y económico? ¿Cómo se puede medir su impacto real? Hace tres o cuatro décadas la respuesta sería sencilla. Contabilizar los paros en cadenas de producción industrial, obras, terminales de trenes o aeropuertos resulta fácil; pero en los últimos años la economía española ha experimentado varios procesos que complican considerablemente la foto.
¿Qué cambios? Para empezar, España ha visto cómo el sector terciario ganaba peso desde mediados del siglo pasado hasta representar más del 65% del PIB. Si hablamos de empleo, los servicios aglutinan el 76,5% de la población ocupada, cifra que se dispara por encima del 80% en ciertas comunidades autónomas.
A esos datos se añade el aumento del teletrabajo, que si bien sigue en niveles inferiores al promedio europeo se ha convertido en un concepto familiar para cientos de miles de españoles. Se calcula que alrededor de 3,2 millones ya desempeñan sus tareas en remoto al menos de forma ocasional.
Hay otro factor que complica valorar el impacto real de una huelga: la automatización y digitalización, favorecida por la inteligencia artificial. No es una cuestión menor. En 2025 la firma Redwood Software estimaba que el 73% de las empresas habían aumentado su partida para automatización. Se trata de un dato internacional y en España todavía son minoría quienes aseguran trabajar en fábricas plenamente digitalizadas, pero aun así es un dato elocuente.
¿No hay forma de medirlo entonces? Sí, sí la hay. Como recuerdan Kiko Llaneras y Jacob Vicente en El País, los analistas que quieren medir el alcance del 11N tienen varios recursos a su alcance, incluido el que tal vez más se ha repasado (y citado) durante las últimas horas: el consumo de energía eléctrica.
Red Eléctrica Española (REE) publica a diario un informe con dos datos reveladores: su previsión de demanda de energía y el consumo real, que va actualizando sobre la marcha. Para el primer valor (el pronóstico) los técnicos de REE tienen en cuenta factores como el día de la semana o la época del año, pero no variables como una convocatoria de huelga general.
Es un matiz importante porque la brecha entre su estimación inicial y el consumo real nos habla de una anomalía que se explica, al menos en parte, por cambios en la producción y consumo del país. Como se puede ver en los gráficos de arriba, ayer ese desfase llegó a ser considerable a media mañana y media tarde, una ‘fotografía’ muy distinta a la que dejaron los últimos miércoles.
¿Cómo de preciso es? Esa es la clave. No es lo mismo medir el seguimiento de una huelga fijándonos en los parones de cadenas de montaje o el absentismo en unas oficinas que hacerlo tirando de los indicadores de REE. Al fin y al cabo, en la demanda eléctrica influyen otras variables, como la meteorología.
Eso sin contar con que no todos los sectores tienen el mismo impacto en el balance eléctrico (una fábrica puede pesar más que muchas tiendas juntas) y los servicios mínimos de una empresa siguen apuntalando parte de la demanda, independientemente del porcentaje de plantilla que secunde la huelga.
¿Es el único desafío? No. Hay otra pregunta aún más complicada. Si tenemos en cuenta el peso creciente del sector servicios, el aumento del teletrabajo, el abanico de posibilidades creado por la IA o el aumento de autónomos y freelances en España, ¿hasta qué punto son efectivas las huelgas en 2026? ¿Conservan la misma capacidad de presión que hace 20 o 30 años, cuando frenar una fábrica tenía un impacto directo y evidente en los ingresos de la empresa?
Al fin y al cabo en modelos de negocio digitales y automatizados, los trabajadores pueden parar un día sin que eso afecte a la demanda y el flujo de ingresos. Por ejemplo, es el caso de las plataformas de streaming, las lavanderías automáticas, servicios self-service o banca online, por citar algunos casos. En un mundo donde negocios de ese tipo son más habituales… ¿Pierden capacidad de presión las huelgas, más allá de su alarde de fuerza en las calles?

articles.title: In reversal, American Cancer Society urges routine prostate cancer screening
articles.text:
In a significant update to its guidelines for prostate cancer screening, the American Cancer Society is now recommending that men get routinely screened for prostate cancer with a PSA test.
Men at average risk should get a PSA test every two years from age 50 to 69, according to the new guidelines released Thursday.
Men considered at high risk due to race and family history should start testing earlier, at 45, and most are recommended to get tested every year. Specifically, yearly testing starting at age 45 is recommended for all Black men, who have higher rates of prostate cancer. Non-Black men should also get yearly testing starting at 45 if a close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer before age 65, or if more than one of their relatives has had prostate cancer. On the other hand, if only one close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer and it was diagnosed at age 65 or older, non-Black men in this case should start PSA screening at 45, but are recommended to get testing only every two years.
Men ages 70 to 74 should consult their doctor on continuing screening, while those 75 and up are not recommended to get screened.
The new guidance departs from ACS’s previous iteration, published in 2010, which made no universal recommendations for routine screening. Men at age 50 were recommended to use shared-decision making with their doctors on whether or not to get tested. The recommendation was similar to that from the US Preventive Services Task Force, a federal panel that regularly evaluates evidence and makes recommendations on such preventive medical care. (The USPSTF is currently working on an update to its prostate cancer screening recommendation, though it should be noted that the panel has recently been overhauled by anti-vaccine Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and new members are reportedly rife with conflicts of interest.)

articles.title: El CMO de Google para Latinoamérica contó cómo la IA cambió su forma de hacer publicidad: armó un "sistema operativo" de marketing
articles.text:
Ramiro Sánchez, CMO (Chief Marketing Officer) de Google para América Latina, subió al escenario de El Ojo de Iberoamérica en Buenos Aires con una pregunta para la sala: cuántos trabajan en marketing o en agencias, y cuántos sienten que es muy difícil entender lo que pasa todo el tiempo. Todas las manos quedaron arriba. “Funcionó”, dijo. Esa es la tesis de su presentación.
Lo que contó después, con Paula Marsilli de la agencia Monks a su lado en el escenario, es cómo Google resolvió ese problema puertas adentro. Sánchez armó lo que él mismo llama un “sistema operativo” de marketing para la región y mostró el primer resultado: tres de cada cuatro piezas creativas salen aprobadas.
Un sistema que junta tendencias, reglas de marca y límites legales
La idea, en palabras de Sánchez, era tener en un solo lugar todo lo que sabe su equipo y la agencia: qué tendencias importan, en cuáles conviene entrar y cómo hablaría la marca en cada caso según sus propias reglas.
A eso se suma lo que casi nunca entra en una charla de creatividad: qué funciones del producto están disponibles en cada país y cuáles no, y qué se puede decir y de qué manera por restricciones legales. “Hay cosas que se pueden decir de una manera o no se pueden decir de esa manera”, explicó.
Su diagnóstico fue preciso. Google tiene herramientas como Gemini y Nano Banana, su generador de imágenes, que según él funcionan “fenomenalmente”. El problema era que seguían metidas en el mismo proceso de trabajo de siempre. Cambiar la herramienta sin cambiar el proceso no alcanzaba.
Ese proceso lo describió con detalle. Una marca escribe un briefing, el documento con el que le encarga una campaña a la agencia. Lo revisan varias personas. La agencia lo recibe, alguien lo interpreta a su manera, vuelven preguntas, vuelven ideas, se revisa otra vez. “Es un proceso no solo frustrante a veces, sino también lento”, dijo.
Lo que pidió fue comprimir esa parte burocrática para que los creativos hagan lo que mejor hacen: el gusto, el humor, lo local, “las cosas humanas que hacen que una marca sea relevante”. El sistema prepara el punto de partida; la gente pone el criterio.
El Mundial fue la primera prueba
El sistema salió al aire durante el Mundial de este año, bajo el nombre de Proyecto Aura, y después se usó en Rock in Rio, en septiembre. Marsilli, vicepresidenta de cuentas regionales de Monks, lo presentó como un “sistema vivo” pensado para anticipar lo que la audiencia quiere ver, en el momento justo.
Sánchez descartó la lectura fácil. “Cualquiera pensaría: okey, el Mundial es fácil porque todo el mundo está hablando de fútbol. El problema es la sutileza”, dijo. Hablar de fútbol en Brasil, en México o en Argentina no es lo mismo, y la marca tenía que entrar solo en las conversaciones donde tenía sentido que Gemini estuviera.
Los ejemplos que dio fueron conversaciones que se encendieron durante el torneo y a las que la marca se sumó mientras duraban. Una de esas tendencias, admitió él mismo, hoy ya nadie la recuerda. Esa es la velocidad a la que apuntaba.
Tres de cada cuatro piezas aprobadas
El resultado que más destacó no fue de audiencia sino de proceso. La interacción positiva con el contenido subió mucho, dijo, sin dar cifras. El dato que sí dio es el que, según él, más contenta pone a una agencia: tres de cada cuatro piezas eran aprobadas. “Esto es mucho mejor que antes”, afirmó, sin precisar la tasa anterior.
A mi lectura, ese número dice más del briefing que de la creatividad. Si tres de cada cuatro ideas pasan, el encargo llega más preciso y el creativo arranca desde ideas con alta probabilidad de funcionar, tal como Sánchez lo describió. El sistema no reemplaza al creativo: le ahorra las vueltas.
Marsilli contó que ahora están probando cómo llevar el mismo esquema a momentos sin un Mundial de por medio, al día a día de la marca, país por país y lengua por lengua. Ahí es donde se va a ver si el sistema sirve fuera de los grandes eventos.
El marco de la charla: marcas que la gente quiera y las máquinas entiendan
La presentación de Sánchez fue parte de la conferencia “Building Brands at the Speed of Culture” (construir marcas a la velocidad de la cultura), que abrió Alejandro Olascoaga, director general de Monks México, en la 29ª edición de El Ojo, el festival de creatividad latina que se celebra en Buenos Aires.
Olascoaga planteó el marco con una idea que tomó de otra charla del festival: una marca hoy tiene que ser querida por las personas y, a la vez, preferida por las máquinas, porque si los algoritmos de IA no la leen y no la distribuyen, la campaña más linda pierde oportunidades.
Y propuso dejar de pensar en campañas de seis meses para pensar en ecosistemas vivos.
Lo que Sánchez mostró es la versión concreta de esa idea: no una campaña hecha con IA, sino una forma de trabajar donde la IA arma el encargo y las personas deciden qué sale al aire. Quien controla el briefing controla la creatividad, y Google decidió que ese control lo tenga un sistema.

articles.title: Quel avenir pour Jensen Huang ? Elon Musk se dit déjà prêt à l'embaucher
articles.text:
Jensen Huang a finalement quitté ses fonctions de président et directeur général de Nvidia, ainsi que son siège au conseil d’administration, avec effet immédiat. Un véritable coup de tonnerre pour le cofondateur de l’entreprise qui n’a pour l’instant rien dit de ses projets. Elon Musk, lui, s’est déjà manifesté sur les réseaux sociaux, avant l’annonce officielle.
Alors que le conseil d’administration de Nvidia se réunissait pour décider du sort de son patron, le compte du blog financier ZeroHedge a lancé sur X : « Elon, s’il te plaît, embauche Jensen ». Environ une heure et demie plus tard, le patron de SpaceX et de Tesla lui a répondu : « Ce serait un honneur ».
 @zerohedge That would be an honor
— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) November 12, 2026
Le 8 novembre, il avait approuvé d’un simple « Je suis d’accord » un message de Shaun Maguire, associé du fonds Sequoia Capital. Celui-ci reconnaissait que Jensen Huang avait fait « quelque chose d’incroyablement stupide », mauvais pour l’Amérique, tout en le jugeant « irremplaçable pour le leadership américain dans l’IA » et en estimant qu’une seconde erreur n’arrangerait rien.
 I agree
— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) November 8, 2026
Elon Musk est l’un des plus gros clients de Nvidia
Cette proximité entre les deux milliardaires n’a rien de surprenant. Les entreprises d’Elon Musk comptent parmi les plus gros acheteurs de puces Nvidia. Même si SpaceX aimerait bien fabriquer ses propres GPU pour réduire sa dépense, le milliardaire a annoncé durant l’été aux investisseurs que son entreprise construirait son infrastructure d’intelligence artificielle exclusivement sur du matériel Nvidia. En octobre, SpaceX a par ailleurs fait état d’un engagement d’environ 40 milliards de dollars pour louer des puces Vera Rubin.
Quant aux deux hommes, ils se connaissent depuis longtemps et Jenseng Huang aime rappeler qu’il a livré en personne à Elon Musk, en 2016, le tout premier supercalculateur DGX-1 de Nvidia.
Reste à savoir si cette réponse ira plus loin qu’un échange sur X. L’avenir de Jensen Huang dépendra aussi de l’enquête ouverte par le FBI sur sa relation avec Alice Huang, soupçonnée par Washington de travailler pour la Chine, ce que Pékin dément. En attendant, la directrice financière Colette Kress assure l’intérim, pendant que le conseil d’administration cherche un successeur.

Le Samsung S92H est une évolution en douceur du S90F, mais ses quelques améliorations en font un excellent téléviseur. La qualité d’image est toujours au top, la réactivité en jeu se montre excellente, et on trouve désormais l’antireflet du fabricant, toujours aussi efficace. En bonus, le pic lumineux est en progression sur cette dalle de 55 pouces, mais évidemment pas au niveau des TV les plus haut de gamme du fabricant. Quelques points faibles subsistent, à commencer par l’absence de Dolby Vision et une partie audio seulement correcte. Le S92H n’en reste pas moins un modèle polyvalent, au bon rapport qualité-prix, d'autant plus pour ceux qui veulent profiter de l’antireflet sans avoir à débourser une somme plus importante pour acquérir le S95H ou le S99H.

articles.title: 55 000 € pour une batterie d’occasion : Mercedes propose de remplacer un pack défectueux avec 300 000 km
articles.text:
Acheter une voiture électrique d’occasion relève d’un sacré coup de poker. La tentation est forte vu la décote, certes, mais l’état de la batterie peut aussi laisser craindre le pire. Il suffit de tomber sur un exemplaire aux packs bien fatigués pour déchanter après quelques années. C’est ce qui est arrivé au propriétaire d’une Mercedes EQS qui pensait avoir flairé un bon plan. Hélas, 300 000 km passés, la batterie semble arriver en bout de course.
La personne, qui a remarqué une décharge anormalement rapide du pack, a emmené son EQS450+ dans une concession de la marque, en Croatie. Le diagnostic est implacable : la batterie est gravement endommagée. L’analyse révèle des cellules abîmées et un déséquilibre dû à l’autodécharge. Pire encore, l’accumulateur est tellement usé que chaque section ne pouvait être réparée individuellement.
55 000 € pour du reconditionné : la facture d’occasion qui passe mal
Un remplacement complet est donc nécessaire. Problème, Mercedes ne produit plus les batteries du modèle en question. Il faudra ainsi se contenter d’un pack d’occasion. Embêtant, même si on pourrait alors imaginer un prix de remplacement maîtrisé, l’ensemble n’étant pas neuf. C’est malheureusement tout le contraire qui s’est produit : le constructeur propose une batterie reconditionnée contre… 55 000 €.
Et la garantie, alors ? Comme la majorité des marques, Mercedes garantit bien ses packs pendant 8 ans ou 160 000 km. Pour ce propriétaire, l’échéance est malheureusement bien derrière. L’entreprise EV Clinic spécialisée dans l’entretien des véhicules électriques a pour sa part mené sa petite enquête. Ses membres se sont rendus au siège de CATL, le fournisseur de la batterie, pour savoir combien vaut réellement une cellule d’EQS.
12 000 € chez le fabricant : l’enquête qui pointe un énorme surcoût
Les estimations se sont chiffrées à environ 12 000 €. Bien moins que le devis proposé par Mercedes. Cas isolé ? On ne pense pas : cet écart spectaculaire concernerait très probablement tous les autres constructeurs. De fait, EV Clinic préconise plutôt de remplacer les packs défectueux par des batteries d’occasion compatibles coûtant au maximum 15 000 €. Même en rajoutant la main-d’œuvre, on restera bien en-deçà d’une batterie reconditionnée.
Rappelons que la Mercedes EQS est l’équivalent électrique de la célèbre Classe S. Dans sa version 450+, cette limousine embarque naturellement de gros accumulateurs d’une capacité nette de 107,8 kWh permettant 780 km d’autonomie. Cela pourrait en partie expliquer le coût de remplacement très élevé. Rappelons qu’après restylage, la limousine allemande retient des batteries de 122 kWh permettant jusqu’à 925 km d’autonomie. Un record qui sera très prochainement surpassé par les 960 km de la Lucid Air.

articles.title: Lego mantiene fuera de línea su mercado de piezas usadas BrickLink y no dice cuándo volverá
articles.text:
Lego mantiene desde el 5 de noviembre fuera de línea BrickLink, el mercado donde los coleccionistas compran y venden piezas, figuras y sets usados, y no sabe cuándo lo reactivará. La empresa dijo que detectó “actividad inusual” en la plataforma y que investiga qué ocurrió, según el medio tecnológico The Verge.
Lego no precisó si el sitio sufrió un ataque informático ni si los datos de los clientes quedaron afectados, según la BBC, que contactó a la empresa. Lego publicó en la página de inicio de BrickLink un mensaje solo después de ese contacto.
“Nuestra prioridad inmediata era proteger el sitio, a nuestros miembros y la integridad de BrickLink”, afirmó la empresa en el comunicado, actualizado el 11 de noviembre. Antes de volver a abrir, dijo, necesita contener el problema, investigar cómo ocurrió y revisar si hay otros fallos relacionados.
Durante los primeros días, el aviso en el sitio hablaba de mantenimiento. Después, un mensaje prometía el regreso para la tarde del 11 de noviembre. Ese texto fue borrado y hoy no hay estimación, según The Verge y la BBC.
Vendedores sin su principal canal de venta
BrickLink se define como el mayor mercado secundario de Lego del mundo. Según el medio especializado The Brick Post, tiene más de un millón de miembros registrados en cerca de 200 países. Nació como proyecto de un aficionado y Lego lo compró en 2019, según la BBC.
Muchos de esos miembros tienen tiendas en el sitio y viven de vender allí, o complementan con ello sus ingresos. El medio Brick Fanatics informó que varios vendedores aseguran que sus ingresos cayeron de forma drástica durante la caída del servicio y que se quejan de la falta de comunicación de la empresa.
Algunos migraron a Brick Owl, una alternativa. Ese sitio también estuvo fuera de servicio varias horas el 11 de noviembre, según Brick Fanatics. La caída además afectó el anuncio de los próximos sets del Programa de Diseñadores de BrickLink, informó The Brick Post.
Un cobro dudoso en medio de la caída
Melanie Hoskin, una profesional de ciberseguridad que colecciona Lego desde hace 45 años, contó a la BBC que recibió varios enlaces para pagar una edición limitada que ya había reservado y abonado en la plataforma. Según su relato, la empresa llegó a decirle que podía bloquearla de BrickLink porque no creía que el pago se hubiera cobrado.
Lego aclaró a la BBC que desconoce problemas de pago más amplios. El caso de Hoskin está resuelto; ella dijo sentirse como si la hubieran acusado de robo. Se desconoce si ese fallo tiene relación con el motivo por el que el sitio quedó fuera de línea.
BrickLink ya estuvo caído por un incidente de seguridad en la misma época del año, hace tres años. Entonces Lego apagó el sitio tras recibir una amenaza y una exigencia de rescate, y al volver pidió a los usuarios cambiar sus contraseñas con requisitos más estrictos, aunque aseguró que las cuentas no habían sido comprometidas. Hasta ahora Lego no ha dado una fecha de regreso: su último comunicado, del 11 de noviembre, indica que el trabajo de investigación continúa.
Nuevos productos de LEGO
LEGO presentó en el CES 2026, durante su primera conferencia de prensa en el evento, el sistema LEGO Smart Play junto con el Smart Brick, un ladrillo con la forma clásica 2x4 que incorpora sensores de luz, color y sonido, además de un acelerómetro que detecta movimientos y golpes, lo que le permite reaccionar en tiempo real con sonidos, luces y efectos.
El sistema se completa con Smart Tags, que programan reacciones específicas, y Smart Minifigures, que suman estados de ánimo y sonidos propios a través del altavoz integrado en el bloque; los Smart Bricks también pueden formar una red descentralizada que les otorga “conciencia espacial” para reconocer su ubicación dentro de una construcción y así habilitar juegos como carreras en tiempo real.

articles.title: La dimisión de Huang hace que Nvidia se deje 550.000 millones de dólares en valor de bolsa
articles.text:
Tras la publicación de una exclusiva de The New York Times, Jensen Huang admitió en un memorando a sus empleados que había tenido una aventura extramatrimonial. La polémica tal vez no habría llegado mucho más lejos si no fuera porque su amante ya estaba siendo investigada por presunto espionaje para China.
La respuesta de los accionistas de Nvidia no se hizo esperar: a partir de ese momento, sus acciones iban a iniciar un desplome bursátil superior al 14%, lo que implica una pérdida de capitalización cercana a los 550.000 millones de dólares en solo cuatro días.
El primer romance le costó muy caro. Nvidia venía de marcar un récord histórico durante el mes de octubre, con unas acciones valoradas en unos 243,37 dólares y una capitalización cercana a los 6 billones de dólares. Sin embargo, el viernes 6 de noviembre el precio de sus acciones se había templado y su cotización afrontaba el fin de semana con unos nada despreciables 186,64 dólares por título, fijando la capitalización total de Nvidia en unos 4,5 billones de dólares.
Sin embargo, tras conocerse la aventura de Huang y la posterior investigación por espionaje, el lunes dibujaba un panorama muy distinto. La acción comenzó un rápido descenso que llegó a registrar el 8% de pérdidas, pero al final del día recuperó su precio y se situó en unas pérdidas de "solo" el 4,3%. Por ponerlo en contexto, eso son más de 200.000 millones de capitalización. El martes no mejoró.
La tendencia bajista siguió su curso, y Nvidia cerraba un martes de pesadilla con una caída del 5,47% que se sumaba a los malos resultados del lunes, dejando el precio de las acciones a 168,89 dólares. En solo dos días, la compañía había perdido 400.000 millones de capitalización.
La segunda infidelidad y el castigo nocturno. En la apertura de los mercados del miércoles, todo apuntaba a que la tormenta había arreciado y el indicador bursátil aparecía por primera vez en verde marcando una subida del 2,92%. La alegría les iba a durar poco.
El NYT publicó que Huang había tenido una segunda aventura con Kimberly Powell, vicepresidenta que depende directamente de Huang. El artículo, además, deslizaba que la junta preparaba la destitución de Huang y su salida de la compañía. Tras el cierre, las acciones perdieron todo lo ganado y se desplomaron por debajo del 8,4%.
La dimisión le da la estocada. Para terminar de rematar a los accionistas, Nvidia anunció que Huang dejaba la presidencia, la dirección ejecutiva y el consejo, con efecto inmediato. Colette Kress, hasta ahora directora financiera, será la CEO interina hasta que la compañía designe a un sucesor definitivo.
La noticia ha caído como un jarro de agua fría entre los inversores, que hundieron la cotización de Nvidia un 14%, hasta los 148,80 dólares. No obstante, cuando se recuperaron del susto, se moderó la caída fijando el descenso en el 7% al momento de publicar esta noticia, con un precio de 165,15 dólares por título. En total, en poco menos de cuatro días, Nvidia se ha dejado un 13%, lo que supone una capitalización de 4,01 billones de dólares. Es decir, la tormenta Huang se ha llevado por delante casi 550.000 millones de dólares del capital de Nvidia.
Ahora la principa preocupación para Colette Kress es qué explicaciones va a dar a los inversores en la presentación de resultados del tercer trimestre que la empresa mantiene para el martes 17 de noviembre. 550.000 millones es muchísimo dinero incluso para Nvidia.

articles.title: Outlook, Teams, Copilot: Microsoft kämpft gegen massiven Cloud-Ausfall
articles.text:
Outlook, Teams, Copilot: Wieso die Microsoft-Dienste gerade Probleme machen
Eine stundenlange Störung hat viele Unternehmen und Verbraucher von Microsofts Cloud-Angeboten wie dem E-Mail-Dienst Outlook abgeschnitten. Betroffen war dadurch eine ganze Palette von Diensten des Windows-Riesen. Beim Bürokommunikations-Angebot Teams etwa konnten Aufgaben versagen, die auf die Kalender-Anbindung angewiesen sind. Nicht nutzbar für Unternehmenskunden war zum Teil auch der KI-Assistent Copilot.
Exchange und Microsoft 365: Störung trifft Nutzer weltweit
Microsoft dokumentierte über Mitteilungen auf der Online-Plattform X den Kampf gegen die Ausfälle, der zunächst ohne durchschlagenden Erfolg blieb. Der Software-Riese berichtete zunächst von Problemen bei Exchange-Mailboxen in den USA. Danach hieß es vom Unternehmen, dass die Störung weltweit Nutzer des Cloud-Dienstes Microsoft 365 treffen könne. Man versuche, den Datenverkehr an möglicherweise problematischen Servern vorbeizuleiten, hieß es.
Enttäuschte Hoffnungen: Microsoft-Server hängen sich erneut auf
Im nächsten Schritt schien Microsoft einen Erfolg vermelden zu können: Auf betroffenen Servern sei ein Prozess entdeckt worden, der sie lahmlege. Danach hieß es, man bringe einen Teil der Server wieder ans Netz – „und sie bleiben soweit stabil“. Eine Stunde später folgten enttäuschte Hoffnungen: Die Server könnten sich wieder aufhängen, sobald Datenverkehr sie erreiche, berichteten die Microsoft-Ingenieure.
Microsoft-Infrastruktur: Isolierter Neustart bringt neuen Rückschlag
Im nächsten Anlauf wurde dann versucht, Teile der Infrastruktur isoliert hochzufahren, und dabei sehe man „positive Ergebnisse“, hieß es. Wenig später musste Microsoft wieder einen Rückschlag einräumen: Die Maßnahmen griffen nicht so wie erwartet. Wie lange die Störung noch andauern könnte, blieb zunächst unklar.
Nicht der erste Ausfall: Microsoft-Cloud schon Ende August gestört
Ausfälle von Online-Diensten gehörten zum Alltag – meist sind sie aber nur von kurzer Dauer. Manchmal allerdings sind die Probleme so gravierend oder so schwer zu finden, dass es zu stundenlangen Störungen kommt. Microsofts E-Mail-Dienste hatten erst Ende August einen stundenlangen großflächigen Ausfall durchlebt. Nutzer konnten sich über Stunden hinweg nicht einloggen oder Nachrichten senden und empfangen. Als Ursache nannte Microsoft damals ein Problem in der Cloud-Infrastruktur.

articles.title: AntiFox AI agents hijacked by hackers to carry out theft of AWS credentials
articles.text:
AntiFox AI agents hijacked by hackers to carry out theft of AWS credentials
ARTEX forks are wreaking havoc
- Attackers are abusing the AI-powered penetration testing tool AntiFox to search for credentials and compromise AWS environments
- Campaigns leveraged web-server intrusions and stolen cloud credentials to map infrastructure and access sensitive resources
- Researchers urge organizations to monitor for web shells, rotate exposed secrets, and enforce least-privilege access controls
Cybercriminals are using an open source AI-powered pentesting platform called AntiFox to steal login credentials and access people’s Amazon Web Services (AWS) environments.
This is according to security researchers Arctic Wolf, who recently disclosed their findings on GitHub, explaining how unnamed threat actors were hosting their own instances of the tool on Alibaba Cloud infrastructure and were using its automated capabilities to analyze compromised systems, search for passwords, and access cloud resources.
What is AntiFox?
AntiFox is an AI-powered, open source penetration testing platform built by a Chinese developer. Penetration testing is a process cybersecurity professionals usually use to identify weaknesses in their IT infrastructure, and while tools like AntiFox are not malicious by design, they are often abused in different attacks. This happens all the time with tools such as Cobalt Strike or ConnectWise ScreenConnect, too.
Arctic Wolf said that in some of the attacks they observed, threat actors first compromised internet-facing Microsoft IIS web servers, although they could not determine exactly how.
They then installed web shells to execute malicious server commands remotely and from there, they were going through application files and configuration settings, looking for database login credentials and other valuable secrets. The researchers also saw attempts to use these credentials to connect to internal production databases.
In other cases, attackers would use valid AWS credentials obtained elsewhere to sift through cloud environments and uncover accounts, permissions, databases, storage servers, and other important resources.
Commenting on the report, Amazon told BleepingComputer its services work as intended and urged customers to keep their passwords a secret: "AWS services were not compromised and operated as designed. The research describes threat actors using credentials taken from customers’ compromised applications to access their AWS accounts. As always, we recommend all customers follow security, identity, and compliance best practices, including granting least-privilege permissions, requiring IMDSv2 on EC2 instances, keeping long-term access keys out of application configurations, and turning on Amazon GuardDuty. Customers who suspect unauthorized activity in their accounts should follow guidance for remediating potentially compromised credentials or contact AWS Support."
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
AntiFox was built as a fork of ARTEX 0.1.1, another Chinese-developed AI-powered penetration testing framework that’s been filling headlines lately. Earlier this week, security researchers Censys said they identified 1,465 hosts running exposed ARTEX consoles, of which roughly 10% also ran at least one other tool commonly used in cyberattacks.
They also found 32 publicly accessible directories on ARTEX hosts, some of which exposed exploit binaries, post-exploitation tools, and other sensitive files.
The ghost of ARTEX
ARTEX was released in late July 2026 by a developer called Autumn-27, to serve as an AI-powered upgrade to ScopeSentry, a tool Censys described as a “widely used Chinese asset-discovery and vulnerability-scanning platform.” Its popularity skyrocketed, and by early October, reports started coming out of ARTEX being used in cyberattacks. Soon after the developer distanced themselves from these attacks, turned the tool closed-source, and made no subsequent releases.
Since then, numerous researchers observed it being used in different attacks, including a hit on South Korea financial institutions. Microsoft saw China-aligned group Storm-0940 use it, as well.
Arctic Wolf now recommends organizations monitor their web servers for suspicious activity, such as random files appearing on the networks, or operating-system commands being executed unapproved. They should also investigate unusual AWS activity, including rapid requests across multiple services and attempts to access stored credentials from unfamiliar infrastructure.
Unfamiliar web shells should be terminated on the spot, compromised systems reviewed, and any and all exposed passwords, API keys, and cloud credentials rotated without delay. The researchers also advise restricting application permissions to the resources needed for normal operations and enabling detailed logging to help detect suspicious access and unauthorised changes to stored data.

articles.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a lower-cost model said to outscore Argon - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Google releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a lower-cost model said to outscore Argon
Google LLC today released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a lower-cost model in its Gemini 4 artificial intelligence family that it says outscores its frontier Gemini 4 Argon model on an independent intelligence ranking.
Measured on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high thinking level, Hydrogen scored 51 to Argon’s 50, according to Google. A fourth thinking level called xhigh, new with Hydrogen, takes the score to 54.
The rollout is different, too. Argon spent nearly two weeks with members of Google’s Fairwind Program, a group of vetted cybersecurity defenders, before paying developers could get at it on Oct. 13. Hydrogen skipped that stage. Anyone can use it from today, including people on the free version of the Gemini app.
Koray Kavukcuoglu, who became head of Google DeepMind in August when Demis Hassabis moved into a chairman role, wrote in the announcement that Hydrogen is “built for rapid execution.”
Orchestrator, which Google added to its Antigravity coding tool today, picks between Hydrogen and Gemini 4 Carbon as a session goes along. Google’s runs of the Terminal-Bench 4.0 coding test found Orchestrator getting close to Carbon’s success rate on an average of 24% less quota.
Gemini 3.8 Flash, which came out in September, is the yardstick for most of the other numbers in the announcement. Against it, Hydrogen finished tasks 2.5 times faster at the default setting. On Terminal-Bench 4.1, which tests work done at a command line, Hydrogen more than tripled the older model’s 18.2% with a score of 57%.
Among the early testers Google quoted, Andrew Carr, a former OpenAI scientist who is now chief scientist at 3D animation startup Cartwheel Inc., said the model caught two problems with an approach his team had been stuck on for 10 days. Discovery Loop Inc., the startup former Google Chief Scientist Jeff Dean co-founded after leaving in August, was another.
Kavukcuoglu said in late September that Google wanted Gemini 4 out “much earlier” than the end of the year. Three Gemini 4 models have now shipped in just over six weeks. Hydrogen arrived two days after Carbon, which also started out with Fairwind members, opened up to paying developers and Google AI Ultra subscribers.
Hydrogen is available today in the Gemini API, Google AI Studio and Google Search, and paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers can also use it in Antigravity. It costs $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens across the full 1 million-token context window. Argon costs $2 and $10 until its introductory pricing ends Nov. 30, then moves to $4 and $20.

articles.title: AI networking adds security: Nvidia unveils Scale-In - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
As AI agents take control, Nvidia rethinks the security playbook
Nvidia Corp. recently added a new pillar to its AI networking infrastructure with the unveiling of Scale-In.
Scale-In brings purpose-built acceleration to secure, manage and operate agentic AI factories. It is designed to deliver secure access, high-performance data movement, tenant isolation, simpler operations and more predictable performance as agents assume increasingly larger roles within AI factories.
“In agentic AI, it’s a completely different use case because now we’re dealing with many agents that need to run on the infrastructure,” said Gilad Shainer (pictured), senior vice president of networking at Nvidia. “You need to increase security because you need to make sure that those agents are contained in their sandbox and are not doing the wrong things. You need to build an infrastructure that needs to ensure security all around…what happens in the memory, what happens on storage. This is why we needed to bring an infrastructure which actually enabled the security across everything. And that’s what Scale-In is.”
Shainer spoke with theCUBE’s Dave Vellante for theCUBE + NYSE Wired: AI Factories – Data Centers of the Future interview series on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how Nvidia’s Scale-In architecture is designed to help transform scaled compute into a secure and operational AI factory platform.
Since the August introduction, Nvidia has expanded its agent security strategy. In September, the company introduced its Open Agent Safety Platform, combining OpenShell with Nvidia Sentry for out-of-band monitoring and hardware-based security enforcement. An October announcement added the OpenShell Reference Architecture, integrating Vera Rubin infrastructure, Vera CPUs and BlueField-4 to support secure agent execution across enterprise systems. Nvidia’s announcement outlines the expanded architecture.
In-silicon security for AI networking
Scale-In is powered by Nvidia BlueField-4 and Nvidia DOCA and connected over Nvidia Spectrum-X Ethernet. BlueField-4 is Nvidia’s fourth-generation data processing unit, a networking platform built for agentic AI factories and large-scale infrastructure needs. BlueField is essential to the management of agentic AI security, according to Shainer.
“You can think about BlueField or Blue-Field-4 as a device that has in-silicon security engines that are working out of band and collecting telemetry from everything, from memory, from storage, from GPUs, from CPUs,” Shainer told theCUBE. “That’s why that infrastructure connects to all other infrastructures and ensures security all around. That out-of-band monitoring enables BlueField to actually understand exactly what agents are doing.”
Along with BlueField-4, Nvidia DOCA also powers Scale-In deployment. This software platform enables the rapid creation of apps and services that offload, accelerate and isolate data center workloads.
Using DOCA, developers can create software-defined, cloud-native, DPU- and SuperNIC-accelerated solutions. Like Nvidia CUDA, which provides a programming platform for GPU workloads, DOCA gives developers access to DPU acceleration capabilities.
“DPU brings the in-silicon engines security engines, storage accelerations,” Shainer explained. “DOCA is the framework, the software, the APIs that enable you to access all of those engines that BlueField-4 provides.”
Nvidia has further reinforced agentic AI security with its open-source runtime offering called OpenShell. The tool is designed to govern agent execution, access and inference routing. Nvidia combined OpenShell with BlueField-4 because it wanted a device that could collect information outside the GPU and monitor an environment that no agent could influence.
“I want to also have another device which is completely separated, completely isolated from the agents, that can monitor everything out-of-band,” Shainer said. “That’s what we’re doing with BlueField-4, bringing all the security elements together with OpenShell, and now you have a secure infrastructure for agents. This is how the combination of OpenShell and BlueField-4 brings all the security elements that we need for gen AI.”
The more recent OpenShell Reference Architecture builds on that approach with Nvidia Sentry, which runs on BlueField-4 using DOCA software. According to Nvidia, Sentry continuously monitors agent behavior and can quarantine agents that attempt to move outside their defined software boundaries. The combination extends OpenShell’s runtime controls with an independent enforcement layer.

articles.title: Apex Neural Rendering Beats NVIDIA DLSS in Both Image Quality and Performance
articles.text:
Thursday, November 12th 2026
Apex Neural Rendering Beats NVIDIA DLSS in Both Image Quality and Performance
According to a company called Apex Compute, there is a new player in neural rendering. The company has developed Apex Neural Rendering, which reportedly offers higher quality and performance than NVIDIA's DLSS implementations. It includes three key components: frame generation (ANR FG), super resolution upscaling (ANR SR), and ray reconstruction denoising for ray tracing (ANR RR). Running frame generation on NVIDIA's GeForce RTX 5090 at 4K, the ANR FG achieves a latency of 1.01 ms per generated frame at a 2x setting, while NVIDIA's DLSS Frame Generation records 1.26 ms. We are not sure which version of DLSS FG was tested, but we can assume it was the latest version.
Regarding memory consumption, ANR FG uses only 214 MB of GPU memory, while DLSS FG requires more than double that, at 562 MB. Reportedly, the ANR FG neural network weights fit within just 0.17 MB, which is incredibly efficient. Based on samples on the company's website, the image quality that ANR delivers matches DLSS and even surpasses it in some cases. Apex Compute also managed to get Hogwarts Legacy and The Last of Us Part II Remastered working, showing the difference compared to DLSS, resulting in frame generation with more visual fidelity. ANR FG is a beta injector built around OptiScaler, which works in any game offering NVIDIA DLSS Frame Generation. You can view the results below.Supported GPUs include all of NVIDIA's GeForce RTX 20 series and newer, as well as the GeForce GTX 16 series. On the AMD side, support starts from the Radeon RX 5000 series and extends to the Steam Deck. Intel's Arc A-series and B-series are also supported, and surprisingly, Apple's M1 and later are compatible as well. The operating systems tested and supported include the now end-of-life Windows 10, Windows 11, Linux, SteamOS with Proton, and macOS 26 or later. Benchmarks comparing quality, image noise, and more are showcased below.Finally, Apex Compute will open-source this ANR framework with its components soon, which will be available on GitHub.

articles.title: FAA expands AI advice to manage air traffic congestion across entire US airspace
articles.text:
The US government has expanded the use of an AI tool for advising air traffic controllers to assist in managing air traffic across the entire national airspace system. Airline executives have voiced support for the rollout, but the US labor union representing air traffic controllers has said it was not involved in designing or testing the AI-driven system.
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) says the $875 million SMART system has helped reroute 180 flights since being implemented in airspace over Washington, DC, on September 21. The agency claims that this saved an average of 10 minutes per flight and almost 80 gallons of fuel per flight—and it is apparently hoping such results can be replicated nationwide through the expanded deployment.
“After a successful initial rollout to the National Capital Region in September, the FAA will now use SMART in the airspace of all 22 centers across the country to reduce delays, reduce fuel consumption and improve the travel experience for the flying public,” according to the agency statement posted on November 10.
The FAA fact sheet describes SMART as a cloud-based system that combines information about “weather patterns, flight paths, traffic flow and controller staffing metrics” to predict air traffic patterns. It is designed to make scheduling recommendations, identify optimal flight routes, and determine the best order of arrivals for aircraft.
However, a human team of FAA specialists based in DC is ultimately responsible for validating the SMART system recommendations before passing them along to air traffic control facilities across the country, according to the agency.
Let's take it as a given that these are conscientious professional people. But what do you think they're going to do when they're feeling overwhelmed or exhausted?

articles.title: Surfshark proves it does not record your data with a fresh independent no-logs audit
articles.text:
Surfshark proves it does not record your data with a fresh independent no-logs audit
Big Four accounting firm KPMG inspected Surfshark's network and found no signs of activity logging
- KPMG confirmed Surfshark does not log browsing traffic or IP addresses
- The evaluation covered standard, static, and multi-port servers
- While single snapshots, regular audits still set a clear privacy benchmark
Surfshark has once again called in outside experts to inspect its infrastructure. Independent Big Four accounting firm KPMG examined the provider’s server setup and confirmed that its systems follow its strict no-log claims.
For anyone shopping for the best VPN, privacy commitments can sound like empty marketing phrases. Almost every service advertises that it leaves no digital trace. Independent checks help bridge the gap between promises and actual technical proof, which is why Surfshark regularly opens its doors to outside inspectors.
This latest verification confirms that the provider does not store browsing histories, IP addresses, connection timestamps, or outgoing traffic. According to Surfshark's official announcement, the audit specifically tested whether user traffic can be monitored or retrieved from live server memory.
Surfshark – the best cheap VPN
Surfshark is a fast, easy-to-use VPN that seriously beats the competition when it comes to subscription pricing. Its two-year Starter plan works out at $2.49 a month (plus tax), but we think Surfshark One is the best value plan as it adds an antivirus, data breach monitor, alternative ID, and now new anti-scam tools. All of this starting from the equivalent of  just $2.79 a month. 
Surfshark's no-log audit: what KPMG actually inspected
Auditors reviewed the technical configuration of Surfshark's production servers, covering standard nodes, static IP locations, and multi-port routing setups. The inspectors assessed whether operational practices matched the guarantees outlined in the service's no-logs policy.
The final assessment found no discrepancies. Surfshark's infrastructure runs entirely on RAM-only servers. Because these machines lack traditional hard drives, all temporary operational data is wiped clean the moment a server reboots or powers down.
This is not the company’s first trip through the review process. Last year, Surfshark cleared an independent audit with Deloitte, following an earlier review that verified its first no-logs audit years ago.

What an independent VPN audit actually mean for your privacy?
It is worth asking the hard question: does an audit guarantee absolute anonymity? No, it does not.
An audit provides a point-in-time assessment. It proves that on the days KPMG tested the network, the configurations complied with stated policies. It cannot monitor changes an engineering team might make months later, nor does it turn a VPN into a magic shield against online fingerprinting, account tracking, or malware.
Still, routine testing remains the gold standard for consumer privacy. When providers make full audit findings public, users can verify that their personal internet traffic is not quietly sitting in a log file.

articles.title: Connecting AI to the Physical World - EE Times
articles.text:
Artificial intelligence is advancing rapidly. Models are becoming more capable, computing platforms more powerful, and tools for building intelligent applications more accessible. As AI moves into robots, industrial machines, vehicles, and drones, however, its progress depends on a practical question: How effectively can these systems obtain information from the physical world?
An intelligent machine needs more than processing power; it needs relevant data about its surroundings, the state of other machines, and the conditions in which it operates. Some information comes from its own sensors.
Other information must arrive from nearby devices, infrastructure, remote systems, or shared computing resources. The usefulness of that information depends on its quality, timing, and availability.
This creates an important opportunity for wireless technology. AI can make use only of information that devices can capture, process, and deliver. When the connection is unreliable, inflexible, or unsuitable for the environment, valuable information may arrive too late, lose essential context, or never reach the systems that need it.
The next stage of physical AI therefore requires progress in the devices and communications systems that connect intelligence to its surroundings. Software-defined radio (SDR) and the software intellectual property that makes it work have an important role to play.
Where standard modems fall short
Standard modems serve many applications well. Specialized systems may need capabilities or control interfaces that a particular modem does not expose. The relevant question is whether the device supports the behavior the application requires within its operating constraints.
A factory robot may need predictable, low-latency communication to coordinate with nearby machines. Inspection cameras may need substantial uplink capacity to send detailed images for analysis. A drone operating beyond terrestrial coverage may need a non-terrestrial link, while a remote sensor must conserve battery power.
Requirements can also change during a mission. A robot may alternate between coordinated movement and image collection. If infrastructure coverage becomes unavailable, an appropriately equipped system may exchange data through nearby devices. Each mode places different demands on capacity, delay, and energy use.
Designing AI processing and communications together helps manage these demands. A device can analyze routine observations locally, send short status updates, and upload detailed recordings when needed. This reduces unnecessary traffic and leaves more capacity for information that must arrive promptly.
Standard modems may support some of these needs, but developers often have limited access to the underlying communications software. If an application requires behavior beyond the modem’s supported features, configuration changes alone may not be enough.
This creates a development gap. AI software can evolve quickly, while adapting the wireless device may require changes to its signal processing, radio hardware, and system design, followed by extensive testing. SDR helps bridge this gap by giving developers more control over communications through software within the capabilities of the hardware.
Making wireless adaptable with SDR
3GPP standards define capabilities for various communications needs, including low-latency services, high data throughput, direct device-to-device (D2D) links, and non-terrestrial connectivity. A product must implement and integrate the relevant capabilities; their inclusion in a standard does not make them available on every platform due to business and use case constraints.
SDR implements key radio functions in programmable processing resources in software running on CPUs, DSPs, vector engines, or GPUs, supported by FPGAs and dedicated ASIC accelerators. Developers can configure and optimize those functions within the capabilities of the hardware and the requirements of the standards.
For example, a robot may need low latency when coordinating movement, more uplink capacity when uploading inspection images, and direct links when exchanging information with nearby robots. Supporting these changing needs requires an integrated software framework that manages the available communications features and resources.
Communications software IP supplies the algorithms, protocol implementation, and hardware integration that make this practical. Standards establish interoperable behavior; implementation choices influence the resources needed to deliver it. Reusable and validated software gives developers a starting point for product engineering and reduces the amount they must build themselves.
Using radio measurements to inform decisions
A programmable radio can also provide information about the conditions in which it operates. Link quality and interference measurements help explain whether a connection can support the application. With suitable hardware, signal processing, and system support, radio signals can also contribute to positioning and sensing.
These functions serve different purposes. Link measurements describe communications conditions; positioning estimates where devices are; sensing may detect movement or changes in the surroundings. Combining them can improve system decisions, but each capability needs its own implementation and validation.
In a network that supports relaying or mesh operation, routing decisions can take account of signal quality, delay, and available capacity. Position and movement information may help anticipate a weakening link. The system can then assess an alternative route before the current connection becomes unusable, where a suitable path exists.
Radio measurements are useful when they lead to an appropriate response. A device might change supported transmission settings, defer a large upload, or report that the requested service cannot be maintained. The response must reflect both the application’s priorities and the options available to the network.
This creates a feedback loop between the physical environment and communications behavior. SDR provides access to relevant measurements and controls; the wider software architecture determines how those inputs affect the application and network.
Connecting AI decisions with communications controls
The next step is to expose this feedback through application interfaces. An AI application can express what information it needs to exchange and its delivery requirements, while the communications software maps those requests to supported controls. This separates application intent from the details of radio implementation.
For example, a robot may request priority for coordination messages or additional capacity for inspection images. The framework can evaluate those requests against current resources, apply supported settings, and report the resulting service. A request for a particular performance level must be checked against what the system can deliver.
Information also flows back to the application. If a link degrades, the robot may reduce its upload rate, process more data locally or reconsider a task that depends on remote information. This makes network conditions part of mission planning rather than an assumption hidden from the application.
Vicinity’s communications software IP and integration expertise provide a foundation for developing these interfaces. The available functions depend on the selected platform and software implementation. Defined controls and tested operating limits help developers connect AI decisions to communications behavior without assuming unrestricted access to every radio function.
Developing both ends of the wireless link
Application interfaces alone cannot resolve every performance constraint. Some requirements depend on coordinated behavior between a terminal and its serving network. Vicinity’s experience across base stations, terminals, and direct D2D communications allows these dependencies to be considered together during system design.
Development begins with the customer’s information requirements and deployment conditions. What must be exchanged, how quickly, and over what coverage area? Which parts of the network can be controlled? The answers guide the choice of processing resources, radio design, and communications features.
Having expertise on both sides of the wireless link is valuable. Improving a terminal can be difficult when its requirements depend on infrastructure behavior that cannot be changed. Similarly, base-station enhancement may have limited value if the connected devices cannot support it. Where a deployment permits control of both ends, coordinated development creates more room to optimize the complete system.
Vicinity combines this system perspective with partners in silicon, baseband, RF, antennas, and core networks. Its work on 5G base stations and terminals, positioning, D2D communications, and non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) spans multiple 3GPP releases. This experience supports the selection and integration of capabilities appropriate to each customer’s product.
From prototype to commercial product
Turning a laboratory prototype into a commercial product requires careful engineering. The device must deliver the required wireless performance within practical limits on power consumption, cost, size, and heat while remaining reliable and easy to maintain.
Meeting these requirements depends on how efficiently the software uses the hardware. Open-source software offers flexibility, but adapting and optimizing it for different platforms can require substantial effort, particularly where processing capacity and power are limited.
Vicinity starts with the customer’s application and practical challenges, then tailors the software and system design around selected hardware platforms. Platform-specific optimization helps achieve the performance and efficiency needed for a viable product. This approach draws on Vicinity’s experience developing and deploying 5G base stations and terminals, including work on positioning, D2D communications, and NTNs across multiple 3GPP releases.
Validation then checks performance under representative operating conditions. Alongside throughput, testing examines latency and its variation, behavior during movement or interference, recovery after interruptions, and operation with multiple devices. Acceptance criteria should follow the application’s needs so that a successful test demonstrates useful performance in the intended setting.
After deployment, regression testing, version control, and careful feature integration support continued development. A receiver improvement may increase processor load, while a scheduling change may affect other traffic. Updates need to be assessed across the system so new capabilities preserve the behavior on which customers already rely.
Differentiations and ownership
This engineering foundation gives customers scope to build products around their own application expertise. They can integrate distinctive features, tailor supported wireless behavior, and develop system designs for particular operating environments. Differentiation comes from how these capabilities serve the customer’s market.
Customers retain ownership of their commercial products and control over their product roadmap. Access to and rights to modify the underlying communications software depend on the agreed licensing arrangement. Making that distinction clear helps align the development model with the customer’s plans for future changes and support.
Vicinity provides the communications IP and engineering support on which customers can build. Reusing that foundation supports a path to manufacturing and deployment at scale while leaving customers room to develop their own features and application value. The architecture and support model must also accommodate the intended product lifetime.
Connecting the next wave of AI
As AI moves further into the physical world, its value increasingly depends on timely information and reliable interaction with the systems around it. Robots, sensors, and autonomous devices need communications that support the conditions in which they operate, from factory floors to remote locations.
SDR helps meet this need by making wireless capabilities adaptable. Developers can tailor connectivity to their applications and evolve it as requirements change. Vicinity provides the communications software IP and platform expertise to turn that flexibility into commercial products.
Vicinity invites hardware partners, device manufacturers, AI developers, researchers, and system integrators to join its ecosystem. Partners can contribute platforms, applications, and deployment knowledge, while Vicinity contributes communications software IP and integration expertise.
A practical collaboration starts with a defined use case and measurable operating requirements. Partners can then select the required capabilities, validate them together, and develop a route to commercial production. This gives new physical AI applications a concrete path from an initial idea to products that can be deployed and supported at scale.
