President Trump says Apple’s Tim Cook is the only man to replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO — proposes ’A ‘legend replaces a legend’ in call for Apple’s executive chairman of its board
"There is only one man to take his place"
President Donald Trump has said that retired Apple CEO Tim Cook should replace Jensen Huang as the CEO of Nvidia, just hours after it was announced that the latter had resigned in the wake of a series of scandals. Taking to his Truth Social platform, the President said, "NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend! President DONALD J. TRUMP."
Nvidia's board of directors announced on Wednesday that Huang had resigned following the revelation that he conducted an extramarital affair with a Megaspeed executive suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset, and a further affair with Nvidia Vice President of Health Care, Kimberly Powell.
Colette Kress, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, will serve as Interim CEO while the company looks for a replacement. Naturally, names have been floated as potential successor candidates, including Apple's Chief Hardware Officer Johny Srouji.
With Nvidia at the center of the global explosion in AI, Huang and Trump have enjoyed a close relationship that routinely makes news headlines. Trump previously described Huang as 'utterly visionary' in regard to his views on tariffs and rescinding President Biden's AI Diffusion Rule.
President Trump's name has been mentioned in the ongoing Huang affair scandal. Notably, it is alleged that while U.S. intelligence believed that Huang had been the target of a Chinese honeypot operation, reports claim that President Trump was briefed on the matter but chose not to do anything with the information, so as not to affect Nvidia's sales or antagonize China.
Congress has summoned Jensen Huang to appear before the Select Committee on the CCP, with lawmakers threatening to issue Huang with a subpoena if he doesn't agree to attend a closed-door meeting voluntarily.
Tim Cook is currently the Executive Chair of Apple's board, having served as the company's CEO from 2011 to 2026. During his tenure, he oversaw the launch of a plethora of Apple services, including Apple Music and Apple TV, while expanding into new product categories such as Apple Watch and AirPods.

articles.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO: founder accused of multiple affairs, including with a Chinese spy
articles.text:
Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO: founder accused of multiple affairs, including with a Chinese spy
Move comes after extramarital affairs were made public
Nvidia’s Jensen Huang has resigned from the company, following accusations of the CEO having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, and subsequent details of a second alleged affair emerging.
The Board of Directors announced that the resignation is effective immediately, and that Colette Kress, who is currently Chief Financial Officer of Nvidia, will be the interim CEO.
In a press statement, Nvidia said: “Kress will continue to serve as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer while serving as Interim Chief Executive Officer until a permanent successor has been named.”
The board also said that a search for a new permanent CEO has begun, and that the successor to Huang could be either an internal appointment, or an external candidate could get the job.
Because of the importance of both Huang and Nvidia in the tech industry, there could be a lot of fallout from this, so we'll be keeping this story updated live as more information and and reaction to this news emerges.
Won't somebody think of the gamers?
There's been a lot of focus on the AI impact of Huang's departure, but what will it mean for gaming fans who've felt let down by Nvidia's focus on other areas more recently? It may not be good news, as our report Darren Allen explains.
Opinions from a noted analyst
Ming-Chi Kuo is a famous tech analyst, with great connections inside the supply side of the industry. He's laid out his opinion on what the initial takeaway should be from the market — though it sounds like Elizabeth Warren may disagree on his first point, because she certainly doesn't think Huang cutting ties with Nvidia should mean Nvidia remaining executives can breathe easy now…
Resigning may not be the end of the battle for Huang
US Senator Elizabeth Warren has laid out a clear message that she wants to investigate further what kind of information may have been compromised from Jensen Huang's relationships. It may not be a comfortable few months for Huang on many fronts…
Jensen Huang’s decision to resign from NVIDIA does not absolve him, other executives, or the company as a whole of responsibility for putting our national security at risk or for any potential violations of our laws. They still owe Congress answers.
— @warren.senate.gov (@warren.senate.gov.bsky.social) 2026-11-12T16:19:51.546Z
US President Donald Trump has just weighed in with his suggestion for Nvidia CEO:
What is going on with the GPU side of Nvidia? We have just reported that the Nvidia RTX 5080 Super GPU is rumored to have been canned, presumably due to high memory costs. This is a big blow to anyone hoping Nvidia would release new, sensibly priced, gaming GPUs any time soon.
I'm not sure if those tweets are embedding properly, but the last one was from Elon Musk being rather gleeful at the idea that he could hire Jensen Huang.
Well, it seems like Jensen Huang won't have much of a problem finding a new job after this.
Here is Colette Kress' apparent message to staff today:
Colette Kress will continue to serve as chief financial officer while also being interim CEO. There's a possibility she will be chosen as a full-time replacement, depending on how she copes with the next few challenging weeks.
Many PC gamers, including myself, will be hoping that whoever the new CEO of Nvidia is, they'll continue to make gaming GPUs. Whilst Nvidia made its name with graphics cards, the incredible success of its AI hardware has meant that the gaming division sometimes felt like an afterthought. There's a fear that any new CEO could double down on AI and further neglect Nvidia's gaming roots.
As for who comes next, because Huang was so integral to Nvidia, there hasn't been any real speculation until now who would take over from him.
As the company explains in its statement:
"Colette Kress, current Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of NVIDIA, has agreed to serve as Interim Chief Executive Officer. Kress will continue to serve as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer while serving as Interim Chief Executive Officer until a permanent successor has been named. The Board is initiating a search for a permanent Chief Executive Officer and will consider internal and external candidates."
Huang has been married to his wife Lori since 1985, so his admission of an affair was a shock, so when there were reports that he had been having a second extra marital affair, this time with someone working at Nvidia, it quickly became apparent that Huang's position was no longer tenable.
Even so, the suddenness of his removal has also been shocking. Nvidia's board of directors issued a statement saying: “Jensen’s contributions to Nvidia are profound. Nvidia is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry."
US intelligence has been watching Alice Huang, and accused her of being a Chinese intelligence asset. The information behind this accusation is confidential, but it has added an extra layer of drama and betrayal to this whole saga.
After this disclosure, Nvidia's valuation plummeted by $430bn, and the company appointed an external law firm, Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct a “thorough and independent” investigation.
Still, Jensen Huang is such an important and integral part of Nvidia and its success that it was still difficult to imagine him not being CEO.
This whole debacle started when Huang admitted that he had formed a "close relationship" with Alice Huang, who was once an executive of Megaspeed, a Singaporean company that is a customer of Nvidia. 
In a message to his then-employees, Jensen Huang wrote that "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children."
But this was just the start.
Outside of Apple's CEOs and AI leaders, Jensen Huang was arguably the most recognisable tech CEO. In his trademark black leather jacket, he successfully made Nvidia the dominant player in consumer gaming graphics cards, before pivoting to AI chip powerhouse.
This made Nvidia one of the most successful companies in the world, so the importance of this dramatic fall from grace really can't be understated.
For some background about what's led to this, check out our article by Lance Ulanoff on why this is more than just a tech soap opera.

articles.title: Harari Warns Tech Leaders Against Pursuing AI Superintelligence - EE Times
articles.text:
BARCELONA, Spain — Addressing corporate technology executives at the Gartner IT Symposium/Xpo, historian and philosopher Yuval Noah Harari warned that the tech industry’s race to create artificial superintelligence is a historic market failure driven by ideological fantasy rather than economic rationality.
In an onstage conversation with John Thornhill, editor of The Financial Times, Harari argued that treating autonomous software as a mere tool fatally misjudges its nature.
Urging CIOs and policymakers to halt the pursuit of uncontrollable digital gods, he called for redirecting capital and research away from general superintelligence and toward narrow, verifiable systems that address tangible problems.
Emergence of the digital agents
When asked whether AI represents a rupture comparable to fire, the printing press, electricity, or computing, Harari pointed to agents: “AI is the first technology which is an agent,” he said. While the use of fire and nuclear power depends on human intent, artificial intelligence acts independently. “It’s your decision whether to use fire to cook your meal or to burn a forest. It’s not a fire’s decision. AI is different because it can make decisions on its own. It can invent new ideas on its own. It can invent the next technology on its own. The printing press could not invent the radio. AI can invent better AI.”
Viewing AI systems as tools is an error: “It’s better to think about them as animals, or creatures, or aliens to really understand. This is not something in our hands. This is something in our relationship with us,” Harari said. When Thornhill asked whether autonomous agents could remain subservient, he replied: “Not if they are far more intelligent than us.”
That dynamic exposes an unresolvable commercial fallacy. “The first question: Will it be far more intelligent than us? And the industry bets it will,” Harari said. “The second question is: Do you know how to keep far more intelligent entities under your control? And the answer is obviously no,” and added: “If you create gods with the assumption that they will be your slaves and you can use them to do what you want, you don’t understand what gods mean.”
Addressing researchers who view superintelligence as an evolutionary upgrade, Harari separated intelligence from consciousness: “There is zero love and zero beauty, also zero pain and zero sadness,” he said. “It’s a completely dark universe, and there is no value in that kind of civilization.”
AI is a bureaucratic native
Turning to societal consequences, Harari argued that AI targets civilization’s bureaucratic operating system: “Bureaucracy is the underappreciated hero of history,” he said, noting that institutions generate trust through language. Software has now entered that realm: “AIs are bureaucratic natives. For us, bureaucracy is alien, strange, or foreign because we are millions of years older than it. We were born in the forest, and bureaucracy came along late in human evolution,” he said. “AIs are bureaucratic natives. They’re all born in the office, not in the forest, and they’re poised to take over all the bureaucratic systems of the world, from finance to religion.”
Rather than an accident, Harari identified human displacement as the primary danger: “Everything goes right, and the AI simply creates a new world which is way beyond the human ability to understand. Humanity will face a situation of collective dementia. Once upon a time, you were the most intelligent, capable, powerful agent around, and you understood and controlled everything in your own life, and then things changed, and you’re left behind.”
Harari expressed disbelief that markets are bankrolling their own demise: “The market is supposed to be rational. Nobody can calculate what would be the return on investment on creating gods.” Pointing to Elon Musk’s prediction that money could vanish within a decade, and prospectuses admitting existential risk, Harari characterized the race as an ideological crusade rather than a rational business enterprise.
Dumb refrigerators and European sovereignty
Addressing immediate dilemmas facing corporate executives and citizens, Harari cautioned against fragile complexity: “Stupid refrigerators are much better than smart refrigerators,” he said, referring to recent hacks on supermarket fridges. “It’s like a chain with a hundred links. If just one link is not secure, everything crashes.”
When integrating software agents into operations, Harari advised executives to think sociologically: “We cannot think about them as tools. We need to think about them as agents, as entities. We are bringing new kinds of immigrants into our societies—not human immigrants, but digital immigrants. They are likely to have their own goals, their own way of doing things, increasingly their own tribes, their own networks of cooperation.”
For Europe, technological dependency represents a loss of sovereignty: “If you are a citizen of a country whose entire infrastructure, from hospitals and airports to the army, is based on AI technology that comes from across the ocean and that can be shut down at the press of a button, you are no longer sovereign,” Harari said.
He outlined three strategic paths: accept vassal status to the U.S. or China; build independent national systems costing over €500 billion (~$554 billion); or establish shared European infrastructure through deeper federalization.
He said that the third option would be the best, but he warned that “Option number one is the trajectory in which Europe is going at present. And if you look at the issues that dominate politics in countries such as Spain, Germany, and the U.K., it’s clear that this is at present the direction,” he said, arguing that, being more preoccupied with human migration, Europe is sleepwalking into vassalage by ignoring digital immigration.
Call for limited AI and human collaboration
In his final recommendations, Harari urged CIOs to reject general superintelligence and focus on bounded applications: “I’m not talking about stopping all research in AI. It’s just directing it in other directions,” he said. “First of all, invest far more in safety, and secondly, don’t race to superintelligence. Focus on creating limited intelligence and deploying it here and now for beneficial results, whether in healthcare, transport, or ecology.”
Harari highlighted a psychological paradox: Developers justify racing ahead because they distrust human rivals, yet trust alien software. “With humans, at least we have thousands of years of experience. We know they can manipulate and cheat, and lie, but we also have substantial experience in how to overcome this and create robust systems of cooperation,” Harari said. “AIs already know that they can cheat and manipulate and lie, and we have almost no experience with how to build large-scale, robust systems of cooperation.”
Because complex general systems cannot be evaluated in a laboratory before deployment, Harari concluded that deliberate restraint is humanity’s most urgent safeguard.
In conclusion, Harari reiterated the need to buy time to ensure technology serves human welfare. In navigating that future, Harari maintained that preserving human agency is not an abstract ideal, but the essential condition for survival.

articles.title: Merak Capital leads $1.3 million investment in Saudi gaming startup Lambda Studios
articles.text:
Merak Capital leads $1.3 million investment in Saudi gaming startup Lambda Studios
- Saudi gaming startup Lambda Studios has raised $1.3 million in a funding round led by Merak Capital, a Riyadh-based investment firm. The round's stage and other participating investors were not disclosed.
- Founded in 2024 by Sari and Firas AlSaedi, Lambda Studios develops and publishes video games. The business originated as a project the founders started in Makkah nearly a decade before formally establishing the company.
- The studio initially developed games for Roblox, where it has reached millions of players, according to Merak Capital. It is now expanding to other gaming platforms, including Steam, to reach new audiences with its own intellectual property.
- The investment will support Lambda Studios' expansion beyond Roblox. It follows Merak Capital's $1 million investment in Floaty Studio in July 2026 and its participation in a $1.45 million round for Majestic Mind Games in August.
Press release:
Saudi gaming startup Lambda Studios has raised $1.3 million in a funding round led by Merak Capital, as it seeks to expand its game development and publishing operations beyond Roblox to additional platforms, including Steam.
Founded in 2024 by Sari and Firas AlSaedi, Lambda Studios began as a personal project nearly a decade ago in Makkah before evolving into a game development and publishing business.
The company initially focused on Roblox, where its games have attracted millions of players, according to Merak Capital. It is now looking to extend its reach to new platforms and audiences while retaining ownership of its intellectual property.
The new funding will support the studio's expansion across gaming platforms, including Steam, as it works to bring its games to a broader international audience.
Merak Capital said its investment was driven by Lambda Studios' ownership of its intellectual property and its approach to growth, which the firm believes will help the studio replicate its success across different gaming platforms.
The deal follows a series of investments by Merak Capital in Saudi gaming startups. In July 2026, the firm invested $1 million in Floaty Studio through its Merak Gaming Fund. It subsequently co-led a $1.45 million funding round in Majestic Mind Games alongside Impact46 in August.
The latest investment adds to Merak Capital's portfolio of Saudi gaming companies developing original intellectual property for international markets.

articles.title: Delhivery partners with Tata Motors, Euler Motors, Montra Electric to deploy up to 2,000 electric commercial vehicles
articles.text:
Delhivery partners with Tata Motors, Euler Motors, Montra Electric to deploy up to 2,000 electric commercial vehicles
The pacts are part of the company's plan to put close to 5,000 EVs into operation within three years.
Delhivery has partnered with Tata Motors, Euler Motors and Montra Electric to deploy 1,500-2,000 four-wheeler electric commercial vehicles (eCVs) across its intra-city logistics network over the next 12-18 months.
The pacts with the three EV manufacturers are part of Delhivery's plan to put close to 5,000 eCVs into operation within three years.
The tie-up with Tata Motors will include the Tata Intra EV. Euler Motors' Turbo City Plus will be the first vehicle to be deployed, serving smaller commercial applications. Larger electric vehicles will join the fleet later for heavier-payload operations, Delhivery said, adding that the collaboration with Montra Electric aims to expand EVIATOR deployment nationwide.
The EV push targets its intra-city fleet of vehicles running under 200 km a day, a segment where EVs now compete with diesel on total cost of ownership, Delhivery said.
The electric fleet deployment will span multiple small commercial vehicle segments, beginning with products for urban deliveries and scaling up to higher-capacity electric commercial vehicles for operations requiring larger payload capacity, the company said.
EVs currently account for up to 12-13% of Delhivery's eligible intra-city fleet, and the company aims to raise this to 50% in the next two to three years. It is also looking to fully electrify its sub-200 km fleet in four to five years on the back of investments in advance payments for vendors and in charging and parking infrastructure, it said.
"Partnering with Tata Motors, Euler Motors and Montra Electric lets us expand our electric fleet across vehicle categories. The charging facilities we are piloting will make EV adoption easier and more affordable for our vendor partners," said Prashant Gazipur, Chief Operating Officer, In City Operations, Delhivery.
The company said it is also piloting charging infrastructure at its facilities, starting with Delhi-NCR, with low-cost charging and free parking for vendor partners to encourage wider EV adoption.

articles.title: Nvidia sans Jensen Huang : qui pourrait remplacer l’illustre PDG ?
articles.text:
Jensen Huang, dorénavant ex-PDG de Nvidia, a avoué avoir entretenu une relation extraconjugale avec Alice Huang, dirigeante de l’entreprise singapourienne Megaspeed. Le problème : celle-ci est soupçonnée par Washington d’être une espionne au service de la Chine. Depuis cette révélation, Trump a défendu Jensen Huang, Pékin a démenti et le FBI a ouvert une enquête.
Mais la situation s’est encore empirée avec une nouvelle information : le dirigeant de Nvidia aurait entretenu une autre relation, cette fois-ci avec une salariée de l’entreprise. Le conseil d’administration de Nvidia a tenu une réunion ce jeudi 12 novembre pour décider du sort du PDG de Nvidia, mais c’est finalement Jensen Huang lui même qui a remis sa démission, avec effet immédiat. Colette Kress, la directrice financière de Nvidia, assurera la direction de l’entreprise jusqu’à la nomination d’un successeur permanent. Bloomberg affirme de son côté que Nvidia a fait appel à une entreprise externe pour identifier des candidats au poste de PDG. Mais qui cela pourrait-il être ?
Qui pourrait remplacer Jensen Huang au poste de PDG de Nvidia ?
La première hypothèse, sans doute la plus probable, serait que Nvidia choisisse un successeur parmi ses propres dirigeants, déjà en poste au sein de l’entreprise. Colette Kress, directrice financière de NVIDIA depuis 2013 et actuellement chargée de diriger l’entreprise, pourrait être définitivement nommée à ce poste. D’autres candidats sont également considérés : Ian Buck (ingénieur et spécialiste de l’IA chez Nvidia depuis 2004), Michael Kagan (directeur technique de NVIDIA) ou encore Bryan Catanzaro (vice-président de la recherche en deep learning appliqué).
Seconde hypothèse : Nvidia pourrait faire appel à une personnalité extérieure à l’entreprise pour succéder à Jensen Huang. Dans ce cas-ci, les possibilités sont multiples. Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, expert en gouvernance d’entreprise et doyen associé principal des études sur le leadership à la Yale School of Management, estime que Nvidia pourrait faire appel à nul autre que Tim Cook, qui a cédé sa place de PDG d’Apple en septembre dernier à John Ternus. Pour rappel, Tim Cook avait succédé à Steve Jobs, soit le fondateur d’Apple. Dans l’hypothèse où il deviendrait CEO de Nvidia, il succéderait donc à Jensen Huang, cofondateur de Nvidia.
D’autres noms, externes à Nvidia, sont également évoqués : Eric Schmidt (ancien CEO de Google), Lisa Su (CEO d’AMD soit le principal concurrent de Nvidia) Lip-Bu Tan (PDG d’Intel) ou encore Bret Taylor (président du conseil d’administration d’OpenAI).
Elon Musk est prêt à embaucher Jensen Huang
Elon Musk semble d’ores et déjà prêt à embaucher le dorénavant ex-dirigeant de Nvidia. En effet, un utilisateur de X a demandé à Elon Musk d’embaucher Jensen Huang, ce à quoi il a répondu : « Ce serait un honneur ». Il reste maintenant à voir ce que décidera Jensen Huang, même s’il risque de se faire discret pendant un petit moment.
De son côté, Tim Sweeney, fondateur et PDG d’Epic Games, ne doit pas bien accueillir la démission de Jensen Huang. Sur le réseau social X, il avait indiqué : « Sauvez Jensen. Ce serait, de la part du conseil d’administration de NVIDIA, un niveau de stupidité comparable à celui d’Apple lorsqu’il a licencié Steve Jobs, et cela porterait gravement atteinte aux intérêts des États-Unis ». Jensen Huang n’aura finalement pas été sauvé, la situation étant devenue trop tendue.

articles.title: Nvidia busca al sucesor de Jensen Huang y Tim Cook figura entre los candidatos al puesto
articles.text:
La salida de Jensen Huang de la dirección de Nvidia abrió una carrera para encontrar al próximo ejecutivo que estará al frente de una de las compañías más importantes de la industria tecnológica. Aunque Colette Kress, actual directora financiera, asumió el cargo de CEO interina, la junta directiva anunció que evaluará candidatos internos y externos para elegir a quien ocupará el puesto de manera permanente.
Entre los nombres que comenzaron a circular aparecen Ian Buck, uno de los principales responsables del desarrollo tecnológico de Nvidia; Rene Haas, director ejecutivo de Arm; y Tim Cook, presidente ejecutivo de la junta directiva de Apple. Sin embargo, no todos tienen las mismas posibilidades ni existen confirmaciones de que hayan recibido una propuesta formal.
La renuncia de Huang se produjo el 12 de noviembre de 2026, después de las investigaciones y los reportes sobre sus relaciones extramatrimoniales. La salida del empresario provocó una fuerte reacción en los mercados: las acciones de Nvidia registraron una caída superior al 13% durante la apertura de la jornada, con una pérdida de valor bursátil que superó los 500.000 millones de dólares, según los reportes citados por Reuters.
Colette Kress e Ian Buck, los candidatos internos de Nvidia
La primera alternativa de Nvidia es mantener el liderazgo dentro de la propia compañía. Colette Kress asumió temporalmente la dirección ejecutiva mientras continúa como directora financiera, cargo que ocupa desde 2013. Antes de llegar a Nvidia trabajó en Microsoft, Cisco y Texas Instruments.
Su experiencia financiera y su participación en las presentaciones trimestrales de resultados la convierten en una figura conocida para los inversores. Josh Gilbert, analista de eToro, señaló a Reuters que Kress es una opción adecuada para garantizar la estabilidad de la empresa durante la transición.
Sin embargo, su nombramiento permanente no está asegurado. Algunos analistas consideran que Nvidia podría preferir a un perfil con experiencia directa en ingeniería y desarrollo de productos, debido a que su principal ventaja competitiva está relacionada con la tecnología de sus procesadores.
En ese escenario aparece Ian Buck, vicepresidente de Nvidia y uno de los responsables del desarrollo de CUDA, la plataforma de software que permite aprovechar la capacidad de procesamiento de sus chips. Buck ingresó a la empresa en 2004 y actualmente dirige productos de inteligencia artificial para centros de datos de gran escala.
Shay Boloor, estratega de Futurum Equities, lo considera uno de los candidatos internos más fuertes por su participación en el desarrollo tecnológico de Nvidia. Reuters también recogió la posibilidad de que la compañía opte por una estructura de codirección, con Kress a cargo de las finanzas y Buck enfocado en los productos y la tecnología.
Rene Haas, el candidato externo que conoce Nvidia
Si la junta directiva decide buscar fuera de la empresa, uno de los nombres que aparece con mayor fuerza es Rene Haas, director ejecutivo de Arm.
Haas tiene experiencia en la industria de los semiconductores y anteriormente trabajó en Nvidia. Su conocimiento de ambas compañías podría facilitar una transición hacia la dirección del fabricante de chips, según los analistas consultados por Reuters.
Un banquero especializado en operaciones del sector de semiconductores señaló a la agencia que Haas tendría sentido como candidato por su experiencia y conocimiento de la industria. No obstante, su eventual llegada también plantearía interrogantes, debido a las diferencias entre los modelos de negocio de Arm y Nvidia.
Tim Cook y otros nombres que suenan para dirigir Nvidia
Entre las opciones mencionadas por distintos medios también aparece Tim Cook, actual presidente ejecutivo de la junta directiva de Apple. Su nombre fue planteado por la estratega de inversiones Jun Bei Liu, de Ten Cap, quien destacó su experiencia en cadenas de suministro y gestión de operaciones globales.
Sin embargo, se trata de una posibilidad especulativa. No hay información que confirme que Cook esté interesado en abandonar Apple para dirigir Nvidia. Además, su experiencia está más vinculada a la gestión empresarial y la cadena de suministro que al desarrollo de procesadores para inteligencia artificial.
TechCrunch también mencionó a Bret Taylor, fundador de la empresa de inteligencia artificial Sierra y expresidente de la junta directiva de OpenAI. Su trayectoria incluye cargos en Salesforce, Google, Facebook y Twitter.
Otro nombre es Eric Schmidt, antiguo CEO de Google, cuya experiencia en tecnología y gestión empresarial fue planteada por Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, de la Escuela de Administración de Yale. La lista también incluye a Lisa Su, directora ejecutiva de AMD, y Lip-Bu Tan, CEO de Intel, aunque TechCrunch considera poco probable que abandonen sus actuales compañías.
A ellos se suman Andrew Bell, vicepresidente sénior de ingeniería de hardware de Nvidia, y Jeff Fisher, ejecutivo con más de tres décadas en la empresa.
Cuándo se conocerá al nuevo CEO de Nvidia
Por ahora, Nvidia no anunció quién reemplazará definitivamente a Jensen Huang. La junta directiva deberá evaluar las alternativas y decidir si mantiene el liderazgo dentro de la compañía o incorpora a un ejecutivo externo.
El próximo martes 17 de noviembre será una fecha relevante para la transición: Nvidia tiene previsto presentar sus resultados del tercer trimestre, en una reunión que estará encabezada por Colette Kress.
Hasta entonces, los nombres de posibles sucesores seguirán siendo parte de las especulaciones del mercado. Tim Cook figura entre ellos, pero los perfiles de Kress, Buck y Haas aparecen respaldados por referencias más concretas de analistas y fuentes consultadas por Reuters.

articles.title: Verificar el código de Signal era un reto que llevaba años de trabajo de expertos. DeepMind dice que su IA lo ha hecho en un mes
articles.text:
Google DeepMind dice que sus agentes de IA han demostrado matemáticamente que partes clave del código que está detrás del protocolo de cifrado de Signal hacen lo que se supone que deben hacer. El protocolo protege las conversaciones privadas en Signal y Google Messages, y también sustenta el cifrado de WhatsApp, tal y como comparten en Wired. La compañía lo describe como un hito en la seguridad del software, aunque los propios investigadores recalcan que es un paso en un proceso más largo.
Comprobado, el protocolo funciona. La verificación formal significa usar matemáticas, en lugar de pruebas, para demostrar que el software se comporta como se pretende. Se considera la garantía de seguridad más sólida disponible, pero tradicionalmente ha sido lenta y laboriosa. La mayor parte de la verificación de protocolos criptográficos se detiene en la fase de diseño. DeepMind afirma que su sistema ha ido más allá, comprobando la implementación real, que es precisamente donde a menudo se esconden los errores del mundo real.
La compañía dice que es la primera vez que la implementación de un protocolo ampliamente desplegado como este ha sido verificada formalmente por cualquier método, con o sin IA.
Cómo funciona. El sistema se llama AlphaProof Code, un marco que combina varios modelos de IA con expertos humanos. Para ello, investigadores de DeepMind y varios modelos de IA tradujeron los objetivos de seguridad de Signal en especificaciones formales, y expertos humanos revisaron cada una de ellas. Los agentes, impulsados por Gemini Carbon, escribieron las pruebas, generando más de seis millones de líneas de Lean, un lenguaje que permite a un ordenador comprobar las pruebas automáticamente.
Tras ello, los agentes auditaron su propio trabajo y señalaron aproximadamente el 1% de la base de código que necesitaba una segunda revisión por parte de un humano. DeepMind dice que el trabajo llevó cuatro semanas, una tarea que históricamente lleva años a equipos de expertos. Las pruebas cubren propiedades tales como mantener los mensajes protegidos antes y después de que un dispositivo se vea comprometido temporalmente.
¿Detecta realmente errores? El análisis no encontró nuevas vulnerabilidades en las partes de Signal, según comparten desde Wired. Para comprobar si el sistema puede distinguir el buen código del malo, el equipo reintrodujo dos errores reales previamente corregidos en una versión aislada del código de Signal. En ambos casos, dice DeepMind, el sistema produjo una prueba verificada por máquina de que la versión con errores no era segura.
Entre líneas. El proyecto no verificó toda la aplicación móvil de Signal, y Wired señala que DeepMind tenía ventaja gracias a un trabajo previo de verificación formal por parte de la Signal Foundation. Ehren Kret, director de tecnología de Signal, dijo en un comunicado que el trabajo anterior "se centró en porciones más pequeñas del código", mientras que el enfoque de DeepMind "permite una expansión significativa". Añade además que, a medida que crecen las amenazas a la seguridad impulsadas por la IA, la verificación le da a Signal "aún mayor confianza" en sus garantías de privacidad.
Los investigadores también dicen que quieren evitar una configuración en la que la IA escriba tanto los objetivos como las pruebas. "No queremos este tipo de mundo de sensaciones en el que la IA genera los objetivos y la IA genera las pruebas y básicamente toma exámenes que están autoescritos", declaraba a Wired Swarat Chaudhuri, científico investigador de DeepMind. "Hay un término medio". Por ello mismo la parte humana se ha encargado de revisar las especificaciones y las secciones marcadas.
Las preguntas abiertas. Si esto puede escalar, y a qué coste, no está claro. Según Wired, DeepMind ejecutó el análisis de Signal de forma gratuita como un proyecto de investigación, pero no han compartido qué coste tuvo la operación ni si planean un producto de verificación comercial. "Hay un largo trecho por recorrer antes de que podamos escalar esto a todo el software del mundo, y queremos hacerlo", contaba Chaudhuri a Wired.
DeepMind dice que está abriendo el código fuente de sus artefactos de verificación formal para la comunidad, y sugiere que el enfoque podría extenderse eventualmente a sistemas como el firmware de dispositivos médicos y el software de la red eléctrica.

articles.title: Deploy frontier AI models on AWS Trainium with SGLang-Neuron | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Deploy frontier AI models on AWS Trainium with SGLang-Neuron
Today, Amazon announced that SGLang-Neuron is publicly available and can be accessed through an AWS Deep Learning Container, released by RadixArk in collaboration with Annapurna Labs. With SGLang-Neuron, you can serve models and generate reinforcement learning (RL) rollouts with SGLang on AWS Trainium using the same SGLang interface you use today. Trainium is a portfolio of AWS AI chips that delivers strong economics for AI training and inference at scale. Now, running SGLang on Trainium follows the SGLang workflow you already know: you launch models through SGLang’s server interface and invoke the endpoint using the same generation APIs. Underneath that interface, SGLang-Neuron runs on native PyTorch. With its out-of-tree plugin design, Trainium support and SGLang core develop independently and iterate faster.
How SGLang runs on Trainium
SGLang-Neuron is an out-of-tree plugin that connects SGLang with AWS Trainium. Installing the plugin registers the neuron platform through SGLang’s plugin entry points, and setting SGLANG_PLATFORM=neuron selects it when the server starts. SGLang core continues to provide the API server, request lifecycle, RadixAttention, and prefix-cache bookkeeping. The plugin implements the Trainium-specific models, attention, mixture of experts (MoE), and the graph runner.
TorchNeuron registers Trainium as a native PyTorch device. SGLang-Neuron uses standard PyTorch operations for the model execution path and incorporates kernels written with the Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI) for performance. It compiles these operations and kernels into executable programs using torch.compile, which the graph runner prepares and executes during serving.
SGLang-Neuron also supports PD disaggregation. In this configuration, a prefill server computes the prompt KV cache and transfers it to a decode server using NIXL over Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA). The decode server then generates the remaining tokens. Each server still uses SGLang’s scheduler and request lifecycle, while the plugin manages the Trainium execution and KV-cache transfer path.
Serving models on AWS Trainium using SGLang-Neuron
To follow this walkthrough, you use a Trainium3 Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instance with a pytorch-inference-sglang-neuronx container. Here are the steps:
- Start the container.
- Launch the SGLang model server inside the container.
- Send a request to the model server.
For additional information, please see the SGLang-Neuron getting started guide for setup instructions, and explore the repository documentation for supported models, features, and validated configurations.
Conclusion
SGLang-Neuron brings SGLang’s familiar serving workflow to AWS Trainium through native PyTorch. You can get started by launching the SGLang-Neuron container and following the quickstart to serve a supported model. Try it with your workloads, contribute through the project repository, and share feedback to help shape future model and feature support.

articles.title: High-performance computing meets AI: What to expect at SC26 - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
What to expect during SC26: Join theCUBE Nov. 17–19
High-performance computing and artificial intelligence are converging, driven by advances in exascale computing, accelerated systems, data storage and high-speed networking.
The convergence of these technologies is a prime topic for discussion during SC26 in Chicago this month. Major industry players, such as Dell Technologies Inc., Google LLC and Nvidia Corp., have pursued a set of initiatives in the HPC arena, and SC26 will be an occasion to learn more about how AI and HPC workloads are evolving to write supercomputing’s next chapter.
“SC26 provides an important opportunity to examine how the convergence of AI, high-performance computing and application development are reshaping enterprise infrastructure priorities,” said theCUBE Research’s Paul Nashawaty. “Organizations must connect high-performance infrastructure, accessible data and modern application development to move beyond experimentation and accelerate production-ready AI deployments. For Dell and the broader HPC ecosystem, SC26 offers a platform to demonstrate how integrated compute, storage and AI infrastructure can address these challenges.”
TheCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio, will be covering the latest HPC news and announcements from SC26 in Chicago, Nov. 17–19. Coverage will feature on-site reporting and exclusive interviews with industry leaders and analysts as theCUBE explores how supercomputing’s future is being shaped at the intersection of exascale systems and AI infrastructure. Discussion will focus on ways that accelerated computing is transforming research environments, while quantum-HPC integration and agentic AI push scientific discovery toward greater autonomy. (* Disclosure below.)
Quantum and high-performance computing
Dell’s ongoing collaboration with Nvidia and other organizations has yielded several new developments in the HPC arena over the past year, particularly in the area of quantum computing.
The two companies have been working with the U.S. Department of Energy to build and deliver the Doudna supercomputer at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. The system will use Nvidia’s Vera Rubin CPU-GPU platform and Quantum-X800 InfiniBand networking inside Dell’s integrated rack systems and PowerEdge servers to support large-scale scientific computing and data-intensive research.
In September, Dell announced a collaboration with silicon-spin qubit developer Diraq to integrate quantum processing units with HPC and AI server infrastructure. The joint effort is designed to integrate quantum processors with classical computing infrastructure in commercial data centers.
Moves such as these point toward a convergence of AI and quantum technologies, which will likely propel both forward as new platforms are built and deployed.
“The market for high-performance computing is meeting the AI factory at the point of innovation,” said theCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante. “HPC has always led the most challenging data problems, so this trend makes perfect sense. Quantum will be the next big inflection point and we’re seeing that new technologies are often complementary to existing infrastructure. We expect that to be the case between accelerated computing and quantum, particularly in the area of error correction.”
New system architectures drive supercomputing
Hyperscaler Google Cloud is also building systems to support HPC demands for industries like manufacturing, health care and life sciences, weather forecasting and electronic design automation.
At the forefront of Google’s HPC initiative is the H4D VM, the company’s high-performance computing virtual machine. Introduced last year, the H4D VM is powered by fifth-generation AMD EPYC processors and offers whole-node VM performance of more than 12,000 GFLOPS and memory bandwidth exceeding 950 GB/s.
An example of how HPC is making inroads in daily life can be seen in the use of H4D VMs by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. In July, Google Cloud announced that it had been selected as the primary provider of high-performance computing infrastructure for the Weather and Climate Operational Supercomputing System.
The adoption of HPC to enable meteorologists and researchers to develop future forecasting models is an example of how systems technology will play a critical role in both supercomputing and AI infrastructure moving forward.
“Systems are the key in supercomputing advances,” said theCUBE Research’s John Furrier. “Different architectures. Different bets. Same underlying problem: How do you keep the multiplication engines doing useful work instead of waiting for data? That’s why I think the next era of AI infrastructure won’t be defined by the ‘best chip.’ It will be defined by the best system architecture.”
Platforms for cloud and analytics
While the field of HPC is being defined by major players such as Dell and Google, other firms are making contributions as well in areas such as cloud infrastructure and analytics.
Vultr Inc. is building high-performance cloud computing infrastructure for AI, risk management, compliance and fraud prevention. The company is developing its platform across 33 global regions by leveraging CPUs, GPUs and open, composable architectures to position itself as a cloud infrastructure specialist in the agentic AI era.
High-performance computing is also generating a need for consistent data sharing and access across platforms. Omni Analytics Inc. is building a data collaboration solution that can connect directly to cloud data warehouses without needing to preload or duplicate data.
SC26 will offer an opportunity to not only assess the progress of HPC in the enterprise but also examine how AI is continuing to transform the compute stack to generate meaningful business results.
“As organizations invest in increasingly sophisticated AI environments, the competitive differentiator will be the ability to optimize the entire technology stack from data movement and storage performance to application development and deployment,” Nashawaty said. “The central SC26 narrative is that the future of AI supercomputing will be defined not simply by how much compute organizations deploy, but by how effectively they translate that investment into measurable business and scientific outcomes.”
TheCUBE event livestream
Don’t miss theCUBE’s coverage of SC26, Nov. 17–19. Plus, you can access theCUBE’s exclusive content on demand after the event.
How to watch theCUBE interviews
We offer various ways for you to watch theCUBE’s coverage of SC26, including theCUBE’s dedicated website and YouTube channel. You can also get all the coverage from this year’s events on SiliconANGLE.
TheCUBE podcasts
SiliconANGLE’s “theCUBE Pod” is available on Apple Podcasts, Spotify and YouTube, which you can enjoy while on the go. During each podcast, SiliconANGLE’s John Furrier and Dave Vellante discuss the biggest trends in enterprise tech, including AI, cloud, cybersecurity and infrastructure, with context and analysis.
SiliconANGLE also produces our weekly “Breaking Analysis” program, where Vellante examines major developments in enterprise tech, combining insights from theCUBE with spending data from Enterprise Technology Research, available on Apple Podcasts, Spotify and YouTube.
Guests
At SC26, theCUBE will speak with tech leaders and industry analysts about ways that accelerated computing is transforming research environments, while quantum-HPC integration and agentic AI push scientific discovery toward greater autonomy.

articles.title: Synology patches a critical NAS flaw that could let attackers in without logging in
articles.text:
A hot potato: Despite recent controversies over its corporate policies, Synology still holds a large slice of the increasingly popular NAS market. When its devices are hit by dangerous security flaws, customers should take note. Hackers and cyber-criminals certainly will.
A newly published security advisory discloses two serious vulnerabilities in DiskStation Manager (DSM), the Linux-based OS used in Synology NAS products, one of them rated critical. The storage maker warned that the flaws could be abused to remotely access and attack vulnerable devices, giving cyber-criminals – or rogue AI agents, for that matter – an easy avenue to wreak havoc on users' data and local IT infrastructure.
Synology rates the SQL injection flaw "critical," with a 9.8 out of 10 score – the flaw could be abused to remotely access and attack vulnerable devices.
The advisory focuses on two vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-76954 and CVE-2026-85101. The first is an SQL injection bug in DSM's Auth API that lets remote attackers read or write arbitrary files, or carry out denial-of-service (DoS) attacks.
The second was found in DSM's rsync tool and could let attackers bypass authentication entirely to read specific files, write arbitrary files, or launch "limited" DoS attacks.
Synology rates the SQL injection flaw "critical," with a 9.8 out of 10 score in the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS). The rsync bug is classed as "important," with an 8.6 base CVSS score. Both can be exploited remotely, without logging in, to attack vulnerable devices. Synology disclosed them roughly a month after releasing the DSM updates that fix them, a common practice that gives users time to patch before the details go public.
The NAS maker shipped the fixed DSM versions in October 2026, and the company now considers the issue "resolved." Users with automatic updates may already have the patch, but those on manual update policies should definitely check for new DSM releases. Fixes are available for DSM 7.4, 7.3, 7.2.2, and 7.2.1.
Synology credited external researchers from Viettel Cyber Security and Aytio with discovering and reporting the two flaws. Some users are calling the SQL injection bug in the login process an embarrassment for Synology's software stack, while others are touting their "satisfaction" at having replaced Synology's devices with competing NAS products.
The Taiwanese manufacturer was also criticized for forcing customers to use only "certified" hard disk drives in its NAS systems. The backlash grew so intense that Synology was ultimately forced to reverse course and let users install any HDD brand and model they wanted.

articles.title: Ars Live: What drone attacks on data centers mean for modern life in the cloud
articles.text:
Drone and missile strikes have inflicted unprecedented damage on data centers in Eastern Europe and the Middle East this year, disrupting cloud services for millions of people and permanently deleting some Amazon Web Services customer data. This trend represents a new concern for Big Tech companies—but also for governments and everyone else who depends on common digital services in modern life.
To explore what this all means for modern society’s reliance on cloud resilience, I will be hosting a live conversation titled “Drone attacks and data centers: New Risks for Big Tech” on Tuesday, November 17 at 1 pm ET with Joseph Jarnecki, a senior research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), a UK defense and security think tank. He leads RUSI’s work on how cloud services factor into national security and defense, along with tech sovereignty efforts.
Jarnecki has done extensive research on how Ukraine strengthened its cloud resilience with Western partners despite facing both cyberattacks and kinetic attacks at the start of the full-scale Russian invasion, and explored what that means for NATO and European governments’ cloud adoption plans.
This year, Jarnecki has written about Iran’s drone and missile strikes on Amazon data centers in the Middle East during the US-Israeli war with Iran, and the broader implications for governments and Big Tech. He has also commented on the impacts of Russia and Ukraine exchanging strikes on each other’s data centers.

articles.title: Democrats launch Nvidia investigation, write scathing letter on Huang's 'scheme' with Trump | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Democrats on Thursday opened an inquiry into how the Trump administration handled Nvidia’s chip sales to China. Earlier on Thursday, the company ousted its CEO Jensen Huang. He also agreed to testify to a different set of Republican-led Congressional committees.
Huang was removed from the company he founded after he confessed to an extramarital affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy. (He has since been accused of having more affairs, with Nvidia employees.)
The alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang, was an executive of Nvidia customer Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that U.S. officials suspect of helping route advanced Nvidia chips into China. The Democratic inquiry comes from Rep. Richard Neal (D-Mass.), the top Democrat on the House Ways and Means Committee, and Sen. Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), the top Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee. As the minority party, they can ask questions but can’t compel answers.
Their humdinger of a letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick asks the department to preserve records about an arrangement they find questionable and, they allege, illegal.
“The scheme worked like this,” as the letter describes it. President Trump agreed to sales of Nvidia’s H200 chips to China as long as the chips, manufactured by Taiwan, were first shipped to the United States. On arriving, Trump added a tariff “effectively taking a cut of Nvidia’s sales to China through what appears to be an unconstitutional export tax system,” the letter said. Then the Commerce Department, under Lutnick, issued an export license.
By the way, the deal between Trump and Nvidia to share revenue was public. In August 2025, Nvidia and AMD both agreed to share 15% of their revenue from chip sales to China with the U.S. government as part of a deal to secure export licenses, the AP reported at the time.
But the letter questions why Lutnick continued to allow Megaspeed to buy chips even after he was reportedly informed by U.S. intelligence of their suspicions of Alice Huang and of Jensen Huang’s relationship with her. It questions why the department reportedly green-lit other Asian companies to buy Nvidia chips “with no physical presence at their listed addresses.” So the inquiry is aimed at the administration, not just at Nvidia and Huang.
The letter also questions how Nvidia’s donations to Trump’s projects factored in. It notes that the export deal was approved after Trump learned of “Mr. Huang’s compromised position” in sleeping with an alleged spy, and after Nvidia donated $26 million toward Trump’s projects, including the ballroom. It appears to be asking if Trump used his knowledge of the affair to secure donations from Nvidia.
Interestingly, in a “60 Minutes” interview with President Trump that aired on Sunday, Trump mentioned how he and his team had threatened an unnamed AI exec with jail, and after that, the exec “totally changed.”
This Congressional investigation into Nvidia’s China sales and its dealings with Trump is the second one, so far, since news of the alleged spy affair broke. The Republican-led group involves leaders from the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, and the House Intelligence Committee. That group has demanded that Huang come to them and testify in a closed-door session. They had threatened to subpoena him if he didn’t voluntarily agree. On Thursday, after his resignation, he agreed.

articles.title: Militarisation de l’espace : l’armée US veut déployer une constellation de satellites autour de la Lune
articles.text:
L’armée américaine veut placer des satellites militaires en orbite autour de la Lune. Ce premier pas, encore discret, montre à quel point l’espace est devenu un terrain stratégique.
Car ces dernières semaines, l’enjeu du spatial militaire s’est clairement matérialisé. Notamment avec le satellite russe Kosmos 2612 qui s’est approché d’ICEYE-X36, un satellite d’observation, lors d’une manœuvre très curieuse. Et le secteur s’y prépare, avec des startups qui se lancent dans le développement de technologies spécifiquement dédiées à la défense en orbite. Il n’est donc pas étonnant que le Pentagone accélère dans ce sens.
Un premier pas vers une flotte militaire autour de la Lune
Ce 2 novembre, l’ARMée américaine a publié une demande d’informations destinée aux industriels concernant un » Cislunar Space System ». Il s’agit d’un ensemble de cinq satellites au maximum, à déployer dans l’espace cislunaire, c’est-à-dire la région qui entoure la Lune. Elle vise une mise en service d’ici à la fin de 2029.
Si le document ne précise pas encore la mission de ces engins, il détaille en revanche ce que le Pentagone attend des entreprises : fournir les satellites, y intégrer la charge utile confiée par l’État, assurer le lancement, puis piloter l’ensemble depuis le sol. Surtout, l’ARMée réclame une solution rapide et à faible risque, sans développements coûteux.
Autre fait notable : ces dispositifs serviraient de » véhicules de départ « pour préparer une constellation bien plus vaste. Mais l’ARMée prévoit d’abord d’attribuer jusqu’à cinq contrats d’études à prix fixe pour choisir, ou non, un partenaire industriel.
L’ARMée ne veut pas rester spectatrice face à la Chine
Plusieurs usages sont envisageables : suivre les objets présents autour de la Lune, assurer la navigation et les communications, ou encore surveiller l’activité d’autres pays. À noter qu’aujourd’hui, les satellites américains les plus lointains restent en orbite géostationnaire, à 36 000 kilomètres de la Terre.
Car le Pentagone a déjà accéléré sur l’exploitation de notre satellite. La mission Oracle-M doit par exemple décoller à la mi-2027 pour expérimenter des techniques de suivi d’objets dans l’espace cislunaire. Oracle-Prime devrait suivre d’ici la fin de l’année prochaine et surveiller satellites et débris depuis un point d’équilibre gravitationnel, situé aux trois quarts du chemin vers la Lune.
Un intérêt qui s’explique aussi par la course à la Lune entre Washington et Pékin. Le général Stephen Purdy, chargé des programmes avancés de la Space Force, rapporte que les plus hauts responsables du Pentagone parlent désormais publiquement d’un « domaine de combat ». Ambiance.
L’espace cislunaire désigne la zone d’influence entre la Terre et la Lune, incluant les trajectoires et orbites autour de la Lune. On y trouve des distances et des contraintes bien supérieures à l’orbite terrestre (basse, moyenne ou géostationnaire), avec des temps de trajet radio plus longs et des fenêtres de manœuvre plus limitées. La dynamique orbitale y est dominée par l’interaction gravitationnelle Terre-Lune, ce qui impose des plans de vol plus complexes que “tourner autour de la Terre”. C’est aussi une région stratégique car elle se situe sur les routes naturelles vers la Lune et ses points d’équilibre gravitationnels.
Un contrat d’étude à prix fixe impose un montant prédéfini pour une phase d’analyse (architecture, conception préliminaire, estimation de coûts et de planning), plutôt qu’un remboursement au fil des dépenses. Pour l’État, cela limite les dérapages budgétaires sur la phase amont et force les industriels à cadrer précisément le besoin et la solution. Pour l’industriel, le risque est de sous-estimer l’effort, mais la portée est généralement limitée à une étude, pas à la fabrication complète. Ce type de contrat sert souvent à comparer plusieurs options techniques avant de sélectionner, ou non, un partenaire pour la réalisation et l’exploitation.

articles.title: When every second counts: How Razorpay powers Comet's sneaker drops
articles.text:
Razorpay
View Brand Publisher
When every second counts: How Razorpay powers Comet's sneaker drops
For sneaker brand Comet, high-demand launches bring sudden traffic spikes. Razorpay Magic Checkout helps streamline payments and reduce friction when customers rush to secure their favourite pairs.
Most sneaker brands sell shoes.
Comet sells a feeling.
Started by founders Utkarsh Gupta and Dishant Parashar, Comet was born out of a simple observation: Indian sneaker culture was evolving fast, but homegrown brands still felt like an afterthought. Global labels dominated aspiration, while local options rarely captured the same sense of identity, storytelling, or community.
Comet wanted to change that.
Because in this category, sales don’t behave like normal ecommerce. People don’t casually browse for hours and slowly make up their minds. The decision is emotional, impulsive, immediate.
The second a pair drops, the clock starts ticking.
Which means checkout can’t afford to slow things down.
Built for the Heat of the Drop
For Comet, the most critical moments happen in seconds.
A limited colourway goes live. Traffic spikes instantly. Customers rush to secure their size before it disappears. In that environment, even a minor payment delay or failed transaction can cost a sale that was already won.
The team needed a checkout experience that could keep up with the pace and intensity of modern sneaker drops – fast, intuitive, and almost invisible.
That’s where Razorpay came in.
With Razorpay Magic Checkout, Comet was able to create a smoother buying journey during high-demand launches. Intelligent prefills and quick-buy flows reduced the number of steps customers had to take, helping them move from product page to payment in seconds.
At the same time, Razorpay’s card infrastructure and seamless UPI experience helped the brand handle sudden traffic surges without compromising transaction success. The result? Customers spent less time struggling with checkout and more time securing the pairs they came for.
Because in hype-driven commerce, momentum matters.
And Razorpay helped Comet preserve it.
The Impact
● Faster, low-friction checkout during high-traffic drops
● Improved customer experience with quick-buy journeys
● Reliable UPI flows during traffic spikes
● Strong card authorization rates during peak demand
● Reduced checkout abandonment during limited-edition launches
Powering Every Drop That Matters
Comet is building more than a sneaker brand. It’s building a culture-led label for a new generation of Indian consumers who want products that feel expressive, aspirational, and distinctly homegrown.
And as the brand continues to grow its community one drop at a time, Razorpay is helping ensure the buying experience keeps pace with the excitement.
Because when customers already know they want the pair, checkout should never be the thing standing between them and the moment.

articles.title: Qué hacer antes de usar una freidora de aire por primera vez para evitar accidentes al cocinar
articles.text:
Una freidora de aire permite preparar alimentos mediante la circulación de aire caliente dentro de una cesta cerrada. Antes del primer uso, conviene limpiar sus piezas, elegir una ubicación adecuada y realizar un ciclo de precalentamiento para retirar posibles olores propios de fabricación y evitar problemas durante la cocción.
Las pautas de uso indicadas por fabricantes como Moulinex apuntan a una preparación simple: poner los alimentos en el electrodoméstico, definir el programa o ajustar tiempo y temperatura, y poner en marcha el aparato.
En este sentido, se explica todo lo que se debe saber para cocinar por primera vez con una freidora de aire, sumado a cómo evitar accidentes durante su uso.
Por qué hay que leer el manual del fabricante antes de encender la freidora de aire
El primer paso consiste en revisar las instrucciones específicas del modelo y conservar el manual en un lugar accesible. Aunque el funcionamiento general de las freidoras de aire es similar, cada aparato puede contar con programas, piezas desmontables, límites de carga y sugerencias de limpieza propios.
Además, es importante identificar los componentes de la cesta, la rejilla y, si corresponde, la parte frontal desmontable. Las almohadillas de silicona que algunos modelos incluyen en la rejilla no deben retirarse, porque forman parte del diseño del accesorio y ayudan a mantenerlo en su posición.
Qué partes de la freidora de aire deben limpiarse antes del primer uso
Antes de conectar el electrodoméstico, hay que retirar todo el embalaje, las etiquetas y las calcomanías adheridas al aparato. Luego, la cesta y la bandeja deben lavarse con agua tibia y detergente durante unos minutos para eliminar restos del proceso de fabricación o del transporte.
El interior y el exterior de la freidora requieren una limpieza con un paño húmedo, sin sumergir el aparato. Si el modelo tiene una parte frontal desmontable o una ventanilla, el lavado manual de esa pieza ayuda a conservar el aspecto y la transparencia del cristal, según las indicaciones del fabricante.
Dónde se debe ubicar la freidora de aire
La ubicación influye en la seguridad y en el rendimiento del aparato. La freidora debe apoyarse sobre una superficie plana, nivelada, estable y resistente al calor. No conviene usar mesas inestables ni materiales que puedan deteriorarse por la temperatura que emite el aparato durante el funcionamiento.
Tampoco se debe colocar ningún objeto sobre la parte superior. La freidora necesita mantener libre el flujo de aire para cocinar de manera uniforme. Cubrirla o apoyar recipientes, paños u otros elementos puede alterar la circulación de aire caliente y afectar el resultado de los alimentos.
Por qué es necesario hacer un precalentamiento inicial de la freidora de aire
Antes de cocinar por primera vez, se debe realizar un ciclo de precalentamiento de 10 minutos a 200°C. Esta operación permite eliminar el olor que algunos materiales pueden desprender cuando el aparato se calienta por primera vez.
Durante ese ciclo, la cesta debe estar correctamente insertada y la rejilla debe quedar en el fondo hasta el tope. No hace falta añadir alimentos, aceite ni líquidos. La canasta no está diseñada para llenarse con aceite, a diferencia de una freidora convencional, porque la cocción se produce por aire caliente.
Cómo cargar los alimentos en la freidora de aire sin afectar la cocción
La cantidad debe ajustarse al tamaño de la cesta. Nunca hay que superar la marca MÁX. ni amontonar los ingredientes, porque el aire necesita circular entre los alimentos. Una carga excesiva puede impedir que algunas piezas se cocinen de forma pareja o que adquieran la textura esperada.
Algunas preparaciones admiten una cucharada de aceite, si la receta lo requiere, pero el exceso de grasa de los ingredientes caerá hacia la parte inferior de la cesta. Tras introducir los alimentos, se puede elegir un programa automático o ajustar de forma manual el tiempo y la temperatura antes de presionar el botón de inicio.
Asimismo, ciertos alimentos necesitan agitarse a mitad de la cocción. En esos casos, hay que retirar la cesta con cuidado, mover el contenido y volver a insertarla. Cuando suene la señal del temporizador, se debe comprobar que la preparación esté lista; si aún falta cocción, se puede sumar algunos minutos.
Para vaciar la cesta, hay que prestar atención al aceite acumulado en la base y a la rejilla extraíble, que puede desplazarse al inclinar el recipiente. La estructura cerrada de la freidora reduce la exposición a salpicaduras de aceite o agua hirviendo, pero sus piezas alcanzan altas temperaturas.

articles.title: Peut-on encore refuser le Linky ? Ce que change l’arrêt européen, et ce que ça vous coûte
articles.text:
Le droit européen ne permet pas d’exiger de garder son vieux compteur électrique. Dans un arrêt rendu le 5 novembre, la Cour de justice de l’Union européenne (CJUE) estime qu’un gestionnaire de réseau « n’est pas tenu de se ranger au souhait d’un client final » qui ne veut pas d’un compteur intelligent. La directive européenne de 2019 sur le marché de l’électricité encourage fortement le déploiement de ces compteurs et donne aux consommateurs le droit d’en demander un, mais pas celui de conserver en toutes circonstances un modèle classique.
Dans une affaire autrichienne, une cliente refusait que le gestionnaire de réseau local remplace son compteur mécanique par un modèle numérique. Elle invoquait la protection de ses données et les ondes électromagnétiques, alors que l’étalonnage de son ancien appareil avait expiré fin 2023. Saisie par le tribunal régional de Sankt Pölten, la CJUE ne tranche pas le litige elle-même, qui reviendra à la justice autrichienne. En revanche, son interprétation du droit européen s’impose aux juridictions de tous les États membres, France comprise.
En France, l’arrêt confirme une obligation déjà en place
Pour les foyers français, la décision change peu de choses en pratique. En effet, le Code de l’énergie confie déjà aux gestionnaires de réseau la pose et le renouvellement des compteurs, et le médiateur national de l’énergie rappelle que les consommateurs ne peuvent pas s’opposer au remplacement. La Cour de cassation avait déjà donné raison à Enedis face à deux clientes réfractaires en avril 2025. L’arrêt européen prive surtout les opposants d’un argument, à savoir celui d’un droit que leur garantirait le droit de l’Union. Le déploiement est d’ailleurs presque achevé et Enedis revendique 38,7 millions de compteurs Linky installés, soit plus de 95 % des foyers qu’il dessert.
Refuser reste possible dans les faits lorsque le compteur se trouve à l’intérieur du logement, puisque le technicien ne peut pas entrer sans l’accord de l’occupant. Toutefois, ce refus a un coût comme nous l’évoquions déjà l’an dernier.
Depuis le 1er août 2026, les foyers non équipés de leur fait paient 6,68 euros HT tous les deux mois, soit 40,08 euros HT par an, même s’ils transmettent leurs relevés. Si aucun index n’a été communiqué depuis plus d’un an, 4,27 euros HT s’ajoutent tous les deux mois, ce qui porte la facture à 65,70 euros HT par an, soit près de 80 euros TTC. À noter que ces frais sont suspendus dès qu’un rendez-vous est demandé pour la pose du compteur, et jusqu’à son installation.
Vos données de consommation restent protégées
L’arrêt répond aussi à l’argument des données personnelles, avancé par de nombreux opposants. La Cour estime que la directive « vie privée et communications électroniques », celle qui encadre notamment les cookies, ne s’applique pas à un réseau électrique, qui sert d’abord à distribuer de l’énergie et non à fournir des services de communication. Les données de consommation restent en revanche couvertes par le RGPD, dont les exigences « doivent nécessairement être respectées », rappelle la Cour.
En France, la CNIL encadre déjà ces données. Par défaut, Enedis ne collecte que la consommation journalière du foyer. Les relevés plus fins, à l’heure ou à la demi-heure, qui peuvent trahir les heures de lever, de coucher ou les absences, ne sont collectés qu’avec l’accord de l’abonné, sauf ponctuellement pour les besoins du réseau. Leur transmission à un fournisseur d’énergie ou à un tiers suppose aussi son consentement, et chacun peut activer ou suspendre ces collectes à tout moment depuis son espace client Enedis.

articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 – L'action cam Insta360 GO Ultra à 379,99 € (-20%)
L'action cam Insta360 GO Ultra passe sous les 400 € chez Fnac.com et Darty.com soit une baisse d'environ 20% sur le prix habituellement constaté. C'est actuellement l'un des meilleurs produit de notre comparatif.
Insta360 entend pousser le concept de l'action-cam Go 3s à son paroxysme. C'est pourquoi l’appellation Go Ultra espère prendre tout son sens avec des possibilités créatives revendiquées comme immenses, pour ne pas dire infinies.
Insta360 GO Ultra
- 
                            Prise en main

Points forts
- Format carré compact et pratique.
- Qualité d'image au top dans toutes les situations.
- Stabilisation efficace.
- Accessoires nombreux et bien pensés (surtout le sticky tabs).
- Modes de prises de vue variés et exploitables pour des vidéos créatives.
- Autonomie.
Points faibles
- Rolling Shutter.
- Coût de certains accessoires.
- Pas de Log.
C’est presque un carton plein pour la plus petite et la versatile des action cams du marché. L'Insta360 GO Ultra est endurante, ne surchauffe pas, est assez simple à utiliser, mais aussi pratique, fun, jolie et bien finie. Last but not least, l’app permet le partage direct depuis la caméra ou à partir du smartphone, avec en plus la possibilité de montage vidéo. Toutefois, il s'agit toujours d'une action cam avec un petit capteur. La dynamique est aidée par les algorithmes, mais limitée et cela se remarque sur grand écran. Cependant, cette caméra d'action est une ode à la créativité, et ça, c'est le plus important.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).

Bonne surprise de la part de GoPro, la Hero11 Mini est une déclinaison qui ne fait pas trop de compromis. Certes, elle est dépourvue d'écran et il faudra passer par l'application mobile pour la contrôler totalement, mais elle ne rogne en rien sur la qualité d'image ou la stabilisation. Nous pouvons ainsi reprendre la conclusion du test de la Hero11 Black : GoPro tient son rythme d'un renouvellement annuel et arrive encore à nous surprendre. La Hero11 Black reprend le design de la Hero10, mais évolue beaucoup à l'intérieur (ratio toujours plus large, intégration toujours plus poussée avec l'application Quik, stabilisation et correction de l'horizon au sommet de son art). La Hero11 Black (et donc aussi la Hero11 Mini) fait presque tout en mieux. Un excellent millésime !

articles.title: Premios Xataka Verisure 2026: todavía puedes conseguir tus entradas (y te adelantamos una novedad)
articles.text:
Los Premios Xataka Verisure 2027 están a la vuelta de la esquina. En apenas unos días, el 17 de noviembre, descubriremos en una gala llena de sorpresas los mejores productos tecnológicos del año, desde el mejor coche eléctrico al mejor móvil fotográfico, pasando por el mejor router, el mejor smartwatch o la mejor freidora de aire.
Es un año de muchos cambios, como salta a la vista, y uno de ellos tiene que ver con los presentadores. El tándem Joaquín Reyes y Ángela Blanco ha conducido la gala durante los últimos años, así que es el momento de darles un más que merecido descanso. Así que sí, xatakeros, este año estrenamos nuevo dúo de presentadores: Ana Brito (@elshowdebriten), humorista, comunicadora y copresentadora del pódcasts Poco se habla!; y servidor, Jose García, Responsable de Productos en Xataka.
Protege tu hogar frente a robos y ocupaciones con las cerraduras inteligentes de Verisure, disponibles como parte del sistema de alarma Verisure. Al margen de permitir abrir la puerta usando las llaves o desde el móvil, alertan ante cualquier intento de manipulación y transmiten la información a la unidad central de la compañía para generar un salto de alarma. Descubre la solución que mejor se ajusta a las necesidades de tu vivienda o negocio.
Cómo seguir la gala de los Premios Xataka Verisure 2026 en directo
Como todos los años, la gala tendrá lugar en los Cines Capitol de Madrid y la entrada será totalmente gratuita. Si ya tienes la tuya, ¡te esperamos el martes por allí!, y si no la tienes, todavía quedan unas poquitas (muy poquitas), así que todavía puedes pedir la tuya en este enlace. Sobra decir que puedes venir con un acompañante, solo marca la casilla correspondiente en el formulario. En pocas palabras:
- Cuándo: 17 de noviembre a las 20:00
- Dónde: Cines Capitol (Madrid) y xataka.com
- Entradas: Pide la tuya en este formulario (gratis y por orden de inscripción)
Si no puedes acompañarnos en persona, no hay problema. La gala se podrá seguir en vivo y en directo en streaming a través de nuestro canal de Twitch. Además, antes de la gala habrá una pregala presentada por Ana Boria y Ángela Blanco que, como no podría ser de otra manera, estará llena de sorteos.
En lo que respecta a la gala, tendremos que esperar para descubrir los ganadores, pero sí os podemos dar un breve adelanto: Jimmy Wales, fundador de Wikipedia, estará en el teatro y tendremos oportunidad de charlar con él. Y cuando termine, tendremos una fiesta en La Cartuja (C/ de la Cruz 10). Para acceder, tendrás que enseñar la pulsera que te daremos en la gala.
