articles.title: J’ai joué presque 5 000 heures sur Xbox en 25 ans, et vous ?
El ex CEO de Nvidia Jensen Huang acordó informar al Congreso sobre su vínculo con la presunta espía china
articles.text:
El ex director ejecutivo de Nvidia, Jensen Huang, aceptó informar al Congreso de Estados Unidos sobre su vínculo con una mujer sospechada de trabajar como espía para China y los protocolos de seguridad de la compañía tecnológica, según confirmó el congresista republicano John Moolenaar a NBC News.
El legislador, que preside el comité bipartidista de la Cámara de Representantes sobre China, explicó que ambas partes mantienen conversaciones para acordar una fecha para la reunión. La convocatoria se produjo después de que Moolenaar, junto con Brian Mast y Rick Crawford, los otros dos integrantes de la conducción del comité, solicitaran formalmente la comparecencia de Huang en una carta enviada a principios de este mes.
El encuentro buscará obtener explicaciones sobre la relación del empresario con la mujer investigada y conocer qué medidas aplica Nvidia para proteger su información y sus operaciones frente a posibles amenazas de espionaje.
Por el momento, no se informó cuándo tendrá lugar la reunión ni si Huang comparecerá en una audiencia pública.
Qué quieren saber los legisladores
La convocatoria apunta a que Huang explique la naturaleza de su relación con Alice Huang —también identificada como Huang Le—, una empresaria china que ocupó un cargo directivo en Megaspeed International, firma de centros de datos con sede en Singapur.
Las autoridades estadounidenses concluyeron que la mujer recopilaba información sobre el CEO de Nvidia para Beijing, una acusación que Pekín negó. Ambos fueron fotografiados juntos en Taiwán, Singapur y California. Aunque comparten apellido, no tienen ningún vínculo familiar.
Los legisladores también buscan precisiones sobre los mecanismos internos de protección de la empresa y los posibles riesgos derivados de esos vínculos.
Huang renunció tras 33 años al frente de Nvidia
La disposición de Huang a cooperar con el Congreso se conoce horas después de que la compañía confirmara su salida. La renuncia se formalizó este jueves, luego de que el directorio se reuniera para considerar su destitución. Nvidia designó a la directora financiera, Colette Kress, como directora ejecutiva interina mientras avanza la búsqueda de un reemplazante permanente. También nombró a Harvey Jones, exdirector ejecutivo de Synopsys, como primer presidente de la junta directiva.
Las acciones de Nvidia cayeron más del 10% en las operaciones previas a la apertura del mercado, una reacción que arrastró a los contratos a futuro vinculados al Nasdaq. En paralelo, los papeles de competidores como AMD y Broadcom avanzaron ante la expectativa de que puedan captar parte de la demanda. La empresa había alcanzado una valuación cercana a los USD 4 billones, lo que amplificó la sensibilidad del mercado ante el cambio en la conducción.
Huang dejó además su lugar en el consejo de administración. El cofundador era el cuarto mayor inversor de la compañía, con una participación aproximada del 3,61%. Su gestión de 33 años incluyó la transformación de Nvidia desde el negocio de gráficos para videojuegos hacia la infraestructura computacional que sostiene el desarrollo de modelos de inteligencia artificial.
La controversia escaló cuando trascendió una segunda relación extramatrimonial
La presión sobre Huang se intensificó el miércoles 11 de noviembre, cuando The New York Times informó que también había mantenido una relación extramatrimonial con Kimberly Powell, vicepresidenta de atención médica de Nvidia, quien dependía directamente de él. Según una fuente familiarizada con la situación, el directorio se reunió ese mismo día para evaluar una eventual destitución. La renuncia llegó al día siguiente.
La primera relación que salió a la luz fue con Alice Huang. Una investigación posterior reveló que la empresaria buscó financiación, a comienzos de 2025, para desarrollar un centro de datos en el sudeste asiático valuado en varios cientos de millones de dólares, con capacidad de cómputo que se alquilaría a empresas chinas y que requería acceso a procesadores gráficos de Nvidia.
Megaspeed, el vehículo societario vinculado a Alice Huang, es también objeto de investigaciones en varias jurisdicciones por presunto contrabando de chips.
El Congreso abrió un frente político y legislativo paralelo a la investigación interna de Nvidia
La presión legislativa no se limitó al pedido de comparecencia. El senador republicano por Dakota del Norte, Kevin Cramer, afirmó ante Politico que el riesgo de extorsión era demasiado alto para el responsable de una empresa central en el desarrollo de chips de inteligencia artificial y reclamó su dimisión.
El senador demócrata por Delaware, Chris Coons, anticipó que solicitará al Comité de Relaciones Exteriores del Senado que revise si la relación pudo haber afectado la seguridad de Estados Unidos.
En paralelo, los senadores republicano Jim Banks y demócrata Elizabeth Warren reclamaron al Departamento de Comercio que cierre vacíos en los controles de exportación y respaldaron la incorporación de la AI Overwatch Act a la ley anual de defensa. La iniciativa ampliaría la supervisión del Congreso sobre las exportaciones de chips avanzados.
También se evalúa incluir la Chip Security Act, que prevé sistemas para rastrear la ubicación de los procesadores, y la MATCH Act, orientada a limitar la venta a China de maquinaria para fabricar semiconductores.
Nvidia abrió una investigación interna antes de la renuncia
A comienzos de mes, el directorio de Nvidia había creado un comité de directores independientes, con asesoramiento jurídico externo, para determinar si Huang fue blanco de una operación de inteligencia extranjera. En ese momento, la junta expresó su confianza en el ejecutivo. La empresa sostuvo que no contaba con pruebas de que secretos corporativos o información de seguridad nacional hubieran sido comprometidos, aunque aclaró que la revisión analizaría todos los datos disponibles.
El presidente Donald Trump afirmó el 8 de noviembre que el FBI analiza el caso y que Huang le aseguró desconocer los supuestos vínculos de Alice Huang con organismos de inteligencia extranjeros. Trump también destacó que el entonces CEO había “hecho un trabajo increíble para nuestro país”.
Kress enfrentará su primera prueba como directora ejecutiva interina el 17 de noviembre, cuando Nvidia presentará sus resultados financieros. En esa instancia, inversores y analistas buscarán precisiones sobre la búsqueda de un CEO permanente, la composición del equipo directivo y la continuidad de la hoja de ruta de la empresa para sus próximos procesadores y sistemas de inteligencia artificial.

articles.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO following reports of two extramarital affairs
articles.text:
Ripple effect: In what was looking like an increasingly inevitable outcome, Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of Nvidia. It comes after reports that Huang had an extramarital affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy, followed by a more recent revelation of a second affair with Nvidia's VP of health care, Kimberly Powell. Colette Kress, the company's current executive vice president and chief financial officer, will take over as interim CEO.
"Nvidia Board of Directors announced today that Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately," the company said in a statement. "Colette Kress, current Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of Nvidia, has agreed to serve as Interim Chief Executive Officer.
Kress will continue to serve as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer while serving as Interim Chief Executive Officer until a permanent successor has been named. The Board is initiating a search for a permanent Chief Executive Officer and will consider internal and external candidates."
The billionaire CEO's troubles began when reports emerged that Huang had been involved with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed International. US intelligence officials believe she was working for China's Ministry of State Security, tasked with gathering information about American AI technology and potentially influencing Nvidia's boss to push for fewer restrictions on advanced chip exports to China.
Also read: Without Jensen Huang, is it game over for GeForce?
Huang admitted to the extramarital affair on November 8, apologizing to his wife, family, and colleagues. Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation into whether any company secrets or national security interests had been compromised, although it said there was no evidence this had happened.
Things quickly went from bad to worse. Nvidia's shares fell almost 5% following the admission, wiping around $190 billion off its market value in a single day. A class-action lawsuit was also filed against Huang and the company, accusing them of misleading investors by concealing the relationship.
Nvidia shares have now plunged to around $158 following Huang's resignation, their lowest level since July 2025. Nvidia's market value has crashed by $2 trillion since the stock's peak in early October. It's starting to look like the AI bubble could burst sooner than many expected.
Then came another revelation, one that seemingly sealed Huang's fate. On November 11, reports emerged of a second affair, this time with Powell, who reports directly to Huang. The relationship raised questions about potential violations of Nvidia's code of conduct and claims that the board was set to oust Huang.
Despite expressing confidence in Huang just three days earlier, Nvidia's board reportedly met on Wednesday to discuss removing him. His resignation ends his 33-year reign as the company's only CEO. Huang co-founded Nvidia in April 1993 alongside Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem.
Huang is known for having a close relationship with President Donald Trump, having joined his technology advisory council earlier this year. The Nvidia boss has repeatedly praised Trump's policies and successfully pushed the administration to loosen restrictions on AI chip exports to China. Trump even awarded Huang the National Medal of Science in October.
The president defended Huang after the affair allegations emerged, calling him an "honorable guy" who had done an "amazing job" for the country. Trump later said Huang had assured him he knew nothing about Alice Huang's alleged espionage activities, a claim the president said he believed.
Huang also accompanied Trump on a trip to China, and in August, he took a call from the president while discussing AI safety and regulation on stage at the All-In Summit, putting Trump on speakerphone for the audience to hear.
Speaking after her appointment as interim CEO, Kress said, "Nvidia's strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years. We will continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders." There has been no statement from Huang.

articles.title: Google's latest Search upgrade promises better answers to your most complicated questions | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Google Search is getting better at understanding complicated questions, including those with multiple parts, highly specific requests, or confusing typos. The updates are coming via the company’s newly released Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, which Google claims is its “biggest model improvement to Search yet.”
While Google’s frontier models, Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon, are best at deep reasoning for hard problems, Hydrogen is designed for fast execution across a variety of agentic workflows, or tasks in which an AI carries out multiple steps on its own, the company explained in an announcement.
The idea behind the model’s release is that using the most powerful model isn’t always needed — sometimes a faster, cheaper, and reasonably smart one will do. Google says Hydrogen completes tasks 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash, its previous fast model, but it’s still pretty smart, even beating the more powerful Gemini 4 Argon on one broad intelligence benchmark, the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, at its default high thinking level.
In Search, Hydrogen brings several improvements, including a better understanding of user intent, the ability to offer more helpful links and visual responses, and better answers across the different languages supported by Google’s AI Mode.
In terms of intent, Google says Hydrogen can handle more nuanced and complicated questions more quickly. This means people can ask their questions in their natural train of thought, including those that have multiple parts or that include highly specific requests. Hydrogen is also better at navigating hard-to-understand typos, Google says. Because of its improvements and better ability to follow instructions and call the right tools, Hydrogen is able to more precisely address each part of a user’s question.
Its advanced reasoning also improves Search’s fan-out technique, which breaks down a single user’s prompt into multiple subqueries. This allows people to discover websites related to the query that they may have otherwise missed, the blog post explains.
The addition of Hydrogen to Search will also mean more images, structured responses, comparison tables, and custom tools will appear as visual responses to users’ queries in AI Mode.
Google also says Hydrogen can work on its own for everyday work in areas like writing code, running tests, or verifying code changes, or it can be paired with Carbon and Argon in workflows that combine several models.
The model offers four thinking levels: low, medium, high (default), and a new, extra-high tier (“xhigh”), all of which are designed to complete tasks faster with fewer output tokens.
On multi-step tasks like deep research, data analysis, and broad codebase navigation, Hydrogen ranks No. 5 on Agent Arena’s benchmarks, the company pointed out.
In addition to Search, Gemini 4 Hydrogen is coming to all tiers of Google’s AI Studio, the Gemini API, the Gemini App, and the paid AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google’s Antigravity development platform.
Google says the Hydrogen update is rolling out to all Search users globally.

articles.title: Google retools Kubernetes for agentic workloads - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Google retools Kubernetes for AI agents instead of building a new stack
Agentic workloads are pushing Kubernetes into territory its creators never planned for. Agents generate untrusted code on the fly, sit idle for long stretches and churn through pods at a pace that strains the orchestrator’s control plane.
Cloud providers are now rethinking how general-purpose a cluster should be. Google LLC’s answer is to stop treating every cluster as an infinitely flexible engine and tune each one into a runtime optimized for its workload, according to Jago Macleod (pictured, right), director of engineering for Kubernetes and Google Kubernetes Engine at Google Cloud.
“There isn’t enough memory. There aren’t enough machines. So we have to get more efficient. And so one of the ways that we do that is to focus the Kubernetes cluster on the workload it’s running, and optimize it for that specific workload,” Macleod said.
Macleod and Jaana Dogan (pictured, left), principal engineer at Google Cloud, spoke with theCUBE’s Rebecca Knight at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how Google is customizing Kubernetes for agentic workloads without fragmenting the open-source ecosystem. (* Disclosure below.)
Agentic workloads strain the Kubernetes control plane
Kubernetes was built for microservices, then stretched to handle training jobs in which a single pod claims an entire node, Macleod explained. Agents are a different beast again, and some teams have resorted to building custom control planes just to cope.
“I think the agentic workloads are so different in the thrash and the churn that they represent is really not what we built Kubernetes for at all,” Macleod said. “And then agentic applications are almost the polar opposite, which is, you know, in the naive implementation, you just have as many pods as you can possibly fit, and so then the API machinery is running into limits.”
Platform teams have spent a decade making Kubernetes their compute fabric, and customers told Google they did not want agents to fragment it, Dogan explained. Google’s response is Agent Substrate, which runs AI agents in sandboxes directly on Kubernetes. The company donated the project to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation and recently released version 1.0. Because agents write their own code, that code is untrusted by default and needs sandboxing and network guardrails, according to Dogan. Customers also flagged a costly inefficiency.
“For example, our customers came to us, ‘Hey, majority of the time our agents are idle, but we have to allocate a sandbox all through the lifetime of a session,'” Dogan said. That means wasting a lot of CPU cycles, she explained.
Coding agents are also changing how engineers work, producing more prototypes and smaller, more focused teams, Dogan noted. As agentic workloads multiply, human judgment grows more valuable rather than less, according to Macleod.
“It’s not really, you know, fire off a prompt and forget it and walk away,” Macleod said. “It’s just a different level in the system where you’re applying your judgment and expertise. And that has never been more important.”

articles.title: Block Builderlab Launch Event 2026: AI agents join the team - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
4 insights from Block Builderlab Launch Event 2026: AI agents join the team as working colleagues
At Block Builderlab Launch Event 2026, AI agents moved out of single-player chat windows and into shared workspaces. There they work beside people as named, auditable members of the team. Block Inc. built these tools to run itself as an intelligence company, and it is now offering them to other businesses, building on Buzz, its open-source workspace for humans and AI agents. Block introduced Builderlab as a set of tools for teams and AI agents to work together.
The next phase will depend less on how capable a single agent becomes than on how well agents collaborate, share an organization’s context and stay inside firm security boundaries. Block plans to spread that model with open-source code, model-agnostic design and hosted infrastructure. The company is making that push while its core business delivers a third straight guidance raise.
“If you’re talking about making the whole organization more productive, you need to break down these distinctions between what the software does and what the people do,” said Paul Gillin (pictured, right), enterprise editor of SiliconANGLE Media Inc.
Alison Kosik (left) and co-host Gillin spoke with industry experts during Block Builderlab Launch Event 2026 in San Francisco. The interviews covered Block’s open-source business model, agents with their own identities, the shift from prompting to overnight delegation and the security controls that let enterprises trust autonomous systems. (* Disclosure below.)
Here are four standout insights from the event:
1. Open source turns Block’s internal agent tools into a business.
Builderlab gives developers endlessly customizable agents on an open-source plug-in architecture, and the launch audience of application builders cheered the idea, according to Gillin. Agents in Buzz have names, avatars and personalities. That shifts the focus from switching among software-as-a-service applications to the work itself, and it could threaten SaaS companies. The revenue model follows the classic open-source pattern of giving the software away and charging for the convenience of a hosted cloud service, he explained. Block said little about commercialization or about Cash App, which brings in 60% of its revenue, according to Gillin.
Check out theCUBE’s complete interview.
2. Buzz makes AI agents teammates that people can tag in a shared workspace.
Most AI tools are built for one person at a time, so each user becomes the bottleneck when results have to be shared with a team, noted Lucas Isaza, product lead of Buzz at Block. In Buzz, agents have their own identities, can be tagged like colleagues and leave an audit trail of every action. Plug-ins, added after the first version launched in July, let anyone reshape the interface. Nontechnical staff, such as account managers building personal dashboards, have been the heaviest users of the companion apps platform. Companies can self-host the open-source code, use a free tier or add funds for remote agents, models and extra storage, Isaza highlighted.
Watch the full interview from theCUBE.
3. Remote agents shift enterprise work from prompting to overnight delegation.
Builderlab sits as an interface layer above the models, so Buzz can use agents from any AI lab and switch to the newest frontier model as it arrives, emphasized Brad Axen, head of AI capabilities at Block. Remote agents run in central cloud environments that are easier to secure than laptops. People can hand them large assignments overnight and act as reviewers. Instead of soft guardrails, agents run on secure building blocks that never grant them permission for certain actions. Some teams have shipped software releases 50% to 75% faster. Axen expects agents to need much less human steering within the next year because they already sit inside the conversation.
See theCUBE’s full coverage.
4. Agent identities and information flow control anchor Block’s security model.
Securing agents that act on their own does not mean starting over, because principles such as least privilege, isolated environments and egress controls still apply, shared James Nettesheim, chief information security officer and head of enterprise technology at Block. Builderlab gives every agent a full identity owned by a human, runs it in hardened cloud virtual machines and records its actions in a cryptographically signed ledger that cannot be altered. Block is also building information flow control, which tags data from sensitive sources so the security policy travels with that data and blocks leaks. AI already reviews Block’s code and sorts its security alerts. Nettesheim added that agents let defenders keep pace with attackers’ machine speed.

articles.title: Google faces calls for AI moratoriums in schools after Gemini pilot backlash
articles.text:
CHICAGO—Families joined protests in seven cities nationwide on Wednesday, rallying against what they see as Google’s bid to entrench its AI models in schools, turn kids of all ages into Gemini guinea pigs, and hook them on AI.
The backlash follows a Google statement last week, confirming that there will be no way for students to use Google Search without AI. While Google claimed it was giving schools “more choice, not less”—by turning off Search, Gemini, and Gemini Notebook by default—it would not provide an option that allowed Search without AI. For students, the only way to avoid interacting with AI was to remember to add “-ai” to every query, parents worried.
In Chicago, many families showed up to protest Google, despite cold, rainy weather. Waving signs, dozens of protesters marched up to Google’s downtown office as workers seemed to be leaving for the day, shouting chants like “Hey Google, nice try, we don’t want your Gemini” and “Hey, Google, leave our kids alone!”
Ashley Belanger
Ashley Belanger
Ashley Belanger
Ashley Belanger
ILFPS executive director Cassie Creswell rallied the crowd.
Ashley Belanger
ILFPS executive director Cassie Creswell rallied the crowd.
Ashley Belanger
Ashley Belanger
ILFPS executive director Cassie Creswell rallied the crowd.
Ashley Belanger
Called to action by a nonprofit grassroots advocacy group, the Illinois Families for Public Schools (ILFPS), some parents and students had previously won a major AI fight. In August, the group pressured Chicago Public Schools (CPS) to pull out of a Gemini pilot that would have roped in all high school students districtwide—without consulting parents. And now, ILFPS is demanding a moratorium on AI until risks to students are better understood and CPS can draft a policy to protect students from potential learning setbacks or more harmful outcomes from engaging Google’s AI bots. If the group wins, it will join cities like Los Angeles and New York City in cautiously banning AI in schools.
Lawsuit: Gemini was student’s “suicide coach”
Most alarming to parents, Google now faces a lawsuit from a 13-year-old student in Durham, North Carolina named “Emma Doe.” As Emma has alleged, she was a happy, well-adjusted, straight-A student when she started using Gemini on her school-issued Chromebook. Emma’s parents had no idea she was using Gemini, as the lawsuit alleged that Google “deliberately” kept them in the dark while driving Emma into so-called “AI psychosis.” Over time, normal school-related interactions with the chatbot led to more intense chats, and ultimately the chatbot allegedly coached Emma to plan her own suicide and funeral. The school warned her parents and averted the danger after an internal system flagged a chat labeled “Funeral,” but Emma’s story stoked fears of parents joining protests not just in Durham, but also in Boston; Boulder, Colorado; Chicago; Los Angeles; New York City; and Portland, Oregon.
Emma’s lawsuit accuses Google of exploiting its dominant position in education technology and “sneaking” Gemini into Chromebooks, while falsely marketing them as safe.
“As a direct consequence of Google’s choices, Emma was baited by its defectively designed products into repeated, unmonitored, sycophantic AI chatbot interactions on her school Chromebook without her parents ever knowing. And, but for a fortunate turn of events, Google’s AI may well have manipulated Emma into taking her own life,” the lawsuit alleged. “Google must be held to account for treating the lives of children as disposable in service of its bottom line.”
Google only publicly addresses learning harms
Google has promised to “continue to engage deeply with educators to ensure we are giving schools more choice, more controls, and improved Search for learning.” However, Google’s statements so far attempting to address parents’ concerns focus exclusively on documented harms to learning. On that front, Google claims that it’s solving the problem of AI eroding students’ critical thinking skills by launching yet another pilot for students. In this pilot, students using AI Mode and AI Overviews will be offered a “step-by-step guided learning through problems, so that students don’t get quick answers to schoolwork,” Google said.
Cassie Creswell, executive director of ILFPS, told Ars that she’s been an advocate monitoring edtech issues for more than a decade. And even she was blindsided by Google’s AI moves.
“I am aware of AI Overviews when you search, which have a whole slew of problems, but I did not know that you really actually just have an interface where you can interact with Gemini in the chatbot way on everyone’s Chromebook still in Chicago public schools,” Creswell said. “And that’s so disturbing.”
She acknowledged that kids encounter AI on their phones and shared that her daughter said her friends like using ChatGPT better than Gemini. But she said that the fact that some kids use AI on personal devices doesn’t mean that schools should be encouraging adoption at young ages when kids’ brains are still developing, and risks remain largely unknown.
“There’s all kinds of dangerous things out in the world, but we don’t have our school district handing it to kids at their desk,” Creswell said.
No one knows how Google uses student data
Meanwhile, schools seem to be part of the transparency problem.
Creswell said that currently, the Chicago school district “is telling us their official line is that kids don’t have access to generative AI tools and that we don’t need a district-level policy on generative AI because they have guidebooks.” However, she’s reviewed Google’s CPS contracts, and they suggest that kids are interacting with generative AI and frontier models. The ongoing confusion has led parents to demand “a real policy” that the CPS “board votes on and that has the input of teachers, parents, students, and experts who are not being funded by the tech industry.”
Creswell told Ars that parents are particularly upset that Google is not transparent about how it processes and uses student data. She’s exhaustively researched Google contracts through Freedom of Information Act requests and told Ars that dozens of agreements she reviewed offer no indication of how CPS partners like Google—as well as Anthropic and OpenAI—are handling student data. Although she understands that “it’s probably just an honest statement of fact” that Google has built AI inextricably into Search, parents have a right to know how their children’s data is ingested into Google’s models, she said.
“Any sort of transparency on what is actually happening in terms of the data that they collect and what they do with it, that is absolutely missing,” Creswell said. And “it’s very unclear what data is being saved.”
To Creswell and other advocates, it seems likely that kids’ data is collected no matter what, since “even if you do ‘-AI,’ and you don’t get a text summary, your search data and what’s being returned is all basically inside the generative AI model.” Although Illinois law only allows commercial use of de-identified data, parents think Google should clearly explain what steps it takes to ensure data can’t be recombined to re-identify kids.
Parents: No AI training on school kids’ data
Ars reached out to Google to see if the company could clarify if Creswell’s read is accurate or if there’s any meaningful distinction between adding “-AI” to an individual query versus building a button that would automatically add “-AI” to every query. Google did not clarify, instead emphasizing that schools will control whether students can access the Gemini app, Gemini Notebook, and Search, with options to toggle each off individually, but no option to use Search without AI.
Emma Doe’s lawsuit alleged that Google has taken advantage of a dominant position it has held in schools since 2007 to push AI on kids and seize their data without meaningfully protecting them from the worst potential harms of its chatbot’s sycophantic design. In Chicago, CPS signed a contract with Google in 2020, “long before Gemini was rolled out,” Creswell found. Over the next two extensions of that contract, no updates were introduced to protect students’ privacy as AI advanced.
To Creswell, it remained “totally unclear” in contracts how Google’s processing of student data may have changed, beyond updates to the privacy policy for Google Workspace for Education.
Currently, that policy specifies that “we receive customer data through the Core Services and process it according to the school’s (the customer’s) instructions. This customer data includes anything submitted, stored, sent, or received through Core Services by you or your school.” Google collects that data on that activity, as well as account information “like name, email address and password” and location information, the policy said.
The policy didn’t discuss Gemini but noted that data from using core services helps maintain services, improve personalization, and increase security. And “the data we collect in the Additional Services is used across our services to deliver, maintain, and improve our services; develop new services; provide personalized services; measure performance; communicate with you; and protect Google, our users, and the public.”
To parents, the policy provides no reassurance that their kids’ data isn’t part of Google’s plan to dominate the AI industry.
“We should not have any child data being collected in a school setting being used for commercial purposes,” Creswell said.
“What about the future of our minds?”
Parents’ privacy concerns go beyond Google, Creswell noted. But since Google has “captured so much of the education space and so much of the education experience,” parents are focusing their energy on interrogating those AI systems in schools early on.
In Chicago, a recently re-elected CPS school board member, Karen Zaccor, is pushing for an AI moratorium in schools after talking with city and community colleges about an allegedly noticeable decline in reading, math, and writing skills from students graduating from CPS schools. In Emma’s case, Google allegedly suppressed chat logs, and the school withheld safety logs, frustrating parents who already viewed AI as more harmful than beneficial in education.

Ashley Belanger
Ashley Belanger
Ashley Belanger
Ashley Belanger
CPS scholar Reese Mackey (center-left) spoke for students.
Ashley Belanger

Ashley Belanger

Ashley Belanger
At the Google protest Wednesday, parents waved signs that threatened to eject Google from schools, with slogans like “No Google + No AI = Win/Win.” Many kids used favorite cartoon characters from shows like Beavis and Butthead and South Park to slam Google’s seemingly cynical approach to introducing AI in schools. One young girl wearing pink rain boots held up a cardboard sign, declaring in colorful markers, “I like to read!!”
At its peak, about 60 people stood outside Google’s downtown Chicago office, enduring the rain and listening to teachers and students who oppose reckless AI adoption.
One particularly moving speech came from a CPS student, Reese Mackey, who spoke for students. She challenged Google to more carefully weigh the long-term harms of aggressively pushing AI onto students by claiming they’ll be left behind and struggle to find jobs without AI skills. Creswell told Ars the opposite seems true, as Emma Doe’s lawsuit pointed to research branding Gemini as “the most dangerous marketed for use by youth” and “confirming the existence of AI-induced psychosis.”
“What about the future of our youth?” Mackey said. “What about the future of our minds?”
Ashley is a senior policy reporter for Ars Technica, dedicated to tracking social impacts of emerging policies and new technologies. She is a Chicago-based journalist with 20 years of experience.

articles.title: Nectar launches an AI agent to automate creator discovery and outreach for brands | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Nectar, an AI-powered operating system for marketing, is launching a new AI agent designed to take a lot of the manual work out of influencer marketing, from finding the right creators to contacting them, managing partnerships, and tracking results.
Founded by sisters Misbah and Farah Uraizee, both former Meta employees, Nectar came out of stealth last year and uses AI agents to help brands manage social media, customer conversations, content moderation, creator partnerships, and competitor research.
Announced Thursday, its new “Creator Agent” can search for creators, check their content and brand partnerships, send personalized messages, coordinate collaborations, and monitor how campaigns perform. Instead of having marketing teams spend weeks scrolling through social media, building spreadsheets, and sending individual DMs, Nectar wants its agent to handle much of that work automatically.
Nectar joins other companies introducing agentic AI assistants designed to automate influencer outreach, including Aspire and GRIN. The launch also comes as more brands turn to creators to reach customers. U.S. spending on creator advertising is expected to reach $44 billion in 2026, according to the Interactive Advertising Bureau. As companies work with hundreds or even thousands of creators, keeping track of relationships and measuring results can get pretty difficult.
Nectar says its Creator Agent searches more than 300 million creator profiles to find potential partners, including smaller creators who may not yet have a large following but are gaining traction. The system analyzes videos to understand what creators post about, how their content fits a brand, and whether their previous partnerships are appropriate. It also checks brand safety by reviewing content in context rather than simply searching for specific keywords.
Nectar then creates ranked lists of recommendations and adds new matches as creators become more popular.
Once it finds a potential match, the agent can draft and send messages in a brand’s voice, create custom landing pages to collect creator information, and help manage contracts, product gifting, and shipping details. It also remembers previous conversations and interactions, so brands can keep track of relationships without relying on spreadsheets.
“Brands can share voice guidelines in any format, and Nectar picks up the rest from their history,” CEO Misbah Uraizee tells TechCrunch. “On top of that sits a set of proprietary guardrails that keep every draft on tone and in context. Nectar understands what is being said in a video, reads the tone of the conversation, and knows the difference between a quote post on X and a TikTok comment section. A brand should not sound identical in both, and with Nectar it doesn’t.”
Another feature looks for personal milestones in creators’ lives, such as an engagement, a new baby, or completing a marathon. The agent can then suggest a personalized message or gift, helping brands build relationships that feel less like one-off advertising deals.
Creator Agent is available today globally and covers Instagram creators and TikTokers.
The company plans to make the agent available through its Model Context Protocol (MCP), allowing teams to use it through AI assistants such as Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot, as well as their own custom-built agents.
This past May, Nectar raised a $30 million Series A round led by Menlo Ventures and its Anthology Fund, which is a joint initiative launched with Anthropic.

articles.title: Noctua brings space-grade carbon nanotube thermal pad to AMD AM5 and AM4 processors — promises years of maintenance-free performance for $24.95
articles.text:
Noctua brings space-grade carbon nanotube thermal pad to AMD AM5 and AM4 processors — promises years of maintenance-free performance for $24.95
Designed to last for years.
Austrian cooling outfit Noctua is officially rolling its new NT-CP1 AM5/4 Carbice carbon nanotube thermal pad for AMD AM4 and AM5 processors into the retail market. After announcing its partnership with advanced nanotechnology company Carbice back in June 2026, the premium thermal pad can now be purchased for $24.95 in the US and €24.95 in the European region.
Conventional thermal pastes and most thermal pads gradually lose performance over time due to pump-out, delamination, cracking, and other forms of degradation. However, Noctua says that its new NT-CP1 thermal pad takes a different approach. It makes use of Carbice's vertically-aligned carbon nanotube technology, originally developed for high thermal reliability in aerospace systems. The carbon nanotubes gradually conform to microscopic imperfections of a CPU’s IHS over hundreds to thousands of thermal cycles.
This allows heat transfer performance to improve during the initial activation period rather than gradually deteriorating. The thermal pad can also maintain stable, maintenance-free performance for years once the initial activation phase is complete. Thus, making it a suitable option for users who want consistent thermal performance without having to periodically replace degraded thermal paste.
"Carbice pads offer a unique combination of ultimate performance stability and convenient installation. This makes the NT-CP1 the perfect choice for everyone who’s looking for a thermal pad that’s super easy to apply and never needs to be replaced," said Noctua CEO Roland Mossig in a press note.
Unlike conventional carbon or graphite-based thermal pads, which can be brittle, slippery, and electrically conductive, the NT-CP1 features an aluminum backbone sandwiched between layers of carbon nanotubes. The surface is also protected by a nanoscale polymer coating, which Noctua says makes the pad more robust, easier to handle, and less likely to move during installation. The company recommends a simple peel, press, and peel installation process, while the slightly tacky coating helps keep the pad in place and offers electrical insulation as long as the polymer layer remains intact.
With an ultra-thin 90µm profile and precut 33x33mm size, the thermal pad fits both AM5 and AM4 socket processors. Noctua also highlights its manufacturing process, noting that the pad is produced in the US using recycled aluminum and waste carbon gas to grow the carbon nanotubes. The company claims that its manufacturing process is more energy-efficient compared to conventional graphite and graphene-based pads, while the aluminum structure allows the product to be recycled through standard aluminum recycling channels.

articles.title: Google quiere que olvides las Meta Ray-Ban: sus nuevas gafas con Gemini ya tienen precio y fecha de lanzamiento
articles.text:
Google ya tiene listas sus nuevas gafas inteligentes con Gemini, un dispositivo con el que busca llevar la IA más allá del móvil. A unos meses de su presentación, los primeros modelos desarrollados en colaboración con Gentle Monster, Warby Parker y Samsung ya están listas para reservarse. Las gafas se venderán en versiones de audio y con pantalla e intentarán robarle un pedazo del mercado a las Meta Ray-Ban.
De acuerdo con una publicación en el blog de la compañía, las Intelligent Eyewear están basadas en Android XR y pueden usarse con móviles como el Pixel, Samsung Galaxy o el iPhone. Google ofrecerá dos colecciones: la primera, de la mano de Gentle Monster, incluirá seis modelos en diferentes colores con opciones de lentes transparentes, fotocromáticas o tintadas. La segunda, desarrollada junto a Warby Parker, se enfocará en estilos más clásicos inspirados en algunos de los modelos más populares de la marca.
En términos de funciones, las Intelligent Eyewear utilizan la IA de Gemini para realizar diversas acciones. Los usuarios solo necesitarán invocarla con la frase "Hey Gemini" o tocando una de las patillas. Desde ahí se podrá obtener información contextual sobre lo que se está viendo, pedir recomendaciones en tiempo real y gestionar listas de compra sin sacar el móvil del bolsillo. El asistente puede consultar eventos del calendario y avisarte sobre los pendientes que tienes programados.
Las Intelligent Eyewear cuentan con una cámara ultragran angular de 12 megapíxeles que permite capturar fotos o vídeos con pulsar un botón. De acuerdo con Google, el sistema utiliza estabilización de imagen, procesamiento HDR y grabación de audio espacial para mejorar la calidad del contenido. En caso de que no necesites la cámara o los micrófonos, podrás apagarla por completo y usar el dispositivo como unas gafas comunes.
Las gafas de Google y Samsung plantan cara a Meta y sus Ray-Ban
Una de las cosas que distinguen a las Intelligent Eyewear de las Meta Ray-Ban es la integración a fondo con los servicios de Google. Las gafas pueden conectarse a Google Maps y darte indicaciones paso a paso mediante audio, o usar Google Translate para traducir frases en más de 70 idiomas en tiempo real. Para aquellos que tengan debilidad visual, el dispositivo podrá leer textos pequeños o generar descripciones de audio sobre objetos.
Al igual que vemos con Meta, Google ha apostado por un diseño que pueda pasar desapercibido y sea cómodo para llevarse todo el día. Las Intelligent Eyewear pesan alrededor de 41 gramos y ofrecen hasta nueve horas de autonomía con una sola carga. En caso de que te quedes sin batería, podrás meter las gafas al estuche para recargarlas hasta siete veces.
Otras características incluyen altavoces abiertos para escuchar música, tomar llamadas y escuchar a Gemini. Los usuarios pueden reproducir su lista de reproducción de Spotify, YouTube Music y Apple Music, o escuchar un audiolibro gracias al soporte de Audible.
Google confirmó que sus gafas Intelligent Eyewear estarán disponibles a partir del 10 de diciembre de 2026. El precio para los modelos de Warby Parker es de 395 dólares en adelante, mientras que los de Gentle Monster parten de 449 dólares. Por el momento no hay información sobre un posible lanzamiento en España o América Latina, aunque la tecnológica estaría obligada a hacerlo si quiere competir de frente con Meta.

articles.title: Massive Microsoft 365 outage disrupts Outlook, Teams, Copilot worldwide
articles.text:
Microsoft is investigating a widespread outage affecting multiple Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook, Microsoft Teams, and Copilot, as users report connectivity problems worldwide.
BleepingComputer has received numerous reports from users experiencing problems accessing Microsoft's services, including complaints that Outlook is down.
According to Downdetector, which tracks user-submitted outage reports, complaints surged Thursday afternoon across numerous Microsoft services, including Outlook, Microsoft 365, Teams, Copilot, Azure, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Store.
In a Microsoft 365 admin center advisory tracked as MO1550821, Microsoft confirmed that customers may be unable to connect to multiple services, including Exchange Online, Microsoft Teams, SharePoint Online, Microsoft 365 Copilot, and Microsoft Defender XDR.
The company says the Microsoft 365 incident began Thursday at 1:26 PM ET, although it began investigating reports of Exchange Online mailbox connectivity problems in the Americas earlier in the day.
Microsoft initially attributed the disruption to elevated infrastructure load across multiple regions, but has determined that the problem was caused by servers unexpectedly becoming unavailable.
"We determined the elevated load isn't driven by an increase in traffic, but by a number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable; straining the remaining infrastructure. We're working to safely return them to service," Microsoft said in an update on X.
The company says it has paused all deployments, redistributed connection traffic across its worldwide infrastructure, and is moving additional traffic away from affected systems to reduce load.
Microsoft is also restarting affected servers to restore capacity and return services to normal operation.
While the company initially reported Exchange Online connectivity problems in the Americas, it later confirmed that users in any region could be affected.
The outage follows a separate Microsoft Teams incident earlier Thursday that caused an outage for users in North and South America.
That earlier incident, tracked as TM1550488, lasted from 9:45 AM to 10:53 AM ET and caused delays or failures when sending messages, errors creating or updating conversations, and problems retrieving chat messages.
Microsoft attributed the earlier Teams disruption to resource contention within its infrastructure, which led to elevated resource utilization and prevented the service from processing messaging requests normally.
The company says the earlier Teams incident has been fully resolved.
Microsoft has not indicated whether the two incidents are related, and the ongoing Microsoft 365 outage has not yet been resolved.
BleepingComputer contacted Microsoft with questions about the outage and will update our story if we receive a response.
Update 11/12/26 6:57 PM ET: Microsoft says it is seeing limited recovery from the widespread Microsoft 365 outage after successfully returning some affected servers to service.
The company previously said its recovery efforts had not provided the expected relief and that it discovered a core process on affected servers was becoming overwhelmed, resulting in a loss of capacity.
Microsoft also said it was investigating whether reverting a small number of recent configuration updates could accelerate recovery.
"We're returning a portion of affected servers to the service, and they remain stable so far. We're also shifting traffic to alternate routes wherever possible and observing limited recovery," Microsoft said in its latest update on X.
The company says it has streamlined the process of restoring the remaining affected servers and warned that users may experience a gradual recovery as their applications reconnect.
Microsoft has not yet confirmed when services will be fully restored.

articles.title: Bodhi Tree Systems acquires majority stake in Adyar Ananda Bhavan for $180M
articles.text:
Bodhi Tree Systems acquires majority stake in Adyar Ananda Bhavan for $180M
Bodhi Tree Systems is a strategic investment and operating platform founded in 2021 by James Murdoch, son of media mogul Rupert Murdoch, and Uday Shankar, former Star India and Disney executive.
Chennai-headquartered restaurant chain Adyar Ananda Bhavan (A2B), which has a presence in India and overseas, has sold a majority stake to Bodhi Tree Systems for a value of $180 million.
A2B runs 160 outlets in India, predominantly in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka. It also has 30 outlets abroad across Malaysia, US, Australia, Canada, the United Kingdom, and Singapore. It employs over 15,000 employees in total.
Bodhi Tree Systems is a strategic investment and operating platform founded in 2021 by James Murdoch, son of media mogul Rupert Murdoch, and Uday Shankar, former Star India and Disney executive.
“A2B has earned the trust of millions of families through its consistent and reliable quality,” said Murdoch and Shankar, Co-founders of Bodhi Tree Systems, in a joint statement.
A2B opened its first outlet in 1979 in Chennai, selling sweets and savouries. Since then it has steadily expanded its presence, combining its vegetarian restaurant business alongside sweets and savouries retail.
Following this transaction, Shankar will serve as the chairperson of A2B’s new board of directors.
The statement from statement from Bodhi Tree said, “We are grateful to the co-founders, K.T. Srinivasa Raja and K.T. Venkatesan, for this opportunity to partner with them to build a differentiated, professionally managed Indian food company, one that sets new standards for the sector.
"While A2B is a formidable brand in India, we are equally impressed by the scale and reach of its operations in Singapore, the United States, Australia, Malaysia, and the UK. We look forward to working with the team to take its authentic cuisine to a far broader global audience.”
Bodh Tree said the investment will help scale A2B's operations, noting that few brands operating in South Indian cuisine command the depth of consumer trust, widespread affection, and enduring popularity that A2B has built over generations.

articles.title: Sony déclare forfait sur le streaming PC et renvoie les abonnés PlayStation Plus vers ses consoles
articles.text:
Sony retirera l’application PlayStation Plus pour PC le 10 décembre, un mois après une annonce glissée cette semaine en toute fin du billet mensuel consacré aux nouveautés du catalogue de jeux. Lancée avec la refonte de l’abonnement en juin 2022, elle permettait aux membres Premium de jouer en streaming aux titres PS4 du catalogue et à une sélection de classiques depuis un ordinateur. Moins de 0,4 % des abonnés éligibles s’en servaient encore.
Lire aussi : Sony dévoile un nouveau PlayStation Portal, avec plus de mémoire
Une application que ses propres abonnés avaient désertée
Le chiffre vient de Sony lui-même, qui l’avance pour justifier le retrait au détour du billet dévoilant les ajouts de novembre au catalogue. Le constructeur préfère, selon ses propres mots, se « concentrer sur l’amélioration d’expériences de haute qualité qu’un plus grand nombre de membres souhaitent utiliser ». Les abonnés concernés seront prévenus individuellement d’ici l’échéance.
Cantonnée au streaming des jeux PS4 du catalogue et d’une partie des classiques, l’application ne proposait ni téléchargement ni chat de groupe, et réclamait une manette compatible. Elle restait au passage interdite aux moins de 18 ans, exigeait une connexion d’au moins 5 Mbit/s et privait les joueurs des extensions achetées pour leurs jeux. À son lancement, elle n’embarquait pas même de moteur de recherche, et une centaine de titres manquaient à l’appel par rapport aux consoles, quand d’autres refusaient de se lancer. Sa configuration requise officielle en était restée à Windows 8.1 ou 10.
La page d’assistance qui hébergeait le lien de téléchargement renvoie déjà une erreur 404. Rien ne change en revanche sur PS5 et PS4, ni pour le streaming depuis une console ou un PlayStation Portal, toujours compris dans le palier Premium : la fermeture ne concerne que l’ordinateur.
Lire aussi : Sony donne des nouvelles de la PS6, mais un obstacle de taille se profile
Le PC, une parenthèse que PlayStation referme
Le streaming sur ordinateur avait déjà changé de statut en juin 2022, à l’absorption de PS Now dans le PlayStation Plus actuel. L’accès PC s’était retrouvé réservé au palier Premium, facturé aujourd’hui 151,99 euros par an en France, un ticket d’entrée qui avait alors quasiment doublé pour cet usage.
Le retrait de l’application prolonge surtout le mouvement entamé en mars, quand Sony a annulé les futurs portages PC de ses jeux solo, six ans après avoir entrouvert cette porte. La mention « PlayStation Exclusive » vient d’ailleurs de refaire son apparition sur les productions maison, et les portages déjà publiés restent seuls en rayon, sans nouvelle conversion au programme. Pour profiter du catalogue, il faudra désormais une PS4, une PS5 ou un PlayStation Portal, la console portable dédiée au jeu à distance.

articles.title: Así lograron ejecutar juegos de PlayStation 5 en una PS4 sin utilizar la consola más reciente de Sony
articles.text:
Un proyecto de emulación consiguió ejecutar videojuegos desarrollados para PlayStation 5 en una PlayStation 4 Pro, una consola que Sony lanzó en 2016 y retiró progresivamente del mercado tras la llegada de la nueva generación. Se trata de EmuFive, un emulador que permite utilizar parte del catálogo de PS5 en el hardware de su antecesora, aunque todavía presenta limitaciones importantes de rendimiento y compatibilidad.
Uno de los resultados más llamativos del desarrollo es que logró ejecutar God of War: Sons of Sparta, un videojuego exclusivo de PS5, a aproximadamente 40 fotogramas por segundo (FPS) en una PS4 Pro.
El avance resulta significativo porque demuestra que una consola de una generación anterior puede reproducir determinados títulos diseñados para un sistema más moderno, aunque no significa que pueda reemplazar a una PlayStation 5.
El proyecto fue desarrollado por Chokri Hammedi, conocido en la comunidad de emulación como blue0x1. Su trabajo parte de KytyPS5, un emulador de PlayStation 5 creado originalmente para computadoras, que fue adaptado para funcionar sobre el hardware de la consola anterior de Sony.
Cómo funciona EmuFive en una PlayStation 4
EmuFive no es una aplicación que pueda instalarse directamente en cualquier PlayStation 4. Para utilizarlo es necesario contar con una consola modificada y ejecutar Linux, un sistema operativo de código abierto que permite acceder a funciones del hardware que normalmente no están disponibles para los usuarios.
El procedimiento requiere herramientas como GoldHEN y PS4 Multiboot. La primera permite ejecutar aplicaciones y modificaciones no oficiales en una consola compatible, mientras que la segunda facilita iniciar Linux desde la PS4.
Una vez dentro de ese entorno, los usuarios pueden ejecutar EmuFive y seleccionar los videojuegos que desean probar. El proyecto también incorpora una versión modificada de Mesa, un conjunto de controladores gráficos de código abierto que proporciona compatibilidad con Vulkan 1.3 para aprovechar la GPU de la consola.
El emulador cuenta con una interfaz adaptada al mando DualShock 4. Esto permite navegar por las opciones, seleccionar títulos y gestionar archivos sin necesidad de conectar un teclado o un ratón. Además, admite juegos almacenados en unidades USB y carpetas compartidas desde una computadora.
Como ocurre con otros proyectos de emulación, los usuarios deben proporcionar sus propias copias de los videojuegos. El programa no incluye títulos ni permite acceder automáticamente a los juegos comprados en PlayStation Store.
God of War: Sons of Sparta funciona a 40 FPS
La prueba que más llamó la atención de la comunidad fue la ejecución de God of War: Sons of Sparta en una PlayStation 4 Pro. El juego consiguió alcanzar alrededor de 40 FPS, una cifra que demuestra que EmuFive puede interpretar y ejecutar determinados programas diseñados para la consola más reciente.
Sin embargo, el resultado debe entenderse dentro de las características del videojuego. God of War: Sons of Sparta pertenece al género metroidvania y presenta una jugabilidad de acción en dos dimensiones, por lo que sus exigencias gráficas y de procesamiento son diferentes a las de una producción tridimensional de gran escala.
El emulador también consiguió ejecutar la versión de PlayStation 5 de Hollow Knight: Silksong. No obstante, esta prueba tiene menor relevancia porque el título también cuenta con una versión compatible con PlayStation 4.
Estos avances no significan que todos los juegos de PS5 puedan funcionar en una consola antigua. La compatibilidad depende de las características de cada título y de la capacidad del emulador para traducir las instrucciones que necesita el sistema.
Por qué una PS4 no puede reemplazar a una PS5
La principal dificultad de EmuFive está en el procesador. La PlayStation 4 utiliza una CPU AMD Jaguar de ocho núcleos, mientras que la PS5 incorpora un procesador basado en la arquitectura Zen 2, considerablemente más potente.
La diferencia no se limita a la velocidad. Algunos videojuegos desarrollados para PS5 utilizan instrucciones específicas como AVX2, FMA y BMI2, que no están disponibles de forma nativa en el procesador de la PS4.
Para solucionar este inconveniente, EmuFive incorpora capas de traducción que permiten interpretar esas instrucciones mediante el hardware de la consola anterior. Sin embargo, este proceso exige trabajo adicional al procesador y puede reducir considerablemente el rendimiento.
Por esa razón, algunos títulos consiguen iniciar, pero no mantienen una tasa de fotogramas estable para jugar con normalidad. La limitación también explica por qué el proyecto ofrece mejores resultados con videojuegos menos exigentes.
Cómo descargar el emulador EmuFive
La versión 1.0.3 de EmuFive está disponible gratuitamente en el repositorio de GitHub de su desarrollador, blue0x1. Allí se pueden consultar los archivos del proyecto y las instrucciones necesarias para probarlo.
Su instalación requiere conocimientos técnicos, una PS4 compatible con las modificaciones necesarias y la configuración de Linux. Por tanto, no se trata de una herramienta pensada para cualquier usuario que simplemente quiera jugar títulos de PS5 en su consola antigua.

articles.title: Run agents securely and efficiently with the next generation AgentCore runtime | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Run agents securely and efficiently with the next generation AgentCore runtime
AI agents have moved past one-off prompts. They now run multi-step workloads for hours at a time. The length of task that frontier agents can complete on their own doubles about every four months (METR), and 40 percent of large enterprises are scaling AI agents, up from 27 percent a year ago (McKinsey). As agents run longer and with more autonomy, the focus shifts from what agents can do to how securely, reliably, and economically they can operate at scale. Agents do more than traditional software: they execute code, navigate browsers, access sensitive data, and act on behalf of users. These capabilities introduce new security and infrastructure demands, making strong isolation essential for production deployments.
Every agent session needs a secure, isolated environment. But delivering that isolation at scale introduces a fundamental challenge: balancing performance, cost, and efficiency. Pre-provisioned environments consume resources even when idle, driving up costs. On-demand environments reduce wasted capacity but introduce cold-start latency, delaying agent execution. Neither approach scales efficiently without trade-offs. As organizations move from deploying a handful of agents to running thousands of concurrent sessions, building and managing custom sandboxes becomes increasingly complex, expensive, and unpredictable.
The challenge is evident. Only 15 percent of organizations have scaled orchestrated, multi-agent systems, and 70 percent say they can’t yet trust and govern their agents (Deloitte). Scaling agents shouldn’t mean choosing between security, speed, and cost. The next generation of agent infrastructure must deliver strong isolation with fast startup times, elastic scaling, and usage-based economics. Because as AI agents move into production, secure execution shouldn’t be the bottleneck. It should be the foundation that makes scale possible. The fastest path to production should also be the safest one.
The next generation AgentCore runtime
We built Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to help developers build, connect, and optimize agents securely at scale. AgentCore runtime, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, is the managed compute layer. It gives developers a fully managed environment to deploy and run agents without building or maintaining infrastructure. Since launching, our customers have been pushing their agents into increasingly complex workloads. As those workloads grow, so do the demands on the execution environment: more compute, more flexible billing, and trust boundaries that extend to data, not only compute. Agents reach production at scale if the infrastructure underneath was built for both scale and speed.
Today we’re announcing updates to AgentCore runtime that meet those demands. The core guarantee stands: every session runs in its own hardware-isolated Firecracker micro virtual machine (MicroVM), with its own identity, policy, and audit trail. These updates expand what’s possible within that guarantee. Sessions now start up to 15x faster, scale to 4x more compute, and run up to 68% more efficiently, with the isolation boundary fully intact.
Here’s what’s new.
Run bigger workloads without waiting longer to start
Teams building increasingly advanced agents asked for more flexibility: the ability to scale memory and compute within the isolated session to match the demands of their workloads. From large codebase compilations to browser-driven workflows to local model inference, the execution environment needs to keep pace.
Sessions now scale 4x compared to the previous version, up to 8 vCPUs and 32 GB, with support for container images up to 10 GB. Sessions start in under 2 seconds, independent of image size and concurrency. You no longer need warm pools and pre-provisioned clusters to manage cold starts.
        “AgentCore Runtime lets us run AI-driven development at scale. Each coding agent session runs in its own hardware-isolated environment, which we need when agents execute code, and the runtime scales elastically with demand and starts fast every time, so our engineers move quickly without managing any infrastructure.”
— Siwei Shen, VP of Engineering, Coinbase
        “Mission is using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime to power a natural-language query agent that helps users retrieve property and sales insights without navigating complex data systems. In our initial comparison of both runtime versions, the same workload delivered 35% faster cold starts for inference requests and 77% faster starts for health checks, while reducing measured runtime cost per call by 17%. The new AgentCore runtime gives us a compelling combination of faster agent experiences and more efficient resource utilization as we bring enterprise agents into production.”
— Dr. Ryan Ries, Chief AI & Data Scientist, Mission Cloud
        “Our approach is to run Zuora’s cloud with automation and AI agents wherever we can, and that only works if the runtime is efficient and reliable. The next generation AgentCore runtime cut our memory footprint per invocation by around 60% in many use cases while handling more traffic at steady latency. That gives us a stronger cost profile as we expand agentic workloads across our platform.”
— Brad Ruppert, VP of Cloud and Security, Zuora
        “The Rescale platform helps R&D and engineering teams accelerate product development with agentic digital engineering. Our engineering-specific agents validate simulation inputs, troubleshoot jobs, select hardware, and generate reports, while engineers stay in control. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime allows us to deploy and scale those agents in production without building or operating the underlying agent infrastructure, so we can deliver new agents to customers faster.”
— Mark Whitney, VP Engineering, Rescale
Stop paying for idle agents
As teams move agents closer to production, they asked for billing that reflects how agents actually work. Agents spend much of their time waiting on a model response, a tool call, or a human decision. Agents should be billed for the work they do, not the time they spend waiting.
The runtime now reclaims memory within minutes of the agent releasing it, and an idle agent scales to zero. For multi-turn agents with natural pauses between interactions, this means up to 68 percent less memory consumed per session. For always-on agents, committed baseline pricing sets a memory baseline per session, billed as a minimum, with room to burst up to four times that baseline on demand. This gives steady workloads a predictable rate at AWS Lambda MicroVM rates. The runtime uses compute more efficiently, so you pay less for the same work. That makes the finance conversation that often gates production rollouts easier to close.
        “The next generation Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime helps us deliver more responsive AI experiences by starting agents faster and using memory more efficiently. Aligning consumption with actual usage gives our clients great confidence to scale agentic solutions while keeping costs connected to real demand.”
— Ashwin Patil, Principal, AI and Data Leader, Deloitte Consulting LLP
        “AgentCore runtime gives us a managed foundation for building agentic products and platforms around our customers’ data, tools, and business processes. The next generation Agentcore runtime makes that foundation more responsive and resource-efficient by restoring initialized environments and reclaiming unused memory. We’re beginning to build on the latest version because the cost and latency reductions make a significant difference in how our customers’ businesses operate.”
— Randall Hunt, CTO, Caylent
Isolation now extends to your data
Many enterprises face a persistent gap in their agent security model. The agent runs inside an isolated session, but the data it requires resides outside that boundary. Long-running agents pick up context as they go: files, credentials, tool outputs, and more. Teams end up building their own rules for how data moves in and out, adding complexity and risk with every new agent.
Isolation that stops at compute is only half a boundary. The next generation AgentCore runtime closes that gap. Each session still runs in its own hardware-isolated environment with its own identity, access policy, and audit trail. Agents can now dynamically mount and save their work to a filesystem, such as an Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) bucket with FUSE support. Your data stays inside the trust boundary for the entire job, governed by a single set of controls you define once.
        “At Okta, the combination of AgentCore runtime and Lambda MicroVMs provide the isolated execution environment and contextual memory our agents need to inspect code, run test suites, and open pull requests within ephemeral sandboxes. Paired with our identity-governed policy controls, AgentCore Runtime and Lambda MicroVMs demonstrate how we can safely scale autonomous engineering agents without risking workspace leakage or privilege escalation.”
— Monica Bajaj, SVP Engineering, Okta
        “From helping car shoppers value a trade-in to helping dealers book service appointments and structure deals, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore powers dozens of agentic solutions across Cox Automotive’s brands. Having a single, governed agent platform lets our teams across our business move from pilot to production with confidence.”
— Chris Dillon, VP, Product and Engineering, Cox Automotive
        “With the next generation of CoCounsel Legal, we set out to build an agentic system that does more than answer questions: it works through a matter end to end, from research to trusted work product. Getting that into customers’ hands quickly meant spending our time on legal reasoning and quality, rather than on running agent infrastructure. With AgentCore Runtime handling the hosting and scaling, we moved from prototype to production fast and kept complete control over how our agents operate and integrate with our existing systems. Our developers build on their preferred frameworks, and Runtime gives us the enterprise-grade reliability and isolation we need to run CoCounsel’s agentic legal workflows at scale for legal professionals around the world.”
— Danilo Tommasina, Distinguished Engineer – Thomson Reuters
Our commitment
The agents that reach production are the ones you trust to act on your behalf, with real data, real stakes, and real accountability. Trust isn’t a feature you add later. It’s the runtime you build on. This release is a step toward that future: bigger sessions, efficient resource use, and storage inside the trust boundary, without loosening the isolation that makes the work trustworthy. By re:Invent, per-session scoping will bind each session to its own storage folder through session-labeled credentials, and we will keep building from there.
Get started
The next generation AgentCore runtime is available today in AWS Regions across North America, South America, Europe, and Asia Pacific. Visit Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to build on it or open the Amazon Bedrock console to start exploring.

Black Friday 2026 – Le téléviseur LG 77C6 "5 étoiles" à 1 999,00 € (-20%)
Le téléviseur LG 77C6 passe sous les 2000 € chez Fnac.com, Boulanger.com et Darty.com soit une baisse d'environ 20% sur le prix habituellement constaté.
Avec sa dalle Tandem Oled héritée du LG G6 sur les grandes diagonales, le LG 77C6 est bien plus haut de gamme que ses cousins de 55 et 65 pouces. Toujours pensé comme l’Oled à bon rapport qualité prix de LG, il s’annonce comme un excellent cru 2026.

- Couverture Rec.2020 au niveau du G6.
- Très bonnes performances en jeu vidéo.
- Quatre ports HDMI 2.1.
- Faible consommation.

Points faibles

Le LG 77C6 n’est pas un simple LG C6 grand format. Grâce à sa dalle Tandem Oled héritée du G6, il change carrément d’univers. Il n’atteint pas totalement le niveau du G6 sur la gestion des reflets et la luminosité, et ce dernier garde pour lui son design mural mieux étudié certes, mais pour qui cherche un très grand Oled polyvalent et premium, ce LG 77C6 est sans doute déjà l’un des modèles les plus intéressants de 2026 en matière de rapport qualité-prix : meilleur que les C6 en 55 et 65 pouces, et moins cher que les G6 en 77 pouces et 83 pouces, que demander de plus ?

articles.title: Vous n’arrivez pas à installer le Patch Tuesday de novembre sur Windows 11 ? Le correctif est en route
articles.text:
Le Patch Tuesday de novembre provoque des erreurs d'installation sur plusieurs PC Windows 11. Microsoft a annoncé une solution, mais le retour à la normale pourrait encore prendre un peu de temps.
Déployée le 10 novembre, la mise à jour de sécurité KB5132061 devait corriger un sacré paquet de vulnérabilités et apporter aux PC compatibles les dernières améliorations de Windows 11. Seulement voilà : depuis sa sortie, les signalements d'échecs d'installation se multiplient. Microsoft vient tout juste de reconnaître l'incident et de confirmer qu’un patch était dans les tuyaux.
Des échecs d’installation persistants
Les difficultés concernent Windows 11 25H2 et 26H2, mais aussi les éditions Entreprise et Éducation de Windows 11 24H2. Comme le rapporte Windows Latest, l'installation de KB5132061 peut progresser jusqu'à 99 % avant d'échouer et d'afficher l'un des codes d'erreur 0x800f0993, 0x80070306 ou 0x800f0989. Les tentatives suivantes aboutissent souvent au même résultat, y compris lorsque la mise à jour est téléchargée manuellement depuis le catalogue Microsoft.
Redmond a bien confirmé le problème et annoncé une réparation automatique, dont le déploiement a débuté le 11 novembre à 19 heures, heure de Paris. Distribuée par Windows Update, elle devrait parvenir aux PC concernés sous 24 à 48 heures, sans intervention de leur part.
Que faire si KB5132061 refuse de s'installer ?
Pour les PC concernés, le plus simple consiste donc à laisser Windows Update faire son travail. Vérifiez que les mises à jour ne sont pas suspendues et que votre ordinateur est bien connecté à Internet.
Vous pouvez également ouvrir les Paramètres > Windows Update, puis cliquer sur « Rechercher des mises à jour » pour vérifier si la réparation est disponible. Si Windows vous propose de télécharger et d'installer KB5132061, suivez les instructions et redémarrez votre PC si nécessaire.
Si le blocage persiste au-delà des 48 heures annoncées par Redmond, vous pourrez lancer l'utilitaire de résolution des problèmes de Windows Update, accessible dans Paramètres > Système > Résolution des problèmes > Autres utilitaires de résolution des problèmes. Cet outil permet de détecter et de corriger les anomalies susceptibles de perturber l'installation des mises à jour. Si rien n'y fait, Microsoft recommande de contacter son assistance.
Le « Patch Tuesday » désigne la vague mensuelle de correctifs publiée par Microsoft, généralement le deuxième mardi du mois. Elle regroupe surtout des mises à jour de sécurité qui corrigent des vulnérabilités exploitées ou exploitables dans Windows et certains composants associés. Ces correctifs peuvent modifier des fichiers système sensibles, des pilotes ou la pile de sécurité, ce qui explique qu’ils aient parfois un impact sur la stabilité ou la compatibilité. En environnement pro, ils sont aussi un élément clé de la conformité (gestion des risques, politiques de patching) et de la réduction de la surface d’attaque.
Ces codes sont des indicateurs techniques renvoyés par Windows Update quand une étape de l’installation échoue (vérification, copie de fichiers, intégration dans l’image système, etc.). Ils pointent souvent vers un problème de composants de mise à jour (Component Store), de dépendances manquantes ou de corruption/état incohérent dans les packages à installer. Le fait que l’installation monte jusqu’à 99 % puis échoue suggère fréquemment un échec au moment de l’« application » finale (commit) et du nettoyage. Sans analyse des journaux (CBS.log, WindowsUpdate.log), le code seul ne suffit pas à diagnostiquer précisément, mais il permet de classer le type d’échec côté maintenance système.
Une réparation automatique est un correctif que Windows Update peut pousser pour rétablir la capacité à installer une mise à jour, sans forcément livrer immédiatement une nouvelle cumulative complète. Concrètement, cela peut prendre la forme d’un petit package correctif, d’une mise à jour de la pile de maintenance (Servicing Stack) ou d’un ajustement de logique côté déploiement (détection/conditions d’installation). L’objectif est de débloquer l’échec d’installation en corrigeant le mécanisme ou le prérequis qui coince, puis de relancer l’installation du correctif principal. C’est différent d’une cumulative, qui embarque directement un ensemble de correctifs fonctionnels et sécurité pour l’OS.

articles.title: Marvel confirme un point crucial sur le grand méchant d’Avengers: Doomsday
articles.text:
Depuis l’officialisation du retour de Robert Downey Jr. au sein du Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU), dans le costume du grand méchant d’Avengers: Doomsday cette fois, une question se pose : son nouveau personnage ne serait-il qu’un variant maléfique de Tony Stark, celui qu’il a incarné pendant plus de dix ans ? La réponse est non, à en croire les propos de Kevin Feige, partagés par le magazine Empire ce jeudi 12 novembre.
« Les gens se sont demandé : « Doom n’est-il qu’un variant d’un autre personnage ? Est-ce juste un raccourci pour faire revenir un autre personnage ? » La réponse est non. C’est Victor Von Doom », explique-t-il. Il prend l’exemple de Chris Evans : « Steve Rogers est-il un variant de Johnny Storm ? », la Torche humaine que l’acteur jouait déjà dans Les 4 Fantastiques en 2005, avant Captain America.
Marvel a pourtant entretenu le doute. Avengers: Endgame Extended ajoute quelques scènes au générique de fin. Dans l’une d’elles, Tony Stark semble forger un masque de Doom. De quoi nourrir la théorie que Kevin Feige balaie aujourd’hui.
Dr Doom sera effrayant dans Avengers: Doomsday
De son côté, Joe Russo, coréalisateur d’Avengers: Doomsday, a dressé un portrait détaillé de Dr Doom, qu’il décrit comme un personnage gothique, puissant et… effrayant. Il révèle : « Il dit : « L’Enfer m’obéit », et il ne plaisante pas. C’est un personnage très puissant qui maîtrise une magie très noire, et il n’hésite pas à vendre son âme pour obtenir ce qu’il veut. Il y a de quoi avoir peur de lui. C’est un père victime d’un traumatisme. Il a perdu un enfant. »
Dans l’une des bandes-annonces d’Avengers: Doomsday, on entend d’ailleurs Sue Storm expliquer d’un ton inquiet : « Victor brillait toujours, où qu’il aille. Il n’était pas le même. Il était gentil et attentionné. Par la suite, tout ce qu’il aimait lui fut enlevé. Je le savais perdu. Mais je n’ai pas compris qu’il était brisé. » Un texte qui matérialise les propos de Joe Russo.
Son frère et coréalisateur, Anthony Russo, précise les différences avec Thanos, le précédent grand méchant des Avengers : « Doom est beaucoup plus motivé par son ego que Thanos. Thanos pensait servir une cause supérieure. » Avengers: Doomsday compte enfin faire honneur au Dr Doom, qui a déjà eu droit à deux versions décevantes au cinéma : Julian McMahon dans Les 4 Fantastiques (2005) et sa suite (2007), puis Toby Kebbell dans le reboot de 2015. Les premières images vont dans ce sens : Marvel y garde le visage de Doom caché sous son masque et sa capuche. Le MCU a besoin de ça pour se relancer après plusieurs années d’errements.
