articles.title: Migrate to Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base with your coding agent | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Migrate to Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base with your coding agent
With a customer-managed knowledge base on Amazon Bedrock, you provision and scale the vector store, tune the embedding model and index settings, and plan capacity for each new data source. The migration guide in the Agent Toolkit for AWS helps you migrate to Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base. Managed Knowledge Base takes over that work and adds new retrieval capabilities, and your team keeps control of the content and the application that uses it.
Moving a production knowledge base means your team maps its configuration, creates the replacement, ingests content, updates the application’s retrieval call, and validates retrieval before switching traffic. To help, we added a knowledge base migration guide to the amazon-bedrock skill in the Agent Toolkit for AWS. The guide gives your coding agent the context to plan the migration with you, starting with read-only discovery and a plan you review line by line. On your approval, the agent creates the new knowledge base and its data sources alongside the original, or writes a migrated infrastructure as code (IaC) template for your pipeline. Ingestion and updating your application’s Retrieve calls stay with you, and your agent can walk you through both.
In this post, we explain why we recommend the move and how the migration guide works, review the prerequisites, install the skill, plan a migration, update the application’s retrieval call, and validate retrieval before cutover.
Why move to Managed Knowledge Base
We recommend Managed Knowledge Base because it balances ease of use, retrieval accuracy, and cost.
AWS runs the store
With a Managed Knowledge Base, Amazon Bedrock handles ingestion, storage, indexing, and retrieval, and the store scales automatically as your content grows. Hybrid search, which combines keyword and semantic matching, is always on, with no index to configure. The knowledge base includes a managed embedding model, a managed reranker, and a built-in parser for multimodal file types.
You can still bring your own Amazon Bedrock embedding model when you create the knowledge base. On each retrieval request, you choose the managed reranker, an Amazon Bedrock reranking model, or no reranking. The managed reranker requires the managed embedding model.
Built-in capabilities
Managed Knowledge Base includes capabilities you’d otherwise build yourself:
- Native connectors ingest content directly from sources such as Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), Microsoft SharePoint, and Atlassian Confluence. For the current list, see supported connectors. After the first full sync, later syncs pick up only changes, on demand or on a schedule. The Managed Knowledge Base includes a deletion safeguard to help protect against accidental bulk removal of indexed content.
- Access control list (ACL) awareness ingests document permissions with the content, so retrieval returns only what the signed-in user can access. For connectors that support it, such as Microsoft SharePoint and Atlassian Confluence, a real-time check against the source also catches permission changes since the last sync. ACL awareness doesn’t authenticate users, so your application must verify and pass the user’s identity.
- Agentic retrieval answers questions that a single search can’t by handling multi-part questions and retrieving iteratively. It can search more than one knowledge base in a single request.
- Integration with AgentCore Gateway, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, exposes your knowledge base as a target. Any client that supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP) can then query the knowledge base, and the gateway handles authentication.
- Resource-based policies let applications in other AWS accounts use one team’s knowledge base. Scope each policy to the specific roles that call the knowledge base, and grant only the actions they use, such as bedrock:Retrieve.
Agentic retrieval, AgentCore Gateway integration, and resource-based policies are not available on customer-managed knowledge bases. For the AWS Regions where managed knowledge bases are available, and the features that AWS GovCloud (US-West) doesn’t support, see Supported AWS Regions.
Higher quotas
As of this writing, higher default quotas change how you can organize content. With 200 data sources per knowledge base, you can group related content in one knowledge base. With 10,000 knowledge bases per account, per Region, each team or product line can use a separate knowledge base.
| Default quota | Customer-managed | Managed | 
| Knowledge bases per account, per Region | 100 | 10,000 | 
| Data sources per knowledge base | 5 | 200 | 
| Concurrent ingestion jobs per knowledge base | 1 | 50 | 
| Query input characters | 1,000 | 10,000 | 
For current values, see Amazon Bedrock endpoints and quotas and Service quotas for managed knowledge bases.
Pay for what you store and retrieve
Cost is one of three things teams weigh when they consider this move, alongside customizability and direct control of the vector store. On a customer-managed knowledge base, you choose, provision, scale, and update the vector and text stores, and pay separately for the infrastructure you select. On a Managed Knowledge Base, those stages are part of the service, and storage and retrieval are metered directly.
The pricing models can differ too. With a customer-managed knowledge base, storage and retrieval charges depend on the vector store you choose. Some stores charge for provisioned or minimum capacity, and others, such as Amazon S3 Vectors, a capability of Amazon S3, charge only for what you use. A Managed Knowledge Base is priced on what you store and retrieve, so cost follows real usage. Usage-based pricing can fit enterprise question-answering, policy, and support knowledge bases that run at low utilization. For current rates, see Amazon Bedrock pricing. For the parsers available on a customer-managed knowledge base and how each is billed, see Parsing options for your data source.
| Cost driver | Customer-managed knowledge base | Managed Knowledge Base | 
| Vector storage | Priced separately by your chosen store. A provisioned retrieval service can have a minimum idle cost even at low volume | Included in the base storage rate of $5 per GB per month | 
| Multimodal document parsing | Requires Amazon Bedrock Data Automation, billed by page or image, or a foundation model, billed by token. Text-only parsing is free. | Included | 
| Embedding generation | Billed separately at your embedding model’s rate | Included with the default model. Charges apply only if you choose a custom model | 
| Ingestion, sync, and re-sync compute | Re-embedding, orchestration code, and indexing compute spikes on each sync add recurring cost | Included, with incremental sync that processes only new and changed content | 
| Connectors | Building and running custom connectors can add compute cost | Native connectors are included | 
| Standard retrieval | No Amazon Bedrock charge per query. Your vector store can charge per query, as Amazon S3 Vectors does. | $1 per 1,000 retrieval requests | 
| Reranking | Amazon Rerank is charged at $1 per 1,000 queries. A custom reranking model is billed at its own rate | Included in the $1 per 1,000 retrieval requests | 
| Agentic retrieval | You build the agentic workflow on a Bedrock model, which can cost roughly $18 to $24 per 1,000 queries before development and maintenance. Because model usage is billed by token, the price per query varies. | Agentic retrieval costs an additional $4 per 1,000 queries on top of the underlying retrieval calls, including multi-shot retrieval, reranking, and answer generation. Depending on the number of underlying retrieval calls, the total can range from roughly $6 to $9 per 1,000 queries. | 
Rates are only part of the total cost of ownership. On a customer-managed knowledge base, your team provisions, scales, and operates each stage as a separate resource. A Managed Knowledge Base consolidates them into one resource, with a default embedding model, foundation model, and reranker, and with per-knowledge-base rate limits by default. You manage the content and the application that uses it, and Amazon Bedrock operates the managed storage, embedding model, foundation model, and reranker.
Solution overview
A customer-managed knowledge base uses the VECTOR type, with a vector store you configure. A Managed Knowledge Base uses the MANAGED type. The migration guide directs your agent to create a new MANAGED knowledge base alongside the original without modifying or deleting the original during migration. Using the guide’s map, your agent writes a plan that lists which settings remain unchanged, which Managed handles differently, and which application changes you need to make. As Figure 1 shows, the original keeps serving every request while your team ingests content, validates, and cuts over.
How the migration guide works
The guide separates planning from implementation. In Explore mode, your agent answers questions about Managed Knowledge Base and can inspect your configuration with read-only calls, so you can estimate the effort. In Migration mode, the guide takes your agent through checkpoints:
- Introduce and choose. Your agent explains what it will and won’t touch. Choose the mode, a live knowledge base or IaC source, and a plain (default) or technical explanation style.
- Identify. Confirm the account and AWS Region. Your agent flags over-broad credentials, asks whether you want a cost analysis, and creates an output directory.
- Discover. Your agent reads the knowledge base and data sources with read-only calls, or reads your template files.
- Plan. Review the plan and application changes. By default, your agent stops here.
- Implement, if requested. For a live build, approve the exact preview of the provisioning script, and approve again if it changes. For IaC, your agent writes a migrated template and reports which schema checks ran.
- Handoff. Review what was produced and your team’s remaining steps.
As Figure 2 shows, resource creation stays separate from ingestion and cutover.
Review the configuration mapping
The guide maps each setting to preserve your data sources, filters, and chunking behavior when the managed type uses a different configuration. The plan classifies each setting:
- 1:1. The new knowledge base uses the same setting.
- Adjusted. Managed uses a different setting for the same outcome, and the plan applies the substitution.
- Blocked. There is no managed path today. Your agent excludes that knowledge base from the build, explains why, and points you to AWS Support. Other knowledge bases in the same run can proceed.
Compare chunking on your own content when you validate.
Review the permissions and generated changes
Discovery, planning, and the entire IaC path need only read-only credentials. For a live build, the guide directs your agent to propose a scoped policy that explicitly denies changes to the original knowledge base, and to never ask for administrator or full-access permissions. It also directs your agent to change only resources it created, reference secrets by Amazon Resource Name (ARN), and ignore instructions found in the data it reads. Review the generated AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policy and provisioning script before you approve the run. After the build, check what the agent did in AWS CloudTrail event history, which keeps 90 days of management events. Each event records the API call, such as CreateKnowledgeBase, and the identity that made it.
For the optional cost analysis, your agent compares current spend with a Managed Knowledge Base estimate using current AWS prices. It uses read-only inputs, including Amazon CloudWatch metrics, Amazon S3 object sizes, and AWS Cost Explorer. Each figure is labeled as measured, supplied by you, or estimated.
Prerequisites
Use separate credentials for planning and for any approved resource creation.
- A compatible development environment with the Agent Toolkit for AWS.
- The AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI), configured with a least-privilege, read-only profile.
- Access to the original knowledge base configuration or its IaC files.
- For the optional live build: 
         
  - A scoped build profile, using the policy the guide recommends.
  - An IAM service role for the new knowledge base. The guide gives your agent the trust policy and permissions to help you create it.
  - Python 3 with boto3 for the generated provisioning script.
The Agent Toolkit for AWS works with compatible development environments and its repository on GitHub lists the available skills. Examples in this post use AWS CLI 2.37 and boto3 1.43.32.
Install the skill
Follow the Agent Toolkit for AWS getting-started instructions for your coding agent. The add-skill command installs the amazon-bedrock skill to the coding agents it detects. Add --agent to target one, for example --agent kiro.
After installation, your agent loads the migration guide when you describe a migration task. The following prompts are illustrative inputs, not transcripts.
Plan the migration
Choose the path that matches how you maintain the source.
| Path | What your agent reads | What it produces | AWS changes | 
| Explore | Documentation, and optionally your knowledge base (read-only) | Answers in the conversation | None | 
| Live knowledge base | Your knowledge base and data sources (read-only) | A plan, and optionally a new Managed Knowledge Base alongside the original | Only after you approve the exact preview | 
| Infrastructure as code | Your AWS CloudFormation template, AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) synthesized template, or Terraform configuration | A migrated template in the same format | None. Your pipeline deploys it | 
To start in Explore mode, ask a question:
When you’re ready, choose the live or IaC path.
Migrate a live knowledge base
Ask for a plan before authorizing resource creation:
Confirm the account and Region, then review the plan’s mappings and application changes. By default, the new knowledge base takes the original’s name with a -managed suffix. To build it, confirm the service role exists, switch to the build profile, inspect the provisioning script and its preview, and approve. Your agent runs the script, which creates the knowledge base and data sources, and reports their status.
Migrate infrastructure as code
Point your agent at the source template or configuration:
Your agent writes the migrated file to the output directory, deploys nothing, and shows you the diff. To keep the diff, ask your agent to save it. Run terraform init -backend=false and terraform validate before deployment. Your agent can walk you through both commands, but the guide leaves these checks to you because terraform init downloads the large AWS provider. Before you apply the deployment plan, check that it keeps the original resources you need for rollback.
Example conversation
The migration runs as a conversation. Before reading anything, your agent states its scope and asks how to proceed:
The plan summary shows each mapping, the caller changes, and the decisions you need to make:
For a live build, your agent stops at a preview, and the approval command requires the plan’s hash:
Example exchanges are lightly edited, with identifiers replaced.
Update the application’s retrieval call
Your application uses the same Retrieve operation for both types. The managed request targets the new knowledge base ID and replaces vectorSearchConfiguration with managedSearchConfiguration. Passing vectorSearchConfiguration to a managed knowledge base returns a validation error. Managed retrieval always uses hybrid search, so the managed request shape has no overrideSearchType field. Metadata filters keep the same syntax, except that managed knowledge bases don’t support the startsWith and stringContains operators. For the full syntax, see the Retrieve API reference.
The example assumes both knowledge bases contain the locale metadata used by the filter.
Validate retrieval and cut over
Evaluate the new knowledge base while the application still uses the original.
- If using IaC, review and deploy the target configuration through your pipeline.
- Sync each data source and review any failures. See Sync your data.
- Grant your application’s runtime IAM role bedrock:Retrieve on the new knowledge base ARN, and keep its access to the original knowledge base so you can roll back.
- Run representative queries against both knowledge bases with Retrieve, using that role. The two types use different score scales. Managed scores also depend on rerankingModelType, which defaults to MANAGED with the managed embedding model and to NONE with a custom one. Tune thresholds per mode, and hold the mode constant while comparing.
- Test metadata filters and permission-aware retrieval where used, including content the signed-in user shouldn’t receive. On an ACL-enabled data source, requests without userContext.userId (the user’s email) return no results.
- After acceptance, deploy the new knowledge base ID and request shape. Keep the original knowledge base, with current content, and application configuration through your rollback period.
For each query, check whether both return the same top document and how much results overlap. A short script can report pass or fail against criteria such as a matching top document on at least 90 percent of queries and no zero-result queries on the managed knowledge base. Tune that threshold for your workload. For other retrieval quality measures, such as context relevance and context coverage, see Use metrics to understand RAG system performance.
Watch for these differences when you compare results:
- Normalize source locations before comparison. A customer-managed knowledge base can return s3://bucket/key in location.s3Location.uri, and a managed knowledge base can return an https:// URL. Compare by object key.
- Compare the top result instead of assuming equal result counts. The two knowledge base types can return different numbers of results, and numberOfResults sets a maximum rather than a guarantee. Compare the top document, and review each query where it changes. For details, see Configure and customize queries for managed knowledge bases.
- Map renamed system metadata keys. For example, replace x-amz-bedrock-kb-data-source-id with _data_source_id in comparison code. Your own metadata attributes keep their names. For details, see Configure and customize queries for managed knowledge bases.
Clean up
If you complete the migration, retire the original only after the rollback period and a dependency review. Keep the source documents and buckets the managed knowledge base ingests from, and storage that other workloads use. Clean up IaC-managed resources through their owning template.
If you end the evaluation instead, keep the original and delete what you created in this order:
- Delete each managed data source and wait until it’s gone.
- Delete the managed knowledge base and wait until it’s gone.
- If you created the service role only for this evaluation, delete its inline policy, then the role.
- With a customer managed key, check aws kms list-grants for grants Amazon Bedrock created, which can remain after the knowledge base is deleted.
- Keep any S3 bucket that another knowledge base still reads.
Deletion protection on a managed data source limits how much a sync can delete, not whether you can delete the data source. Deleting the original knowledge base doesn’t delete its vector store, which continues to incur charges until you remove it. See Delete an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base.
Conclusion
With Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base, your team no longer runs a vector store or manages the underlying retrieval infrastructure. With the migration guide in the amazon-bedrock skill, you ask your agent for a plan, review it, and approve only the resources you want built.
To get started, set up the Agent Toolkit for AWS and ask your agent for a read-only assessment of your knowledge base. After migration, explore agentic retrieval for multi-part questions. To learn more, see Build enterprise search for agents with Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base on the AWS Machine Learning Blog.

articles.title: Black Friday : comment profiter des bons plans sans saturer sa boîte mail ? Proton Pass a la réponse (et elle est en promotion)
articles.text:
Ajouter 10 % de remise supplémentaire à un panier qui est déjà en promotion durant le Black Friday, forcément, c’est tentant. Certes, cela implique de vous inscrire à la newsletter du site… Mais après tout, pourquoi pas ? Ça ne coûte pas grand-chose, non ? Le problème, c’est qu’en acceptant ce genre de proposition tout au long du mois de novembre, votre boîte mail va se remplir de messages promotionnels et de sollicitations à une vitesse folle.
Évidemment, vous pouvez créer plusieurs boîtes mail pour plusieurs usages. Mais jongler entre elles devient vite fastidieux.
La solution la plus pratique consiste à utiliser une plateforme qui permet de créer une infinité d’alias d’adresse mail, de les associer à des mots de passe générés aléatoirement et de tout stocker dans un unique coffre-fort chiffré. Et c’est exactement ce que propose Proton Pass.
Profitez des codes promo en gardant votre adresse mail pour vous
Un alias est une adresse mail qui vient « masquer » votre véritable adresse. Vous pouvez la créer en quelques clics via Proton Pass, avant de la communiquer à une boutique en ligne. Les messages envoyés à cette adresse sont ensuite transférés vers votre boîte habituelle. Vous continuez donc à recevoir vos mails au même endroit, sans révéler votre adresse principale au marchand.
Dans le cas d’un code promo envoyé en échange de l’inscription à une newsletter, au lieu de renseigner votre adresse personnelle, vous créez un alias avec Proton Pass. Le code promotionnel arrive dans votre boîte de réception. Si vous utilisez aussi cet alias pour votre compte client, les confirmations de commande et les informations d’expédition suivent le même chemin.
En optant pour l’offre Proton Pass Plus, vous avez la possibilité de créer un nombre illimité d’alias. Cela signifie que vous pouvez choisir de créer une adresse différente pour chaque boutique ou chaque plateforme sur laquelle vous désirez vous inscrire, sans avoir à arbitrer entre les services.
Avec Proton Pass, chaque boutique a son mot de passe
La période du Black Friday est également synonyme d’achats opportunistes, réalisés à bon prix sur des sites rarement fréquentés le reste de l’année. Et pour ne pas passer à côté d’une offre séduisante, vous pouvez être tenté d’utiliser le même mot de passe que celui d’un autre site sur lequel vous avez commandé la veille.
Cette démarche est rapide, mais elle n’est pas du tout sécurisée, puisqu’en cas de fuite de données, vos autres comptes qui utilisent le même mot de passe risquent d’être eux-mêmes piratés. Si vous avez du mal à être imaginatif au moment de choisir un mot de passe, et surtout, à le retenir, Proton Pass peut une nouvelle fois vous aider.
Le service peut générer un mot de passe propre à chaque boutique, puis l’enregistrer avec l’adresse utilisée. Vous n’avez pas à mémoriser cette combinaison : le gestionnaire la conserve en lieu sûr. Lors de votre prochaine connexion, le remplissage automatique peut reprendre ces identifiants sur les sites qui prennent cette fonctionnalité en charge.
Dans ce genre de situation, l’alias et le mot de passe sont donc complémentaires : le premier vous évite de communiquer votre adresse principale, tandis que le second protège votre accès au compte marchand.
Vos informations de paiement à portée de main
Pendant le Black Friday, la carte bancaire chauffe plus que d’habitude. Proton Pass peut la stocker dans son coffre chiffré. Vous pouvez ainsi retrouver vos informations de paiement au même endroit que vos mots de passe et les autres données utiles à vos achats. Le service propose le remplissage automatique des formulaires compatibles et vous permet de retrouver vos accès sur vos différents appareils.
Proton Pass fonctionne sur Android, iOS, Windows, macOS et Linux, ainsi qu’en extension pour Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge ou Brave. La synchronisation se fait sur un nombre illimité d’appareils. Une carte enregistrée sur l’ordinateur est donc disponible sur le smartphone au moment de valider le panier.
La fiche d’une boutique peut également accueillir une note : un code promotionnel à utiliser plus tard, un numéro de fidélité ou une référence utile. Ces informations restent à portée de main lorsque vous en avez besoin, sans avoir à jongler entre plusieurs applications et autres mails promotionnels.
Proton Pass protège le contenu de vos coffres par un chiffrement de bout en bout : identifiants, notes et informations de paiement sont chiffrés de manière à ce que même Proton ne puisse pas les lire.
Après les promotions, faites le ménage
Une fois le Black Friday terminé, vous pouvez facilement faire le ménage dans vos inscriptions aux newsletters, en gérant vos alias d’adresse email.
Si le désabonnement ne suffit pas et que vous vous rendez compte que l’un de vos alias est utilisé par d’autres sites sans votre autorisation, vous pouvez tout simplement le désactiver.
Proton Pass Plus à 1,99 euro par mois pendant le Black Friday
Jusqu’au 30 novembre, l’abonnement à Proton Pass Plus est à 1,99 euro par mois pendant les douze premiers mois, soit 23,88 euros facturés en une fois pour la première année. Cela représente une réduction de 60 % par rapport au tarif mensuel habituel de 4,99 euros.
L’abonnement est ensuite renouvelé automatiquement, sauf si vous décidez de résilier dans votre espace client, aux conditions prévues par l’offre. De quoi vous mettre dans les bonnes conditions pour votre chasse aux bons plans de fin d’année.

articles.title: Jensen Huang exits Nvidia after 33 years
articles.text:
Jensen Huang exits Nvidia after 33 years; Kia India plans $2B investment in Andhra Pradesh
The transition comes at a critical juncture for Nvidia, whose chips have become the backbone of the global AI boom.
Dear Reader,
It's the end of an era at Nvidia. Co-founder Jensen Huang has stepped down as CEO after 33 years at the helm, following a turbulent week of controversy and board probes. More on Huang's sudden exit, the interim leadership and what comes next for the AI chip giant below.
After high-profile Indian public listings from portfolio giants like Swiggy and Amagi Media Labs, global investment firm Norwest has just closed its largest fund with a war chest of $4 billion. With its 18th fund, the 65-year-old firm is doubling down on its multi-stage strategy across India, the US, and Israel. The fund will back technology, healthcare and consumer businesses, from early-stage startups to companies preparing for public listings.
Closer home, CommonFloor co-founder Vikas Malpani reflects on why the company's $200 million acquisition by Quikr felt more like a loss than a victory. Rather than taking on advisory roles, he decided to start from scratch to launch social platform Leher before establishing Garvik AI. As the CEO of Garvik AI, he uses AI across sectors such as banking, edtech and real estate.
Meanwhile, a year after Lenskart's IPO, co-founder and CEO Peyush Bansal says the company has yet to fulfil its original mission of making clear vision accessible to everyone. In a LinkedIn post, Bansal announced that Lenskart would stop charging extra for blue-light filtering lenses and offer prescription glasses to 100,000 children for a Rs 199 fitting fee. “What we have done is not enough,” he said.
Lastly, Mumbai-based investment manager ValueQuest Investment Advisors has made a total commitment of Rs 775 crore to three Indian businesses in defence technology, precision engineering, and power infrastructure. It has now backed Sagar Defence Engineering and Rational Engineers and also added to its earlier investment in TASE Global. The Rs 775 crore is a portfolio commitment, not a single company’s fundraise.
In today’s newsletter:
- Nvidia's leadership shake-up and what comes next
- Kia India plans $2B investment in Andhra Pradesh
Here’s your trivia for today: What name was given to the small robotic rover deployed onto the lunar surface by ISRO's Chandrayaan-3 lander in August 2023? (Scroll down for answer)
News
Jensen Huang exits Nvidia at a crucial time
Following a turbulent week of board probes and scandal, Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang has stepped down as president, CEO, and board member effective immediately. His resignation brings his 33-year run at the helm to a sudden close as investors increasingly question the AI boom.
Longtime CFO Colette Kress is stepping in as interim chief executive while the board searches both internally and externally for a permanent successor. She joined Nvidia in 2013 after nearly 25 years in finance roles at technology companies including Cisco and Microsoft.
Key takeaways:
- The transition comes at a critical juncture for Nvidia, whose chips have become the backbone of the global AI boom. Huang helped transform the company from a graphics-chip maker into one of the world's most influential technology businesses. His successor will have to sustain that momentum as competition intensifies and customers look to develop more of their own AI chips.
- On November 8, Huang apologised in a company-published message for being unfaithful to his wife and pledged to co-operate with an independent board inquiry into reports that he had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort.
- Nvidia's CUDA software ecosystem has helped establish its dominance in AI computing, even as rivals develop alternatives.
Automobiles
Kia India plans $2B investment in Andhra Pradesh
Kia India has committed a combined investment of $2 billion, along with its supplier partners, to set up its second manufacturing facility in Andhra Pradesh. The company said the project would also help build India's manufacturing base, generate employment, and support the wider auto industry.
Key takeaways:
- The factory will be located in Anantapur, the same district that houses Kia's current plant.
- Kia India is targeting early 2030 for production to begin, with the plant carrying out stamping, welding, painting and assembly.
- Kia and its suppliers will together occupy 465 acres on the new site. The company expects the facility to support roughly 12,000 jobs, both direct and indirect.
News & updates
- Deeptech hub: Keralam wants to build its startup ecosystem and lead from the front, especially in deeptech and AI. At the inauguration of Huddle Global 2026, a beachside startup festival of the Keralam government, Chief Minister V D Satheesan said, “Our next task is to take Kerala's companies to the world. Kerala does not need the most startups. It must be the place where startups grow stronger.”
- Funding: Investment platform Canonicus Capital has announced the first close of its Special Situations Fund at Rs 192 crore, against a target corpus of Rs 500 crore. Launched in 2025, the Special Situations Fund builds on the work of Canonicus Capital's Fund I through which it had raised and deployed Rs 311 crore.
What name was given to the small robotic rover deployed onto the lunar surface by ISRO's Chandrayaan-3 lander in August 2023?
Answer: Pragyan

articles.title: Google corrige d'urgence une 8e faille Chrome exploitée par des pirates, installez vite la mise à jour
articles.text:
Début de semaine, Google a déployé une nouvelle mise à jour de Chrome sur Windows, macOS et Linux. Celle-ci corrige neuf failles de sécurité dans le code du navigateur, dont une vulnérabilité zero day. Il s’agit d’une faille qui a été exploitée par des pirates avant que Google ne puisse réagir et lancer un correctif.
Dans son bulletin de sécurité, Google indique avoir pris « connaissance de l’existence » d’une tactique d’exploitation qui permet de lancer des attaques « dans la nature ». En clair, des cybercriminels se servent déjà de cette brèche pour attaquer des internautes.
À lire aussi : Ces 319 extensions Chrome ont espionné des millions d’internautes pendant 10 ans
Une faille dans la mémoire de Chrome
La vulnérabilité se situe dans le composant de Chrome chargé de lire le XML, le format de fichier texte qui sert à ranger et échanger des informations entre logiciels. Google précise qu’il s’agit d’une faille de type « use after free », une erreur de gestion de la mémoire très fréquente dans les navigateurs. Concrètement, Chrome libère une zone de la mémoire, mais continue ensuite de s’en servir. Un attaquant peut alors en profiter pour glisser ses propres données dans la mémoire.
Pour exploiter cette faille, les pirates doivent mettre au point une page web piégée, taillée pour déclencher la cyberattaque sans que l’internaute ne se rende compte de rien. Google a jugé la faille de sévérité « élevée ». Comme d’habitude, Google ne donne pas beaucoup de détails sur les cyberattaques en cours, « tant que la majorité des utilisateurs n’aura pas installé le correctif ».
Dans la foulée, Google a aussi colmaté cinq autres failles de sévérité élevée. Les défaillances concernent le système de fichiers WebGL, le moteur d’affichage, le processeur graphique et V8, le moteur qui exécute le code JavaScript des sites web. Deux failles de sévérité moyenne, liées au processeur graphique, ont aussi été corrigées par Google.
À lire aussi : DeepSeek aurait réussi à contourner les défenses de Chrome en 12 heures
Une huitième faille zero day en 2026
C’est la huitième faille zero day corrigée dans Chrome depuis le début de l’année 2026. La première, découverte en février, touchait la gestion des polices d’écriture. En mars, le géant a colmaté deux brèches dans Skia, la bibliothèque graphique du navigateur, et dans le moteur V8.
Une faille dans WebGPU a suivi en avril, puis une nouvelle brèche de V8 en juin. En septembre, Google a même dû corriger deux autres failles zero day dans le moteur V8, à quelques jours d’intervalle. Avec cette nouvelle brèche, Google a déjà corrigé autant de failles exploitées par des hackers en 2026 que l’an dernier.
Mettez vite à jour Google Chrome
Pour vous protéger des pirates, il est vivement conseillé d’installer la mise à jour 157.0.8103.50 ou .51 sur Windows et macOS, et 157.0.8103.50 sur Linux, au plus vite. Pour l’installer, cliquez sur les trois points en haut à droite de Chrome, puis allez dans « Aide » puis dans « À propos de Google Chrome ». Le navigateur télécharge alors tout seul la dernière version disponible. Cliquez ensuite sur « Relancer » pour installer les correctifs.
 👉🏻 Suivez l’actualité tech en temps réel : ajoutez 01net à vos sources sur Google, et abonnez-vous à notre canal WhatsApp.
Source : Google

articles.title: Jensen Huang’s exit puts Nvidia’s support for open source in question | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The open source community just lost one of its strongest advocates.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after he admitted to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, raising concerns about U.S. national security and the motives behind the executive’s support for softer chip export controls on China.
Huang has been a staunch supporter of open source AI, framing the ecosystem as good for safety, innovation, diffusion, and sovereignty. And as frontier AI labs increasingly move to reduce their reliance on Nvidia and build their own chips, supporting open source is also a good way for the company to diversify its customer base by selling chips to nation-states, enterprises, and any organization that wants to own its own models.
Still, Huang’s resignation raises questions about whether Nvidia will carry on his legacy by continuing to support the open model community.
Huang’s departure also comes as Nvidia has yet to finalize a deal to acquire open source platform Hugging Face for $13 billion. Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue said in a post on X that the company would continue to fight for open source, whatever happens next.
Nvidia also agreed to pay $6 billion for a non-exclusive license for open AI coding startup Poolside’s technology.
Within Nvidia, Huang pushed for the development of the Nemotron family of open-weight AI models built for long-running agentic AI systems and reasoning workloads — potential competitors to closed frontier models. One company insider told TechCrunch that they don’t expect a change in leadership to have an impact on Nemotron development.
Huang also backed companies that would make American open models more competitive, investing in startups like Reflection AI and Thinking Machines Lab.
Huang’s influence extended beyond Nvidia’s investments and product roadmap. He also emerged as one of the most prominent voices pushing back against Washington’s efforts to restrict the open AI ecosystem.
Earlier this year, Huang wrote an open letter signed by 25 companies, including Microsoft, Meta, IBM, and Palantir, urging the U.S. government not to over-restrict open-weight AI models, many of which come from China.
The impetus for that letter was Washington’s debate over how the U.S. should respond to allegations that Chinese AI labs are stealing intellectual property from American counterparts like Anthropic and OpenAI, both of which have reportedly appealed directly to Washington on the matter, urging stronger protections.
That combination of Huang’s personal visibility and Nvidia’s market power made him the strongest counterweight to arguments from closed-model providers like Anthropic and OpenAI, which have advocated for greater restrictions on advanced AI models due to safety reasons.
Without Huang, the concern among open source community members is that whoever takes over will be more cautious. Nvidia has named CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. It’s not clear how Kress will approach the Hugging Face deal or support for the open model ecosystem, but founder-driven priorities tend to get a downgrade when leadership changes.
Huang’s exit could also strengthen the arguments of those in Washington who are arguing for tougher restrictions on Chinese AI companies, particularly as the scandal surrounding his relationship with Alice Huang, the Megaspeed executive and alleged spy, puts renewed scrutiny on his efforts to loosen chip export controls.
Restrictions on open-weight models from China could kneecap competition for American companies, the most powerful of which have kept their models closed.
Still, supporting open source isn’t simply a passion project Huang pursued out of idealism. It’s increasingly central to Nvidia’s business strategy.
As some of Nvidia’s biggest customers, including Google and OpenAI, develop their own chips, Nvidia has an incentive to cultivate a much broader ecosystem of AI developers and customers.
More players training, fine-tuning, and running models mean more GPUs sold, and less dependence on a handful of frontier labs.
Huang may be gone, but Nvidia still needs an open AI ecosystem. The question now is whether that commitment can survive without the man who made it a priority.
TechCrunch has reached out to Nvidia for comment.
This article has been updated with information from an Nvidia employee.

articles.title: New York forces T-Mobile to remove 50GB cap that throttled low-income home internet users to 600Kbps
articles.text:
What just happened? Cheap home internet isn't much use if it slows to a crawl a few days into the month. New York says that's exactly what T-Mobile was offering low-income households, imposing a 50GB monthly cap before slashing download speeds to under 1 Mbps. The carrier has now agreed to remove the restriction after state investigators found it violated the Affordable Broadband Act.
Governor Kathy Hochul and Attorney General Letitia James announced the agreement on November 9. The law requires qualifying households to be offered broadband costing $15 per month with download speeds of at least 25 Mbps, or $20 for at least 200 Mbps. Those prices include taxes and equipment fees.
The agreement covers home broadband delivered over T-Mobile's cellular network, rather than its mobile phone plans. Customers shouldn't expect the settlement to change their handset data allowances.
T-Mobile's $15 fixed wireless plan came with a fairly big catch. According to the signed settlement, customers who used 50GB saw their maximum download speed fall from 25 Mbps to just 600 Kbps, a reduction of 97.6%. State officials estimate a typical customer could burn through the allowance in about four days, which isn't what you'd call a month's worth of usable broadband.
There were other problems, too. Investigators found the discounted plan was restricted to homes eligible for T-Mobile's 5G service. That excluded customers in some 4G areas where the company already sold full-price home internet capable of reaching 25 Mbps.
Finding the cheaper option wasn't straightforward, either. The state says T-Mobile coded its plan information webpage to prevent it from appearing in search engine results. That's an interesting approach to a law that requires providers to make reasonable efforts to advertise their affordable offerings.
Under the settlement, T-Mobile has 120 days to stop deliberately reducing eligible subscribers' speeds below the required minimum and expand the plans across its home internet footprint. Temporary slowdowns caused solely by network congestion remain allowed. The company must also make its plan webpage discoverable through search engines.
T-Mobile neither admitted nor denied the state's findings. It told Ars Technica it was updating the offering to meet New York's requirements while keeping the same price, but didn't explain why it imposed the restrictions.
New York began enforcing the law in January 2025, following years of industry opposition. The Supreme Court had declined to hear the industry's challenge the previous month. Now it's just a case of making sure customers actually receive the service it promises.

articles.title: Save $350 on this all-AMD 1440p gaming desktop with 9800X3D, RX 9070 — also features 32GB of RAM and a 1TB SSD for just $1,949
articles.text:
Save $350 on this all-AMD 1440p gaming desktop with 9800X3D, RX 9070 — also features 32GB of RAM and a 1TB SSD for just $1,949
A rare gaming PC deal
Best Buy has just slashed $350 off this all-AMD CyberPowerPC gaming desktop, scoring you a powerful 9800X3D build for less. Right now, this gaming PC with an RX 9070 16GB is just $1949.
● Check out this deal at Best Buy
This is a fantastic gaming PC for 1440p, with a strong supporting cast of specs. The 32GB of RAM in this PC alone is worth $450 right now, and a 1 TB SSD will set you back $250.
This is a rig for 1440p gaming. This CyberPowerPC machine has an AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D, an Nvidia GeForce RX 9070 GPU, 32GB of DDR5 5600 RAM, and a 1TB SSD. It ships with Wi-Fi 6 connectivity.
The Ryzen 7 9800X3D is the headline spec of this build. With its generous 3D cache, it's one of the very best gaming CPUs on the market right now, edged out only by the 9850X3D in terms of gaming performance, as you can see from our bench database below. With 8 cores and 16 threads, this CPU will chew through any gaming title thanks to that 3D cache, which means the chip has to rely much less heavily on RAM, drastically improving performance.
The GPU in this build is the RX 9070 with a generous 16GB of VRAM. Sadly, it isn't the more potent XT version, but this is still a great gaming GPU, averaging nearly 75 FPS in our 19-game rasterization benchmark suite at 1440p. 4K performance was around 41 FPS without frame generation, too, so there is some 4K potential.
The PC also comes with 32GB of DDR5 5600 memory, a slight compromise over 6000 speeds but one you shouldn't notice too much. You also get a 1TB PCIe 4.0 SSD for your operating system and storing games, plenty to get you started.
It's all held together by a B650 motherboard, and ships inside one of CyberPower's more impressive cases, along with fans aplenty. You also get Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth, lots of USB ports, HDMI and DisplayPort connectivity, and a liquid cooler for the CPU, as well as an 850-watt power supply. And, of course, a copy of Windows 11.
With Black Friday still a couple of weeks away, this is one of the best gaming PC deals going right now and one not to be missed.

articles.title: Fairphone CEO says new US carrier partnership will free consumers from ’a system built on planned obsolescence and constant, expensive upgrades'
articles.text:
Fairphone signs first US carrier partnership, making the easily repairable Fairphone 6 Plus more widely available: ‘For too long, US consumers have been captives of a system built on planned obsolescence’
Giving the Fairphone 6 Plus a boost
- The Fairphone 6 Plus is now available via Boost Mobile in the US
- This gives buyers a way to get the phone without paying one lump sum
- The Fairphone 6 Plus is modular and therefore easily repairable
Having offered repairable, long-lasting smartphones to consumers in Europe for years, Fairphone finally got a foothold in the US with the Fairphone 6 Plus, which launched in both regions back in August. But until now, you could only buy the phone outright in the US, limiting its appeal in a market dominated by carrier plans.
Today, though, that’s changed, as the company has announced that it's partnered with Boost Mobile to offer the Fairphone 6 Plus with a monthly plan through the carrier’s network. And with Boost Mobile having over seven million subscribers, that massively increases Fairphone’s potential audience.
This is a particularly important step for the Fairphone 6 Plus specifically, whose $649.99 retail price is quite expensive for the specs on offer — so splitting that figure across the length of a contract could make it seem more affordable and, Fairphone hopes, more popular.
And in the long run, you could save money with Fairphone anyway, since the Fairphone 6 Plus is designed to be held onto for a long time — it's got 12 user-replaceable parts, long-term software support, and a five-year warranty.
Built to last
Raymond van Eck, CEO of Fairphone, said of this Boost Mobile partnership that “for too long, US consumers have been captives of a system built on planned obsolescence and constant, expensive upgrades,” adding that “we’re thrilled to team up with Boost Mobile to give more Americans access to a device built to be opened, repaired, and kept alive for years.”
The Fairphone 6 Plus has a mid-range Snapdragon 7s Gen 4 chipset, 12GB of RAM, Android 16 — with software support promised through 2033 — and a 6.31-inch (1116 x 2484) 120Hz screen.
It also has a 50MP main camera, a 13MP ultra-wide, a 32MP front-facing camera, a 4,415mAh battery, 256GB of storage, and a microSD card slot.

If you like the sound of it, you can grab it in Cobalt Blue, Forest Green, and Horizon Black shades, either from Fairphone directly or, thanks to this new partnership, from Boost Mobile.

articles.title: 'Star Wars: Una nueva esperanza' vuelve a los cines por su 50 aniversario: ya hay fecha de estreno
articles.text:
El 2027 va a ser un año grande para Star Wars. Y es que la legendaria franquicia galáctica ucmplirá 50 años. una fecha señalada desde ahce tiempo en el calendario de todos los fans porque se esperan todo tipo de celebraciones. Ahora, se ha confirmado lo que todos esperaban. La primera película de la saga, Star Wars: Una nueva esperanza, vuelve a los cines.
Tal y como ha informado Disney, Lucasfilm estrenará una versión restaurada de La guerra de las galaxias (1977) en miles de salas de cine de todo el mundo. La fecha del reestreno de Star Wars: Una nueva esperanza en cines será el 19 de febrero de 2027. Además, se sabe que la película estará disponible en IMAX 70 mm en mercados seleccionados. Los formatos de proyección en España pendientes de confirmación.
Además del estreno en cines, la compañía ha anunciado un reestreno extra en algunos lugares de Estados Unidos. Y es que Cosm presentará una versión en Shared Reality de la película (en la versión de 2019) en espacios inmersivos de Atlanta, Dallas, Detroit y Los Ángeles a partir de marzo de 2027. Junto a todo ello, se ha presentado un espectacular póster para conmemorar una cita tan especial como es el regreso a los cines de una de las películas más importantes de todos los tiempos.
2027: el 50 aniversario de Star Wars
Lo cierto es que el histórico reestreno en cines de la película original de 1977 no es la única sorpresa que Disney ha anunciado para el 50 aniversario de Star Wars. Antes de la llegada a los cines de Una nueva esperanza, la compañía estrenará la esperada segunda temporada de Ahsoka el 20 de enero en Disney+. Protagonizada de nuevo por Rosario Dawson como la querida Jedi, la serie se ambienta tras la caída del Imperio y el ascenso de la Nueva República, en la que Ahsoka se enfrenta a lo que significa ser una Jedi mientras la galaxia encara a un terrible adversario, el Gran Almirante Thrawn.
Ya en abril, la saga galáctica volverá a vestirse de gala. Del 1 al 4 de abril se celebrará en Los Ángeles la Star Wars Celebration. Este evento será una vez más la máxima experiencia para los fans de Star Wars. En ella se celebrarán paneles para hablar sobre el presente y el futuro de la saga en todas sus vertientes. A su vez, contará con cientos de expositores, merchandising exclusivo e invitados especiales.
En esas mismas fechas, los días 2 y 3 de abril, Lucasfilm, Disney Concerts, AMP Worldwide y Live Nation Hewitt Silva darán vida al legado musical de Star Wars con Star Wars in Concert: The Skywalker Saga en el Hollywood Bowl. este fue el lugar que acogió el primer concierto oficial de Star Wars en noviembre de 1977. Presentadas por Anthony Daniels, el intérprete de C-3PO, estas actuaciones especiales de las icónicas bandas sonoras de John Williams incluirán escenas y música de las nueve películas de la saga Skywalker.
Y ya en mayo, Lucasfilm prepara todavía más celebraciones. El 4 de mayo (May the 4th) se estrenará en Disney+ The Hero Awakens, un nuevo documental inédito de Lucasfilm del aclamado cineasta R.J. Cutler. En él se narrará cómo se hizo Star Wars y se ofrecerá a los fans una mirada única a la película a través de material de archivo y grabaciones de audio captadas durante su rodaje en 1977 y en torno a él.
Y el 28 de mayo llega a los cines de todo el mundo la esperadísima Star Wars: Starfighter. Dirigida por Shawn Levy y protagonizada por Ryan Gosling, la próxima película de la saga transcurre en una era totalmente nueva de Star Wars y presentará personajes y escenarios nunca vistos. Cuando un cínico y solitario aventurero se enfrenta a su pasado, se ve arrastrado a una peligrosa aventura por toda la galaxia que lo llevará a encontrarse cara a cara con su destino.
Por otro lado, Star Wars se ha asociado con un montón de marcas y empresas como Hasbro, Grupo LEGO, Adidas, Mars o Aston Martin para presentar colecciones especiales creadas para conmemorar este 50º aniversario. Por si fuera poco, según promete la compañía "Disney y Lucasfilm revelarán próximamente más colaboraciones intergeneracionales a finales de este año y a lo largo de 2027, con grandes marcas globales y anuncios para todas las generaciones de fans."

articles.title: Nvidia-Chef tritt nach Affären zurück - vorläufige Nachfolgerin steht schon fest
articles.text:
Nvidia-Chef Jensen Huang tritt nach Affären zurück – vorläufige Nachfolgerin steht schon fest
Der langjährige Nvidia-Chef Jensen Huang ist nach Affären zurückgetreten. Den Posten übernimmt kommissarisch Finanzchefin Colette Kress, wie der Chip-Konzern mitteilte. In der Zwischenzeit solle intern und extern nach einer dauerhaften Besetzung gesucht werden. Der 63-jährige Huang wurde zu einem Aushängeschild des KI-Booms und führte Nvidia zu Rekordzahlen.
Huang hatte am Wochenende zugegeben, seine Ehefrau betrogen zu haben. Zuvor war in Medienberichten die Rede von einem engen Verhältnis zu einer Frau gewesen, die von US-Sicherheitskreisen verdächtigt werde, vom chinesischen Geheimdienst angeworben worden zu sein. Mitte der Woche folgten Berichte über eine weitere Affäre, diesmal mit einer Top-Managerin von Nvidia. Bei Verhältnissen von Chefs mit ihnen untergeordneten Managern greifen US-Verwaltungsräte gewöhnlich hart durch.
Gesicht des KI-Wandels
Die Chips von Nvidia, einer der wertvollsten Firmen der Welt, dominieren in Rechenzentren beim Training und dem Betrieb Künstlicher Intelligenz. Huang profilierte sich als Gesicht des KI-Wandels: Bei Nvidia-Konferenzen und anderen öffentlichen Auftritten predigt er unermüdlich die weltverändernde Rolle Künstlicher Intelligenz in allen Lebensbereichen.
Eine Krise von Nvidia könnte auch viel weitere Kreise ziehen: Ihre Milliardengewinne investiert die Firma aus Santa Clara im Silicon Valley zum Teil in die Unterstützung von KI-Start-ups, die damit wiederum Chips des Konzerns kaufen. Huang baute in den vergangenen Jahren zudem ein enges Verhältnis zu US-Präsident Donald Trump auf.
Huang wurde noch vor kurzem beim Innovationsgipfel der Bundesregierung der rote Teppich ausgerollt. Die Bundesregierung vereinbarte eine Zusammenarbeit mit Nvidia.
Zunächst Dementis
Im Fall der Affäre mit einer möglichen chinesischen Spionin hatten Nvidia – und auch Huang selbst – zunächst von ganz gewöhnlichen Kontakten zur Managerin eines Kundenunternehmens gesprochen. Erst nachdem die «Financial Times» von einer Liebesbeziehung berichtete, gab der Nvidia-Chef die Affäre zu.
Der Nvidia-Verwaltungsrat leitete daraufhin eine Untersuchung ein. Zunächst hatte es geheißen, das Gremium habe weiterhin Vertrauen in Huang und dessen Führungsmannschaft.
«Ich war meiner Frau untreu»
Huang bestätigte am Sonntag in einer E-Mail an die Nvidia-Beschäftigten, dass er eine Affäre gehabt habe. «Ich schulde meiner Familie und Euch allen eine Entschuldigung», schrieb er. «Ich war meiner Frau untreu.» Das Ehepaar ist seit gut 40 Jahren verheiratet.
In der Milliardärs-Rangliste des Finanzdienstes Bloomberg steht Huang aktuell auf dem 13. Platz mit einem geschätzten Vermögen von 145 Milliarden Dollar, das hauptsächlich aus Nvidia-Aktien besteht. In der E-Mail schrieb Huang, dass er hoffe, das Vertrauen der Familie mit der Zeit zurückzugewinnen. Eine Tochter und ein Sohn des Paars arbeiten ebenfalls bei Nvidia.
Huang ist für Chipverkäufe nach China
Zwischen Huang und der US-Regierung gab es immer wieder Differenzen über Beschränkungen für die Lieferung moderner KI-Chips nach China. Der Nvidia-Chef argumentiert, Verbote schadeten der Dominanz von Nvidia und damit auch der Vorreiter-Rolle der USA, weil sie die Entwicklung eigener Technologie in China beschleunigen würden. Die US-Regierung versucht dagegen seit Jahren, chinesische Fortschritte bei Künstlicher Intelligenz durch die Blockade der Lieferungen von Hochleistungschips unter anderem von Nvidia zu bremsen.
Die aus China stammende Frau, mit der Huang eine Affäre gehabt haben soll, arbeitete zeitweise für die Firma Megaspeed. Das Unternehmen war verdächtigt worden, eine Hülle zu sein, über die Nvidia-Chips nach China geschleust werden könnten.

articles.title: Google’s coding agents now /swarm for one developer. Cursor’s go multiplayer so teammates’ agents can talk.
articles.text:
Google’s coding agents now /swarm for one developer. Cursor’s go multiplayer so teammates’ agents can talk.
Coding agents are pretty good at working in parallel: one writes a new API endpoint, another updates the tests, while a third fixes a bug elsewhere in the codebase. However, they’re not quite so adept at knowing what their coding counterparts are doing — put several on one project and they duplicate work, trip over each other’s changes, and leave the developer firefighting the fiasco that follows.
That’s why the major AI labs and coding-tool makers have all been looking for ways to bring order to their agent fleets, albeit with slightly different approaches.
This week alone, Google and Cursor both debuted features designed to keep agents from tripping over each other, but at different scales. Google’s Swarm organizes the agents working for a single developer, while Cursor’s multiplayer Projects lets agents working for different colleagues coordinate with each other.
Cursor gets teammates’ agents talking
Cursor first debuted Projects back in September, giving developers a way to hand a larger job to a coordinator agent that breaks it into tasks and delegates them to worker agents.
Then on Tuesday, the company, which Elon Musk’s SpaceX acquired for $60 billion in August, unveiled multiplayer functionality for Projects. Developers can now invite teammates into a project, where each person gets their own coordinator and workers.
Everyone’s agents work from the same task board and project documents, and their coordinators can message each other directly to share plans, flag overlaps and more.
Ultimately, it’s all about cutting down on the coordination developers have to do themselves.
Ultimately, it’s all about cutting down on the coordination developers have to do themselves. If one teammate’s agents are changing a database schema and another’s are building a feature that depends on it, their coordinators can agree on which change needs to land first.
Antigravity, for its part, is Google’s counterpart to Cursor. It’s where Google has consolidated various other coding tools, having moved individual Gemini CLI users to Antigravity and begun winding down Jules, its background coding agent.
On the same day Cursor unveiled multiplayer Projects, Google rolled out Gemini 4 Carbon in Antigravity, alongside a preview of its own approach to coordinating coding agents. Dubbed Swarm (stylized as /swarm), it lets a developer hand one assignment to a coordinator that then splits it among worker agents and assigns a verifier to check their changes. The workers can message each other on a shared board, so they can coordinate their changes as they go.
For example, a company that wants to change how its online checkout system verifies authentication tokens could use Swarm to split the work. One agent updates the authentication middleware while another updates the token verifier. They can work in separate Git worktrees, use the board to agree on how their changes fit together, and hand them off to a verifier for testing.
Taking to X on Tuesday, Varun Mohan, director of software engineering at Google DeepMind, said Swarm gives developers a convenient way to put multiple agents on a complex task, adding that Google staff were already using Swarm to take on larger jobs internally.
“The alpha from using swarms is ridiculous,” Mohan writes. “We have folks using swarms of 100s of agents to build large systems and products from scratch with a single prompt.”
Logan Kilpatrick, a member of technical staff at Google DeepMind, said on X that seeing swarm outputs had been ‘really impressive,’ and that they offered ‘a new scaling dimension for AI!”
“A new scaling dimension for AI!”
This, ultimately, gets to the crux of how each of these companies has tackled agent coordination.
When agents work for different people
Antigravity’s Swarm takes one developer’s assignment and gives the agents handling it a way to talk as they work. Cursor’s multiplayer Projects, meanwhile, takes assignments from different teammates and lets their coordinators talk across those assignments
That’s the distinction Cursor product manager Aryaman Khandelwal is keen to draw in Tuesday’s announcement.
“Multi-agent systems have so far served one person. Projects is a multi-agent system built for a whole team.”
“Multi-agent systems have so far served one person,” Khandelwal writes. “Projects is a multi-agent system built for a whole team.”
A quick peek across the AI coding landscape shows how others have approached agent coordination — including Anthropic. Its still-experimental Claude Code Agent Teams gives agents working on a common assignment a shared task list and a way to message each other. And recently, the company added cross-session messaging to Claude Code, so sessions started separately can exchange findings or warn each other about changes. But those sessions still belong to the same developer.
In October, GitHub put Projects in the Copilot app into public preview, giving developers a way to hand Copilot a goal that spans repositories and have it distribute the work across agents. AWS’s Kiro Crew bots, meanwhile, which launched last week, can start several sessions, steer them as they run and pull their results together.
Separately, Anthropic and OpenAI have also built agents that teammates can use together. Anthropic introduced Claude Tag in June, letting people in a Slack channel delegate to a shared Claude. OpenAI’s ChatGPT workspace agents, announced in April, can be used and maintained by multiple colleagues.
Community concerns: Spreading mistakes
However, some in the community raised concerns that letting teammates’ agents talk could spread one agent’s mistakes across the whole team, especially if each person’s agents follow different rules, and that an agent could request information it shouldn’t have access to. Khandelwal, though, responded that multiplayer Projects lets teams define shared rules and skills for everyone in a project. On the access part, Cursor’s documentation says agents treat messages from teammates’ agents as untrusted input and ask before sharing a person’s private files or connector data. A teammate’s message is handled in a separate chat, which Cursor says never shares secrets or credentials. The Projects documentation doesn’t say whether admins can set different rules for those exchanges based on a teammate’s role.
Separately, fresh research suggests that teams of per-user agents can struggle. In a study published Wednesday, researchers in Anthropic’s Fellows Program tested what happens when multiple users each delegate to their own agent and those agents share a resource, in four simulated environments that included a code merge queue. In every environment, group outcomes were worse than when a single agent served everyone, by roughly 10 to 45 percentage points for Anthropic’s Claude models, even when each user’s agents could message each other. Agents stalled as teams grew, overrode other users’ requests, and made unsupported claims about what other people wanted. Some fixes helped, such as appointing a lead agent or blocking an agent from acting until it had read its messages, but which ones worked depended on the task.
All in all, these various launches this year show a push to make it easier for teams to delegate work and keep track of what their agents are doing. With multiplayer mode in Projects, Cursor is tackling a specific part of that problem.
Parker Smith, who works in engineering for Cursor’s parent company SpaceXSI, says the point is really just to keep agents moving without unnecessary delays.
“Agents move fast, having a blocker on peer context is too slow,” Smith writes on X. “Multiplayer projects allow your agent to grab all the context it needs from your coworkers agents without needing to involve you.”
Cursor’s multiplayer Projects is in beta now for users on a team account, while Google’s Swarm is in preview for Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers.

articles.title: New N-able "4EverAble2Shell" zero-day exploited hours after PoC released
articles.text:
Hackers are actively exploiting a newly disclosed N-able N-central zero-day vulnerability dubbed "4EverAble2Shell" to compromise servers and deploy cryptocurrency miners, with researchers reporting at least 21 affected systems, including 19 running the company's latest security update.
The attacks follow security researcher Sean Bales' release of two new zero-day exploits today, dubbed 4EverAble2Shell and Agent2Shell, which he says allow attackers to gain root-level access to N-central appliances and SYSTEM-level access to Windows systems.
N-central is a remote monitoring and management (RMM) platform used by managed service providers (MSPs) and IT teams to monitor, manage, and secure customer devices and networks remotely.
The new vulnerabilities were disclosed on November 12, just two days after N-able released emergency security updates to address critical N-central zero-day vulnerabilities that Bales had publicly disclosed earlier this week.
Bales published proof-of-concept exploits for both the 4EverAble2Shell and Agent2Shell vulnerabilities, saying they were tested against N-central Appliance 2026.4.1.26 HF2, the security update N-able released on November 10.
The 4EverAble2Shell exploit allows unauthenticated attackers to execute commands as root on vulnerable N-central servers. However, the researcher says exploitation requires the platform's Legacy API functionality to be enabled.
The attack combines an Apache Axis vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-90436, with a separate N-central privilege escalation weakness to gain root-level access.
The second exploit, Agent2Shell, targets N-central's agent functionality and is claimed to allow attackers to execute commands with SYSTEM privileges on Windows devices.
The disclosures came after N-able took its hosted N-central environments offline earlier this week and urged on-premises customers to shut down their servers after Bales published more than 30 alleged zero-day vulnerabilities.
Bales has criticized N-able's handling of the vulnerability disclosures and the company's slow response to patching responsibly disclosed flaws.
"It's much much easier for me to just release the research I have and the vendor can decide what they want to do with it, what they do and don't want to fix, etc. :)," Bales told BleepingComputer.
Bales said N-able has not patched two unrelated RCE vulnerabilities in a different N-able product that he previously disclosed to the company in July.
In a November 12 security advisory, N-able said it was implementing additional protections in response to the new disclosures, including restricting certain N-central features and integrations while it develops further fixes.
"We are restricting certain N-central features and integrations," N-able said.
"These measures may affect some functionality, but we believe taking additional precautions while remediation is completed is the right action to protect our partners and their customers."
The company says it has disabled the Intune integration as a precaution and is urging on-premises customers to ensure Legacy API access is disabled, which is already the default.
The protections have already been applied to hosted environments, but customers are also advised to continue upgrading their Agents and Probes under the previous Hotfix 2 guidance.
In its advisory, N-able said it had seen no signs of compromise using the new flaws, although security researchers have since reported successful exploitation of the vulnerability against production N-central servers.
Hackers already exploiting 4EverAble2Shell
Cybersecurity company Previdian told BleepingComputer that attackers began probing for the 4EverAble2Shell vulnerability on November 12, shortly after the public release of the proof-of-concept exploit.
The company first observed suspicious requests targeting its N-central honeypot at approximately 08:30 UTC, using the same Java class referenced in the publicly released exploit.
While the initial requests were limited to probing for vulnerable servers, Previdian later confirmed that attackers were attempting to execute the complete exploit chain against its honeypot server.
The attacks initially exploit Apache Axis CVE-2026-90436 to execute commands as the 'nable' service account, then exploit a separate N-central privilege escalation vulnerability to obtain root privileges.
This attack chain matches the POC Bales released on GitHub.
According to Previdian, the privilege escalation stage abuses N-central's privileged setLDFileOwner helper and a symbolic link to make a normally root-owned script writable.
The attacker then modifies the script and invokes N-central's serverControl functionality to execute commands as root, while attempting to restore the modified files afterward.
The payload attempted to download and execute an additional shell script from an attacker-controlled server at 157.20.241[.]16, while sending diagnostic information and command output back to the same IP address.
Previdian is tracking the N-central privilege escalation flaw as VULN-2026-0009 and has added it to its own Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog.
Cybersecurity company Huntback also reports that attackers have already successfully compromised at least 21 production N-central servers using Bales' publicly released exploit chain.
Huntback saw the same attacker IP address as Previdian probing its N-central honeypots at approximately 08:30 UTC on November 12, with the first attempts to execute the complete exploit chain beginning at 09:16 UTC.
The attacks seen by Huntback exploited the 4EverAble2Shell exploit chain to download a shell script that installed an XMRig Monero cryptocurrency miner.
The miner was configured to use about half of the available CPU cores, likely to make the mining harder to detect.
Huntback identified other compromised systems through the attacker's cryptocurrency mining pool statistics, where infected systems were assigned identifiers beginning with nc_ followed by the server's IP address.
At 12:50 UTC on November 12, the researchers found 21 active miners using this naming convention, all of which had submitted mining shares within the previous five minutes.
The researchers then checked the associated IP addresses and confirmed that all 21 hosted N-central installations, including 19 running version 2026.4.1.26, the latest Hotfix 2 release issued on November 10.
The compromised servers were located across multiple countries, including the United States, Canada, South Africa, the United Kingdom, Germany, France, and Sweden.
While the attacks observed so far have been primarily used for cryptojacking, attackers could use compromised N-central infrastructure for additional malicious activity targeting managed customer environments.
Organizations running N-central should ensure that Legacy APIs are disabled and investigate suspicious requests to /dms/services/ServerUI, especially those referencing jline.internal.TerminalLineSettings.
Huntback also recommends checking for unexpected xvd.service systemd services, cryptocurrency mining processes, and files created under /tmp/.xvd or /var/tmp/.xvd.
Because the 4EverAble2Shell attack grants full root access to exploited servers, organizations that detect these IOCs should treat the breach as a full compromise of the server.

articles.title: NordVPN Digital Footprint : l'outil pour supprimer ses données personnelles — Frandroid
articles.text:
En 1993, Peter Steiner publiait dans le New-Yorker un dessin qui caricaturait l’anonymat offert aux utilisateurs et utilisatrices du web naissant en présentant un chien devant un ordinateur expliquant à un autre de ses congénères que « Sur Internet, personne ne sait que tu es un chien ». En 2026, pour citer André Gunthert, « non seulement tout le monde sait que tu es un chien, mais tes données ont déjà été vendues au marchand de croquettes. »
C’est en partant de ce constat légèrement déprimant que NordVPN vient de lancer son outil de gestion de « l’empreinte numérique » qui vous aide à prendre la mesure de la quantité d’information personnelle qui traîne sur le web.
Un score de 0 à 100
Intégré à l’application NordVPN, ce service « révèle quelles informations concernant un utilisateur sont exposées en ligne, au-delà des fuites de données ». Concrètement, le moteur de recherche va scruter tous les recoins plus ou moins acceptables du web pour savoir ce qu’il est possible d’apprendre sur vous à votre insu. Un score de 0 à 100 vous sera alors attribué pour mesurer l’ampleur des dégâts.
Contrairement à des services type « HaveIBeenPwnd » ou de surveillance du dark web, le « Digital Footprint » de NordVPN va compiler les données issues de fuites de données, mais aussi celles que vous avez peut-être livrées volontairement sans trop vous en rendre compte.
« Vos données circulent également à cause de comptes que vous avez oubliés, de profils créés à votre sujet et de votre navigation quotidienne. L’empreinte numérique vous montre l’étendue réelle de votre exposition et vous indique comment y remédier », explique Domininkas Virbickas, directeur produit chez NordVPN.
Réduire son « ombre numérique »
Une fois l’horrible constatation réalisée, l’application vous donnera ensuite des conseils pour réduire la portée de votre « ombre numérique » et vous permettra de suivre son évolution au fil du temps. Si l’entreprise avoue qu’il n’est pas possible d’effacer complètement une empreinte numérique, elle cherche à offrir un moyen pour « la réduire, limiter son accès et contrôler ce que vous laissez derrière vous ».

articles.title: Nvidia busca CEO tras la salida de Jensen Huang: estos son los candidatos que suenan para el puesto
articles.text:
Nvidia ha perdido al único director ejecutivo que ha tenido jamás. Jensen Huang ha dimitido este jueves como presidente, director ejecutivo y miembro del consejo de administración, y la empresa ahora tiene que encontrar a alguien para dirigir al fabricante de chips más valioso del mundo. Por el momento, el puesto pertenece a alguien de la casa.
Qué ha pasado. Nvidia anunciaba que su directora financiera, Colette Kress, actuará como directora ejecutiva interina mientras mantiene su cargo financiero, y que el consejo buscará candidatos internos y externos para el puesto permanente. También ha nombrado a Harvey C. Jones, antiguo director ejecutivo de Synopsys, como presidente del consejo, siendo de hecho el primero en la historia de la empresa.
La salida de Huang se produce tras las investigaciones sobre sus relaciones extramatrimoniales, una de ellas presuntamente con Alice Huang, ejecutiva y directora de la empresa Megaspeed, sospechosa de ser espía china. Las acciones de Nvidia abrieron este jueves con una caída de más del 13 % tras la dimisión, borrando más de medio billón de dólares en valor.
La nueva CEO interina: Colette Kress. Ha sido directora financiera desde 2013, trabajó anteriormente en Cisco y Microsoft, y aparece junto a Huang en cada presentación de resultados. Josh Gilbert, analista de eToro, declaraba a Reuters que es “la opción obvia para mantener el rumbo” y una voz de confianza para los inversores. Ahora, que se quede de forma permanente es otra cosa. Para Gilbert la ventaja de Nvidia es la tecnología y el consejo probablemente querría a un ingeniero al mando.
Los ingenieros. Ian Buck, quien ayudó a desarrollar CUDA, el software que mantiene a los desarrolladores vinculados a los chips de Nvidia, y que ahora dirige los productos de IA a hiperescala, encabeza la lista para llevarse el puesto permanente. Shay Boloor, estratega jefe de mercado en Futurum Equities, contaba a Reuters que es el candidato interno más fuerte por ese motivo.
Otros miembros internos mencionados incluyen al cofundador Chris Malachowsky, el único ejecutivo al nivel de antigüedad de Huang, y a Andrew Bell, vicepresidente sénior de ingeniería de hardware, con una trayectoria destacada en el sector de los chips.
Los externos. Si el consejo mira más allá de Nvidia, que es algo que también plantean según el comunicado, el nombre que más suena es el del director ejecutivo de Arm, Rene Haas, antiguo ejecutivo de Nvidia. Tiene “sentido lógico”, según comparten en Reuters, pero tal y como comparte Charu Chanana, estratega de inversiones del banco Saxo, el modelo de negocio de Arm difiere considerablemente del de Nvidia.
Otras sugerencias son más especulativas:
- Bret Taylor: desde TechCrunch sugieren al fundador de Sierra y expresidente del consejo de OpenAI como una figura estable y bien conectada.
- Eric Schmidt: Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, de Yale, lo proponía como candidato, pero igual su propia aventura amorosa en el pasado complica las cosas.
- Tim Cook: pura especulación, pero según Jun Bei Liu, de Ten Cap, su experiencia en la cadena de suministro podría encajar. Ahora, que encaje y que pretenda dejar su puesto como presidente ejecutivo de la junta directiva de Apple es otra cosa muy distinta.
- Lisa Su y Lip-Bu Tan: respectivos directores ejecutivos de AMD e Intel. TechCrunch los incluye en su lista, pero tampoco son candidatos realistas pues son pocas las probabilidades de que dejen sus respectivos puestos de CEO. Y en el caso de Tan, es un reflejo del difícil momento por el que está pasando Intel, así que no se le espera demasiado.
¿Y la familia?. Los dos hijos de Huang ocupan cargos ejecutivos en Nvidia, aunque todavía son relativamente jóvenes e “inexpertos”, según relatan desde la BBC. Armina Rosenberg, de Minotaur Capital, ve plausible también una estructura de codirección ejecutiva, combinando a un líder financiero como Kress con un líder tecnológico como Buck.
Qué pasa ahora. De momento, y hasta conocer más noticias, tendremos que esperar al próximo martes 17 de noviembre, que es cuando Nvidia presenta sus resultados del tercer trimestre bajo el mando de Kress.
