articles.title: Sony poursuit son ménage sur PC, et ferme un service PlayStation boudé par 99,6 % des abonnés
articles.text:
Discrètement, Sony vient d'annoncer la fermeture prochaine de son application PlayStation Plus sur PC. Un service (tout aussi discret) qui n'aura jamais vraiment trouvé son public, puisque moins de 0,4 % des abonnés Premium éligibles l'utilisaient.
Le ménage continue chez PlayStation, et après avoir progressivement revu sa stratégie concernant les jeux PC, Sony s'attaque cette fois à un service dont l'existence était probablement inconnue d'une bonne partie des joueurs. Le constructeur vient en effet d'annoncer la fermeture de son application PlayStation Plus sur PC, avec une échéance fixée au 10 décembre 2026 (soit dans un petit mois à peine).
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Moins de 0,4 % des abonnés Premium concernés
Derrière cette application se cachait notamment une fonctionnalité de cloud gaming permettant aux abonnés PlayStation Plus Premium de jouer à certains titres du catalogue PlayStation directement depuis leur ordinateur, sans posséder de console donc. Un héritage de l'ancien PlayStation Now, qui avait été intégré à l'offre PlayStation Plus lors de sa refonte.
Pour justifier cette décision, Sony avance un argument pour le moins imparable : la fréquentation du service. Ou plutôt, la non fréquentation du service. Dans son communiqué officiel, le géant nippon explique que « moins de 0,4 % des abonnés PlayStation Plus Premium éligibles » utilisaient l'application sur PC.
Un chiffre particulièrement faible, qui pousse donc le constructeur à revoir ses priorités. Sony explique notamment vouloir concentrer ses efforts sur les expériences réellement plébiscitées par ses membres, et à compter du 10 décembre, le streaming cloud via l'application PC ne sera donc plus disponible.
Bien sûr, cette fermeture à venir ne concerne en aucun cas les abonnements PlayStation Plus eux-mêmes, ni les avantages associés sur PS4 et PS5. Les abonnés pourront donc continuer à profiter normalement de leur formule sur leurs consoles.
PlayStation veut ramener ses exclusivités à la maison
Chez PlayStation, cette disparition intervient dans un contexte loin d'être anodin, puisque depuis plusieurs mois, Sony prend ses distances avec le marché PC, après avoir pourtant multiplié les portages de ses grandes exclusivités sur Steam et l'Epic Games Store.
Comme nous l'évoquions récemment, le constructeur entend désormais réserver ses grandes productions solo développées en interne à l'écosystème PlayStation. God of War, Spider-Man ou encore The Last of Us avaient pourtant ouvert la voie à une stratégie plus ouverte, mais qui touche désormais à sa fin.
La fermeture de l'application PlayStation Plus sur PC ne constituera pas, à elle seule, un quelconque bouleversement stratégique. Elle vient toutefois ajouter une nouvelle pièce à une tendance qui se dessine depuis plusieurs mois, avec un Sony qui souhaite avant tout valoriser ses consoles et leurs exclusivités, plutôt que multiplier les passerelles avec un écosystème concurrent.
- Une PS5 plus compacte, plus légère
- Le repositionnement du bouton Eject
- Un SSD de 1 To (822 Go d’espace disponible au déballage)

articles.title: Applications open for Villgro Africa MedTech Innovation Programme - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
The Villgro Africa MedTech Innovation Programme is looking for locally-led, invention-based enterprises developing tech-enabled medical hardware that addresses healthcare needs.
Open to innovators in Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi and Ethiopia with at least a functional proof of concept or prototype, the Villgro Africa MedTech Innovation Programme is seeking startups with diagnostic and patient-monitoring devices; therapeutic equipment; maternal and newborn health technologies; and connected medical devices.
Six selected enterprises will receive tailored technical and venture-building support over 24 months, covering product development and validation; regulatory and quality readiness; manufacturing; market development; and investment readiness.
Applications are open here until November 16.

articles.title: Qué hace Nvidia y cómo logró convertirse en una de las empresas más valiosas del mundo gracias a la inteligencia artificial
articles.text:
Nvidia se convirtió en una de las compañías más importantes de la industria tecnológica gracias a los procesadores que permiten entrenar y ejecutar sistemas de inteligencia artificial. Sus chips están presentes en los centros de datos de empresas como Microsoft, Google y Amazon, y son una pieza fundamental para el funcionamiento de herramientas como ChatGPT y otros modelos capaces de generar textos, imágenes y videos.
El crecimiento de este negocio llevó a la compañía estadounidense a alcanzar una capitalización bursátil cercana a los 4,2 billones de dólares en noviembre de 2026, lo que la ubicaba como la segunda empresa más valiosa del mundo antes de la reciente caída de sus acciones. Sin embargo, Nvidia atraviesa ahora una etapa de incertidumbre tras la renuncia de su cofundador y director ejecutivo, Jensen Huang, quien dejó el cargo con efecto inmediato.
La junta directiva designó a Colette Kress, hasta entonces directora financiera, como CEO interina mientras busca un reemplazo permanente. La salida de Huang provocó una reacción negativa en los mercados: las acciones de Nvidia llegaron a caer más de 12% y pusieron en riesgo alrededor de 500.000 millones de dólares de su valor bursátil, según Reuters.
Qué hace Nvidia y qué productos fabrica
Nvidia es una empresa tecnológica estadounidense fundada en 1993 por Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky y Curtis Priem. Su actividad principal consiste en diseñar procesadores gráficos, conocidos como GPU, y desarrollar plataformas de hardware y software para distintas necesidades informáticas.
En sus primeros años, la compañía se hizo conocida por fabricar tarjetas gráficas para computadoras y videojuegos. Estos componentes permiten procesar imágenes, animaciones y escenas tridimensionales con mayor velocidad. Sin embargo, con el avance de la inteligencia artificial, sus procesadores adquirieron una función mucho más amplia.
A diferencia de una CPU tradicional, que está diseñada para ejecutar diferentes tareas de manera general, una GPU puede realizar miles de operaciones en paralelo. Esta característica resulta especialmente útil para entrenar modelos de inteligencia artificial, que necesitan procesar enormes cantidades de información y efectuar cálculos simultáneos.
Por eso, los chips de Nvidia se utilizan en centros de datos que almacenan y procesan la información necesaria para que funcionen los asistentes virtuales, los generadores de imágenes y otras aplicaciones basadas en IA.
La compañía también desarrolla sistemas completos que combinan procesadores, redes de comunicación y herramientas de software. Entre sus principales plataformas se encuentra Blackwell, diseñada para acelerar las tareas de inteligencia artificial. En 2026 presentó además Rubin, una nueva arquitectura de seis chips orientada a mejorar el rendimiento y reducir los costos de procesamiento.
Por qué sus chips son importantes para ChatGPT y otras inteligencias artificiales
Los modelos de inteligencia artificial necesitan dos procesos fundamentales: entrenamiento e inferencia. El primero consiste en analizar grandes cantidades de datos para que el sistema aprenda patrones y pueda responder a diferentes instrucciones. El segundo ocurre cuando una persona utiliza el modelo y este genera una respuesta.
Ambas actividades requieren una enorme capacidad de procesamiento. Por esa razón, empresas como OpenAI, Google, Microsoft y Amazon invierten miles de millones de dólares en infraestructura tecnológica equipada con procesadores especializados.
Nvidia logró posicionarse como uno de los principales proveedores de ese mercado. Sus GPU permiten ejecutar operaciones matemáticas en paralelo, una capacidad que resulta esencial para desarrollar modelos de lenguaje y otros sistemas avanzados.
Otro elemento importante es CUDA, una plataforma de software creada por Nvidia que permite a los desarrolladores aprovechar la capacidad de sus procesadores para realizar cálculos complejos. Este ecosistema contribuyó a que numerosas empresas y laboratorios incorporaran sus chips en sus proyectos, lo que también dificulta que cambien de proveedor.
Cuánto dinero gana Nvidia gracias a la inteligencia artificial
El negocio de los centros de datos explica buena parte del crecimiento financiero de Nvidia. En su ejercicio fiscal 2026, la compañía registró ingresos por 215.900 millones de dólares, un aumento del 65% respecto al periodo anterior.
De ese total, 193.700 millones de dólares correspondieron al segmento de centros de datos, que incluye los procesadores y sistemas utilizados para inteligencia artificial y computación acelerada. El área de videojuegos generó 16.000 millones de dólares, mientras que la visualización profesional y el sector automotor aportaron otros ingresos.
Estas cifras muestran que Nvidia ya no depende únicamente de las tarjetas gráficas para videojuegos. Su principal fuente de ingresos está relacionada con la infraestructura que necesitan las grandes empresas tecnológicas para desarrollar y ofrecer servicios de inteligencia artificial.
Jensen Huang renuncia a Nvidia y Colette Kress asume el mando
El 12 de noviembre de 2026, Nvidia confirmó que Jensen Huang presentó su renuncia como presidente, director ejecutivo y miembro de la junta directiva. Su salida fue efectiva de inmediato y puso fin a una etapa de 33 años al frente de la compañía que cofundó.
La decisión se produjo después de que trascendieran informaciones sobre relaciones extramatrimoniales del ejecutivo y una investigación independiente de la junta directiva relacionada con reportes sobre un posible intento de inteligencia extranjera. Huang había reconocido ante los empleados que fue infiel a su esposa y manifestó que colaboraría con la investigación. Nvidia señaló previamente que no tenía motivos para creer que se hubieran comprometido secretos de la empresa o la seguridad nacional estadounidense.
Tras su salida, Colette Kress fue nombrada CEO interina. La ejecutiva trabaja en Nvidia desde 2013 y continuará desempeñándose como directora financiera mientras la junta busca un sucesor permanente. También fue designado Harvey C. Jones como presidente de la junta directiva.
El cambio de liderazgo representa un desafío para una empresa cuyo crecimiento estuvo estrechamente relacionado con la visión de Huang y su capacidad para establecer acuerdos con los principales actores de la industria. Ahora, Nvidia deberá demostrar que puede mantener su posición en el mercado de inteligencia artificial sin el ejecutivo que encabezó su transformación.

articles.title: 5 lessons to learn from the book Kaizen by Sarah Harvey
articles.text:
5 lessons to learn from the book Kaizen by Sarah Harvey
Discover five powerful lessons from Kaizen by Sarah Harvey on building better habits, overcoming resistance, and achieving lasting personal growth.
Have you ever decided to change your entire life, only to give up after a few days? Whether it is waking up early, exercising regularly, saving money, or learning a new skill, making major lifestyle changes can feel overwhelming. But what if you could transform your life without changing everything at once?
In Kaizen: The Japanese Method for Transforming Habits, One Small Step at a Time, Sarah Harvey introduces readers to the Japanese philosophy of Kaizen, which focuses on continuous improvement through small, manageable changes.
The book explains how this approach can be applied to different areas of life, including health, relationships, finances, career, and everyday habits. Instead of chasing overnight transformation, Harvey encourages readers to practise patience, understand their existing routines, and make gradual improvements that last.
5 Important lessons to learn from Kaizen by Sarah Harvey.
1. Small changes can lead to big results
One of the biggest lessons from the book is that you do not need to make dramatic changes to improve your life. Sometimes, the smallest actions can create meaningful progress when repeated consistently.
For example, if you want to develop a reading habit, start with just five pages a day instead of forcing yourself to finish an entire book in a week. Similarly, if you want to become physically active, begin with a short daily walk.
The idea is to make changes so manageable that you can continue them without feeling overwhelmed.
2. Understand your existing habits before changing them
Before introducing new habits, take some time to understand your current routine. Many people try to change their behaviour without identifying what is preventing them from making progress.
Harvey encourages readers to examine their everyday activities, identify areas that need improvement, and understand which habits are helping or holding them back.
For example, if you spend too much time scrolling through social media, observe when and why you reach for your phone. Once you understand the pattern, you can gradually replace that habit with something more productive.
3. Break big goals into smaller steps
Large goals can sometimes feel impossible because we focus too much on the final result rather than the actions required to achieve it.
The Kaizen approach encourages breaking ambitious goals into smaller, realistic tasks. Instead of worrying about writing an entire book, focus on writing one paragraph every day. If you want to save money, begin by setting aside a small amount regularly.
These manageable steps make it easier to stay motivated and track your progress.
4. Be patient and stop comparing your progress
Personal growth does not happen at the same speed for everyone. Some habits take weeks to develop, while others require months of consistent effort.
The book emphasises the importance of patience and creating solutions that suit your individual lifestyle. What works for someone else may not necessarily work for you.
Instead of comparing your progress with others, focus on becoming slightly better than you were yesterday. Remember that consistency matters more than perfection.
5. Track your progress and adjust your approach
Making changes is only one part of the process. You also need to understand whether those changes are working.
The book encourages readers to monitor their habits, review their progress, and make adjustments whenever necessary. Keeping a journal or maintaining a simple habit tracker can help you recognise improvements and identify areas that need more attention.
If a particular routine is not working, do not immediately consider it a failure. Find a more manageable approach and try again.
Final thoughts
Kaizen by Sarah Harvey offers a refreshing approach to personal development by reminding readers that meaningful transformation does not happen overnight. Instead of putting pressure on yourself to change everything at once, focus on making small improvements every day.
Whether you want to build healthier habits, improve your finances, strengthen relationships, or become more productive, the Kaizen philosophy encourages you to take one manageable step at a time.
The biggest takeaway is simple: you do not have to become a completely different person tomorrow. You just have to make a small effort to become better today.

articles.title: Your Endpoint Management Platform Could Be Your Biggest Security Risk
articles.text:
Author: Gene Moody, Field CTO at Action1
Endpoint management platforms have become essential in modern IT operations and enterprise security. They allow administrators to deploy patches, install software, execute scripts, enforce configurations, and remotely manage thousands of devices from a centralized system.
Without these types of systems, maintaining consistent security across large environments would be extremely difficult and labor-intensive.
However, the administrative authority that makes these platforms valuable also makes them very attractive targets for attackers. An endpoint management platform already has established and approved communication channels, elevated permissions, and trusted relationships with the devices it manages.
Any attacker who gains control of that infrastructure will be able to use those existing capabilities to distribute malware, execute malicious commands, disable security controls, or disrupt operations across an entire organization. All with the same level of authority as the real admin.
The same capabilities that allow an administrator to secure thousands of endpoints can allow an attacker to compromise them.
When trusted management infrastructure is compromised
Recent incidents demonstrate how compromised remote management infrastructure can extend attacks across compromised environments.
In 2026, Huntress documented attackers abusing compromised BeyondTrust Bomgar remote support infrastructure to deploy ransomware and access downstream organizations. In 2025, ransomware operators compromised an MSP's SimpleHelp platform, using its existing management capabilities to access protected systems, steal information, and deploy ransomware.
Similarly, in 2024, attackers exploited ConnectWise ScreenConnect vulnerabilities, with investigators documenting Play ransomware deployment through a compromised MSP instance. And who will forget the 2024 incident abusing Microsoft Intune to remotely wipe hundreds of thousands of corporate devices at Stryker!
In each of these cases, attackers exploited the administrative reach of infrastructure already trusted by the organization. The incidents warn us why protecting systems against the management platforms’ misuse is essential, and why independently verifying sensitive endpoint operations can help limit the consequences of a successful compromise.
These attacks against centralized management and software distribution systems often lead to compromise well beyond the initially compromised infrastructure.
For cloud-hosted platforms, the security of the provider's hosting environment, management services, and software delivery mechanisms becomes particularly important. A compromise there may affect multiple environments simultaneously.
Why traditional security controls have limitations
Multi-factor authentication, role-based access controls, privileged access management, and activity monitoring are bare minimum safeguards. They help restrict administrative access, limit permissions, and identify suspicious behavior.
However, these protections primarily operate within the management platform's security boundaries.
An attacker exploiting a vulnerability in the underlying system, compromising a privileged service, or hijacking an authenticated administrative session may be granted the ability to issue commands that endpoints recognize as legitimate. Because they are impersonating a user, and the restriction is BY user.
Even with strong authentication and carefully configured permissions, the endpoint may have no independent way to determine whether a sensitive instruction was explicitly approved by a legitimate administrator.
This security implication is: high-risk endpoint operations should have authorization that remains verifiable independently of the management platform delivering them!
Adding owner-controlled authorization
Cryptographically verified authorization, independent of anything the platform stores or directly handles, provides the platform a way to establish that independent security boundary.
Under this approach, sensitive endpoint operations require authorization signed using a private cryptographic key controlled only by the legitimate admin. The endpoint independently verifies the signature before executing the protected instruction.
The management platform can continue coordinating and delivering administrative operations, while the authority to approve protected actions remains separately controlled.
An attacker who compromises the management infrastructure cannot simply create valid authorizations without obtaining the owner’s signing key or compromising the verification process.
Action1 implements this approach through Endpoint Takeover Prevention (ETP).
ETP uses customer-controlled cryptographic authorization to protect high-risk operations, including script execution, software deployment, automations, and remote sessions.
Because the private authorization key is maintained independently of Action1's cloud infrastructure, a compromise of the management platform alone does not provide the ability to authorize these protected actions.
Keep Attackers from Taking Over Your Endpoints
Action1's Endpoint Takeover Prevention (ETP) protects high-risk endpoint actions with customer-controlled cryptographic authorization, even if the management platform is compromised.
Take control of endpoint security with Action1. Your first 200 endpoints are free forever.
Start Now
Of course, the effectiveness of this protection depends on secure key management, endpoint integrity, and appropriate configuration of protected operations, but that becomes customer responsibility by becoming customer privilege. It is protected by a key they, and only they control.
Securing an essential part of enterprise IT
Endpoint management platforms will continue to be essential parts of modern infrastructure by maintaining secure and operationally manageable environments. But they now demand particularly strong safeguards against compromise and abuse. We have new threat metrics, we need new defense metrics,
Organizations should re-evaluate how these platforms are secured, how suspicious activity is monitored, and which protections remain effective if management infrastructure is compromised. Practice failure, so when it happens you can understand it, and contain it more effectively.
Customer-controlled cryptographic authorization adds a crucial layer by ensuring that sensitive endpoint operations require independently verifiable approval.

The goal is to preserve the administrative power organizations depend on while keeping the authority to approve its most sensitive uses under the owner’s control.

articles.title: ¿Cómo Jensen Huang, que proviene de una familia común, construyó el imperio de NVIDIA?
articles.text:
Jensen Huang ha sido el director NVIDIA desde que la cofundó en 1993 hasta este mismo 2026, en el que ha tenido que dimitir tras su escándalo de su infidelidad con una supuesta espía. Pero en este tiempo, sus chips se han convertido en una pieza básica del auge de la inteligencia artificial, aunque su historia empieza bastante lejos de Silicon Valley, en una familia taiwanesa corriente y con un primer trabajo en la cocina de un restaurante. Su trayectoria también pasa por un internado de Kentucky, un Denny’s y un primer chip que estuvo a punto de hundir la empresa.
De Taiwán a Kentucky. Huang, cuyo nombre original es Jen-Hsun Huang, nació el 17 de febrero de 1963 en Tainan, en una familia con un padre ingeniero químico y una madre maestra. Cuando tenía cinco años se mudaron a Tailandia, pero sus padres decidieron no instalarse allí de forma definitiva por la guerra de Vietnam, y acabaron mandando a los niños a Estados Unidos.
El propio Huang explicaba en una entrevista con NPR que ese viaje fue en 1973, en plena agitación social en Tailandia, cuando él tenía nueve años y su hermano, diez. Los dos vivieron primero con un tío en Tacoma, en el estado de Washington, y poco después acabaron en el Oneida Baptist Institute, un internado de Kentucky en el que, como recordaba en esa misma conversación, los alumnos eran duros y las peleas no acababan bien.
Lavaplatos en un Denny’s. Ya en Oregón, Huang empezó a trabajar con 15 años en un Denny’s de Portland, donde fue lavaplatos, ayudante de camarero y camarero, según cuenta el blog oficial de NVIDIA. Y es que él mismo ha recordado en varias ocasiones lo que le dio aquel empleo: “Denny’s me ha enseñado muchas lecciones”, aseguraba en 2023 en ese mismo texto, en el que también recomendaba empezar en la hostelería porque enseña humildad, esfuerzo y hospitalidad.
Ingeniero antes que empresario. Huang se graduó en ingeniería eléctrica en la Universidad Estatal de Oregón en 1984, y allí conoció a Lori Mills, también estudiante de ingeniería, con quien más tarde se casó. Después pasó por AMD, donde diseñaba microprocesadores, y por LSI Logic, donde ocupó puestos de ingeniería, marketing y dirección general entre 1985 y 1993.
Mientras trabajaba en LSI Logic también se sacó un máster en ingeniería eléctrica por la Universidad de Stanford, que terminó en 1992, apenas un año antes de dar el salto y montar su propia empresa.
Una empresa a punto de quebrar. En 1993, Huang fundó NVIDIA junto a Chris Malachowsky y Curtis Priem, y los tres arrancaron con 40.000 dólares de capital. La idea era fabricar chips gráficos para ordenadores y videojuegos, pero su primer producto, el NV1, se basaba en superficies cuadráticas y no en los triángulos que acabaría imponiendo Microsoft con DirectX.
Cuando Microsoft presentó esas especificaciones, el interés por el NV1 se esfumó, y NVIDIA tuvo que rehacer su chip prácticamente sin clientes y con la plantilla muy reducida. El resultado fue el RIVA 128, lanzado en 1997 y ya compatible con el estándar de Microsoft, que volvió a poner a la compañía en el mapa.
Dos años después, en 1999, llegó la GeForce 256, que NVIDIA presentó como “la primera GPU del mundo” por integrar en un único chip la transformación geométrica y la iluminación, entre otras funciones. Una GPU permite al ordenador procesar gráficos y cálculos complejos mucho más rápido, aunque en aquel momento su uso se centraba sobre todo en los videojuegos y los gráficos por ordenador.
De los videojuegos a la IA. Con el tiempo, quedó claro que las GPU, capaces de hacer muchísimos cálculos a la vez, eran buenas candidatas para ejecutar algoritmos de aprendizaje automático, y NVIDIA dejó de ser únicamente una empresa de gráficos para juegos. Y así empezó la evolución hasta convertirse en una potencia de la IA con presencia en campos como los coches autónomos o la robótica.
Pero el gran acelerón llegó con la IA generativa: desde la aparición de ChatGPT, NVIDIA ha multiplicado casi por 13 su negocio de centros de datos. Además de esto, los cinco grandes proveedores de nube suponen algo más de la mitad de esos ingresos, y Huang destacó el alcance de CUDA, la plataforma de software con la que se programan sus GPU.
Huang también se ha hecho reconocible por su chaqueta de cuero, que suele llevar en los anuncios más importantes de la compañía, y por una lista de reconocimientos en la que sobresalen dos. Fortune lo eligió empresario del año en 2017, y en 2019 la Harvard Business Review lo colocó en el primer puesto de su clasificación de los 100 consejeros delegados con mejores resultados del mundo.

articles.title: Deuxième coupure en un mois sur Starshield : l’Ukraine s’inquiète, l’Europe s’agace et cherche une alternative à Starlink — Frandroid
articles.text:
Pour abattre des Shahed à réaction qui volent à plus de 400 km/h selon Kiev, l’armée ukrainienne compte sur des drones intercepteurs qui perdent leur liaison satellite au-delà de 161 km/h.
C’est en tout cas ce qu’affirme Volodymyr Zelensky, qui assure que ses unités constatent depuis plusieurs jours des coupures sur Starshield le long de tout le front et au-dessus des territoires occupés.
Le président ukrainien l’a écrit sur X sans prendre de gants : « ce ne sont pas des erreurs aléatoires, mais des restrictions de vitesse systématiques ». Selon lui, des frappes russes sont déjà passées à travers la défense aérienne à cause de ce plafond.
Starshield, c’est la déclinaison militaire de Starlink, la constellation de satellites en orbite basse de SpaceX, à laquelle l’Ukraine accède par un accord avec le gouvernement américain. Le bridage ne porte pas sur le débit de la connexion mais sur la vitesse de déplacement du terminal : au-delà de 100 miles par heure, l’antenne décroche et le drone perd le contact avec son opérateur. Le scénario n’a rien d’inédit.
Dans la nuit du 14 octobre, le même plafond était apparu sans que les forces ukrainiennes soient averties, clouant au sol 2 000 intercepteurs Bars financés par des Européens, selon Volodymyr Zelensky. Elon Musk avait d’abord renvoyé la balle au Pentagone et à la Maison-Blanche, avant que le Wall Street Journal n’affirme qu’Elon Musk avait lui-même ordonné le bridage. La pleine vitesse était revenue le 24 octobre.
    Pour aller plus loin
« Nos forces n’ont pas été averties » : l’Ukraine accuse SpaceX d’avoir limité Starlink en pleine guerre
            
Un démenti qui n’explique rien
Cette fois, SpaceX nie tout en bloc. « C’est faux. Il n’y a eu aucun changement », a répondu un porte-parole au site américain Axios.
Or le démenti ne porte que sur SpaceX et ne dit rien d’un éventuel réglage décidé ailleurs, alors que le Pentagone avait déjà nié tout ordre lors de la première coupure d’octobre.
Côté ukrainien, Serhii Beskrestnov, conseiller de la présidence pour les technologies de défense, confirme que la vitesse en mouvement est de nouveau limitée. Personne n’a vérifié ces mesures de façon indépendante, mais le précédent pèse lourd, surtout après les révélations du quotidien américain sur le rôle d’Elon Musk.
Le calendrier alimente les soupçons. Les coupures surviennent au lendemain de pourparlers russo-ukrainiens à Abou Dhabi, alors que des émissaires américains rencontrent Vladimir Poutine à Moscou.
De hauts responsables ukrainiens confient au Financial Times soupçonner une manière de faire pression sur Kiev dans ces négociations, sans en apporter la preuve.
La Commission européenne juge ces informations « profondément préoccupantes et, si elles sont confirmées, inacceptables », par la voix de son porte-parole Thomas Regnier, qui réclame un rétablissement urgent du service.
    Pour aller plus loin
Elon Musk a ordonné de brider Starlink en Ukraine, selon le Wall Street Journal
            
Qui tient l’interrupteur ?
Les premiers concernés sont les opérateurs de drones et, par ricochet, les civils des villes visées par les Shahed. La question de fond reste entière depuis octobre : qui, de SpaceX, du Pentagone ou de la Maison-Blanche, a le droit contractuel de brider un service dont dépend une armée en guerre ? Les sénateurs Jeanne Shaheen, démocrate, et Thom Tillis, républicain, notent que SpaceX n’a fourni aucune explication et exigent le retour immédiat du service.
Le dossier arrive devant un Congrès tout juste sorti des élections de mi-mandat du 3 novembre, et démocrates comme républicains réclament désormais des comptes à SpaceX.
    Pour aller plus loin
Elon Musk voulait éviter une Chambre et un Sénat démocrates : c’est raté
            
L’Europe cherche une porte de sortie
Bruxelles pousse depuis des mois ses propres options, comme GOVSATCOM, qui mutualise les satellites gouvernementaux des États membres, ou IRIS², une constellation souveraine attendue en 2029. Eutelsat propose aussi OneWeb, avec environ 600 satellites à 1 200 km d’altitude, soit nettement moins que les milliers d’engins Starlink placés vers 550 km, donc plus proches et plus réactifs.
Quant au projet de quatre opérateurs européens, dont Orange, il vise la connexion directe des smartphones, pas le pilotage de drones militaires. Cette future constellation européenne s’appuiera d’ailleurs sur un partenaire satellite qui reste à trouver.
    Pour aller plus loin
Quatre opérateurs européens, dont Orange, veulent lancer leur propre constellation de satellites pour concurrencer Starlink
            
Que le bridage vienne de SpaceX, de Washington ou d’ailleurs, l’Ukraine découvre pour la deuxième fois en un mois qu’une partie de sa défense aérienne dépend d’un réglage qu’elle ne contrôle pas.
Elon Musk, lui, avait assuré que tout se décidait entre l’armée américaine et la Maison-Blanche, et le milliardaire qui voulait éviter un Congrès démocrate est désormais sommé de s’expliquer par des sénateurs.

articles.title: Windows : deux failles BitLocker permettent de lire les fichiers protégés
articles.text:
Parmi les 1 235 failles corrigées par le Patch Tuesday de novembre, deux vulnérabilités concernent BitLocker. Intégré à Windows, cet outil chiffre le contenu du disque dur. C’est lui qui protège vos données si votre ordinateur portable est perdu ou volé. Concrètement, il rend les fichiers illisibles pour une personne qui ne possède pas la clé de déchiffrement. Sur de nombreux PC, le chiffrement est activé par défaut.
À lire aussi : Windows 11 permet enfin de personnaliser le menu du clic droit
Deux failles qui mettent en danger
La première faille permet tout simplement de contourner le chiffrement de l’appareil. Selon Microsoft, un attaquant peut accéder à toutes les données chiffrées stockées sur le disque. Pour exploiter la défaillance, le pirate doit simplement disposer d’un compte utilisateur sur l’ordinateur. Il n’y a pas besoin de privilèges particuliers.
La seconde brèche est liée à une erreur de gestion de la mémoire. Elle permet de contourner le Secure Boot, le démarrage sécurisé de Windows, une protection qui empêche normalement le lancement de logiciels malveillants. D’après Microsoft, l’attaque ne nécessite ni compte ni intervention de la victime.
Dans les deux cas, le pirate doit d’abord obtenir un accès physique à l’ordinateur. Il n’est pas possible d’exploiter les failles à distance, depuis Internet, ce qui limite le champ des attaques. C’est néanmoins un problème pour les individus qui perdent leur ordinateur ou qui se le font voler. Les deux brèches sont classées « importantes », le niveau juste en dessous de « critique », même si leur exploitation n’a pas été jugée « probable ».
Bonne nouvelle, Microsoft précise que ces deux failles n’ont pas été rendues publiques avant le déploiement du Patch Tuesday. Elles n’ont donc pas été exploitées par des pirates. Les vulnérabilités touchent Windows 10, Windows 11 et plusieurs versions de Windows Server. Ce n’est pas la première fois que BitLocker est touché par une faille cette année. D’autres failles du même type ont déjà été corrigées le mois dernier, lors du Patch Tuesday record déployé par Microsoft.
Pour vous protéger d’éventuelles attaques indiscrètes, installez sans tarder la mise à jour de sécurité de novembre sur votre ordinateur. Ouvrez les Paramètres de Windows, puis allez dans Windows Update, puis cliquez sur « Rechercher des mises à jour ». Redémarrez ensuite l’ordinateur pour finaliser l’installation.

articles.title: Designing Edge AI SoCs At Near-Threshold: Why Foundation IP Can Help You Break Down The Power Wall
articles.text:
Traditional voltage scaling is no longer sufficient to deliver real-time performance within tight energy and thermal limits.
Lowering operating voltage is a key to SoC power optimization. In advanced FinFET processes at ~0.4–0.5V, it can also start to become a design risk. As edge AI pushes inference closer to endpoints, edge-AI SoCs must deliver real-time performance within tight energy and thermal limits. Traditional voltage scaling is no longer sufficient.
SoC designs are shifting towards much more extensive use of near-threshold operation to achieve step-function improvements in performance per watt. But this shift fundamentally changes how chips behave: delays increase non-linearly, variability grows significantly, and underpinning predictable operation becomes a critical enabler to minimizing power.
Design success in this operating regime depends heavily on the underlying quality, modeling accuracy, and integration of Foundation IP with EDA flows and silicon validation. Embedded memories, logic libraries, and I/Os must be selected carefully and any targeted optimization carried out and fully validated at an early stage—not treated as a possible downstream option.
Every SoC designer understands that lowering supply voltage reduces energy—but at near threshold voltages, it changes transistor behavior and challenges traditional design assumptions.
Fig. 1: Energy efficiency improves at lower voltage, but delay and variability increase sharply near threshold.
As shown in Figure 1, reducing voltage lowers energy per operation, but comes with significant trade-offs: delay grows rapidly, variability increases, and noise margins shrink.
In this regime:
Voltage scaling is no longer an isolated optimization—it introduces tightly coupled challenges across the entire design stack.
Meeting power targets at ultra-low voltage is not sufficient; designs must achieve this predictably and without introducing additional silicon risk. This can be where Foundation IP moves from an incidental enabler to a significant part of the design success. The quality of logic libraries, memory compilers, and I/Os can directly determine the robustness of design closure and silicon outcomes.
A unified, silicon-proven Foundation IP platform—tightly coupled with EDA flows, built with the most accurate modelling and characterization methodologies and meticulously validated on silicon —provides the accuracy and consistency needed to enable PPA winning designs at ultra-low voltages, with reliable behavior from early design through signoff.
Memory is a dominant contributor to area and power—and often determines the system’s minimum operating voltage (Vmin) if not architecturally decoupled. This is addressed through flexible architectures:
Fig. 2: Dual-rail memory architecture decouples logic and memory VDD, validated at ISSCC 2025 with a 38 Mb/mm² SRAM at 380/540 mV in 3nm FinFET.
Different AI subsystems require different memory strategies: MAC tiles benefit from small, distributed SRAM blocks; activation units from ULP RFs with wide data-paths; and shared system buffers from high-bandwidth AXI interfaces.
Logic libraries must be engineered specifically with low-voltage operation in mind:
This modeling accuracy is essential to avoid unexpected surprises during low voltage signoff or timing failures on silicon.
In many designs, I/O domains define system-level Vmin. If I/O cannot operate reliably at reduced voltages, it blocks near-threshold logic benefits regardless of how well the core is optimized.
The portfolio spans control interfaces (GPIO, I3C/I2C, SWI3S), high-speed data links (LVDS, RGMII), clock and reference inputs, storage interfaces (SD/eMMC), test I/O, and 2.5D/3D integration I/O for chiplet-based systems—each validated for consistent operation across varying supply levels.
Achieving predictable, optimized operation at ~0.4–0.5V requires tight alignment across Foundation IP, EDA tools, modeling, and silicon validation.
Fig. 3: A closed-loop methodology aligns Foundation IP, tools, and silicon feedback to ensure optimized low-voltage design.
As shown in Figure 3, optimal low-voltage design depends on an iterative, closed-loop enablement process:
Synopsys Application Engineers bridge the gap between IP/EDA R&D experts and SoC designers during the customer design engagement, ensuring that the features are fully exploited and technologies are optimally deployed. The co-optimization of tools and IP keeps device physics, modeling assumptions, and silicon outcomes tightly coupled—transforming near-threshold design into a low risk, production-ready solution.
A power-sensitive AI networking SoC targeting high volumes in an advanced technology node, using near-threshold design, needed expert enablement. Supporting extremely low operating voltages for a design executed under a very compressed schedule. The Foundation IP solution included specially tuned low-voltage logic cells, custom level shifters and a custom dual-rail memory compiler, with specifically targeted PVT corner set all specifically selected to achieve the optimum design trade-offs for the best power efficiency through near-threshold signoff.
The results:
The key outcome: predictable execution without schedule or silicon risk.
Synopsys provides comprehensive documentation, design reviews, PPA tuning sessions, and direct application engineering engagement. DTCO and PPA exploration help customers select optimal IP configurations, while custom characterization services extend the platform for specialized requirements.
As edge AI workloads proliferate, supporting near-threshold operation is becoming a central requirement to enable power-optimized SoC design. Synopsys Foundation IP solutions—logic, memory, and I/O—deliver the architectural rigor, modeling accuracy, and rigorous silicon validation this regime demands. A broad portfolio, with extensive IP sets implemented with design consistency and supporting wide voltage ranges, simplifies IP reuse, enabling easier product migration across process generations and foundries.
Engage Synopsys early to define optimal voltage targets, select the right Foundation IP configurations, and establish a low-voltage-ready methodology tailored to your product goals. The power wall is real—but it’s not insurmountable.

articles.title: Uber Canada adds women driver preference, other safety features
articles.text:
Uber will launch new safety features aimed at women, seniors, and teenagers this month.
The first feature, named Women Driver Preferences, allows women, non-binary people, and teens of any gender to reserve a trip with a woman driver in 14 Canadian cities. Uber also notes that on-demand requests will also be available in select areas, subject to driver availability.
Canadian cities that will have the women drivers preference include Toronto, Vancouver, Montreal, Ottawa, Edmonton, Winnipeg, London, Hamilton, Quebec City, St. John’s, Gatineau, Trois-Rivières, Kitchener-Waterloo, and Kingston.
Further, on-demand requests will be available in Toronto and Montreal, and in select areas of Vancouver, Ottawa, Winnipeg, London, Quebec City, Gatineau, Kitchener-Waterloo and Kingston, subject to driver availability.
Uber initially started testing a similar program in a few markets globally in July of last year, where women drivers could select the option to only pick up female passengers, and women passengers could opt to select female drivers.
The second feature is known as expanded senior accounts. Building on last year’s Canadian launch, seniors can now set up and manage a senior account independently or connect with a family organizer for support with booking rides and managing payments. Uber also adds that seniors who manage their own account can still share their trip status with a loved one.
The expansion also brings larger text, clearer icons, customizable pickup preferences, and the option to let drivers know they are a senior and may need more time at pickup.
The third and final feature is known as live video for teen trips. Essentially, parents and guardians who are linked to a teen account can check in during eligible rides through the driver’s smartphone camera, if the driver has enabled that feature. Interestingly, both teens and drivers are notified when a guardian is watching, and only the linked guardian can view the encrypted stream live.
These new features come a few months after Uber released a new feature that allowed users to book a hotel directly on the app through a partnership with Expedia.
Update Nov. 12, 2026, at 11:46 p.m. ET: Added cities that will have the women driver preferences.

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns following affairs scandal - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns following affairs scandal
Nvidia Corp.’s board of directors today announced the resignation of Jensen Huang, now former chief executive and president of the artificial intelligence chipmaker, amid a scandal, naming Colette Kress, current executive vice president and chief financial officer, as interim CEO.
The news arrives following numerous industry reports that the board intended to replace Huang as CEO after revelations of a second extramarital relationship with an executive at Nvidia, coming mere days after he admitted to an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
News initially broke over the weekend that Huang had an affair with Alice Huang, no relation, an executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed International Pte. Ltd. and an alleged Chinese spy. The Information reported on Tuesday that Alice Huang facilitated $7.5 billion in chip sales to China. According to another report, Jensen Huang also had a relationship with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell, who serves as vice president of healthcare.
The New York Times reported last month that U.S. authorities concluded Alice Huang acted as a Chinese intelligence asset. Upon revelations of the affair, the Associated Press reported that President Trump announced that the Federal Bureau of Investigation was looking into the allegations, while adding, “I think that he’ll be in good shape.”
Late Wednesday, the Nvidia board met to decide whether to oust Huang and discussed a potential replacement as CEO. Huang has no obvious single successor and owns about 3.6% of Nvidia’s stock. Reportedly, the board sought counsel from an outside firm to find someone to fill the role.
With the announcement, Nvidia stock was falling more than 5% in trading today, backing off an even steeper loss at the opening. Yahoo Finance calculated that Nvidia has lost more than $600 billion in market value since the previous Thursday, likely with more shocks to come.
“Nvidia’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” said Kress. “We will continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead.”
Kress has served as executive vice president and CFO since joining in September 2013. Her accolades include leading the company’s finance organization and working to build the company’s dominance in the AI chip industry. Before joining Nvidia, she spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at leading technology companies, including Cisco Systems Inc. and Microsoft Corp.
The CFO was intimately involved with Nvidia’s widespread financing of AI compute providers, in particular its backing of not only AI leaders OpenAI Group PBC and Anthropic PBC — the latter set to go public as early as next week — but also neoclouds such as CoreWeave Inc. and Nebius Group NV. Those financings have been criticized by some as “circular,” meaning Nvidia essentially invested in customers so they could use the money to buy more of its graphics processing units.
The potential successors to Huang, who had 30 direct reports, include no one obvious choice and a succession plan apparently was not in place. Candidates that some have speculated about include Arm Ltd. CEO Rene Haas, who worked at Nvidia years ago, Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji, and Ian Buck, Nvidia’s vice president and general manager of hyperscale and high-performance computing and creator of its CUDA software considered the real moat for its business.
“The sudden resignation of Jensen Huang is about more than succession at the world’s most important AI chipmaker,” Forrester Vice President and Group Research Director Stephanie Balaouras told SiliconANGLE in an email. “Nvidia’s leadership crisis is a stress test for the AI boom. If Nvidia stabilizes quickly under new leadership, the AI infrastructure boom will have demonstrated resilience. If its stock, financing relationships or ecosystem commitments remain under sustained pressure, that would add evidence to the fragile side of the AI bubble ledger.””
Balaouras added that “tech leaders shouldn’t overreact, but they should treat Nvidia’s CEO transition as a prompt to reassess concentration risk across their AI infrastructure, suppliers and investment plans.”
Huang is best known for co-founding Nvidia in 1993 in a San Jose Denny’s and has served as its CEO since. His departure will likely send further ripples through the AI silicon and software industry. He has been deeply involved in Nvidia’s product strategy and built longstanding customer relationships, helming the company as it became the behemoth it is today.
Nvidia commands roughly 80% of the data-center AI chip market, although industry estimates vary by methodology. Epoch Artificial Intelligence Inc. puts its share of AI computing power shipped at 63% in the second quarter of 2026. Other market carve-outs include custom chips built by cloud companies within the broader supply, including Google LLC’s tensor processing units at 25%, Amazon Inc.’s custom silicon at 5% and Advanced Micro Devices Inc.’s AI hardware accelerators at 4%.
Nvidia is expected to report its third-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings on Nov. 17.

articles.title: Microsoft 365 Outage Disrupts Outlook, Exchange Online and Teams
articles.text:
Microsoft 365 suffered a widespread outage Thursday, disrupting access to business email and other cloud services across multiple regions. Microsoft initially reported that users in the Americas were having trouble connecting to Exchange Online mailboxes. It later identified potential disruption to Teams, SharePoint Online, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Defender XDR.
Some users of Google Workspace (formerly G Suite) also reported trouble accessing their Google-hosted email through Outlook desktop and mobile email clients.
Microsoft traced the increased load on its infrastructure to a large number of servers becoming unavailable, leaving the remaining systems to handle the traffic. The company said overall traffic had not increased.
Update: November 12 – 9:00PM ET – Microsoft said restarting affected servers was showing signs of improvement, though it was still monitoring their stability and had yet to confirm full recovery.
Microsoft said a process that establishes secure connections was becoming overwhelmed, causing affected servers to stop handling requests. The company began rolling back a recent network configuration change that coincided with the start of the disruption and was monitoring whether the rollback helped.
Both the Exchange Online incident (EX1550543) and the broader Microsoft 365 incident (MO1550821) remained open in its service health dashboard. Features of many Microsoft 365 services that interact with Exchange Online and email services are impacted. Elements of those services that do not depend on interaction with Exchange Online remain functional, Microsoft said.
Microsoft said a process that establishes secure connections was becoming overwhelmed, causing affected servers to stop handling requests. The company began rolling back a recent network configuration change that coincided with the start of the disruption and was monitoring whether the rollback helped. Microsoft had yet to confirm the root cause or disclose evidence of a cyberattack.
In an update just before 3 p.m. ET, Microsoft said affected servers were failing automated health checks and that it was testing a workaround that bypasses the component responsible for processing those checks. The company said it was also investigating elevated processor usage on affected servers.
Was the Microsoft outage caused by a cyberattack?
At the time of publishing, Microsoft is still investigating what triggered the failures and has disclosed no evidence of a cyberattack.
The company has yet to explain why the health checks failed or why processor usage rose on affected servers. Its service advisories did not report evidence of malicious activity.
The disruption came two days after Microsoft released its November Patch Tuesday updates, which addressed 1,094 vulnerabilities across its products. They included CVE-2026-124194, an Outlook spoofing flaw Microsoft says attackers have exploited. The flaw can expose a user’s authentication material if the user opens a specially crafted file in an affected Outlook client. Microsoft’s service advisories have not linked the vulnerability to the Exchange Online outage.
Microsoft is tracking the Exchange Online disruption under EX1550543 and the broader Microsoft 365 incident under MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin center. As of just before 3 p.m. ET, both incidents were listed as service degradations.

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned
articles.text:
Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang has resigned following revelations that he had two extramarital affairs, plunging the chipmaker at the heart of the global AI boom into crisis.
The 63-year-old will be replaced by chief financial officer Colette Kress, who will serve as interim chief executive.
His exit comes after he admitted to having a relationship with a woman that US authorities believe was a Chinese spy. It also emerged on Wednesday that Huang had an affair with a senior Nvidia executive.
Nvidia shares were down more than 10 percent in pre-market trading, extending earlier losses after the announcement of Huang’s resignation.
Huang, who cofounded Nvidia in 1993, led it to become what was until recently the world’s most valuable company.
Huang’s departure marks a startling end to his more than 33-year tenure, during which Nvidia evolved from a small video-game chip company into the linchpin of the global AI infrastructure boom.
Huang has become one of the most recognizable figures in tech, as Nvidia’s semiconductors became integral to training and running AI systems such as OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Anthropic’s Claude.
Nvidia stock extended its pre-market decline after the company announced that Jensen Huang had resigned as chief executive.
Shares were down 10.2 percent in pre-market trading, a move that would wipe off more than $400 billion in market capitalization.
This story was updated on November 12 with news of Huang’s resignation.

articles.title: Uber, DoorDash, and Airbnb say AI agents aren't taking off — reports reveal near-zero use as consumers reject bots
articles.text:
Uber, DoorDash and Airbnb say AI agents aren't taking off — as users rebel against being 'hyper-efficient at fun'
Sometimes, driving manually is just more fun
- Several firms say almost no one is using AI agents to access their services
- Uber, DoorDash and Airbnb all say the numbers are comically low
- Users have pushed back against AI agents and questioned their necessity
The whole point of using an AI agent, whether that’s Meta’s Muse or OpenAI’s Dots, is that it will save you time, change the way you work and perform the tedious drudgery that you’d rather not do. But several firms, including Uber, DoorDash and Airbnb, have admitted that almost no one is using AI agents to access their services, suggesting that the agentic revolution we were all promised might not be materializing — for now, at least.
The three firms said (via TechSpot) that AI agents had only been used to perform a small handful of transactions in recent weeks, compared to the millions carried out by real people. Uber, for example, had 320 million car rides booked by humans during the week of Halloween. The amount placed by AI agents? Just four, an almost comically low number.
DoorDash CEO Tony Xu shared a similar experience, saying that AI agents were responsible for several hundred orders on the platform. While the numbers aren’t as low as on Uber, TechSpot noted that DoorDash receives billions of orders every year.
And Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky argued that only a negligible portion of bookings on the app are made using AI agents. Chesky surmised that this might be because many people like to research trips themselves rather than hand everything over to an AI that can’t gauge the quality of a rental or the attractiveness of things to do nearby.
The AI agent backlash?
Part of the problem could be that AI agents are, in some cases, a solution in search of a problem. For instance, Uber’s chief financial officer Balaji Krishnamurthy stated that it takes people around 50 seconds to book a ride on the service, so it’s not exactly a longwinded process that AI agents can dramatically simplify.
There’s been something of a backlash on social media, too. On Reddit, one highly-upvoted comment noted that "thinking about what you feel like doing or eating is fun" and that few people are looking to become "hyper-efficient at having fun". An AI agent, they argued, sucks the joy out of life’s seemingly-mundane pursuits.
Another user put it this way: “So instead of opening the DoorDash app to order a pizza, I have to open my AI Agent and tell them I’m hungry and want to eat pizza and it has to be less than $30? Seems like more work to me to use [an] AI Agent.”
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Indeed, a recent report found that far from saving you time, AI tools are forcing many people to work an extra 90 minutes a day, while a separate study noted that workers are spending more time correcting AI content than doing actual work. Combined with the latest news from Uber, DoorDash and Airbnb, there's a growing sense that AI isn't always the time-saving solution it might appear on the surface.
Several companies and governments have already had enough of AI agents. The Wall Street Journal reports that United Airlines is banning AI bots from booking flights, while Alibaba has stopped its workers from using Claude Code and the Swedish government has blocked both Claude and ChatGPT over security concerns.
Perhaps one day AI agents will take off and everyone will be using them to streamline mundane tasks. But on the latest evidence, that day is a long way off — and there's a feeling that not every task is necessarily ripe for automation.

articles.title: Xbox announces Wolfenstein 3
articles.text:
It’s been nearly a decade since Bethesda’s MachineGames released Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus in 2017, and now Xbox is ready to announce a sequel from the studio. Wolfenstein 3 was officially announced today, just days after Bethesda also confirmed that the next Elder Scrolls game will be called The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel.
Xbox announces Wolfenstein 3
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma revealed a new entry in the Wolfenstein series with a brief tease.
In a post, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced the name and a photo of a script. “Looking forward to sharing more,” she said. MachineGames also announced the game in a post, saying the game is “in production” and sharing a photo from a motion-capture session. IGN reports that Brian Bloom (who plays protagonist William Joseph “BJ” Blazkowicz) and Debra Wilson (who plays Grace Walker) are reprising their roles, and they appear to be the featured actors in the photo.
The last mainline entry, Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus, launched in 2017 and continued the story of Blazkowicz in an alternate 1960s where Nazi Germany had won the Second World War. Wolfenstein: Youngblood also debuted in 2019 as a co-op spinoff, starring Blazkowicz’s twin daughters.

articles.title: « Les actes ont des conséquences » : le bras de fer qui secoue l'usine Volkswagen de la future Golf électrique - Numerama
articles.text:
La fin d’année s’annonce particulièrement tendue au siège historique de Volkswagen. Fin octobre 2026, une fuite révélait que le constructeur avait mis sur pause le développement de sa future Golf 100 % électrique (ou ID. Golf), alimentant les craintes sur les difficultés financières du groupe. Le 6 novembre dernier, lors d’une table ronde organisée à Xiamen (Chine) avec un groupe de journalistes français, dont Numerama, le patron de la marque Thomas Schäfer a confirmé ce gel temporaire et en a détaillé la cause.
Quelques jours plus tard, la réponse industrielle du site allemand se précise. Selon les informations publiées ce 11 novembre par Automotive News Europe, Volkswagen a décidé d’abandonner le programme industriel « Gamechanger » et son projet de gigacasting à Wolfsburg, préférant revenir à des méthodes d’assemblage plus conventionnelles pour sécuriser le lancement de ses prochains modèles électriques.
Un coup de pression nécessaire à l’usine de Wolfsburg
À Xiamen, le 6 novembre, Thomas Schäfer n’a pas cherché à enrober la situation pour expliquer pourquoi le programme ID. Golf a été figé : la sanction visait directement son usine mère. « Chaque usine a un objectif de réduction des coûts à respecter. Toutes les usines Volkswagen ont atteint leur objectif. Pas Wolfsburg. Ils ont raté leur cible d’environ 300 millions d’euros », a détaillé le dirigeant avec une franchise rare.
Face à ce dérapage budgétaire, Thomas Schäfer a choisi l’épreuve de force : le développement du véhicule resterait suspendu tant que la direction du site n’aurait pas présenté un plan d’économies à la hauteur du manque à gagner. Une réunion était prévue la semaine suivante, celle du 9 novembre. « Pour l’instant, c’est en pause, parce que 300 millions d’euros, c’est le coût de développement de la carrosserie d’une nouvelle voiture. Si vous gaspillez l’argent, vous ne pouvez pas avoir de nouvelle voiture. C’est aussi simple que cela », a-t-il tranché.
Thomas Schäfer nous a assuré que les futurs modèles restaient dans les temps. Le calendrier a pourtant déjà glissé, puisque l’ID. Golf, longtemps attendue en 2028, est désormais annoncée par Volkswagen pour le « début des années 2030 ». L’usine de Wolfsburg doit néanmoins rapidement améliorer ses résultats financiers.
Interrogé sur la portée psychologique d’un tel coup de frein au sein d’un groupe souvent critiqué pour son inertie, Thomas Schäfer a assumé la méthode forte : « L’équipe doit apprendre que les actes ont des conséquences. Nous sommes tous dans le même bateau, nous devons tenir nos chiffres pour nous défendre dans cet environnement ultra-concurrentiel. Si une équipe ne fait pas sa part du travail, il doit y avoir des conséquences. »
Wolfsburg renonce au gigacasting et revoit sa méthode de production
L’arbitrage tombe cinq jours après ce rappel à l’ordre, mais il dépasse le seul cas de Wolfsburg. Un porte-parole du groupe Volkswagen a confirmé ce mercredi 11 novembre que le programme « Gamechanger » ne sera pas déployé « sous sa forme initialement prévue ».
Concrètement, Volkswagen renonce à transformer Wolfsburg en usine vitrine équipée de presses géantes de gigacasting, une technique popularisée par Tesla qui consiste à mouler d’immenses sections de châssis en aluminium d’une seule pièce. Selon le Handelsblatt, le seul centre de fonderie aurait coûté plusieurs centaines de millions d’euros, et l’ensemble du programme quelques milliards. Un investissement qui a longtemps fait débat en interne.
Côté produits, ce renoncement permet toutefois de préserver l’essentiel. Le développement de la future plateforme SSP (Scalable Systems Platform) se poursuit, et les versions électriques du T-Roc, puis de la Golf, doivent toujours sortir de Wolfsburg, pour un volume annoncé de plus de 500 000 unités par an à elles deux. Côté direction, le transfert de la Golf thermique vers l’usine mexicaine de Puebla, prévu en 2027, reste au programme. Simplement, ces futures compactes électriques seront assemblées selon des procédés plus classiques, bien moins gourmands en investissements initiaux.
En une semaine, Wolfsburg a perdu son chèque en blanc, pour l’ID. Golf comme pour son usine vitrine. Sur le principe, c’est une bonne chose.
Volkswagen renonce à rattraper Tesla sur l’usine du futur. Sur le plan financier immédiat, la décision se défend, puisque le groupe évite d’engager quelques milliards d’euros au moment où ses comptes se tendent. Pour autant, Gamechanger devait justement faire baisser le coût de fabrication de l’ID. Golf et du T-Roc électrique. En revenant à des lignes classiques, Volkswagen économise sur l’investissement de départ, mais il lui faudra prouver que ses deux futures stars peuvent quand même sortir à un prix compétitif. Pourvu que le calcul tienne !

articles.title: Azure Logic Apps Standard Gets a Local CLI in Preview
articles.text:
Microsoft has released a public preview of a local command-line interface for Azure Logic Apps Standard, shipped as the logicapp extension for the Azure CLI. It adds project creation, workflow authoring, a local runtime, connector and connection management, run inspection, and test scaffolding to a tool that until now only managed deployed apps, so that a Standard workflow can be created, run, and tested without Visual Studio Code.
The extension installs automatically the first time an az logicapp developer command runs on Azure CLI 2.67.0 or later, and adds 19 command groups with 64 commands beside the thirteen existing cloud-management commands, which it leaves untouched. On the authoring side, project create creates or adopts a local project; workflow create, set, export, and validate work on individual workflow.json files with offline validation by default, and runtime start, stop, and show manage a local host on port 7071, launching the Azurite storage emulator when the project is configured for development storage.
The remaining groups reach into running and deployed apps. connector and connection inspect built-in and managed connectors and wire connections into a project or a deployed app, run and trigger history start, wait on, cancel and resubmit executions and download an action’s recorded inputs and outputs, and deployment package produces what the documentation calls a deterministic deployment package. Named context shortcuts hold a target so later commands do not repeat it.
(Source: Microsoft Community Hub)
The doctor and test commands say the most about who the tool expects to be typing. runtime doctor only reads: project files, tool versions, cached bundle evidence, loopback ports. It "never installs, downloads, starts, stops, repairs, decrypts settings, changes context, or contacts cloud storage," and it exits 1 for a required failure and 2 when a required check comes back unknown. Testing is split into three steps for the same reason. test create scaffolds a native SDK test project and stops before restoring a package or running anything, test plan writes a preflight report without executing a test, and test run is the only command that builds and runs them, under a deadline. The announcement lists limitations on that last step. In the pull request that added the extension, author Riley Evans goes further: native SDK test code is trusted rather than sandboxed, and the agent bootstrap command does not exist yet.
Sagar Sharma, a Microsoft MVP, wrote on LinkedIn that this is deliberate. The CLI is "literally pitched as adding determinism to local AI-assisted coding": an agent validates, runs, inspects and tests, then repeats until the run is green, and secrets reach it through stdin rather than on the command line. Sharma had already called the CLI the sleeper hit of Microsoft's recent Logic Apps announcements in an earlier write-up, on the grounds that an agent without a deterministic way to validate and run a workflow is guessing. Named contexts, capability discovery and the handling of secrets were his evidence that someone had designed for that case.
Sonny Gillissen, also a Microsoft MVP, put the same point in terms of a team's week. A new hire clones a repository and has a local runtime up "in minutes, instead of hours." A coding assistant drafting a workflow from a business requirement works "with an authoritative shell instead of assumptions." Integration flows get tested from the CI/CD pipeline instead of by hand. He called the CLI a bridge from today's development process to a fully automated one and, in passing, said an agent could test a workflow locally "without ever touching Azure at all."
That passing remark is the one Christos Panagiotidis, a Microsoft MVP and certified trainer, would test first. His pilot plan is explicitly a proposal rather than a report of a run, and its two main cautions come straight from Microsoft's own walkthrough. That walkthrough uses live Azure and Microsoft 365 resources, and some of its commands change deployed connections, so a local run has remote effects, whatever the terminal suggests.
Microsoft itself notes that validation "does not establish authorization or business correctness." Panagiotidis adds a housekeeping point: CLI extensions do not update with the CLI, so anyone comparing results across runs needs the CLI, extension, runtime and project versions recorded next to each result.
Microsoft has said a broader command surface will follow soon. Until then, the designer stays in VS Code. The CLI edits workflow.json directly; it cannot change the state of a running local app, and the pull request's own limits section concedes that Linux CI results prove neither native SDK execution nor execution against live Azure.

articles.title: See what AI looks like in production at Microsoft Ignite
articles.text:
See what AI looks like in production at Microsoft Ignite
If you’re deciding which AI pilots to move into production, Microsoft’s Satya Nadella and Judson Althoff’s opening keynote at Microsoft Ignite will show you where the company is taking the tools you’ll use to build and run those agents. They take the stage at 10 a.m. Pacific on Tuesday, November 17.
After the opening keynote, you can experience how customers put AI into production at scale, see where Microsoft is taking the tools those customers use, and compare notes with industry colleagues already doing the work. The breakout sessions (and hallway networking) offer the opportunity to double-click into results after an actual deployment.
With the rapid advancement of AI tools and resources, the best playbook is often the one your peers have already tested. Microsoft Ignite gives leaders a place to compare deployment strategies and lessons learned face to face, with organizations just getting started and others already getting results from AI in production.
Microsoft tells The New Stack that over four days, more than 100 organizations will take the stage across keynotes, breakout sessions and theater stages.
Microsoft tells The New Stack that over four days, more than 100 organizations will take the stage across keynotes, breakout sessions and theater stages. The organizations span AI startups such as Replit and Harvey, financial firms including Morgan Stanley and BNY, and companies such as Toyota and Siemens. If you’re choosing a first project (or deciding which pilot deserves more budget), the range at Ignite should give you a chance to gauge how teams with different goals are making those same decisions you’re facing.
How Microsoft AI solutions work together
Microsoft calls its approach Frontier Transformation. It starts with what people want to accomplish, the information AI agents need to help them, and finally, the controls an organization needs once AI is in use.
For employees, Microsoft 365 Copilot puts AI into tools they already use, including Teams and Word. Microsoft Fabric brings business data and analytics together, and Microsoft IQ gives Copilot and agents context, pulling from in-house data, workplace activity, documents, and the web. Developers can use GitHub and GitHub Copilot to write and review code, then use Microsoft Foundry to build, test, and deploy agents on Azure infrastructure. Finally, Agent 365 gives IT teams a place to see which agents are running, monitor their activity, and set policies.
Customer stories will also be a big part of each of the four innovation sessions.
Where should your AI actually run? Mark Russinovich and Pavan Davuluri will lead “AI Infrastructure From Cloud to Edge,” with examples of Microsoft using its own tech as “Customer Zero” (what Microsoft calls its high-stakes version of dogfooding). PricewaterhouseCoopers will appear in person, and OpenAI, Adobe, and Replit will share featured videos in this session. If you’re deciding what to run in Azure vs. closer to users, this session will offer the insight you need.
Microsoft reports that more than 40,000 people at Lilly use Copilot
How do you get people using agents in their everyday work? Lilly’s Bryce Williams is scheduled to join Microsoft’s Jacob Andreou in person for “Expanding What’s Possible: How AI Is Redesigning Work.” Microsoft reports that more than 40,000 people at Lilly use Copilot, and that more than 150 agents support work across research, clinical trials, and operations. If your team is rolling out Copilot, Lilly will showcase what helped its teams adopt it at scale.
How do you ensure your agents are working from the right information? In “Harnessing Your IQ With a Continuously Improving Agent Platform,” Arun Ulag and Jay Parikh will look at how agents use company data and knowledge, with planned spotlights on AEMO and NTT Data. You’ll hear how teams decide what an agent should be able to see and how they test whether it’s drawing on the right information.
How will you know your agents are working once they’re rolled out? Charles Lamanna and Hayete Gallot will lead “Observability at Every Layer for Every Role,” with planned videos from Royal Philips and KPMG, plus an onstage interview with the Bank of England. The Bank says nearly all of its employees use Microsoft 365 Copilot each week. Some agents that started as experiments are now in wider use, including one that answers staff questions about leave and pay. If you’re curious how to tell when an agentic system is trusted and ready for prime time, you’ll find out here.
If you’re curious how to tell when an agentic system is trusted and ready for prime time, you’ll find out here.
Between sessions, you can explore demonstrations in Moscone South, where planned customer installations include Alaska Airlines, Unilever, and more, with technical experts on hand. Theater sessions and lightning talks will also offer more time for questions.
There’s also a reason to step outside onto Howard Street between Third and Fourth streets, where plans include NFL and Premier League installations and a Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS Formula One car display.
If you’re heading to San Francisco, there’s still time to register for Microsoft Ignite and browse the session catalog. If you’re following from home, you can use the same registration page to get a free digital pass.
How to watch Microsoft Ignite 2026
Tune in to Live at Microsoft Ignite at 10 a.m. Pacific (1 p.m. Eastern) on Tuesday, November 17, to watch the opening keynote from Nadella and Althoff in full. The broadcast continues over the next three days with demos, customer stories, and executive interviews. The New Stack‘s own Jennifer Riggins will join the anchor desk throughout the show to talk through what the announcements mean for teams building and running AI in production.
Alysa Taylor, Microsoft’s Commercial Chief Marketing Officer, says to “Come with a challenge you’re excited to solve, whether that’s bringing ambition into the flow of work, connecting intelligence across your organization with the right data and context, or scaling AI innovation to drive meaningful business impact.
“Take in what you see on stage, then go deeper with the builders, customers, and leaders who are working through these same opportunities. The real value is connecting inspiration to action, and leaving with ideas you can put to work.”
Leave some time for networking after your sessions, too. If someone just described an agent you could imagine running in your organization, ask what it costs to scale, which metrics they are watching, or how they got their colleagues to adopt it.

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after alleged affairs
articles.text:
Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia’s president and CEO following revelations of affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy.
In a release published by Nvidia, the company confirmed that current executive vice president and CFO, Colette Kress, will serve as interim CEO until a permanent successor to Huang can be named. Kress will also continue to serve as CFO during this time.
“Jensen’s contributions to NVIDIA are profound. NVIDIA is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry,” Nvidia said.
The company’s shares have been in free fall since the news of Huang’s affairs broke, and his departure will likely spur further declines. As of writing, Nvidia’s stock was down nearly 13 per cent on Thursday.
Huang’s affair raised concerns among U.S. national intelligence leaders, leading to an FBI investigation. Further, U.S. lawmakers demanded Huang testify about the allegations, especially given Huang’s efforts to lobby U.S. President Donald Trump to ease restrictions on AI chip sales to China.
China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs called the spying allegations “pure fabrication” and claimed the reports were an effort to destabilize U.S.-China relations.
On Nov. 11, the New York Times reported on Huang’s second alleged affair, this time with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare.
Nvidia has played a significant role in the AI industry, with its chips powering much of the technology. Huang’s affairs and departure will likely spur increased scrutiny of Nvidia and its dealings, which have been at the centre of a circular cycle where the company invested in AI companies that would then use the money to buy Nvidia’s chips.
