articles.title: Google Wallet peut maintenant ouvrir la porte de votre maison, mais à plusieurs conditions
articles.text:
Voilà une fonctionnalité qui devrait plaire à tous ceux qui perdent trop souvent leurs clés ou qui restent bloqués devant la porte le temps de les trouver dans leur sac ou leurs poches. Google Wallet pour Android permet enfin de déverrouiller votre serrure connectée directement avec votre smartphone. L’application utilise pour cela les technologies NFC et UWB.
Quels appareils sont compatibles ?
Vous vous en doutez, cela ne fonctionne pour l’instant qu’avec certains modèles d’appareils. Ainsi, cela fonctionnera si vous utilisez une serrure compatible Matter avec la nouvelle norme ouverte Aliro. Au lancement, seuls trois modèles sont compatibles :
- L’Aqara U400 qui gère à la fois le NFC et l’UWB ;
- La Schlage Sense Pro limitée au NFC dans un premier temps (mais qui sera mise à jour pour l’UWB) ;
- La Nuki Keypad 2 NFC qui se contente du NFC.
Côté téléphone, un modèle sous Android 9 ou supérieur équipé d’une puce NFC suffit pour un déverrouillage par contact direct. En revanche, profiter de la technologie UWB et du mode mains libres demande un smartphone compatible, comme les Pixel 10 Pro, 10 Pro XL et 10 Pro Fold ou certains appareils Samsung Galaxy. Vous aurez également besoin d’un hub Google compatible Matter ou avec un routeur Thread comme le Nest Hub, le Nest Hub Max, le Nest Wifi Pro ou encore le Google TV Streamer.
Sécurité et configuration
Une seule clé numérique enregistrée dans Google Wallet permet de piloter l’ensemble des serrures compatibles installées dans un même foyer. Le système se lie donc directement au domicile que vous aurez configuré dans l’application Google Home plutôt qu’à un appareil spécifique.
Le déverrouillage sans contact demande évidemment que le téléphone ait été déverrouillé dans les heures précédentes et le mode mains libres par UWB reste désactivé par défaut pour éviter les ouvertures intempestives en passant devant sa porte. L’ajout d’une serrure compatible déclenche automatiquement une suggestion dans Google Home, même s’il reste possible de l’effectuer manuellement via les paramètres de l’application.
Ces nouvelles fonctionnalités ne concernent pour l’instant que les testeurs de la « Version Preview publique » de Google Home, mais devraient atteindre l’ensemble des utilisateurs dans les semaines à venir. Si vous êtes concernés, rendez-vous dans votre application Google Wallet puis dans « Paramètres de l’application Home > Clé Google Wallet ».

articles.title: SA fintech startup Lumepay raises $6m pre-seed round - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
South African cross-border payments startup Lumepay has raised US$6 million in pre-seed funding, alongside US$10 million in capital float, as it builds institutional-grade payment infrastructure for African businesses.
Led by CEO Harry Huang, Lumepay provides cross-border payment solutions for SMEs, corporates and institutions. Its rail-agnostic platform combines traditional finance and stablecoins to enable fast, cost-effective and transparent B2B transfers within and across African jurisdictions.
The startup launched Lumetrade, its digital asset and stablecoin trading venue, in April, before rolling out its payments platform in June, and has now raised US$6 million in pre-seed funding. The round was backed by founder-led angels and South African fintech investors. The US$10 million capital float was secured to give clients access to deep, reliable liquidity.
“The future of cross-border payments isn’t traditional finance or stablecoins; it’s a combination of both, backed by the FX depth to make them work for real businesses,” said Huang. “Our integrated approach addresses the real drivers of friction: fragmentation, liquidity inefficiency and execution risk.”
Lumepay is now live in Nigeria, Ghana, Tanzania, Malawi, Mozambique and Kenya, as well as the West and Central African CFA franc zones, and is awaiting further regulatory approvals to expand its payment capabilities in these markets.
Last month, the startup received regulatory clearance from the Central Bank of Kenya, marking its entry into East Africa. Businesses in Kenya can now use Lumepay to pay international suppliers in currencies including Chinese yuan, US dollars and Indian rupees, and to move money across intra-African trade corridors.
“In the months since the raise, we’ve turned plans into working products: diversified and reliable liquidity; a platform that handles cross-border payments end to end; a growing network of partners and payment rails; and regulatory clearance in South Africa and Kenya,” said Luc Varejes, Lumepay’s COO.
In South Africa, Lumepay works with Nedbank as its Third-Party Payment Provider (TPPP) sponsoring bank, while sister business Lume Trade, an authorised financial services provider covering crypto asset intermediary services, banks with Standard Bank.
“Working with Nedbank and Standard Bank across our two businesses reflects the compliance standards we have built from day one,” said Tatenda Nhemachena, Lumepay’s chief legal and compliance officer.
The pre-seed funding has been used to build out Lumepay’s core infrastructure, including its payment rails, banking relationships, regulatory approvals and licensed partner network. The startup is now focused on expanding its regulatory footprint across Southern, West and Central Africa, with Malawi, Mozambique and the CFA franc regions key targets, as it lays the groundwork for a Series A round.

articles.title: Exclusive: Menlo IRIS extension gives security teams control over AI use without a new browser - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Exclusive: Menlo IRIS extension gives security teams control over AI use without a new browser
Browser security company Menlo Security Inc. today launched the Menlo IRIS Browser Extension, a new offering that adds its enterprise browser security controls to the browsers employees already use with no need to switch them to separate secure ones.
Delivered as a centrally managed extension, Menlo IRIS is said to give security teams visibility into and control over generative artificial intelligence use, data movement, files and third-party extensions. Installation is claimed to take only hours, as no additional hardware is needed.
Chief Executive Bill Robbins, who took over the top job from co-founder Amir Ben-Efraim in February, said security teams have known for some time that the browser is a blind spot. Many have nonetheless held off on fixing it to avoid replacing an existing security stack, which typically means a big migration project, he added.
“Menlo IRIS removes those obstacles,” Robbins said. “Even a small team can get essential security running quickly on the browsers employees already use.”
To make its case, Menlo pointed to Verizon Communications Inc.’s 2026 Data Breach Investigations Report, released in May, which found regular AI use on corporate devices tripled from 15% to 45% of employees in a single year. Some 67% of people accessing AI services on corporate devices were found to be using noncorporate accounts, with more than 15% of users at the average company also running unauthorized AI browser extensions.
Among the headline capabilities is an audit of third-party browser extensions. Menlo says the audit covers every extension installed across a company, with an enterprise-wide inventory, real-time risk profiling and management controls all included. Few security teams have a count of the extensions their users have installed, according to Menlo. The company also warned that an extension’s risk profile can change at any time without notice.
Data-loss controls cover the clipboard, printing, uploads and downloads, with watermarking, read-only pages, restrictions on developer tools and screenshot deterrence also included. Web filtering steers users toward sanctioned tools, including generative AI services, with limits on what data can be entered into them offered as an alternative to banning the tools outright.
File security is part of the package as well, with inline inspection for data loss prevention violations, viruses and malware. For customers that want it, content disarm and reconstruction can be switched on to strip malicious content from files so they remain usable. Also available as an add-on is HEAT Shield AI for protection against zero-day phishing, social engineering and malvertising at the time of the click.
Deployment is through the Chrome Web Store, Microsoft Intune, Jamf or other device management tools, with support for Chrome, Edge, Safari, Firefox and Chromium-based AI browsers. Since nobody has to switch browsers, security patches from each browser’s vendor are said to keep reaching users as normal.
Most controls are enforced inside the browser session itself, which the company says removes the need for a proxy to route traffic. Menlo IRIS is intended to sit alongside existing network and endpoint tools.
The Menlo IRIS Browser Extension is available now.
Menlo Security has raised $250 million in funding, including a $100 million round in November 2020. Investors in the company include Vista Equity Partners Management, JPMorgan Chase & Co., American Express Ventures and General Catalyst Group Management.

articles.title: Claude zockt GTA 4 und andere Games: Wie dich der Agent dabei anstellt
articles.text:
Claude zockt GTA 4 und andere Games: Wie sich der KI-Agent dabei anstellt
Während es viele menschliche Spieler:innen gar nicht mehr erwarten können, ihre ersten Runden in GTA 6 zu drehen, gibt es einen nichtmenschlichen Gamer, der noch seine Runden in älteren Teilen der Reihe dreht. Dabei handelt es sich um den KI-Agenten des Reddit-Users „Wonderful Ad„, der Claude dazu gebracht hat, GTA 4 und viele weitere Titel zu zocken.
Wie kann Claude GTA 4 spielen?
Um das realisieren zu können, hat sich der User Hilfe von Claude Code geholt. Zusammen mit dem Coding-Agenten hat er einen MCP-Server entwickelt, der die Verbindung zwischen Claude, dem Endgerät des Users, und damit auch dem Spiel herstellen kann. Wie er schreibt, bekommt Claude dadurch seine „eigene Tastatur, Maus, Gamepad und Bildschirmaufnahme“, um Inhalte zu erkennen und zu steuern.
Games wie GTA 4 werden dabei im Hintergrund auf dem PC des Users ausgeführt. Er kann das Gerät also auch nutzen, während Claude parallel zockt. Zudem können mehrere Instanzen von Claude gleichzeitig in verschiedene Spiele geschickt werden. Den Aufwand betreibt der User, um eigens entwickelte Mods für eine Vielzahl von Spielen automatisiert testen zu lassen.
Die bloße Anbindung an die Spiele bringt Claude aber noch lange nicht dazu, plötzlich den Story-Modus von GTA 4 durchzuzocken. Stattdessen kann die KI nur einfache Befehle im Spiel ausführen. So etwa das Fahren, Fliegen oder Laufen zu gesetzten Wegpunkten auf der Karte. Um das zu ermöglichen, bekommt jedes Spiel ein eigenes Profil von Claude Code. Darin sind Informationen enthalten, wie die Minikarte aussieht, wie sich die Kamera drehen lässt und wie Wegpunkte aussehen.
Was anhand der aufgenommenen Spielszenen schnell klar wird: Ein professioneller Gamer wird Claude so schnell nicht. Gerade beim Steuern der Spielfigur zu Fuß läuft die KI immer wieder gegen Wände, Autos und Personen. Sie sucht im Grunde nur die möglichst direkte Verbindung zwischen der aktuellen Position und dem gesetzten Wegpunkt.
Wie schlägt sich Claude in anderen Games?
Neben GTA 4 hat der Entwickler Claude auch noch auf einige weitere Games losgelassen. In Detroit: Become Human zockte die KI die erste Szene des Spiels, in der ein Android mit einem anderen Androiden verhandelt, der eine menschliche Geisel genommen hat. Hier musste Claude immer wieder Entscheidungen treffen, um das Schicksal aller Beteiligten zu entscheiden.
Auch hier zeigen sich aber die Limitierungen. Claude wählt lediglich offensichtliche Optionen auf dem Bildschirm aus. Zusätzliche Informationen aus der Umgebung zu erhalten, indem die Kamera gedreht wird, funktioniert bislang nicht. In Cities: Skylines versuchte Claude auch noch, eine Stadt zu errichten. Die Bewohner verließen sie aber schon kurz nach dem Einzug wieder, da Anschlüsse für Trink- und Abwasser fehlten.
Wer das Projekt selbst ausprobieren möchte, kann das dank des GitHub-Projekts tun. Die Anbindung sollte allerdings laut dem Entwickler nur für Offline-Games vorgenommen werden. Die Integration könnte bei Multiplayer-Spielen zu einer dauerhaften Sperre durch die Anti-Cheat-Systeme führen.

articles.title: Keralam aims to be value led destination for deeptech startups
articles.text:
Keralam positions itself as a value-driven launchpad for deeptech startups
The Keralam government is keen to enhance the value of its startup ecosystem especially with the deeptech segment providing financial and other infrastructure support
Keralam wants to build its startup ecosystem and lead from the front, especially in deeptech and AI.
At the inaugural of Huddle Global 2026, a beachside startup festival of the Keralam government, Chief Minister V D Satheesan said, “Our next task is to take Kerala's companies to the world. Kerala does not need the most startups. It must be the place where startups grow stronger.”
The state which had about 300 startups in 2016 now has around 9,200 such young companies with a combined valuation of $1.7 billion. The startup segment of Keralam has attracted over Rs 8,500 crore of funding.
Huddle Global has been positioned by the Keralam government as a showcase of its startup ecosystem and the inaugural edition was held in 2018.
The chief minister said there will be a shift in its approach for its startup ecosystem where the first phase was all about a mission and the second phase is to scale this mission.
He also highlighted that the state government has been supporting the startups through a fund of funds programme and is looking to strengthen this initiative by increasing the limits of its innovation grants, R&D support and seed funding.
“Our aim is simple. In Kerala, a good idea should never fail for the lack of capital,” Satheesan remarked.
The Chief Minister also stressed on the role of future technologies coming into play and the State government is looking to strengthen its incubation network through stronger partnerships with academia.
P K Kunhalikutty, Minister for Industries, IT, Future Technology and Startups, Keralam said, “Our focus will also be on emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence.” He further added that the government will bring in more initiatives in this segment to attract investments.
“Kerala is entering an important phase of economic transformation. We are focusing on attracting domestic and international investment, promoting emerging industries and creating new opportunities for sustainable growth,” the minister said.
S Suhas, Special Secretary, Electronics and IT Department, government of Keralam, highlighted the progress made by the startup ecosystem in the State. This includes building an edge AI chip, a satellite launch along with SpaceX, a mechanical manhole cleaning machine that has bagged in contract in Singapore etc.
“In Keralam one no longer has to ask whether it can build startups. The question today is how big they can grow,” he remarked.
The official said the government has taken numerous steps to encourage the startups in the State, especially becoming the first customers for these young companies.
He also stressed the growth of innovation centres in Keralam with over 600 colleges having such facilities with 63 incubators and over 10 lakh square feet of startup space.
The target of the Keralam government is to have around 100 deeptech startups valued at Rs 100 core and above.

articles.title: Jensen Huang renuncia como CEO de Nvidia, el gigante de los chips de IA, tras 33 años en el cargo
articles.text:
Jensen Huang renunció como CEO de Nvidia y dejó al fabricante de chips de inteligencia artificial (IA) sin la figura que convirtió a la empresa en una potencia de la IA. Su salida abre una sucesión en una compañía valorada en 4 billones de dólares y amenaza con alterar la red de proveedores, servicios en la nube y laboratorios tecnológicos que Nvidia ayudó a financiar.
La directora financiera, Colette Kress, asumirá como directora ejecutiva interina mientras la empresa busca un reemplazante permanente. Nvidia también designó a Harvey Jones, exdirector ejecutivo y miembro del consejo de Synopsys, como su primer presidente de la junta directiva.
Huang dejará además su puesto en el consejo de administración. El cofundador de la compañía era su cuarto mayor inversor, con una participación aproximada del 3,61%.
Las acciones de Nvidia bajaron más de 10% en las operaciones previas a la apertura del mercado, una caída que presionó al conjunto de las cotizaciones. La reacción se produjo cuando los inversores ya mostraban inquietud por el consumo de efectivo y el aumento de la deuda de los grandes grupos tecnológicos, pese a su tradicional disponibilidad de liquidez.
Una sucesión bajo presión sobre la ejecución tecnológica
La salida de Huang plantea dudas sobre la capacidad de Nvidia para sostener la coordinación de un ecosistema que incluye fabricantes, operadores de infraestructura en la nube y grandes laboratorios de inteligencia artificial. La empresa había invertido su creciente flujo de efectivo en esos actores, que a la vez se convirtieron en compradores y socios de sus chips.
El riesgo principal no está en la hoja de ruta tecnológica, que ya resulta visible para los próximos años, sino en la ejecución, afirmó a Reuters Michael Feldman, gestor de cartera de ClearBridge Investments. “Jensen ha sido el principal responsable de un sistema extraordinariamente complejo”, sostuvo, y añadió: “En un mundo con verdaderos cuellos de botella, esa coordinación constituye en sí misma una ventaja competitiva”.
Durante años, Nvidia fue identificada sobre todo con los jugadores que buscaban gráficos de alto rendimiento. La capacidad de sus procesadores para realizar múltiples cálculos en paralelo los transformó después en una pieza central del desarrollo de inteligencia artificial y en un activo estratégico de la competencia tecnológica entre Estados Unidos y China.
Ese ascenso convirtió a Nvidia en la empresa más valiosa del mundo y dio a Huang una notoriedad inusual entre los directivos tecnológicos. En Taiwán y Corea del Sur, seguidores le pedían firmas en libros, carteles e incluso en sus cuerpos, mientras que las menciones de empresas durante sus presentaciones podían mover las acciones.
Las relaciones investigadas y el vínculo con China
La presión sobre Huang aumentó tras informaciones sobre una relación con Alice Huang, exejecutiva de la empresa de computación en la nube Megaspeed, con sede en Singapur. Las autoridades estadounidenses concluyeron que ella era agente de la inteligencia china, mientras Pekín negó que fuera espía.
Ambos fueron fotografiados juntos en Taiwán, Singapur y California, y no tienen parentesco. Washington también investigó a Megaspeed, socio oficial de Nvidia con acceso prioritario a sus chips, ante sospechas de que pudo ayudar a China a obtener procesadores avanzados restringidos por los controles de exportación estadounidenses.
A comienzos de mes, el consejo de administración de Nvidia abrió una investigación dirigida por consejeros independientes y con asesoramiento jurídico externo para establecer si Huang había sido blanco de una operación de inteligencia extranjera. En ese momento, la junta expresó su confianza en el ejecutivo.
La controversia escaló el miércoles 11 de noviembre, cuando The New York Times informó que Huang también había mantenido una relación extramatrimonial con Kimberly Powell, vicepresidenta de atención médica de Nvidia, quien dependía directamente de él. Según una persona familiarizada con el asunto, la junta se reunió ese día para considerar su destitución.
La renuncia puede tener efectos sobre la política estadounidense de exportación de chips. Huang había defendido preservar el acceso de Nvidia al mercado chino y mantenía vínculos estrechos con el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump.
Trump afirmó el domingo 8 de noviembre de 2026 que Huang había “hecho un trabajo increíble para nuestro país” y que el entonces jefe de Nvidia le dijo que desconocía que la empresaria china con la que mantuvo una relación fuera una espía.

articles.title: Nigerians can pay without cards or transfers, yet remain completely unaware
articles.text:
The next time a point-of-sale (PoS) agent asks for a bank card, inserting it may not be necessary. Some Nigerian cards can already complete transactions with a single tap.
TechCabal tested this at a local PoS merchant. Using a Verve debit card issued through ALAT, the digital banking platform of tier-2 Nigerian lender Wema Bank, the team held the card near the terminal instead of inserting it. The machine recognised the card, requested a PIN, and dispensed ₦1,500 ($1.11) from the ₦1,600 ($1.19) transaction, which included a ₦100 ($0.074) merchant fee. The cash withdrawal went through without the card being inserted into the machine.
It was a small transaction, but it demonstrated a payment capability already available on some Nigerian cards and PoS terminals, yet still unfamiliar to many consumers.
The feature is easier to spot than it may seem. Look for a small contactless symbol on the card or PoS terminal: four curved lines that resemble radio waves. The symbol is often mistaken for the Wi-Fi logo, but it signals something different. On a card, it means the card can make contactless payments; on a terminal, it means the machine can accept them. The tap works through Near Field Communication (NFC), a technology that lets devices exchange data when they are close to each other.
Contactless payments are not new to Nigeria. In May 2015, Unified Payments, a Nigerian payment processing company, introduced a Near Field Communication (NFC) payment solution.
In September 2022, global payments company Mastercard, Nigerian commercial bank Providus Bank, French digital security company Thales, and African payments technology company Interswitch launched tokenised tap-to-pay solutions for smartphones and wearables, following nine months of development.
Now, Google Pay’s October 2026 market entry and a growing number of homegrown fintech solutions are drawing renewed attention to a technology that has been in use in Nigeria for more than a decade.
These developments could expand how Nigerians pay and receive money. Customers can use compatible smartphones instead of physical cards, while merchants can turn NFC-enabled smartphones into payment terminals. Other companies are exploring contactless payments linked to bank accounts and digital wallets. But wider adoption will depend on whether banks, merchants, and consumers can make the technology work in everyday transactions.
From contactless cards to Google Pay
The most visible development in Nigeria’s contactless payments market came on October 28, when Mastercard and Interswitch announced that eligible Mastercard holders could use Google Pay to make contactless payments with compatible Android devices.
The launch, announced at the 2026 edition of Moonshot by TechCabal, lets customers add supported Mastercard cards to Google Wallet and pay at merchants with compatible contactless terminals using their phones. Instead of presenting a physical card, customers authenticate on their phone and hold it close to the PoS terminal.
The partnership brings together three different parts of the payment experience. Google provides the digital wallet through which customers store and access their payment credentials. Mastercard provides the card network and tokenisation infrastructure, while Interswitch connects participating card issuers to the processing and tokenisation capabilities required for the service to work.
The innovation lies in turning regular NFC-enabled smartphones into payment devices while existing card networks continue to handle the transactions.
Interswitch is working with five Nigerian banks—GTBank, Wema Bank, ProvidusUnity Bank, Zenith Bank, and FirstBank—to expand tokenised payments across digital wallets and banking apps. But the partnership does not give every customer of those banks immediate access to Google Pay. Google’s published list currently supports selected cards from FirstBank, GTBank, Providus Bank, UBA, and Zenith Bank.
Wema Bank, despite its involvement in Interswitch’s initiative, is absent from that list. So are Verve and AfriGO cards. Even customers with eligible cards still need NFC-enabled Android phones and merchants with compatible contactless terminals. The rollout exposes a gap between the institutions building Nigeria’s tap-to-pay infrastructure and the customers who can use it today.
Once users have added and verified an eligible card on an NFC-enabled smartphone, they can tap at a local PoS terminal to make payments. For merchants, however, accepting contactless payments requires more than an NFC-enabled terminal. Acquiring banks and payment processors must support the transaction, and the terminal must recognise the customer’s card network or digital wallet. A PoS machine can carry the contactless symbol and still reject certain payment methods.
Nigerian fintech companies are also working to expand where customers can tap and what they can tap with. CashAfrica, a payments startup, has introduced a contactless mobile payment service in partnership with the fast-food chain Chicken Republic. Nearpays, another Nigerian payments startup, is developing software that allows merchants to accept contactless payments directly on compatible smartphones.
Nearpays uses software-based point-of-sale technology (SoftPOS) to turn an NFC-enabled Android phone into a payment terminal. A merchant enters an amount in the Nearpays application, and the customer taps a contactless card or supported device against the phone. The software initiates the transaction through the payment processing system.
“We’ve built a product that sits as a mediator and can communicate easily to both parties,” Nearpays founder and chief executive officer Victor Daniyan told TechCabal.
According to Daniyan, Nearpays routes domestic card transactions through the Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System (NIBSS), the country’s payment switch, and international card transactions through Visa, with banking partners involved in processing.
The model could reduce one of the costs of accepting card payments: PoS hardware. Merchants with compatible smartphones may be able to accept payments without acquiring another device, although processing fees, security requirements, and settlement arrangements still apply. Its commercial appeal will depend on whether those savings outweigh the costs of using the service.
The approach has gained ground beyond Nigeria. In 2025, Visa, the global payments giant, said its Tap to Phone technology processed over $33 billion in payments, underscoring the scale of smartphone-based acceptance in other markets. But those figures offer no guarantee of similar adoption in Nigeria, where merchants and customers already have a familiar alternative in bank transfers.
Together, Google Pay, CashAfrica, and Nearpays show how companies are expanding contactless payments from both ends of a transaction. They are changing the devices customers use to pay, and the equipment merchants need to accept payment.
However, underneath those interactions, payment credentials still need to reach financial institutions securely, without unnecessarily exposing sensitive account or card information.
What tokenisation changes, and what it does not
A phone can imitate a payment card without storing or transmitting the card’s original number during each transaction. That is one of the advantages of tokenisation, the security technology underpinning services such as Google Pay, the newly launched product in Nigeria.
When a customer pays with Google Pay, the phone does not need to share the original card number with the merchant. Instead, it uses a digital stand-in for the card. That is essentially what tokenisation does.
Think of it as giving someone a spare key that works only under certain conditions, while keeping the original key safe. The token represents the customer’s card, but it cannot be used in all the same ways as the card number it replaces.
When a customer adds an eligible Mastercard to Google Wallet, the bank verifies the card, and Mastercard’s Digital Enablement Service (MDES) helps create a token linked to the phone. Each payment also carries a unique security code, called a “cryptogram,” which helps the payment network check that the transaction is authentic. The code changes with each transaction, making captured payment information harder to reuse.
If the phone goes missing, the bank or wallet provider can disable its token without necessarily cancelling the physical card.
Tokenisation works alongside NFC, but the two do different jobs. NFC lets the phone and PoS terminal exchange information when they are close together. Tokenisation helps keep the customer’s original card details out of that exchange. Banks and payment networks still check and approve the transaction before money moves.
Not every contactless card uses the same token system as Google Wallet. Tokenisation also protects online payments, where customers do not tap anything.
For Nigerian payment companies, the greater opportunity may lie in expanding contactless payments beyond card networks.
Bank transfers already dominate much of Nigeria’s digital payment activity. In its Payments System Vision 2028 (PSV 2028) strategy document released in June, the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) said that web and Internet transfers accounted for 51.9% of retail non-cash transaction volumes as of June 2024, compared with 28.5% for PoS transactions.
Nigerians have become accustomed to paying directly from their accounts, creating a commercial challenge for any product that asks them to adopt another payment method.
CashAfrica is attempting to build on that behaviour by developing account-based tokenisation. Rather than requiring a customer to hold a physical card, the company said it can create a digital identifier (a token) linked to a bank or fintech account and use it to initiate contactless payments.
Malik Asamu, the company’s founder and chief executive officer, argued that the opportunity lies in adapting contactless infrastructure to a market where consumers are more accustomed to using accounts than cards.
“If we can build an innovation that allows us to tokenise accounts, like we do cards, that then means that you can tokenise an account in the same model that you tokenise a card,” Asamu told TechCabal.
CashAfrica’s approach differs from Mastercard’s card-tokenisation model. Mastercard substitutes a card credential that already operates on its payment network. The fintech aims to make account balances accessible via a contactless payment experience, which requires identifying the account, authenticating the customer, and initiating a transaction through participating financial institutions.
The payment journey Asamu described, however, still involves an intermediary wallet. Customers first transfer money in the CashAfrica Cash Mobile app, select “Tap to Pay,” authenticate with a PIN or biometrics, and tap a compatible merchant terminal.
That introduces a commercial hurdle. A customer who already has money in a bank account must move it into another wallet before paying. For someone accustomed to making an instant transfer from a banking app, the additional step could offset the convenience of tapping a phone.
CashAfrica’s longer-term ambition is to make contactless payments available through existing banking and fintech applications.
Tokenisation protects card details, but it cannot prevent all forms of payment fraud. EMVCo, the international body that sets payment technology standards, said the technology limits what criminals can do with stolen card information.
However, in Nigeria, fraud increasingly relies on tricking customers into revealing sensitive information or gaining unauthorised access to their accounts. According to NIBSS, financial institutions lost ₦25.85 billion ($19.2 million) to digital payment fraud in 2025, even as losses fell by 51% from the previous year.
NIBSS noted that social engineering, account compromise, SIM-swap fraud, and phishing are among the industry’s biggest threats. A token can protect a card number, but it cannot stop a customer from being tricked into approving a fraudulent payment.
Regulation introduces another constraint. Under the CBN’s June 2023 rules, contactless payments through accounts and wallets can proceed without additional verification up to ₦15,000 ($11.14) per transaction and ₦50,000 ($37.14) cumulatively per day. Higher-value transactions require appropriate verification and authorisation, with further restrictions applying above the daily threshold.
Tokenisation can make digital payment credentials safer to use across devices. But it cannot, on its own, make banks integrate with new payment services, persuade merchants to accept them, or convince customers to abandon payment methods they already know and trust.
Will more Nigerians tap?
Nigeria’s digital payments market continues to expand. In 2025, the CBN said that electronic payment transaction volumes rose by 2.6% to 47.88 billion, up from 46.65 billion the previous year. The value of these transactions increased by 26.1% to ₦4.36 quadrillion ($3.28 trillion), from ₦3.46 quadrillion ($2.6 trillion) in 2024.
Nigeria’s growing digital payments market gives contactless providers a large customer base to potentially convert, but not necessarily a ready market. Bank transfers already allow customers to pay merchants directly from their accounts, often without a card or PoS terminal. A tap—whether using smartphones, cards, or other wearables—must offer a noticeable advantage in speed, convenience, or reliability to change that behaviour.
The United Kingdom offers an example of how that shift can happen. Contactless payments accounted for just 3% of all UK transactions in 2015. A decade later, they accounted for 39% of payments, with 19.2 billion recorded in 2025, according to UK Finance.
Years of investment in everyday acceptance underpinned much of the growth that contactless payments experienced in the UK. In 2012, London’s transport authority introduced contactless bank card payments on buses and extended them to the Underground and rail network in 2014.
Commuters could pay fares using cards they already owned, without obtaining a separate travel card, and benefit from the same fares and daily caps available through the Oyster system. By 2017, passengers had made more than one billion contactless journeys across London’s public transport network.
The wider banking industry also made the technology easier to use. Banks issued more contactless cards, merchants installed compatible terminals, and payment limits increased to accommodate more purchases. By the end of 2024, 89% of cards in circulation in the UK supported contactless payments, according to UK Finance.
The UK example suggests that adoption depends on giving customers frequent opportunities to tap, without requiring them to change how they hold or access their money. Public transport helped establish the habit, while widespread card issuance and merchant acceptance brought the technology into everyday shopping.
Nigeria already has its own example of contactless payments becoming routine. In Lagos, commuters use Cowry cards to tap onto regulated buses, trains, and ferries. Touch and Pay, the fintech operating the system, said it had surpassed five million users by 2025 and reported processing over ₦20 billion ($14.9 million) in transactions in 2024.
But Cowry operates through a dedicated transport payment system: commuters either load funds onto a physical card and tap it at transport terminals, or fund their Cowry account and pay using the app’s quick response (QR) code scanner. Participating transport operators accept both methods.
Extending contactless payments across ordinary retail transactions presents a different challenge because banks, card networks, and merchants must support compatible payment methods.
Google Pay, CashAfrica, and Nearpays are attempting to bring contactless payments into everyday transactions, but wider acceptance alone may not be enough to persuade Nigerians to change how they pay.
Nearpays’ proposition is partly about the merchant. The fintech’s solution lets NFC-enabled smartphones accept contactless payments without a hardware PoS terminal, potentially lowering the barrier to entry for businesses that want to accept card payments.
But the benefit to customers is less clear-cut. In our ₦1,500 ($1.11) withdrawal test, tapping the Verve card eliminated the need to insert it into the terminal, but the transaction still required a PIN.
Yet, for tap-to-pay to gain ground beyond transport and become commonplace in retail payments, security cannot be compromised in pursuit of convenience, especially at its current early stage of adoption.
With the speed advantage potentially amounting to mere fractions of a second over existing digital payment methods, and authentication still required in some cases, tapping may struggle to offer Nigerians a compelling reason to change how they pay. Without a clearer advantage, it risks remaining just another cool way to make a payment.

articles.title: Una comunidad exige a un propietario que quite el cañizo del muro de separación con el vecino: la justicia dice que se deja porque no afecta a los elementos comunes ni a la estética de la fachada
articles.text:
Instalar un cañizo para separar tu casa de la del vecino se puede convertir en un problema con la comunidad de propietarios. Justo eso es lo que vivió un vecino de Las Palmas de Gran Canaria al que la junta exigió retirar el cañizo que había colocado en el muro de separación porque, a su juicio, afectaba a la estética del edificio. Sin embargo, el propietario decidió acudir a la justicia y terminó saliéndose con la suya al lograr que se anulara el acuerdo.
Como recoge NoticiasTrabajo en su información sobre el conflicto vecinal, la comunidad había aprobado un requerimiento para que el hombre retirara la instalación en un plazo de 2 meses. Tras advertirle que podrían tomar medidas judiciales si no lo hacía, el vecino impugnó la decisión al considerar que le causaba un perjuicio injustificado. ¿Lo mejor para él? El Juzgado de Primera Instancia número 16 de Las Palmas de Gran Canaria le dio la razón y el acuerdo se declaró nulo.
Cuando la comunidad recurrió la decisión, la Audiencia Provincial de Las Palmas confirmó la decisión del juzgado. El cañizo estaba instalado en un muro interior de separación entre viviendas y, como no afectaba a la fachada del edificio, nunca alteró la configuración ni entraba en conflicto con los elementos comunes. Así, el argumento de que perjudicaba la estética no fue suficiente para obligar al propietario a retirarlo.
En este punto entra en juego el artículo 7 de la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal, que permite realizar modificaciones dentro de una propiedad privada siempre que no se altere la seguridad, la estructura general o el estado exterior del edificio, ni se perjudiquen los derechos de otros propietarios. Por eso, no todas las instalaciones que desagradan a la comunidad pueden prohibirse, ya que también hay que comprobar dónde se encuentran y si realmente incumplen alguna de estas limitaciones.
A todo esto debemos sumar que el artículo 18 de la misma ley permite impugnar determinados acuerdos comunitarios ante los tribunales. En este caso, la Audiencia desestimó el recurso de la comunidad y mantuvo la nulidad del requerimiento, por lo que el propietario pudo conservar el cañizo. Eso sí, la sentencia no era firme cuando se publicó la noticia y todavía cabía recurrir ante el Tribunal Supremo si se cumplían los requisitos legales.

articles.title: Jensen Huang agrees to testify before Congress | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before Congress, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said on Thursday, according to reports from Bloomberg and NBC News.
Huang, who stepped down as CEO following reports of an alleged affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, agreed to testify Wednesday after several senior lawmakers threatened to subpoena him.
Huang has agreed to testify before Congress by Thanksgiving, which falls later this month.
The development comes after House Republicans Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford sent Huang a letter on November 4 requesting that he appear before their committees. Moolenaar chairs the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, Mast chairs the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, and Crawford chairs the House Intelligence Committee.
“Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very important company to the United States of America,” Mast said to reporters. “I don’t want to see anything hurt in Nvidia, but he has some very serious questions to answer.”
The testimony will take place behind closed doors, though Mast said he expects the briefing to be recorded on video and transcribed.

articles.title: Hundreds of streaming services and nothing to watch
articles.text:
“Fifty-seven channels, and nothin’ on.”
Bruce Springsteen famously said those words during a concert and later in a song in the 1990s about the number of TV channels seemingly growing disproportionately to the availability of enjoyable content.
Within a few years, there would be hundreds of TV channels and still, some would argue in hyperbolic frustration, “nothing to watch.”
The advent of streaming services was poised as a potential solution to this problem. It granted viewers easy, on-demand access to thousands of movies and shows, which, theoretically, could ensure that viewers could always find something to watch.
According to a survey from Nielsen’s Gracenote, though, that’s not exactly the case today.
Gracenote, a Nielsen-owned content data business, surveyed 3,000 video streaming users in the US, Brazil, France, Germany, Mexico, and the UK who were at least 18 years old for its “2026 State of Play: Amid fragmentation frustrations, UX is the future of streaming” report. It found that many struggle to find something to stream. However, this is not necessarily because there’s nothing good on, but rather because they find it difficult to home in on good content on streaming services.
For example, over 51 percent of respondents said that “the abundance of content and [streaming] services is making it harder to find something to watch.”
Further, 19.2 percent of respondents said that, on average, they either “always” or “often” don’t know what to watch, can’t find anything, and then decide to do something else. And 27.4 percent of respondents said that, on average, they either always or often try to watch a specific program but end up not watching it because they couldn’t find it on streaming.
“Through the lens of catalogue size and streaming usage, connecting the 83.4 percent who don’t always know what they want to watch should be fairly straightforward, especially as companies increasingly use customer data to create personalized experiences that foster long-term engagement and loyalty. Audiences, however, aren’t finding what they’re looking for, and content discovery challenges are mounting,” the report reads.

articles.title: Conexus Venture Capital raises additional $5 million for Fund II | BetaKit
articles.text:
Regina’s Conexus Venture Capital (CVC) has raised more for its latest fundraising round than originally planned, adding another $5 million to its Fund II after reopening to investors earlier this year.
The news: CVC announced the additional fundraise on Nov. 12, bringing the total closing dollar figure to $35 million. CVC, which initially closed investment to Fund II in November of 2025, cited strong participation demand from investors and early portfolio momentum as key to its decision to re-open the fund.
From the source: “We are grateful to our investors for their continued confidence in our team, our thesis, our fund, and, most importantly, our founders,” Jordan McFarlen, CVC’s managing director, said in a press release. “Reopening the fund due to increased demand is an excellent signal. We’re excited to put the capital to work.”
The context: As the venture capital (VC) branch of Conexus Credit Union, CVC typically invests in early-stage tech companies, an area of Canadian VC that has seen significant declines in recent years. CVC’s Fund I ranked among the top performers in its size category in 2019. Fund II has grown its portfolio by 10 companies as of press time, including investments into fellow Regina startup Offstreet, Saskatoon’s Alto Technologies, Judi.ai, and Cyder, among others.
CVC hasn’t disclosed who contributed to the initial or follow-on raises for Fund II, but the firm’s parent credit union is the anchor limited partner, putting $15 million into the pot. In an interview with Regina’s Leader-Post, McFarlen said investment came from both repeat participants and new financiers.
Final thought: The Canadian VC landscape has been shrinking in the past half-decade, with the Canadian Venture Capital Association (CVCA) reporting that spending fell from nearly $15 billion in 2021 to $8 billion in 2025. Early-stage investment has, in particular, been impacted by that drawback of private dollars. However, 2026 has seen two high-profile deals in Western Canada that delivered significant returns to early-stage investors, including PurposeMed’s acquisition by Grindr and CoolIT Systems sale to Ecolab. CVC’s reopening of Fund II amid increased investor demand may indicate changing tradewinds when it comes to the perceived risk around early-stage investment.

articles.title: Whoop launched a social network where every user has a ‘verified heartbeat’
articles.text:
Starting Thursday, Whoop members can share their data from its wearables on the app’s new Whoop Humans social network. Users can make their metrics, activities, and achievements visible to other Whoop wearers, post Story-like “Moments” with photos and captions, and add comments and reactions on other members’ posts.
Whoop launched a social network where every user has a ‘verified heartbeat’
Whoop’s new Humans platform is like Instagram Stories with updates from your friends’ fitness tracker data.
Whoop claims its platform is “entirely human,” unlike other social media platforms that are “saturated with artificial intelligence, automated accounts and bots, and manufactured content.”
Whoop CEO Will Ahmed says Humans is “the most verifiably human network ever launched. Every account represents a real person with a verified heartbeat.” Whoop says its existing Teams social feature “will remain available,” allowing people to share strain, recovery, and sleep data along with group leaderboards.
In the Community tab in Whoop’s app, users can scroll through Moments from people they’re following, like tapping through your Stories feed on Instagram but with your friends’ fitness tracker data. In one of Whoop’s examples, swiping up on a user’s Moments post with a photo from their run shows a map with their route and details like their pace and distance. The Community tab also shows cards for people in your “community” with their sleep, recovery, and strain scores.
Whoop says users choose which activities, achievements, and metrics they want to share on Humans, including Recovery, Strain, Sleep, HRV, and resting heart rate. Any activities marked as sensitive aren’t shared by default. There’s also an option to keep Moments posts private and a “Stealth Mode” for temporarily hiding health and performance data without changing your sharing settings.

articles.title: Hobbyist turns $45 USB-C hub into a working Nintendo Switch 2 dock by patching its firmware — console’s proprietary handshake needs about 540 bytes of code to answer
articles.text:
Hobbyist turns $45 USB-C hub into a working Nintendo Switch 2 dock by patching its firmware — console’s proprietary handshake needs about 540 bytes of code to answer
The hub now tells the console it’s Nintendo’s own dock.
A hobbyist going by mkopec turned an approximately $45 Cable Matters USB-C hub into a working Nintendo Switch 2 dock, using only about 540 bytes of code to mod the firmware. That mod lets the hub masquerade as an official dock, as mkopec detailed in a blog post. 
The edited firmware replies to Nintendo’s vendor messages and returns the same identity as the official dock, and makes TV mode work, which was not the case with the hub’s stock firmware. A separate fix with minor firmware rewriting also corrects washed-out HDR over HDMI, a nice bonus.
The modder, who writes that “Nintendo went in a proprietary direction (as they so often do),” decided to modify the hub’s firmware to make a working travel dock, as Nintendo’s official dock can be bulky. Unlocking the additional functionality did not come with a noticeable cost, as the hub “still works normally with my PC and my phone.” Grabbing an off-the-shelf USB-C hub and turning it into something more is quite the trick.
The stock hub has no problem charging the console, but it shows no picture, even though it negotiates both power and DisplayPort Alt Mode. Capturing the official Switch 2 dock’s traffic with a USB Power Delivery (USB-PD) sniffer, the modder found that it advertises two Standard or Vendor IDs: one for DisplayPort and one for Nintendo’s own mode.
The console enters Nintendo’s mode first, then DisplayPort, and, once DisplayPort is configured, it sends Nintendo’s vendor messages. This is the exchange of proprietary messages for negotiation, although the company told us last year that it “does not have any intention to hinder or invalidate legal third-party dock compatibility.”
The modification only required adding about 540 bytes to a firmware of just 32 KiB. The Cable Matters 7-in-1 triple display hub, like most, is simply an amalgamation of separate, specialized chips, in this case: a VL103 as the USB-PD controller, a VL817 USB hub chip for the USB ports, an RTD2142 DisplayPort Multi-Stream Transport chip for the DisplayPort-to-HDMI function, and XT25F16B flash memory chips. The VL chips are from VIA Labs, the RTD2142 is from Realtek, and the stock hub reports VIA’s vendor ID, which is an identity that needed to be changed for this mod.
The modder first used the WITRN K2 inline USB-PD sniffer on the official dock. Then, it was a matter of dumping the VL103’s firmware with the vli plugin of fwupd, the Linux firmware update tool, before flashing the VL103 with the changes over USB and through the VL817.
Changes were made incrementally, with seven versions in all, starting with answers to Nintendo’s discovery, mode entry, and echo commands, then an update to power delivery to offer 15 V at 2.8 A like the dock, changing the reported vendor ID to Nintendo’s, masquerading entirely as the official dock and getting TV mode working, and finally a full sequence match that removed a pause of about 3 seconds.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The process appears to contradict claims two accessory makers made to The Verge that the dock check uses encryption with a dedicated chip, as, in this case, copied identity data and fixed replies were sufficient.
Getting TV mode to work would have already been an accomplishment worth celebrating, but the modder took it further: the picture over HDMI was washed out with HDR turned on, and it was simply a matter of narrowing down the cause. The end theory was a mistake in how the hub’s AVI InfoFrame signaled BT.709, the standard dynamic range color space, instead of HDR’s wider BT.2020.
The theory was confirmed by a 108-byte patch to the RTD2142’s firmware, flashed with flashrom over I2C carried on the DisplayPort AUX channel through the same USB-C cable, which marks the signal as BT.2020 whenever HDR is in use. One third-party dock’s firmware contains a debug string, “switch2 color space patch,” which suggests this is a known issue. HDR through the hub’s own DisplayPort port is still washed out.
Separately, the hub’s firmware has no variable refresh rate (VRR) support, but because the patched hub identifies as the official dock, the console now offers VRR. However, turning VRR on froze the DisplayPort picture, and HDMI remained at 60 Hz. In a separate Linux test, with the hub patched to advertise Adaptive-Sync and an EDID override in place, the screen went black as soon as the frame rate varied, so the feature was left off.
The modder’s post shares no code, patch files, or repository, although the method is well-explained. The USB ports and Ethernet weren't tested rigorously, and the post does not say which Switch 2 system version was used. The modder also doesn’t understand many of Nintendo’s commands, so the hub’s version replies are copies of the official dock’s, and unrecognized commands still get the hub’s stock reply.
That’s important because Nintendo’s system update 21.0.0 left some third-party docks charging but with no video output. While vendors provided updated firmware as a fix, the modder’s ad hoc solution has no vendor behind it, so would-be modders could end up on their own.

articles.title: 'Every company we’re talking to is asking the same thing': Leaders agree AI is vital for their workplace — but only 10% say they're doing anything about it
articles.text:
'Every company we’re talking to is asking the same thing': Leaders agree AI is vital for their workplace — but only 10% say they're doing anything about it
AI can’t adopt itself
- Research finds that 80% of IT leaders recognize AI needs a digital workplace
- But only 10% have led an AI transformation in their organization
- Lenovo report highlights the existence of an “AI readiness divide” where ambition is not matched by preparation
AI offers the promise of greater productivity, but if your business isn’t prepared, that promise is wasted, new research has claimed.
A survey from Lenovo show that while 80% of IT leaders understand the potential for AI needs in the workplace, only 10% of them have put in place the digital transformation to facilitate success.
The sixth volume of the Lenovo Work Reborn report provides the results of a 1,200-person survey, conducted with IT leaders across the UK, US, Canada, Australia, and eight other countries, some worrying implications for AI readiness - but also asserts that a divide is becoming apparent, various levels of unpreparedness potentially limiting opportunities for businesses and organizations that have fallen behind.
Scaling slow
The report highlights various surprises. First, it seems that while AI is scaled across business functions, just 10% of organizations have approached its implementation with a rethink on how work is produced. Similarly, just 10% of businesses have governance that covers AI tools, agents, and data access.
Elsewhere, businesses seem to be unable to measure AI’s value, with many adopting a “fire and forget” approach to its implementation. Just 10% responded saying that an ROI measurement is in place to understand AI’s impact in delivering results.
The Lenovo report presents the findings with a score on its AI Workplace Readiness Index. This is a metric that measures five dimensions of AI workplace readiness: architecture, operations, trust, workforce, and value. Organizations that score well in all five are considered to be ahead when it comes to AI implementation.
Organizations with AI fully in use across their core business functions are given an average score of 4.1 our of 5. At the other end of the scale, organizations that are still evaluating AI score 2.7.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Creating value with AI
Talk is cheap, and declaring a desire to embrace and implement AI is very different from actually doing so. Establishing an AI-ready digital workplace means more than positive words – leaders need to put in the groundwork and have the budget in place to make it happen.
Rakshit Ghura, Vice President and General Manager at Lenovo Digital Workplace Solutions, says “Every company we’re talking to is asking the same thing: what value are we actually getting from AI? That’s where workflow-level measurement matters. Are cycle times down? Are repeat incidents falling? Is the outcome better?” That is, says Ghura, “how you show where AI is creating value.”
Updating the workplace is a no-brainer. As Ghura also notes, “a workplace designed for the pre-AI era” prevents AI from being used effectively. “The opportunity is to redesign how people and AI work together, with the technology, support and governance around them built for how work is changing."

- Le Tineco Floor One S7 Stretch Steam à 329,99 € au lieu de 549,99 €
- Le Tineco Floor One S9 Artist Steam Pro à 599,99 € au lieu de 849 €
- Le Dreame T16 Pro Heat-A à 479,99 € au lieu de 629 €
- Le Ecovacs Deebot T90 Max Pro Omni à 399 € au lieu de 599 €
- Le Dreame L50s Pro Ultra-A à 499 € au lieu de 749 €
- Le Ecovacs Deebot T90S Pro Omni Care Kit à 549 € au lieu de 799 €
Le Roborock F25 Steam fait passer la vapeur sous les 350 €
Dernier arrivé dans la gamme F25 de Roborock, le F25 Steam ajoute un mode vapeur à la recette des balais laveurs de la marque et avait obtenu la note de 8/10 lors de notre test. À 338 € au lieu de 599 €, soit 250 € de remise, il devient le balai vapeur le plus abordable de cette sélection, ce qui en fait le point d'entrée le plus logique pour qui veut essayer le nettoyage à la vapeur sans dépasser les 400 €.
- Une vapeur pour les taches séchées : annoncée à 180 °C, une température relevée en sortie de chaudière et non au contact du sol, elle ramollit les salissures incrustées avant le passage du rouleau.
- Une prise en main facilitée : l'aspiration de 25 000 Pa s'accompagne de roues motorisées et d'une tête capable de se coucher à 180° pour passer sous les meuble…
- À savoir : l'autonomie mesurée par la rédaction tombe à 21 minutes en mode vapeur, contre une cinquantaine de minutes en mode Auto, et la vapeur consomme beaucoup d'eau, ce qui oblige à remplir plus souvent le réservoir d'un litre.
Tineco Floor One S7 Stretch Steam : la vapeur qui file sous les meubles
Lancé à 699 € à l'automne 2025, le S7 Stretch Steam réunit la mise à plat du S7 Stretch et la vapeur du S7 Steam dans un même appareil, une combinaison qui lui avait valu un 8/10 dans nos colonnes. Avec 220 € de remise sur le prix de référence affiché par Amazon, il se négocie aujourd'hui à un peu plus de la moitié de son prix de lancement.
- Une vapeur stable : la technologie HyperSteam produit une vapeur à 160 °C, avec une température qui reste constante tout au long du nettoyage.
- Une mise à plat bien pensée : l'appareil se couche entièrement pour filer sous les lits et les canapés sans perdre ses 22 000 Pa d'aspiration, et sa brosse nettoie le long des bords.
- À savoir : en mode vapeur, l'autonomie retombe autour de 25 minutes en usage réel.
Tineco Floor One S9 Artist Steam Pro : le haut de gamme vapeur repasse sous les 600 €
Le S9 Artist Steam Pro occupe le sommet de la gamme vapeur de Tineco, avec un design plus travaillé que celui des S7 et plusieurs fonctions absentes du reste de la sélection. À 599,99 € au lieu de 849 €, il perd 249 € et repasse juste sous la barre des 600 €.
- Un mode ReverseScrub pour les taches collées : la brosse inverse son sens de rotation à la demande pour frotter une zone précise, en complément d'une vapeur HyperSteam annoncée à 160 °C.
- Une conduite assistée : la technologie SmoothDrive propulse l'appareil dans toutes les directions, ce qui allège nettement la manipulation malgré le gabarit, et le nettoyage des bords se fait lui aussi sur trois côtés.
- À savoir : les 90 minutes d'autonomie annoncées concernent le mode silencieux, alors qu'il faut plutôt compter une demi-heure en vapeur.
Dreame T16 Pro Heat-A : l'eau chaude à 90 °C dans un balai
Sorti cet été à 629 €, le T16 Pro Heat profite d'une remise de 149 € dans sa version Heat-A, qui ne se distingue du modèle standard que par son coloris gris foncé et sa distribution sur Amazon. Clubic l'a testé et noté 7/10, en saluant notamment son aspiration et son travail le long des plinthes.
- Un profil très bas : avec seulement 9,85 cm d'épaisseur une fois couché à plat, il se glisse sous les meubles bas.
- L'eau chaude plutôt que la vapeur : le lavage à l'eau chauffée jusqu'à 90 °C s'appuie sur une aspiration de 30 000 Pa et sur une brosse extensible qui va chercher la saleté jusqu'aux plinthes, avec un réservoir d'eau propre généreux de 900 ml.
- À savoir : la vapeur reste réservée au T16 Pro Steam, l'autonomie passe d'environ 70 minutes en mode Éco à 22 minutes avec l'eau chaude.
Ecovacs Deebot T90 Max Pro Omni : 40 000 Pa d'aspiration pour moins de 400 €
Présenté à l'IFA en septembre, le T90 Max Pro Omni reprend l'essentiel de la gamme T90 d'Ecovacs à un tarif plus contenu, et passe ici à 399 € au lieu de 599 €. Avec 200 € de remise, c'est le robot le moins cher de cette sélection.
- Une aspiration de haut de gamme : les 40 000 Pa annoncés grâce au système BLAST s'accompagnent d'une brosse ZeroTangle 4.0 conçue pour empêcher les cheveux et les poils de s'enrouler.
- Un rouleau lavé à l'eau chaude : le rouleau OZMO Roller 3.0 se nettoie en continu pendant le passage, puis la station OMNI le lave à 100 °C et vide le bac à poussière, tandis que le système TruEdge 3.0 le décale pour longer les plinthes.
- À savoir : la détection d'obstacles se passe de caméra, ce qui la rend moins fine que celle du T90S Pro Omni pour repérer câbles et chaussettes.
Dreame L50s Pro Ultra-A : le robot qui enjambe les seuils passe sous les 500 €
Successeur du L40s Pro Ultra, le L50s Pro Ultra a été lancé au printemps à 749 € et perd ici 250 €, ce qui le ramène sous la barre des 500 €. Contrairement aux deux Ecovacs de la sélection, il nettoie avec deux serpillières rotatives plutôt qu'avec un rouleau, et compense par une aspiration Vormax de 30 000 Pa et une double brosse HyperStream qui limite l'emmêlement des cheveux.
- Un double bras flexible : la brosse latérale et l'une des serpillières s'étendent pour aller chercher la poussière dans les angles et le long des plinthes.
- Une station qui gère presque tout : les serpillières y sont lavées à l'eau chauffée jusqu'à 100 °C puis séchées à l'air chaud, la poussière est aspirée automatiquement dans un sac prévu pour une centaine de jours et le réservoir du robot se remplit seul.
- À savoir : le robot donne le meilleur de lui-même sur les sols durs, et sur les tapis à poils longs il faut retirer les serpillières à la main.
Ecovacs Deebot T90S Pro Omni Care Kit : le plus autonome des trois robots
Lancé fin septembre à 799 €, le T90S Pro Omni est le modèle le plus complet de la famille T90, et cette version Care Kit ajoute un rouleau de rechange, une brosse latérale et un flacon de 260 ml de solution nettoyante. À 549 €, soit 250 € de remise, il conserve les 40 000 Pa du T90 Max Pro Omni en y ajoutant ce qui manque à ce dernier.
- Une navigation plus aboutie : la reconnaissance d'obstacles AIVI 3D 4.0 associe lumière structurée et caméra RGB, et la transmission à quatre roues TruePass l'aide à franchir des seuils de 2,5 cm sans s'immobiliser.
- Une station encore plus autonome : le rouleau et le bac d'eau sale sont lavés à 100 °C puis séchés à l'air chaud, la solution nettoyante est dosée automatiquement et la recharge PowerBoost récupère 10 % de batterie en trois minutes pendant le lavage du rouleau.
- À savoir : les 150 € d'écart avec le T90 Max Pro Omni ne se traduisent pas par une aspiration plus forte, et ne se justifient que si la caméra, le franchissement de seuils et le dosage automatique comptent dans le logement à équiper.

articles.title: Apify rotates API tokens, prompts 2FA resets after breach
articles.text:
Apify has rotated critical internal secrets and revoked some third-party OAuth connections after detecting unauthorized access to its internal systems.
The incident occurred between November 9 and 10 and was detected the next day at 12:13 UTC. The company reacted by cutting off the attacker's access and launching an investigation to determine the impact.
Apify's response involved invalidating internal credentials, rotating API tokens, and resetting all active sessions.
Apify is a Czech web scraping and browser automation platform for developers. Businesses use its services to collect data for websites, search results, and social media posts.
The platform grew significantly with the generative AI boom, and reports having 80,000 customers, including Microsoft, Samsung, T-Mobile, Accenture, Siemens, the European Commission, and Roche.
Rotating customer API tokens and passwords
“On 9 and 10 November 2026, an unauthorized third party gained access to parts of Apify’s internal systems,” Apify said in an update on the incident.
Apify said it also revoked OAuth connections to external integrations, including GitHub, out of an abundance of caution. Impacted users can expect to be informed via email when it’s safe to reconnect.
In one notification, Apify said it had found no indication that account data stored on its platform had been affected by the incident. A sample seen by BleepingComputer informs that impacted customers' Apify API tokens and Apify Proxy passwords have been rotated.
In another letter sent to affected customers, the company advises recipients to reset their two-factor authentication (2FA) through the Apify Console, warning that their 2FA codes may have been exposed while assuring them that their passwords remain safe.

articles.title: SSD usé par les pilotes Radeon : AMD publie enfin le correctif, voici comment l'appliquer — Frandroid
articles.text:
Un PC qui ne fait rien ne devrait pas user son SSD. Pendant des mois, de nombreuses machines équipées d’une carte Radeon ont pourtant écrit des gigaoctets inutiles sur leur disque système, à cause d’un service d’AMD qui tournait en boucle.
Le coupable, AMD External Events Utility, sert notamment à faire fonctionner FreeSync, la technologie qui cale le rafraîchissement de l’écran sur les images envoyées par la carte.
Comme on l’expliquait dans notre premier article sur ce bug des pilotes Radeon, AMD l’avait reconnu sans donner de date. Faute de mieux, des bidouilleurs avaient publié leurs propres scripts de contournement sur GitHub.
Le correctif est arrivé le 12 novembre avec Adrenalin 26.11.1, quelques jours après qu’un message d’alerte publié sur Reddit a remis le sujet sur le devant de la scène.
Ses notes de version citent deux problèmes réglés : des « écritures excessives sur le disque système » au repos, sur les Radeon RX 7000 et plus récentes, et des écritures du même genre au moindre déplacement d’une fenêtre.
Ce second symptôme rappelle le bug repéré l’an dernier avec le pilote chipset d’AMD. Les utilisateurs relevaient des débits de 0,3 à 5 Mo/s, ce qui paraît dérisoire jusqu’au calcul : à 1 Mo/s, un PC allumé en permanence écrit 86 Go par jour, et 432 Go à 5 Mo/s.
Un SSD de 1 To est garanti pour environ 600 To d’écritures, sa valeur TBW au-delà de laquelle le fabricant ne promet plus rien. Dans le pire des cas, le bug pouvait donc épuiser cette endurance en moins de quatre ans, contre une vingtaine d’années au rythme le plus bas.
    Pour aller plus loin
Votre carte graphique AMD Radeon use peut-être votre SSD sans que vous le sachiez
            
Un pilote optionnel et une liste de cartes restreinte
Premier détail qui compte, la version 26.11.1 est « optionnelle ». AMD la destine aux joueurs pressés d’avoir les derniers correctifs, et le logiciel Adrenalin ne la propose que si on a choisi de recevoir ces versions.
Le pilote recommandé, certifié WHQL (un label de stabilité délivré par Microsoft), reste le 26.10.1 d’octobre, qui ne corrige rien. La formulation d’AMD pose une autre question, puisque le correctif des écritures au repos ne cite que les RX 7000 et plus récentes. Le pilote prend pourtant en charge les RX 5000 et RX 6000, et les témoignages concernaient plusieurs générations de cartes graphiques Radeon. AMD ne dit pas si ces modèles sont épargnés ou simplement oubliés.
La liste des problèmes connus réserve aussi une petite ironie. Sous Windows 10, le nouveau pilote peut désactiver Smart Access Memory, la fonction qui laisse le processeur accéder d’un bloc à toute la mémoire de la carte graphique pour gagner un peu de performances en jeu. Or, couper cette option (appelée Resizable BAR dans le BIOS) figurait justement parmi les parades bricolées par les utilisateurs touchés.
    Pour aller plus loin
Quelles sont les meilleures cartes graphiques de 2026 ? Le comparatif et classement des RTX 50, RX 9000
            
Que faire selon sa configuration
Tout le monde n’a pas la même chose à faire. Pour vérifier l’état du disque, le logiciel gratuit CrystalDiskInfo affiche son pourcentage de santé et le volume total écrit depuis sa mise en service. Une baisse de quelques points n’a rien d’alarmant, mais une chute rapide justifie de regarder du côté des meilleurs SSD M.2 avant la panne.
- RX 7000 ou RX 9000 : on installe 26.11.1 depuis le site d’AMD, puis on vérifie dans le Moniteur de ressources (« resmon » dans la recherche Windows) que le processus atieclxx.exe a cessé d’écrire.
- Service coupé à la main : on le repasse en démarrage « Automatique » dans services.msc après la mise à jour, sinon FreeSync et les raccourcis d’Adrenalin restent inactifs.
- Fichiers remplacés ou script GitHub : ceux qui ont appliqué la parade des fichiers amdkmpfd ou un outil tiers lisent sa notice, car certains bloquent des fichiers que l’installateur d’AMD ne touche pas. En cas de doute, on réinstalle le pilote proprement avec l’outil AMD Cleanup Utility.
- RX 5000, RX 6000 ou Ryzen avec une carte Nvidia ou Intel : on surveille le même processus et on garde le service coupé si les écritures continuent. AMD ne dit pas si son pilote chipset est concerné.
    Pour aller plus loin
Meilleurs SSD M.2 NVMe en 2026 : notre sélection face à la hausse des prix

articles.title: Apache Patches Critical HTTP Server RCE Found by Anthropic, Google
articles.text:
Apache has patched a critical HTTP Server vulnerability that could allow unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE), following independent discoveries by Anthropic and Google researchers.
Tracked as CVE-2026-119618, the flaw affects Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70. The issue was addressed on November 11 with the release of version 2.4.71. It resides in mod_http2, the module responsible for handling HTTP/2 traffic.
The vulnerability involves a race condition in which multiple threads improperly access shared resources, potentially corrupting server memory.
According to Red Hat, an attacker could exploit the issue remotely without authentication to execute arbitrary commands and gain control of the server process. Red Hat assigned the vulnerability a CVSS score of 9.8 and explained that “only servers that have HTTP/2 enabled are affected; servers configured to serve only HTTP/1.1 are not vulnerable.”
Apache credited Anthropic’s OSS Scanner with reporting the flaw on October 26. Anthony Weems and Simon Scannell of Google Cloud Vulnerability Research independently reported the same vulnerability on November 3.
Cloud security firm Wiz reported that 64% of cloud environments in its data contained resources running affected Apache versions, while 51% had publicly exposed instances. The company cautioned that these figures do not account for server configuration, so they do not necessarily represent exploitable installations.
Red Hat says public research has demonstrated a reliable exploit against a server with mod_http2 enabled, but its advisory does not identify the research.
Wiz noted that when its blog was published on November 11, no exploit was available and there were no reports of exploitation in the wild.
A publicly available proof of concept (PoC) on GitHub reports reproducing memory corruption and Apache process crashes, but does not demonstrate remote code execution.
Organizations are advised to install Apache HTTP Server 2.4.71 or vendor-supplied packages. Disabling HTTP/2 can temporarily prevent exploitation if updates cannot be deployed immediately.
Defiant also warned that WordPress security updates cannot resolve the issue because it affects the underlying web server.
Apache HTTP Server 2.4.71 also fixes two other vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-106023, an important issue that can crash server processes, and CVE-2026-109163, a low-severity stack buffer overflow.

articles.title: Pese a las acusaciones de abuso de menores y la petición del Gobierno, TikTok no será prohibido en España
articles.text:
Así lo ha confirmado la propia Agencia Española de Protección de Datos, al que el Gobierno solicitó el bloqueo de la red social. Finalmente, el organismo público no bloqueará TikTok por los contenidos de pederastia y abuso de menores que ha expuesto la investigación de Maldita y, de momento, se limitará a que se eliminen los “contenidos concretos y determinados que supongan un tratamiento ilícito de datos de menores”.
No obstante, la polémica está lejos de terminar. Tras una investigación de Maldia, que expuso contenido de abuso de menores y pederastia en la red social, el Gobierno solicitó el bloqueo de la red social en España a la vez que la Fiscalía de Criminalidad Informática investiga “los posibles delitos relacionados con la elaboración y difusión de contenidos de abuso sexual infantil”.
Ahora la Agencia Española de Protección de Datos ha decidido que, de momento, no se bloqueará el acceo a TikTok en España, pese a que reconoce que "los delitos que atentan contra niñas y niños son especialmente graves y exigen una respuesta inmediata". Aunque no bloquerará la red social tras la petición del Ministerio de infancia, sí que ha uesto en marcha una serie de medidas, como ha confirmado la propia Agencia.
No habrá bloqueo de TikTok, de momento
De momento, el organismo público ha solicitado a Maldita.es la relación de los enlaces con el contenido de abuso para requerir a TikTok información concreta sobre sus actuaciones para la retirada de los contenidos denunciados y, posteriormente, ordenar el bloqueo que impida el acceso a los enlaces y contenidos concretos y determinados que supongan un tratamiento ilícito de datos de menores, pero de forma quirúrgica y no a la totalidad de la red social. Para la AEPD, se tratará de una medida concreta, proporcionada y adecuada, de acuerdo a la ley.
La investigación de Maldita ha sacado a la luz un submundo de contenidos de abuso de menores en TikTok, y aunque todavía sigue en marcha, puede ser el primer paso para una investigación más profunda. en el seno de la Unión Europea que puede traer enormes problemas a TikTok por la supuesta falta de moderación de contenidos, sobre todos los relacionados con menores.

articles.title: Microsoft veut vous laisser désactiver les réponses IA dans Bing
articles.text:
Microsoft est sur le point de donner une véritable leçon à Google. La firme de Redmond vient en effet d’annoncer dans un billet de blog qu’elle allait permettre aux utilisateurs de son moteur de recherche Bing de désactiver les réponses générées par l’intelligence artificielle.
Microsoft propose une extension pour donner le choix aux utilisateurs
Avec cette annonce, la firme de Redmond va à contre-courant de ce qui se fait actuellement, notamment du côté de Google qui a activé ses AI Overview dans les résultats de recherche, sans offrir d’option pour les désactiver.
« En matière d’IA, nous pensons que les utilisateurs de Bing devraient avoir le choix dans la manière dont ils effectuent leurs recherches. C’est pourquoi Bing propose des expériences de recherche à la fois basées sur l’IA et traditionnelles, y compris une extension de navigateur qui permet aux utilisateurs de désactiver facilement les fonctionnalités d’IA dans Bing » a ainsi expliqué Microsoft.
Microsoft, qui explique ainsi que ses recherches ont montré que les utilisateurs veulent avoir la possibilité de choisir si l’IA doit être impliquée dans chacune de leurs sessions de recherche, a ainsi développé une extension de navigateur permettant de désactiver à la volée les réponses générées par l’IA.
Proposée gratuitement sur Google Chrome et Microsoft Edge, l’extension Microsoft Bing AI Search Choice, c’est son nom, donne accès à un simple bouton qui permet de basculer d’une recherche avec des réponses IA à une recherche classique « à l’ancienne », dans son moteur de recherche Bing. Attention toutefois, l’installation de l’extension sur votre navigateur définit Bing en tant que moteur de recherche par défaut. Si l’initiative est à saluer, on peut se demander pourquoi la firme de Redmond n’a pas intégré directement l’option dans son navigateur Microsoft Edge.
Les utilisateurs pourront donc choisir d’activer les réponses IA s’ils cherchent à obtenir des résumés rapides, ou de les désactiver s’ils préfèrent privilégier des résultats de recherche classiques.
Des opérateurs de recherche pour s’affranchir de l’IA
Une bonne nouvelle n’arrivant jamais seule, Microsoft a par ailleurs indiqué que vous pouvez à présent utiliser un opérateur à ajouter dans vos requêtes pour esquiver les réponses générées par l’IA sans avoir à installer la moindre extension.
En rajoutant simplement « -ai » après une requête lancée dans Bing, le moteur de recherche n’affichera aucune réponse générée par l’intelligence artificielle. À noter que l’astuce n’est pas réservée qu’à Bing. Si vous utilisez le moteur de recherche de Google, l’ajout de la mention -ai après une requête vous permettra également de vous affranchir des résultats AI Overviews de la firme de Mountain View.
