articles.title: Karnataka open to subsidising GPU access for startups through AI hub
articles.text:
Karnataka may subsidise GPU access for startups through AI hub
The state could offer support beyond the Centre’s IndiaAI Mission. It is also considering shared manufacturing space for small companies near Bengaluru.
Karnataka is exploring whether it can subsidise access to graphics processing units (GPUs) for startups through its upcoming artificial intelligence hub at IIIT Bangalore. Karnataka IT and BT Secretary N. Manjula raised the possibility at a panel on how the state can support women in tech and entrepreneurship, after a founder building industrial smart cameras asked about cheaper computing power.
GPUs speed up AI model training and testing, and rental costs can limit how often early-stage startups experiment and refine their models.
When asked whether Karnataka could offer support on top of the Centre’s IndiaAI Mission, Manjula told YourStory after the panel, "We are open to looking at it.”
The central programme gives eligible startups access to subsidised cloud computing. Manjula gave no details on the budget, eligibility criteria, or the timeline for state support.
Rising hardware costs
IIIT Bangalore Director Debabrata Das said hardware costs, particularly for memory, had risen fourfold over the past year, with GPU prices seeing the next-biggest increase. He said the AI hub was looking at giving startups access to computing resources to test ideas and develop proofs of concept.
The Karnataka Cabinet approved the AI hub in September at an estimated cost of Rs 35 crore. The hub will offer AI training and startup support, and its planned AI Living Lab will provide computing infrastructure and a place to test applications. Das said more details were expected at the Bengaluru Tech Summit, which will be held from November 17 to 19.
Women-led startups account for 30–35% of ELEVATE winners
The panel provided women founders an opportunity to raise challenges they encounter at different stages of building and scaling their businesses.
Addressing the gathering, Manjula said, “Karnataka has consistently worked towards building a strong technology and startup ecosystem through policies and programmes that support the entire innovation journey, from skilling and research to incubation, funding and commercialisation. However, it is equally important for us to understand how these policies translate on the ground.
"This interaction is an opportunity to hear directly from women entrepreneurs, understand the challenges they face and identify areas where we can do better. The feedback shared today, particularly on access to funding, markets and infrastructure, will help us take these conversations forward and work towards more actionable solutions.”
Highlighting the state’s targeted interventions, she spoke about programmes such as Women@Work, WEscalate, BioWise and ELEVATE Shakti, which support women through skilling, incubation, mentoring, research exposure and financial assistance.
Under the latest edition of ELEVATE Shakti 2026, 63 women-led startups were selected, with grant support of Rs 23.19 crore committed. The broader ELEVATE Grant-in-Aid Programme has supported more than 400 women-led startups since 2017, with committed support of Rs 118.98 crore.
Women-led startups account for 30–35% of the winners of Karnataka’s ELEVATE programme each year, Manjula said. She added that the state had identified about 11 technology business incubators at academic institutions outside Bengaluru as part of its efforts to support founders beyond the city.
The cost of getting to proof of concept came up during the discussion. A biotech founder said she was using her savings to generate the early evidence she needed to qualify for a funding programme.
C-CAMP CEO Taslimarif Saiyed pointed to grants and incubators that can help founders at that stage and offered to discuss what support C-CAMP could provide.
Shared space for small manufacturers
Karnataka is also looking at a parcel of land roughly an hour from the Bengaluru airport where small companies could start manufacturing before they are able to afford premises of their own, Manjula said at the panel. She said discussions were at an early stage and raised the possibility of renting out space and setting up common facilities that companies in areas such as electronics and robotics could share.
Karnataka weighs how to deploy its Rs 300 Cr deeptech fund
A committee examining how Karnataka should deploy its Rs 300 crore deeptech fund of funds has drawn up recommendations and is expected to submit them to the government shortly, Manjula told YourStory. She gave no timeline for when investments could begin.
The Rs 300 crore figure matches the allocation for a fund of funds in Karnataka’s report on its LEAP initiative. Under this model, the state can channel public money through venture capital funds that invest in startups. That can help draw in private capital and leaves investment decisions to the fund managers.

articles.title: El país sin mar que más se acerca a tener una costa: hizo el negocio del siglo al ceder un tramo de carretera a Ucrania antes de que llegara Rusia
articles.text:
Cuando la Unión Soviética se desintegró en 1991, Moldavia se convirtió en un país independiente con un pequeño problema geográfico: tenía el mar Negro prácticamente a las puertas, pero carecía de litoral. Ocho años después, sus dirigentes encontraron una solución que pasaba por un insólito intercambio territorial con Ucrania. Moldavia cedió un trozo de carretera y recibió a cambio unos cientos de metros de ribera. Aquella operación terminaría convirtiéndose en uno de los negocios más importantes de su historia.
A las puertas del mar. Encajada entre Rumanía y Ucrania, Moldavia ocupa una superficie de 33.846 kilómetros cuadrados y carece de costa marítima. Su extremo meridional, sin embargo, alcanza uno de los grandes corredores comerciales de Europa: el Danubio, el segundo río más largo del continente, que desemboca en el mar Negro.
Durante sus primeros años de independencia, Moldavia dependía de sus vecinos para buena parte de sus importaciones y exportaciones. Para un país cuya economía estaba estrechamente vinculada a la agricultura y que necesitaba importar petróleo y gas, disponer de una vía comercial propia hacia aguas internacionales podía cambiarlo todo.
El negocio del siglo. En 1995, el Gobierno moldavo decidió construir una terminal petrolera en Giurgiulești, una localidad situada en la confluencia de los ríos Prut y Danubio. El proyecto inicial, desarrollado con inversores griegos, pronto atravesó dificultades financieras.
La gran oportunidad llegó en 1999, cuando Moldavia y Ucrania alcanzaron un acuerdo territorial largamente negociado. Moldavia cedió a su vecino un tramo de 7,77 kilómetros de la carretera que conecta Odesa con Reni y obtuvo aproximadamente 450 metros de ribera del Danubio. Aquella diminuta franja de terreno permitió ampliar el proyecto original y construir un puerto capaz de recibir buques marítimos.
Un puerto marítimo sin tener mar. El 26 de octubre de 2006 comenzó a funcionar la terminal petrolera del Puerto Internacional Libre de Giurgiulești. En marzo de 2009 abrió una terminal de pasajeros y cuatro meses después se inauguraron las instalaciones para el transporte de cereales.
En 2011 se añadió una terminal de mercancías. Situado a 133,8 kilómetros de navegación del mar Negro y con una profundidad máxima de siete metros, el puerto puede recibir tanto embarcaciones fluviales como marítimas. Moldavia había conseguido algo extraordinario: disponer de acceso comercial a aguas internacionales sin tener un solo kilómetro de costa marítima.
450 metros que valen millones. Con el paso de los años, Giurgiulești se convirtió en una de las infraestructuras más importantes de Moldavia. Su terminal petrolera tiene capacidad para almacenar 63.000 toneladas de combustible, dispone de dos terminales de cereales y cuenta con conexiones ferroviarias que facilitan el transporte internacional de mercancías. Las inversiones de las empresas instaladas en el puerto superaban los 100 millones de dólares en 2022.
Actualmente, según los datos recogidos por Interfax, concentra más del 70% de las importaciones y exportaciones moldavas transportadas por vía acuática. El pequeño terreno que Ucrania había cedido a Moldavia se había convertido en una puerta comercial al resto del mundo.
El favor que Ucrania recuperó 23 años después. Cuando Rusia invadió Ucrania en febrero de 2022 y bloqueó sus puertos del mar Negro, Giurgiulești adquirió una importancia que nadie podía imaginar en 1999. El puerto comenzó a facilitar la exportación de cereales ucranianos y la entrada de combustible en el país.
En mayo de 2022, el volumen mensual de productos petrolíferos gestionados por sus instalaciones había pasado de una media de 34.000 toneladas a 65.000, más de la mitad destinadas previsiblemente a Ucrania. Aquel año, Giurgiulești alcanzó un récord de 1,8 millones de toneladas de mercancías. El país que había ayudado a Moldavia a conseguir una salida comercial al mar encontraba ahora en ella una alternativa para sortear el bloqueo ruso.
El puerto que todos quieren. La importancia estratégica de Giurgiulești terminó despertando el interés de varios países. En 2024, Rumanía inició negociaciones para adquirir la empresa que gestiona el Puerto Internacional Libre, propiedad del Banco Europeo para la Reconstrucción y el Desarrollo desde 2021. Entre los interesados también figuraban los multimillonarios búlgaros Kiril y Georgi Domuschiev, propietarios de un importante conglomerado marítimo.
Bucarest considera que Giurgiulești puede desempeñar un papel fundamental en la reconstrucción de Ucrania y complementar las operaciones del puerto rumano de Constanza, con el que ya mantiene conexiones ferroviarias para el transporte de contenedores.
El negocio continúa. Las autoridades moldavas han autorizado la adquisición de Danube Logistics, la empresa operadora del puerto, por parte de la compañía estatal rumana que administra Constanza. La operación contempla inversiones superiores a los 24 millones de euros para construir una terminal de contenedores, modernizar el ferrocarril y ampliar las instalaciones de almacenamiento.
Lo importante es que Moldavia conserva la propiedad del terreno: lo que cambia de manos es la empresa que dispone de una concesión de 99 años para explotar el puerto. Así, más de un cuarto de siglo después, aquel intercambio territorial sigue demostrando su extraordinario valor. Moldavia no pudo cambiar su geografía del todo, por supuesto, pero consiguió que dejara de ser un obstáculo. Y para ello le bastó con cambiar unos kilómetros de asfalto por 450 metros de río.

articles.title: 650 km d’autonomie pour 50 000 € : Volvo s'attaque directement au roi Tesla Model Y avec ce futur SUV
articles.text:
Volvo poursuit le développement de sa gamme électrique pour obtenir le plus rapidement possible un portfolio aussi complet que pertinent. 2027 verra ainsi l’arrivée d’un modèle entièrement inédit qui viendra se glisser entre l’EX40 et l’EX60. Le futur EX50 ira tailler des croupières au Tesla Model Y avec son autonomie XXL et sa recharge ultra rapide. Son prix devrait démarrer aux alentours des 50 000 €. Une future menace en vue ?
Ce n’est en tout cas pas une menace surprise car l’EX50 devait initialement remplacer les vieillissants XC40 et EX40 en un seul et même modèle électrique. Mais ça, c’était à l’époque où Volvo voulait faire une croix sur le thermique. Les choses ont changé depuis, avec une demande toujours incertaine sur les modèles à batterie. Le récent revirement de l’Europe sur l’échéance de 2035 en est une preuve supplémentaire.
4,60 mètres et 50 000 € : le gabarit idéal pour faire plier le Model Y ?
Raison pour laquelle le duo XC40/EX40 survivra pour concurrencer les BMW iX1, Mercedes GLA et Audi Q4 e-tron, plus compacts. L’EX50, lui, jouera le rôle de modèle électrique mondial avec un gabarit idéal. Dans sa récente conférence sur les résultats financiers du troisième trimestre, le constructeur a confirmé à demi-mot l’arrivée de ce véhicule : 2027 verra « un nouveau modèle pour l’Europe et deux modèles spécifiques au marché chinois ».
Plus long que les 4,44 mètres de l’EX40, l’EX50 devrait mesurer 4,60 ou 4,70 mètres, ce qui lui permettra de mieux cibler les 4,79 mètres du Tesla Model Y. L’EX60 s’étendant sur 4,80 mètres est plus proche de l’américain, certes, mais il le surpasse complètement en termes de prix ! C’est bien là que l’EX50 aura sa carte à jouer. Il misera aussi sur une technique avancée, en reposant très probablement sur la plateforme SPA3 utilisée par l’EX60.
Recharge de 10 à 80 % en 16 minutes : la claque technique assénée à la concurrence
L’EX50 se permettra ainsi de reprendre les batteries de son grand frère. On aura alors le choix entre un pack de 80 ou 91 kWh offrant respectivement 600 et 650 km d’autonomie. L’accumulateur de 112 kWh donnant 810 km sur l’EX60 serait prometteur pour abattre la concurrence, mais il pourrait être trop encombrant pour les entrailles du futur EX50. Le rayon d’action maximal restera dans tous les cas supérieur à celui du Model Y.
Côté recharge rapide, le suédois ne chômera pas avec sa plateforme 800 V. La puissance de 400 kW en courant continu DC de l’EX60 sera ainsi de la partie pour un 10 à 80 % de batterie en environ 16 minutes. Le Model Y est là encore loin derrière. Il gardera en revanche la main côté prix. Sauf si Volvo fait un effort ? Probablement produit en Slovaquie, le suédois pourrait être éligible aux aides de l’État, si son tarif passe sous les 47 000 €. Un autre défi…

articles.title: ServiceNow launches AI-powered engine to accelerate migrations from CRM rivals - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
ServiceNow launches AI-powered engine to accelerate migrations from CRM rivals
ServiceNow Inc. is bidding to steal business from other customer relationship management vendors with an artificial intelligence-powered engine that it says can reduce enterprise CRM implementations from months to weeks.
The new Autonomous CRM Engine uses AI to analyze existing CRM environments, recommend business process improvements and automate deployment of redesigned workflows on ServiceNow’s platform.
The offering represents a competitive challenge to established CRM providers such as Salesforce Inc. and Microsoft Corp. by potentially lowering the switching costs that help vendors retain customers. The initial rollout targets only Salesforce installations, and others are planned.
The announcement comes amid growing concern about the costs and limitations of aging CRM systems. Gartner Inc. last year warned that legacy CRM platforms can create hidden maintenance expenses, integration dependencies and security risks that impede modernization. The researcher predicts that by 2028, most enterprises will identify outdated CRM systems as an obstacle to effectively using AI.
Gartner recommends that organizations evaluate technical debt, integration dependencies, data quality and the full cost of maintaining legacy CRM systems before deciding whether to modernize or replace them.
The discovery process is one of the most time-consuming aspects of CRM modernization, said Terence Chesire, group vice president of CRM and industry workflows at ServiceNow. Organizations typically must interview employees across departments and geographies to understand how sales and service processes operate.
“We’re able to collapse that into literally days where we show them how all their sales processes occur by product line,” he said.
Autonomous CRM Engine uses metadata application programming interfaces to examine business objects, configuration settings, custom scripts and workflows. It organizes that information into a graph database and applies AI to reconstruct how activities such as sales approvals, customer escalations and service requests actually function.
ServiceNow claims the analysis can expose discrepancies between documented procedures and everyday practices, including approval steps employees routinely bypass.
More than migration
Beyond transferring existing processes to a new platform, ServiceNow uses the discovery information to recommend redesigned workflows based on industry practices. Business leaders can examine proposed changes in a visual workspace and modify processes to accommodate unique business characteristics. Once approved, changes can be deployed directly into ServiceNow’s CRM environment.
Chesire acknowledged that automation doesn’t eliminate difficult organizational decisions or integration challenges. “The parts that potentially get extended are all those linkages to other systems because we always land inside a heterogeneous environment,” he said.
ServiceNow addresses those dependencies through its Workflow Data Fabric, which provides access to external information without the need to move or copy it. Its integration capabilities also extend to older applications through robotic process automation.
Gartner cautions that CRM modernization projects must account for hidden application dependencies, regulatory data-retention requirements and business processes that may rely on retired systems. It also recommends establishing clear data ownership and governance policies before making changes.
The research firm suggests measuring modernization success through operational improvements rather than retired applications. It suggests performance targets such as annual operating cost reductions of at least 20%, retention of 95% of historical data in searchable archives and a 35% reduction in duplicate or inconsistent records.
Customer results
Chesire acknowledged that ServiceNow hasn’t conducted comparative productivity studies against competing CRM platforms, although the company demonstrates its technology to prospects using their own business processes and data. The firm cited several customer examples to demonstrate the potential benefits of consolidating customer operations.
Germany soccer league Bundesliga-Gruppe GmbH consolidated fan services from seven digital channels onto ServiceNow in about a month and now resolves 89% of fan inquiries on first contact, according to ServiceNow. Bell Canada connected 26 applications and 8,800 data silos to one platform to support 12,000 field employees, while Everpure Inc. eliminated 13 legacy systems and now resolves 72% of customer issues before they’re reported.
Chesire said AI adoption is increasing pressure to modernize systems whose business logic is buried in custom code. ServiceNow plans to extend Autonomous CRM Engine’s capabilities to continuously monitor configurations and eventually improve CRM operations autonomously.
The engine is available now, with additional capabilities planned for 2027.
ServiceNow said its CRM and Industry Workflows business has surpassed $2 billion in annual contract value. Its CRM net new annual contract value tripled both sequentially and year-over-year in the third quarter.

articles.title: Qvyon Technologies emerges from stealth with $8 million USD to prepare physical AI for dangerous edge cases | BetaKit
articles.text:
The former CEO of automotive tech company LeddarTech has launched a physical AI startup to help autonomous vehicle and other robot makers deal with one of the big obstacles to real-world deployment: unpredictable, dangerous edge cases.
Montréal-based Qvyon Technologies, led by co-founder and CEO Frantz Saintellemy, publicly launched on Thursday with $8 million USD ($11.4 million CAD) in seed financing. The round, which closed in April, consists of $6 million USD in equity from Mac Venture Capital, BDC Capital’s Black Entrepreneurs Fund, BKR Capital, and Spotlight VP, as well as $2 million in venture debt from RBCx.
“We see an opportunity for us to scale very rapidly and to create a foundational company here in Canada.”
Frantz Saintellemy, Qvyon
Qvyon’s goal is to allow companies to test and validate AI-enabled robots and self-driving vehicles before putting them to work. As generative AI capabilities have ramped up interest in deploying smart robots in factories and on roads, the unpredictability of the physical world (and random human behaviours) has created challenges for companies hoping to earn public trust and drive adoption.
Saintellemy told BetaKit that when he was working on autonomous vehicle software at LeddarTech, the biggest challenges were finding enough real-world data to reliably test and validate the systems.
Founded in 2007 as a spin-off of Québec’s National Optics Institute, it developed environmental-sensing solutions for autonomous vehicles and driver-assistance systems. After going public on the Nasdaq in 2023, the company faced challenges repaying its debts, eventually cutting nearly all its staff and filing for bankruptcy last year. Some of Qvyon’s other founding members are from LeddarTech as well.
Now, Saintellemy and the team are taking the lessons learned beyond the automotive sector to help companies validate their robots across all kinds of hazardous situations.
“These situations were difficult to anticipate, expensive to capture, sometimes dangerous to reproduce, and sometimes statistically impossible to recreate in nature,” Saintellemy said in an interview. “But these are the types of scenarios any autonomous system must learn to handle.”
Simulation and synthetic data alone couldn’t solve the problem, he said, so Qvyon took a different approach. Its software product, MIMIC Core, blends real-world data—which a company can input from its own cameras or sensors—with an AI system that can then generate tons of variations from one recording, allowing a company’s engineers to learn where their systems are making mistakes.
Jason Baibokas, managing director at BDC Capital who leads the Black Entrepreneurship Fund, said in a statement to BetaKit that every industry putting AI into physical action will have to prove it’s safe before deployment. “Qvyon is building the answer,” he said.
RELATED: LeddarTech cuts 95 percent of staff in bid to rescue its business
“Edge cases” with unfortunate outcomes have hurt public perception for companies like self-driving giant Waymo, which has had cars accidentally drive over an exploding firework or be unable to navigate out of gridlock.
Some self-driving companies have developed validation tech in-house. Toronto-based Waabi has its Waabi World AI system to train and improve the performance of its autonomous vehicles on synthetic data, which it says is a cheaper, safer, and more scalable method than traditional road testing-first strategies.
Qvyon says its tech can be a complement to existing AI simulators, like a “reality infrastructure” layer on top that uses real-world data—which Saintellemy is hoping to sell to similar companies in the driving and industrial sectors. One of its first customers is the autonomous trucking company NuPort Robotics, based in Markham, Ont., which partnered with Canadian Tire and says it is testing trucks with customers in multiple provinces.
Beyond the self-driving sector, it has landed another customer in US manufacturer Voltava, which Qvyon says will use its tech to validate inspection systems in factories.
Qvyon’s roughly 20-person team plans to use the funding to deploy the MIMIC platform and land customers in the US, Europe, and Japan, with a roadmap to launching new products in 2027: a system to measure and document test results, and one to improve the AI system using information from machines already in use.
“We see an opportunity for us to scale very rapidly and to create a foundational company here in Canada,” Saintellemy said.
Feature image courtesy Qvyon Technologies.

articles.title: Trump floats Apple chairman Tim Cook as Jensen Huang's successor | TechCrunch
articles.text:
In the wake of the industry-shaking news of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation on Thursday, U.S. President Donald Trump is floating the idea that former Apple CEO Tim Cook should take over the position.
In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote that “only one man” could take Huang’s place: Tim Cook of Apple.
“A Legend replaces a Legend!” he wrote.
Cook stepped down as Apple’s CEO on September 1, 2026, after 15 years running the company, but he’s still very much involved with Apple. While John Ternus took over as Apple’s CEO, Cook transitioned into the role of executive chairman of Apple’s board of directors, which sees him continuing to engage with global policymakers and manage international relationships, including Apple’s relations with China.
Trump is not the only one to suggest Cook as a replacement for Huang. Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, Senior Associate Dean for Leadership Studies at Yale School of Management, who studies CEO leadership and corporate governance, penned an op-ed in Time on Wednesday, suggesting Cook should be among the potential candidates. He wrote that Cook has “an unparalleled track record of succeeding a bigger-than-life founder,” in reference to Cook taking over from Apple founder Steve Jobs.
Whether or not Trump agrees with this opinion, or is simply blasting off an idea that hopped into his mind, is anyone’s guess.
“Tim Nvidia,” however, doesn’t quite have the same ring as “Tim Apple” does.

articles.title: Apple HomeView looks like a smart hub, but fills a different niche
articles.text:
Apple’s HomeView is the company’s newest line of products that are sort of in competition with the likes of Google’s Nest Hub and Amazon’s Echo Hub.
However, the HomeView is quite different from those other devices—it fills a specific niche that just isn’t for me, at least not yet.
Location matters
I live with roommates, and so I decided to keep the HomeView in my bedroom. It’s also literally the only room in the house that didn’t already have smart speakers, and I didn’t want to go through the process of setting up my roommates on the smart hub. I’d have to invite them all to my “Home,” and it wasn’t worth it.
So, I kept the HomeView in my room and added my partner to my Apple Home account, so he could use it when he was over. I should mention, I didn’t need to actually add my roommates to the HomeView, they could use it in ‘Guest’ mode, but setting that up was too much hassle.
So the HomeView is in my room, on the night table beside my bed. The HomeView’s placement is quite important because, unlike a Nest Hub or an Echo Hub, your HomeView is meant to be touched. You swipe down from the top to invoke Siri or swipe up from the bottom to pull up your home page, which looks a lot like your iPhone with widgets and apps. I can access my calendar, messages, music, Apple TV, even some book apps. So it’s been good to have it beside my bed so I can check my messages or tomorrow’s weather while my phone’s on the wireless charger.
And profiles are important for the HomeView because it can dramatically change the experience. My partner and I needed to set up face and voice recognition and connect it with our Apple accounts, which allows it to show a personalized experience based on who’s interacting with the device.
Personalization includes showing my calendar, my text messages and my dashboard. If my partner looks at it, it’ll pull up his profile instead. And if he unlocks his profile and I try to look at his messages, it’ll stop it from happening and require his face or smartphone to allow it. Further, if a room is too dark, you’ll need to unlock the HomeView with your phone.
Siri AI
We’ve mostly used the HomeView to ask Siri queries, play music, and share what we’re watching. Awkwardly, the feature we use most, Siri, gets interrupted by the many devices in my room. I also have the Apple TV 4K, and my iPhone, so sometimes when I try to invoke the HomeView, my devices get confused. Eventually, I turned off the microphone on the HomeView because most of the time I was speaking to the Apple TV.
Still, as I mentioned, it’s pretty easy to activate Siri with the HomeView by swiping down on the screen. Probably what I use it for the most is to set alarms for the morning. I’m typically already in bed, so reaching over to activate the HomeView is pretty easy. Otherwise, I would use it for Siri AI’s broad world knowledge, but I ended up mostly using my Apple TV for this.
Besides using it for Siri, I really liked using the Handoff feature that lets you continue what you were doing on your phone on the HomeView with a simple touch. So if I’m watching a YouTube video or surfing the net on my iPhone, I’ll just tap the HomeView, and it’ll quickly transfer over.
When I’m using the iPhone 18 Pro, it’s nice to switch to the larger display; I’ll be watching a video and tap the HomeView and finish it there. Also, when I want to show my partner something, it’s easy to just tap the HomeView, and we’re both surfing Safari or showing each other what we’re listening to. It’s incredibly easy, and the animation is so smooth. The feature is enjoyable and something that the other ‘Hub’ devices can’t do.
Playing some tunes
The HomeView is great for music. The HomeView features two custom full-range drivers with a down-firing woofer, and two force-cancelling radiators are built into the base. The HomeView is loud, easily filling my bedroom, and when I tried it in the living room, it worked great — but my HomePod (2nd gen) provides a better listening experience.
The bass is great too, and the listening experience is incredibly rich and crisp. And Dolby Atmos offers a multidimensional music experience. My partner is a huge pop music girly with AirPods in his ears 24/7, but now he loves sharing what he’s listening to by tapping his phone to the HomeView. It shows animated album art too, and you can easily pop up the lyrics with a tap.
The HomeView is definitely more than what I use it for. I think the HomeView would work better for me in my kitchen, living on the counter, where I don’t also have an Apple TV and iMac. Plus, a HomeView in the kitchen would be great for cooking, which offers an ingredient experience with the list of items you need, measurements, and step-by-step instructions.
The HomeView would also be more useful if I had more home products, like smart lights or a smart thermostat. Unfortunately, my house isn’t smart enough for the HomeView.
Maybe a little too late?
It feels like Apple is playing catch-up this year; its first touchscreen laptop, first folding phone, and first hub-like device. And while the PROLED MacBook and the Duo both fit in well OK in this tech world, the HomeView feels a little late.
And despite the HomeView looking like the Nest Hub, it feels like it’s trying to carve its own niche, and is sort of like Google’s Pixel Tablet, though you can’t just grab it and walk away. I think that might have been a more useful device for me, like an iPad that could attach to a charging hub and speaker with MagSafe.
The HomeView isn’t bad, but I think I would prefer that alternative. But I’m looking to move on my own next year, and maybe I’ll have more of a smart home and a kitchen that I can put the HomeView in. But until then, I’ll be jamming out in my room, setting reminders, checking my messages and asking Siri questions with the HomeView.
The HomeView comes out on November 13 and costs $429. It’s available for pre-order now.

articles.title: Xbox owners are getting more customizations for backgrounds and the Guide menu
articles.text:
Microsoft is starting to test new customization options for Xbox consoles today. Xbox Insiders will be able to start testing new rotating backgrounds, new library options for digital games, and the ability to move the Xbox Guide menu to the right-hand side.
Xbox owners are getting more customizations for backgrounds and the Guide menu
Xbox Insiders get to test the new features today.
Xbox Insiders get to test the new features today.
“Xbox Insiders can now save favorite dynamic backgrounds and shuffle through them automatically,” says Eden Marie, principal software engineering lead at Xbox. “You can also choose Shuffle at the start of any background category. Have your background change each time you sign in, or set it to change hourly, daily, or weekly.”
Microsoft is also improving how you organize disc-to-digital games on an Xbox console. Xbox Insiders who have claimed a digital license from a disc-based game will be able to see these titles in a separate category in the library section. You’ll also be able to hide the digital license icon on game tiles.
Finally, Xbox Insiders will be able to choose whether the Guide menu appears on the left or right side of a screen. “Alpha Skip-Ahead members can try them first,” says Marie. “We’ll bring them to more Xbox Insiders and players over time.”

articles.title: Voyager 1 vai ficar tão longe da Terra que sinal levará um dia para chegar
articles.text:
A Voyager 1, da NASA, está prestes a alcançar uma distância histórica: em 18 de novembro, a sonda deverá se tornar o primeiro objeto construído por seres humanos a ultrapassar a marca de um dia-luz de distância da Terra. Isso significa que um sinal de rádio enviado do planeta levará aproximadamente 24 horas para chegar até a espaçonave.
O marco está previsto para as 7h16 (horário de Brasília), quando a Voyager 1 estará a cerca de 26 bilhões de quilômetros do Sol, ou aproximadamente 172 unidades astronômicas. A sonda viaja a cerca de 16,9 quilômetros por segundo em relação ao Sol.
A conquista ocorre enquanto equipes da NASA trabalham para manter a espaçonave em funcionamento. Recentemente, engenheiros conseguiram solucionar um problema por meio de uma intervenção chamada de “Big Bang”, que substituiu componentes por alternativas que consomem menos energia.
Como funciona o reparo “Big Bang” da Voyager 1?
- A solução envolveu a substituição de três unidades da espaçonave: dois aquecedores principais e um antigo gravador digital de fita de oito canais. Os equipamentos foram trocados por componentes secundários de menor consumo energético;
- A operação precisou ser feita de maneira coordenada porque os componentes também ajudam a aquecer a espaçonave, mantendo seus sistemas em funcionamento nas temperaturas extremamente baixas do espaço interestelar;
- A intervenção foi especialmente importante depois que a Voyager 1 perdeu contato com a Terra em 20 de outubro. A comunicação ficou interrompida por aproximadamente 48 horas, até ser restabelecida pela equipe responsável pela missão;
- O método já havia sido utilizado com sucesso para manter a Voyager 2 em funcionamento em agosto.
Leia mais:
- Conheça a única tecnologia (humana) a deixar o Sistema Solar
- O que existe no ponto mais distante da Terra já alcançado por uma nave?
- Falta uma semana! Espaçonave vai atingir 1 dia-luz de distância da Terra
Voyager 1 perde energia a cada ano
Lançada em 5 de setembro de 1977, a Voyager 1 depende de geradores termoelétricos de radioisótopos alimentados por plutônio-238 para produzir eletricidade. O material radioativo perde potência gradualmente, o que reduz a energia disponível para os instrumentos da sonda.
A perda é de aproximadamente quatro watts por ano. Atualmente, a espaçonave ainda utiliza pouco mais de 200 watts, quantidade comparável à necessária para alimentar um cobertor elétrico.
Para economizar energia, a NASA já precisou desligar equipamentos científicos. Em 2026, por exemplo, o experimento de partículas carregadas de baixa energia foi desativado.
Sem a intervenção recente, os responsáveis pela missão provavelmente precisariam desligar outro instrumento importante em 2027.
Atualmente, permanecem ativos o Subsistema de Ondas de Plasma e um magnetômetro, que permitem continuar coletando informações sobre o ambiente interestelar.
Voyager 1 explora o espaço interestelar há décadas
As duas sondas Voyager foram lançadas em 1977 para explorar os planetas gigantes do Sistema Solar. A Voyager 1 passou por Júpiter em 1979 e por Saturno em 1980, antes de seguir em direção ao espaço interestelar.
As espaçonaves foram as primeiras missões a coletar diretamente informações da região além da heliosfera, a estrutura formada pela influência do vento solar ao redor do Sistema Solar.
Com o avanço da missão, os sinais enviados pelas sondas ficam cada vez mais fracos, exigindo o trabalho da Rede de Espaço Profundo da NASA, que monitora e recebe as transmissões.
A Voyager 1 deve completar 50 anos no espaço em 2027. Mesmo com limitações de energia e dificuldades de comunicação, a equipe continua trabalhando para prolongar a vida útil da histórica missão.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Introduction To FP8 Formats: Part 1
articles.text:
The rationale behind 8-bit floating-point data formats, their ecosystem momentum, and hardware support.
The industry is moving from high-precision formats (FP32, FP16, BF16) to lower-precision data types for Machine Learning (ML) inference and training. In cloud and data center environments, lower-precision data types deliver higher throughput by packing more compute per cycle from the same platform. On edge and mobile devices, smaller formats reduce model size, memory footprint and bandwidth, which directly affects power consumption and latency.
Arm, Intel, and NVIDIA published an OCP 8-bit Floating Point Specification (OFP8). It is an interchange format that allows software systems to share the models easily. FP8 is not a future concept, it is being deployed today. It is already supported by NVIDIA’s Hopper H100 GPU, with software deployment appearing in major ML frameworks.
Arm added the FP8 support to the Arm v9 ISA and is exploring the best way to integrate the FP8 across all the ML platforms.
This blog post explains the FP8 data formats, the new Floating-point Mode Register (FPMR), and the instruction set that makes FP8 practical on Arm CPUs.
Unlike IEEE FP64, FP32, and FP16, FP8 is not a single format, it is a family. The whitepaper FP8 Formats for Deep Learning proposes an FP8 format consisting of two encodings: E4M3 and E5M2.
With only 8 bits available, FP8 makes a trade-off between precision and dynamic range. A single encoding cannot fit all tensors equally well. Activations and weights usually have a smaller and more stable value distribution after training or calibration. They can therefore benefit from more mantissa bits, which help represent nearby values more precisely. Gradients can change much more during forward and backward passes. They can therefore benefit from more exponent bits and a larger dynamic range, which helps avoid overflow or underflow.
The two encodings enable software to choose the right format for each tensor role. Use E4M3 when precision is more important and use E5M2 when dynamic range is more important. This is the key idea from FP8, and Arm reflects the same idea in the FPMR register. With FPMR, each source operand can independently select which FP8 format it uses.
|  | E4M3 | E5M2 | 
| Exponent bits | 4 | 5 | 
| Mantissa bits | 3 | 2 | 
| Bias | 7 | 15 | 
| Max normal value | 448 | 57344 | 
| Special values | NaN only | Inf and NaN | 
E4M3 uses 1 sign bit, 4 exponent bits, and 3 mantissa bits, with a bias of 7. E4M3 uses most bit patterns for normal finite numbers instead of saving many of them for special values. This helps E4M3 extend dynamic range, which is more useful for deep learning workloads.
E5M2 uses 1 sign bit, 5 exponent bits, and 2 mantissa bits, with a bias of 15. E5M2 follows IEEE 754 conventions for the exponent field and special values, including infinities and NaNs. Because of this, it can be viewed as IEEE FP16 with fewer mantissa bits, like how bfloat16 and TF32 can be viewed as IEEE FP32 with fewer bits. This makes conversion between E5M2 and IEEE FP16 straightforward, while still providing a wider dynamic range than E4M3
When hardware executes an FP8 instruction, it must know the format of each source operand, the format of the destination result, and the scale factors to apply.
Because FP8 modes can change per tensor, software may need to update the format and scaling settings frequently inside performance-critical code. For this reason, Arm introduced a dedicated control register – FPMR. FPMR is separate from FPCR. Hardware can recognize and rename FPMR writes more efficiently, making per-tensor FP8 mode changes closer to a normal register write rather than a pipeline-serializing control update.
FPMR contains the following fields:
| Field | Bits | Description | 
| F8S1 | [2:0] | Format of 1st FP8 source. 0b000 = E5M2, 0b001 = E4M3. | 
| F8S2 | [5:3] | Format of 2nd FP8 source. Same encoding as F8S1. | 
| F8D | [8:6] | Destination result Format for instructions that convert other floating-point formats to FP8. Same encoding as F8S1. | 
| OSM | [14] | Overflow Saturation for FP8 multiplication instructions. | 
| OSC | [15] | Overflow Saturation for FP8 convert instructions. | 
| LSCALE | [22:16] | Unsigned Log2 down-scaling factor. Result × 2^(−LSCALE). | 
| NSCALE | [31:24] | Unsigned Log2 up-scaling factor for widening FP8 sources. | 
| LSCALE2 | [37:32] | Second down-scaling value for dual-source convert instructions. | 
The 2023 and 2024 architecture extensions add FP8 instructions across Advanced SIMD, SVE and SME. The following table summarizes the architectural features and the instructions they provide.
| Architectural features | Supported category | Instructions | Description | 
| FEAT_FP8 | Advanced SIMD/SVE/SME | FCVTN, FCVT, F1CVT, F2CVT, BF1CVT, BF2CVT, FSCALE | FP8 convert instructions; a floating-point scale instruction. | 
| FEAT_FP8FMA | Advanced SIMD/SVE | FMLALB, FMLALT, FMLALLBB, FMLALLBT, FMLALLTB, FMLALLTT | FP8 widening multiply-accumulate. | 
| FEAT_FP8DOT4 | Advanced SIMD/SVE | FDOT (.S) | FP8 → FP32 4-way dot product. | 
| FEAT_FP8DOT2 | Advanced SIMD/SVE | FDOT (.H) | FP8 → FP16 2-way dot product. | 
| FEAT_SSVE_FP8FMA | SME | FMLALB, FMLALT, FMLALLBB, FMLALLTT | FP8 widening multiply-accumulate in Streaming SVE mode. | 
| FEAT_SSVE_FP8DOT4 | SME | FDOT (.S) | FP8 → FP32 4-way dot product and accumulate in Streaming SVE mode. | 
| FEAT_SSVE_FP8DOT2 | SME | FDOT (.H) | FP8 → FP16 2-way dot product and accumulate in Streaming SVE mode. | 
| FEAT_SME_F8F32 | SME | FMOPA, FDOT, FVDOTB, FVDOTT, FMLALL | FP8 outer product and accumulate into FP32 ZA tile; FP8 dot product and accumulate into FP32 ZA array; FP8 widening multiply-accumulate into FP32 ZA array; | 
| FEAT_SME_F8F16 | SME | FMOPA, FDOT, FVDOT, FMLAL | FP8 outer product and accumulate into FP16 ZA tile; FP8 dot product and accumulate into FP16 ZA array; FP8 widening multiply-accumulate into FP16 ZA array. | 
| FEAT_F8F32MM | Advanced SIMD/SVE | FMMLA | FP8 matrix multiply-accumulate to FP32 | 
| FEAT_F8F16MM | Advanced SIMD/SVE | FMMLA | FP8 matrix multiply-accumulate to FP16 | 
All FP8 compute instructions read the source format from FPMR (F8S1/F8S2) and apply scaling via LSCALE/NSCALE. These widening instructions always use FP8 data as the input format. Accumulation uses a wider type, such as FP16 or FP32. This keeps the bandwidth advantage of FP8 inputs while preserving numerical stability during accumulation.
For more detailed information about FP8, see the Arm Architecture Reference Manual for A-profile architecture and the FP8 Formats for Deep Learning paper.
Part 2 will explore FP8 instructions, from conversion and scaling to dot products, matrix multiplication, and outer products in Advanced SIMD, SVE, and SME.
Leave a Reply

articles.title: Anthropic offre un reset gratuit des limites de Claude à ses abonnés, voici comment en profiter
articles.text:
Anthropic veut se faire pardonner pour les récents « désagréments ». L’entreprise américaine offre ainsi une réinitialisation des limites d’utilisation à ses abonnés payants. Attention, cette opération n’est valable que pendant une durée limitée. Voici comment en profiter.
Un reset pour toutes les limites des abonnements payants
Via son compte X ClaudeDevs, Anthropic a annoncé une réinitialisation complète et gratuite des limites d’utilisation pour les abonnés Pro, Max, Ultra et Team. Ce reset couvre tous les modèles et toutes les limites. À noter que les utilisateurs du forfait gratuit ne peuvent pas bénéficier de cette offre. Pour les abonnés payants, ce reset est activable jusqu’au 10 décembre 2026 à 23 h (heure de Paris).
Anthropic explique avoir décidé d’offrir ce reset des comptes payants pour deux raisons. Premièrement, l’entreprise américaine confie avoir corrigé récemment quelques « petits problèmes qui consommaient plus de limites que prévu », sans préciser lesquels. Deuxièmement, Anthropic reconnaît en quelque sorte que le reset offert le 9 novembre, à l’occasion du lancement de Claude Fable 5.2, n’a pas réellement profité aux abonnés qui avaient déjà atteint leurs limites hebdomadaires. Pour rappel, cette première réinitialisation ne restaurait que le quota hebdomadaire consommé sur les modèles Fable, en plus de recharger le quota de la session de cinq heures. L’entreprise de Dario Amodei veut donc maintenant se faire pardonner, même si ces problèmes n’ont « pas affecté tout le monde ».
Comment activer ce reset de Claude ?
Pour activer la réinitialisation de votre compte Pro, Max, Ultra ou Team, il suffit de vous rendre dans les paramètres, puis de cliquer sur « Utilisation ». Autre possibilité : accéder directement à l’adresse suivante : http://clau.de/reset.
Les personnes concernées peuvent réinitialiser leur compte jusqu’au 10 décembre. Bien entendu, le mieux à faire est de réinitialiser son compte à un moment où les limites d’utilisation sont atteintes. Pour rappel, Claude dispose de deux types de limites d’utilisation : un premier quota renouvelé toutes les cinq heures et un second, hebdomadaire, qui se réinitialise chaque semaine à une date et une heure définies pour chaque compte.

articles.title: Intersport retire 500 € au Nakamura Crossover V LTD, son VTC électrique à cadre ouvert
articles.text:
À mi-chemin entre le vélo de ville et le VTT, les VTC électriques ont l’avantage de s’adapter à presque tous les terrains. Ils permettent de se déplacer au quotidien sur le bitume, tout en s’aventurant sur les chemins le week-end, sans trop sacrifier le confort. Le Nakamura Crossover V LTD coche justement ces cases, et profite en ce moment d’une remise de 500 € chez Intersport.
Ce modèle de la marque maison d’Intersport s’affichait à 1 899,99 €. Pendant le Black friday, il est aujourd’hui proposé à 1 399,99 €, soit une remise immédiate de 500 €.
C’est quoi, ce Nakamura Crossover V LTD ?
Un VTC, ou vélo tout chemin, se place entre le vélo de ville et le VTT. Le Crossover V LTD suit cette logique. Son cadre en aluminium est ouvert, avec un enjambement bas : on monte dessus sans passer la jambe par-dessus la selle, ce qui peut s’avérer pratique si on porte une grosse veste. À l’avant, une fourche suspendue offre 120 mm de débattement. Les pneus renforcés de 40 mm de large sont prévus pour le bitume comme pour les chemins de terre.
L’assistance vient d’un moteur central Naka E-Power Mid de 70 Nm, placé au niveau du pédalier. Cette position abaisse le centre de gravité et équilibre le vélo, contrairement aux moteurs logés dans le moyeu d’une roue. Un capteur mesure l’effort du cycliste pour doser l’aide, avec quatre niveaux d’assistance et un mode boost. La batterie de 460 Wh est intégrée au cadre. Intersport annonce jusqu’à 100 km d’autonomie dans des conditions optimales, et 3h30 pour une recharge.
L’équipement est complet pour un usage quotidien. Le vélo a une transmission Shimano Acera à 8 vitesses, des freins à disque hydrauliques Shimano MT200, un porte-bagages, des garde-boue, une béquille et un éclairage LED alimenté par la batterie. Un écran couleur TFT, connecté en Bluetooth, affiche les informations de trajet et le niveau d’assistance. LE VAE pèse en revanche 24,3 kg : il roule très bien, mais le monter au troisième étage sans ascenseur risque d’être sportif.
À ce prix, le Crossover V LTD est-il une bonne affaire ?
Les 500 € de remise représentent plus d’un quart du prix initial. À 1 399,99 €, le Nakamura Crossover V LTD devient particulièrement intéressant face aux autres VAE de cette gamme de prix. Là où beaucoup se contentent d’un moteur placé dans la roue arrière, il propose un moteur central de 70 Nm, des freins à disque hydrauliques et une fourche suspendue. Un équipement plutôt généreux pour un vélo capable de vous accompagner aussi bien dans vos trajets quotidiens que lors de sorties sur les chemins le week-end (c’est la période des champignons !).
Black Friday 2026 : tout ce qu’il faut savoir
Depuis une dizaine d’années, le Black Friday s’est infiltré dans le calendrier commercial des grandes marques et enseignes françaises. Avec l’expérience, on peut vous dire que cet événement fait partie des meilleurs moments pour faire de bonnes affaires.
Les dates du Black Friday
Bien qu’il porte encore le nom du vendredi noir, le Black Friday s’étend désormais sur un mois chez de nombreux revendeurs. Un format moins typique qui lui retire un peu son petit côté FOMO. On dirait presque les soldes, finalement. Mais c’est aussi moins le rush, ce qui est une bonne chose pour ceux qui veulent faire des achats plus raisonnés. Globalement, on peut résumer ce Black Friday en quatre temps forts :
- Début novembre : les avant-premières Black Friday.
- Autour du 20 novembre, selon les enseignes : la Black Week commence généralement plusieurs jours avant le jour J.
- 27 novembre : la date du Black Friday, même si les offres commencent généralement avant et se prolongent le week-end des 28 et 29 novembre.
- 30 novembre : le Cyber Monday.
Quels sites participent au Black Friday ?

Que faut-il acheter pendant le Black Friday ?
Globalement, tous les rayons profitent des remises, mais il ne faut pas pour autant se jeter sur les premiers prix bradés. N’oubliez pas que pour les enseignes, ce moment est aussi l’occasion de déstocker de vieux produits, dont les plus remisés frôlent parfois l’obsolescence.
Qu’il s’agisse d’un téléviseur, d’un smartphone, d’un casque sans fil ou d’un aspirateur balai, on ne peut que vous conseiller de suivre nos guides d’achat dédiés pour savoir quels modèles valent le coup en 2026.
Pour les produits phares comme les AirPods, la PS5, la Switch 2, un iPhone ou un Samsung Galaxy, sachez que nos tests sont là pour vous aider à savoir s’ils méritent votre argent.
Quoi qu’il en soit, chez Numerama, nous faisons déjà le tri à votre place en relayant uniquement des bons plans pertinents : des offres sur des produits à la fois intéressants et proposés parmi les meilleurs prix observés en ligne.

articles.title: Chez Logitech, la sortie de GTA VI mérite un jour de congé pour 7 000 salariés
articles.text:
Une journée manette en main, avec l’accord du patron : c’est le nouvel avantage proposé par Logitech. Chacun pourra choisir son jeu et utiliser cette journée jusqu’en novembre 2027.
À une semaine à peine de la sortie de GTA VI, certains joueurs regardent leur calendrier de congés avec insistance. Chez Logitech, une case supplémentaire vient de s’ouvrir. Le fabricant de périphériques a annoncé le 10 novembre son « Logi Game Day », une journée offerte à ses équipes pour jouer. L’entreprise présente cette initiative comme une première à l’échelle du groupe.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Chacun choisit son jour et son jeu
Le dispositif concernerait environ 7 000 employés dans le monde. Les stagiaires peuvent également en bénéficier, précise Tom’s Hardware. Chacun pourra choisir sa date au cours des douze prochains mois, sans obligation de forcément poser sa journée pour jouer à GTA VI. 
Logitech G organisera néanmoins un événement diffusé en direct ce jour-là, depuis son siège Amériques de San Jose. Robin Piispanen, directeur général de Logitech G et ancien joueur compétitif, animera les festivités. Dans le communiqué du fabricant, il cite GTA VI, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 et Forza parmi les jeux auxquels les équipes pourraient consacrer leur temps.
D’autres entreprises ont déjà adapté leur calendrier. Le préparateur automobile californien Burger Motorsports a ainsi annoncé une fermeture le 19 novembre, après plusieurs demandes de congés de ses employés, rapporte GTA BOOM. Une décision plus radicale que la journée laissée au choix des équipes de Logitech.
Logitech revendique les bénéfices du jeu vidéo
« Il est temps d’en finir avec le cliché selon lequel jouer est une perte de temps », estime Hanneke Faber, directrice générale de Logitech. Le fabricant défend l’idée que certaines compétences mobilisées en jeu peuvent aussi servir au travail.
Pour appuyer ce discours, le groupe cite son étude Ctrl Tomorrow, réalisée par Burson en mai et juin 2026 dans neuf pays, dont la France. Sa méthodologie distingue 8 168 adultes et un questionnaire séparé auprès de 1 350 décideurs IT. Selon le résumé qu’en donne Logitech, 81 % des joueurs interrogés associent le jeu à davantage de confiance, moins d’anxiété et de meilleures performances professionnelles au quotidien.
Une autre enquête publiée par Logitech, menée par Harris Poll auprès de 600 décideurs IT aux États-Unis, au Royaume-Uni et en Australie, avance que 98,8 % jugent leurs compétences de joueur liées à celles utilisées dans leur métier. Les répondants citent notamment la réflexion stratégique, la résolution de problèmes et la capacité à travailler sous pression.
Ce dernier panel est toutefois composé exclusivement de joueurs réguliers : tous déclarent jouer au moins cinq heures par semaine. Le résultat renseigne donc sur leur perception de leur propre pratique, sans permettre de comparer leurs performances à celles de non-joueurs.
Ces études commandées par le fabricant ne démontrent pas qu’offrir une journée pour jouer améliore la productivité. Pour les employés, l’avantage est en revanche immédiat : du temps supplémentaire pour leur loisir. Logitech n’a pas précisé si cette journée serait reconduite chaque année.

articles.title: Square takes Squaremates AI agent out of beta and opens up to sellers' own AI software - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Square takes Squaremates AI agent out of beta and opens up to sellers’ own AI software
Block Inc.-owned commerce platform Square today made its Squaremates artificial intelligence business agent generally available to sellers in the U.S., after the agent entered open beta in April under the name Managerbot.
For sellers who would rather stay in the AI software they already use, Square is also offering a new command-line tool and an updated Model Context Protocol server.
Running a business is “an endless string of judgment calls that are all on the owner,” said Willem Avé, global head of intelligence at Square. “We built Squaremates to help share that load,” he said.
Each seller’s agent now runs in its own secure workspace with access to cloud compute. Square said that gives it room for longer jobs. A seller could ask it to find customers who’ve lapsed over a given stretch of sales, for instance, and have it draft a discount to win them back.
A beta feature lets Squaremates build restocking orders directly on a supplier’s website, and the seller places them from there. Email access for its daily briefing is coming soon.
Fraser Thompson, who leads strategy and operations at Los Angeles-based Burgers Never Say Die LLC, put Squaremates to work on the restaurant’s house-made cheese sauce. “I dip my fries in it, I dunk my burger in it,” he said. “So I’m thinking, how are we not selling more of this stuff?”
Digging into attachment rates and customer segments showed that “our OGs, the regulars who’ve been with us since day one, love it.” The restaurant started promoting it on social media with what Thompson called “silly posts,” and he said that a few months later “we’d 12x’d our cheese sauce.”
“A lot of sellers already have an AI tool they like working in,” Avé said. The updated server, Square MCP, lets a third-party assistant answer questions about the business and make changes once the account is connected. Square CLI is aimed at sellers and developers who want to script or build on top of their accounts, and it gives their own tools and agents access to Square’s application programming interfaces.
Squaremates Apps are custom applications a seller writes with an AI coding tool and the CLI, which Square then hosts with a live connection to the seller’s business. Splitting cash tips by hours worked is one of the uses Square suggests.
Donnie McClanahan, who has four cafes around Knoxville, Tennessee, built a labor board app with the CLI and an AI coding agent. It pulls schedules and timecards from every location onto one screen. A lot of his mornings used to go to “playing catch-up just figuring out who’s where,” he said.
Sellers can try the tools at the Squaremates Tour, a run of in-person events Square kicked off recently. Apart from the features still in beta or coming soon, everything announced today is available to U.S. sellers at no additional cost. Squaremates itself is not yet available to sellers on Square’s Multi-Account Suite.

articles.title: Kia India to invest $2B in second plant in Andhra Pradesh
articles.text:
Kia India to invest $2B in second plant in Andhra Pradesh
Spread across a combined 465 acres for Kia and its suppliers, the new facility is expected to generate around 12,000 direct and indirect job opportunities.
Kia India has committed a combined investment of $2 billion, along with its supplier partners, to set up its second manufacturing facility in Andhra Pradesh.
The carmaker signed a memorandum of understanding with the state government to formalise the plan.
The factory will be located in Anantapur, the same district that houses Kia's current plant. It will add 2 lakh units of annual manufacturing capacity, taking Kia India’s combined capacity across both plants to over 6 lakh units a year.
Kia India is targeting early 2030 for production to begin, with the plant carrying out stamping, welding, painting and assembly. This plant will manufacture new models across ICE and EV powertrains, the company said in a statement.
Kia and its suppliers will together occupy 465 acres on the new site. The company expects the facility to support roughly 12,000 jobs, both direct and indirect.
In comparison, the first plant, across 945 acres, employs 24,237 people through direct and indirect roles. Set up with an initial investment of $2.9 billion, the facility builds the Seltos, Syros, Sonet, Carens, Carens Clavis, Carnival and Sorento models, spanning ICE, EV, CNG and hybrid versions.
Gwanggu Lee, Managing Director and CEO, Kia India, said, “India is central to Kia’s long-term growth ambitions, and the trust our customers have placed in us since we began operations in Anantapur has been instrumental in our journey."
He continued, "Our second manufacturing plant marks a significant new chapter, strengthening our ability to respond to customer demand with greater speed and flexibility, while supporting the introduction of new models across ICE and EV powertrains.
"As we enter our next phase of growth, we remain committed to contributing to India’s automotive ecosystem and building on the strong foundation we have created here. This will further expand our Made-in-India footprint, strengthening our ability to serve both domestic and overseas markets.”
Kia said the project would also help build India's manufacturing base, generate employment, and support the wider auto industry.

articles.title: Microsoft confirms Windows security updates installation issues
articles.text:
Microsoft has confirmed reports that the November 2026 security updates are failing to install on Windows 11 systems with the October preview update.
This follows widespread reports that the KB5132061 update fails to install, with affected users seeing the installation process lock midway and then trigger 0x800f0989 or 0x800f0993 errors.
"When attempting to install the November 2026 Windows security update (the Originating KBs listed above), some devices might be unable to complete the installation. Affected devices might repeatedly attempt to install the update or display error code 0x80070306, 0x800f0989, or 0x800f0993," Microsoft said in a service update seen by BleepingComputer.
"This issue affects a limited number of devices that installed the October 2026 non-security preview update (KB5127936). Devices that did not install the October 2026 non-security preview update are not affected."
Microsoft also told IT administrators that the installation issues will resolve automatically for all affected customers by Friday morning and that end users do not need to take any action to receive the fix.
"All affected devices should be repaired in 24 to 48 hours starting from November 11, 2026, 10am PT. Once your device receives the repair, it will automatically download and install the November 2026 security update via Windows Update," it added.
The company also urged admins still receiving reports of installation issues after 48 hours to contact Microsoft Support.
This is not the first time Microsoft has had to address Windows update installation issues since the start of the year. In March, it had to pull a buggy Windows 11 non-security preview update (KB5079391) because of 0x80073712 errors during installation.
In May, it also fixed installation failures and 0x800f0922 errors when deploying the May 2026 Windows 11 security update (KB5089549).
More recently, in June, Microsoft warned users that they may encounter issues installing the latest monthly updates and see 0x80073712 or 0x800f0993 errors on some Windows devices upgraded to Windows 11 24H2 or 25H2.

articles.title: Jensen Huang ha salvado a NVIDIA seis veces. La séptima crisis es él mismo y le ha costado el puesto
articles.text:
Jensen Huang ha dimitido como CEO de NVIDIA tras dos semanas en las que el consejo ha pasado de expresar su confianza en él a preparar su destitución. Según Bloomberg, ya trabajaba con una firma externa para buscar candidatos y barajaba nombrar a un CEO interino. NVIDIA todavía no ha dicho quién le sustituye.
Huang ha dirigido NVIDIA durante más de tres décadas y la ha sacado del borde de la quiebra en al menos seis ocasiones. Esta vez el problema no era externo, sino él mismo, y la empresa no tiene a nadie preparado para relevarlo.
Qué ha ocurrido. El caso ha escalado en cinco pasos:
- 29 de octubre. NVIDIA califica de “nada inusual” la relación de Huang con Alice Huang, ejecutiva de Megaspeed. La inteligencia estadounidense la había señalado como sospechosa de desviar chips e información sobre NVIDIA a China.
- 8 de noviembre. Huang admite una infidelidad con la mencionada en un correo enviado a su plantilla. El consejo abre una investigación independiente y lo respalda.
- 10 de noviembre. NVIDIA contrata al bufete Wachtell Lipton para la investigación independiente. La acción encadena dos caídas que suman un 10%.
- 11 de noviembre. The New York Times publica que Huang también tuvo una relación con Kimberly Powell, vicepresidenta de Healthcare y subordinada directa suya. La acción cae más de un 7% tras el cierre del mercado.
- 12 de noviembre. Huang dimite como CEO.
Lo que más pesa contra él son los desmentidos iniciales, más que la infidelidad en sí. Gary Gensler, expresidente de la SEC, ha dicho a Semafor que Huang “parece haber engañado al público”. Ya hay demandas de accionistas en marcha.
El contexto. Durante años, Huang abría sus presentaciones internas con la misma frase: “Nuestra empresa está a 30 días de quebrar”. No exageraba. La acción se ha desplomado un 90% dos veces antes de llegar a empresa más valiosa del mundo.
- 1996. El NV1 apostó por cuadriláteros cuando DirectX impuso los triángulos, y Sega canceló el chip. Huang viajó a Japón a reconocer el error. Sega convirtió la deuda en 5 millones de dólares de capital, y Huang despidió a 60 de sus 100 empleados.
- 2002. El pinchazo de la burbuja puntocom, la pelea con Microsoft por la Xbox, las cuentas reexpresadas a petición de la SEC y un GeForce FX que llegó tarde y peor que la competencia.
- 2008. Cargo de unos 200 millones de dólares por chips de portátil defectuosos. La acción cayó un 76% durante el año en el contexto de la crisis de entonces.
- 2018. Resaca cripto tras la caída de Bitcoin y compañía. NVIDIA se quedó con los almacenes llenos de GPUs sin demanda y un 54% de caída de un trimestre para otro.
- 2022. Ethereum deja de minar con GPUs y Estados Unidos veta el A100 y el H100 en China.
- 2025. La licencia obligatoria para el H20 le cuesta un cargo de 4.500 millones de dólares y deja su cuota en China a cero.
Entre bambalinas. En cada crisis, Huang ha seguido el mismo guión:
- Reconocer el error pronto.
- Recortar donde duele.
- Y no tocar la apuesta a largo plazo.
En 2008 despidió al 6,5% de la plantilla y en el mismo comunicado prometió seguir invirtiendo en CUDA. Fue algo que en su momento sonó contradictorio, casi suicida, porque ese software encarecía cada GPU sin que aparentemente nadie lo pidiera. Así que Huang estaba empeorando su eficiencia en época de vacas flacas. Hoy la IA moderna funciona sobre él y de hecho CUDA es el mejor foso que tiene NVIDIA.
Casi todo lo que es hoy NVIDIA fue decidido durante un mal momento para la empresa.
- En 2012 se lanzó a por las redes neuronales, que entonces eran cosa de laboratorios universitarios, con una dudosa rentabilidad.
- En 2019 pagó 6.900 millones de dólares por Mellanox porque intuyó que el cuello de botella acabaría estando en la red. Acertó de lleno.
Cuando Sequoia entró en 1993, la empresa valía 7 millones. Hoy vale más de 4 billones y llegaron a ser 5,7.
El rastro del dinero. Su salida llega tras la presión de un consejo al que él mismo ha hecho extremadamente rico. Según Bloomberg, Mark Stevens y Tench Coxe, dos de los consejeros, sumaban casi 15.000 millones de dólares en enero de 2025, con la acción bastante más baja que hoy. Otros dos, Harvey Jones y Brooke Seawell, tenían unos 1.000 y 750 millones. Los cuatro están en el consejo desde los años noventa. Ese consejo parecía que iba a ser indulgente con su affaire, pero el segundo caso, con una subordinada, es mucho más difícil de dejar pasar. Hay precedentes en grandes empresas estadounidenses que acabaron con el CEO fuera, como el de McDonald's en 2019 o el de Intel en 2018.
Hasta ahora, la gran lealtad del consejo tenía lógica porque cada vez que apostó por Huang contra el mercado, ganó.
El contraste. Apple, Microsoft, Google y Amazon han relevado a su fundador sin hundirse, pero llevaban años preparándolo. Tim Cook ya era director de operaciones antes de pasar a CEO en 2011. Y Andy Jassy es quien levantó el negociazo que es AWS para Amazon. El único relevo a la fuerza, el de Jobs en 1985, casi hace quebrar a la empresa.
NVIDIA no tiene a su Tim Cook. Huang ha montado una estructura sin número dos. No es habitual que sesenta personas reporten a un CEO cada día. Con él se va quien decidía dónde estaría el cuello de botella dentro de cinco años. Y se va en mal momento, porque la ley de Moore ya no da chips mejores cada año, y China avanza hacia sus propios semiconductores.
Sí, pero. El estilo que ha salvado a NVIDIA, con control total, un consejo leal y cero contrapesos, es también el que ha dejado que un asunto personal acabe salpicando a la empresa.
Aún falta tela por cortar. La investigación interna sigue abierta. Lo de que Alice Huang es una espía viene de la inteligencia estadounidense y no se ha probado en público. Trump había dicho que Huang debería seguir, y Huang conserva cerca del 3,4% de la empresa gracias a sus 811 millones de acciones.
Y ahora qué. Quedan dos incógnitas inmediatas:
- Quién se queda al mando.
- Y si Huang sigue en el consejo.
El 17 de noviembre NVIDIA presenta resultados, los primeros en 33 años sin él como CEO. Y el 18 estaba prevista su reunión a puerta cerrada con tres presidentes de comités de la Cámara de Representantes.
En mayo, contó en How I Built This que, sabiendo lo que le esperaba, no volvería a fundar NVIDIA. Pensaba en treinta años de sobresaltos. No contaba con la madre de todos los sustos.

articles.title: Alfonso Muñoz: “Este requisito está dando lugar a la denegación de muchas jubilaciones anticipadas”
articles.text:
El funcionario de la Seguridad Social Alfonso Muñoz señala que hay un requisito económico que está provocando “la denegación de muchas jubilaciones anticipadas voluntarias”. Se trata del hecho de que la pensión calculada tenga que ser superior a la mínima a la que tendría derecho el solicitante a los 65 años de edad (teniendo en cuenta su situación familiar).
En esta modalidad se puede adelantar el retiro máximo hasta dos años antes de la edad ordinaria correspondiente. Además, hacen falta al menos 35 años de cotización efectiva. De estos, al menos dos tienen que estar dentro de los 15 anteriores a la jubilación o, en los casos previstos por la norma, al cese de la obligación de cotizar. Sin embargo, esto no es suficiente. Por otro lado, el artículo 208 de la Ley General de la Seguridad Social indica que no se podrá acoger a esta modalidad si la pensión resultante no supera el umbral.
Ejemplo de cuantía para 2026
Por ejemplo, un trabajador de 63 años tiene 40 cotizados y tiene una pensión calculada de 1.058 € mensuales. Vive con su mujer, que no trabaja y no tiene pensión.
En el caso de nuestro ejemplo, veríamos que para un titular de 65 años la mínima es de 1.256,60 euros/mes (con cónyuge a cargo). Si no tuviera cónyuge, la mínima sería de 936,20 euros/mes. Por otro lado, si se diera la situación de que tuviera cónyuge no a cargo, esta mínima bajaría a 888,70 euros/mes. Las cantidades son en catorce pagas.
Para que tenga cónyuge a cargo, deben vivir juntos y haber dependencia económica. En 2026, la dependencia económica se consigue si el cónyuge no es titular de ninguna pensión pública (en los términos de la norma) y además tienen unos rendimientos computables (sin contar la pensión que queremos complementar) de menos de 11.013 euros/año entre los dos.
En nuestra situación, la mujer estaría a cargo si se cumple ese límite de rendimientos. Como nuestra pensión calculada es menor que la mínima, no podríamos optar a la jubilación anticipada voluntaria. Por otro lado, si nuestros rendimientos computables fueran superiores al límite, pasaríamos a estar en la categoría de cónyuge no a cargo.
