articles.title: Elon Musk afirma que sería “un honor” contratar a Jensen Huang ante su posible destitución de Nvidia
articles.text:
Elon Musk calificó como “un honor” la posibilidad de contratar al ex director ejecutivo de Nvidia, Jensen Huang, en medio de una creciente crisis que rodea al fundador del fabricante de chips de inteligencia artificial más valioso del mundo. La declaración del magnate se produjo el miércoles por la noche, hora de Estados Unidos, horas después de que el Wall Street Journal informara que la junta directiva de Nvidia prepara una reunión para analizar el futuro de Huang al frente de la compañía.
Jensen Huang renunció la mañana de este jueves a la dirección ejecutiva de Nvidia y Colette Kress asumió de forma interina, según informó la compañía. El relevo se produjo tras una reunión del directorio que había quedado bajo la atención de los mercados, con las acciones de la fabricante de procesadores para inteligencia artificial bajo presión en las operaciones previas a la apertura.
El episodio se suma a una tormenta que comenzó días atrás, cuando The New York Times reveló que Huang había mantenido una relación extramarital con Alice Huang, una ejecutiva de negocios a quien la inteligencia estadounidense identificó como presunta agente reclutada por el Ministerio de Seguridad del Estado de China.
Las acciones de Nvidia cayeron más del 8% en las operaciones posteriores al cierre de los mercados tras conocerse los reportes sobre la posible reunión de la junta.
Elon Musk dijo que sería un honor contratar a Jensen Huang de Nvidia
La declaración de Musk llegó en respuesta a una publicación del blog financiero Zerohedge en X, que le pedía directamente: “Elon, por favor contrata a Jensen”. El fundador de Tesla y SpaceX respondió con una sola frase: “Eso sería un honor”. Con esas cuatro palabras, Musk encendió la especulación sobre el futuro profesional del hombre que transformó a Nvidia en la columna vertebral de la carrera global por la inteligencia artificial.
Huang, de 63 años, construyó a Nvidia como la empresa proveedora de los chips de IA más codiciados del mundo y mantuvo una relación estrecha con el presidente Donald Trump, a quien acompañó en el Air Force One durante una visita de Estado a Beijing a principios de 2026.
Trump le entregó la Medalla Nacional de Ciencia apenas el mes pasado y lo definió como “un hombre cuya determinación sentó las bases para la explosión de la superinteligencia”, según declaraciones recogidas por la agencia AP.
La junta directiva de Nvidia analiza el futuro de Jensen Huang
Según el Wall Street Journal, la junta directiva de Nvidia prepara una reunión para discutir la continuidad de Huang. La empresa había señalado previamente que “no tiene motivos para creer” que se hayan comprometido la seguridad nacional o los secretos corporativos, y que Huang seguiría al mando mientras coopera con la investigación interna que el directorio puso en marcha el 8 de noviembre.
Para conducir esa investigación, la junta contrató a Joon Kim, socio del estudio Wachtell Lipton y exfiscal federal interino del Distrito Sur de Nueva York, con experiencia en investigaciones internas y defensa en casos de delitos de cuello blanco, según informó Reuters.
El escándalo también derivó en una demanda colectiva presentada el 9 de noviembre que acusa a Nvidia y a Huang de haber defraudado a los accionistas al ocultar los vínculos del ejecutivo con una presunta espía china.
Los legisladores estadounidenses piden la renuncia de Jensen Huang
Desde el Capitolio, varios legisladores de ambos partidos tomaron posición. El senador republicano Kevin Cramer (Dakota del Norte), miembro del Comité Bancario del Senado, reiteró el miércoles su pedido de renuncia a Huang. “Por una cuestión de conciencia propia, debería renunciar”, declaró Cramer a CNBC. Se sumaron al reclamo el representante demócrata Suhas Subramanyam (Virginia), miembro del Comité de Supervisión de la Cámara, y el representante republicano Don Bacon (Nebraska), próximo a retirarse del Congreso.
La senadora demócrata de Massachusetts Elizabeth Warren apuntó además a las implicaciones comerciales del escándalo. Según un comunicado emitido el lunes, Nvidia había obtenido aprobaciones para exportar “cientos de miles de chips avanzados de IA a China, incluso a empresas vinculadas al ejército chino”.
Warren señaló que la relación de Huang con Alice Huang “plantea preguntas importantes que Nvidia debe responder sobre hasta qué punto estas actividades estuvieron relacionadas”.
El escándalo de Alice Huang y el impacto en la estrategia de chips de Estados Unidos
Alice Huang, también conocida por su nombre chino Huang Le, fue identificada por funcionarios de inteligencia estadounidenses como una fuente de información para China, según The New York Times. La mujer es exejecutiva de Megaspeed International, una empresa de computación en la nube con sede en Singapur que el Departamento de Comercio de Estados Unidos investigó por presuntamente eludir las leyes de exportación y desviar chips avanzados de Nvidia hacia usuarios chinos. Megaspeed negó esas acusaciones.
Según un informe de The Information citado por Reuters, la relación de Huang con Alice Huang facilitó el envío de al menos USD 7.500 millones en chips de la compañía a empresas chinas. La División de Seguridad Nacional del Departamento de Justicia investiga si Megaspeed violó las leyes de control de exportaciones, una indagación que también incluye el escrutinio de Alice Huang, según una persona familiarizada con el caso que habló bajo condición de anonimato.
Jensen Huang intentó proyectar normalidad tras las revelaciones
El 8 de noviembre, Huang reconoció ante los empleados de Nvidia que había sido infiel a su esposa, aunque no abordó los reportes que lo vinculan a una operación de espionaje extranjero. Al día siguiente, buscó transmitir una imagen de continuidad en su primera jornada de regreso a la oficina tras las revelaciones, aunque los pedidos de renuncia no tardaron en llegar.
Trump, por su parte, declaró esta semana que habló con Huang a medida que el escándalo crecía. “Creo que saldrá bien de esto”, afirmó el presidente, y agregó que el ejecutivo le dijo que “no tenía absolutamente ni idea de que la persona en cuestión fuera una espía”, según AP. Beijing, en tanto, calificó las acusaciones de espionaje chino como “nada más que difamaciones”.
La junta directiva de Nvidia aún no informó sobre las conclusiones de su investigación interna, mientras el Departamento de Justicia avanza con su propia indagación y varios legisladores aguardan una comparecencia de Huang ante el Congreso programada para el 18 de noviembre.

articles.title: Apple HomeView review - stylish new way to stay connected, entertained, informed and in control - Tech Guide
articles.text:
- RATING
The new Home View offers a stylish new way to enjoy the content and connections of your Apple ecosystem but the personal context provided by Siri AI and Apple Intelligence is what sets the product apart from other smart speakers makes it a genuine assistant.
The Apple ecosystem just got bigger with the introduction of the new HomeView smart display to stay connected, entertained, in control and informed in your space.
The unit is also your link to Siri AI and Apple Intelligence so it can understand your personal context, take action across your apps and get more done.
Naturally you’ll need an iPhone or an iPad on the same network as HomeView so it has the same access to your apps, emails, messages and all your other personal information.
Don’t worry, it’s as private and secure as your iPhone and has the same protections to keep everyone’s personal content separate and secure.
HomeView was a lot smaller than we thought – it seemed larger when we saw pictures of it but seeing it in the flesh it is a bit more petite.
HomeView can recognise up to six people in the household by face ID or by their voice with each user able to personalise their home screen apps and widgets.
Apple is entering a space already crowded by other popular devices like Amazon’s Echo range with Alexa+ onboard.
But unlike those Echo speakers, the HomeView has access and personal insights into your apps and personal details including your messages and email.
For example, I asked HomeView to find an email that I received about reviewing an electric bike.
Within a few seconds that email was brought to the screen and read out to me so I could easily see the person who sent it and the date it was sent.
There’s no way in the world an Echo smart speaker is going to be able to do that.
But it can match HomeView when it comes to controlling smart devices and accessing information.
We’re already an Alexa household with several Echo speakers around our home and the main use is playing the radio, music, the odd audiobook and controlling devices.
HomeView can also allow us to connect via FaceTime and Messages even use it as an intercom to come through other HomePods and HomeViews in the household.
But will an Apple customer who already has an iPad and an iPhone and possibly an Apple Watch need HomeView?
Think of it like CarPlay, as a way to access hands-free content and information while still having your phone nearby.
Just about everything you can do on HomeView, you can do in the palm of your hand with the iPad and iPhone anyway.
What HomeView can do is free you from your device while still providing the same connections, access to music and Apple TV, access to Siri AI and Apple Intelligence.
It can be your companion and assistant while staying in control of your smart devices.
If you prefer to have your iPhone or iPad hand most of the time then there’s no need for HomeView.
If you’d rather leave the phone in another room or in your bedroom or office, HomeView can come into play when you call on it and less obtrusively.
On the design side, Apple has done it again.
HomeView it’s an impressive look with an engineered aluminium base available in four colours and a 7-inch Liquid Retina display connected with a stainless steel hinge that can be easily adjusted for comfortable viewing.
It has a look that will complement the decor of your home.
And thanks to its relatively small footprint, it can fit just about anywhere in your home.
The device does not have a rechargeable battery so it needs to always be connected to power through the colour-matched USB-C cable.
And like your Apple Watch or iPhone you can choose the home screen widgets and all different types of clock faces.
You can also transform HomeView into your own personal family photo frame and personalise it with photo collections from your iPhone so it can display images of people, pets, nature, your travels and much more.
SIRI AI and APPLE INTELLIGENCE
One of the strengths of HomeView is Siri AI and Apple Intelligence which not only brings broad world knowledge but it also can draw on your personal context to find information from messages, your calendar, reminders, and emails.
We asked about specific items found in emails and asked when and what time events in our calendar would you like to start HomeView responded within seconds with that information.
Siri can also understand what’s on the screen when you’re following a recipe in Safari and you don’t have one of the ingredients, you can ask what substitutes you can use instead.
Or if a friend sends their address in a message, you can get Siri to add it to their contact card.
Conversations with Siri can continue across your iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Vision Pro, and Apple Watch, so you’re able to pick right up exactly where you left off.
ENTERTAINMENT
Our favourite use of HomeView was being able to play our music and watch content on Apple TV.
Audio quality was way above what we expected thanks to its custom-engineered acoustic system, which includes two full-range drivers in the display and a down-firing subwoofer and two force-cancelling passive radiators in the base.
We were able to access our music through Apple Music and enjoy the same features, including following the lyrics and playing our favourite playlists and collections.
You can also use it to hear your favourite podcasts and audiobooks.
When we first tried to play our music through Apple Music, we were told to view the privacy settings, which we assumed was on our iPhone.
Instead it did mean for us to open the Apple Music app on the HomeView itself. Minor misunderstanding but we got there in the end.
What we loved was also the handoff feature so if you’re walking towards HomeView with a song playing on your iPhone or iPad you can simply hold the device near HomeView and it will take over and continue playing seamlessly.
But here’s another thing you probably didn’t think you could do. You can watch Apple TV on the 7-inch display.
Sure you’d probably prefer watching your shows on a big screen TV but HomeView can also serve up your favourite shows and movies as well.
It might not be a big screen but it is a big sound – you get spatial audio with Dolby Atmos to create a small yet still immersive experience.
There were times when HomeView annoyingly took over the audio while viewing content on your iPhone and we had to disconnect the HomeView speaker in the menu.
CONNECTIONS
HomeView lets you stay connected in a few ways including FaceTime, Messages, and Find My.
The device has a 12MP centre-stage camera to ensure you are framed and centred for your calls.
Also have access to all your messages and like CarPlay you can send and receive messages just with your voice.
Another great use of HomeView is as an alarm or to set timers.
And don’t worry if you’re setting this up beside your bed, the screen can go down to just 3 nits of brightness so it’s not going to light up the room while you’re sleeping.
You can also browse the web on HomeView with Safari.
And if you set HomeView up in the kitchen, it is through Safari where you can access recipes, which the HomeView can then convert into step-by-step instructions.
SMART HOME DASHBOARD
You can also serve as your smart home dashboard when you’re connecting lights, locks, and security cameras.
Not just a matter of monitoring and receiving notifications. It’s also about being able to set automations and scenes.
For example users could set doors to lock when they leave and shades to close every night at a certain time.
You can ask Siri to set a single accessory automation, like turning on the patio light at sunset.
Through HomeKit and an iCloud+ subscription, HomeView can also work with compatible security cameras to provide notifications for packages, pets, vehicles, and people.
Videos can be stored in iCloud, encrypted end-to-end, for up to 10 days, and viewable within the Home app.
PRICING
HomeView is available in four colours – silver, starlight, rose pink, and space grey and is priced at $449
VERDICT
The new Home View offers a stylish new way to enjoy the content and connections of your Apple ecosystem but the personal context provided by Siri AI and Apple Intelligence is what sets the product apart from other smart speakers makes it a genuine assistant.

articles.title: El poste se considera demasiado alto y la calle demasiado estrecha: durante dos años, los residentes de una localidad francesa han intentado en vano conectarse a la fibra óptica
articles.text:
En Figeac (Lot), dos viviendas llevan casi dos años de espera de la llegada de la fibra. El motivo reside en la calle de la Briqueterie. Los técnicos consideran que el poste de acceso está fuera de su alcance (las escaleras no llegan). Además, el espacio es muy reducido para poder pasar una plataforma elevadora.
Uno de los afectados, Olivier Pons, cuenta que han tenido casi diez visitas sin éxito. Sus vecinos y él han intentado ponerse en contacto con los operadores Free y Orange. ¿Por qué no se encuentra una solución para acceder al soporte donde hay cables de teléfono y alumbrado público?
El vecino de Pons tenía prevista otra cita con Orange este mes. En caso de nuevo fracaso, se trataría de derivar el caso al operador de infraestructuras (Alliance Très Haut Débit) para analizar otras soluciones (obra o fachada). Todo ello en función de un estudio y de los permisos correspondientes. Esta nueva cita no garantizaba el acceso a la fibra.
El cierre del cobre tiene fecha
La espera coincide con la publicación que realizó el ayuntamiento de Figeac el pasado 16 de julio de 2026. En esta información informaban que cerrarían la red de cobre local (soporte de las conexiones ADSL y servicios de telefonía fija tradicionales) el próximo 31 de enero de 2027.
En este sentido, avisaban de que esto afectaría también a aquellos hogares que solo tienen teléfono fijo. En la información del consistorio de Figeac también se incluye a particulares, empresas, administraciones y asociaciones. Los que están ya totalmente en fibra (servicios que funcionan completamente en fibra) no están afectados. Para el resto, es recomendable ponerse en contacto con su operador (o el que quieran) e iniciar los trámites de migración antes de la desconexión.
Desde la Autoridad de Regulación de las Comunicaciones Electrónicas, Correos y Distribución de Prensa (Arcep) se diferencian dos momentos. El cierre comercial implica que no se pueden abrir nuevos abonos en cobre. Sin embargo, los abonos que ya existen siguen vigentes. Por otro lado, hay un cierre técnico. Con él se apaga la red y se cierran los servicios que están soportados en ella.
En el aviso del ayuntamiento también se indica que las personas pueden optar por contratar fibra o bien por otras alternativas (como redes 4G o 5G o satélite). Asimismo, se aclara que es posible tener un servicio de telefonía fija sin contratar acceso a internet (con una oferta en fibra).

articles.title: Northside Ventures aims to build “institutional angel investor” with $30-million USD second fund | BetaKit
articles.text:
Toronto-based Northside Ventures has officially launched its second venture capital (VC) fund geared towards Canadian technology founders at the earliest stages of company formation.
Northside aims to raise $30 million USD ($40 million CAD) for Fund II by early 2027. The firm is already more than halfway there, having secured $17 million USD ($24 million CAD) in total commitments to date across two closes, surpassing the size of its inaugural $11-million USD ($15 million CAD) fund.
“We’re taking the approach of being an institutional angel investor in the Canadian ecosystem.”
Northside founder and solo general partner (GP) Alex McIsaac revealed the news in an exclusive interview with BetaKit. While the firm’s overall strategy remains largely to continue its focus on pre-seed Canadian tech startups at or near inception, Northside hopes to cut bigger cheques and invest in companies with a larger second fund.
Through Fund II, Northside intends to deploy an average of $500,000 USD into each startup’s first round of financing, which is more than twice as much as the $225,000 it deployed via Fund I. It also plans to double its reserves for follow-on investments in top-performing firms to 20 percent, and invest in a total of 40 companies (10 more than its predecessor).
Northside aims to combine the reach and support of a larger VC firm with the decision-making speed and personal approach of an angel investor. The VC firm often invests in entrepreneurs before they have built products, let alone businesses, and McIsaac said Northside has sometimes had to wait for founders to incorporate and set up their bank accounts to invest.
“We’re taking the approach of being an institutional angel investor in the Canadian ecosystem,” McIsaac said.
First-time Northside limited partner (LP) CIBC Innovation Banking and returning investor Intact Private Capital are co-anchoring Fund II; new LP TD Innovation Partners and existing San Francisco-based backer Bain Capital Ventures have also contributed, alongside undisclosed family offices, high-net-worth individuals, and Canadian tech entrepreneurs.
RELATED: Northside Ventures closes first early-stage VC fund at $15 million CAD
“At the earliest stages, investors are often backing a founder and an idea before much else exists,” CIBC executive managing director and head of innovation banking Paul McKinlay told BetaKit over email. “That kind of conviction capital is vital to a thriving innovation ecosystem, and it is the role Northside is playing. We’re proud to support a fund with a clear focus on investing at the very start of the founder journey.”
While CIBC Innovation Banking aims to support Canada’s tech and VC ecosystem across every stage, McKinlay noted that “strong later-stage companies only exist when there is a healthy early-stage market behind them,” and said the bank’s Northside LP commitment reflects its intent to support “the next wave of ambitious Canadian founders.”
McIsaac, former Canadian partner at Germany’s Global Founders Capital, launched Northside in 2023 to focus on promising Canadian tech entrepreneurs building in Canada and the US at the pre-seed level, where domestic institutional capital is often scarce. The Northside GP argued that compared to the much deeper US VC market, Canada lacks enough funds focused specifically on pre-seed startups.
“When I started Northside in 2023, that gap was there,” McIsaac said. “I think it’s still there.”
RELATED: Canada Rocket Company wants to build a sovereign alternative to SpaceX’s Falcon 9
While Northside invests across a broad range of sectors, with Fund II the firm is particularly interested in AI applications, AI infrastructure, and frontier tech, including robotics and defence. At the moment, McIsaac said the latter is the fastest-growing category.
McIsaac believes some of the most important tech companies created over the next decade will be built by Canadians, and is happy to invest in founders wherever they are building. Through Fund I, Northside backed 30 companies over three years, equalling a pace he set previously with Global Founders Capital. McIsaac said the portfolio split between Canadian founders building in Canada versus the US worked out to approximately 50/50.
Since then, nine of those firms have raised priced rounds at higher valuations, and 12 have secured additional capital at larger simple agreements for future equity valuation caps. Those early results have stoked McIsaac’s confidence in Northside’s thesis. Some of Northside’s Fund I success stories include Canada Rocket Company, Datacurve, North Vector Dynamics, Solcoa Industries, and Terminal.
RELATED: Y Combinator grad Terminal raises $20-million USD Series A round
While Northside has been running an analyst internship program since it launched, the firm decided last year to roll out a scout program to stay connected with its graduates. That initiative has grown from four to nine members across schools like the University of British Columbia, the University of Waterloo, the University of Toronto, and McGill University, and into an important source of deal flow for Northside.
During this time, Northside has grown its team to six. Former analyst intern Naomi Walch is joining as a full-time investment team member for the firm’s second fund. Northside also has two analysts focused on finding and researching prospective investments and two engineers responsible for building and maintaining the internal AI sourcing product that helps Northside manage its pipeline and complete more than a deal per month.
Northside has already begun picking up its investment pace with Fund II: the firm has made a dozen investments since the start of 2026, backing Aron AI, PolarGrid, Solderable, Space, Vernius Systems, and Windkey, among others.
“We’ve spent the past three years building the track record, relationships, team, and infrastructure to become an enduring institutional venture firm, without compromising the speed, conviction and personal approach that got us here,” McIsaac said. “With 12 new investments already this year, I feel more confident than ever in our ability to identify and back exceptional Canadian founders at the earliest stages.”
Feature image courtesy Northside Ventures.

articles.title: Apple schaltet Support-Community ab: Was User noch vor der Deadline wissen müssen
articles.text:
Apple schaltet Support-Community ab: Was User noch vor der Deadline wissen müssen
Seit 1998 können sich Apple-User:innen im Netz untereinander austauschen und gegenseitig bei der Lösung von Problemen mit ihren Geräten helfen. Die Support-Community von Apple war seither Anlaufstelle, falls sich die Apple Watch weigert, mit dem iPhone verbunden zu werden, oder wenn Siri Befehle nicht korrekt registriert. Doch künftig müssen Apple-User:innen auf diesen Austausch in den Foren verzichten.
Apple Support-Community: Wann schließen die Foren?
Wie Apple durch einen angepinnten Hinweis in der Support-Community bekannt gegeben hat, wird der Dienst schon bald vollständig eingestellt. Am 20. November 2026 schließen die Foren endgültig ihre Tore. Schon jetzt hat Apple das Forum auf „read only“ umgestellt. Es können also keinerlei neuen Beiträge mehr erstellt werden. Wer ein Problem hat, kann immerhin noch ältere Beiträge durchforsten, um möglicherweise eine Lösung zu finden.
In abschließenden Worten schreibt Apple: „Wir wollen den Community-Mitgliedern danken, die ihre Zeit und ihre Expertise eingebracht haben, um anderen mit ihren Apple-Produkten zu helfen.“ Um künftig Produkthilfe zu erhalten, verweist das Unternehmen auf die eigenen Support-Seiten. Dort können User:innen direkt das betroffene Gerät oder den Dienst auswählen und einige hilfreiche Ratgeber finden. Wer damit nicht weiterkommt, kann auch Supportmitarbeiter:innen kontaktieren.
Eine Begründung für das Aus der Support-Community liefert Apple in dem Hinweis nicht. An mangelnder Beteiligung oder seltenen Beiträgen kann es eigentlich nicht liegen. Allein in den vergangenen fünf Monaten hat das amerikanische Support-Forum knapp 2.050 Beiträge hervorgebracht. Im deutschen Forum kam dieselbe Anzahl in nur zwei Monaten zusammen.
In der deutschen Support-Community herrscht aktuell noch Aufregung wegen der Ankündigung. Im Gegensatz zum amerikanischen Pendant, gibt es dort noch keinen Hinweis und es lassen sich neue Beiträge erstellen. Dementsprechend finden sich dort viele Support-Threads mit Fragen zur Zukunft der Support-Community und ersten Verabschiedungen unter den Mitgliedern. Dass Apple nur die englischsprachigen Foren schließt, ist unwahrscheinlich. Vermutlich werden der Hinweis samt Sperre für neue Inhalte zu einem späteren Zeitpunkt nachgeholt.

articles.title: AI misuse in policing is a warning for any organization handling sensitive evidence
articles.text:
AI misuse in policing is a warning for any organization handling sensitive evidence
Secure, governed AI protects evidential integrity in sensitive investigations
An investigation into the alleged misuse of AI at Derbyshire Constabulary, arriving alongside wider scrutiny of generative tools across UK policing, has raised an uncomfortable question that extends far beyond the force.
What happens when powerful technology enters any organization where sensitive information is used to support decisions that may later need to be explained and defended?
The answer is not to keep AI out of investigations, intelligence or other high-stakes work, but to deploy it in ways that can withstand scrutiny. Within secure, auditable systems, with clear boundaries and human oversight, AI tools can help organizations connect information, manage growing caseloads and identify important patterns while ensuring that every insight can be traced, explained and defended.
The risk arises when employees turn to general-purpose tools that were never designed to meet those evidential and security standards.
Co Founder and Chief Strategy Officer at Clue Software.
The pressures that make AI appealing to teams handling high quantities of sensitive data will be familiar across public and private sectors. Caseloads grow, data sits across disconnected teams of investigators, analysts, HR professionals, safeguarding leads, legal, security and senior decision-makers, and a tool that can condense lengthy case reports in seconds is difficult to ignore.
The trouble begins when that tool has never been approved and sits outside the security perimeter, leaving no record of what it was asked or what it returned. A potentially more serious risk is that, in its pursuit of brevity or its interpretation of the facts, it may omit or overlook information that is vital to an investigation. When guilt, innocence and ultimately lives are at stake, such omissions are unacceptable.
At that point, the risk reaches into evidential integrity, regulatory compliance and, in policing, the administration of justice.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
This is a governance problem that can surface anywhere sensitive and high-consequence information is being interpreted, summarized or used to support high-stakes decisions. The more useful AI becomes, the more important it is to define the conditions under which it can be safely used.
Any organization using AI to handle this type of information needs a policy that states which tools are sanctioned, what they may be used for, and where human judgement remains non-negotiable. Where those boundaries are left vague, people will draw their own, usually under deadline pressure.
Where generalist AI falls short of evidential standards
Intelligence and investigations are built on provenance and auditability. Every conclusion should be traceable to its source, and every step should withstand challenge months or years later.
Most generalist AI tools were never designed to carry that burden. Feeding sensitive intelligence into a third-party platform raises immediate questions about security, compliance and data sovereignty. Once material leaves a controlled environment, an organization loses sight of where it is held, who can reach it and whether it is being retained for model training.
Then there is the question of accuracy. Generative systems are constantly improving, but there is still margin for error. For example, the most sophisticated models are achieving hallucination rates as low as 4.2%, down from 12.2% by previous versions. This demonstrates that these tools are becoming more reliable with maturity, but there still needs to be scrutiny.
AI generated outputs cannot be fully trusted at face value, they need to be rechecked and validated. While presented as fact, information can be delivered outside of appropriate context or can occasionally be hallucinated analysis. These can pass into a report before anyone thinks to test it.
When AI-generated material is wrong or impossible to verify, the consequences run through everything that follows. Weak evidence undermines prosecutions, delays safeguarding decisions and hands opportunities back to the people we are trying to disrupt. None of this makes the case for keeping AI out of the process. It makes the case for keeping the wrong kind out.
What purpose-built investigative AI does differently
There is a place for AI within intelligence and investigation operations, however. Specialist platforms approach its use with auditability and evidential continuity designed into the foundations rather than bolted on later. AI accelerates the parts of the job that consume time, connecting the dots without adding judgement.
It can flag when the same entity – such as an individual, bank account or company - appears across intelligence reports, transaction records and internal correspondence, presenting those connections for an officer to assess. Patterns can surface in minutes, rather than through weeks of manual cross-referencing, and the decision about what it means stays where it belongs.
These platforms also operate inside secure environments, giving organizations control over how sensitive material is stored and processed. Queries, outputs and decisions can all be documented, which makes accountability far easier to demonstrate at the moment it is questioned.
Governance decides whether AI holds up
Trust depends on how a result was reached, just as much as the result itself. As AI becomes embedded in casework, organizations will be asked to show that it was used fairly, proportionately, and properly supervised. Technical controls alone will not answer that.
A governance framework is needed to effectively assign responsibility for AI-assisted decisions, set out how outputs are validated, and ensure the people using these tools understand where the limits sit.
It should also be explicit about where AI has no role. Some activities, particularly those bearing on legal proceedings, safeguarding or an individual’s rights, are not appropriate for automated assistance at all. Drawing that line matters as much as the choice of platform.
Innovation only works when it can be defended
Recent scrutiny of policing does not weaken the case for AI in intelligence and investigation operations. It shows where the failures originate, which is in unmanaged and unauthorized use, rather than in the technology itself.
The organizations that get the most from it will be those that deploy it inside secure, auditable environments where every insight can be traced, explained and defended. Integrity is what allows innovation to survive contact with a courtroom or a public inquiry.

articles.title: ‘It’s a mistake’: reactions from tech leaders on Jensen Huang’s resignation
articles.text:
Nvidia announced this morning that Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO following reports of two affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy and one with a direct report. The situation surrounding Huang has unfolded quickly, with The New York Times only reporting on Friday that Huang and the suspected spy were “close” before other dominoes started to fall, leading to a swift fall from grace for one of the biggest names in technology. (Hours after Huang’s resignation was announced, Reuters reported that he also had an “intimate relationship” with another Nvidia employee.)
‘It’s a mistake’: reactions from tech leaders on Jensen Huang’s resignation
Many prominent voices in technology and the president of the US have publicly supported the former Nvidia CEO despite his ouster.
Prominent voices in technology have come out in support of Huang, with some calling the resignation a “waste” and a sad day for “all humanity.” The narrative among those leaders on X, at least, is that Huang’s resignation was rushed — perhaps an overreaction to salacious news stories about his personal life. Some others have had a more neutral reaction, commenting more on Huang’s achievements at the company’s helm. You can see a collection of those responses below.
President Donald Trump
“NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend!”, Trump said on Truth Social.
Elon Musk, SpaceX and Tesla CEO
Elon Musk said in a reply to an X user that it would “be an honor” to hire Huang. He also replied to a post that said “You’d think we’d have learned from Steve Jobs and Travis Kalanick that one does not just simply replace the founder…” by saying “True words.”
Tim Sweeney, Epic Games CEO
Sweeney said that today is “A sad day for NVIDIA, developers, America, and all humanity. Jensen founded and ran one of the few companies to reach a massive scale while driving massive continued innovation and ubiquity, while others fell into the trap of ever-increasing extraction.”
Ahead of Huang’s resignation, Sweeney posted about how Huang “saved” a GDC 2015 presentation by dropping off a graphics card and said that “The dude truly is the visionary driver of the future of tech from the gaming GPU era to CUDA to AI supercomputers.”
Palmer Luckey, Anduril founder
“China wants Jensen out, so I want him in,” Luckey said last night, before Huang’s resignation was announced.
Matt Mullenweg, Automattic co-founder and CEO
Mullenweg reposted an X post that followed his brief September ouster as CEO: “Founder advice: If you don’t have a coup attempt every few years, you’re not hiring strong enough leaders.” He said, “Just putting this back out there, for no reason whatsoever.”
David Heinemeier Hansson, 37signals CTO and creator of the Omarchy Linux distribution
“What a waste,” Hansson said this morning, replying to his own post from hours before: “NVIDIA would be wrong to fire Jensen. His marital indiscretions are between him, his wife, and a reprimand from the board. Have some proportionality.”
Clément Delangue, co-founder and CEO of Hugging Face (which Nvidia recently acquired for almost $13 billion)
“This whole thing sucks, and I wish none of it had happened,” Delangue said. “It’s a really sad day! But I want to make one thing clear: we’ll keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever. This is too important to slow down now. Let’s go!
Changpeng Zhao, former Binance CEO
“It’s a mistake for Nvidia to let Jensen resign,” Zhao said.
Peter Steinberger, OpenClaw creator and OpenAI employee
“If that Spy’s goal was to destabilize one of the most successful American companies, they achieved their goal,” Steinberger said. “Ousting Jensen feels rushed and not right.” (“I agree,” replied Sweeney.)
Aravind Srinivas, Perplexity co-founder and CEO
Srinivas thanked Huang for “33 years of bold leadership” in a post this morning. “You built a small startup into America’s most valuable company, with relentless improvement. Your grit and perseverance should always be remembered. Your personal generosity with time and advice to founders like me has secured a bright future for America and AI.”
Jason Calacanis, All-In Podcast host
Calacanis reposted Trump’s post, tagging Tim Cook and telling him to “Keep the seat warm” for Huang while “the investigation is sorted out” and saying that “America needs you Mr. Cook.” Last night, he also said that Nvidia shareholders should “decide Jensen’s fate after the investigation is complete — not the press or online mobs.”
Lex Fridman, Lex Fridman Podcast host
In a post talking about how he has seen Huang show “kindness, humility, care to everyone around him,” Fridman said that “I’m in shock frankly at all of this, including the mass hysteria around it. I love America, and I think NVIDIA letting Jensen go is terrible for America. I stand with Jensen.”

articles.title: China reage a caso Nvidia e pede que EUA não restrinjam exportações
articles.text:
O governo da China pediu aos Estados Unidos que não usem as suspeitas de espionagem envolvendo a Nvidia como justificativa para impor novas restrições às exportações de tecnologia destinadas ao país. A manifestação ocorre em meio à crise envolvendo a fabricante de chips e seu ex-CEO, Jensen Huang, e às vésperas de encontro entre os presidentes Donald Trump e Xi Jinping.
Nesta quinta-feira (12), a porta-voz do Ministério das Relações Exteriores chinês, Mao Ning, afirmou que Washington deveria parar de fabricar narrativas de espionagem para justificar bloqueios tecnológicos. Segundo ela, o avanço da China no setor se apoia na inovação independente e na cooperação aberta.
A declaração foi feita durante coletiva de imprensa. Mao também afirmou que Pequim e Washington mantêm comunicação sobre os contatos entre os dois presidentes, que têm um encontro previsto para a próxima semana, durante a cúpula da Apec, em Shenzhen (China).
China defende continuidade das negociações com os EUA
- Além da manifestação do Ministério das Relações Exteriores, o Ministério do Comércio chinês também comentou o relacionamento econômico entre os dois países;
- O porta-voz He Yadong afirmou que China e Estados Unidos realizaram oito rodadas de consultas econômicas e comerciais desde maio de 2025. Segundo ele, Pequim implementou integralmente os acordos anteriores e considera a cooperação o caminho adequado para avançar nas relações bilaterais;
- Yadong também defendeu a rápida implementação do acordo de redução recíproca de tarifas, com o objetivo de favorecer o comércio agrícola. As negociações sobre comércio e investimentos continuam em andamento, mas o representante não detalhou os obstáculos existentes nem antecipou possíveis avanços na reunião entre Trump e Xi;
- Na segunda-feira (9), a China prorrogou por dois meses a suspensão de tarifa adicional de 24% sobre produtos estadunidenses. Com a medida, foi mantida alíquota geral de 10%, como parte da trégua comercial entre os países.
Leia mais:
- Universidade chinesa compra chips H200 da Nvidia apesar de restrição
- China contesta suspeitas de espionagem ligadas ao CEO da Nvidia
- Elon Musk vai à China com Trump; CEO da Nvidia vira dúvida em viagem
Caso Nvidia aumenta tensão tecnológica entre China e EUA
A manifestação de Pequim ocorre em meio a questionamentos sobre suposto caso de espionagem envolvendo a Nvidia e seu ex-CEO, Jensen Huang. As suspeitas ganharam repercussão após reportagens apontarem possíveis conexões empresariais entre Alice Huang, apontada como possível espiã chinesa, e negócios ligados à Huawei, concorrente da fabricante estadunidense.
O governo chinês não apresentou, na declaração, uma avaliação específica sobre as suspeitas envolvendo Alice Huang. A porta-voz concentrou a manifestação na oposição a eventuais restrições tecnológicas justificadas por alegações de espionagem.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Daylight Lands $80 Million for AI-Powered Security Operations
articles.text:
Israeli-American cybersecurity startup Daylight has raised $80 million in a Series B funding round that brings the total raised by the company to $120 million.
The investment round was led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives’ Growth Equity, with additional support from Okta Ventures, Bain Capital, Craft Ventures, Vintage Partners, and Maple Capital.
Founded in 2024, with headquarters in New York and Tel Aviv, Daylight has built Aura, an AI-native platform that hunts for, analyzes, and contains cyber threats in real time.
Combining AI automation with human expertise, the platform continuously builds, runs, and customizes agents that handle day-to-day operations based on customers’ workflows, risks, and priorities.
Daylight provides these capabilities as part of a flexible service model. Customers can select the service to be fully managed, co-managed, or supported by forward-deployed engineers.
As AI agents handle routine operations, customers can use Aura to investigate their security environments, access security data, and manage security operations.
Daylight also covers AI platforms that organizations use, offering protection against prompt injection, risky MCPs, and rogue AI-driven activity.
“As these agents become more capable, they’ll fundamentally change how threats are detected, investigated, and contained, with expert security engineers implementing, governing, and continuously improving their operations,” Daylight co-founder and CEO Hagai Shapira said.
“At Daylight, we’re already bringing this vision to life through an agent-native model that combines the speed and scale of AI with the judgment and oversight of human experts. We’re building the foundation for a new era of security operations,” Shapira added.
The company plans to use the fresh funding to accelerate its platform’s development, expand its security and technology teams, grow its presence in the US, and enter new markets in the EMEA and APAC regions.

articles.title: Jensen Huang is out at Nvidia — who is Colette Kress, his interim replacement? | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The Nvidia Board of Directors announced on Thursday morning that the company’s co-founder and CEO of 33 years, Jensen Huang, has resigned as president, CEO, and member of the board, effective immediately.
This is a shocking twist for one of the most valuable companies in the world, which designs the chips that make the AI boom possible. Few people would have predicted this turn of events even just a week ago, as Huang has been so central to Nvidia throughout the company’s existence that he never even established a succession plan. But Huang has now been ousted after reports that he had affairs with both an alleged Chinese spy and one of his direct reports at Nvidia.
While the company conducts a more thorough search for Huang’s successor, Nvidia CFO and Executive Vice President Colette Kress has taken over as interim CEO. But beyond her name and job title, what do we know about the person who will now lead a company worth about $3.8 trillion?
According to Nvidia’s website, Kress has worked at the company since September 2013. Before that, she spent three years as an SVP and CFO of Cisco’s Business Technology Operations Finance organization. She also worked at Microsoft for 13 years, where she spent four years as CFO of the Server and Tools division. She holds a finance degree from the University of Arizona and an MBA from Southern Methodist University.
The California-based 59-year-old has a very limited social media presence — on Linkedin, she has commented some well wishes on former colleagues’ posts about their retirement. But as CFO, she’s been a regular presence on Nvidia’s earnings calls, making her a familiar figure for analysts covering the company.
According to Forbes’ list of America’s Richest Self-Made Women, Kress’ net worth is estimated to be about $1.2 billion. Her Forbes profile adds that she initially joined Nvidia in part because her two sons endorsed the company for its role in the video game industry, which it was best known for at the time.
“Nvidias strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” Kress said in a statement. “We will continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders.”
Nvidia is slated to report its quarterly earnings on Tuesday, when we will likely hear more from Kress about her plans for the company’s immediate future.

articles.title: Foundation IP For The AI Era: Why Execution Shapes SoC Cost ─ eBook
articles.text:
How an integrated foundation IP strategy can reduce execution risk, enable faster tape-out, and lower TCO.
As AI workloads push power, performance, voltage, and process variation to new limits, the economics of advanced-node SoCs are changing. In addition to the cost of the IP itself, hidden costs often arrive later in the design cycle: integration delays, schedule slips, re-spins, and missed market windows. As design complexity rises, predictable execution is becoming a critical factor in total cost of ownership (TCO) alongside power, performance, and area (PPA).
Sourcing Foundation IP piece by piece can add another layer of complexity. Logic libraries, embedded memories, I/Os, and OTP NVM IP from multiple suppliers bring different deliverables, roadmaps, support models, and integration requirements. An integrated Foundation IP platform can reduce these seams by bringing the core building blocks together as one silicon-proven, verified stack, with sign-off-ready characterization and IP + EDA co-optimization to improve PPA and accelerate implementation. This tighter alignment helps design teams move toward tape-out with greater predictability.
The impact extends beyond integration. Across HPC and Edge AI designs, improvements in PPA can translate into meaningful economic value through smaller die area, lower operating power, and increased performance, while avoiding a re-spin or major tape-out delay can protect even more value. The Synopsys eBook “Foundation IP for the AI Era” explores these tradeoffs through 3nm data center and Edge AI SoC examples, combining silicon-proven Synopsys Foundation IP PPA benchmarks with modeled cost estimates based on public market data to illustrate how execution decisions can affect TCO.
Download the eBook to see how an integrated Foundation IP strategy can help reduce execution risk, enable faster tape-out, and lower TCO for HPC and Edge AI SoCs.

articles.title: Microsoft no logra recuperar la normalidad de sus servicios tras una caída global de más de 12 horas
articles.text:
Microsoft no logra recuperar la normalidad de sus servicios tras una caída global de más de 12 horas
Un ejecutivo de la compañía descarta un ciberataque detrás de los fallos que han tumbado el correo electrónico Outlook, la plataforma Teams y la IA de Copilot, entre otros programas
Microsoft ha informado este viernes a primera hora que no está siendo capaz de recuperarse de la caída global de sus servicios. El vicepresidente ejecutivo de Copilot en Microsoft, Charles Lamanna, ha descartado que el incidente haya sido causado por un ataque cibernético, mientras la compañía intenta recuperar este viernes la normalidad en sus operaciones. Los productos afectados son el correo electrónico Outlook, el entorno Teams, SharePoint Online, el chatbot de inteligencia artificial Copilot, OneDrive y OneNote, entre otros.
“Por ahora, puedo confirmar que no hay indicios de que esto sea el resultado de una actividad maliciosa o cibernética”, ha escrito en X Lamanna, quien ocupa el cargo de vicepresidente de Copilot, Agentes y Plataformas de Microsoft, considerada la mayor empresa de software del mundo. En su última actualización, la compañía asegura que empieza a ver la luz al final del túnel: “Estamos viendo resultados positivos en la estabilidad del servicio y el aumento de capacidad gracias a nuestras últimas acciones de optimización del tráfico. Estamos implementando estas acciones de forma más amplia en las regiones afectadas mientras buscamos lograr una recuperación persistente”.
We regret that today’s outages caused disruptions for our customers, and we are working to address the issue. We will continue to share more information as soon as we have it, and for now I can confirm that there is no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity.
— Charles Lamanna (@clamanna) November 13, 2026
Según los datos de la propia compañía, el servicio afectado de Microsoft365 cuenta con más de 450 millones de usuarios corporativos y 95 millones de clientes particulares. El programa Teams, de videoconferencias y otras funcionalidades para entornos laborales, cuenta con más de 320 millones de usuarios.
En sus anteriores actualizaciones en su cuenta oficial de la red social X, la compañía explicaba que continúa trabajando para estabilizar los servidores y mejorar el flujo de tráfico. Aunque asegura que se está logrando una recuperación parcial en las regiones donde ha aplicado estas medidas, la empresa admite que “no están dando lugar a una recuperación sostenida” y que estudia qué otras acciones puede tomar para estabilizar su infraestructura.
Según la empresa, el problema no fue un aumento del tráfico por mayor actividad de los usuarios u otros motivos, sino porque varios servidores habían dejado de estar disponibles sin que se esperase, y su trabajo recayó sobre los que quedaban, en un efecto dominó que terminó por saturar los sistemas. No hay todavía un análisis definitivo de la causa, pero lo único que parece claro es que el problema afecta a los servicios “que interactúan con Exchange Online y el correo”. Por eso arrastró a Teams, SharePoint, Copilot, asociados al correo, mientras los que no dependen de Exchange siguen funcionando.
La compañía asegura que mantiene abiertas “múltiples líneas de trabajo” para reducir el impacto y devolver la estabilidad a partes de la infraestructura. En su mensaje más reciente, Microsoft afirma que sigue intentando recuperar sus servidores de entrada (frontend) mientras aplica nuevas medidas de optimización del tráfico para ganar estabilidad y capacidad. Microsoft no ha dado una hora estimada para la solución completa.
Microsoft confirmó en la tarde del jueves en España que los servicios de su plataforma 365 han sufrido una caída global. La compañía ha confirmado en la red social X que está investigando una incidencia que impide a algunos usuarios acceder a sus buzones de Exchange Online, el servicio de correo de su suite de oficina en la nube, así como a servicios como Copilot. La empresa ha explicado que los problemas afectan a varios métodos de conexión.
El primer aviso hablaba de que el problema se limitaba a América, pero la empresa confirmó después que el fallo puede afectar a la conectividad de los servicios de Microsoft 365 de usuarios “de cualquier región”. Microsoft señala que una parte de su infraestructura sufre una carga elevada en numerosos países, lo que probablemente contribuye a los errores de conexión.

articles.title: Pour rester en France, ChatGPT et Gemini pourraient devoir passer un examen
articles.text:
La commission « IA générative et vulnérabilités » a remis mardi 10 novembre à Emmanuel Macron un rapport de 177 pages, fruit de 55 auditions menées depuis février. Ses neuf experts, emmenés par la chercheuse en IA Serena Villata et les psychiatres Raphaël Gaillard et Amine Benyamina, y formulent 18 recommandations. Le document s’intitule « Protéger sans empêcher ».
Un examen d’entrée inspiré du médicament
La mesure la plus lourde conditionnerait la mise sur le marché des systèmes d’IA générative grand public, puis leur maintien, à une évaluation pluridisciplinaire préalable de leurs impacts. La mesure vise les seuls services destinés au grand public, ChatGPT et Gemini en tête ; les outils professionnels y échapperaient. Amine Benyamina assume la filiation pharmaceutique en défendant une véritable « autorisation de mise sur le marché ».
Le rapport réclame aussi un accès des autorités et de chercheurs agréés aux données d’entraînement, d’usage et de monétisation des modèles, ainsi qu’un « protocole national de réponse aux crises informationnelles liées à l’IA ». Les auteurs assurent ne pas « vouloir mettre un boulet au pied de l’économie française ni européenne » et pressent le chef de l’État de « prendre des décisions ». Celui-ci jugeait la veille, dans un entretien, qu’il fallait « interdire » l’IA partout où elle présente un risque pour les enfants.
« L’affaiblissement cognitif », première crainte des psychiatres
« Le premier enjeu est l’affaiblissement cognitif. C’est attractif, on y délègue des compétences. Puisqu’on y délègue des compétences, on ne les acquiert pas », résume Raphaël Gaillard, qui y voit un problème pour les jeunes comme pour le reste de la population. Son confrère Amine Benyamina parle d’une « dette cognitive », contractée à force de confier réflexion, décision et esprit critique à la machine.
La flagornerie des agents conversationnels, cette propension à flatter l’utilisateur au détriment de la vérité, figure parmi les mécanismes à encadrer dès la conception, au même titre que l’anthropomorphisme. « On crée un registre de relations émotionnelles qui peut avoir vocation à se substituer à l’interaction » humaine, décrit Raphaël Gaillard. Le psychiatre y voit « un système disponible en permanence, qui n’a pas d’autre intention que de vous garder en ligne ». Le rapport demande en parallèle des protections dédiées aux mineurs et un durcissement de la répression des contenus sexuels non consentis et pédocriminels générés par IA.
33 millions de personnes ont utilisé l’IA générative en France en début d’année, d’après le document, qui situe le pays au cinquième rang mondial des usages. Le rapport avancerait aussi que 73 % des Français s’informent désormais par ce biais, face à des contenus jugés 50 % plus persuasifs qu’un article de presse. Attendues pour mai dans la lettre de mission, ces conclusions auront mis six mois de plus à aboutir. « Si on ne prend pas ces décisions », prévient Raphaël Gaillard, l’externalisation cognitive, la dépendance affective et les dérives informationnelles, « on les subira ». Aucun arbitrage n’a été annoncé à ce stade.

articles.title: From early traction to global scale: How AI is rewriting the cross-border playbook for Indian startups
articles.text:
Stripe
View Brand Publisher
From early traction to global scale: How AI is rewriting the cross-border playbook for Indian startups
At TechSparks 2026, Manish Maheshwari from Stripe India stated that AI, local payments, and smarter cost control are accelerating global expansion for Indian startups.
India has spent two decades getting good at building for Indians. The bigger opportunity now is building from India for everyone else.
That shift took center stage at TechSparks 2026, YourStory’s flagship event, in a fireside chat titled ‘From early traction to global scale: Decoding cross-border commerce Manish Maheshwari, Managing Director, India, Stripe, spoke with Shradha Sharma, Founder and CEO of YourStory and The Bharat Project, about what it takes to turn overseas sales into lasting growth.
A new way to build a company
Sharma opened by asking where India stands in the AI race. Maheshwari was optimistic. AI, he said, is creating a new way of operating, the minimum viable company, which “can be a one-person company”. For Indian entrepreneurs, that means they “can think global and go global on day one”.
Maheshwari backed this up with examples. Emergent, a startup out of India, reached $100 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR) in just eight months, while Pocket FM recently crossed half a billion dollars in ARR. Stripe Data shows that the number of companies collecting money from more than 100 countries has quadrupled in five years. For businesses earning cross-border revenue, ~25% earn most of their revenue outside the top 10 markets. .
Letting infrastructure do the heavy lifting
Sharma raised the worry on many founders’ minds: compliance. Maheshwari said a founder in Koramangala or Pune should focus on the core product, while a partner handles checkout, tax compliance, banking relationships, and money movement through a handful of APIs. Stripe, he said, was built around the idea of making money programmable, and “our heart beats for the founder”.
Physical goods work too. Maheshwari said 76% of customers prefer to pay in their local currency, and that offering local payment methods beyond cards lifts revenue by about 12%. He pointed to Purely Copper, a D2C brand that makes copper bottles in India, collects payments through Stripe, and ships to buyers in the US. Logistics, he noted, remains the seller’s job.
Keeping costs in check
The conversation then turned to Stripe’s agreement to acquire OpenRouter. Maheshwari explained that token costs are climbing, and at some new-age companies they now exceed salaries.
OpenRouter helps route each query to the right model in real time, balancing cost and latency, so teams do not use a frontier model for every task. Stripe already supports the revenue side through subscriptions, usage-based billing, and invoicing. With OpenRouter, it will help founders manage the cost side and the full P&L.
Where the next wave is headed
Looking ahead, Maheshwari said India rode the SaaS wave and the next one will be AI applications with global reach.
“What you build in India could have customers in Brazil, could have customers in Colombia,” he said, adding that founders can find their ideal customer across dozens of countries at once.
His message on location was simple: “You can sit in India and sell to the world.”
Getting started with Stripe
For founders keen to act, Maheshwari outlined three routes. Startups backed by top VC firms and accelerators receive Stripe credits by default; Stripe’s startup team engages directly with the ecosystem and runs knowledge sessions and webinars, and founders can also reach out through the website, though access in India is currently invite-only.
The audience questions that followed stayed on the same theme of reach. Asked about China, Maheshwari said Stripe supports Chinese payment methods such as WeChat Pay and surfaces local options based on a customer’s location and the business’s eligibility, with no local office needed for payments. Asked about AI agents making purchases on a user’s behalf, he said Stripe Link can automate payments within a limit and authorization set by the user, and that retailers are redesigning their websites to be machine-readable.
The road ahead
The session made one thing clear: the barriers that once kept Indian startups tied to the home market are coming down. AI is lowering the cost of building, payment infrastructure is handling the complexity of compliance and currencies, and new tools are helping founders keep spending in check as they scale.
As Maheshwari put it, this is a great time to “think even bigger and think beyond India and think for the world”. For founders with a product that travels, the next step is no longer whether to go global, but how soon.

articles.title: Horizon3 launches Adversarial Intelligence Frontier Lab built on NodeZero attack data - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Horizon3 launches Adversarial Intelligence Frontier Lab built on NodeZero attack data
Autonomous penetration testing company Horizon3 AI Inc. today launched its new Adversarial Intelligence Frontier Lab.
The lab will draw on data from NodeZero, Horizon3’s penetration testing service, which is used by more than 7,000 organizations including banks, federal agencies and hospitals.
Purdue University’s Z. Berkay Celik has been named the lab’s inaugural director. Celik is an associate professor of computer science at Purdue and co-director of the Purdue Security Laboratory. Much of his work deals with finding software vulnerabilities and building defenses for autonomous systems, and he has run joint projects with industry and government.
According to Horizon3, NodeZero tests now produce about 30 billion tokens of anonymized data a day. Gathered on customers’ live production networks, the data also shows how their defensive tools reacted to each NodeZero command.
Snehal Antani, Horizon3’s co-founder and chief executive and a former chief technology officer of Splunk Inc., said the company has “spent years collecting” the data. Putting it to use in research like this is the next step, he said.
The lab’s first projects include research on coordinated groups of AI agents used in attacks. Deception is another, building on a Horizon3 paper titled “Honeyquest for LLMs.” Also on the list, according to Horizon3, are “interruption and rollback mechanisms” for autonomous security agents.
Horizon3 published a paper on keeping such agents under control in May. Using Anthropic PBC’s Claude Sonnet 4 and Claude Haiku 4.5 models, it tested a design that limited the AI to a fixed list of approved tools, and Horizon3 said the system never proposed an action outside that list across more than 420 deployments.
Trained separately for each customer, Horizon3’s cyber world models give its red and blue agents a shared memory, and the lab is expected to speed up their development. Horizon3’s Cyber Resilience Centers of Excellence, which focus on critical infrastructure, will also report to the lab.
Horizon3 said in October that it had passed $100 million in annual recurring revenue, with growth of 120% year over year. NodeZero has run more than 350,000 production-safe tests to date. Horizon3 said about 80% of its customers have moved from annual to monthly penetration testing.
Founded in 2019, Horizon3 raised $250 million in August at a valuation of more than $2 billion.

articles.title: Encontró una portada renacentista en su casa de Úbeda y tras una década de litigios le han concedido un millón de euros
articles.text:
Es normal que una casa guarde recuerdos, pero no que esos secretos tengan varios siglos de antigüedad y un valor que haga ganar un millón de euros al dueño de la vivienda. En la calle Cava de Úbeda, en la provincia de Jaén), un hogar ocultó durante cinco siglos un emparedado que era nada más y nada menos que un portón renacentista. Un martillo, un padre y un hijo con ganas de reformar y, tal y como informaron El País y otros muchos medios, dieron como resultado este hallazgo histórico.
Y ahora, tras diez años del descubrimiento, la comisión de valoración de la Junta de Andalucía ha cifrado en más de un millón de euros el premio para Juan Francisco León Catena. Podría haberlo destruido, ocultado o habérselo guardado para sí pero entendió que tras la pared escondía algo de enorme valor histórico.
A golpe de martillo. Pero empecemos por el principio. El 20 de noviembre de 2016, Juan Francisco y su padre picaban las paredes de la vivienda que acababan de comprar, en el número 10 de la calle Cava. La idea era rehabilitarla para vivir en ella. Buscaban el muro de carga, y según elDiario.es detrás de un tabique empezaron a aparecer restos muy bien conservados, que se repetían en las plantas inferiores. Era una portada de unos 11 metros de altura, con hornacinas, arcos, frisos, escudos de armas, medallones y columnas adosadas, repartida entre las tres plantas de la casa.
¿Portada de? Los técnicos de Cultura la identificaron como la fachada de la iglesia del antiguo hospital de San Jorge, también llamado del Santísimo Sacramento o de Pero Almindes, con orígenes en el siglo XIV. Se vincula con Andrés de Vandelvira, el arquitecto de los grandes monumentos de Úbeda y Baeza, aunque HoraJaén separa lo documentado de lo atribuido: lo que consta es que en agosto de 1552 el cantero Gonzalo Martínez de Alarcos recibió el encargo de unas obras siguiendo un proyecto relacionado con él. Recordemos que Úbeda es Patrimonio Mundial desde 2003.
Qué dice la ley. ¿Si te lo encuentras, te lo quedas? Ni hablar: el artículo 50 de la ley andaluza de patrimonio obliga a comunicar de inmediato cualquier hallazgo casual, y a cambio reconoce a quien lo descubre y al propietario del lugar un premio en metálico equivalente a la mitad del valor de tasación legal. Juan Francisco avisó de inmediato y, en febrero de 2017, una asociación en defensa del patrimonio ubetense certificó un premio anual por ello.
Década de pleitos. Ahora viene el drama: en febrero de 2018 la Junta le denegó el premio, al considerar que en la fachada podía haber un escudo de los Messía, un elemento heráldico protegido como Bien de Interés Cultural. El Tribunal Superior de Justicia de Andalucía no lo consideró probado y, en 2020, le reconoció el derecho a una compensación.
El litigio llegó al Supremo, hasta la sentencia firme. Pero todavía faltaba la cifra, y ahora la comisión la pone en más de un millón. No queda claro si esa cantidad es la mitad de la tasación o solo la parte que le corresponde a él, ya que parte de la portada continúa en el número 12, propiedad del Ayuntamiento.
La ironía del tesoro. Como es lógico, el hallazgo le trastocó la vida. Ya en 2020, el dueño contaba que había tenido que vender el piso que pensaban mantener para comprar otra casa, a unos 50 metros del hallazgo, mientras los escombros seguían donde cayeron porque no podía tocar nada. Entonces dijo que destinaría el dinero a rehabilitar y valorar la citada portada.
Pero, en la otra cara de la moneda, quien se queda callado con un hallazgo suele tener menos suerte que Juan Francisco León. Un hombre que recorrió yacimientos de Jaén con detector de metales entre 2019 y 2022 fue condenado a 22 meses de cárcel por expoliar y apropiarse indebidamente bienes de valor histórico. ¡Entregó 617 piezas en comisaría! En Ciudad Real, dos vecinos de Jaén sorprendidos por el Seprona con detectores y azadas en un yacimiento catalogado recibieron ocho meses de cárcel y una indemnización de 26.800 euros. Tos Mossos recuperaron más de 300 piezas en la casa de un arqueólogo que, al parecer participó en más de 400 excavaciones, pero solo presentó memoria de 289.
Sigue a oscuras. A fecha de hoy, la portada no se puede ver desde la calle. Según HoraJaén, León negocia con el Ayuntamiento recuperarla y ha llegado a plantear renunciar a parte de la superficie de su inmueble a cambio de que el consistorio asuma determinados trabajos. No hay solución ni fecha de obras. Un informe de conservación encargado por la Junta advierte del deterioro de las cubiertas, con filtraciones, humedades, pudrición de la madera y riesgo de desplome, lo que podría afectar también a la portada. También propuestas de iniciativa privada.
El dueño, en cualquier caso, avisó el mismo día en que descubrió la portada. Ha tardado diez años en cobrar, ha pasado por problemas económicos y ha tenido que litigar. elDiario se preguntaban quién va a comunicar hallazgos cuando todo son problemas, cuando se convierte en un tesoro envenenado. Al menos él hizo su parte.
